rows.original: The first thing you realize as you come to is that it's cold. By and large, your dazed and groggy mind registers that this isn't just because you've been stripped of all your gear and clothing, but also because you've been stretched out and tied at the wrists and ankles to a large stone slab — or at least, what feels like one, on account of you not being able to turn your head to look at what's under you. The deep, rust-heavy smell of old blood reaches your nose, and desperation grows in your heart as you realize what's in store for you. Alas, the bonds holding you in place are far too strong for you to break — they don't even seem like any sort of rope you've ever seen before, thick, black and wound with pulsating veins of green and purple. [pc.strengthRange 65|As strong as you are, testing them yields neither slack nor hope that you could ever hope to break them; these are clearly unnatural|You test your bonds out of desperation, and lamentably discover that they're as unyielding as you expected. These things are clearly unnatural.] ...Not that it would have made any difference. Surrounding you are dozens upon dozens of hooded shapes, all ready to pounce should you somehow affect your freedom. Looks like someone's overcompensating here, although with how you messed up his plans the last time, can you really blame him? Are you in a cave? Under the night sky? You can't tell — the only light comes from a number of standing torches set around where you've been stretched out, and they aren't strong enough to illuminate a ceiling, if there is one. It's just you, the cultists, and the darkness — — And a lone figure striding up towards you, the hooded figures parting to let him approach. Tollus. Of course, who else would it be? "Well, well," he says as he comes to a stop by your side, leaning on the altar nonchalantly. "We meet again, [pc.name] — although under much different circumstances this time. It was so nice of you to run into the arms of my underlings and save me the trouble of looking for you." Slowly and with great deliberation, Tollus draws a dagger from his robes, an ugly affair of dull wrought iron set with a gleaming blade of pure energy. He fiddles with the ritual weapon for a few moments, making sure you get a good look at it as he passes from hand to hand while he speaks. "You've been quite an annoyance, [pc.name], and I hate being annoyed. This is a rather grand house of cards I'm building here. It's enough that I have to put up with raging bulls like Kasyrra barging around and upsetting my plans without do-gooders like you causing me grief, too." [pc.isDK|Do-gooder? Even if you're not about to let Kasyrra corrupt the world on her terms, you wouldn't call yourself a hero of any kind.|Do-gooder, ha. That's one way to put it.] If he's going to kill you, just do it already. Tollus just smirks, clearly taking pleasure in drawing this out, making absolutely sure you know you're at his mercy. What was that saying again, that an evil man will want to gloat and watch you squirm, but a good man will kill you with hardly a word? "Kill you? Oh no, that would be a terrible waste. Do you know that demoness is absolutely infatuated with you? Such unbecoming behavior for a powerful mistress such as her... these emotions make her unstable, unfit for the clear-headed rule that is going to be necessary in the world she seeks to create. "Happily, I will help her achieve her grand vision, even at the cost of removing the roadblock that she presents to herself." He plans to usurp her. "Usurp? That's such an ill-sounding word. No. I merely want the best for our dark mistress and her goals, and her infatuation with you is quite troublesome, really. But I have plans to aid Mistress Kasyrra in shedding such paltry concerns..." Which is why he's looking for relics from the Godswar, specialist tools for dealing with demons. You get it now, even if you don't have all of the picture. "Very clever. Very clever. However, in order to test my theories in the coming days, I'll need a demon, you see. You'll do." That's a lot of rationalising away why he should be usurping Kasyrra. Come on, he can do better than that, right? He's supposed to be evil and all. A wicked grin spreads across Tollus's face. "You know, you're absolutely correct. I don't need to justify anything to you, or myself for that matter; I just have to do it, that's all. Now then, without further ado —" Tollus stares at you for a moment to let his words sink in, then draws the point of his dagger across the altar's surface, a soft scraping sound breaking the silence. "Any last words, [pc.name]?" [pc.isDK |You scowl and tell Tollus in no uncertain terms what exactly you think of him, putting all your vigor into struggling as you do so. Perhaps, perhaps by some miracle... "Oh my," he replies, feigning shock. "Such language. How unbecoming of the would-be champion. At the same time... such vitality. You'll make an excellent demon for my tests. Ssh, it'll all be over soon, and then we'll give you untold depths of pleasure so great you'll never want for anything else ever again." Twisting your lips in a scowl, you gather your spit in the back of your throat and jerk violently against your bonds in a thrust, aiming straight for the disgusting little man. Alas, you're not quite strong enough for your spit to reach its mark, and you watch in dismay as it arcs through the air and lands with a splat on the altar's stone surface. Tollus says nothing, but the smirk on his face as he cleans away your spit from the altar's surface tells you all you need to know. "Ah, [a] [pc.mf|man|woman] of action; very fitting. Not that it will avail you much now." |You glare at Tollus, but refuse to say anything. Even if he intends to rip out your soul, you're not going to let him have the satisfaction of seeing you blubber and beg for mercy, or even worse, lash out in impotent fury. That's just exactly what he wants, and bound as you are right now, it's one of the few things you can still do in a last act of defiance, no matter how impotent. "No? No famous last words? No speeches about how evil will never prevail?" Tollus stares at you for a few more seconds, until it's clear that you're not going to let yourself be goaded into the outburst he clearly desires. "Fine. Do as you will, it doesn't change your fate. ] Tollus raises the dagger high with both hands, looks down at you, and smiles. "Goodbye." There's a glint of light as the magical blade flashes down, and burning agony flares in your chest as Tollus buries it deeply in your ribs and twists the blade. Plunging his gnarled fingers into your chest, he rips out not your heart, but something brilliant and gleaming, beating with a frantic light as it's torn from your body. The last coherent memory you have is that of you lying in shock on the altar while Tollus holds the radiance of your soul aloft, rivulets of power running through his fingers and down his arms as he laughs. You can no longer bear the pain, and fall into the sweet embrace of darkness. But you do not die.

rows.raw: " The first thing you realize as you come to is that it's cold. By and large, your dazed and groggy mind registers that this isn't just because you've been stripped of all your gear and clothing, but also because you've been stretched out and tied at the wrists and ankles to a large stone slab — or at least, what feels like one, on account of you not being able to turn your head to look at what's under you. The deep, rust-heavy smell of old blood reaches your nose, and desperation grows in your heart as you realize what's in store for you. Alas, the bonds holding you in place are far too strong for you to break — they don't even seem like any sort of rope you've ever seen before, thick, black and wound with pulsating veins of green and purple. [pc.strengthRange 65|As strong as you are, testing them yields neither slack nor hope that you could ever hope to break them; these are clearly unnatural|You test your bonds out of desperation, and lamentably discover that they're as unyielding as you expected. These things are clearly unnatural.] ...Not that it would have made any difference. Surrounding you are dozens upon dozens of hooded shapes, all ready to pounce should you somehow affect your freedom. Looks like someone's overcompensating here, although with how you messed up his plans the last time, can you really blame him? Are you in a cave? Under the night sky? You can't tell — the only light comes from a number of standing torches set around where you've been stretched out, and they aren't strong enough to illuminate a ceiling, if there is one. It's just you, the cultists, and the darkness — — And a lone figure striding up towards you, the hooded figures parting to let him approach. Tollus. Of course, who else would it be? "Well, well," he says as he comes to a stop by your side, leaning on the altar nonchalantly. "We meet again, [pc.name] — although under much different circumstances this time. It was so nice of you to run into the arms of my underlings and save me the trouble of looking for you." Slowly and with great deliberation, Tollus draws a dagger from his robes, an ugly affair of dull wrought iron set with a gleaming blade of pure energy. He fiddles with the ritual weapon for a few moments, making sure you get a good look at it as he passes from hand to hand while he speaks. "You've been quite an annoyance, [pc.name], and I hate being annoyed. This is a rather grand house of cards I'm building here. It's enough that I have to put up with raging bulls like Kasyrra barging around and upsetting my plans without do-gooders like you causing me grief, too." [pc.isDK|Do-gooder? Even if you're not about to let Kasyrra corrupt the world on her terms, you wouldn't call yourself a hero of any kind.|Do-gooder, ha. That's one way to put it.] If he's going to kill you, just do it already. Tollus just smirks, clearly taking pleasure in drawing this out, making absolutely sure you know you're at his mercy. What was that saying again, that an evil man will want to gloat and watch you squirm, but a good man will kill you with hardly a word? "Kill you? Oh no, that would be a terrible waste. Do you know that demoness is absolutely infatuated with you? Such unbecoming behavior for a powerful mistress such as her... these emotions make her unstable, unfit for the clear-headed rule that is going to be necessary in the world she seeks to create. "Happily, I will help her achieve her grand vision, even at the cost of removing the roadblock that she presents to herself." He plans to usurp her. "Usurp? That's such an ill-sounding word. No. I merely want the best for our dark mistress and her goals, and her infatuation with you is quite troublesome, really. But I have plans to aid Mistress Kasyrra in shedding such paltry concerns..." Which is why he's looking for relics from the Godswar, specialist tools for dealing with demons. You get it now, even if you don't have all of the picture. "Very clever. Very clever. However, in order to test my theories in the coming days, I'll need a demon, you see. You'll do." That's a lot of rationalising away why he should be usurping Kasyrra. Come on, he can do better than that, right? He's supposed to be evil and all. A wicked grin spreads across Tollus's face. "You know, you're absolutely correct. I don't need to justify anything to you, or myself for that matter; I just have to do it, that's all. Now then, without further ado —" Tollus stares at you for a moment to let his words sink in, then draws the point of his dagger across the altar's surface, a soft scraping sound breaking the silence. "Any last words, [pc.name]?" [pc.isDK |You scowl and tell Tollus in no uncertain terms what exactly you think of him, putting all your vigor into struggling as you do so. Perhaps, perhaps by some miracle... "Oh my," he replies, feigning shock. "Such language. How unbecoming of the would-be champion. At the same time... such vitality. You'll make an excellent demon for my tests. Ssh, it'll all be over soon, and then we'll give you untold depths of pleasure so great you'll never want for anything else ever again." Twisting your lips in a scowl, you gather your spit in the back of your throat and jerk violently against your bonds in a thrust, aiming straight for the disgusting little man. Alas, you're not quite strong enough for your spit to reach its mark, and you watch in dismay as it arcs through the air and lands with a splat on the altar's stone surface. Tollus says nothing, but the smirk on his face as he cleans away your spit from the altar's surface tells you all you need to know. "Ah, [a] [pc.mf|man|woman] of action; very fitting. Not that it will avail you much now." |You glare at Tollus, but refuse to say anything. Even if he intends to rip out your soul, you're not going to let him have the satisfaction of seeing you blubber and beg for mercy, or even worse, lash out in impotent fury. That's just exactly what he wants, and bound as you are right now, it's one of the few things you can still do in a last act of defiance, no matter how impotent. "No? No famous last words? No speeches about how evil will never prevail?" Tollus stares at you for a few more seconds, until it's clear that you're not going to let yourself be goaded into the outburst he clearly desires. "Fine. Do as you will, it doesn't change your fate. ] Tollus raises the dagger high with both hands, looks down at you, and smiles. "Goodbye." There's a glint of light as the magical blade flashes down, and burning agony flares in your chest as Tollus buries it deeply in your ribs and twists the blade. Plunging his gnarled fingers into your chest, he rips out not your heart, but something brilliant and gleaming, beating with a frantic light as it's torn from your body. The last coherent memory you have is that of you lying in shock on the altar while Tollus holds the radiance of your soul aloft, rivulets of power running through his fingers and down his arms as he laughs. You can no longer bear the pain, and fall into the sweet embrace of darkness. But you do not die."

rows.original: How long has it been? The crystal walls of your prismatic prison are impenetrable to a soulless monster like you. The prism was designed as an artifact to entrap and pacify wraiths, and so far it's served its purpose excellently when applied to demons, too. You've long since lost track of any sense of time in this place[party.hasCompanions|, nor have you any inkling of what might have happened to [party.compNames]]. In your current state, it's hard to care. Your tormentor — you vaguely remember his name as Tollus — shows up from time to time to conduct experiments. Sometimes he transforms various parts of you in the process, testing formulations and spells he intends to use on himself, but a demon's shapeshifting nature always ensures that you're able to return to what you consider your native form. A perfectly reusable test subject, as he likes to point out. At first, your demonic nature causes you to rage at him, for what he did to you, but this crystal world is a madhouse. There's nothing to look at but your own appearance in this prismatic prison, no escape from it for hours, days, months, until your own consciousness starts to slip and fade. And when you're aware of what you've become... this isn't a dream, because demons aren't capable of dreaming. And then all the emotions you have just vanish into the ether. You can just faintly recall that you weren't always a demon, that you were something, someone else in the past... but what were you? Your mind draws a blank. The Sorran artifact Tollus retrieved... it does its job well. Far too well, perhaps. You don't know how long you've been here, but on one of Tollus's visits, he has someone else with him — another demon, winged, horned... you vaguely remember her. Did you know her when you were... in the before time? There's something missing, though. Something about her that she once had, but no longer possesses. "Let me go!" she roars, her teeth bared. "As your dark mistress, I demand —" "You'll demand nothing, Kasyrra," Tollus replies with a sneer. "I've had enough of you and your demands; in time, you'll forget all about them. But look, here's someone you might recognize — you can spend the rest of eternity in here with [pc.himHer] and be happy, can't you? I don't even have to come back into this place any longer, since I can just tap both your powers from outside. Your constant pining for [pc.name] has made things troublesome, and I really can't have you diverting resources away from our ultimate goal. In your absence, Dark Lady, I'll be sure to be a good regent and fulfill your vision." Kasyrra's eyes grow wide as she catches sight of you. "[pc.name]! Can it be truly —" She whips her head back to where Tollus was a moment ago to find the space empty and void, and then screams in rage. You watch blankly as Kasyrra hammers on the walls of the prism, just like you did all that time ago, tearing at the impenetrable, reflective surface until her claws break off and she's bleeding from her fingers. It's all right. She'll come to understand in time that there's no escape from this world. But at least it'll be nice to be able to spend some time in this vast, reflective emptiness with another demon. Forever... That's a very long time to have spent alone. At last, Kas gives up trying to break free of this prison and falls to her knees, holding her bleeding fingers. Perhaps for the first time since you've met her on that stormy night, she appears dejected, miserable, vulnerable. The demoness isn't one to openly sob, but you can see tears forming in the corners of her eyes as she turns to regard you. You feel... you haven't felt anything for a long while, but the sight of Kas in here with you stirs something within your bosom, awakening something that ought to have died a long time ago. Her full lips turn into a pout, then twist, as if uncertain as to what fashion of rage to unleash upon you; at last, she leaps to her feet and starts pounding on your chest, the tears finally flowing freely down her cheeks. "It's all your fault, you big idiot!" she screams, venting her sorrowful rage on you, her fists a blur. A mortal form would have been pummelled to pulp within seconds, but as Tollus was fond of informing you now, you're a demon. "Do you know how long I spent looking for you after you just vanished? And to think that the slimy little man had you under my nose all this while!" He... he took your soul. You vaguely remember that you should do something, and wrap your arms around Kas' curvaceous form; she leans into your embrace, still sniffling. "That's where he got all that power from." Kasyrra says with a sigh. "I ought to have been more suspicious, [pc.name]. I should've started asking hard questions. But he was being so efficient, so useful, enough that I had the time to go on a wild goose chase looking for you... "...And now I'm here. With you. I suppose I got what I wanted, didn't I?" Kasyrra lets out a choked, bitter laugh, perhaps expecting you to say something, but you're not sure. It's been so long since you had a conversation, an actual one, and it feels like something new, something strange. Tollus said she was infatuated with you... "I'm not just infatuated with you — well, I might have been to begin with. But... you dummy. I could've taken your soul any time, from the moment we first met. And yet... for some reason, I couldn't bring myself to do it. That's not right. Demons don't think that way, not usually. And it troubled me, in all those nights when I was looking for you... why? Why couldn't I bring myself to do it? "Then I knew why... I love you, [pc.name]. That's impossible. Demons don't love — they don't care for anyone or anything but themselves, that's what happens when you lose your soul. But I did anyway. It defied everything I learned and discovered about the nature of the soul during my time in Lethice's service. I told myself it was just for science, I wanted to investigate this phenomenon, find a way to explain it, observe your soul for a while before harvesting it for my own... and somewhere along the way..." rows.original: Sanders notices you looking at the door leading to the cloister, and nods. "I take it you'd like to spend some time in seclusion from the world and focus on getting yourself right with the gods?" The thought had crossed your mind, yes. "If that's what you want, we'd appreciate a donation of five hundred coins," Sanders explains matter-of-factly. "Not just for the upkeep of the various relics within that greatly contribute to an atmosphere conducive to the correct mindset, but for your board over the three days, as well as the various peripherals involved in your meditation. Additionally, you'll need to supply some sort of primary component for the incense to be used. "Now, you were instrumental in helping us set up the cloister, for which I've reduced the requested donation to its barest minimum, but even a chapel like this has operating expenses. Well, would you still like to use the cloister?" If you wish to use the cloister, it will cost you 500 coins and some winterstem, take three days, and burn off 10-20 corruption based on your current corruption level. Is this what you want?

rows.raw: " "All right, then. Give me a moment to make the necessary preparations; I'll be back shortly." With that, Sanders turns and paces back into the rectory. But no, she's more than welcome to join you for your little retreat if she likes. Your pink kitty winks and taps you with her tail. "I'll be with Dogmeat if you need me," Brint says as he turns and clomps out of the chapel. "Glorious idiot had the most insane of ideas last time we were talking; I think I'll take him up on the offer." | Brienne looks around and shrugs. If that's what she wants, she's more than welcome to join you in the cloister. You've already paid the fee, after all. "Thanks." | You turn to Kiyoko. Does she want to join you in the cloister? "Hmm. I will respectfully decline. This manner of worship is a little too far removed from the appropriate rites dedicated to Keros; I will return home and make the necessary arrangements. Besides, I would like to take some of the following days to check in on our [kiyoko.numKits 2 |children |daughter ]." All right, then. You'll see her in three days. Your kitsune wife turns and is gone with a swish of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails. | "I'll head up back to the castle while you're out of it," Atugia says, thumbing over her shoulder at the chapel entrance. rows.original: After ten minutes or so, Brother Sanders returns with a large iron key, which he slides into the oaken door and turns. The cloister is welcoming as always, lit by manyhued colors streaming in from the stained glass windows, and Sorra's Succor lies displayed high on a wall above several tapestries presumably depicting scenes from the Godswar. Stepping ahead of you, Brother Sanders fills the censer with several sweet oils, then adds the winterstem before lighting the wick and watching the aromatic fumes disperse into the air. "Aah. Nothing like a good spot of warm oil to clear the mind and soothe the joints. All right then, [pc.name], I'll leave you to your meditations and reflections."
rows.translation: 大约十分钟后，桑德斯修士拿着一把大铁钥匙回来了。他将钥匙插入橡木门中转动了一下，修道院里一如既往地充满了温馨的氛围——彩色光线从彩绘玻璃窗中照射进来，照亮了整个空间。而索拉的救赎则高高展示在墙上，其下方挂着几幅大概描绘着神战场景的挂毯。 桑德斯修士走在你前面，他将几种芳香精油倒入香炉中，然后加入冬茎，点燃灯芯，接着看着那些芬芳的烟雾散布在空气中。“啊，没有什么比来一点温热的好油更能让头脑清醒、舒缓关节的了。那么好吧， [pc.name]，我就不打扰你冥想与反思了。”

rows.original: With everything out of the way, you set aside your stuff against a wall and take up a place on one of the simply woven prayer mats. [party.hasAll cait etheryn |Cait and Ryn take up spots to either side of you, and you steady yourself, trying to get into the right frame of mind for this. Sure, Cait's cute butt and kitty titties are a distraction unto their own, but the warm aroma of winterstem soothes your thoughts and wipes the lingering traces of desire from your mind — something that Ryn is equally glad for as she gulps in big lungfuls of the stuff. "Phew," Ryn mutters with a soft sigh. "Relief at last." Relief from what, you don't need to ask. |[party.comp cait etheryn |Cait takes up the prayer mat to your left, wiggling about as she makes herself comfortable on her knees. Sheesh, even when she's not trying, she's still making herself as attractive as possible, eh? Guess it's got to be an ingrained instinct at this point. |Ryn takes up the prayer mat to your right, letting out a soft sigh as she makes herself comfortable on her knees. Taking deep lungfuls of the warm, steamy incense rising from the censer, she looks the most relaxed you've seen her in a long time. "Phew. Relief at last.." Or at least, relief that doesn't need to be of a sexual nature. "This feels just like the chapel of Lumia back in the palace used to, perhaps even more so. I like it." You do, too. |With the heavy stone walls muting all sound in the chapel, let alone that of Hawkethorne itself, you're left alone with the steady rhythm of your own breathing, the gentle hiss of the gilded censer, and the ringing of your ears. Despite all this, the cloister doesn't feel stuffy at all — instead, there's a sense of solemn gravitas in the air that presses down upon you. ] ] The gentle yet firm presence of the Sorran relic shines down upon the entirety of the cloister, and you focus your thoughts. [pc.bgMulti acolyte arcanist |Meditative exercises are no stranger to you given your religious upbringing, and you methodically draw a veil over each of your senses in succession until you feel truly at peace. As you carefully regulate your breathing and hold it there for a while, a sense of centeredness and security washes over you, starting from the tips of your toes before working its way up your body and into your head. |You're familiar enough with meditation, even if it's not of the religious sort. Mental exercises were part and parcel of your training as an arcanist, after all. With your full concentration at hand, it's a small matter to gather your thoughts into a neat little package and shunt them into a corner of your mind, leaving a dark, peaceful blankness behind your eyes for you to luxuriate in and begin the task of keeping your mental house in order, narrowing the world to a manageable size. |You've not had any formal training in such mental exercises, but the cloister's atmosphere is so calming that you find yourself lapsing into a reverie anyway. Gradually, you feel the world around you recede as your senses narrow and mind expands, the winterstem helping you on your way. It's a little awkward and you feel out of place doing this, but you're determined to make it work. ] Finally, only you and the shortspear on the wall remain[party.hasAll cait etheryn |, with Cait and Ryn on either side of you |[party.comp cait etheryn |, with Cait at your side |, with Ryn at your side ], your mind keen and sharp like the edge of a knife. ] Thoughts flow... as does emptiness. There're still a few stray worries lingering on the edges of your consciousness, but the energy that washes outwards from the relics sweeps them away like debris on a retreating tide, leaving your mind clean and pristine, ready to face what lies ahead. No doubt there'll be very many tempting foes in your path before this is over, and you'll want to face them with a clear mind. Time loses all meaning... You're not sure how long you remain like this, your inner eye focused towards the immaterial and metaphysical. A sensation of long, drawn-out peace, helped along by the slow-burning, perfumed oils. In a sense, it's like being asleep, but whether it's because of the nature of your seclusion or what you've been secluded with, you feel completely lucid throughout the whole thing, just... disoriented, as if your senses are sending you messages your mind can't quite parse. The next thing you know, light's streaming in from the stained glass window, bright, early morning light accompanied by [var0 |Shar shaking you by the shoulder, telling you it's time for breakfast. |a small card left by the censer reminding you to take breakfast in the mornings. Good old Sanders. ] Despite you not feeling in the least bit hungry, you head out back to the rectory with [party.hasAll cait etheryn |Cait and Ryn |[party.comp cait etheryn |Cait |Ryn |your thoughts still swimming in your head ] ], to be greeted by a warm omelette and fresh-baked bread. The next two days are more or less the same. Settling in the cloister, entering that same dream-like reverie, feeling not in the least bit tired when roused for meals despite you having been kneeling in the same position for hours on end. [party.hasAll cait etheryn |Cait and Ryn are quiet and contemplative in the moments all three of you are lucid together, passing knowing looks between the three of you but never quite giving voice to whatever it is that you're experiencing — a touch of the divine, perhaps. |[party.comp cait etheryn |Cait is quiet and thoughtful over these days, quite the change from her usual bubbly self. Perhaps this isn't a form of religious devotion she's particularly used to, being a Mallachite, but she is certainly taking this seriously. |Ryn is surprisingly devout over these days. While she didn't strike you as the particularly religious type when you first met her, she did mention that the palace where she lived had a chapel to Lumia, didn't she? You wonder if it could have helped through all those years living under her abusive sister... |Sanders never asks about your experiences when you sit down for meals with him, but the knowing look on his face tells you he's familiar with what you're going through, or at least something very similar. ] ] At last, the third day draws to a close, and with it your time away from the world. As long as it's lasted, the oil in the censer's almost all gone now, the winterstem you added but fragrant ashes at this point. Morning light streaming in through the stained glass windows, you crane your head up to gaze upon the Sorran shortspear up in its place of honor. There's a palpable sense of absolution, or a weight being lifted from your shoulders; it's but momentary, but you're certain it was there. Ah... Well, time to be off [party.hasCompanions |and see about getting everyone back together |and make yourself ready ]. There's more work to be done.

"Seen a Yvennese paladin around, Garth?" you ask.
    
    He nods at a woman sat at the other end of the bar, scanning the crowd. "Don't know how you missed her when you walked in, [pc.name]. She's right there. She's even got a room here now."
    
    "Oh. Thanks," you say.

With her facing you like this, you can see under her hood perfectly well, though from some angles it casts shadows across her face. Clasped at her shoulder by a Tiran symbol, her well-worn cloak flows down her back, the mark of any traveller. Her voluptuous bosom is held tightly by her breastplate, though a sizeable gap in the middle allows you a view of the center and underside of her enormous breasts, as well as the incredible cleavage created in their union. rows.original:
"Was it difficult to get here from Yvennes?" you ask. 
    
    "Parts of it, at least, were not so bad," Alice says. "The roads are well-travelled, and on horseback I made good time. But upon crossing the border... it was like entering another world." She shakes her head in disbelief. "Animals rising up to attack me. Creatures I have never before seen. It was madness. How do people live here? Has it always been like this?"
    
    "It's more of a recent problem," you say. "It's a long story, but I should acquaint you with it. It'll be dangerous for you to walk around without knowing."
    
    You recount the story of Kasyrra's invasion, minus a few key details. Alice's expression goes from curious, to alarmed, to worried over the course of your spiel, and by the time you finish, she's deep in thought.
    
    "By Tira, what of the princess?" she mutters to herself, rubbing her temples. You pretend not to hear, and when she raises her head. "So the land is cursed."
    
    "You could interpret it like that," you agree.
    
    "Hmmm," Alice murmurs. "That explains much. I had begun to wonder if the earth itself would waylay me."
    
    You think back to the alraune. "That is not an impossibility."

    "Was it difficult to get here from Yvennes?" you ask. 
    
    "Parts of it, at least, were not so bad," Alice says. "The roads are well-travelled, and on horseback I made good time. But upon crossing the border... it was like entering another world." She shakes her head in disbelief. "Animals rising up to attack me. Creatures I have never before seen. It was madness. How do people live here? Has it always been like this?"
    
    "It's more of a recent problem," you say. "It's a long story, but I should acquaint you with it. It'll be dangerous for you to walk around without knowing."
    
    You recount the story of Kasyrra's invasion, minus a few key details. Alice's expression goes from curious, to alarmed, to worried over the course of your spiel, and by the time you finish, she's deep in thought.
    
    "By Tira, what of the princess?" she mutters to herself, rubbing her temples. You pretend not to hear, and when she raises her head. "So the land is cursed."
    
    "You could interpret it like that," you agree.
    
    "Hmmm," Alice murmurs. "That explains much. I had begun to wonder if the earth itself would waylay me."
    
    You think back to the alraune. "That is not an impossibility."
    
    "I can hardly be surprised by now," Alice sighs. "I suppose I will keep my sword at the ready whenever I venture beyond the town walls... and pray to Tira that my charge is safe."

rows.original: "I've never been to Yvennes," you say. "What is it like?" Alice thinks for a moment. "The small villages and towns are not unlike Hawkethorne. It is not an easy life, working to live. The life of a baker or a blacksmith would make a noble blanch. The capital, though, is quite different. Opulence is not quite the right word, but it is close." "Have you seen Khor'minos?" you ask. She shakes her head. "I have not. I would like to, should I have the time. I imagine it is quite different from Garonne – a different aspect of majesty. Garonne's beauty is the result of decades of work from artisans. It was made to be beautiful. As I understand it, Khor'minos is a city of industry." "It is," you agree. "Form follows function. It is a very impressive city, though – or was, before the siege. It still is, but..." "We had heard news of the king closing the borders," Alice says, frowning. "Tis true, then?" You nod. "They have their hands full internally. A quarantine was enacted some time ago." "I imagine the court of Yvennes will be quite interested in what happens in the wake of this," Alice says. "The military might of the minoans is very well-known. The border princes are ever wary, to say the least." You suppose it's not hard to imagine Khor'minos coming out of this significantly weakened... but it will depend on how you handle the threat of Kasyrra.

rows.original:
"Tell me about yourself," you say.
    
    "There is not much to tell," Alice says. "I was born in a border region of Yvennes as the only daughter of a blacksmith and a baker. I grew up to become a squire, and then a paladin of Tira. I do have two younger sisters now, though." She gives an affable sigh. "And a third on the way."
    
    "What do you do when you’re not adventuring in a foreign land?" you say with a smile.
    
    She thinks. "I pray. I practice my swordsmanship. I travel to aid people in need, as is the creed of my order. That is enough for me. I have the rest of my life to pontificate – the time I can spend helping people with my sword arm is limited."
    
    You nod. "I understand. Purpose doesn't need to be complex."
    
    Alice smiles. "Exactly. Tis true I live a simple life. But I do find it gratifying to know mine efforts bring about a modicum of improvement for the people we serve."
rows.translation:
“跟我说说你自己吧，”你说。
    
    “没什么好说的，”爱丽丝说。“我出生在伊薇恩的边境地区，是一位铁匠和一位面包师的独生女。我长大后成了一名侍从，之后又成了蒂拉的圣骑士。不过我现在确实有两个妹妹了。”她亲切地叹了口气。“还有第三个也快出生了。”
    
    “你不在异国冒险的时候会做什么？”你微笑着问。
    
    她想了想。“我祈祷。我练习剑术。我按照我们教团的信条，四处帮助需要帮助的人。这对我来说就足够了。我余生还有时间空谈理论——而我能用手中之剑帮助他人的时间是有限的。”
    
    你点了点头。“我明白。目标并不需要多么复杂。”
    
    爱丽丝笑了。“正是如此。我确实过着简单的生活。但知道自己的努力能为我们所侍奉的人们带来一点点改善，我确实感到欣慰。”

rows.original:
"So you belong to an order of paladins," you say.
    
    Alice nods. "The Order of the Hourglass. We venerate Tira's aspects as the goddess of death and of time. A pillar of our order is spending what time we have wisely."
    
    "And death?" you prompt.
    
    "Death comes for us all, in the end," Alice says. "It is what gives our lives meaning, what gives them value. It is what drives us to accomplish things both great and small. That is why our lady Tira is the goddess of both death and time. They go hand in hand, together, towards the horizon."
    
    "What does the order do?" you ask.
    
    "We counsel. We aid. We protect. We venture," Alice says. "Though it might seem mundane, all things we do are informed by our worship of The Lady of Death. I am here to keep unrightful death at bay."
    
    "Have you stopped by the church here?" you ask.
    
    Alice nods. "Just briefly, to pray when I first arrived. Brother Sanders was pleasant."
    
    "He used to be a paladin himself, you know," you say.
    
    She smiles. "He did not seem surprised I was here. Perhaps I will ask him about his faith one day."
rows.translation:
“所以你是属于某个圣骑士团体的，”你说道。
    
    爱丽丝点了点头。“沙漏圣骑士团。我们尊崇蒂拉身为死亡与时间女神的诸般面向。我们团体的一个重要信条，就是明智地使用我们所拥有的时间。”
    
    “那死亡呢？”你追问道。
    
    “死亡终将降临到我们每个人身上，”爱丽丝说。“正是死亡赋予我们生命意义，赋予它们价值。正是死亡驱使我们去成就或大或小的事业。因此，我们的蒂拉女神既是死亡之神，也是时间之神。两者相伴相随，一同走向地平线。”
    
    “这个教团都做些什么？”你问道。
    
    “我们提供劝诫。我们施以援手。我们给予保护。我们外出冒险，”爱丽丝说。“这些事看似平凡，但我们所做的一切都源于对死亡女神的崇拜。我在这里，是为了阻止不该发生的死亡。”
    
    “你去过这里的教堂吗？”你问道。
    
    爱丽丝点了点头。“只是刚到的时候去祈祷了一小会儿。桑德斯修士人很好。”
    
    “你知道吗，他以前自己也当过圣骑士，”你说道。
    
    她笑了笑。“他似乎并不惊讶我在这儿。也许哪天我会问问他关于信仰的事。”

rows.original: "I think I have the measure of you," you say, giving her a smile. "Let's talk about the reason you're here in Hawkethorne." Alice leans forward at the bar, as though to guard your conversation from unfriendly ears. "I am here in pursuit of a woman. The third princess of the Trusant family, of Yvennes. She has been abducted – or was abducted, I do not know which – and taken out of Garonne heading northwest. I have been following the trail for quite some time, and as far as I can tell it ends here." "Abducted?" you say. "Yes," Alice says. "But along my journey I have begun to believe that she has escaped them and, for some reason, has not returned home. Perhaps she believes she would be in danger, returning along the route she was taken..." She shakes her head. "I cannot say." "Why do you think she escaped?" you say. "I was able to track down a few people who had seen her, and even one that travelled with her," Alice says. "She was consistently unaccompanied by anyone else, and though the merchant she travelled with was perhaps regrettably wise enough not to ask questions of a lone woman on the road, he did say it seemed like she was running from something." "What is her name?" you ask. "Evelyn," Alice replies.

rows.original: "Alice..." you start, then sigh. "Let's get a table. This is going to be a long conversation." With food and drink at hand, you lean forward to talk to Alice. "Firstly, let me ask. Who sent you to get Evelyn back, and what was their reasoning?" "I was sent by my order," Alice says. "We were informed by the royal family themselves." "So the royal family told you she was abducted," you note. She nods, and you sigh. "Evelyn is here," you say, and Alice's eyes go wide as she leans forward. You hold up a hand to halt her inevitable questions. "She is safe, and not under any form of duress. She was not abducted from Yvennes – she fled of her own accord." Alice is silent for a few moments, searching your eyes for any mistruths before she slowly speaks. "But she is safe?" You nod. [evelyn.dragon |"Yes, although... she has changed a lot. You would probably not immediately recognize her were you to see her now." |"Yes. She has been living unharmed in Hawkethorne for some time now." ] "I would like to see her, even so," Alice says. "If what you say is true, I must confirm it." "I understand," you say. "I can take you to see her. But let's talk, first. I don't believe that you're a threat, but I need to know the full details behind you coming here." You hold her gaze steady. "The royal family contacted your order for their aid." She nods, and you stay silent for a moment. "Do you think they knew she wasn't abducted?" you ask. Alice frowns, thinking. "I do not know." "Did they pick you specifically?" "No," she replies. "They beseeched the order for help, and I was the one sent." You lean back, thinking it over. It's possible, then, that the order could have sent someone else. Someone that might not have as many compunctions about dragging an itinerant princess back home, her own desires be damned. That they sent Alice was either good fortune or, perhaps a benefactor in the order... no, that would be too much of a coincidence. They couldn’t have known... unless the family told them. You frown. There are too many unknowns. "I believe it is impossible to say if the family knew or not," Alice says. "Perhaps there are clues... suspicions within the castle. But they will never be spoken, and the family will not be eager to say they were thwarted by a runaway princess." "So in the end it’s impossible to say whether you were lied to, or whether they made a misinformed assumption," you say. "Hmm." "Are you quite certain she wasn't abducted?" she asks. You nod. "I am. Do you want to rest, or would you prefer to meet her now?" "The sooner I can verify all of this, the better," Alice says. "We can depart immediately." [evelyn.dragon |"Very well," you say. You rise from your seat, and she joins you. You look at her, deciding whether or not to employ the Ways. A paladin of Tira can probably keep a secret. "We'll head to the town square first." Alice nods, and the two of you exit the inn together. |"Very well." You rise from your seat. "That won't be necessary," you say, nodding at her sword as she gets up. "Leave it with Garth." "You are asking a lot of me," she says, hand resting on its hilt. "We will be meeting in the town square. I promise no harm will come to anyone, least of all the princess," you say. "My entire party and I will be looking out." Her gaze roves over the crowd in the inn before she decides against protest, putting her sword behind the counter. rows.original:
You consider yourself a pretty solid judge of character. Alice doesn't seem to be anything other than what she presents herself to be, which is a noble paladin in pursuit of a woman she thinks has been kidnapped. Now that you've spoken to her, the odds of this becoming a fight seem pretty low.
    
    "Alright," you say. "You've convinced me of your goodwill. I'll take you to see Evelyn."
    
    Alice leans forward, her eyes going wide as she opens her mouth to ask her inevitable question, and you hold up a hand.
    
    "No questions," you say. "The next part won't be up to me. Let's go, if you're ready."
    
    Alice stops, then nods. "As you say, then."
    
    "Leave your sword with Garth," you say, 
    
    "You are asking a lot of me," she says, hand resting on its hilt.
    
    You shrug. "The princess wouldn't appreciate me escorting an armed paladin into her company."
    
    Alice's gaze roves over the crowd in the inn before she decides against protest, putting her sword behind the counter. Garth silently moves the mugs from around it, pushing it further forward to keep it hidden from sight.
    
    You take her upstairs, passing down the row of doors until you come to a particular room, and knock. You hear footsteps, then a sense of waiting.
    
    "It's me. And the paladin is with me," you say.
    
    There's a moment of silence before you hear Evelyn sigh. "I will trust you have this in hand, [pc.name]."
    
    The lock clicks, and you push the door open as Evelyn takes a few steps back. It's an uncomfortable meeting. Alice pauses when she sees Evelyn, but says nothing, looking to you. She doesn't know what the princess looks like, you realize.
    
    "Do you have anything that would prove the identity of the princess?" Evelyn says to her.
    
    Alice nods. "I have with me an enchanted script that will reveal her by way of blood."
    
    "May I see it?" Evelyn asks.
    
    While Alice is fishing the script out of her pack, you see Evelyn has hidden a dinner knife. She surreptitiously pricks her finger just in time to take the parchment from Alice's hand, and the entire thing immediately begins to turn scarlet.
    
    It takes a second before the enormity of what's just transpired dawns on Alice, and she hastily removes her mask to take a knee before Evelyn.
    
    "Princess," Alice says. "I cannot begin to express how happy I am that you are safe."
    
    "Thank you," Evelyn says with a note of amusement. "Your name, paladin?"
    
    "Alice Deschamps," she replies. "In the wake of your abduction, the royal family sought out my order to track you down."
    
    "My abduction," Evelyn muses. "I see."
    
    "If you do not mind my asking, how did you escape your captors?" Alice asks. She looks at you, and brightens as she seemingly puts two and two together. "Ah, of course...!"
    
    "Not quite," you admit.
    
    Evelyn chuckles. "There were no captors, I am afraid." She turns, seating herself on the bed. "I think, owing to your evident desire to see my safe, you've earned the right to know what actually happened."
    
    Evelyn begins to talk of her escape from Garonne, and subsequent misadventure into the Marches. It's a story you've heard before, but only in snippets. You tell the part of the alraune's presence, and Evelyn follows with her transformation upon being captured by its minions.
    
    Alice looks alarmed. "You were physically transformed, princess?"
    
    Evelyn smirks. "Yes, that is how I have come to wield the royal scepter between my thighs. Perhaps at a later point I can demonstrate for you – I'm sure the two of you would work wonderfully together." Alice blushes as Evelyn continues. "Hawkethorne has been my refuge since then."
    
    "I have found it to be quite similar to the village I grew up in," Alice offers, and there's a moment of silence.
    
    "Alice," Evelyn says. "What do you intend?"
    
    Alice lowers her gaze, lost in thought. "I do not know, my lady. I do not believe I can return without causing a bigger problem than needs exist." She looks up, eyes fixed on Evelyn. "What of you, my lady?"
    
    Evelyn looks at you and smiles. "I am not wholly sure myself. The one thing I am certain of is that freedom is a quality I have enjoyed thus far. To that end, I will not be returning to Yvennes."
    
    Alice nods, seemingly in thought. "Perhaps... perhaps I will stay in Hawkethorne myself. I believe I can do good here."
    
    "There's always something to be done for someone with a sword arm," you say. "The people would doubtless be happy with your presence. I could recommend you to Garth, if you want to stay."
    
    "Tis a start, then," Alice says.
    
    "Do you think Yvennes will send more people after you?" you ask.
    
    Alice sighs. "I would hope they quail at the thought of losing more soldiers to an uncertain foe. But it is possible."
    
    You nod. "As far as they know, you didn't even make it here."
    
    "T'would not be surprising were that the truth," she says. "I have not seen a land so untamed in my life. You cannot even leave the walls of Hawkethorne lest you be attacked. There is something perilously wrong with this place."
    
    "I'm working to make that less so," you say. "Hopefully you can help. For the sake of the people living here, if nothing else."
    
    Alice nods. "I will, at the least, walk patrols. Assuming I can find a place to stay."
    
    "Garth will be reasonable," you assure her. "You're much better fare than his usual, after all."
    
    "It seems as though you have a goal," Evelyn purrs, standing up from the bed. "I am glad. Your humility and reasonableness do you proud, Alice."
    
    Alice bows her head. "Thank you, my lady. I will withdraw for now – I must get my affairs in order."
    
    "Of course," Evelyn murmurs, and she calmly pulls you into a kiss while squeezing your ass. "Mmm. Come and see me soon, [pc.name]."
    
    Your cheeks redden slightly at the attention – Alice is blatantly staring, not quite open-mouthed but clearly surprised. "I will. Thank you, Evelyn."
    
    With a knowing wink, Evelyn slips away and you exit her room with Alice.
    
    "I had not known you and the princess were... intimately involved," Alice says carefully.
rows.translation:
你认为自己是个相当擅长判断人物性格的人。爱丽丝给人的印象就是她所表现出来的那样——一个为了寻找她认为被绑架的女性而不懈努力的高尚圣骑士。现在你已经和她谈过了，这场冲突发生的可能性似乎相当低。
    
    好吧，”你说，“你已经让我相信你是出于好意。我会带你去见伊芙琳。”

爱丽丝向前倾了倾身子，眼睛瞪得大大的，正准备提出那个不可避免的问题，而你则抬起了手。

“没有问题，”你说，“接下来的事情就由不得我了。如果你准备好了，我们就走吧。
    
    爱丽丝停下了脚步，然后点了点头。“正如你所说，那就这样吧。”

“把你的剑留给加思吧，”你说。

“你这对我的要求未免太大了，”她说，手放在剑柄上。

你耸了耸肩：“如果公主看到我带着一名全副武装的圣骑士出现在她面前，她肯定不会高兴的。
    
    爱丽丝的目光在酒馆里的人群中扫视了一圈，最终决定不再抗议，将剑放回了柜台后面。加思则悄悄地将周围的杯子移开，把柜台往前推了推，好让剑不再被人看到。

你带着她上楼，沿着一排排门走去，直到来到某个特定的房间，然后敲了敲门。你听到了脚步声，接着是一段等待的时间。
    
    是我。那位圣骑士也在我身边，”你说道。

一阵沉默之后，你听到伊芙琳叹了口气：“我相信你一定能处理好这件事。 [pc.name]锁“咔嗒”一声打开了，你推开门，这时伊芙琳已经后退了几步。这次会面显得有些尴尬。当艾丽丝看到伊芙琳时，她停住了脚步，但什么也没说，而是看着你。你突然意识到，她根本不知道这位公主长什么样子。

“你有什么可以证明这位公主身份的东西吗？”伊芙琳问道。
    
    爱丽丝点了点头：“我带有一份被施了魔法的卷轴，通过血液就能揭示她的真实身份。”

“我能看看吗？”伊芙琳问道。

当爱丽丝从背包里取出那份卷轴时，你注意到伊芙琳早已藏好了一把餐刀。她趁机悄悄刺破了手指，然后迅速从爱丽丝手中接过了那份卷轴。刹那间，整份卷轴的颜色竟然变成了猩红色。
    
    过了片刻，爱丽丝才意识到刚刚发生的事情的严重性，她急忙摘下面具，跪在伊芙琳面前。

“公主，”爱丽丝说道，“我实在无法用言语来表达看到您平安无事我有多高兴。”

“谢谢你，”伊芙琳带着一丝笑意说道，“你的名字是……勇士吗？
    
    爱丽丝·德尚，”她回答道，“在你被绑架之后，王室找到了我的组织，请求我们帮你找到你。”

“我的被绑架……”伊芙琳若有所思地说道，“原来如此。”

“如果我不冒昧的话，你是怎么从绑匪手中逃脱的？”爱丽丝问道。她看着你，似乎突然想明白了什么，脸上露出了笑容：“啊，原来如此……！
    
    不完全是，”你承认道。

伊芙琳轻笑了一声：“恐怕根本没有什么抓捕者。”她转过身，坐在床上：“我想，既然你如此迫切地想知道我是否安全，那么你就有权知道到底发生了什么。伊芙琳开始讲述她是如何从加龙河逃脱的，以及之后在边境地区遭遇的种种不幸。这个故事你以前也听过，只不过只是零零碎碎的一些片段而已。你讲到了阿尔劳恩魔花的作用，而伊芙琳则接着讲述了自己被它的爪牙抓住后所发生的变化。
    
    爱丽丝显得十分惊讶：“你的身体竟然发生了变化，公主？”

伊芙琳微微一笑：“没错，正是因为这样，我才能将王权象征握在手中。或许以后有机会，我可以给你们演示一下——我相信你们俩一定会配合得非常默契的。”听到这里，爱丽丝的脸颊顿时红了。伊芙琳继续说道：“从那以后，鹰棘镇就成了我的避风港。
    
    我觉得它和我成长的那个村庄非常相似，”爱丽丝说道，随后是一阵沉默。

“爱丽丝，”伊芙琳问道，“你究竟有什么打算？”

爱丽丝低下头，陷入沉思。“我不知道，夫人。我认为，如果我回去，只会引发比现在更严重的麻烦。”她抬起头，目光紧紧地盯着伊芙琳，“那您呢，夫人？
    
    伊芙琳看着你，微笑着说道：“我自己也不太确定。但有一件事是肯定的：自由是我迄今为止一直珍视的品质。因此，我不会再回到伊文尼斯去了。”

爱丽丝若有所思地点了点头：“也许……也许我会留在鹰棘镇。我相信我在这里能够发挥自己的作用，做一些有益的事情。
    
    对于一个擅长使用剑的人来说，总是有事情可做的，”你说，“人们肯定会欢迎你的加入。如果你想留下的话，我可以向加斯推荐你。”

“那也算是个好的开始吧，”爱丽丝说道。

“你认为伊文尼斯还会派人追杀你吗？”你问道。
    
    爱丽丝叹了口气：“我真希望他们一想到会因为一个不可预知的敌人而失去更多的士兵，就会胆怯起来。但这也是有可能的。”

你点了点头：“在他们看来，你甚至根本就没有来到这里。”

“如果事实真是这样，我也不会感到惊讶，”她说，“我这辈子还没见过如此荒芜、未开化的地方。你甚至无法离开鹰棘镇的城墙，否则就会遭到攻击。这个地方肯定存在着某种极其危险的问题。
    
    我正在努力让这种情况变得不那么严重，”你说，“希望你能帮忙。至少也是为了这里的人们着想。”

爱丽丝点了点头：“至少我会去巡逻。前提是我能找到一个住处。”

“加思会通情达理的，”你安慰她，“毕竟，你比他平时遇到的那些人要好多了。
    
    看来你是有目标的，”伊芙琳轻声说道，一边从床上站起来。“我很高兴。你的谦逊与理智确实为你赢得了荣誉，爱丽丝。”

爱丽丝低下了头：“谢谢您，夫人。我现在就告退了——我还有些事情需要处理。
    
    当然，”伊芙琳轻声说道，一边平静地吻了你一下，一边捏了捏你的屁股。“嗯，尽快来看我吧。 [pc.name]听到这个称呼，你的脸颊微微泛红——爱丽丝正直直地盯着你看，虽然没有张大嘴巴，但显然很惊讶。“好的，谢谢你，伊芙琳。”

伊芙琳会意地眨了眨眼，然后悄悄离开了，你便和爱丽丝一起走出了她的房间。

“我之前并不知道你和公主之间的关系……这么亲密。”爱丽丝小心翼翼地说道。

    "Alice Deschamps," she replies. "In the wake of your abduction, the royal family sought out my order to track you down."
    
    "My abduction," Evelyn muses. "I see."
    
    "If you do not mind my asking, how did you escape your captors?" Alice asks. She looks at you, and brightens as she seemingly puts two and two together. "Ah, of course...!"
    
    "Not quite," you admit.
    
    Evelyn chuckles. "There were no captors, I am afraid." She turns, seating herself on the bed. "I think, owing to your evident desire to see my safe, you've earned the right to know what actually happened."
    
    Evelyn begins to talk of her escape from Garonne, and subsequent misadventure into the Marches. It's a story you've heard before, but only in snippets. You tell the part of the alraune's presence, and Evelyn follows with her transformation upon being captured by its minions.
    
    Alice looks alarmed. "You were physically transformed, princess?"
    
    Evelyn smirks. "Yes, that is how I have come to wield the royal scepter between my thighs. Perhaps at a later point I can demonstrate for you – I'm sure the two of you would work wonderfully together." Alice blushes as Evelyn continues. "Hawkethorne has been my refuge since then."
    
    "I have found it to be quite similar to the village I grew up in," Alice offers, and there's a moment of silence.
    
    "Alice," Evelyn says. "What do you intend?"
    
    Alice lowers her gaze, lost in thought. "I do not know, my lady. I do not believe I can return without causing a bigger problem than needs exist." She looks up, eyes fixed on Evelyn. "What of you, my lady?"
    
    Evelyn looks at you and smiles. "I am not wholly sure myself. The one thing I am certain of is that freedom is a quality I have enjoyed thus far. To that end, I will not be returning to Yvennes."
    
    Alice nods, seemingly in thought. "Perhaps... perhaps I will stay in Hawkethorne myself. I believe I can do good here."
    
    "There's always something to be done for someone with a sword arm," you say. "The people would doubtless be happy with your presence. I could recommend you to Garth, if you want to stay."
    
    "Tis a start, then," Alice says.
    
    "Do you think Yvennes will send more people after you?" you ask.
    
    Alice sighs. "I would hope they quail at the thought of losing more soldiers to an uncertain foe. But it is possible."
    
    You nod. "As far as they know, you didn't even make it here."
    
    "T'would not be surprising were that the truth," she says. "I have not seen a land so untamed in my life. You cannot even leave the walls of Hawkethorne lest you be attacked. There is something perilously wrong with this place."
    
    "I'm working to make that less so," you say. "Hopefully you can help. For the sake of the people living here, if nothing else."
    
    Alice nods. "I will, at the least, walk patrols. Assuming I can find a place to stay."
    
    "Garth will be reasonable," you assure her. "You're much better fare than his usual, after all."
    
    "It seems as though you have a goal," Evelyn purrs, standing up from the bed. "I am glad. Your humility and reasonableness do you proud, Alice."
    
    Alice bows her head. "Thank you, my lady. I will withdraw for now – I must get my affairs in order."
    
    "Of course," Evelyn murmurs, and she calmly pulls you into a kiss while squeezing your ass. "Mmm. Come and see me soon, [pc.name]."
    
    Your cheeks redden slightly at the attention – Alice is blatantly staring, not quite open-mouthed but clearly surprised. "I will. Thank you, Evelyn."
    
    With a knowing wink, Evelyn slips away and you exit her room with Alice.
    
    "I had not known you and the princess were... intimately involved," Alice says carefully.
    '

rows.translation: 你对伊芙琳的爱与执着，让你一次又一次地回到她身边。
rows.raw: "Your love for and devotion to Evelyn keeps you coming back to her."

rows.original: The two of you share a... special relationship.
rows.translation: 你们两个人之间存在着一种……特殊的关系。
rows.raw: "The two of you share a... special relationship."

rows.original: "She has me completely wrapped around her finger," you admit, a little sheepish. "I've never been... conquered in such a manner before. I would do anything for her if she asked." Alice seems more surprised than anything. "By the princess? I... she did seem to have quite a presence..." "More than that, truly," you say. "Whenever she has me in hand, I feel like I belong there. She's a born ruler. You can tell she's a princess when she's on top of you, that's for sure."

rows.original:
"I love her," you confess. "She's everything to me. I'm really not sure what I'd do without her. I want to help her with anything I can."
    
    "Which is why you were investigating me?" Alice guesses.
    
    You nod. "When she told me a paladin from Yvennes was here, my first thought was that I might need to fight. I'm glad you turned out to be reasonable."
    
    Alice smiles. "Indeed. It was quite a surprise to learn about the princess."
rows.translation:
“我爱她，”你坦白道。“她对我来说意味着一切。我真的不知道没有她该怎么办。我想尽我所能帮助她。”
    
    “所以你才会调查我？”爱丽丝猜测道。
    
    你点了点头。“当她告诉我一位来自伊薇恩的圣骑士在这里时，我第一个念头就是可能得动手打一场。很高兴你最后这么通情达理。”
    
    爱丽丝笑了。“确实如此。得知那位公主的事，真是让我吃了一惊。”

"We have a... special relationship," you say, smiling despite yourself. "I'm not sure I know anyone else quite like Evelyn."
    
    "That is hard to imagine," Alice agrees.
    
    "Isn't it?" you say. "She's seemingly one-of-a-kind."
    
    "There is a conceivable future where she rules over Yvennes," Alice muses.

rows.original: You walk downstairs with Alice to talk to Garth. The old wolf is more than happy to put a person that will actually pay him up in a room, and the situation is all but resolved. "What will you do now?" you ask. "I suppose I shall patrol the roads," Alice says. "The village is already guarded, but merchants are afraid to tread here. Some protection would go a long way towards quelling their rightful fears." You nod. A Tiran paladin can probably handle most things encountered on the roads... except Kasyrra herself, but she's quite busy elsewhere. Having her around will be a blessing for the people out here on the frontier. "You're sure the paladin of Yvennes can handle the life of Hawkethorne?" you say, smiling. Alice chuckles. "I was born to a baker and a blacksmith, after all. It is not so different." After a brief talk Alice excuses herself to her room, promising to see you later. Once she's settled in, she'll be back in the inn – 24 hours from now.
rows.translation: 你和爱丽丝一起下楼去和加斯谈话。这只老狼非常乐意把一个真正会付钱给他的人请到房间里来，这样一来，问题几乎就解决了。 “你现在打算怎么做？”你问道。 我想我应该去路上巡逻吧，”爱丽丝说道。“村子已经有守卫了，但商人们还是不敢来这里。如果能提供一些保护，的话，肯定能让他们消除这些合理的恐惧。” 你点了点头。一个蒂拉教会的圣骑士应该能够应对路上遇到的大多数情况吧…… 除了卡希拉本人，不过她现在忙得不可开交。如果她能在这里帮忙，对边境的民众来说无疑是一大福音。 “你确定伊文尼斯的圣骑士能够胜任鹰棘镇的工作吗？”你微笑着问道。 爱丽丝轻笑道：“毕竟，我出生在一个面包师和铁匠的家庭里，这两份工作其实也没什么太大区别。” 简短交谈过后，爱丽丝便告辞回了自己的房间，承诺稍后会再来见你。等她安顿妥当，24小时后就能在客栈再次见到她。

rows.original: Your queen was very specific in her instructions. She specifically said to tell the paladin that Evelyn has been stolen away by a dragon – which, in a sense, she has. Your own interpretation of Alice's character aside, you're happy to give Evelyn what she wants. "Alright," you say. "I had to be sure of your genuine intentions before I told you this... Evelyn is here, though not in Hawkethorne. She's being held in a dragon's lair." Alice looks puzzled, then seemingly understands. "A metaphor." "Quite literal," you say. "Let's go, and bring your sword." She'll see for herself. All you have to do is get her there. You escort the armored paladin out into the wilderness, away from civilization and towards the lair of the dragon. With a silent nod, you indicate the entrance and draw your weapon. Alice follows suit, stepping in front of you. You proceed inside, and what awaits you doesn't disappoint. An imperious dragoness stands in front of her golden treasure hoard, eyeing the two of you with a tyrannical smirk. She wears ornate armor, hugging her curves and accentuating her incredible body – the need of protection is for mortals, it seems to say. A dragon pays no heed. She is your queen, and your lover. "By the gods," Alice breathes. "T'is truly a- stay back, [pc.name]!" She does cut quite the gallant figure brandishing her sword and facing down a monster of legend like that. You take a few steps back, not wanting to interfere with your queen's fun. "Where have you taken the princess, fiend?" Alice demands of the dragon. "I swear if you have harmed her, I will not hesitate to end you." "The princess?" Evelyn says, her green eyes dazzling in their intensity as she gazes at the paladin. A razor-thin smile spreads across her lips. "She's still here." The tiniest bit of tension disappears from Alice's stance, but she maintains her guard. "What have you done to her?" Evelyn laughs. "You think I'm going to tell you anything, trespasser? Come." She spreads her wings, beating the air. She's enjoying this, you can tell. "Defeat me and I will show you what you seek." Far be it from you to get in the way of your beloved queen.
rows.translation: 你的女王把指示说得非常明确。她特意要求你告诉圣骑士，伊芙琳被一头巨龙掳走了——某种意义上，事实也确实如此。不论你自己如何解读爱丽丝的性格，你都乐意给伊芙琳想要的东西。 “好吧。”你说道，“我得先确定你是真心诚意，才能告诉你这件事……伊芙琳就在这里，但不在鹰棘镇。她被囚禁在巨龙的巢穴里。” 爱丽丝一脸困惑，随后似乎明白过来。“这是个比喻。” “完全是字面意思。”你说道，“我们走吧，带上你的剑。” 她很快就会亲眼看见。你只需要带她到那里。 你护送身披铠甲的圣骑士进入荒野，远离文明，前往巨龙巢穴。你默默朝入口点点头，拔出武器。爱丽丝也随即拔剑，走到你前面。你们进入巢穴，里面等待着的景象果然没有令人失望。 一位威严的龙女站在金光闪闪的宝藏堆前，以暴君般的得意笑容打量你们。她身穿华美铠甲，紧贴曲线，衬托出令人惊叹的身体——仿佛在说，只有凡人才需要铠甲保护，巨龙根本不屑一顾。 她是你的女王，也是你的爱人。 “诸神在上。”爱丽丝轻声说道，“这真是头——退后，[pc.name]！” 她挥舞长剑，直面传说中的怪物，姿态确实英勇非凡。你后退几步，不愿妨碍女王享受乐趣。 “恶徒，你把公主带到哪里去了？”爱丽丝质问巨龙，“如果你伤害了她，我发誓自己会毫不犹豫地杀死你。” “公主？”伊芙琳说道。她凝视着圣骑士，绿色双眸迸发出夺目的强光；嘴角随即扬起如刀锋般纤细的微笑。“她仍然在这里。” 爱丽丝的姿态稍稍放松，幅度小得几乎无法察觉，但她仍保持警戒。“你对她做了什么？” 伊芙琳笑了起来。“你以为我会告诉一个擅闯此地的人任何事情吗？来吧。”她展开双翼，拍击空气。你看得出来，她很享受这一切。“打败我，我就让你看见自己寻找的东西。” 你可不会妨碍心爱女王的乐趣。

rows.original: Alice's sword blazes to life, an eerie purple flame emanating from its blade as she swings it in a ferocious downward arc. It's a strong, confident blow, and[var0 | Evelyn has to leap aside to avoid it. The paladin keeps coming, her longsword seeming to stretch an extra inch or two at the apex of every swing, an illusion created by her masterful footwork. Scratches begin to appear along Evelyn's forearms as she fights. She fights like an animal, swaying low to the ground before swinging upwards with such force that Alice is forced to jump back. But it's only a temporary retreat, and she's back upon Evelyn before you can blink. The battle rages on, and with your trained eye you can tell: Evelyn is going to lose. It's not going to be by much, but it is going to happen, and it's going to be in less than twenty seconds. She's not fighting as brutally as she could be – she doesn't want to take this woman's life. Alice, on the other hand, has no such compunctions. She swings her sword with her full might and fury against the supposed tormentor of her princess, each blow fully intended to kill or maim. She fights for her kingdom. The situation requires action from the dragon queen's faithful right hand. You calmly position yourself behind the paladin, who's far too focused on fighting the angry dragon in her face to notice. It doesn't take much. One swift kick to her calf, and she buckles with a gasp of surprise. Evelyn capitalizes at once, leaping upon the paladin and disarming her with a violent movement that sends her sword spiralling through the air, tumbling end over end. You glance over at the dragoness. "We should train more often." Evelyn huffs in dismay. "Brute strength is a match for technique, but not for both technique and strength." "Damn... you," the paladin manages, sucking wind. "You... were in league with... her?" "[pc.name] has been in my service for quite some time now," Evelyn purrs. "It was perhaps a touch silly to come to a dragon's lair alone, paladin." Alice coughs, shuddering. "At- at least show me the princess. I have to know she is safe." "Tell me," Evelyn says. "Do you even know what your precious princess looks like, paladin? Or how you intend to identify her?" "I have... a script," Alice says. "It is magically enchanted to change color upon receipt of Trusant blood." "Hm," Evelyn muses for a moment. Then she rips Alice's pack from her side, rooting through it with one hand and holding the paladin down with the other. "This?" Alice says nothing, looking on in slight confusion as Evelyn moves to prick her hand on the point of her horn. Her puzzlement deepens while the dragoness grasps the parchment, scarlet blooming outwards from where her fingertip presses against it. The entire parchment is red in seconds, curling up at the edges as though it had sucked her blood. Alice's expression changes several times in an instant, her confusion only growing worse and worse until she arrives at the inevitable conclusion. "You- you are... the princess? rows.translation: 爱丽丝的剑猛然燃烧起来，剑刃上散发着诡异的紫色火焰，她用力将剑向下挥舞。这一击充满力量与自信[var0 | 伊芙琳不得不迅速闪开才能避开它。 那位圣骑士依然不断进攻，他的长剑在每次挥舞的瞬间似乎都会延长一两英寸，这种错觉其实是她娴熟的步法所营造出来的。在战斗中，伊芙琳的前臂开始出现擦伤。她像一只野兽一样战斗，先低身贴近地面，然后以巨大的力量向上挥击，迫使爱丽丝不得不向后跳开。 但这只是一种暂时的退避，转眼间她又重新与伊芙琳展开了战斗。战斗仍在激烈进行，以你训练有素的眼光来看，伊芙琳注定会失败。虽然差距不会太大，但失败的事实不可避免，而且这一切将在不到二十秒的时间内发生。她并没有使出全力进行攻击——她并不想夺走这个女人的生命。 而爱丽丝却没有这样的顾虑。她用尽全力、满怀怒火地挥舞着剑，攻击那个被她认为是她公主的迫害者，每一击都旨在杀死或致残对方。她是在为她的王国而战。 在这种情况下，龙后忠诚的得力助手必须采取行动了。 你冷静地站在那位圣骑士身后，而她完全专注于与眼前那条愤怒的巨龙战斗，根本没有注意到你的存在。你并没有用太多力气——只是一脚踢在她的腿上，她就惊讶地踉跄了一下。 埃弗琳立刻抓住了这个机会，跳上圣骑士的身体，用一记猛烈的动作夺走了她的武器，使得她的剑在空中旋转着飞了出去，她自己也重重地摔在了地上。你瞥了一眼那条雌性巨龙，心想：“我们真的应该多训练一些才行。 伊芙琳沮丧地哼了一声：“单纯的蛮力虽然可以对抗技巧，但同时兼具技巧与力量的话，就无能为力了。” “该死……你……”圣骑士喘着粗气说道，“你……竟然和她合谋了？[pc.name]已经为我效力好一段时间了，”伊芙琳轻声说道，“不过，独自来到龙的巢穴，或许有点太愚蠢了，圣骑士。” 爱丽丝轻咳了一声，浑身发抖：“至少让我见见公主吧。我必须确认她安全无恙。告诉我，”伊芙琳说道，“你到底知不知道你那位珍贵的公主长什么样子，圣骑士？又或者你打算怎么认出她来？” “我有一个……咒语，”爱丽丝回答，“这个咒语被施了魔法，一旦接触到特鲁桑特的血液，它的颜色就会发生变化。嗯，”伊芙琳沉思了一会儿。然后她一把夺过爱丽丝的背包，一只手在里面翻找，另一只手则按住那位圣骑士。“就是这个吗？” 爱丽丝什么也没说，只是困惑地看着伊芙琳用角尖刺自己的手。当那位女龙握住那张羊皮纸时，她的困惑愈发加深了——她的指尖触碰纸面的瞬间，猩红色的颜色便从那里开始蔓延开来。短短几秒钟内，整张羊皮纸都被染成了红色，边缘还开始卷曲起来，仿佛被她的血液侵蚀了一般。 爱丽丝的表情在瞬间发生了几次变化，她的困惑之情愈发加深，最终得出了一个不可避免的结论。 “你、你是……公主？但是、可是这怎么可能为什么为了查明你的真实意图，”伊芙琳说道，“为了证明你并非我父亲派来的野蛮人，也是为了传递某种信息。” “嗯，”爱丽丝缓缓说道，“我想这确实有点道理。你根本无法确定我不是个强盗……或者是一个行事更为暴力的圣骑士。即便如此，我们总可以坐下来好好谈谈的吧……” “嗯，”伊芙琳低声说道，从她低头注视艾丽丝的神情来看，显然她根本就没有在听。还有另一个原因。” rows.raw: ' Alice's sword blazes to life, an eerie purple flame emanating from its blade as she swings it in a ferocious downward arc. It's a strong, confident blow, and[var0 | Evelyn has to leap aside to avoid it. The paladin keeps coming, her longsword seeming to stretch an extra inch or two at the apex of every swing, an illusion created by her masterful footwork. Scratches begin to appear along Evelyn's forearms as she fights. She fights like an animal, swaying low to the ground before swinging upwards with such force that Alice is forced to jump back. But it's only a temporary retreat, and she's back upon Evelyn before you can blink. The battle rages on, and with your trained eye you can tell: Evelyn is going to lose. It's not going to be by much, but it is going to happen, and it's going to be in less than twenty seconds. She's not fighting as brutally as she could be – she doesn't want to take this woman's life. Alice, on the other hand, has no such compunctions. She swings her sword with her full might and fury against the supposed tormentor of her princess, each blow fully intended to kill or maim. She fights for her kingdom. The situation requires action from the dragon queen's faithful right hand. You calmly position yourself behind the paladin, who's far too focused on fighting the angry dragon in her face to notice. It doesn't take much. One swift kick to her calf, and she buckles with a gasp of surprise. "Ah," Alice says, blushing. "That... that does ring true." You smile. "If it's any consolation, she wasn't that dissimilar before she changed... it was just a different type of power she held." Alice says. You nod.[pc.bg scholar | As a scholar yourself, it's always been easy enough to detect a kindred spirit. rows.translation: 伊芙琳叹了口气，然后走进了温水里，你和爱丽丝也跟着走了进去。确实在为女王付出如此多的努力之后，能够放松下来，确实让人感觉很好…… “你们两个组合起来，一定会是一支非常出色的团队，”伊芙琳闭上眼睛，向后靠在椅背上说道，“我能够想象到那幅画面。” 你很清楚她所说的这种合作方式是什么意思——如果她的言外之意还不够明显的话，那么她那随时准备挺立起来的阴茎微微颤动、变得坚硬的样子，无疑已经说明了一切。 爱丽丝，”在一段宁静的沉默之后，伊芙琳开口说道，“你究竟有什么打算？” 爱丽丝低头望着水面，双手交叠放在膝上。“我不知道，夫人。我认为，如果我回去，只会引发比现在更严重的麻烦。”她抬起头，目光紧紧地盯着伊芙琳，“那您呢，夫人？ 我短期的计划与这片土地有关。至于未来，我的血脉中既流淌着特鲁桑家族的传承，也蕴含着传说中的力量，”伊芙琳说道，“这种组合确实非常强大。” 片刻的沉默。 “那么，你打算争夺王位吗？”爱丽丝问道。 你有什么异议吗？”伊芙琳问道。 爱丽丝闭上了眼睛：“这不是我该插手的事情。” “嗯，看来你还是有点理智的，”伊芙琳低声说道，“而且你也有先见之明，知道不应该回来。我挺喜欢你的，爱丽丝。但现在你打算怎么办呢？”她狡黠地笑了笑，“留在我身边吗？我向你保证，我的床非常宽敞。 爱丽丝犹豫了一下，显然在思考该如何才能最好地安抚这位龙女。“啊，不，我的女士……我不会再给您带来太多麻烦了。我想我会回到鹰棘镇，看看在那里能否为人们做一些有益的事情。” 你点了点头。“对于一个拥有武艺的人来说，总会有事情可以做的。人们肯定会欢迎你的到来的。如果你愿意留下来的话，我可以向加斯推荐你。 那也算是个开始吧，”爱丽丝说道。 “你觉得伊薇恩会再派人来追你吗？”你问道。 爱丽丝叹了口气：“我希望他们一想到会再失去士兵去对付一个不确定的敌人，就会退缩。但也是有可能的。” 你点了点头：“在他们看来，你根本就没有来到这里。 如果那是真相的话，我也不会感到惊讶，”她说，“我这辈子从未见过如此原始、未受人类影响的地方。你甚至无法离开鹰棘镇的城墙，否则就会遭到攻击。这个地方肯定存在着某种危险的问题。” “埃弗琳和我正在努力改变这种状况，”你说道，同时瞥了瞥那条懒洋洋地躺着的龙女。她懒洋洋地睁开一只眼睛，对你笑了笑。“希望你能帮助我们。至少也是为了这里居住的人民着想。 爱丽丝点了点头：“至少，我会去巡逻吧。前提是我能找到一个住的地方。” “加斯会通情达理的，”你安慰她，“毕竟，你比他平时遇到的那些人要好多了。” “你们的到访确实让这里变得很有趣，我真舍不得让你们离开，但你们已经在这里待了段时间了……”伊芙琳轻声说道，同时将头倾向爱丽丝的方向。等我们在这里的事情忙完了，你就应该回到鹰棘镇，开始建立各种人脉关系。”她微笑着说，“当然也要来看看我们。也许在我们在各自的领地巡逻时，我们的路会再次交汇。 当你整理好自己准备离开时，伊芙琳突然拉住你，给了你一个漫长而热烈的吻，同时她的手也在你的身上游走。当爱丽丝在外面等着你时，她还捏了捏你的屁股，然后在你耳边低语道：“干得不错。 [pc.name]她意味深长地眨了眨眼，最后还轻轻抚了抚你的屁股，然后便悄悄离开了，而你则走出了洞穴。 “我会送你回鹰棘镇，”你对爱丽丝说，“之后我们可以再考虑让你在寒霜猎犬旅馆多住一段时间。她点了点头，然后瞥了你一眼：“你为什么没有告诉我这件事？” “伊芙琳非常高兴能见到你，”你说道，“她让我告诉你，公主被一条龙带走了，让我带你去找她。你应该明白，她依然是伊文尼斯的公主，但她同时也是一条龙。而且她还想战斗。” “那你相信她不会做得太过火吗？”她问道。 你点了点头。“我认为我的女王绝不是那种会为了取乐而杀害无辜之人的人。” “但如果她那……‘严厉的性格’占了上风呢？爱丽丝按下了按钮。 你看了她一眼，说道：“当她把你吸引到她的床边时，你难道没有感觉到她是如何将那种‘强势的性格’发挥出来的吗？” “啊，”爱丽丝红着脸说道，“那……确实是真的。 爱丽丝笑了起来，你突然想起了一个细节：“啊，对，书。她非常喜欢书。实际上，她逃跑的时候把那些书也从加龙河畔带走了。那些是她踏上这段旅程时唯一带上的东西。”你低头望着前方的道路，“我觉得，那些是她能带走的、属于她故乡的唯一纪念。” “她喜欢书吗？”爱丽丝问道。 你点了点头。[pc.bg scholar | rows.original: Alice accompanies you to the statue in the center of Hawkethorne, and casts a glance in your direction as you're walking. "Who are you here, really?" she says. "The people we are passing... they are not looking at me. They are looking at you." You glance over the foot traffic passing through the square. [dayNight | |There isn't much at this hour, but stumbling drunks and their friends are still passing by. ]There is some truth to it – there isn't a person in Hawkethorne that hasn't heard of you at this point, and in such a village laying your eyes on a person of significance is an event. Though the paladin of Tira is an eyecatcher, a lot of people are probably curious what she's doing in proximity to you, not the inverse.

I will take my time educating her before I return her to civilization, I believe." She pulls you in for a long kiss, rolling on top of the paladin as you leave the room. If you know Evelyn's libido, no doubt the two of them are going to be getting very familiar with each other for the next several hours... You make your return to Hawkethorne, settling in at the Frost Hound. No doubt Alice will be along some time later. Probably a day from now. '

rows.original: You immediately head up to Evelyn's room, and knock on her door. "It's me," you say. The door opens, and you step inside with Evelyn. "The paladin is here," you say. "I think we might have gotten lucky. She wasn't sent by the royal family, she was sent by her Order. As far as she knows, she's here to rescue an abducted princess." Evelyn tuts. "How simple that would be." You nod. "I think we can resolve this with a meeting. In the town square, for safety – I'll have all of my companions watching out, and I'll be with you myself." You watch her consider it, turning the matter over in her mind, before she finally nods. "Very well. I will place my hopes in you and meet this paladin on neutral ground." You smile. "Thanks. Don't worry – she'd never make it past me if she tried it. I'll go first. You come and meet us in a few minutes – no need to let her know you're staying here right now. I'll see you soon." You turn and leave, walking down to Alice and giving her a curt nod. "Everything's in place." "The princess will meet us?" she asks, rising from her chair. "In the town square," you reaffirm. "Let's go." You make an interesting sight, the two of you. The adventurer and the paladin standing together in Hawkethorne's town square, waiting for someone. The winds of ice caress you, though Alice seems unconcerned. "Will she come?" Alice asks. "She will," you reply. She looks around [dayNight |at the crowds of people passing through the village |at the people passing by ]. After several moments of observation, she seems to notice something. Alice peers at you. "Who are you here, really? These people... they are not looking at me. They are looking at you." You glance over the crowd. There is some truth to that – there isn't a person in Hawkethorne that hasn't heard of you at this point, and in such a village laying your eyes on a person of significance is an event. Though the paladin of Tira is an eyecatcher, most people are probably curious what she's doing in proximity to you, not the inverse.
