While you don't think you've made any noise, the warg must have nevertheless sensed you; the moment you get within reach of the druidess' things, it turns its head straight at your skulking form and barrels into action. Yapping and snarling like a rabid creature, it lunges for your throat; you have barely enough time to draw your [pc.weapon] to defend yourself even as the druidess emerges from the water. It's a fight!]]"

rows.original: Perhaps not, then. Even though poor Garret would like to be able to stretch his limbs and wrestle some hairy, hulking wild animals for fun, he'll just have to remain in his cage a little longer until you decide on a course of action.
rows.translation: 也许吧。虽然可怜的加雷特很想伸伸四肢，和那些毛茸茸的巨型野生动物搏斗一番来解解闷，但他还是得再待在笼子里一段时间，直到你决定该采取什么行动为止。
rows.raw: "\n        Perhaps not, then. Even though poor Garret would like to be able to stretch his limbs and wrestle some hairy, hulking wild animals for fun, he'll just have to remain in his cage a little longer until you decide on a course of action."

rows.original: Not that you're afraid or anything, but you don't feel confident in facing down the druidess and her pet right now. Best to prepare carefully succeed at first, rather than rush in ahead unprepared. Is there something else you can do to help your chances here? Maybe, maybe not. But you know where to find the druidess when you are ready to resolve this situation.
rows.translation: 倒也不是说你害怕或者别的什么，但你现在并没有信心去正面应对那位女德鲁伊和她的宠物。最好先仔细准备、确保一次成功，而不是毫无准备就贸然冲上去。 还有其他办法能帮你提高胜算吗？也许有，也许没有。但等你真的准备好解决这一局面时，你知道该去哪里找那位女德鲁伊。
rows.raw: " Not that you're afraid or anything, but you don't feel confident in facing down the druidess and her pet right now. Best to prepare carefully succeed at first, rather than rush in ahead unprepared. Is there something else you can do to help your chances here? Maybe, maybe not. But you know where to find the druidess when you are ready to resolve this situation."

rows.original: It's but a short distance to the hall, and Garret looks up in his cage as you burst through the door, key in hand. "Are you holding what I think you're holding?" Oh yes. Now, if he doesn't mind standing back... you don't know how long you have until either druidess or warg realizes the key is missing. Who knows, they might already be on their way. "C'mon, then." Levering himself to his feet, Garret smashes a fist against a palm and cracks his knuckles. "I've been waiting for a little payback." Grimacing, you fit the key into the cage's lock. Both are old and speckled with rust, but the tumblers click and the bolts move; you step back as Garret sends the cage door crashing open with a powerful kick. "All right," he growls. "Let's go." You look Garret up and down. He's completely naked — unless one counts fur as clothing — does he want a weapon or something? "Haven't got the time to go searching for my kit," comes the reply as he breaks out into a quick jog. "And as for weapons... like I told you, my entire body's a bloody masterwork weapon. Let's go!" Seeing Garret lope through the trees and over muddy paths, it's easy to see how he managed to make his way to Westbank with little trouble. With how much alacrity he moves, the numerous protruding roots and thick undergrowth might as well not be there; it takes quite a bit of effort to just keep up with him, and he only slows as you approach the riverbank once more. "All right, [pc.name]. You see that?" Yes, you do. The druidess has just emerged from the river and is bending over her things, looking distinctly puzzled as she slips into her robes, but not alarmed — yet. Seems like she's noticed the key is missing, but hasn't come to the conclusion that it's been stolen. Well, that's about to change very soon. "Here," Garret growls. "I'll draw the witch's attention by going straight for the beast. When she's got her eyes on me, you take her from behind and spoil any spell she might cast." Sounds like a plan. You give Garret a thumbs-up, and without further ago he bursts out of the treeline, a blur of gray and white as he catches the warg in a flying tackle. It's quite the sight to see — two canine forms tumbling on the rocky riverbank in a large furry ball of fury and bloodlust. The warg claws at Garret's chest and arm, leaving deep red gashes through his fur, but he ignores the pain, pins the beast to the ground and smashes his fist into its muzzle with a very loud and satisfying crunch. Whining, the warg recoils from the sheer brutality of Garret's blow, leaving an opening for him to press the attack over and over again, knuckles pounding away like pistons. Gods above, he's punching out all its blood. Time for you to move, then. As expected, the druidess has her attention focused on Garret, presumably preparing to cast some sort of spell; you're easily able to close the distance and bring down your [pc.weapon] on her. Unfortunately, she whirls and dances away at the last moment, pirouetting around to face you, shreds of silver and green fabric from her armored robes floating to the ground in the wake of your attack. Faced with imminent danger, she abandons all possibility of coming to her pet's aid, and rounds upon this new threat. She looks at you. You look at her. And then without hesitation, the druidess draws back the string of her bow, a silvery arrow of icy frost materializing at her fingers, nocked and ready to loose. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 大厅就在不远处，当你手持钥匙冲进门来时，加雷特在笼子里抬头看着你。 你手里拿的，真的是我想象中的那个东西吗？ 哦，对了。现在，如果他不介意稍微退后一点的话……你根本不知道还有多久，那位德鲁伊女巫或那些战争生物才会发现钥匙不见了。谁知道呢，他们可能已经在路上了。 那好吧，我们走吧。加雷特站起身来，用拳头敲打自己的手掌，使指关节发出咔嚓声。我一直在等待机会来报复一下。 你面带苦色，将钥匙插入笼子的锁孔中。锁和钥匙都十分老旧，上面布满了锈迹，但钥匙还是顺利地转动了，螺栓也跟着移动了。就在这时，加雷特用一脚猛力踢开了笼门，你赶紧后退了几步。 好吧，他低吼着。我们走吧。 你上下打量着加雷特。他全身赤裸——除非把毛皮也算作衣服的话——他是不是需要一件武器之类的东西呢？ 没时间去寻找我的装备了。他开始小跑起来，同时得到了回复。至于武器……就像我之前说的，我的整个身体本身就是一件绝妙的武器。我们走吧！ 看到加雷特在树林中穿梭、在泥泞的小路上快速移动，就不难理解他为何能如此顺利地到达西岸。他行动起来如此敏捷，那些突出的树根和茂密的灌木丛对他来说似乎根本不存在；要想跟上他的步伐，确实需要花费不少力气。而只有当他们再次接近河岸时，他的速度才会有所减缓。 好吧， [pc.name]你看到了吗？ 是的，你没看错。那位女德鲁伊刚刚从河里出来，正在整理她的物品，她穿上一件件长袍时，脸上明显带着困惑，但还没有感到惊慌——至少现在还没有。看起来她已经注意到钥匙不见了，但还没有意识到钥匙被偷了。不过，这种情况很快就会改变的。 在这里。加雷特低吼了一声。我会直接冲向那只怪物，从而吸引女巫的注意。等她把目光集中在我身上时，你们就从背后袭击她，阻止她施展任何法术。 听起来是个不错的计划。你向加雷特点了点头，他立刻从树林中冲了出来，灰白相间的身影在空气中一闪而逝，然后以一记飞扑动作抓住了那只战争犬。这一幕实在令人印象深刻——两只犬类形态的生物在岩石遍布的河岸上翻滚打斗，形成了一团充满愤怒与杀意的毛茸茸的团块。那头魔兽用爪子抓向加雷特的胸部和手臂，在他的皮毛上留下了深红色的抓痕，但他毫不在意疼痛，将这只野兽按在地面，然后用拳头猛击它的嘴部，发出一声震耳欲聋、令人满意的巨响。魔兽发出哀鸣，因加雷特这一记凶猛的打击而退缩，这给了他连续进攻的机会，他的指关节像活塞一样不断地敲打着魔兽的头部。 天啊，他真是把它的血液全部抽干。 那么，是时候你行动了。正如预料的那样，那位女德鲁伊将注意力集中在加雷特身上，大概是在准备施展某种法术；你完全可以轻松地接近他，并将其击败。 [pc.weapon]她本可以出手相助的。然而，不幸的是，在最后一刻，她突然转身旋转起来，转过身来面对你，她那身铠甲上银色和绿色的布料碎片在你的攻击之后飘落到了地上。面对迫在眉睫的危险，她完全放弃了救助自己宠物的可能性，而是转而对付这个新的威胁。 她看着你，你也看着她。然后，这位德鲁伊毫不犹豫地拉紧弓弦，一支由冰霜构成的银色箭矢出现在她的手指之间，已经上弦，随时准备射出。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: "There's something you should know before we begin. I am Etheryn of House Ridell, second in line to the throne of the Winter City." "You're a terrible negotiator if you begin by hobbling yourself," the druidess says with a scowl. "Am I supposed to be impressed by your rank? No, quite the opposite, in fact. You know who and what I am, and you still... yes, you are. The cut of your face, the features... you need not provide further proof of your lineage, princeling. Your resemblance to your grandfather is striking." Hmm. She knows how Etheryn's grandfather looked? That would put her at a good deal older than she would appear at first glance — but then again, elves do age well, be they pale or wyld. "No. I say so for the purpose of being completely honest with you, mistress — um —" "Hethia. Hethia Runasdottir, servant to the Old Wyld, grower of the first circle. Although, it must be said the title means little in this day and age, thanks to your... grandmother, probably. I've lost track of the years. Although I'll admit to being curious — what's a princeling like you doing so far from the Winter City?" "There's trouble afoot; I left silently to seek as much help as I could garner. From pale elves, if I could reach the other settlements, but mostly from other peoples. And —" Etheryn swallows hard — "I'm no princeling, I'm a princess! My sister declared it so!" "What?!" Hethia recoils, as if Etheryn had actually struck her. For once, you see true disgust on the druidess' face in place of her calm, measured expression; her fingers tighten about her bow, as if she's trying to decide to turn Etheryn into a pincushion where she stands. Then it turns into a sneer. "Oh, really? So the Winter City has sunk to such depths that there aren't enough women to take matters in hand? That the royal family has to dress up a half-sexed and call him a princess, and the court is perfectly fine with this? We prophesied that there would be dire consequences for abandoning the ancient powers for these so-called Living Gods, but I didn't quite expect it to be so soon!" [etheryn.highConfidence|Etheryn clenches and unclenches her fists, trembling ever so slightly. For a moment, she looks as if she's about to shatter, but manages to compose herself by degrees until her voice is flat and emotionless. "I've done nothing but approach you in good faith and honesty, druidess, and you do nothing but mock me. That's usually considered — I don't know, some might call it hobbling oneself?" A sniff. "Hmph. Excuse me if I've no love for the royal line of the Winter City." "It was not my decision to change the state religion — and the pale elves themselves were more than happy to follow these Belharan deities who'd aided them during the Godswar, as opposed to the silence of the Old Wyld. If you must blame someone, then blame the powers that you serve for abandoning the pale elves in their time of need." Hethia scowls. "That isn't exactly what happened." "Then hear me out like you said you would, instead of throwing out snide remarks while I'm speaking. |At those words, Etheryn looks away, breathing heavily and unable to meet Hethia's gaze. Shaken, perhaps, and definitely cowed, but still not out of the fight yet. Not if you can help it. Taking a step forward, you plant a hand on Etheryn's shoulder, letting her feel the firm, warm grip of your fingers, letting her know you're there for her. A pause. A glance. A smile. And then, by degrees, Etheryn stops shaking and steadies herself to finish what she said she'd do. "Please don't mock me. Here I am, trying to parley with you in good faith and good will, and you throw that straight back into my face, especially considering the fact that you said you'd hear me out. Or are you the kind who takes kindness for weakness?" A sniff. "Excuse me if I have no love lost for the royal line of the Winter City, especially when it manifests in the form of a cowardly half-sexed princeling having to play the role of a princess." "You're right about that, I've never been the bravest of people. But is it better to be born brave, or be born a coward and overcome it to confront a druidess of the Old Wyld?" "Hmph."] "Like I said, there is trouble afoot in the Winter City. My sister, Alissa — she has secluded herself in the palace and has recalled all the city's warriors, leaving none to patrol the Frostwood. Many question the decision, but none challenge the Queen — and few see her, anymore. Not after she took up with some mysterious advisor who appeared out of nowhere, that is." A small discussion ensues, but it's nothing that you hadn't heard from Etheryn when the two of you first met, mostly over the situation of the Winter City and the pale elves in general. At the end of it all, Hethia looks piqued by Etheryn's tidings, though you can tell she's trying hard to hide her interest. "Hmp." "Which is why I'm pleading with you, Mistress Hethia. Now isn't the time for infighting between the boer'alvar, but instead we should unite and overcome this mutual enemy that threatens our people. While traveling south through the woodlands, it's not been lost on me that many new threats have arisen in both the Old Forest and the Frostwood. Unnatural, twisted ones, which I believe share the same root as what ails the Winter City. "We may not like each other, but I believe what we can come to is a mutually beneficial arrangement. The loggers believe that you are keeping them here. But to be frank, is it not the other way around? That instead of threatening them, you are shielding them against what lurks in the forest instead?" Hethia scowls. "Where are your gods now, Etheryn? Call upon the Seven to aid you in this hour of need! Why do you need me, need us who still follow the Old Wyld that failed the pale elves centuries ago?" Man, that must be a serious thorn in Hethia's side. Etheryn throws you a glance, and you nod at her — it really does need to be pulled before the druidess can be swayed to your point of view. Etheryn swallows hard, but forces herself to stay calm despite the obvious attempt to provoke a rise out of her. "My sister Alissa — I can't be absolutely sure, but my suspicion is that she's been neglecting to keep the rites which serve as our link to Lumia. It wouldn't surprise me, given how she's been behaving of late. "Mistress Hethia, I don't think you're a bad person; you wouldn't have protected the loggers otherwise and would have enacted a harsher punishment upon them for daring to cross you. Yes, I do have some idea of what happened here. Together, we can escape this logging camp. Together, we can overcome this obstacle — and the threat which faces the pale elves as a whole." Hethia sighs, looks down at her warg, then looks back up at Etheryn. She seems to be considering Etheryn's words. "You managed to slip past the wards I erected." "It was no easy task. I had help." Etheryn gestures to you. A sigh. "You have no idea how tiring it was, keeping those up against the things which would test them. And the fact that you managed to make it through nevertheless... hmp." "Yes?" "Well, scion of the royal bloodline, I'm forced to admit that you're resourceful, at least. And maybe despite your nature, you're not as faint of heart as you imagine yourself to be." The druidess considers Etheryn some more, sizing her up from head to toe. "You believe you can get everyone out safely?" "Yes." You note that at the very least Hethia's stopped calling Ryn a princeling, even if she won't acknowledge her as a woman. A small victory, to begin with. "You promise much, royal scion. Getting a large group of people through the trees is far different from a small party." "I'm not without resources. You don't really want to be here, do you, Mistress Hethia? You'd rather be rushing back to your circle, to see if they're still standing, to make sure they worry for you no longer, to help them shore up the defenses for what's to come. You'd rather not be stuck here babysitting a handful of other peoples who don't understand what you're doing and have no gratitude for it, right? "Old wounds from generations past can be reopened and picked at later — let me reiterate, what we need to do now is unite in the face of a common threat." "I won't make any promises." "I'm asking for none. Not from the circles, at least. What I'm offering you here is an opportunity to be relieved of what you see as your duty, and the freedom to return to your own. Give us the loggers and the naive would-be hero — surely they've suffered enough to sate whatever appetite for punishment you might have had. My companion and I will escort them safely to their homes. Then you'll be free to return to those you care for." Hethia doesn't say anything, but the druidess' pale silver-green eyes search Etheryn's face, then yours. For a moment, she looks very, very tired, then sits down on her warg's back. The beast barely flinches, clearly used to bearing its mistress' weight. "Alright, royal scion Etheryn. If you believe you can do all this, you're free to take the loggers with you. Here." She reaches into her armored robes and tosses a large keyring to Etheryn, who deftly catches it out of the air. "The key to the beastman's cage. I was rather enjoying a regular dose of doggy dick on demand, but all good things must come to an end." Etheryn bows slightly. "My gratitude, Mistress Hethia." "I suppose you have mine, too." Looking back and forth between Etheryn and you, Hethia fits a saddle upon the back of her warg and hops astride it, clearly used to it serving as her mount. You have to admit, it does look quite impressive. "You're not like that dog who went and attacked my precious Norathar without so much as thinking. If I'm completely honest, I'd have him give her his dick as well." She... she would do that? "He may walk on two legs, but he's enough of a dumb brute that it wouldn't count as bestiality." She sniffs in a manner entirely befitting a haughty noblewoman. "Well. I shall see you around, royal scion. If this threat is as dire as you make it out to be, I have little doubt that our paths will cross again." "I hope they do. It will likely mean that you and yours have decided to set aside old differences." "We shall see." With a pat to the warg's head, Hethia sets it off in a quick, loping gait, and is soon out the gates and gone amongst the trees. There's no time to lose — now that Hethia is gone, the wards she was protecting the camp with will no doubt start to fade soon.
rows.translation: 在开始之前，有件事你需要知道。我是里德尔家族的伊瑟琳，是冬城的王位第二继承人。 如果你一开始就给自己设置限制，那你根本就不是个会谈判的人。女德鲁伊皱着眉头说道。难道我就该因为你的身份而对你刮目相看吗？不，并非如此。你明明知道我是谁、是什么人，却仍然……是的，你确实这么做了。你的面容、你的五官……你根本不需要再证明自己的出身了，王子殿下。你和你祖父的相似之处实在太明显了。 嗯。她知道伊瑟琳的祖父长什么样？这意味着她的年龄应该比乍看之下要大很多——不过，话说回来，无论是苍白种族还是野性种族，精灵们的寿命确实都很长。 不，我这么说是为了对您完全坦诚，夫人——嗯—— 赫希娅。赫希娅·鲁纳斯多蒂尔，古老荒野的仆从，第一圈的守护者。虽然不得不说，在这个时代，这样的头衔已经没什么意义了——不过这大概要归功于你的……祖母吧。我已经记不清具体是过了多少年。不过我确实很好奇：像你这样的贵族子弟，为什么会远离冬城来到这里呢？ 出麻烦了，我悄悄离开去尽可能多地寻求帮助。如果能够到达其他定居点的话，可以从苍白精灵那里获得帮助，但主要还是依靠其他族群。还有——伊瑟琳艰难地咽了口唾沫—— 我可不是什么王子，我是公主！我姐姐就是这么说的！ 什么？！赫希娅猛地后退了一步，仿佛伊瑟琳真的对她出手了一般。这一次，你可以在这位德鲁伊女巫的脸上看到真正的厌恶之情，而不是她那一贯冷静、沉着的表情；她的手指紧紧地握住弓，仿佛在考虑是否应该将伊瑟琳当场射成刺猬一样。 然后，那厌恶之情变成了冷笑。哦，真的吗？那么冬城已经堕落到这种地步，连足够的女性来处理这些事务都找不到了吗？以至于王室不得不把一个具有半性特征的人打扮成公主，而宫廷里的人对此也毫无异议？我们早就预言过，抛弃古老的力量去崇拜这些所谓的‘现世神祇’，必然会带来严重的后果，但没想到会这么快就发生！ rows.raw: ' "There's something you should know before we begin. I am Etheryn of House Ridell, second in line to the throne of the Winter City." "You're a terrible negotiator if you begin by hobbling yourself," the druidess says with a scowl. "Am I supposed to be impressed by your rank? No, quite the opposite, in fact. You know who and what I am, and you still... yes, you are. The cut of your face, the features... you need not provide further proof of your lineage, princeling. Your resemblance to your grandfather is striking." Hmm. She knows how Etheryn's grandfather looked? That would put her at a good deal older than she would appear at first glance — but then again, elves do age well, be they pale or wyld. "No. I say so for the purpose of being completely honest with you, mistress — um —" "Hethia. Hethia Runasdottir, servant to the Old Wyld, grower of the first circle. Although, it must be said the title means little in this day and age, thanks to your... grandmother, probably. I've lost track of the years. Although I'll admit to being curious — what's a princeling like you doing so far from the Winter City?" "There's trouble afoot; I left silently to seek as much help as I could garner. From pale elves, if I could reach the other settlements, but mostly from other peoples. And —" Etheryn swallows hard — "I'm no princeling, I'm a princess! My sister declared it so!" "What?!" Hethia recoils, as if Etheryn had actually struck her. For once, you see true disgust on the druidess' face in place of her calm, measured expression; her fingers tighten about her bow, as if she's trying to decide to turn Etheryn into a pincushion where she stands. Then it turns into a sneer. "Oh, really? So the Winter City has sunk to such depths that there aren't enough women to take matters in hand? That the royal family has to dress up a half-sexed and call him a princess, and the court is perfectly fine with this? We prophesied that there would be dire consequences for abandoning the ancient powers for these so-called Living Gods, but I didn't quite expect it to be so soon!" [etheryn.highConfidence|Etheryn clenches and unclenches her fists, trembling ever so slightly. For a moment, she looks as if she's about to shatter, but manages to compose herself by degrees until her voice is flat and emotionless. "I've done nothing but approach you in good faith and honesty, druidess, and you do nothing but mock me. That's usually considered — I don't know, some might call it hobbling oneself?" A sniff. "Hmph. Excuse me if I've no love for the royal line of the Winter City." "It was not my decision to change the state religion — and the pale elves themselves were more than happy to follow these Belharan deities who'd aided them during the Godswar, as opposed to the silence of the Old Wyld. If you must blame someone, then blame the powers that you serve for abandoning the pale elves in their time of need." Hethia scowls. "That isn't exactly what happened." "Then hear me out like you said you would, instead of throwing out snide remarks while I'm speaking. |At those words, Etheryn looks away, breathing heavily and unable to meet Hethia's gaze. Shaken, perhaps, and definitely cowed, but still not out of the fight yet. Not if you can help it. Taking a step forward, you plant a hand on Etheryn's shoulder, letting her feel the firm, warm grip of your fingers, letting her know you're there for her. A pause. A glance. A smile. And then, by degrees, Etheryn stops shaking and steadies herself to finish what she said she'd do. "Please don't mock me. Here I am, trying to parley with you in good faith and good will, and you throw that straight back into my face, especially considering the fact that you said you'd hear me out. Or are you the kind who takes kindness for weakness?" A sniff. "Excuse me if I have no love lost for the royal line of the Winter City, especially when it manifests in the form of a cowardly half-sexed princeling having to play the role of a princess." "You're right about that, I've never been the bravest of people. But is it better to be born brave, or be born a coward and overcome it to confront a druidess of the Old Wyld?" "Hmph."] "Like I said, there is trouble afoot in the Winter City. My sister, Alissa — she has secluded herself in the palace and has recalled all the city's warriors, leaving none to patrol the Frostwood. Many question the decision, but none challenge the Queen — and few see her, anymore. Not after she took up with some mysterious advisor who appeared out of nowhere, that is." A small discussion ensues, but it's nothing that you hadn't heard from Etheryn when the two of you first met, mostly over the situation of the Winter City and the pale elves in general. At the end of it all, Hethia looks piqued by Etheryn's tidings, though you can tell she's trying hard to hide her interest. "Hmp." "Which is why I'm pleading with you, Mistress Hethia. Now isn't the time for infighting between the boer'alvar, but instead we should unite and overcome this mutual enemy that threatens our people. While traveling south through the woodlands, it's not been lost on me that many new threats have arisen in both the Old Forest and the Frostwood. Unnatural, twisted ones, which I believe share the same root as what ails the Winter City. "We may not like each other, but I believe what we can come to is a mutually beneficial arrangement. The loggers believe that you are keeping them here. But to be frank, is it not the other way around? That instead of threatening them, you are shielding them against what lurks in the forest instead?" Hethia scowls. "Where are your gods now, Etheryn? Call upon the Seven to aid you in this hour of need! Why do you need me, need us who still follow the Old Wyld that failed the pale elves centuries ago?" Man, that must be a serious thorn in Hethia's side. Etheryn throws you a glance, and you nod at her — it really does need to be pulled before the druidess can be swayed to your point of view. Etheryn swallows hard, but forces herself to stay calm despite the obvious attempt to provoke a rise out of her. "My sister Alissa — I can't be absolutely sure, but my suspicion is that she's been neglecting to keep the rites which serve as our link to Lumia. It wouldn't surprise me, given how she's been behaving of late. "Mistress Hethia, I don't think you're a bad person; you wouldn't have protected the loggers otherwise and would have enacted a harsher punishment upon them for daring to cross you. Yes, I do have some idea of what happened here. Together, we can escape this logging camp. Together, we can overcome this obstacle — and the threat which faces the pale elves as a whole." Hethia sighs, looks down at her warg, then looks back up at Etheryn. She seems to be considering Etheryn's words. "You managed to slip past the wards I erected." "It was no easy task. I had help." Etheryn gestures to you. A sigh. "You have no idea how tiring it was, keeping those up against the things which would test them. And the fact that you managed to make it through nevertheless... hmp." "Yes?" "Well, scion of the royal bloodline, I'm forced to admit that you're resourceful, at least. And maybe despite your nature, you're not as faint of heart as you imagine yourself to be." The druidess considers Etheryn some more, sizing her up from head to toe. "You believe you can get everyone out safely?" "Yes." You note that at the very least Hethia's stopped calling Ryn a princeling, even if she won't acknowledge her as a woman. A small victory, to begin with. "You promise much, royal scion. Getting a large group of people through the trees is far different from a small party." "I'm not without resources. You don't really want to be here, do you, Mistress Hethia? You'd rather be rushing back to your circle, to see if they're still standing, to make sure they worry for you no longer, to help them shore up the defenses for what's to come. You'd rather not be stuck here babysitting a handful of other peoples who don't understand what you're doing and have no gratitude for it, right? "Old wounds from generations past can be reopened and picked at later — let me reiterate, what we need to do now is unite in the face of a common threat." "I won't make any promises." "I'm asking for none. Not from the circles, at least. What I'm offering you here is an opportunity to be relieved of what you see as your duty, and the freedom to return to your own. Give us the loggers and the naive would-be hero — surely they've suffered enough to sate whatever appetite for punishment you might have had. My companion and I will escort them safely to their homes. Then you'll be free to return to those you care for." Hethia doesn't say anything, but the druidess' pale silver-green eyes search Etheryn's face, then yours. For a moment, she looks very, very tired, then sits down on her warg's back. The beast barely flinches, clearly used to bearing its mistress' weight. "Alright, royal scion Etheryn. If you believe you can do all this, you're free to take the loggers with you. Here." She reaches into her armored robes and tosses a large keyring to Etheryn, who deftly catches it out of the air. "The key to the beastman's cage. I was rather enjoying a regular dose of doggy dick on demand, but all good things must come to an end." Etheryn bows slightly. "My gratitude, Mistress Hethia." "I suppose you have mine, too." Looking back and forth between Etheryn and you, Hethia fits a saddle upon the back of her warg and hops astride it, clearly used to it serving as her mount. You have to admit, it does look quite impressive. "You're not like that dog who went and attacked my precious Norathar without so much as thinking. If I'm completely honest, I'd have him give her his dick as well." She... she would do that? "He may walk on two legs, but he's enough of a dumb brute that it wouldn't count as bestiality." She sniffs in a manner entirely befitting a haughty noblewoman. "Well. I shall see you around, royal scion. If this threat is as dire as you make it out to be, I have little doubt that our paths will cross again." "I hope they do. It will likely mean that you and yours have decided to set aside old differences." "We shall see." With a pat to the warg's head, Hethia sets it off in a quick, loping gait, and is soon out the gates and gone amongst the trees. There's no time to lose — now that Hethia is gone, the wards she was protecting the camp with will no doubt start to fade soon.'

rows.original: Before long, you're back in the dusty hall, striding up to Garret's cage at a comfortable pace. He cocks an ear up at you, then heaves a sigh of — is it relief? — as he realizes who it is. "You're back again, I see." Yes, you are. Pulling out the keyring, you dangle it front of the bars for a bit, and watch Garret's eyes widen slightly. "Oh. You got her? Well done." To be fair, you didn't so much get Hethia as convince her to leave peacefully. It could've come to blows, especially if you'd started off on the wrong foot, but everything seems to have worked out just fine. She wasn't a bad person, just under a lot of pressure, and that does things to people. Garret raises an eyebrow. "You're defending the witch who put me in a cage and used me as a pet dog?" Hey, you seem to remember him saying something about volunteering for the task in order to keep her ire off the loggers. That, and he did get some pussy out of it. "You say that like it means something." Looking around him, Garret gets to his feet, then decidedly kicks over the little dog dish in his cage; sending it crashing against the rusted bars and splintering into a dozen pieces. "Come on, let's blow this joint. It's a long trek back to Hawkethorne." Indeed. The key fits smoothly into the lock, and although the bolt is a bit rusted it still moves with a little effort. Grumbling and growling, Garret steps out of his cage, stretching and flexing. "Gods above, that's better out than in." So... does he know where Hethia put his stuff? Especially his clothes? He shrugs. "She didn't have much use for the stuff I was lugging around, so your guess is as good as mine. I'll go look around the sheds and storehouse; you go and tell the other folks it's safe to come out, okay? I'd come along, but it's not a good idea to go talking to people without any clothes on." rows.translation: 女德鲁伊用魔法弓连续射出的那些银色冰箭，让你根本无法承受。你的关节感到剧痛且僵硬，四肢也不听使唤，仿佛被冰封住了。最终，你的体力耗尽，整个人重重地摔倒在地，那种彻骨的冰冷麻木感逐渐蔓延到你的全身。 [var0|如果没有你阻止那位女德鲁伊，加雷特本人很快就会倒下，他身上到处都是伤口，鲜血直流。他虽然还活着，但情况非常糟糕——原本棕白相间的毛发现在已经变成了难看的锈红色。那只战争兽正准备扑上去将他彻底杀死，但女德鲁伊突然发出尖锐的哨声，同时打了个响指，将它叫了回来。 ]对结果感到满意，这个高个子的亚马逊精灵站在你面前，当她那冷漠的目光与你的目光相遇时，她显得更加高大威严。她甚至都懒得踢开你[pc.weapon]她知道你已经虚弱得连伸手去拿它的力气都没有了——她那些冰冷的箭所蕴含的魔力已经将你的力量彻底耗尽。 又一个自封的英雄啊？和上一个一样。我并不怪你是个无知的野蛮人，但你已经在本已糟糕的局势上给我带来了无数麻烦。现在的局面已经很微妙了，而你差点就把天平推向错误的方向。 也许你本想回答，但不知为何，你的身体似乎并不愿意这样做。至少，在你的舌头还这么麻木、口腔里仿佛覆盖着一层厚厚的狗毛的时候，你是无法做到这一点的。 现在，该怎么惩罚你呢？我得承认，我其实并不想这么做过于这个女人可真记仇啊，但你们真的该学会别再惹怒老荒野了。先是闯入不该进入的地方，然后又带着种种豪言壮语冲上来……说真的，我本来应该为你们的“勇气”鼓掌的，但现在确实不是时候。 她到底是打算继续做下去，还是怎么着？ 也许你会是个不错的宠物……算了，那样反而有点无聊了。那位女德鲁伊若有所思地静立了片刻，随后她的表情变得明亮起来。当她将一只脚重重地踩在你的胸口上时，你清楚地注意到她竟然没有穿鞋子——这一细节让你印象深刻，因为她的这一动作彻底让你喘不过气来。她用那样的方式压制你，几乎要把你碾得粉身碎骨，让你彻底感受到因输给她而产生的所有羞耻与屈辱。 与此同时，这位女德鲁伊开始撩起她那身铠甲长袍的裙摆——正如你所预料的，她根本没有穿任何内衣。[var1| 不过，人们不禁会想，像她这样的浅色皮肤精灵，到底是会刮掉私处的毛发，还是天生就没有毛发呢？]她的声音尖锐而带有命令式的口吻，就像一把冰冷的刀子一样，直接切入你的思绪，产生的效果也差不多。 如果我还能再狠心一点的话，或许就会退一步，让诺拉塔尔来对付你。她厉声说道，同时回头看了一眼她的战兽。不过今天我确实心情格外宽宏大量。 舔！ 说着，这位女德鲁伊以惊人的速度双膝跪地，然后将她的阴部紧紧贴在你的脸上。你首先感觉到的是那股刺骨的寒冷——如果你的舌头和嘴唇还没有变得麻木的话，当她的阴部像一块滴着融雪的冰块那样触碰到它们时，它们肯定也会立刻失去感觉。女德鲁伊紧紧抓住你的脖子来保持平衡，然后用极其猛烈的力量将她冰冷的手掌压在你的身上，根本不给你任何思考的时间，更不用说喘息的机会了。 难怪加雷特并不愿意成为她的“替代品”…… 呼！ 很快你就明白了——这位女德鲁伊根本不在乎是否能让对方获得快感，整个过程对她来说只是一种展示自己权威、让你蒙羞的手段。你既不能舔她，也不能动弹，于是她只好将自己的阴部摩擦在你的脸上；从你的嘴唇开始，她不断地上下移动，让自己那冰冷的体液洒满你的脸，以此象征性地把你标记为一个被羞辱、被击败的失败者。你所能做的，就是闭上眼睛，趁她握住你脖子的手稍微松开的时候，偷偷喘口气，然后希望这一切能尽快结束。 至少那个自封的英雄还有个可以用得上的家伙。你能听到她在喃喃自语。你？你只不过是个失败者罢了。 时间在模糊中流逝——寒冷恐怕已经影响到了你的思维。不过，最终你还是隐约察觉到那位女德鲁伊站了起来，她的注意力被别的东西吸引了——确切地说，是被那扇大门吸引了。 什么……？ 哼，有人来了，你这个一无是处的失败者。我不会再待下去了……但首先…… 你感觉到她伸手去触碰你，做了……某个动作。之后，那位女德鲁伊跳上了她的战兽背部，像骑着一匹犬类坐骑一样骑在它背上，然后战兽便朝河边奔去，带着她一起离开了。
rows.raw: " The continuous volleys of silvery rime arrows from the druidess magic bow are too much for you to bear. Your joints feel immensely painful and stiff, your limbs unwilling to move, as if they were encased in ice. Eventually, your strength gives, and you keel head over heels onto the ground as a crippling, icy numbness sinks into your being. [var0|Without you holding off the druidess, Garret himself is quickly brought down, bleeding from several ugly gashes all over his body. He's still alive, but in bad shape; fur that was once brown and white is now an ugly rust-red mess. The warg moves to maul him and finish Garret off for good, but the druidess calls it back with a sharp whistle and snap of her fingers. ]Satisfied with the outcome, the tall, amazonian elf comes to stand over you, looking even more towering and imposing as her impassive gaze meets yours. She doesn't even bother to kick away your [pc.weapon], knowing that you're too enervated to even reach for it, the magic from her icy arrows having sapped your strength to nothingness. "Another would-be hero, eh? Just like the last one. I don't blame you for being an ignorant savage, but you've caused me no end of trouble on top of an already bad situation. Things are already quite delicate here, and you almost tipped the balance the wrong way." Perhaps you'd have replied, but somehow your body doesn't quite feel like it. At least, not with your tongue as numb as it is, nor with your mouth feeling like it's been coated with a generous layer of dog hair. "Now, how to go about punishing you? I'd like to think I'm not an overly vengeful woman, but you lot really have to learn to stop tempting the Old Wyld's fury. First encroaching on places you should not, then charging in with all sorts of bravado... I'd applaud you, really, but now's not the time for that." Is she just going to get on with it, or what? "Maybe you'd make a good pet... nah. That's starting to get boring." The druidess appears contemplative for a few more moments, then her expression brightens. The fact that she wears no shoes is firmly impressed upon you as she heavily plants a foot on your chest, knocking out what little wind's left in you. Holding you down like that, she practically grinds you into the dirt, making sure you feel every last tittle and jot of shame and degradation at having lost to her. At the same time, the druidess begins to hike up the skirts of her armored robes, and as you expected, she wears no smallclothes.[var1| One has to wonder, though, whether pale elves like her actually shave their pubes, or are naturally hairless down there.] Her voice, sharp and commanding, cuts through your thoughts like a cold knife, with much the same effect. "If I were feeling any more cruel, I'd probably step back and let Norathar take you," she snaps, glancing back at her warg. "But I'm feeling appropriately magnanimous today. "Lick!" With that, the druidess drops to her knees with amazing alacrity and mashes her cunt in your face. The first thing you realize is that it's frightfully cold — if your tongue and lips weren't numb already, they would be the moment her cunt hits them like an ice cube dripping snowmelt. Gripping you by the neck to steady herself, the druidess presses her icy snatch with ferocious force against you, giving you no time to think, let alone catch your breath. No wonder Garret wasn't very into being her dildo. Brr! It soon becomes clear that the druidess doesn't give a whit about being pleasured — the whole act is just a matter of her dominance and your humiliation. You can't lick, you can't move, so she settles for grinding her pussy against your face; starting from your lips, the druidess snuffles up and down so that her icy girl-fluids are spread all over your face, ritualistically marking you as an abased, defeated loser. It's all you can do to shut your eyes, sneak a breath here and there when her hold on your neck loosens slightly, and hope that it all ends quickly. "At least that other would-be hero had a dick worth using," you hear her mutter. "You? You're nothing but a failure." Time passes in a bit of a blur — the cold must be getting to your brain. Eventually, though, you're dimly aware of the druidess standing up, her attention drawn elsewhere — towards the gates, to be exact. Wha...? "Hmph. We have company, you worthless failure. I'm not about to stick around any longer. But first..." You feel her reach down for you, doing... something. After that, the druidess springs onto the back of her warg, hopping astride it like some kind of canine pony, because it bounds off towards the river, taking her with it."

rows.original: She's gone. "[pc.name]? [pc.name]!" Ye gods. Never have you been so glad to hear Brother Sanders' voice. Then there's Garth, and a handful of other folk... seems like Garth got together that militia he was talking about, and just in the nick of time, too. [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|The old wolf crouches down by his son's comatose form, shaking his head, then with a little grunt of effort picks Garret up and slings him over his shoulder like a sack of potatoes. You dimly wonder if Garret can be moved safely, as injured as he is, but Garth presumably knows what he's doing.] "[pc.name]?" Right. You're here. Brother Sanders grips you by the shoulder, and you feel marginally stronger. Did... did they get the druidess? Sanders shakes his head. "We saw her retreat, but she'd too much of a head start for us to give chase. Not that that's the issue here — we're here to rescue the lot of you, after all. Seems like we arrived in the nick of time." "Mistress Ivris told us the pale elves aren't very accommodating to defeated enemies. Who knows what she might have done?" Garth grunts. "Never tussled with them before. Don't hope to start anytime soon. You've got a face full of it, [pc.name]." Psh. While you still feel distinctly wobbly, you manage to sit up and check yourself over, wondering what it was that the druidess did to you just before she left. It doesn't take you long to discover just what: you've been stripped of almost everything save the clothes on your back. Sure, you'd have done the same if you'd beaten her, but that doesn't stop the loss from stinging terribly. Sanders clears his throat. "So, are you all right?" Yeah, you'll live. See to the others, okay? "We're getting them out as we speak. Looking at the state of things, it looks like the druidess and her pet won; Westbank is done for. Even if she's no longer going to be a problem — which I seriously doubt — we're not putting people so deep in the woods, not with how dangerous the Old Forest has become. Preferably somewhere near the edges, if a new camp's going to go up." Right, right. You're... just a little tired now. "All right, then." Sanders stands and gives you an encouraging pat. "I'll come get you when we're ready to return to Hawkethorne." So it happens that the loggers are led out from behind their barricade and through the gates, all ten of them guarded by Sanders, Garth and twenty militiamen through the trails of the Old Forest. Sanders lends you a shoulder to lean on, and Garth [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|lugs his son's bloody body like a sack of potatoes all the way back. Despite his age, he doesn't appear winded by the burden in the least, despite Garret's meaty bulk.|leads Garret on as well. Garret's found some ill-fitting clothes to cover himself with for the trek home, and there's a distinct cold silence between father and son for the whole trip back.] With Sanders forging a path through the forest with his powers, the emerald tip of his staff glowing to light the way, the trip home is fairly uneventful. From there on out, it's only a few hours until the lot of you are back at the gates of Hawkethorne. The guards look almost relieved to see everyone back — almost as if they'd been entertaining the thought that the small militia group might not even return. Job done, the militiamen and loggers alike begin dispersing one by one, returning to their homes until it's just you, Sanders, Garth and Garret. [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|"Leave the boy with me," Sanders tells Garth. "I'll work on him tonight." Garth looks uncertain of that. "He'll live. Bitches dig scars — he'll have plenty after today." "That may be true, but you're too hard on him." Garth bares his teeth ever so slightly. "Hey, Sanders. I know you mean well, but don't you tell me how to raise my son, especially when you don't have one of your own." "Telling you how to raise Garret has nothing to do with it. It's the simple truth. Are you going to let me see to him, or not?" Both men stare at each other for a tense moment, a invisible duel of wills being played out, and at last Garth relents. "Here, take the big lunk. I'll come around in the morning to pick him up." With that, Garth shrugs off the comatose Garret off his shoulder and into Brother Sanders' embrace. The latter catches poor Garret without so much as flinching, and sighs at one of the gate guards. "Would you please help me get Garret to the chapel?" The gate guard looks to his friend for confirmation, and upon receiving it, moves off with Sanders, Garret hoisted between the both of them. After they've disappeared in the direction of the town square, Garth takes a few steps in the direction of the Frost Hound, then stops. "[pc.name]." Yes? "Sorry about all this. Being beaten down is never fun. You okay there?" Well, your tongue is still kinda numb and tingly, and admittedly you've felt better, but you don't think you're in any danger of giving up the ghost at the moment. "Go on, then — go get some sleep. Everyone knows a good night's rest in an inn will fix everything wrong with you. I'll see you in the morning. [party.has brint|Help me out will you please, Brint? I'll get you sorted once I'm done with [pc.name].]" That is... sounding quite good, actually. You're still a little shaky and wobbly, so Garth helps you all the way back to the Frost Hound and up the stairs to your room, where you quickly dump the few things the druidess didn't steal from you to the ground and are asleep before your head hits the pillow. |"So, a would-be hero ending up needing rescuing himself." "Get off my back, old man. It's not like you didn't send [pc.name] after me." "[pc.name] at least has proven [pc.himHer]self more capable than you already, even if what happened today proves that [pc.heShe] still has some ways to go. You, on the other hand..." Garret grunts. "Old man, I don't want to do this out in the open. You want to kick up dirt, wait until we're indoors before starting, okay?" "Hmph. Fine." Sanders glances at father and son and shakes his head, pulling you aside. "As much as I expected. Allow me to help you back, [pc.name]. You don't look too hearty.[party.has brint| Brint, would you mind please helping me? You're heading there too, after all.]" After the trek back through the Old Forest? Yeah, you're pretty bushed. Could do with a long nap, too. The expression on your face tells Sanders all he needs to know — taking you by the hand, he leads you on a slightly roundabout route back to the Frost Hound, well away from Garth and Garret. Helping you up the stairs to your room, the kindly priest drops you off at the door and bids you a good night before leaving. Somewhere deep within the Frost Hound, there's a raucous caucus going on, but you're too exhausted to care anymore. It's but a moment for you to toss aside what little the druidess didn't steal off you, and you're asleep before your head hits the pillow.]
rows.translation: 她走了。 “[pc.name]？[pc.name]！” 天啊，我从来没这么高兴过听到桑德斯修士的声音。还有加斯，以及另外一些人……看来加斯终于组建了他之前提到的那支民兵组织，而且还是在这个千钧一发的时刻。 [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|老狼蹲在儿子昏迷不醒的身体旁，摇了摇头，然后费了些力气把加勒特抱起来，像扛一袋土豆一样把他甩到自己的肩上。你不禁怀疑，以加勒特目前的伤势，这样搬动他是否安全，但加思显然知道自己在做什么。] “[pc.name]？” 对了，你在这里。桑德斯修士抓住你的肩膀，你感觉自己稍微强壮了一些。他们……他们抓到那个女德鲁伊了吗？ 桑德斯摇了摇头。我们看到她撤退了，但她起步太早，我们根本来不及追赶。不过这也不是真正的问题——毕竟我们来的目的是来救大家的。看来我们来得正是时候。 艾薇莉丝女士告诉我们，那些苍白精灵对于被击败的敌人可不会手下留情。谁知道她又会做出什么来呢？加思哼了一声。以前从来没和他们发生过冲突，现在也别指望能很快开始打架。你的脸上可都写得清清楚楚呢[pc.name]。” 哼，虽然你还觉得浑身发软，但还是勉强坐了起来检查自己的身体状况，心里在想那位女德鲁伊在离开之前到底对你做了什么。没过多久，你就发现答案了：除了身上的衣服，你几乎被夺走了所有东西。当然，如果你真的打败了她，你可能也会做出同样的事，但这种损失还是让人感到非常难受。” 桑德斯清了清嗓子。那么，你没事吧？ 嗯，你会活下来的。去照顾其他人吧，好吗？ 我们正在把他们带出来。从目前的情况来看，看起来那位女德鲁伊和她的宠物获胜了，西岸已经完了。即使她不会再构成威胁——但我对此表示怀疑——考虑到古林如今已经变得如此危险，我们也不会把人们派到那么深的森林里去。如果要建立新的营地，最好选择在森林边缘附近的地方。 对，对。你只是……现在有点累了而已。 那好吧。桑德斯站起身来，鼓励性地拍了拍你的肩膀。等我们准备返回鹰棘镇的时候，我会来接你。 于是，那些伐木工们被从他们的路障后面带了出来，经过大门，全部十个人都在桑德斯、加思以及二十名民兵的护送下，沿着古林的小路前行。桑德斯会让你依靠在他的肩膀上，而加思[flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|他像扛着一袋土豆一样，把儿子那血淋淋的尸体一路背了回去。尽管年纪已高，但尽管加勒特体型魁梧，这个负担似乎丝毫没有让他感到吃力。|这也引出了加勒特的故事。加勒特找了一些不合身的衣服来遮盖身体，以便在回家的路上使用，而在整个返程过程中，父子俩之间始终保持着一种冰冷而沉默的氛围。]在桑德斯运用自己的力量开辟出一条穿过森林的道路，他的法杖翠绿色的尖端散发着光芒为前路照亮的情况下，这次回家的旅程相当顺利，没有发生任何意外。 从那以后，再过几个小时，你们所有人就能回到鹰棘镇的大门口了。看到所有人都回来了，守卫们似乎松了一口气——仿佛他们之前还在担心那个小规模的民兵组织可能根本不会回来呢。任务完成之后，那些民兵和伐木工们便开始陆续散去，各自回家去了，最后就只剩下你、桑德斯、加思和加勒特四人了。 [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|把这个男孩留给我吧。桑德斯对加思说道。我今晚就会处理他。 加思对此似乎并不确定。他会活下来的。那些女人就爱留下伤痕……今天过后，他身上会有很多这样的‘伤痕’了。 那可能是真的，但你对他太苛刻了。 加思微微露出了牙齿。嘿，桑德斯。我知道你是好意，但你也别来教我怎么养育儿子，尤其是当你自己都没有儿子的时候。 告诉你如何抚养加勒特跟这件事毫无关系。这就是事实。你到底要不要让我来照顾他？ 两人紧张地对视着，仿佛正在进行一场无形的意志较量，最终加思让步了。拿着这个大块头吧，我明天早上会再来把它取走的。 说着，加思将昏迷不醒的加雷特从肩上甩下来，交到了桑德斯修士的怀里。后者毫不费力地接住了加雷特，然后向其中一名守门人叹了口气。你能帮我把加勒特带到小教堂去吗？ 门卫向他的朋友确认了一下，得到确认后，便带着桑德斯离开了，加勒特被他们两人架在中间。当他们朝镇广场的方向消失后，加思朝寒霜猎犬的方向走了几步，然后停了下来。 “[pc.name]。” 嗯？ 对于发生的一切，我真的很抱歉。被人欺负肯定没什么好受的。你现在没事吧？ 嗯，你的舌头还是有点麻木和刺痛的感觉，而且确实，你现在感觉好了一些，但你觉得目前自己并没有生命危险。 那好吧，去睡吧。大家都知道，在客栈里好好睡一觉就能解决你所有的问题。明天早上见。 [party.has brint|拜托了，布林特，帮帮我吧？等我忙完这件事，一定会好好报答你的。 [pc.name]。]" 其实……听起来还挺不错的。你的脚步还是有点不稳，所以加斯一路扶着你回到了寒霜猎犬号，然后陪你上了楼梯，回到了你的房间。你把那些女德鲁伊没有抢走的东西扔到地上，然后一沾枕头就睡着了。 |所以，一个自以为是个英雄的人，最终却需要别人来救他。 别烦我了，老头。又不是你没有寄过来[pc.name]跟我来。 "[pc.name]至少已经证明了这一点。 [pc.himHer]其实你本来就已经比自己想象中更有能力了，即便今天发生的事情证明了这一点。 [pc.heShe]还有很长的路要走。而你…… 加勒特哼了一声。老兄，我可不想在轻型天化日之下干这种事。如果你想搞些麻烦，那就等我们进了屋再开始吧，好吗？ 哼，好吧。 桑德斯瞥了那对父子一眼，然后摇了摇头，把你拉到了一边。正如我所预料的那样。让我来帮你吧。 [pc.name]你看起来身体状况不太好啊。[party.has brint| 布林特，你能帮我一下吗？反正你也是往那个方向去的。]" 在穿过古林长途跋涉之后？没错，你们确实累坏了，确实需要好好睡一觉。你脸上的表情已经让桑德斯明白了所有该知道的事情——他牵着你的手，选择了一条稍微绕点的路线，带领你们回到了霜犬酒馆号上，避开了加思和加雷特。那位善良的牧师帮助你走上了楼梯，来到了你的房间，将你送到门口后，还祝你晚安才离开。 在霜犬酒馆号的某个角落，正在举行一场热闹的会议，但你已经疲惫不堪，根本无暇关心这些事了。对你来说，只需短短的片刻时间，把那位女德鲁伊没有偷走的那一点点东西扔到一边，然后你就会在头碰到枕头之前睡着了。]
rows.raw: " She's gone. "[pc.name]? [pc.name]!" Ye gods. Never have you been so glad to hear Brother Sanders' voice. Then there's Garth, and a handful of other folk... seems like Garth got together that militia he was talking about, and just in the nick of time, too. [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|The old wolf crouches down by his son's comatose form, shaking his head, then with a little grunt of effort picks Garret up and slings him over his shoulder like a sack of potatoes. You dimly wonder if Garret can be moved safely, as injured as he is, but Garth presumably knows what he's doing.] "[pc.name]?" Right. You're here. Brother Sanders grips you by the shoulder, and you feel marginally stronger. Did... did they get the druidess? Sanders shakes his head. "We saw her retreat, but she'd too much of a head start for us to give chase. Not that that's the issue here — we're here to rescue the lot of you, after all. Seems like we arrived in the nick of time." "Mistress Ivris told us the pale elves aren't very accommodating to defeated enemies. Who knows what she might have done?" Garth grunts. "Never tussled with them before. Don't hope to start anytime soon. You've got a face full of it, [pc.name]." Psh. While you still feel distinctly wobbly, you manage to sit up and check yourself over, wondering what it was that the druidess did to you just before she left. It doesn't take you long to discover just what: you've been stripped of almost everything save the clothes on your back. Sure, you'd have done the same if you'd beaten her, but that doesn't stop the loss from stinging terribly. Sanders clears his throat. "So, are you all right?" Yeah, you'll live. See to the others, okay? "We're getting them out as we speak. Looking at the state of things, it looks like the druidess and her pet won; Westbank is done for. Even if she's no longer going to be a problem — which I seriously doubt — we're not putting people so deep in the woods, not with how dangerous the Old Forest has become. Preferably somewhere near the edges, if a new camp's going to go up." Right, right. You're... just a little tired now. "All right, then." Sanders stands and gives you an encouraging pat. "I'll come get you when we're ready to return to Hawkethorne." So it happens that the loggers are led out from behind their barricade and through the gates, all ten of them guarded by Sanders, Garth and twenty militiamen through the trails of the Old Forest. Sanders lends you a shoulder to lean on, and Garth [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|lugs his son's bloody body like a sack of potatoes all the way back. Despite his age, he doesn't appear winded by the burden in the least, despite Garret's meaty bulk.|leads Garret on as well. Garret's found some ill-fitting clothes to cover himself with for the trek home, and there's a distinct cold silence between father and son for the whole trip back.] With Sanders forging a path through the forest with his powers, the emerald tip of his staff glowing to light the way, the trip home is fairly uneventful. From there on out, it's only a few hours until the lot of you are back at the gates of Hawkethorne. The guards look almost relieved to see everyone back — almost as if they'd been entertaining the thought that the small militia group might not even return. Job done, the militiamen and loggers alike begin dispersing one by one, returning to their homes until it's just you, Sanders, Garth and Garret. [flags.DOG_DAYS_GARRET_RESCUED|"Leave the boy with me," Sanders tells Garth. "I'll work on him tonight." Garth looks uncertain of that. "He'll live. Bitches dig scars — he'll have plenty after today." "That may be true, but you're too hard on him." Garth bares his teeth ever so slightly. "Hey, Sanders. I know you mean well, but don't you tell me how to raise my son, especially when you don't have one of your own." "Telling you how to raise Garret has nothing to do with it. It's the simple truth. Are you going to let me see to him, or not?" Both men stare at each other for a tense moment, a invisible duel of wills being played out, and at last Garth relents. "Here, take the big lunk. I'll come around in the morning to pick him up." With that, Garth shrugs off the comatose Garret off his shoulder and into Brother Sanders' embrace. The latter catches poor Garret without so much as flinching, and sighs at one of the gate guards. "Would you please help me get Garret to the chapel?" The gate guard looks to his friend for confirmation, and upon receiving it, moves off with Sanders, Garret hoisted between the both of them. After they've disappeared in the direction of the town square, Garth takes a few steps in the direction of the Frost Hound, then stops. "[pc.name]." Yes? "Sorry about all this. Being beaten down is never fun. You okay there?" Well, your tongue is still kinda numb and tingly, and admittedly you've felt better, but you don't think you're in any danger of giving up the ghost at the moment. "Go on, then — go get some sleep. Everyone knows a good night's rest in an inn will fix everything wrong with you. I'll see you in the morning. [party.has brint|Help me out will you please, Brint? I'll get you sorted once I'm done with [pc.name].]" That is... sounding quite good, actually. You're still a little shaky and wobbly, so Garth helps you all the way back to the Frost Hound and up the stairs to your room, where you quickly dump the few things the druidess didn't steal from you to the ground and are asleep before your head hits the pillow. |"So, a would-be hero ending up needing rescuing himself." "Get off my back, old man. It's not like you didn't send [pc.name] after me." "[pc.name] at least has proven [pc.himHer]self more capable than you already, even if what happened today proves that [pc.heShe] still has some ways to go. You, on the other hand..." Garret grunts. "Old man, I don't want to do this out in the open. You want to kick up dirt, wait until we're indoors before starting, okay?" "Hmph. Fine." Sanders glances at father and son and shakes his head, pulling you aside. "As much as I expected. Allow me to help you back, [pc.name]. You don't look too hearty.[party.has brint| Brint, would you mind please helping me? You're heading there too, after all.]" After the trek back through the Old Forest? Yeah, you're pretty bushed. Could do with a long nap, too. The expression on your face tells Sanders all he needs to know — taking you by the hand, he leads you on a slightly roundabout route back to the Frost Hound, well away from Garth and Garret. Helping you up the stairs to your room, the kindly priest drops you off at the door and bids you a good night before leaving. Somewhere deep within the Frost Hound, there's a raucous caucus going on, but you're too exhausted to care anymore. It's but a moment for you to toss aside what little the druidess didn't steal off you, and you're asleep before your head hits the pillow.] "

rows.original: Without its mistress around to stay its hand, the druidess' pet warg has devolved into a bestial, frenetic rage; it's simply too much for you to withstand. Sensing weakness, it leaps atop you, and the last thing you feel is a sharp pain as it rips your throat out with its jaws. Your adventure and your life end here.
rows.translation: 没有了女主人约束它的行为，女德鲁伊的宠物座狼已经彻底陷入野兽般的疯狂暴怒；这种狂暴对你来说根本无法承受。它察觉到你的虚弱，猛地扑到你身上，你最后感受到的，是它用下颚撕开你喉咙时的一阵剧痛。 你的冒险与你的生命都在此终结。
rows.raw: " Without its mistress around to stay its hand, the druidess' pet warg has devolved into a bestial, frenetic rage; it's simply too much for you to withstand. Sensing weakness, it leaps atop you, and the last thing you feel is a sharp pain as it rips your throat out with its jaws. Your adventure and your life end here."

rows.original: [var0 |Unable to fight any longer, the druidess collapses insensate to the ground besides her downed pet. [lastStanding.resDefeated |A few violent orgasms wrack her body, sending her squirming in the muck as her body deals with all the pent-up unrequited desire, then she's well and truly out. ] |Snarling and yipping, the warg circles its mistress with determined fury, even though its unsteady gait makes it clear it's on its last legs by now. [party.has arona |Scowling, Arona strides up and plants the handle of her hammer directly between the beast's eyes. There's a sharp crack, it yelps, and falls insensate to the ground. "Damned animals." That looked pretty professional. Does she have a lot of experience with wargs? "I guess. Some of the southern orc tribes keep them as war mounts — I personally don't see the benefit in it. They stink, they slobber all over the place, and worst of all, try to hump anything and everything. You can get more mileage with less of a fuss out of an ordinary steppe or plains horse. "Now that that's done with, how about we see to the plunder, eh?" |This is going to be unpleasant, but someone's got to do it. Swiftly stepping up to the warg, you plant the handle of your [pc.weapon] on the animal's head. It whines, then collapses insensate beside its mistress. Psh. One way or the other, that's that. You stand there for a second or two, catching your breath and letting the fire of battle die from your veins. ] ] Yep, time to loot the body, as the saying goes. [pc.isChamp |You feel a bit like a common criminal, rummaging through the druidess' armored robes, but it's not as if she was the most saintly of types to terrorize an unarmed logging camp. |There's no sense in being squeamish here — the spoils of battle are what they are. Finders keepers, losers weepers, so on and so forth. ] Maybe losing a few things here and there will teach her not to bully ordinary folk like that. Now to see — while you aren't going to be using the armored robes — there's no way you can make those fit — there's the matter of the druidess' bow, fallen in the dirt beside her. Even though you might not be the most learned in pale elf artifacts, you can instantly tell that it's a work of art and just as functional as it's beautiful. [party.has etheryn |"Are you sure we should be taking this, [pc.name]? It seems... wrong to rob a whitewood bow from its owner." Is there some kind of "only the rightful wielder can use this weapon" clause attached to it or something? "Well, no..." Then what's the problem? Sure it's got plenty of cultural significance, but it's clear the druidess was abusing it to terrorize Westbank. That's a pretty good argument for confiscating it, yes? Etheryn still doesn't look too happy about the prospect, but doesn't voice any more objections. That suits you just fine. ] Rummaging through her pockets, you also find a large iron keyring with a single tarnished key hanging from it. This looks to be about the right size and shape to fit the lock to Garret's cage; wasting no time, you hurry over to the hall and practically kick the door down as you barge in. "Whoa, hey," Garret mutters, looking up from the doggy dish in his cage. "What's the big hurry?" You say nothing, simply dangling the keyring before you. That gets Garret's attention well enough; he's instantly up and on his feet, worrying the cage door. "You got it! C'mon, let me out already!" Right, right. It takes a little effort to turn the key and for a moment you fear it might snap off in the lock, but the tumblers creak and the bolt slides back. Garret practically bounds out of the cage, slamming the door open and trampling his little doggy dish to pieces in his haste to finally be free. "Gods above, that was better out than in!" He groans, flexes his limbs in a bid to work the kinks out of them, then gives you a weak grin. "Many thanks, [pc.name]. I hope you gave the elf witch a good beating in my stead." You don't know if it was a good beating, but it certainly was a beating. "That'll have to do, I guess. Come on, let's get out of here. I want to get myself some clothes, and we should probably get everyone out of here before she comes to." Good idea. Come on, it's time to leave. On your way out, though, you spy the fallen druidess and her warg where you left them — while it feels otherwise, it hasn't been that long, and she clearly hasn't had the wherewithal to pull herself and her pet together and leave. [pc.isDK |Well, maybe if she didn't want to be beaten down she shouldn't have tried to hold people hostage without so much as explaining herself or making demands |You might have felt sorry for her, but on the other hand she was taking hostages and going about it all wrong without even bothering to make demands or letting the loggers know what she wanted ]. As Garret meanders off, though, an idea enters your mind as you look between him and the druidess. Maybe... maybe it'd be worth it to give her a taste of her own medicine, see how she likes it being made impotent and helpless at the mercy of another. [pc.isDK |No need to feel bad about it in the least — she forced herself upon Garret, even if he claims that he gave himself up willingly to protect the loggers. There was still duress there, after all, and Garret's enough of a meathead that he probably lied about giving himself up to save face in front of you. |Such a thing might make you squeamish about forcing yourself on her... but these are extenuating circumstances. The druidess did force herself upon Garret — even if he did claim that he gave himself up to protect the loggers from her wrath, he's enough of a meathead that he'd lie about it to save face ]. Either way, maybe if she experienced first-hand what she made others feel like, the druidess might reconsider doing the same to others down the line. [pc.isChamp |...Or at least, that's your justification. ] Well, will you do it? If you do, you can decide exactly what you want to do with the druidess after the fact. Otherwise, it'd be just as easy to keep on walking and pretend nothing's ever happened.
rows.translation: [var0 |再也无力继续战斗，这位女德鲁伊瘫倒在地，失去了意识，她的宠物也同样倒下了。 [lastStanding.resDefeated |几阵剧烈的性高潮让她全身抽搐，在泥泞中不断挣扎，她的身体正在释放那些积压已久、却未能得到释放的渴望，最终，她彻底放松了下来。 ] |这只野兽咆哮着、尖叫着，以极其狂怒的状态围着它的主人转圈，尽管它那不稳的步态清楚地表明，它已经筋疲力尽了。 [party.has arona |阿罗娜怒目而视，大步走上前，将她的锤子柄狠狠地砸在那头野兽的双眼之间。随着一声清脆的断裂声，那头野兽发出惨叫，随即昏厥在地。 该死的动物。 看起来挺专业的。她在处理这类事情上经验丰富吗？ 我想是吧。一些南方的兽人部落会把它们当作战马来使用——不过我个人并不觉得这样做有什么好处。这些动物味道难闻，还会到处流口水，最糟糕的是，它们会试图对任何东西都发起攻击。相比之下，使用普通的草原马匹反而会更省力、更方便。 现在既然那就是事情都办妥了，我们现在去把那些战利品处理掉吧，怎么样？ |这可能会让人不太舒服，但是某人的必须得这么做。你迅速走上战台，将武器的把手[pc.weapon]动物痛苦地哀鸣着，然后昏倒在主人的身旁。 呼…… 不管怎样，事情已经结束了。你站在那里，歇上一两分钟，喘口气，让战斗带来的激动情绪逐渐平息下来。 ] ] 没错，正如俗话所说，是时候抢夺那些战利品了。 [pc.isChamp |你觉得自己有点像个普通的罪犯，正在翻找那位女德鲁伊的铠甲，但毕竟她也不是什么圣洁的人物，竟然会去恐吓一个手无寸铁的伐木营地。 |在这里斤斤计较实在没有意义——战利品就是这样的，谁捡到就归谁，没捡到的人就只能自认倒霉吧。 ]或许失去一些东西会让她明白，不应该那样欺负普通人。 现在看看吧——既然你不会使用那些铠甲，那它们肯定穿不上去；还有那位德鲁伊的女弓，就掉在她身旁的泥土里。虽然你可能对苍白精灵的工艺品了解不多，但你也立刻能看出，那是一件艺术品，既美观又实用。 [party.has etheryn |你确定我们应该选择这个吗？ [pc.name]看来……从它的主人手中抢走一把白木弓，似乎有点不妥。 这种武器是不是附带了“只有合法的持有者才能使用它”这样的限制条件呢？ 嗯，不是吧…… 那么问题出在哪里呢？当然，这个物品具有重要的文化意义，但很明显，那位女德鲁伊是利用它来恐吓西岸地区的居民。因此，没收这个物品确实是一个合理的理由，对吧？ 伊瑟琳对此仍然显得不太满意，但也没有再提出任何反对意见。这样对你来说已经足够了。 ] 在你翻她的口袋时，还找到了一個大的铁钥匙扣，上面挂着一把已经生锈的钥匙。这把钥匙的大小和形状看起来正好适合用来打开加雷特笼子的锁；你没有浪费任何时间，立刻跑到大厅，一脚把门踢开，冲了进去。 哇，嘿，加雷特从笼子里的食盆中抬起头，低声说道。急什么呀？ 你什么也没说，只是把钥匙扣悬在面前。这一举动立刻吸引了加雷特的注意；他立刻站了起来，开始焦急地查看笼子的门。 你做到了！快吧，让我出来吧！ 对，对。转动钥匙确实需要费一点力气，有那么一瞬间你会担心钥匙会在锁里折断，但锁芯终于转动了，门闩也滑了回去。加雷特几乎是从笼子里冲了出来，他猛地推开门，急切地想要获得自由，结果把他的小狗用的碗踩得粉碎。 天啊，这样反而比原来更好了！他呻吟着，活动着手足，试图缓解僵硬的感觉，然后勉强挤出一个微笑。非常感谢， [pc.name]希望你能代我好好教训那个精灵女巫。 你根本不知道那是否是不错虽然过程有些艰难，但结果确实令人满意。a击败。 我想，这样也行吧。快，我们离开这里吧。我需要去拿些衣服，而且在我们等她来的时候，最好把所有人都带出去。 好主意。快吧，该出发了。 然而，在你离开的路上，你看到了那位倒下的女德鲁伊以及她的宠物——虽然感觉上好像过了很长时间，但实际上并没有，显然她还没有办法让自己和她的宠物一起离开这里。 [pc.isDK |嗯，也许如果她不想被人揍的话，就不应该在不说明原因也不提出任何要求的情况下试图劫持别人当人质。 |你或许会为她感到同情，但另一方面，她劫持了人质，而且处理整个事情的方式完全错误——她甚至都没有提出任何要求，也没有让那些伐木工人知道她到底想要什么。 ]然而，当加雷特渐渐走远时，你脑海中突然浮现了一个念头：或许……或许让她尝到自己种下的苦果也是值得的，看看她究竟会如何忍受自己变得无能、陷入他人的摆布之中。 [pc.isDK |你完全没有必要为此感到内疚——她其实是强行将自身强加给了加雷特，即使他声称自己是自愿放弃自己的，只是为了保护那些伐木工人们。毕竟，这其中还是存在强迫的成分，而加雷特又是个足够愚蠢的人，他很可能为了在你面前保全面子而撒了谎。 |这种事情可能会让你觉得强迫她做某事有些过分……但在这种情况下，这些理由确实可以成为借口。那位女德鲁伊确实强迫加雷特做了那件事——尽管他后来声称自己是出于保护伐木工人们免受她的报复才那么做的，但他的性格实在太愚蠢了，甚至会为了保全面子而撒谎。 ]无论如何，如果这位德鲁伊女巫能够亲身体验自己让他人感受到的那些情绪，或许她以后就不会再对别人做出同样的事了。 [pc.isChamp |……或者至少，你是这么为自己辩解的。 ] 那么，你愿意这么做吗？如果你愿意，之后你就可以完全按照自己的意愿来决定如何处理那位德鲁伊女巫了。否则，继续走下去，装作什么都没发生，也同样容易啊。

You want the lot of them? Take them! I'll be glad to be away from this place." With that, Hethia pulls out a large iron keyring and tosses it at your feet, then leaps on her warg. A sharp nudge on the beast's head, and both druidess and mount are gone, leaving you wondering just what happened there — — Oh, you know all right. You pissed her off just a little too much. Well, that could've gone worse than it did... it really sucks that you made that many gaffes, though. Next time you get your foot stuck in your mouth repeatedly, the consequences might be more dire. For now, though, you have the keyring — and on it is a single key that looks like it might fit the lock on Garret's cage. No time to waste, then — you want to be out of here before night truly sets in.
rows.translation: 当赫希娅突然向前冲来时，你不由自主地后退了一步。有那么一瞬间，你怀疑她是否要攻击你，甚至考虑是否该伸手去[pc.weapon]但她深吸一口气，让自己平静下来。 如果我不再浪费时间陪你了，还请见谅。 [pc.race]这纯粹是徒劳无功的举动。 什么？ 现在我明白了，那些寿命短暂的人们通常没有注意自己说话内容的习惯，但即便如此，我也没想到一个表面上试图进行谈判的人会如此迟钝。你想要他们所有人吗？那就拿去吧！我只要能离开这个地方，就心满意足了。 说着，赫希娅掏出一个巨大的铁钥匙扣，扔到了你的脚边，然后跳上了她的坐骑。她轻轻一拨坐骑的头部，这位女德鲁伊和她的坐骑便消失得无影无踪，让你不禁疑惑：刚才究竟发生了什么…… — 哦，你心里应该很清楚。你确实把她惹恼了……不过，事情本可能更糟的……你犯了那么多错，真的挺糟糕的。下次如果你再屡次说错话，后果可能会更加严重。 不过，你现在有了这个钥匙扣——上面有一把钥匙，看起来应该能配得上加雷特笼子上的锁。那就没有时间可以浪费了——你必须在夜幕真正降临之前离开这里。

rows.original: Yes. Perhaps now the two of you can talk. "You want the loggers, right?" Yes, you do; you'll take them off her hands so that she can hurry back and check up on her own. But first, though — you'd like Hethia to make good on her promise earlier on and tell you about the druids leaving the Winter City. "It's a long story," Hethia says with a sigh. She finds a flat-topped rock by the riverside, sits down on it, and gestures for her pet warg to curl up at her feet while you take a seat a respectful distance away from her. "Well, longer than most. "I know you shorter-lived peoples have your own stories of the Godswar. Before that, though, the Pale Elves followed the teachings of the Old Wyld, the primordial force of the natural world, represented by the moon and sun, the feminine and masculine, embodied in the figure of the Wyld Tree. For millennia, these teachings guided the growth of the Winter City and its lands; once, the very land now overrun with the wolf-folk belonged to the pale elves. "Then happened a couple of substandard queens, a military setback and the sudden arrival of the wraiths and their minions, plundering and murdering as they pleased. It took fifty whole years until the queen at that time — Alissa's, the current queen's grandmother — rebuilt the army, fought back the wraiths, and reunified the realm. But it was never the same. Too many of us, long to live and slow to breed, had died. Cities now had to build high walls to defend themselves, trade routes had been destroyed, the whole administration had to be rebuilt from scratch. "All that was taken care of, especially by the Queen, who was very much interested in how to run a government. But still, as much as she reformed the army and the administration, the virtue of the pale elves, the real power of the Winter City, that was over. Having tasted the rotten fruit of the wraiths' temptations, they found it too sweet to bear going without for long. "We druids knew that, and we all wanted to do something to get it back. To fix the Winter City, to bring it back to its golden era. Pale elves used to be virtuous, strong, hard-working, and just. Not anymore. The pale elves born of the Godswar were a fickle bunch, interested in frivolous sex, in spacious entertainments, in spectator sports. We have almost no literary works from that period; they appeared to be uninterested in producing any. Nor did they care to breed and form families to replace the dead from the war. The whole society was a wreck. The few of us who still remembered the Old Wyld wanted to fix this desperately, to use the power of the state to bring the pale elves back to their virtuous, frugal and wise past, when women fought for their people, cared to learn about the mysteries of existence, and took care of their husbands and children. But none of those efforts worked. "What happened? Another religion originating from the far south, that of the Belhar Empire, with alien teachings, alien ideas, alien precepts that nevertheless managed to seize the minds of the Winter City. It grew by preaching to men, to the poor, to slaves, to all manner of disaffected people. Instead of the unified whole of the Old Wyld, it preached of seven different deities, each with their own portfolios. "As much as the Winter City needed reform, nobody desired this kind of reform. To replace the wisdom of the Old Wyld with the suspicious history of some southlanders, to promote this pantheon of knowable deities whom one could meet and converse with instead of the gradual, esoteric secrets of the Old Wyld revealed over millennia. The history of the Winter City was being wiped out before our eyes, the time before the Godswar being reduced to a blank, empty slate, lost forever to memory. 'This is madness,' we said to ourselves. 'The Winter City has to wake up. We can't let this happen.' "But it happened. The Winter City never woke up; we went to the Queen, and in doing so, learned the truth. In exchange for the power to fight the wraiths, she had made a deal with this goddess named Lumia, had sworn sacred oaths to her, and the price of this foreign goddess' aid was to turn the pale elves as a people to her worship. I don't blame the Queen; she was a pragmatic woman who just wanted a stable land that obeyed her commands. As soon as we were gone from the Winter City, Queen declared worship of the seven Living Gods to be the official religion of the pale elves, and that was that." Having finished her tale, Hethia sinks back down into her seat and licks her dry lips. "The Old Wyld is not exactly a god as the Seven are. It is a force, rather than an entity. It does not live or die depending on how many people believe in it, just as the sun will not cease to exist if one spends their entire lives underground. But the time of it influencing any kind of civilization has passed, at least for now." You see. "Do you, now? [pc.name], you may be the first outsider in a long while to hear this tale, and yet... no." Hethia appears to be thinking. "Well, if you're willing to assume responsibility for these people, then I leave the loggers in your care. The spell will quickly fade once I depart." And Garret? "The would-be hero?" Hethia smiles a thin, dry smile, shakes her head, then tosses you a large iron keyring with a single key on it. "Well, he has a fine doggy dick, but you're welcome to have sloppy seconds if you like. Remember to feed him twice daily and change the water in his bowl thrice." You're glad this meeting could come to a peaceable end. You didn't want to have to fight her. "I wouldn't have held back." You'd have expected no less. "In that case, I suppose this is it. You'll handle the loggers, won't you?" This camp is clearly done for — you'll take them safely through the forest. "If you could get through the wards I put up, you can do that just fine. I'll be off, then. Safe travels, and perhaps we'll meet again." The way she said that last bit, it's almost as if she was certain of it. "The Old Wyld tells me as much, [pc.name]. Now, I must be off." Levering herself off her seat, Hethia hops astride her warg with an easy leap and settles in on its back. Turning back to give you a nod, the druidess gives her mount's head a gentle pat, and they're off towards the gates, leaving you behind in a matter of moments. No time to lose, then. Time to get Garret.
rows.translation: 好的。也许现在你们两个可以谈谈了。 你是想要那些伐木工，对吧？ 没错，你就应该这么做；你得从她手中接过那些东西，这样她才能赶紧回去照顾自己。不过在此之前——你希望赫希娅能履行她之前的承诺，告诉你关于那些离开冬城的德鲁伊们的情况。 这是个漫长的故事。赫希娅叹了口气说道。她在河边找了一块平顶的石头坐下，然后示意她的宠物战兽蜷缩在她的脚边，而你则在她稍远的地方找了个地方坐下来。嗯，比大多数人都长。 我知道你们这些寿命较短的人类也有自己关于神战的故事。但在那之前，苍白精灵们遵循的是古老荒野的教诲——那种源自自然界的原始力量，以月亮和太阳为代表，象征着阴与阳，而这种力量则通过荒野之树的形象得以体现。数千年来，这些教诲一直指引着冬城的发展及其周边地区；曾经，如今被狼人族占据的这片土地，也属于苍白精灵们。 随后，出现了几位能力不足的女王，军队也遭遇了挫折，而那些幽灵及其爪牙突然降临，为非作歹，肆意掠夺和杀戮。直到五十年后，当时的女王——也就是现任女王的祖母——才重新组建了军队，击退了那些幽灵，重新统一了整个王国。但一切都已不复从前。我们中有太多人，因为寿命过长而繁殖能力低下，最终死去。如今，城市们不得不修建高墙来保护自己，贸易路线也被破坏了，整个行政体系也必须从头开始重建。 所有这些问题都得到了解决，尤其是女王的努力——她对如何运作政府充满了兴趣。然而，尽管她对军队和行政系统进行了改革，但苍白精灵们的品性，以及冬城的真正实力，却依然无法改变。那些被幽灵的诱惑所影响的人，一旦尝到了这种甜头，就再也无法忍受没有它们的生活了。 我们德鲁伊们深知这一点，也都决心要采取行动来改变这一现状。我们要修复冬城，让它重新恢复昔日的辉煌。曾经的苍白精灵们是高尚、强大、勤奋且公正的种族，但如今已不再如此。那些在神战之后诞生的苍白精灵们变得反复无常，他们热衷于无聊的享乐、奢华的娱乐活动以及观赏性的体育运动。那个时期，我们几乎没有任何文学作品；看来他们根本对创作这类作品不感兴趣。他们也不愿意繁衍后代、建立家庭，来弥补战争中失去的人。整个社会已经陷入混乱。我们这些还记得古老荒野的人，迫切地想要改变这种状况，希望利用国家的力量，让这些苍白精灵重新回到他们过去那种善良、节俭且智慧的生活状态——那时，女性会为自己的族群奋斗，热衷于探索存在的奥秘，也会悉心照料自己的丈夫和孩子。但是，这些努力都没有取得任何效果。 发生了什么？又有一种源自遥远南方的宗教出现了，那就是贝尔哈尔帝国的宗教。它宣扬着外来的教义、观念和准则，但却成功吸引了冬城的民众。这种宗教通过向普通人、穷人、奴隶以及所有那些对现状不满的人传播教义而逐渐发展起来。与古老的荒野所代表的统一信仰不同，它推崇七位不同的神明，每一位神明都拥有自己独特的职责和信徒群体。 尽管冬城确实需要改革，但没有人希望看到这样的改革。用一些南方人那些充满疑点的历史来取代古老荒野所蕴含的智慧，推崇那些可以被人们见到、可以与他们交谈的神明，而不是让人们逐渐去领悟那些历经千年才被揭示出来的古老荒野的神秘奥秘——冬城的历史正在我们眼前被抹去，神战之前的那段历史也被彻底抹得一干二净，永远地从人们的记忆中消失了。 这太疯狂了，”我们暗自心想，“冬城必须醒悟过来，我们不能让这种事情发生。 但事情就是发生了。冬城再也没有苏醒过；我们找到了女王，也因此了解到了真相。为了获得对抗那些幽灵的力量，她与一位名叫卢米娅的女神达成了协议，向她立下了神圣的誓言。而这位外来女神所提供的帮助，代价就是让那些苍白精灵全体转而崇拜她。我并不责怪那位女王；她只是一个务实的女性，只是希望自己的国家能够安定下来，人们能够服从她的命令。我们一离开冬城，女王就宣布将七位生神作为苍白精灵的官方宗教，事情就这样定了下来。" 讲完故事后，赫希娅重新坐回座位上，舔了舔干裂的嘴唇。老荒野并不像那七神那样属于真正的神灵。它更是一种力量，而非一个有实体的存在。它的存在与否并不取决于有多少人信仰它，就如同一个人即使终其一生都生活在地下，太阳也不会因此而停止运转一样。不过，至少目前来说，它已经不再能够对任何文明产生影响了。 你瞧。 你现在才这么说吗？ [pc.name]，你可能是很长时间以来第一个听到这个故事的外人，然而……并非如此。赫希娅似乎在思考着什么。好吧，如果你愿意为这些人负责的话，那我就把这些伐木工交给你照顾了。等我离开后，那个咒语很快就会失效的。 那加雷特呢？ 那个自封的英雄？赫希娅露出一个干涩而勉强的微笑，摇了摇头，然后扔给你一个只有一把钥匙的铁制钥匙扣。嗯，他的阴茎确实挺大的，不过如果你喜欢的话，也可以尝尝剩下的部分。记得每天喂他两次饭，还要每天换三次他水碗里的水。 你很高兴这次会议能够和平结束。你本来并不想和她发生争执。 我当时是不会犹豫的。 这也正是你所能预料到的。 那样的话，我想事情就到此为止了吧。你会负责处理那些伐木工人的，对吧？ 这个营地显然是为这个目的而设立的——你可以安全地带领他们穿过森林。 如果你能突破我设置的防御屏障，那你肯定能做到。那么我就先走了。祝你们一路顺风，也许我们还会再见面。 她说最后那句话的方式，让人觉得她几乎是对此深信不疑的。 老野地也告诉了我同样的事情， [pc.name]现在，我必须离开了。赫希娅从座位上站起身来，轻松地跳上她的坐骑，稳稳地坐到了它的背上。她回头向你点了点头，然后轻轻拍了拍坐骑的头部，接着他们便朝着城门方向飞驰而去，不一会儿就离开了你。 那么，没有时间可以浪费了。是时候去救加雷特了。

rows.original: Upon hearing this, Hethia stares at you ineffably, clearly trying to read you while on the defensive. You'd like to imagine she's getting nothing from you, but overconfidence is how so many've met their demise. "What's it to you? Trying to find a weakness you can exploit?" No, no. But since you're trying to parley here, it's only natural that you'd try to see her side of the issue as well, right? You have to understand where she's coming from if you're to come to a peaceful resolution here, and you can't do that if you don't understand who she is. Hethia considers your words, keeping that cold, steely gaze fixed on you. Hey, she doesn't have to say anything she doesn't want to. But you'd rather try to make some inroads towards understanding her than to make a gaffe later on. Hopefully she can try and meet you halfway. She can speak; you'll stay quiet and hear her out until she's done. "Very well. My full name and title is Hethia Runasdottir, servant to the Old Wyld, grower of the first circle. This probably means little to you, [pc.race], but it was once a position of some import amongst the pale elves of the Winter City. This all changed when —"
rows.translation: 听到这些话，赫希娅用一种难以言喻的眼神盯着你，显然是在试图读懂你的心思，同时也在保持警惕。你可能会认为她根本无法从你这里得到任何信息，但过度自信往往是许多人失败的原因。 这关你什么事？是在试图找出可以利用的弱点吗？ 不，不是这样的。但既然你在这里试图进行协商，那么你自然也会尝试了解她的立场，对吧？如果你想找到一个和平的解决方案，就必须理解她的想法和立场，而如果你不了解她是谁，那就根本无法做到这一点。 赫希娅仔细聆听着你的话语，那冰冷如钢铁的目光始终紧盯着你。 嘿，她完全可以选择不说出任何她不想说的话。但比起以后犯下更大的错误，你还是应该试着去了解她吧。希望她能试着与你妥协。她可以说话，而你可以保持沉默，认真听她把话说完。 很好。我的全名是赫希娅·鲁纳斯多蒂尔，我是古老荒野的仆从，也是第一圈区域的守护者。这些称呼对你来说可能没有什么意义[pc.race]但在过去，这个职位在冬城的苍白精灵中确实相当重要。然而，一切都在……之后发生了改变。
rows.raw: " Upon hearing this, Hethia stares at you ineffably, clearly trying to read you while on the defensive. You'd like to imagine she's getting nothing from you, but overconfidence is how so many've met their demise. "What's it to you? Trying to find a weakness you can exploit?" No, no. But since you're trying to parley here, it's only natural that you'd try to see her side of the issue as well, right? You have to understand where she's coming from if you're to come to a peaceful resolution here, and you can't do that if you don't understand who she is. Hethia considers your words, keeping that cold, steely gaze fixed on you. Hey, she doesn't have to say anything she doesn't want to. But you'd rather try to make some inroads towards understanding her than to make a gaffe later on. Hopefully she can try and meet you halfway. She can speak; you'll stay quiet and hear her out until she's done. "Very well. My full name and title is Hethia Runasdottir, servant to the Old Wyld, grower of the first circle. This probably means little to you, [pc.race], but it was once a position of some import amongst the pale elves of the Winter City. This all changed when —""

rows.original: Hethia glowers at you. "I thought you said you'd stay quiet and hear me out? Or are you already reneging on your words?" Whoa, whoa. You're sorry, you spoke out of turn. You just wanted to hear more, that's all. "If you wanted to hear more, you could've remained silent and not interrupted me mid-sentence. Now we've wasted more time — I understand that you short-lived peoples want to make the most out of what little of it you have, but undue haste makes for all kinds of error." Right, right. You hold out your hands placidly. Perhaps you could try getting on the right foot again? "That would be helpful, yes."
rows.translation: 赫希娅正怒视着你。我记得你说过会保持安静，听我把话说完吧？还是说，你已经违背了自己的承诺了？ 哇，等等。不好意思，你插话了。你只是想继续听而已，对吧？ 如果你想继续听下去，就应该保持沉默，不要在我说话的时候打断我。现在我们又浪费了更多的时间——我理解你们这些寿命短暂的生命体想要充分利用自己所拥有的有限时间，但过于急功近利只会带来各种错误。 对，对。你平静地伸出双手。或许你可以试着再次迈出正确的第一步吧？ 那确实会很有帮助，没错。

You hold out your hands placidly. Perhaps you could try getting on the right foot again? "That would be helpful, yes."'

rows.original: Remain quiet and observe the situation.
rows.translation: 保持安静，观察局势的发展。

rows.original: "- When those who followed the Old Wyld fell out of favor in the Winter City. "I'd not yet been born when it happened, but my mother was. After the event that you people call the Godswar, the royal line of the pale elves chose to abandon worship of the Old Wyld in favor of the deities of the Belharan Empire, who'd descended in the flesh to help combat the scourge spreading across the land. These gods, they were quick gods of the short-lived peoples, unlike the patience of the Old Wyld, which plays the long game. The pale elves demanded immediate action; the gods of the Belharan Empire gave it in the form of flashy miracles and great powers. And so it happened that the pale elves threw away the force which had guided them since their inception, and followed these new, visible gods." Hethia pauses to catch her breath, and you seize the opportunity to do some probing. So, what happened to those who still followed the Old Wyld? Were they exiled? "Not explicitly, no. But there was a sense of immense resentment and animosity towards those who were seen as having failed their people in their time of need. The few who did not convert to the ways of Belhar's Living Gods and resented the royal decree proclaiming it the new official religion of the Winter City took what little they owned and retreated into the forests. Rather than waiting for opinion to be stirred up against them in the open, they saw no reason to linger where they were no longer needed nor wanted. It's a sad story, is it not?" Hmm...
rows.translation: 当那些追随古老荒野的人在冬城失宠时…… 那件事发生的时候，我还没有出生，但我的母亲当时已经在世了。在你们称之为‘神战’的那场事件之后，苍白精灵的王室决定放弃对古老荒野的崇拜，转而信奉贝拉兰帝国的神明们——那些以凡人之躯降临人间、帮助人们对抗那场肆虐全国的灾祸的神明们。这些神明，其实是那些寿命短暂的民族所信仰的急功近利的神灵，与那些能够耐心等待、着眼长远的古老自然之力截然不同。那些苍白的精灵们要求立即得到行动；而贝拉兰帝国的神明们，则通过各种炫目的奇迹与强大的力量来回应他们的诉求。就这样，那些苍白的精灵抛弃了自诞生以来一直引导他们的力量，转而追随这些新的、可见的神明。 赫希娅停下来喘了口气，你趁机追问了一些问题：那么，那些仍然追随古老荒野的人后来怎么样了？他们被流放了吗？ 并没有明确表达出来，但人们对于那些在人们需要帮助的时候却未能履行自己的责任的人，确实怀有深深的怨恨与敌意。那些没有接受贝尔哈尔诸神的信仰，同时也反对将这种信仰定为冬城的官方宗教的统治者颁布的法令的人，便带着自己仅有的财产退入了森林之中。他们没有选择在公开场合等待别人对他们产生反对意见，因此觉得没有必要继续留在那些不再需要他们、也不欢迎他们的地方。这确实是一个令人遗憾的故事，不是吗？ 嗯……

rows.original: It must have been hard on them.
rows.translation: 这对他们来说肯定很艰难。
rows.raw: "It must have been hard on them."

rows.original: Hethia scowls at that. "And of course, there is always the assumption that the new is better than the old, without needing to compare the two at all. Because it's new — you people are obsessed with novelty, and the thrice-damned religion of the Living Gods which you brought up with you has old encouraged that infectious, destructive mindset amongst the pale elves as well." Yes, but — Hethia cuts you off with a sharp movement of a hand. "Either way, it's not exactly proper to suggest to someone who's working hard to keep alive a remnant of her people's culture and history that she should just lay down and accept it. Doubly so if you wanted to get on her good side." Oops. "I'd like to think I'm patient and magnanimous, but everyone has a limit to their patience. Please remember that before you open that mouth of yours."
rows.translation: 赫希娅听到这话后，皱起了眉头。当然，人们总是理所当然地认为新的东西一定比旧的好，甚至根本不需要去比较两者。就因为它是新的——你们人类对新鲜事物有着难以抗拒的迷恋，而你们所信奉的那些关于‘现世神祇’的教义，更是从古至今一直在苍白精灵中培养这种盲目追求新奇、破坏性的思维方式。 是的，但是——” 赫希娅突然抬手打断了你的话。无论如何，对于一个正在为传承自己族群的文化与历史而努力奋斗的人来说，建议她放弃这些努力、接受现实，这种做法实在不太合适。尤其是如果你还想赢得她的好感的话，就更不应该这样做了。 哎呀。 我总以为自己是个有耐心且宽宏大量的人，但每个人的耐心都是有限度的。所以在开口之前，请先想清楚。
