rows.translation: 旧的东西最终会被新的东西取代。事情就是这样的，不是吗？
rows.raw: "The old is eventually replaced by the new. Such is the way of things, is it not?"

rows.original: "Well? I asked you a question. Are you going to answer, or are you playing dumb?" Uh, no, you were just considering your words. "For that long? It looked as if you were just keeping silent and waiting to see what I'd do next." Well, that's not — "I really don't have time to waste here. Pale elves may be long-lived, but that doesn't mean you can waste my time as you please. Let's try to get an actual conversation going with people speaking and listening at appropriate times instead of this nonsense."
rows.translation: “怎么？我问了你一个问题。你是打算回答，还是打算装傻？” 呃，不是，你只是在斟酌自己的措辞。 “那么久？看起来你只是一直沉默着，等着看我接下来会做什么。” 呃，那不是—— “我真的没时间在这里浪费。苍白精灵或许寿命很长，但这不代表你可以随意浪费我的时间。我们还是试着来一场真正的对话吧——该说话的时候说话，该听的时候听，而不是这样胡扯。”

rows.translation: 保持安静，观察局势的发展。

rows.original: "We make do," Hethia replies. "I've known nothing else, so an existence in the forests means nothing to me. And let's be frank — a hard life molds hard people, and I'm glad to be hard, especially with the days ahead of us." Still, there is that sense of injustice... "Which will be righted if I have any say in it, but it's out of reach for now." Can she tell you more about the druids' expulsion from larger pale elf society? Hethia narrows her eyes, clearly suspicious. "Why?" Like you said, you wanted to understand where she's coming from. "You first, then." Well, your motivations are simple — a friend of yours, who has happened to be very kind to you, well — his son is amongst those trapped here, so you're here to get him and everyone back. There, that's as direct and open as you can get. "That friend must mean a lot to you for you to have come this far." He's a decent guy, yeah. You're sure Hethia herself has people for whom she would do much for, right? The druidess takes a moment to consider your question, then nods slowly. "Yes." Well? "I'll tell you later — if I'm in a good mood after this parley is done. For now, though, consider the offer taken." You appear to have gotten Hethia's interest; she may respond to various lines of questioning differently. This may be a valuable clue — for now, how do you wish to proceed?
rows.translation: 我们将就着过吧。赫希娅回答道。我一直以来都只知道这样的生活，所以对于我来说，在森林中生存根本没有任何意义。坦白说，艰苦的环境会造就坚强的人，而我很高兴自己能够变得坚强，尤其是面对前方的那些日子。 然而，那种不公平的感觉依然存在…… 如果我能参与决策的话，这个问题肯定能够得到解决，但目前还无法实现。 她能再告诉你一些关于德鲁伊们被从大型苍白精灵社会中驱逐出去的事情吗？ 赫希娅眯起了眼睛，显然充满了怀疑。为什么？ 正如你所说，你想要了解她的立场和想法是从何而来的。 你先来，然后我再做。 嗯，你的动机很简单——你的一个对你非常友好的朋友，他的儿子正好被困在了这里，所以你来到这里就是为了把他和其他人救出来。就是这样，已经说得非常直白了。 那个朋友一定对你来说非常重要，否则你不会不惜付出这么大的代价来帮助他。 他确实是个不错的家伙，没错。你确定赫希娅自己也会为某些人赴汤蹈火吧？ 这位女德鲁伊沉思片刻，然后缓缓点了点头。是的。 那么？ 等这次谈判结束后，如果我心情好的话，会告诉你答案的。不过现在，就当这个提议已经被接受了吧。 你似乎引起了赫希娅的兴趣；她对不同类型的提问可能会给出不同的反应。这或许是一个有价值的线索——那么，你现在打算如何继续呢？

Hethia narrows her eyes, clearly suspicious. "Why?" Like you said, you wanted to understand where she's coming from. "You first, then." There, that's as direct and open as you can get. "That friend must mean a lot to you for you to have come this far." He's a decent guy, yeah. You're sure Hethia herself has people for whom she would do much for, right? The druidess takes a moment to consider your question, then nods slowly. "Yes." Well? "I'll tell you later — if I'm in a good mood after this parley is done. For now, though, consider the offer taken." You appear to have gotten Hethia's interest; she may respond to various lines of questioning differently. This may be a valuable clue — for now, how do you wish to proceed?'

rows.original: Hethia grumbles and folds her arms in front of her. "Somehow, I don't really feel like explaining myself. Wyld knows that my words will be deliberately misconstrued to mean things that I never intended to convey in the first place." That's a rather unhelpful and hostile attitude to take. "So? The only things I've ever experienced from you short-lived lot is hostility. The last would-be hero tried to sneak up on Norathar and throttle her without so much as even a greeting. How do I know you even care?"
rows.translation: 赫希娅嘟囔着，双臂交叉在胸前。不知为何，我真的没有兴趣为自己辩解。Wyld很清楚，我的话肯定会被故意曲解，从而被理解为一些我根本从未想要表达的意思。 这种态度实在既无帮助，又充满敌意。 所以呢？你们这些短暂存在的东西，给我带来的只有敌意。上一个自封的英雄试图悄悄接近诺拉瑟尔，甚至都不打招呼就想要掐死她。我怎么知道你们到底有没有在乎过别人呢？

Wyld knows that my words will be deliberately misconstrued to mean things that I never intended to convey in the first place." That's a rather unhelpful and hostile attitude to take. "So? The only things I've ever experienced from you short-lived lot is hostility. The last would-be hero tried to sneak up on Norathar and throttle her without so much as even a greeting. How do I know you even care?"'

rows.original: Um, did she just forget what you just discussed? You'd think that trying to open this parley off on a right foot and trying to understand her point of view and where she's coming from would count as caring, right? If you didn't get into depth enough, it's only because she didn't want to recite history here and now! "Could be a —" No, now she's the one being blatantly hostile here. Just what will it take for her to accept that you're trying to meet her halfway here. Silence. And then. "All right, you know what? Fair's fair. You want to know why I'm still here? I'll tell you, although you'll probably be on your guard after I say as much."
rows.translation: 嗯，她难道真的忘记你们刚才讨论的内容了吗？你可能会认为，试图以一个良好的开端来展开这次谈话，试图理解她的观点和她的立场，这本身就体现出了关心和诚意，对吧？如果你没有深入了解她的想法，那只是因为她并不想在这里重提过去的事情罢了！ “可能会是……” 不，现在她才是那个公然表现出敌意的人。究竟需要什么，才能让她明白你其实是在努力与她达成妥协呢？ 沉默。然后。“好吧，你知道吗？公平就是公平。你想知道我为什么还在这里吗？我会告诉你的，不过在我说完之后，你可能会变得警惕起来。”

rows.original: It looks like Hethia is clearly highly defensive about this particular point; pushing on it when you've got no leverage is probably going to get her to clam up even tighter. Another line of questioning may prove fruitful — get her to let slip something you can use to force her to open up. Either way, smashing your head against this wall is going to be a waste of time. "Well?" Fine. Since she doesn't want to dwell on this for now, how about you try something else?
rows.translation: 看来赫希娅在这一点上表现得非常 defensive；如果你没有足够的筹码去继续追问，很可能只会让她更加闭口不言。换一种提问方式或许会更有成效——设法让她无意中透露出一些你可以利用的信息，从而迫使她开口说话。无论如何，强行在这个问题上固执己见只会浪费时间。 那么？ 好吧。既然她现在不想再纠结这件事，那你为什么不尝试别的方法呢？

"Well?" Fine. Since she doesn't want to dwell on this for now, how about you try something else?"

Another line of questioning may prove fruitful — get her to let slip something you can use to force her to open up. Either way, smashing your head against this wall is going to be a waste of time. "Well?" Fine. Since she doesn't want to dwell on this for now, how about you try something else?
rows.translation: 看来赫希娅在这一点上表现得非常 defensive；如果你没有足够的筹码去继续追问，很可能只会让她更加闭口不言。换一种提问方式或许会更有成效——设法让她无意中透露出一些你可以利用的信息，从而迫使她开口说话。无论如何，强行在这个问题上固执己见只会浪费时间。 那么？ 好吧。既然她现在不想再纠结这件事，那你为什么不尝试别的方法呢？

Another line of questioning may prove fruitful — get her to let slip something you can use to force her to open up. Either way, smashing your head against this wall is going to be a waste of time. "Well?" Fine. Since she doesn't want to dwell on this for now, how about you try something else?"

rows.original: On your guard? Why, was she doing something unsavory? Hethia harrumphs. "Perish the thought." Well then, clearly she should take some time in enlightening you. "The blizzard that night... I took it as a portent from the Old Wyld that I was to teach these loggers a lesson for disrespecting its needs and power. I... it was a portent of more than just that. While the loggers might have been callous towards me, I couldn't let the things that'd sprung up in the forest get at them." The spell, the way you seemed to end up wandering in circles when trying to approach the camp, having to constantly fight some misdirecting force — that was her? "Don't underestimate me! I may be but one woman, but my power in the Wyld is great!"
rows.translation: 保持警惕？难道她做了什么不好的事情吗？” 赫希娅哼了一声。但愿这种事永远不会发生。 那么，显然她需要花一些时间来向你解释清楚这些事情。 那个夜晚的暴风雪……我将其视为古老森林发出的预兆，它在告诉我，必须让这些无视森林需求与力量的伐木工们得到教训。不……这其实预示的远不止如此。虽然那些伐木工对我可能很冷漠，但我绝不能让森林里出现的东西伤害到他们。 那个咒语，就是当你试图接近营地时，总会不断地在原地打转，不断与那些误导你的力量战斗——原来就是她在背后搞的鬼吗？ 别小看我！虽然我只是个女人，但在荒野中，我的力量可是不容忽视的！

I took it as a portent from the Old Wyld that I was to teach these loggers a lesson for disrespecting its needs and power. I... it was a portent of more than just that. While the loggers might have been callous towards me, I couldn't let the things that'd sprung up in the forest get at them." The spell, the way you seemed to end up wandering in circles when trying to approach the camp, having to constantly fight some misdirecting force — that was her? "Don't underestimate me! I may be but one woman, but my power in the Wyld is great!"'

rows.original: You're very sorry, but does she have an issue with being underestimated? Hethia winces as if you'd reached out and actually struck her; seems like you hit a raw nerve there. Cold fire flashes in the druidess' eyes as she rounds on you. "What did you say?!" It just sounded like she was very intent on that last point there about not being underestimated. "And what does that have anything to do with the topic at hand?" Uh... you have to admit that she's right. Whether or not that was true, pointing it out has needlessly antagonized the druidess. Maybe you should back up and try again...
rows.translation: 非常抱歉，但她是否介意被人低估呢？ 赫希娅明显感到不适，仿佛你真的触到了她的痛处；看来你确实说到了她最敏感的地方。这位德鲁伊的眼睛中闪过寒光，她转身朝你走来。 你刚才说什么？！ 听起来她确实非常重视最后那一点，也就是不要被低估。 那这与我们正在讨论的主题有什么关系呢？ 呃……你得承认她是对的。不管那件事是否属实，指出这一点反而无端惹恼了那位德鲁伊女巫。也许你应该退一步，再试一次……
rows.raw: " You're very sorry, but does she have an issue with being underestimated? Hethia winces as if you'd reached out and actually struck her; seems like you hit a raw nerve there. Cold fire flashes in the druidess' eyes as she rounds on you. "What did you say?!" It just sounded like she was very intent on that last point there about not being underestimated. "And what does that have anything to do with the topic at hand?" Uh... you have to admit that she's right. Whether or not that was true, pointing it out has needlessly antagonized the druidess. Maybe you should back up and try again..."

rows.original: Remain silent and observe the situation.
rows.translation: 保持沉默，观察事态的发展。

rows.original: You hold your tongue and give Hethia a nod, encouraging her to continue. "It wasn't without effort, though. Every evening I had to commune in order to shore up my powers — such a spell is beyond the personal strength of a single druid, but the Wyld has no limits. All we have to do is to lift those which we impose upon oneself, to be the vessel instead of the source, and the Wyld will follow." And such power was insufficient for the pale elves during the Godswar? "Like I mentioned earlier, the Old Wyld is more subtle. It does not crush, it does not kill, it does not maim — at least, not outright. Its fury is terrible, but not quick. The Living Gods of Belhar had a more attractive way of doing things. Results were... more immediate." You see. "That idiot would-be hero almost ruined everything when he leapt out of nowhere and started wrestling Norathar to the ground, then thinks he's doing me some kind of favor when he chooses to let himself be locked up. I have no regrets about using him — he may not be malicious, but he's a blithering idiot." That sounds like Garret, all right. So...
rows.translation: 你忍住话头，向赫希娅点了点头，鼓励她继续说下去。 不过，这确实需要付出努力。每晚我都必须进行冥想，以增强自己的力量——这样的法术超出了单个德鲁伊的个人能力范围，但荒野之力是没有界限的。我们所要做的，就是放下那些强加给自己的束缚，成为能量的容器而非源头，那么荒野之力自然会追随我们。 而在神战期间，这样的力量对于苍白精灵们来说竟然还不够吗？ 正如我之前所说，古老荒野的惩罚方式更为隐秘。它不会直接碾碎敌人，不会立即杀死他们，也不会造成严重的伤害——至少不会如此直接地表现出来。它的愤怒确实极其可怕，但却不会迅速发作。贝尔哈尔的众神采用了一种更为巧妙的方式来施加惩罚，其效果……要来得快得多。 你瞧。 那个自以为是的蠢货，突然出现把诺拉萨尔扑倒在地，差点把一切都搞砸了。后来他还觉得自己帮了我大忙，主动选择被关起来。使用他，我一点也不后悔——他也许没有恶意，但确实是个十足的白痴。 那听起来像是加雷特，好吧。那么……

Every evening I had to commune in order to shore up my powers — such a spell is beyond the personal strength of a single druid, but the Wyld has no limits. All we have to do is to lift those which we impose upon oneself, to be the vessel instead of the source, and the Wyld will follow." And such power was insufficient for the pale elves during the Godswar? "Like I mentioned earlier, the Old Wyld is more subtle. It does not crush, it does not kill, it does not maim — at least, not outright. Its fury is terrible, but not quick. The Living Gods of Belhar had a more attractive way of doing things. Results were... more immediate." You see. "That idiot would-be hero almost ruined everything when he leapt out of nowhere and started wrestling Norathar to the ground, then thinks he's doing me some kind of favor when he chooses to let himself be locked up. I have no regrets about using him — he may not be malicious, but he's a blithering idiot." That sounds like Garret, all right. So...'

rows.original: Hethia sighs and rubs her temples. "He's just a male. Not a big deal. Besides, what was I supposed to do with him? Kill him? No. Let him loose? Knowing his sort, he'd just turn back and bother Norathar and me again — perhaps at a more critical juncture this time. No, locking him up was the only reasonable thing to do. "Besides, he seemed to like being made into the dog that he was." It's still wrong, isn't it? "So? Go through your life without doing a single morally gray thing, and let me know how far you get. In the meantime, I'll be here caring for a bunch of unappreciative loggers. A bit of dick is the smallest indulgence I could ask for, really." It doesn't look like Hethia is going to budge on the point, and arguing morals here is just wasting time and infuriating the both of you. Maybe you should try something else.
rows.translation: 赫希娅叹了口气，揉了揉太阳穴。他只不过是个男人而已，没什么大不了的。再说，我该拿他怎么办呢？杀了他吗？不行。放他走吗？以他的性格，他肯定会回来继续打扰诺拉瑟和我的——而且这次可能会在更关键的时机再次惹麻烦。所以，把他关起来才是唯一合理的做法。 此外，他似乎乐意被人塑造成他现在的这个样子。 还是不对吧？ 所以呢？如果你一辈子都不做任何有道德争议的事情，那就让我看看你能走到哪一步。而在这期间，我还是要继续照顾这些不懂得感恩的伐木工人们。说实话，偶尔犯点小错，对我来说已经是最大的宽容了。 看来赫希娅在这个问题上是不会让步的，在这里争论道德问题只会浪费时间，还会让你们俩都感到愤怒。或许你应该尝试其他方法。

Knowing his sort, he'd just turn back and bother Norathar and me again — perhaps at a more critical juncture this time. No, locking him up was the only reasonable thing to do. It doesn't look like Hethia is going to budge on the point, and arguing morals here is just wasting time and infuriating the both of you. Maybe you should try something else."

rows.original: It's still wrong to keep him locked up and use him as a dildo, though.
rows.translation: 不过，继续把他关起来并把他当作假阳具来使用，这种做法仍然是错误的。
rows.raw: "It's still wrong to keep him locked up and use him as a dildo, though."

rows.original: You don't think she's a bad person, really.
rows.translation: 你真的不认为她是个坏人，对吧？
rows.raw: "You don't think she's a bad person, really."

rows.original: "Yes?" So, you were just thinking, does she have anything else to add? "No? I wasn't about to interrupt you mid-sentence. You clearly had a thought going on there, didn't you?" Uh, yes. Hethia curls a corner of her lips. "One thing about being raised in the woods is that you learn to do away with needless social posturing and be simple — but not impolite — about things. Don't waste my time with hemming and hawing." Right, right. Now, then, could she please go over that last bit again? Hethia sighs.
rows.translation: 是吗？ 所以，你可能在想：她还有没有什么要补充的吗？ 不是吗？我本来并没有打算在你说到一半时打断你。你当时肯定在思考些什么，对吧？ 嗯，是的。 赫希娅微微勾起了嘴角。在森林中长大有这样一个好处：你会学会摒弃那些不必要的社交做作，做事时保持简洁直接——但同时也不会失礼。别用那些拐弯抹角的话来浪费我的时间。 好的，好的。那么，她能再重复一遍最后那部分内容吗？ 赫希娅叹了口气。

Hethia curls a corner of her lips. "One thing about being raised in the woods is that you learn to do away with needless social posturing and be simple — but not impolite — about things. Don't waste my time with hemming and hawing." Right, right. Now, then, could she please go over that last bit again? Hethia sighs.'

rows.original: Remain silent and observe the situation.
rows.translation: 保持沉默，观察事态的发展。

rows.original: Yes, indeed. Tilting her head ever so slightly to one side, Hethia gives you a quizzical look. "Do explain. So far, everyone I've met of you people has been rather antagonistic towards me; I'd love to hear this." Well, she admitted as much herself, didn't she? Firstly, she insinuated that she didn't really mean to hurt anyone, even if she'd meant to teach them a lesson. "Hmph. It's true that there were... unforeseen complications. But they also couldn't understand the importance of keeping esoteric knowledge, well, esoteric. Still, that hardly makes me a good person, does it? I mean, I did cause a whole lot of trouble, or at least, in their eyes. Certainly that dog of a hero thought as much." That's not all. You're guessing that she's got other fellow druids in the Old Forest, doesn't she? A lesser person would have abandoned the loggers despite the situation she put them in, and gone to see to her own. She didn't have to stay here and use her magics to protect them until help came — and despite their animosity, too. If that doesn't prove that she's not as bad as others make her out to be, you don't know what does. At last, for the first time since you've shown yourself to her, Hethia smiles — just a little. "I suppose I can't deny your flattery, um... did I ask your name again?" It's [pc.name]. "[pc.name]. All right, you know what? I think we can talk."
rows.translation: 确实如此。 赫希娅微微将头偏向一侧，用一种充满疑惑的眼神看着你。请解释一下。到目前为止，我遇到的你们这些人几乎都对我很敌对；我很想听听其中的原因。 嗯，她自己也是这么承认的，不是吗？首先，她暗示自己其实并没有想要伤害任何人，即使她本来是想给他们一个教训。 哼，确实出现了一些……意想不到的麻烦。但他们也不明白保护那些深奥知识的重要性，毕竟那些知识确实很深奥。不过，这难道就能说明我是个好人吗？我的意思是，我确实惹了很多麻烦，至少在他们看来是这样。那个该死的英雄肯定也是这么认为的。 不仅如此。你大概也在猜，她在古林里还有其他的德鲁伊同伴吧？换作一个普通的人，面对这样的处境，早就抛弃那些伐木工们，自己去照顾自己的同伴了。她却选择留在这里，运用自己的魔法保护他们，直到救援到来——尽管那些伐木工们对她怀有敌意。如果这还不能证明她并没有别人所说的那么坏，那你就真不知道什么才能证明了。 终于，在你第一次出现在她面前之后，赫希娅露出了微笑——虽然只是微微一笑而已。我想，我确实无法否认你的奉承话……嗯，我是不是又问过你的名字了？ 是[pc.name]。 "[pc.name]好吧，你知道吗？我觉得我们可以谈谈。

"I suppose I can't deny your flattery, um... did I ask your name again?" It's [pc.name]. "[pc.name]. All right, you know what? I think we can talk.""

rows.original: You take a few seconds to gather your thoughts and study the druidess before speaking. Judging by the situation, it looks like Hethia is rather on edge, and though she's trying not to show it, running a little ragged, too. Keeping to the spirit of the parley and not deliberately antagonizing her should be quite obvious, but insincere flattery is probably not going to do much for you, either. [pc.cunningRange 60|Judging by her race — the already fairly insular pale elves — and that she's probably had nothing but grief from those outside her little druidic circle, you suspect that Hethia might need a little warming to before she'll properly answer your questions. Your intuition suggests that she isn't really a bad person, but you need to wrangle the exact reason for why she's doing what she's doing and to get her to admit as much herself.]
rows.translation: 你花了几秒钟整理思绪，仔细观察那位德鲁伊女祭司，才开口说话。从目前的情形来看，赫希娅显然处于紧张状态，虽然她努力掩饰，但依然显得有些慌乱。遵循谈判的原则，避免故意激怒她，这一点应该是显而易见的；不过，虚伪的奉承恐怕也不会对她产生什么效果。 [pc.cunningRange 60|从她的种族来看——那些本来就相当封闭、与世隔绝的苍白精灵——再加上她很可能在她的那小圈德鲁伊同伴之外，只经历过悲伤与痛苦，你大概会认为，赫希娅可能需要一些温和的引导，才能真正回答你的问题。你的直觉告诉你，她其实并不是一个坏人，但你需要弄清楚她之所以会做出那些行为，究竟是出于什么原因，并且要让她自己承认这一点。]

Your intuition suggests that she isn't really a bad person, but you need to wrangle the exact reason for why she's doing what she's doing and to get her to admit as much herself.]"

rows.original: Can Hethia tell you more about herself?
rows.translation: 赫希娅能再向你介绍一下自己吗？
rows.raw: "Can Hethia tell you more about herself?"

rows.original: Why's Hethia in the camp? What's going on here?
rows.translation: 赫希娅为什么会在营地里？这里到底发生了什么？
rows.raw: "Why's Hethia in the camp? What's going on here?"

rows.original: "Hm? What is it?" You explain that you need to speak with him about the situation at Westbank. "Right. Garth and I are gathering the militia to mount an expedition. If you'd like to join —" No, no, not that. You quickly explain the situation at Westbank to Sanders, giving the old priest the salient details of what you've managed to learn. He listens intently, his brow furrowing as he sits in one of the pews to consider your words, then is silent for a long while. "It's good that Garret and the loggers are unharmed, in body if nothing else. But this elf druidess you speak of..." Garret had suggested that she could be reasoned with. And since both she and Sanders serve the natural world in some fashion... at the very least, you think he'd have a better chance trying to talk her down than you would. [party.has etheryn|"I-I'm not completely sure about that," Etheryn says, most uncharacteristically butting into your conversation. "Pardon me, but it may make things worse..." Sanders raises an eyebrow. "How so, child?" "You serve the Living Gods; Velun to be precise. This druidess almost certainly serves the Old Wyld. When the Royal Family converted to worship of the Living Gods after the Godswar, most of pale elf society followed in their stead — the few who still remained faithful to the Old Wyld and the symbol of the Wyld Tree left the Winter City of their own accord... "Needless to say, there was, and still is, resentment from those who still practice the old faith." Sanders nods. "I'll have to keep that in mind, child, but it won't prevent me from trying." "If you're so determined..." Etheryn looks like she has more to say, but can't work up the nerve to voice it. ] "To be honest, [pc.name], I'm glad you came to me for help. If we can avoid wasting everyone's time, and perhaps even a life or two on an unnecessary confrontation, that'd be ideal. That, and I do have a more personal stake than most in the outcome, especially in light of what you've told me." Oh? It is because of the recent happenings in the Old Forest? "Not quite. I will say that I bear somewhat more responsibility than most for what happened at Westbank," Sanders admits. "You see, when the logging camp was founded some handful of years ago, the would-be loggers came to me for advice, as I serve the Old Man of the Earth. Since there are many superstitions about the Old Forest — and not all of them are empty hearsay — I decided to investigate the locale for myself. "At the time, I did sense some latent power amongst the trees, but after a week of fruitless searching, decided to chalk it up to my aging senses and the claustrophobic confines of the Old Forest. Hawkethorne also needed the timber badly, and I was under pressure by the villagers to give my blessing to the venture. "So I did." He couldn't have known this would happen years down the road, though. "No, but I should've erred on the side of caution and at least suggested a safer site for the camp. I think Velun was trying to tell me something, and I wilfully ignored the warning." Sanders thinks for a moment, then gives you a brisk nod. "I will not evade my responsibilities this time, [pc.name]. I don't know exactly how much a help I can be, but the least I can do is to speak with this elf druid and see what she wants." All right. Does he want to come with you, or... "There're some preparations I need to make first — just in case the druidess is less than friendly. It's been a while since I've taken to the field." He sighs, then stiffens his brow and squares his shoulders. "You go on ahead first, [pc.name]; I'll meet you at the camp gates. The Old Forest and the spell you've described will pose no obstacle to me." All right, if he says so. But he still ought to be careful, okay? The Old Forest has changed, you can tell as much from your time amongst the trees. "I will, child. Now, is there anything else I can aid you with?"
rows.translation: 嗯？怎么了？ 你解释说，你需要和他谈谈西岸地区的现状。 没错。加斯和我正在召集民兵，准备组织一次远征。如果你愿意加入的话—— 不，不是那个。你赶紧向桑德斯解释了在西岸发生的那些事情，把你了解到的关键细节都告诉了那位老神父。他聚精会神地听着，坐在长椅上仔细思考你说的每一句话，随后陷入了长时间的沉默。 加雷特和那些伐木工们没有受伤，至少身体上没有受到伤害，这真是太好了。但是你提到的那位精灵德鲁伊…… 加雷特拥有过有人认为，是可以跟她讲道理的。而且既然她和桑德斯都在以某种方式为大自然服务……至少，你认为他尝试说服她的成功率会比你高一些。 [party.has etheryn|我……我不太确定这一点。伊瑟琳出人意料地打断了你的谈话。抱歉，但这样做可能会让事情变得更糟…… 桑德斯挑了挑眉毛。怎么这么说，孩子？ 你侍奉的是生神，更确切地说，是维伦。而这位女德鲁伊，几乎可以肯定是在侍奉古老的荒野之力。在神战之后，当王室改信生神的信仰时，大多数苍白精灵也纷纷效仿他们的做法——那些依然忠于古老荒野之力以及荒野之树象征的少数精灵，则是自愿离开了冬城…… 不用说，那些仍然信奉旧信仰的人们，过去有过怨恨，现在依然存在。 桑德斯点了点头。孩子，我必须记住这一点，但这并不会阻止我尝试。 如果你真的下定决心的话……伊瑟琳看起来还有话要说，但却没能鼓起勇气把它们说出来。 ] 说实话， [pc.name]，我很高兴你来找我求助。如果我们能够避免浪费大家的时间，甚至避免因为不必要的冲突而让一些人失去生命，那就再好不过了。而且，相比大多数人来说，我对这个结果有着更切身的利害关系，尤其是考虑到你告诉我的那些事情之后。 哦？是因为古林最近发生的一些事情吗？ 不完全是这样。我必须承认，对于在西岸发生的那些事情，我承担的责任要比大多数人都要大。桑德斯承认了。你知道，几年前这个伐木营地建立的时候，那些想要来这里伐木的人都会来找我寻求建议，因为我是‘大地之老者’的代言人。由于关于古古林有很多迷信传说——而这些传说并非都是无稽之谈——所以我决定亲自去调查一下这个地方的情况。 当时，我确实感觉到那些树木中蕴藏着某种潜藏的力量，但经过一周毫无结果的搜寻后，我决定将这种感觉归因于自己逐渐衰退的感官，以及古林那种令人感到压抑的环境。鹰棘镇也迫切需要那些木材，而村民们也在向我施压，要求我批准这次行动。 所以我这么做了。 然而，他当时根本无法预料到多年后会发生这样的事情。 不，但我本应该更加谨慎一些，至少应该建议选择一个更安全的地点来扎营。我觉得维伦其实是想告诉我些什么的，但我却故意忽视了那个警告。桑德斯思考了一会儿，然后迅速点了点头。这一次，我绝不会逃避自己的责任。 [pc.name]我不确定自己能提供多少帮助，但至少可以试着和这位精灵德鲁伊谈谈，看看她需要什么。 好吧。他是想和你一起过来，还是…… 我还需要做一些准备工作，以防那位德鲁伊女士不太友善。我已经有一段时间没有上战场了。他叹了口气，然后皱起眉头，挺直肩膀。你先去吧， [pc.name]；我们在营地门口见吧。古林以及你提到的那个咒语，对我来说根本不是障碍。 好吧，如果他是这么说的的话。但他还是应该小心一些，好吗？古林已经变了，你在树林里待了那么久，应该能感觉到这一点。 我会的，孩子。那么，还有其他什么事情需要我帮忙的吗？
rows.raw: ' "Hm? What is it?" You explain that you need to speak with him about the situation at Westbank. "Right. Garth and I are gathering the militia to mount an expedition. If you'd like to join —" No, no, not that. You quickly explain the situation at Westbank to Sanders, giving the old priest the salient details of what you've managed to learn. He listens intently, his brow furrowing as he sits in one of the pews to consider your words, then is silent for a long while. "It's good that Garret and the loggers are unharmed, in body if nothing else. But this elf druidess you speak of..." Garret had suggested that she could be reasoned with. And since both she and Sanders serve the natural world in some fashion... at the very least, you think he'd have a better chance trying to talk her down than you would. [party.has etheryn|"I-I'm not completely sure about that," Etheryn says, most uncharacteristically butting into your conversation. "Pardon me, but it may make things worse..." Sanders raises an eyebrow. "How so, child?" "You serve the Living Gods; Velun to be precise. This druidess almost certainly serves the Old Wyld. When the Royal Family converted to worship of the Living Gods after the Godswar, most of pale elf society followed in their stead — the few who still remained faithful to the Old Wyld and the symbol of the Wyld Tree left the Winter City of their own accord... "Needless to say, there was, and still is, resentment from those who still practice the old faith." Sanders nods. "I'll have to keep that in mind, child, but it won't prevent me from trying." "If you're so determined..." Etheryn looks like she has more to say, but can't work up the nerve to voice it. ] "To be honest, [pc.name], I'm glad you came to me for help. If we can avoid wasting everyone's time, and perhaps even a life or two on an unnecessary confrontation, that'd be ideal. That, and I do have a more personal stake than most in the outcome, especially in light of what you've told me." Oh? It is because of the recent happenings in the Old Forest? "Not quite. I will say that I bear somewhat more responsibility than most for what happened at Westbank," Sanders admits. "You see, when the logging camp was founded some handful of years ago, the would-be loggers came to me for advice, as I serve the Old Man of the Earth. Since there are many superstitions about the Old Forest — and not all of them are empty hearsay — I decided to investigate the locale for myself. "At the time, I did sense some latent power amongst the trees, but after a week of fruitless searching, decided to chalk it up to my aging senses and the claustrophobic confines of the Old Forest. Hawkethorne also needed the timber badly, and I was under pressure by the villagers to give my blessing to the venture. "So I did." He couldn't have known this would happen years down the road, though. "No, but I should've erred on the side of caution and at least suggested a safer site for the camp. I think Velun was trying to tell me something, and I wilfully ignored the warning." Sanders thinks for a moment, then gives you a brisk nod. "I will not evade my responsibilities this time, [pc.name]. I don't know exactly how much a help I can be, but the least I can do is to speak with this elf druid and see what she wants." All right. Does he want to come with you, or... "There're some preparations I need to make first — just in case the druidess is less than friendly. It's been a while since I've taken to the field." He sighs, then stiffens his brow and squares his shoulders. "You go on ahead first, [pc.name]; I'll meet you at the camp gates. The Old Forest and the spell you've described will pose no obstacle to me." All right, if he says so. But he still ought to be careful, okay? The Old Forest has changed, you can tell as much from your time amongst the trees. "I will, child. Now, is there anything else I can aid you with?" '

rows.original: As you pace towards the chapel and up the stone steps, a lump forms in your throat. The last you saw of Brother Sanders was him walking into the forest with Hethia — try as you might, you can't quite seem to have the old priest's faith in her, nor in his safety. Nevertheless, you force heavy feet forward and up to the chapel's open entryway, peering into the dimness within. It takes a little time for your eyes to adjust, but eventually you do make out the familiar shape of Sanders by the altar with his prayer book. Ah — so you were worrying about nothing, after all. The good Brother is fine, but well... what if he weren't? As you approach, Sanders shuts his prayer book and turns to you with a smile. "[pc.name]. I had a feeling you'd be visiting me." It's good to see he's fine. You were worried. "Not unreasonably so, as I was placing myself quite deeply in Hethia's power. Had she chosen to turn on me, I might've found myself in a bit of a pickle, I admit. I've been wrong about people before, more often than I'd have liked... I'm not a perfect judge of character." Sanders looks pensive for a moment. "But I can't stop trying to believe in others because of that. Either way, I wasn't wrong about Hethia." [pc.isDK|You can't help but think the old priest's outlook on life is more than a bit naive, but then again, he's clearly possessed of enough skill and power to have lived through his bad decisions. If only you had that kind of strength... psh. ] So, if he doesn't mind you asking, how did things turn out? "We had a very pleasant chat," Sanders replies. "It mostly focused on how old things eventually must pass away, to be replaced with the new. And yet the essence of the old still lives on in the new — thus a part of it is immortal." Yes, yes, but what about the situation in the Old Forest? What's Hethia going to do now? "Hethia herself is going to try and return to her circle of druids; she's been away from them for too long. She shares my sentiments, though, that it's unlikely that they've been untouched by the affliction that spreads throughout the land. All the more reason to hurry home, then. "As for the situation... we don't have a plan. I proposed that we formally join forces to help combat the corruption and hopefully contain it, but while she was receptive to the idea, she couldn't speak for the other members of her circle." So, no progress. Sanders sighs. "Not for now, at the very least. She couldn't tell me where this sacred site which started all this trouble was, but we did manage, with a bit of roundabout phrasing, to allow me to determine just where we should keep away from in the future. She has no problem with proper forestry; allowing the woods to grow too thick simply means it becomes a fire hazard come summer. "I'm going to help get a new logging camp up and running, but this time on the edge of the forest. It's too dangerous to go deep inside any more... as you know well enough." Yes. Yes, you do. There's one thing, though... "Yes?" Your trip back to Hawkethorne was rather uneventful, despite the din the dozen of you must have made crashing and smashing your way through the overgrown trail. It's a small wonder nothing went ahead and accosted any of you — did he have a hand in that? "Ah, so you noticed." You do have to thank him properly. Herding two handfuls of spooked, jittery lads through the woods in the dead of night wasn't the most pleasing experience. The help he gave was most welcome. "I didn't do it alone, of course. Hethia aided me." Right, right. "I'm just glad everyone's safe and home. There'll be a bit of a lull while we get things running again, but Garth's got a collection going on so that they and their families can tide things out until they can get back to work again." All's well that ends well, it seems. "Indeed." Sanders smiles. "And that seems to be the end of the matter for now. So, can I do anything else for you, [pc.name]?"
rows.translation: 当你朝着小教堂走去，踏上那些石阶时，一股哽咽感涌上心头。你最后一次见到桑德斯修士，就是他带着赫希娅走进了森林——无论你如何努力，你似乎都无法像那位老神父那样相信她，也无法相信她的安全。尽管如此，你还是艰难地向前走去，来到了小教堂敞开的入口处，向里面昏暗的空间望去。 你的眼睛需要一些时间来适应这种光线，但最终，你还是看到了祭坛旁、拿着祈祷书的桑德斯那熟悉的身影。啊——原来如此。是毕竟，没什么好担心的。那位好心的兄弟并没有什么事，但是……要是他出了什么事怎么办呢？ 当你走近时，桑德斯合上了他的祈祷书，微笑着转向你。"[pc.name]我就觉得你会来看我的。 看到他没事真是太好了，你之前一定很担心吧。 这也并非毫无道理，因为我确实将自己置于赫希娅的掌控之下。如果她选择与我为敌，那我确实会陷入困境，这一点我必须承认。过去，我确实经常在判断他人品性时犯错……我并不是一个擅长判断人性的专家。桑德斯沉思了一会儿。但正因为如此，我依然无法停止尝试去相信他人。无论如何，关于赫希娅的事情，我并没有弄错。 [pc.isDK|你不禁会认为那位老牧师的人生观未免过于天真了，但另一方面，他显然拥有足够的实力与能力，才能在那些错误的决定之后依然活下来。要是你也有那样的力量该多好……唉。 ] 那么，如果他不介意你问的话，事情最终结果是怎样的呢？ 我们的谈话非常愉快。桑德斯回应道。它主要探讨了古老的事物最终如何会消逝，被新的事物所取代。然而，古老事物的精髓依然会在新的事物中延续下去——因此，其中的一部分是永恒的。 是的，是的，但是古林里的情况怎么办呢？赫希娅现在该怎么做呢？ 赫希娅本人也会尝试回到她的德鲁伊团体中；她已经离开他们太久了。不过，她和我的想法是一样的——那些遍布整个地区的灾祸，很可能也已经影响到了他们。因此，她更有理由尽快回家了。 至于这个情况……我们还没有具体的计划。我提议我们正式联手，共同打击腐败现象，希望能将其控制在一定范围内。不过，虽然她对这个想法表示赞同，但她无法代表她所在圈子里的其他成员做出决定。 所以，没有任何进展。 桑德斯叹了口气。至少目前还不是。她没有告诉我这个引发所有麻烦的圣地具体位于哪里，但通过一些迂回的表述，我们还是弄清楚了今后应该避开哪些地方。她并不反对合理的林业管理；只是如果让树林长得太茂密，到了夏天就会带来火灾隐患。 我打算帮忙建立一个新的伐木营地并让它投入运营，但这次要建在森林的边缘。像你们都很清楚的那样，再往森林深处去已经太危险了…… 是的，确实如此。不过，还有一件事…… 是吗？ 你们返回鹰棘镇的旅途其实相当顺利，尽管你们十几个人在那些杂草丛生的小路上行进时，肯定发出过不少嘈杂的声音。真奇怪，竟然没有什么东西突然出现来打扰你们——难道这是他暗中安排的吗？ 啊，原来你注意到了。 你确实应该好好感谢他。在深夜里带着两个惊慌失措、紧张不安的男孩穿过树林，那可绝不是什么愉快的经历。他所提供的帮助实在非常宝贵，令人倍感欣慰。 当然，这不是我一个人完成的。赫希娅也帮了我很大的忙。 好的，好的。 我只是很高兴大家都平安无事，回到了家里。在我们重新恢复正常运作之前，可能会有一段短暂的停滞期，但加斯正在举办一场募捐活动，这样他们和他们的家人就能暂时度过这段困难时期，等到能够重新开始工作的时候。 看来，只要结局好，一切就都值得了。 确实如此。桑德斯笑了。看来目前这件事就到此为止了吧。那么，还有什么我可以为您做的吗？ [pc.name]？”

rows.original: Where in the Old Forest is the logging camp, exactly?
rows.translation: 伐木营地到底在古林的什么地方呢？
rows.raw: "Where in the Old Forest is the logging camp, exactly?"

rows.original: Animals acting strangely aside, was there anything that happened to Westbank?
rows.translation: 先不说那些行为古怪的动物，西岸地区是不是发生了什么事情？
rows.raw: "Animals acting strangely aside, was there anything that happened to Westbank?"

rows.original: Why did Garret go alone ahead of the militia?
rows.translation: 加雷特为什么会在民兵队之前独自前行呢？
rows.raw: "Why did Garret go alone ahead of the militia?"

rows.original: Yawning and stretching, you step down into the Frost Hound's common room, blinking away the last vestiges of sleep that cling to your eyes. That was more comfortable than you'd expected, but alas, there's no rest for the wicked, nor is there any for those trying to stop them. The world isn't going to save itself — "[pc.name]. A moment." Garth doesn't raise his voice, but there's no mistaking his words over the hubbub of the common room. Catching your gaze, the barkeep gives you a nod and motions for you to come over with a tilt of his head, his hands never leaving the ever-present mug and cloth in his grasp. [pc.isDK|Guess you can see what this is all about; you owe the old man as much|It'd be rude by far to refuse an invitation from your host]. Sidling over to the bar in as discreet a manner as you can manage, you ask Garth what's up. "You're intending to go out of town again, aren't you?" Can't very well chase demonesses about if you decide to stay within Hawkethorne's walls, can you? So yes, you do suppose you intend to venture beyond the gates — is there something he needs done? Garth nods. "No one's been heading out into the Old Forest after that night — well, no one except you, really. With all the weird nonsense going on down there, sensible folk are keeping to the lighter woods closer to town. The trees are thinner, the light brighter — fewer places for things to lurk about in waiting and a better chance of seeing what's creeping up on you. "Simply put, that means you're the only one I can ask to see to this job." While Garth doesn't say it, you get the distinct impression that he expects as much for giving you free room and board for the foreseeable future. Either way, there isn't any harm in at least hearing him out, so you make yourself comfortable before motioning for him to go on. "Out west in the Old Forest, there's a logging camp — Westbank, named such on account of it sitting on the western bank of the river. Not much to look at, really, but pretty important to the town as a whole. The lads there fell the trees of the Old Forest, plant new ones, and work the fallen logs a little before floating them to the sawmill downstream to be turned into planks and beams. To give you a rough estimate, I'd say about half the timbers that now make up Hawkethorne once passed through there, so you can imagine how important it is to keep it up and running. "Now, there's a been a problem of late — it actually started before you came, [pc.name], but recent troubles haven't been making it any better, either. About two to three weeks before you arrived in Hawkethorne, we got word that strange things had been going on near the camp. Animals acting oddly, getting too close to the palisades when they should've been rightfully scared of people. A series of close shaves with things in the darkness, too close together to be mere coincidence. "You may laugh, but there's something unsettling about a snowshoe rabbit hopping up to the gates and just sitting and staring for hours on end. It's not just the feeling of being watched, it's the feeling that the bunny is just a puppet — that someone else is looking at you through its eyes. I should know; I've seen such things done before in my younger days on the road. "You thirsty there, [pc.name]?" Sure, why not; a drink to nurse while you hear him out would be great. Setting down the washcloth, Garth sets the mug under the tap and fills it to the brim with mead, letting the foam subside a little before sliding it across the counter to you. [dayNight|A tiny little voice in the back of your mind says something about this being too early in the day to start drinking, but you quickly snuff it out. This is good stuff. ]You raise the mug to your lips, tip your head back, and take a long, deep swig to keep the cold out. If this is a bribe, it's working pretty well. "Right, moving on with the story. Hawkethorne's full of hunters, but we don't have many people who can actually fight aside from me and old man Sanders. It took us a week or so to try and get something of a militia together and head into the Old Forest to investigate. During that time, word comes down from Westbank that a warg's been spotted prowling near the treeline. "My idiot son catches wind of this, and declares that he's going to go up there himself to take care of the problem by himself — I believe his exact words were that he was going to 'punch out all its blood.'" Garth sighs, shakes his head and looks down at the mug he's polishing. "Stupid, stupid, glory-seeking pup. By the time someone's wandered into the Frost Hound and told me what Garret was up to, he's already packed up and left. That was three days before you arrived, [pc.name]. Neither him nor anyone else from the logging camp have shown their faces in Hawkethorne since, and with all the nonsense happening of late no one's been able to go in and check on them." You can see where this is going. If you're intending to head into the Old Forest, then yes, you wouldn't mind checking out this logging camp and seeing what happened there, or if you can find Garth's son in the process. "That's about the long and short of it. I take it there're other things you'll want to know before heading out?" Oh, you have plenty of questions all right.
rows.translation: 你打着哈欠、伸了伸懒腰，走进了寒霜猎犬的公共休息室，眨了眨眼睛，驱散那些还残留在眼底的睡意。这里的环境比你预想的要舒适得多，但可惜，对于那些作恶的人来说，没有休息的机会；而对于那些试图阻止他们的人而言，也同样如此。这个世界是不会自我拯救的 "[pc.name]稍等片刻。 加思并没有提高音量，但在大厅里嘈杂的环境中，他的话依然清晰可闻。酒保注意到你的目光，点了点头，然后歪着头示意你过去，他的双手始终紧握着那杯酒和抹布。 [pc.isDK|你应该能猜到这到底是怎么回事吧——你确实欠那位老人一笔债。|拒绝主人的邀请未免太无礼了。]你尽可能谨慎地走到吧台旁，询问加思发生了什么事。 你又是打算出城去吧？ 如果你决定待在鹰棘镇的城墙之内，那就根本不可能去追那些女恶魔了，对吧？所以，你应该是打算走出城门去吧——是不是有什么事情需要你去处理？ 加思点了点头。从那个晚上之后，就再也没有人敢走进古林了——嗯，其实除了你之外，确实没有其他人会去。鉴于那里发生的那些离奇事件，明智的人们都会选择待在靠近城镇的、树木较为稀疏、光线较好的地方。这样的环境里，潜伏的危险事物会少很多，人们也更容易发现那些悄悄接近自己的东西。 简单来说，这意味着只有你才是我能够邀请来帮忙完成这项工作的人。 虽然加斯没有明说，但你能明显感觉到，他期望你能在未来一段时间内免费为他提供食宿。无论如何，至少听他把话说完也没什么坏处，于是你先让自己坐得舒服些，然后示意他继续说下去。 在西部那片古老的森林里，有一个伐木营地——名叫韦斯特班克，这个名字的由来是因为它位于河流的西岸。这个营地看起来并不怎么样，但实际上对整个小镇来说却非常重要。那里的工人们负责砍伐古古林里的树木，种植新的树木，然后对砍下来的原木进行初步加工，之后再将它们运送到下游的锯木厂，将其加工成木板和其他建筑材料。粗略估计的话，现在构成鹰棘镇的大部分木材中，有一半都是曾经从那里运输过来的。因此，你可以想象维持它的正常运作是多么重要。 最近出现了一个问题，其实这个问题是从……开始的。之前你来了。 [pc.name]，但是最近的麻烦也让情况没有得到任何改善。在你来到鹰棘镇之前的两三周，我们收到了消息，说营地附近发生了一些奇怪的事情。动物们的行为变得异常，本应该对人类感到恐惧的它们，却反而靠得越来越近。还发生了一系列与黑暗中的不明物体近距离接触的事件，这些事件发生的频率太高，绝非巧合。 你们可能会觉得好笑，但当一只雪鞋兔跳到大门前，然后就坐在那里一动不动地盯着你看上几个小时时，确实会让人感到不安。这种感觉不仅仅是因为觉得有人在注视着自己，而更像是那只兔子其实只是一个木偶——有人正通过它的双眼看着你。我应该很清楚这种感觉；在我年轻时，在路上旅行时，我就见过这种事情发生。 你在那儿口渴了吧[pc.name]？” 当然，为什么不呢；在听他讲述的时候喝一杯酒，会让人感觉更好。加思放下毛巾，把杯子放在水龙头下，将蜂蜜酒倒得满满的，等泡沫稍微消退一些后，才把它推到你面前。 [dayNight|你脑海中有一个微小的声音在提醒你，现在才早上，现在还不是喝酒的时候，但你很快就压制住了这个声音。这酒确实不错啊。 ]你将杯子举到嘴边，仰头大口喝下，这样就能让寒冷远离身体。 如果这算是一种贿赂的话，那它的效果确实相当不错。 好的，继续讲故事吧。鹰棘镇到处都是猎人，但我们真正有能力应对这些猎人的人并不多。战斗除了我和桑德斯老人之外，我们花了一周左右的时间才勉强组建起一支民兵小队，然后前往古林进行调查。就在那段时间里，从西岸传来了消息，有人发现有一名战士在树林附近活动。 我那个愚蠢的儿子听说了这件事，竟然宣称要亲自去解决这个问题——我记得他当时说的确切话是，他要“把里面所有的血都打出来”。加思叹了口气，摇了摇头，然后低头看着自己正在擦拭的杯子。愚蠢的、爱慕虚荣的家伙。等到有人走进寒霜猎犬酒馆告诉我加雷特在搞什么名堂时，他已经收拾东西离开了。那是在你到来的三天之前。 [pc.name]从那以后，他以及伐木营里的其他人都再也没有出现在鹰棘镇。再加上最近发生的一连串荒唐事，根本没人能够进去看看他们的情况。 你可以猜到接下来会发生什么。如果你打算进入古林，那么的话，你确实应该去看看这个伐木营地，弄清楚那里发生了什么，或许还能在这个过程中找到加思的儿子。 大致情况就是这么回事。我想在出发之前，应该还有其他一些事情你需要了解吧？ 哦，你们确实有很多问题要问，好吧。
rows.raw: " Yawning and stretching, you step down into the Frost Hound's common room, blinking away the last vestiges of sleep that cling to your eyes. That was more comfortable than you'd expected, but alas, there's no rest for the wicked, nor is there any for those trying to stop them. The world isn't going to save itself — "[pc.name]. A moment." Garth doesn't raise his voice, but there's no mistaking his words over the hubbub of the common room. Catching your gaze, the barkeep gives you a nod and motions for you to come over with a tilt of his head, his hands never leaving the ever-present mug and cloth in his grasp. [pc.isDK|Guess you can see what this is all about; you owe the old man as much|It'd be rude by far to refuse an invitation from your host]. Sidling over to the bar in as discreet a manner as you can manage, you ask Garth what's up. "You're intending to go out of town again, aren't you?" Can't very well chase demonesses about if you decide to stay within Hawkethorne's walls, can you? So yes, you do suppose you intend to venture beyond the gates — is there something he needs done? Garth nods. "No one's been heading out into the Old Forest after that night — well, no one except you, really. With all the weird nonsense going on down there, sensible folk are keeping to the lighter woods closer to town. The trees are thinner, the light brighter — fewer places for things to lurk about in waiting and a better chance of seeing what's creeping up on you. "Simply put, that means you're the only one I can ask to see to this job." While Garth doesn't say it, you get the distinct impression that he expects as much for giving you free room and board for the foreseeable future. Either way, there isn't any harm in at least hearing him out, so you make yourself comfortable before motioning for him to go on. "Out west in the Old Forest, there's a logging camp — Westbank, named such on account of it sitting on the western bank of the river. Not much to look at, really, but pretty important to the town as a whole. The lads there fell the trees of the Old Forest, plant new ones, and work the fallen logs a little before floating them to the sawmill downstream to be turned into planks and beams. To give you a rough estimate, I'd say about half the timbers that now make up Hawkethorne once passed through there, so you can imagine how important it is to keep it up and running. "Now, there's a been a problem of late — it actually started before you came, [pc.name], but recent troubles haven't been making it any better, either. About two to three weeks before you arrived in Hawkethorne, we got word that strange things had been going on near the camp. Animals acting oddly, getting too close to the palisades when they should've been rightfully scared of people. A series of close shaves with things in the darkness, too close together to be mere coincidence. "You may laugh, but there's something unsettling about a snowshoe rabbit hopping up to the gates and just sitting and staring for hours on end. It's not just the feeling of being watched, it's the feeling that the bunny is just a puppet — that someone else is looking at you through its eyes. I should know; I've seen such things done before in my younger days on the road. "You thirsty there, [pc.name]?" Sure, why not; a drink to nurse while you hear him out would be great. Setting down the washcloth, Garth sets the mug under the tap and fills it to the brim with mead, letting the foam subside a little before sliding it across the counter to you. [dayNight|A tiny little voice in the back of your mind says something about this being too early in the day to start drinking, but you quickly snuff it out. This is good stuff. ]You raise the mug to your lips, tip your head back, and take a long, deep swig to keep the cold out. If this is a bribe, it's working pretty well. "Right, moving on with the story. Hawkethorne's full of hunters, but we don't have many people who can actually fight aside from me and old man Sanders. It took us a week or so to try and get something of a militia together and head into the Old Forest to investigate. During that time, word comes down from Westbank that a warg's been spotted prowling near the treeline. "My idiot son catches wind of this, and declares that he's going to go up there himself to take care of the problem by himself — I believe his exact words were that he was going to 'punch out all its blood.'" Garth sighs, shakes his head and looks down at the mug he's polishing. "Stupid, stupid, glory-seeking pup. By the time someone's wandered into the Frost Hound and told me what Garret was up to, he's already packed up and left. That was three days before you arrived, [pc.name]. Neither him nor anyone else from the logging camp have shown their faces in Hawkethorne since, and with all the nonsense happening of late no one's been able to go in and check on them." You can see where this is going. If you're intending to head into the Old Forest, then yes, you wouldn't mind checking out this logging camp and seeing what happened there, or if you can find Garth's son in the process. "That's about the long and short of it. I take it there're other things you'll want to know before heading out?" Oh, you have plenty of questions all right."

rows.original: "Like I said, [pc.name], it's on the western edge of the woods by the river. Most who travel in that direction do so by barge, but you're better off following the old logging trails, even if they haven't been used for a while. Going to be hard to convince anyone to pole a barge upriver these days." Yes, but where exactly is it? Garth sighs. "Forget you're not as used to the lay of the land as most people here. Come on, give me your map — I'll mark it for you." You do just that, and Garth gets out a stick of charcoal from under the bar. When he's done, you've got a squiggle denoting the forest trail you're supposed to take, as well as a black "X" marking out your destination. Huh. That looks fairly remote. "It is," Garth replies. "Like I said, the trails haven't been used in quite a while and have gotten pretty overgrown. You could spend forever searching and never be able to spot it." Well, it's a good thing that you have him to point them out for you. Garth snorts. "Anything else?"
rows.translation: “就像我说的，[pc.name]，它就在河边、树林的西缘。往那个方向去的人大多坐驳船，但你最好沿着那些废弃的伐木小径走，哪怕它们已经很久没人用了。这年头，想找人把驳船撑到上游去可不容易。” 是的，但到底在哪里呢？ 加斯叹了口气。“我忘了，你不像这儿大多数人那样熟悉这片地形。来吧，把地图给我，我帮你标出来。” 你照做了，加斯从吧台底下摸出一根木炭。等他画完，地图上多出一条弯弯曲曲的线，标出你该走的林间小路，还有一个黑色的“X”标着你的目的地。 嗯，看起来那地方相当偏远。 “是的，”加斯答道。“就像我说的，这些小径很久没人走，已经长得相当茂密了。你可能找上一辈子都发现不了它。” 还好有他帮你把它们指出来。 加斯哼了一声。“还有别的事吗？”

rows.original: Garth looks thoughtful for a moment. "Come to think of it, there was an incident a few weeks before all this happened. There was this pale elf lady who came up to the camp, all angry-like. Said that the logging work was coming close to some kind of sacred grove or the other." [flags.ETHERYN_MET| Right. Like Etheryn, then. You glance over to Etheryn, [party.has etheryn|who's looking awkward with the sudden turn of the conversation|who's sitting at one of the nearby tables]. She quickly looks away, clearly uncomfortable with the situation. | Pale elf? "Miss Ivris is a wyld elf, not a pale elf; if you're going to spend any time up in the Frost Marches you'd do well to learn the difference. Most important one being that while wyld elves tend to be little slips of things, their men and women both, the women of the pale elves are just the opposite. Tall. Lean. Powerful. They've given our own shieldmaidens a run for their money in the past, if the stories are to be believed — and there's no reason not to. "Their menfolk... well, those aren't much too different from that of the wyld elves. Which makes sense, since their city up beyond the Frostwood is ruled over by some kind of queen or the other. I don't really know very much else about them, since they tend to keep to themselves, but they're not to be taken lightly, that's for certain." ] Right. So what happened? "The lads were mostly civil, or that's what they said. No sense in getting on a pale elf's bad side for the fun of it — if only she'd tell them where the grove was, they'd steer clear of it. Lady wouldn't tell them, though — whole point of the sacred grove was that she couldn't tell them where exactly it was. Now, the lads aren't going to stop logging altogether, so if she wasn't going to cooperate, they weren't going to either. "That wasn't the end of her complaints, too. Said they were growing the wrong kinds of softwoods and hardwoods in the wrong places, that sort of thing. Eventually the negotiations erupted into one huge argument, and that dashed any chance of talking things out. No one was going to budge, so she eventually just stormed back into the trees where she came from." Isn't there the possibility that — "It did occur to old man Sanders and me that the animals acting oddly might have been her doing, but we'd no idea where she might be, and we weren't about to send lads one by one into the deep woods to look. That was what the militia we'd gathered was going to do." Your guess is that this pale elf lady is some kind of wildling or druidess, then. Garth nods. "Pretty much, I'd say. Now, the lads at Westbank aren't idiots — they don't do dumb shit like clear-cutting the Old Forest. At the very least, it makes sense for them to make sure they have a job tomorrow. They try to take the old trees, the thickest clusters, thin the place out a bit so when the forest fires come in the summer they're not as terrible as they could have been. Old man Sanders follows Velun, so he comes and does an inspection every other season, makes some suggestions as to treating the forest right, gives the camp his blessing. The pale elf lady, though, she didn't recognize the Living Gods." [flags.ETHERYN_MET |"That's... that sounds right," Etheryn pipes up[party.has etheryn|| from her table]. She's clearly hesitant, but takes a moment to summon up the courage to speak. "When the royal family officially converted after the Godswar, my grandmother made worship of Lumia and the other Living Gods our state religion. Some people... well, there was a break between most of us, and the handful who still held faith in the animistic practices of the Old Wyld. In protest, they packed up and left the Winter City, turning their backs on those they considered apostates." So, this lady who came complaining to the camp was probably one of their number? Etheryn shifts uncomfortably, turning her gaze away. "That's likely to be the case. They're rather hard-line about their worship of the Old Wyld — they'd have to be, to throw away everything for their faith, and I can't imagine they've grown more lax over the last couple of centuries in self-exile. Appealing to them in Velun's name isn't going to do much for anyone's case — just the opposite, in fact." ] Well, if you see her on the way there, you might as well stop and have a chat. Garth grimaces. "Oh, she'll stop you all right, but I get the feeling that she'll want to do more than just talk."
rows.translation: 加斯沉思了一会儿。仔细想来，其实是在这一切发生之前的几周，有这样一件小事。有一位皮肤苍白的精灵女士怒气冲冲地来到了营地，声称伐木作业已经接近了一片神圣的树林。 [flags.ETHERYN_MET| 对。那就像伊瑟琳一样。你瞥了一眼伊瑟琳[party.has etheryn|谁会因为谈话方向的突然转变而显得局促不安呢|谁坐在附近的那些桌子中的一张上呢？]她迅速移开了视线，显然对这种处境感到很不自在。 | 淡色精灵？ 艾薇莉丝小姐是荒野精灵，而不是淡色精灵；如果你打算在霜冻边境地区待上一段时间，最好了解一下这两者之间的区别。最重要的是，虽然荒野精灵无论男女通常身材娇小，但淡色精灵的女性却恰恰相反——她们身材高挑、体态纤瘦、力量强大。如果那些故事是真的的话，过去她们确实让我们的女盾卫们感到有些压力……而我们完全没有理由不相信这些故事。 他们的男人们……嗯，那些他们与野精灵并没有太大的区别。这也情有可原，因为他们在霜木之地以外的城市是由一位女王或其他形式的统治者管理的。关于他们，我其实了解得并不多，因为他们通常喜欢独来独往，但可以肯定的是，他们绝不可小觑。 ] 好的。那么发生了什么呢？ 那些小伙子们大多还算守规矩，至少他们是这么说的。没必要为了好玩就惹恼一个苍白精灵——只要她能告诉他们那片树林的位置，他们肯定不会去那里的。不过那位女士就是不肯告诉他们，而这片神圣树林的意义就在于她根本无法指明它的具体位置。现在，那些小伙子们也不会完全停止伐木活动，所以如果她不愿意配合，他们也不会罢休的。 她的抱怨并没有到此为止。她还说他们在错误的地方种植了错误的软木和硬木品种，诸如此类的事情。最终，这些谈判演变成了一场激烈的争吵，彻底破坏了通过对话解决问题的可能性。双方都坚决不肯让步，于是她最终怒气冲冲地回到了她最初所在的那些树林里。 难道没有这样的可能性吗—— 桑德斯老人和我确实想过，那些行为异常的动物可能是她干的，但我们根本不知道她在哪里，也不可能派人一个一个地进入那片茂密的森林去寻找她。我们召集起来的民兵正是准备去做这件事的。 那么，你应该是认为这位皮肤苍白的精灵女士是某种野人或者女德鲁伊吧。 加斯点了点头。差不多吧，我认为是这样。西岸那边的那些人可不是傻瓜——他们不会做出像砍伐古林这样的蠢事。至少，他们会考虑自己明天的工作问题。他们会尽量保留那些老树，尤其是那些最茂密的树丛，让森林的密度降低一些，这样到了夏天发生森林火灾时，损失就会小一些。桑德斯老人追随维伦的脚步，因此每隔一个季节就会前来进行检查，提出一些关于如何合理保护森林的建议，并为营地带来祝福。然而，那位苍白肤色的精灵女士却并不承认那些“现世神祇”的存在。" [flags.ETHERYN_MET |那个……听起来没错。伊瑟琳开口说道。[party.has etheryn|| 从她的桌子上]她显然有些犹豫，但最终还是鼓起勇气开口说话了。在神战之后，当王室正式改信新宗教时，我的祖母将崇拜卢米娅以及其他生神定为我们的国教。有些人……嗯，我们大多数人与他们产生了分歧，那些仍然坚守着古老荒野地区原始信仰的人选择了离开冬城，他们认为那些改信新宗教的人是背信弃义的。 所以，那个来营地投诉的女子，很可能也是他们中的一员吧？ 伊瑟琳感到有些不安，便将目光移开了。很可能就是这样。他们对对‘古老荒野’的崇拜态度非常强硬——为了信仰，他们不得不如此。我想，在过去几个世纪的自流放生活中，他们的态度也不会有任何松动。以维伦的名义去说服他们，对任何人的诉求都毫无帮助，事实上，反而可能会适得其反。 ] 嗯，如果你在去那里的路上遇到了她，不妨停下来聊聊天吧。 加斯做了个鬼脸。哦，她肯定能阻止你们，但我感觉，她想做的不仅仅是谈话而已。

Like Etheryn, then. You glance over to Etheryn, [party.has etheryn|who's looking awkward with the sudden turn of the conversation|who's sitting at one of the nearby tables]. Most important one being that while wyld elves tend to be little slips of things, their men and women both, the women of the pale elves are just the opposite. Tall. Lean. Powerful. They've given our own shieldmaidens a run for their money in the past, if the stories are to be believed — and there's no reason not to. "Their menfolk... well, those aren't much too different from that of the wyld elves. Which makes sense, since their city up beyond the Frostwood is ruled over by some kind of queen or the other. I don't really know very much else about them, since they tend to keep to themselves, but they're not to be taken lightly, that's for certain." ] Right. So what happened? "The lads were mostly civil, or that's what they said. No sense in getting on a pale elf's bad side for the fun of it — if only she'd tell them where the grove was, they'd steer clear of it. Lady wouldn't tell them, though — whole point of the sacred grove was that she couldn't tell them where exactly it was. Now, the lads aren't going to stop logging altogether, so if she wasn't going to cooperate, they weren't going to either. "That wasn't the end of her complaints, too. Said they were growing the wrong kinds of softwoods and hardwoods in the wrong places, that sort of thing. Eventually the negotiations erupted into one huge argument, and that dashed any chance of talking things out. No one was going to budge, so she eventually just stormed back into the trees where she came from." Isn't there the possibility that — "It did occur to old man Sanders and me that the animals acting oddly might have been her doing, but we'd no idea where she might be, and we weren't about to send lads one by one into the deep woods to look. That was what the militia we'd gathered was going to do." Your guess is that this pale elf lady is some kind of wildling or druidess, then. Garth nods. "Pretty much, I'd say. Now, the lads at Westbank aren't idiots — they don't do dumb shit like clear-cutting the Old Forest. At the very least, it makes sense for them to make sure they have a job tomorrow. They try to take the old trees, the thickest clusters, thin the place out a bit so when the forest fires come in the summer they're not as terrible as they could have been. Old man Sanders follows Velun, so he comes and does an inspection every other season, makes some suggestions as to treating the forest right, gives the camp his blessing. The pale elf lady, though, she didn't recognize the Living Gods." [flags.ETHERYN_MET |"That's... that sounds right," Etheryn pipes up[party.has etheryn|| from her table]. She's clearly hesitant, but takes a moment to summon up the courage to speak. "When the royal family officially converted after the Godswar, my grandmother made worship of Lumia and the other Living Gods our state religion. Some people... well, there was a break between most of us, and the handful who still held faith in the animistic practices of the Old Wyld. In protest, they packed up and left the Winter City, turning their backs on those they considered apostates." So, this lady who came complaining to the camp was probably one of their number? Etheryn shifts uncomfortably, turning her gaze away. "That's likely to be the case. They're rather hard-line about their worship of the Old Wyld — they'd have to be, to throw away everything for their faith, and I can't imagine they've grown more lax over the last couple of centuries in self-exile. Appealing to them in Velun's name isn't going to do much for anyone's case — just the opposite, in fact." ] Well, if you see her on the way there, you might as well stop and have a chat. Garth grimaces. "Oh, she'll stop you all right, but I get the feeling that she'll want to do more than just talk.""

rows.original: At the question, Garth growls and makes to spit, but thinks better of it. "Oh, why did the gods curse me with a moron for a son?" Now, now. Let's all take a moment here to calm down and sort out one's thoughts[pc.cunningRange 50|, and then he can tell you all about his son whom he openly lambasts for being a fool and nitwit but secretly loves very much. Garth narrows his eyes at you and manages to look even more dour than normal, which is no mean feat. "Hey, now." Well, it only stands to reason, doesn't it? He just bemoaned his fate for being saddled with a son like Garret, but he wouldn't send you out after him if he didn't give a damn about the pup. After all, hate isn't really the opposite of love — indifference is. At that, Garth says nothing for a little while, but makes several chewing motions with his jaws. Then, at last: "You know, not everyone likes hearing the blunt truth." You knew that already, but the advice's well-taken. You know that he's better at handling hard truths than most of the rabble out there, after all. |. There's no need to lose one's cool when actually trying to do something constructive, yes? Garret eyes the drink he's drawn for you, then taps out a mug of mead for himself. "Don't usually condone drinking on the job, but I think it'll do me more good than harm this time around." Oh, definitely. Besides, it can't hurt for his patrons to see him enjoying his own drink, can it? If it's good enough for him, it's good enough for them. A thin smile. "Bottoms up." Together, Garth and you drain your mugs, and then the old wolf settles back with a sigh, wiping his mouth with the back of his free hand. ] "It's my fault, really," Garth says with a sigh. "Should've made him paint more fences when he was a pup, split some more wood. Work all that energy out of his system, instead of putting it all into dreaming of adventure. I had my fill of adventure when I was younger, and let me tell you, I built this place so that he wouldn't have to suffer any of that nonsense. And what does the ingrate do? Hop up and want to traipse off into the world like his mother did." Silence. "I can hear him now. 'You've had your fun, Dad, then when it comes to my turn, you're not letting me go.' Boy seems intent on learning things the hard way..." All right, you're beginning to see how this is shaping out here. A warg showing up was probably the most exciting thing that's happened near Hawkethorne for years. Being a young, impulsive glory-hunter, Garret leaped on the chance to partake in anything vaguely resembling an adventure, which it wouldn't be if he'd waited for the rest of the militia to mobilize and moved out with them. "We had a bit of an argument the night before," Garth admits after some more silence. "One of many, which is why I didn't think much of it. I told Garret he was an idiot — which he is — and that the first actual threat he met out beyond the woods was going to send him over his head in trouble. He said that if he took down the warg by himself, that'd prove otherwise... I guess I should've said something else, but he'd stormed out of the room. He takes after his mother." Garth sighs. "Sorry to unload this on you, but you did ask for it. No one should be comfortable with airing dirty laundry out in the open." Yes, you did ask for it. But at least now you know exactly why Garret went charging on ahead into the Old Forest, and that might make it easier for you to find him when you make the trip out to the logging camp. "With all the things roaming the woods at this point, he'll probably have holed up somewhere, if not taken refuge in the camp itself. He's daft, but at least I raised him well enough that he's not that daft." You'll keep an eye out, then. Garth nods, watches you finish your mead, then retrieves the mug. "If you find him alive, I think he'll be more than willing to come home at this point. Otherwise... don't bring him back, okay? Gwyn's a good girl — I don't think she'd be able to take it."
rows.translation: 听到这个问题，加斯低吼了一声，还想要吐口水，但最终还是忍住了。哦，为什么神明要让我生出一个这么愚蠢的儿子呢？ 好了，好了。我们现在都花一点时间来平静一下，整理一下自己的思绪吧。[pc.cunningRange 50|然后他就可以向你详细讲述关于他儿子的事情了——他公开批评儿子是个傻瓜、白痴，但实际上却非常爱他。 加斯眯起眼睛看着你，他的表情显得比平时更加阴沉，而要做到这一点其实并不容易。嘿，现在。 嗯，这其实也很合情理，不是吗？他之前一直在抱怨自己为什么会有像加雷特这样的儿子，但如果他真的不在意这个孩子的话，他就不会派你去找他了。毕竟，恨并不是爱的反面，冷漠才是。 这时，加斯沉默了一会儿，只是不停地用下巴做着咀嚼的动作。终于，他开口说道：“你知道，并不是每个人都愿意听到这样的直白真相。” 你本来就已经知道了这一点，但这个建议还是很有用的。毕竟，你知道他比那些普通人更善于面对残酷的现实。 |在实际操作过程中，完全没有必要失去冷静。确实一些有建设性的东西，对吧？” 加雷特看着他为你准备的那杯饮品，然后自己也点了一杯蜂蜜酒。通常我不赞成在上班时喝酒，但这次我觉得这样做对我反而有益无害。 哦，当然可以。而且，让他的顾客看到他享受自己的饮品，也没什么坏处吧？如果这种饮品对他来说足够好，那么对他们来说也应该同样不错。 他露出了一丝淡淡的微笑。干杯。 加斯和你一起喝光了杯中的酒，然后那只老狼叹了口气，放松下来，用空着的另一只手擦了擦嘴。 ] 真的，这是我的错。加斯叹了口气说道。当初它还小的时候，就应该让它多修修围栏、多砍些木头。把那些精力都消耗掉，而不是全都用来幻想冒险。我年轻的时候已经经历过够多的冒险了，相信我，我建造这个地方就是为了让它不必再经历那些无聊的事情。可这个忘恩负义的家伙却怎么着？竟然也想像它妈妈一样，跑到外面去闯荡世界。 寂静。 我现在能听到他的声音了。‘爸爸，你已经玩得够开心了，但等到我的时候，你却不让我说话。’这个孩子似乎非要通过惨痛的经历来学习东西才行…… 好吧，你们应该已经开始明白事情会如何发展了吧。在鹰棘镇附近，出现一名战士恐怕是这些年来发生的最令人兴奋的事情了。作为一个年轻而冲动的追求荣耀的人，加雷特毫不犹豫地抓住了这个参与任何类似冒险活动的机会——如果他等待其他民兵集结后再一起出发的话，这就根本算不上什么冒险了。 前一天晚上我们发生了一点争执。在短暂的沉默之后，加斯终于开口承认了。只是众多类似事件中的一件，所以我也没太当回事。我告诉加雷特，他是个白痴——事实上他确实如此——而且他在森林之外遇到的第一个真正的威胁，肯定会让他陷入麻烦。他说，如果他能独自打败那个怪物，那就证明我的话是错的……我想我当时应该说点别的，但他已经气冲冲地离开了房间。他真和他妈妈一样。 加斯叹了口气。很抱歉要把这件事告诉你，但是你确实自找的。没有人应该乐意把自己的丑事公之于众。 是的，你确实是这么要求的。但至少现在你知道加雷特为什么会冲进古林去了，这样当你前往伐木营地时，可能会更容易找到他。 考虑到现在树林里到处都有那些东西在游荡，他要么躲在某个地方，要么就逃到了营地里。他确实有点傻，但至少我把他教育得还不错，所以他应该不会那个愚蠢至极。 那你就留意着吧。 加斯点了点头，看着你喝完蜂蜜酒，然后拿起了那个杯子。如果你找到他还活着，我想他这时候一定会很愿意回家。否则……就别把他带回来，好吗？格温是个好女孩，我觉得她承受不了这个打击。

rows.original: All right, you've asked all the pertinent questions. You'd better hop to it, then. Missing sons and logging camps aren't going to find themselves. "One more thing." Garth holds up a hand. "Wait here, I've got something to give you." Oh? Setting down his mug and cloth, Garth disappears up the stairs and returns shortly after with a small bundle wrapped in canvas, thrusting it into your hands. Untying the string, you spy several sundry goods within — flint and tinder, a small amount of simple, dry wood, string, wooden poles, and hard metal pegs and a mallet. "I have the feeling that you'll be needing to stay out there in the woods while you wrap up matters at the camp. You won't sleep comfortably, but you'll sleep all right." [pc.bg hunter| [pc.isDK| Sure, why not. You can survive well enough with just sleeping up a tree, but you're not going to take creature comforts for granted. If Garth's willing to give you a gift, hell, you'll take it. | You try to tell Garth that his gift isn't really needed, that someone with your training can sleep well enough in the wild without needing additional camping supplies, but Garth won't have any of it. "If you're going out after my son, it's the least I can do. There's got to be some reason that he hasn't come home yet, and I want you to be as fully rested as possible before facing it. No reason to sell yourself short." Well, if he insists... ] | While you're not too familiar with how to use this camping equipment, Garth is kind enough to give a quick explanation as to how to pitch and strike the tent quickly and efficiently. At any rate, it'll beat sleeping on the bare ground. "Least I can do," Garth says when you try to thank him. "You're going out after my fool of a son, and I want you to be as rested as possible before facing down what's preventing him from coming home." Yeah, that makes sense. If Garret is anything like his father, he's not going to let a small obstacle get in his way; something pretty significant must've happened to hold him up. ] Garth grunts and gives you one final nod before turning to his cloth and mug. "Well, that's about it, [pc.name]. If you need more camping supplies, you can always buy some from Leorah. Good luck out there — or at least, better luck than what some others have been having..." You have acquired some camping supplies. In order to use these, select %"Create Camp" when on a campable map node. The campsite's duration will depend on how dangerous the location is — some camps are permanent, while others may only last for a single use before needing to be struck. You may purchase camping tools and supplies from Leorah in Hawkethorne, should you need any extra.
rows.translation: 好吧，你们已经问完了所有相关的问题。那你们最好赶紧开始行动吧。失踪的儿子和伐木营地可不会自己找上门来的。 还有一件事。加思举起了手。在这里等着，我有东西要给你。 哦？ 加思放下他的杯子和小布，然后上楼去了，不久后带着一个用帆布包裹的小包裹回来了，直接把它塞到了你的手里。你解开绳子，发现里面装着一些杂物——打火石和引火物、少量干燥的木柴、绳子、木棍，还有一些坚硬的金属钉子和一根木槌。 我有种感觉，在你处理完营地的事情之后，你可能需要待在树林里。虽然睡觉不会很舒服，但应该也能熬过去。 [pc.bg hunter| [pc.isDK| 当然，为什么不呢。只要能睡在树上，你也能过得不错，但你也不会把那些舒适的生活条件视为理所当然。如果加斯愿意送你一份礼物，那你当然会接受。 | 你试图告诉加斯，他的那些礼物其实并不是真的必需品，像你这样受过训练的人，在野外完全可以不用额外的露营用品也能睡得很好，但加斯根本不会听你的。 如果你要去找我儿子，这是我至少能做的。他还没回家，肯定有什么原因，我希望你在面对这个问题之前能充分休息，没有必要委屈自己。 好吧，如果他坚持的话…… ] | 虽然你没有太加思对如何使用这些露营装备非常熟悉，他非常热心地为大家简要讲解了如何快速而高效地搭建和拆卸帐篷。总之，这总比直接睡在露地上要好得多。 这是我至少应该做的。加思说，当你试图感谢他时你是要去追我那个愚蠢的儿子，所以在面对阻碍他回家的那些问题之前，我希望你能尽可能地休息好。 是啊，这很有道理。如果加雷特真和他父亲一样，他肯定不会让一些小障碍阻碍自己前进的；肯定发生了什么非常重要的事情，才让他停下了脚步。 ] 加思哼了一声，最后向你点了点头，然后便转向他的布巾和杯子去了。嗯，差不多就是这样了。 [pc.name]如果你还需要更多的露营用品，随时都可以从莱奥拉那里购买。祝你好运吧——至少，希望你的运气能比其他人好一些…… 你已经获取了一些露营用品。要使用这些用品，请在位于可露营地图节点的位置选择“创建营地”。露营地点的持续时间取决于该地点的危险程度——有些营地可以永久使用，而有些则可能只能使用一次后就需要重新搭建。如果你还需要额外的露营工具或用品，可以前往鹰棘镇的莱奥拉那里购买。

rows.original: Garth looks at you and makes a slow, chewing motion before he sets down his mug and cloth on the counter. "You've news of Garret?" Yes, you just said that. "He's not with you, I see." Oh, not to worry. He's not actually hurt or anything, just... unable to return to Hawkethorne with you. Garth's gaze turns to icy steel. "Explain." You do just that, leaving no detail of Garret's little predicament untouched. Garth listens on with a perfectly straight poker face, and when you're finally done, pours you a tall, foaming glass of beer. "Here. For your trouble." Hey, you won't say no to a free drink. Any comment on Garret, though? "It's about what I expected of him. Always enamored of playing the big damned hero... although I'll say that this was unexpected. Or maybe not, it does remind me of how I met his mother." You sip the beer. Mm, not bad. Why, did he choose to sacrifice himself, get locked up in a cage, and be his future wife's sex-pet so that she wouldn't harass his friends? "Two out of three isn't too bad." Apple doesn't fall far from the tree, does it? "That's the problem, [pc.name]. If only he'd taken more after his mother... well, he does. The bad bits, I might say. But if the witch's not going to hurt him, I can relax a bit, make sure the militia's a little more prepared before going out to get him and all the people at Westbank safely out." He won't need to do that if you save everyone first. And he does seem to be a bit blase about his son's safety... "Maybe, maybe. Always good to have a backup plan, though. And Garret's not going to keel over and croak, if he's already survived that long; he's made of tougher stuff than that. Who knows, maybe he's secretly enjoying himself... "Either way, you were kind enough to come back and let me know what's what. If you don't think you can handle this elf witch yourself, I think old man Sanders would be willing to lend a hand." You'll consider it. "Great. Finish up that beer, and do what you need to do, [pc.name]. I'm sure Garret's counting on you to get him out of that cage and away from Westbank — but probably not too quickly."
rows.translation: 加斯看着你，做了一个缓慢的咀嚼动作，然后把他的杯子和布放在柜台上。你有关于加雷特的消息吗？ 是的，你刚刚就是这么说的。 我看，他并不在你身边。 哦，别担心。他其实并没有受伤，只是……无法和你一起回到鹰棘镇了。 加斯的目光变得冰冷如钢铁。解释一下。 你就是这样做的，把加雷特所处的困境中的每一个细节都描述得淋漓尽致。加斯面无表情地听着，而当你终于讲完的时候，他便为你倒了一杯高高的、冒着泡沫的啤酒。 给，算是补偿你刚才的麻烦了。 嘿，免费的饮料你总不会拒绝吧？不过，对于加雷特，你有什么看法吗？ 这正是我对他所期望的。他总是热衷于扮演那种伟大的英雄角色……不过说实话，这次的表现确实出乎我的意料。或许也不算吧，这让我想起当初是如何认识他母亲的。 你喝了一口啤酒，嗯，还不错。为什么他要选择牺牲自己，被关在笼子里，成为他未来妻子的玩物，只为了让妻子不再骚扰他的朋友们呢？ 三分之二已经很不错了。 苹果掉下来也不会离树太远，不是吗？ 就是那个。问题， [pc.name]要是他能多学点他母亲的做法该多好……嗯，其实他也是这么做的。至少在那些不好的方面，他是这么做的。不过既然那个女巫不会伤害他，那我就可以稍微放松一点了，先确保民兵组织做好充分准备，然后再去把他和西岸的所有人安全地带出来。 如果你先救出所有人，他就不需要那么做了。而且他似乎确实对儿子的安全有些漠不关心…… 也许吧，也许吧。不过，有备无患总是好的。而且加雷特已经活了这么久，他肯定不会那么轻易就倒下的——他的体质可比那强多了。谁知道呢，也许他现在还过得挺开心呢…… 不管怎样，你还是好心回来告诉了我事情的真相。如果你觉得自己无法独自应对这个精灵女巫，我想桑德斯老人应该会愿意帮忙的。 你会考虑这个建议的。 太好了。喝完那杯啤酒，然后去做你需要做的事情吧。 [pc.name]我敢肯定，加雷特正指望你能帮他摆脱那个笼子，离开韦斯特班克——不过他大概也不希望你动作太快。
rows.raw: " Garth looks at you and makes a slow, chewing motion before he sets down his mug and cloth on the counter. "You've news of Garret?" Yes, you just said that. "He's not with you, I see." Oh, not to worry. He's not actually hurt or anything, just... unable to return to Hawkethorne with you. Garth's gaze turns to icy steel. "Explain." You do just that, leaving no detail of Garret's little predicament untouched. Garth listens on with a perfectly straight poker face, and when you're finally done, pours you a tall, foaming glass of beer. "Here. For your trouble." Hey, you won't say no to a free drink. Any comment on Garret, though? "It's about what I expected of him. Always enamored of playing the big damned hero... although I'll say that this was unexpected. Or maybe not, it does remind me of how I met his mother." You sip the beer. Mm, not bad. Why, did he choose to sacrifice himself, get locked up in a cage, and be his future wife's sex-pet so that she wouldn't harass his friends? "Two out of three isn't too bad." Apple doesn't fall far from the tree, does it? "That's the problem, [pc.name]. If only he'd taken more after his mother... well, he does. The bad bits, I might say. But if the witch's not going to hurt him, I can relax a bit, make sure the militia's a little more prepared before going out to get him and all the people at Westbank safely out." He won't need to do that if you save everyone first. And he does seem to be a bit blase about his son's safety... "Maybe, maybe. Always good to have a backup plan, though. And Garret's not going to keel over and croak, if he's already survived that long; he's made of tougher stuff than that. Who knows, maybe he's secretly enjoying himself... "Either way, you were kind enough to come back and let me know what's what. If you don't think you can handle this elf witch yourself, I think old man Sanders would be willing to lend a hand." You'll consider it. "Great. Finish up that beer, and do what you need to do, [pc.name]. I'm sure Garret's counting on you to get him out of that cage and away from Westbank — but probably not too quickly.""

rows.original: Ah, the familiar sights, sounds and smells of the Frost Hound. They hit you like a slap to the face the moment you pass through the doors, jerking you to wakefulness[dayNight|. There're a few people in here having their meals, or simply sitting around having a round of drinks — clearly there's no time too early to have a stiff one up here in the Frost Marches.| despite the late hour. At this time of day, the common room is packed with people having a drink or two to relax from the daily grind, and while you get a few glances as you enter none of them linger on you overlong. Guess you're just another fellow patron now, huh. ] You've just found an empty table and are wondering what you should do next when the doors burst open once more and Garret trudges in. A gust of chill air follows at his back, causing the fire to flicker and dance in the hearth; he's still wearing the clothes he picked up at Westbank, and passes through the common room, a sullen aura following him like a stormcloud. As he passes by the bar, Garth clears his throat. "Garret." Garret narrows his eyes. "Old man. Looking to rub salt in my wound?" "I could, but you're humiliated enough as it is. I heard that it wasn't all bad, though." "Right. Of course they wouldn't be able to keep their mouths shut. Why, would you have liked to be in my place? I've heard from old man Sanders what Mom liked to do to you." Garth ignores the byplay. "I wouldn't even have gotten caught in the first place, Garret. You should learn to accept the help of others in areas, to fill in for your weaknesses." "Don't treat me like a pup, old man. I don't need your help all the time." "The fact that you allowed yourself to get caught and thrown in a cage — magic or no — says otherwise." At this point, it's so silent that you probably could have heard a pin drop on the sawdust-covered floor. Garth continues polishing the mug in his hands without so much as budging, despite the stony look Garret's giving him. Half the patrons present are openly staring, while the other half are desperately pretending not to notice the argument. "We shouldn't do this in front of the guests, old man. Let's head on upstairs." Garth nods, and calmly sets down the mug. "Gwyn!" It doesn't take long for Gwyneth to arrive, clutching her skirts as she answers her father's summons. "Daddy?" "Mind the bar for me for a moment. Your brother and I are going to have a talk." Gwyn looks uncertain at that and her ears droop, but she nods and acquiesces. Garth and Garret tromp on upstairs, their footsteps pounding heavily at the wood, and gradually fade away. Huh. If you don't have anything to do at the moment — and if you're feeling voyeuristic, of course — you could always head up and see how that argument goes. Of course, if you'd rather not bother, you can always wash this off and forget about it... Do you want to head up and eavesdrop on father and son?
rows.translation: 啊，那些熟悉的光景、声音和气味——它们就像一记耳光，在你穿过大门的瞬间击中你的面庞，将你从沉睡中惊醒。[dayNight|这里有几个人正在吃饭，或者只是坐着喝着酒——显然，在冰霜边境，什么时候开始喝酒都不为迟。| 尽管已经很晚了。在这个时间段，公共休息室里挤满了人们，他们喝上一两杯酒，放松一下一天的疲惫。当你走进去的时候，确实会收到一些目光，但没有人会长时间地注视你。 看来，你现在只不过是这里的另一位顾客罢了，嗯。 ] 你刚找到一张空桌子，正在思考接下来该做什么，这时门突然再次被推开，加雷特步履蹒跚地走了进来。一阵寒风随之从他身后吹来，使得壁炉里的火焰开始闪烁跳动；他仍然穿着在韦斯特班克时拿到的那些衣服，穿过公共休息室时，周围仿佛笼罩着一层阴沉的气息，就像乌云一般紧随其后。 当他经过吧台时，加雷特清了清嗓子。加雷特。 加雷特眯起了眼睛。老头，是来往我伤口上撒盐的吗？ 我本来可以那么做的，但你现在已经够受羞辱了。不过，我听说其实也没那么糟糕。 没错。他们当然不可能保持沉默。嗯，你难道想取代我的位置吗？我可是从桑德斯老头那里听说了，妈妈以前是怎么对待你的。 加斯对周围的闲言碎语充耳不闻。加雷特，其实我本来根本就不会被抓住的。你应该学会在某些方面接受别人的帮助，这样才能弥补自己的不足。 别把我当小狗一样对待，老头。我并不总是需要你的帮助。 你竟然让自己被抓住并被关进笼子里——无论其中是否涉及魔法——这一事实恰恰说明了相反的情况。 此时四周一片寂静，甚至连针掉在满是木屑的地板上的声音都能听得清清楚楚。加斯依然双手握着那个杯子不停地擦拭，丝毫没有因为加雷特那充满敌意的目光而有所动摇。在场的顾客中，有一半都在公然盯着他们看，而另外一半则拼命装作没有注意到这场争吵。 老兄，我们不该在客人面前做这种事，我们还是上楼去吧。 加斯点了点头，然后平静地将杯子放了下来。格温！ 格温妮丝很快就到了，她紧抓着自己的裙摆，应召去了见她的父亲。爸爸？ 请稍等一下，我需要和你哥哥谈谈。 格温听到这话后显得有些犹豫，耳朵也耷拉了下来，但最终还是点了点头表示同意。加斯和加雷特咚咚咚地跑上了楼，他们的脚步声在木板上发出沉重的回响，随后渐渐消失了。 嗯……如果你现在没什么事做，而且如果你有点好奇的话，当然可以上去看看他们俩的争论进展如何。当然，如果你觉得没必要麻烦，也可以直接忽略这件事，把它忘掉…… 你想上去偷听父子俩的谈话吗？
