rows.original: You know what? Why not? Neither Garth nor Garret seem to be in any state of mind to notice someone spying on them — this should be a piece of cake even for the most fumble-footed of people. You wait for them to tromp upstairs, then [party.hasCompanions|leave [party.compNames] waiting at the table before you ]stand and follow, making it look as if you're just heading up to your room. It's not hard to find father and son — they've sequestered themselves at the end of the hallway on the inn's second storey, the shape of the passage channelling their voices down to you. Finding a nice spot just off the landing where you won't be spotted, you do your best to listen in... "Hmph." Garth's voice. "Do you know the trouble you've caused everyone, Garret? If not for [pc.name] being so kind as to get you out — let's just say we were just about to set off for Westbank ourselves." "I'll find Sanders and apologize to him tomorrow morning. You, though — you never fail to find fault with anything I do, old man. I went all the way to Westbank just to prove myself to you." "Am I supposed to be honored or something? You failed, got caught, and complicated an already bad situation. Not to mention, you made Gwyn worried sick." "Don't use Gwyn against me!" In the aftermath of Garret's outburst, silence. Garth rubs his chin and considers his son. "I suppose I may have crossed a line there..." Garret scowls and sinks back. "Why are you always starting these arguments, old man? You're going out of your way to pick fights with me." "You could stand to lose that defiant attitude as well; I suppose that's where we'll start today. Grab your practice sword and meet me in the yard; we need to work off your aggression." "Bring it on. I'll use my fists instead." A chuckle. "As you wish. I'd like to see if you've learned anything from what you went through. From what I heard, you wrestled the druidess' pet warg into submission. That has to count for something." Silence. And then: "Don't tell me you were actually praising me." "Credit is where credit's due. Although I wouldn't be too sure of myself if I were you — experience trumps youth any day. Now, enough talk — I'll see you in the yard." That seems to be it. Their footsteps, long and heavy, come thundering down the hallway, and you figure it's time to split, quickly heading downstairs and taking your old place at the table. Barely enough time has passed for you to settle in and look nonchalant when Garth and Garret bowl out into the common room, sweeping past Gwyn, through the kitchen, and out the back door. Gwyn looks completely unperturbed by the commotion, calmly polishing a mug, the spitting image of her father. Poor girl must be used to these by now... Looks like that's that, though. You aren't going to be able to sneak past Gwyn to see what else is going on with father and son, so that's the end of it. Well, what now?
rows.translation: 你知道吗？为什么不呢？无论是加斯还是加雷特，现在似乎都完全没有注意到有人在偷窥他们——即使是对最笨手笨脚的人来说，这也应该是一件轻而易举的事。你就等着他们上楼去，然后[party.hasCompanions|离开[party.compNames]在你之前就已经在等待了。 ]站好不动，装作只是要去自己的房间而已。 找到那对父子并不难——他们躲在旅馆二楼走廊的尽头，走廊的构造使得他们的声音能够传到你这里。你在楼梯平台附近找了一个不会被发现的合适位置，然后尽你最大的努力去偷听…… 哼。加斯的声音。加勒特，你知道你给大家带来了多大的麻烦吗？要不是因为[pc.name]您真是太好了，还特地来接您——其实我们本来也正准备动身前往西岸的。 明天早上我会去找桑德斯并向他道歉。不过你啊——你总是对我做的每一件事都挑毛病，老头。我专程跑到西岸去，就是为了向你证明自己。 我难道应该感到荣幸吗？你失败了，被抓住了，还让本已糟糕的局面变得更加复杂。更不用说，你还把格温吓坏了。 别用格温来对付我！ 在加勒特发怒之后，一片寂静。加斯摸着下巴，思考着自己的儿子。 我想，我可能确实有点过分了…… 加勒特皱起了眉头，然后又坐了回去。老头子，你为什么总是挑起这些争论呢？你是故意来找我麻烦的吧。 你也可以改掉那种固执的态度；我想，今天我们就从这里开始吧。拿上你的练习剑，到院子里来见我，我们需要帮你消除那种攻击性。 来吧，那我只好用拳头了。 一阵轻笑。如你所愿。我想看看你从这段经历中学到了什么。据我所知，你成功让那位女德鲁伊的宠物战争兽屈服了，这一点肯定值得肯定。 寂静。然后：别告诉我你真的赞扬我。 该表扬谁就表扬谁。不过如果我是你的话，可能也不会太有把握……经验永远比年轻更重要。好了，废话不多说，我们在院子里见。 看来就这样了。他们那重型而悠长的脚步声在走廊里回荡，你立刻意识到是时候躲开了——迅速下楼，回到原来的座位上。还没等你坐稳下来，装出一副若无其事的样子，加斯和加勒就冲进了客厅，从格温身边经过，穿过厨房，然后从后门走了出去。 格温对周围的喧闹丝毫不在意，她平静地擦拭着杯子，简直和她父亲一模一样。这个可怜的女孩肯定已经习惯了这些……不过，看来这次是真的没办法从格温身边悄悄过去了，想看看里面发生了什么也是不可能的。否则父子俩之间发生了一些事情，所以事情就这样结束了。 那么，现在该怎么办呢？

rows.original: While it might be tempting to sneak up and listen in, especially given how involved you were in Garret's escape from Westbank, you force yourself back into your seat. After all, this is really none of your business — and you wouldn't like someone else eavesdropping in on your conversations, would you? Some of the patrons are still a little ruffled by Garret's entrance, but a round or two of drinks clears that right up. Things settle down in the common room, Gwyn works the bar and taps — something she's clearly had a lot of practice at — and it's as if nothing had ever happened. Almost. An hour or two later, Garret returns — not from the stairs this time, but from the back door where the inn's chicken coop is located. He says nothing, but he's clearly got at least two dark and angry-looking bruises on his face, enough to stand out against the grayish-black of his fur. Prowling up to the bar, he plonks down a couple of coins on the bar and tells Gwyn to get him a tall tankard of mead. Several stares turn his way, until he gives them an angry snarl. "What's so interesting? Don't you have enough shit of your own to deal with?" Garret waits until he's sure most people are decidedly not looking at him, then settles down, planting his elbows on the bar counter. "Fucking gossips." "Daddy beat you up again?" she says as she pours out a draught. "Don't say it like that," Garret replies with a growl. "I think I gave as good as I got. Punching is so much more satisfying than poking away with a sword." "He's right, though. You look a lot less angry now." "Gwyn..." "I'm just glad to have you home and away from that adventure. Some of the people from Westbank dropped in earlier; they were very grateful for you saving them from that witch." Garret says nothing and downs the tankard in a couple of gulps, then adds another two coins to the counter. You get the feeling that this is all that there's going to be, and you should probably move on. Time's a-wasting, after all.
rows.translation: 虽然你很想偷偷走过去偷听，尤其是考虑到你在加雷特从韦斯特班克逃脱的过程中发挥了那么大的作用，但你还是强迫自己坐回了座位上。毕竟，这件事真的与你无关——你也不会希望别人偷听你的谈话吧。你的你们愿意聊聊天吗？” 有些顾客对加雷特的到来还是感到有些不满，但喝上一两杯酒之后，这种情绪就消散了。公共休息室里的气氛渐渐平静下来，格温开始在吧台忙碌着——她显然已经非常熟练地掌握了这项工作——仿佛什么事情都没有发生过一样。 差不多一个小时或两个小时后，加雷特回来了——这次他并不是从楼梯上来，而是从后门回来的，那里正好是客栈的鸡舍所在。他什么话也没说，但他的脸上明显有两条颜色深沉、看起来很明显的淤伤，这些淤伤在他灰黑色的毛皮上显得格外醒目。他悄悄走到吧台前，往吧台上扔了几枚硬币，然后让格温给他拿一杯大杯的蜂蜜酒来。有几道目光投向了他，直到他愤怒地低吼了一声，那些目光才纷纷移开。 有什么好玩的？你自己的麻烦还不够多吗？加雷特等到确认大多数人都已经明确表态之后，才不是看着他，然后坐了下来，将肘部放在吧台上。该死的八卦者。 爸爸又打你了吗？她一边说着，一边喝下了一杯酒。 别那么说。加雷特低吼着回应道。我觉得我已经尽了全力。用拳头出击比用剑轻轻刺击要让人更有满足感。 不过他说得对，你现在看起来没那么生气了。 格温…… 我只是很高兴你能平安回家，远离那些危险。早些时候，有一些来自西岸的人来拜访过我；他们都非常感激你救了他们，让他们摆脱了那个女巫的威胁。 加雷特什么也没说，一饮而尽了杯中的酒，然后又在柜台上又放了两枚硬币。你有一种感觉，这就是全部了，或许应该继续前进了。毕竟，时间在一分一秒地流逝。
rows.raw: ' While it might be tempting to sneak up and listen in, especially given how involved you were in Garret's escape from Westbank, you force yourself back into your seat. After all, this is really none of your business — and you wouldn't like someone else eavesdropping in on your conversations, would you? Some of the patrons are still a little ruffled by Garret's entrance, but a round or two of drinks clears that right up. Things settle down in the common room, Gwyn works the bar and taps — something she's clearly had a lot of practice at — and it's as if nothing had ever happened. Almost. An hour or two later, Garret returns — not from the stairs this time, but from the back door where the inn's chicken coop is located. He says nothing, but he's clearly got at least two dark and angry-looking bruises on his face, enough to stand out against the grayish-black of his fur. Prowling up to the bar, he plonks down a couple of coins on the bar and tells Gwyn to get him a tall tankard of mead. Several stares turn his way, until he gives them an angry snarl. "What's so interesting? Don't you have enough shit of your own to deal with?" Garret waits until he's sure most people are decidedly not looking at him, then settles down, planting his elbows on the bar counter. "Fucking gossips." "Daddy beat you up again?" she says as she pours out a draught. "Don't say it like that," Garret replies with a growl. "I think I gave as good as I got. Punching is so much more satisfying than poking away with a sword." "He's right, though. You look a lot less angry now." "Gwyn..." "I'm just glad to have you home and away from that adventure. Some of the people from Westbank dropped in earlier; they were very grateful for you saving them from that witch." Garret says nothing and downs the tankard in a couple of gulps, then adds another two coins to the counter. You get the feeling that this is all that there's going to be, and you should probably move on. Time's a-wasting, after all.'

rows.original: This is none of your business.

As you're heading up to your room, voices coming down the hallway from one of the empty guest rooms catch your attention. You're well-acquainted with Garth's voice by now, and the other one... yes, it's Garret. Another tiff? Hmm... "Old man. What do you want? Are you here to lecture me some more? Perhaps I didn't make the bed properly, or is there still dust on the windowsill?" Silence. "Hey, if you've got something to say, say it. Don't stare at me like that." "No, no. Nothing of the sort, Garret. I came to say... come what may, you have to watch over Gwyneth, all right?" Garret snorts. "Pah, I'm her older brother." "By a few moments." "Doesn't change that fact. You'll never need to remind me of that responsibility. What's this about?" "Nothing, son. Just promise me — no matter what happens — you must look after Gwyneth. She has the body of a shieldmaiden, but the mind and soul of a puppy. It is what it is — no matter what she does with her life, she'll always need someone else to take care of her." "Of course..." More silence. "What's up with you, old man? Don't tell me you're starting to feel your age." "Hah... I'd gain nothing by lying to myself. I'm feeling the wind in my bones more than I used to, but that's not the problem I have here." "Then what is it? Is it about the weird crap going on out beyond the gates? The stuff with the demoness and all?" "More so, yes. This isn't a campfire story, nor is it a legend, Garret. Failure is always a possibility. Why do you think I'm letting [pc.name] stay here for free? [pc.HeShe]'s the best chance that we have. A few coins isn't going to matter if Savarra itself is at stake." "Hah, so that's what this is about. You're supposed to say something smart like 'I have complete faith in your victory' and charge the sop anyway. I don't see Ivris or Ogrish giving their shit out for free. Why should you?" "So you'd charge [pc.name] to stay here?" "No, but not because [pc.heShe]'s out to save the world or somesuch. More because I owe [pc.himHer] one." "Hmph." "Is your body working right, though, old man? Speak up if you're not feeling well. I mean, it'd be terribly inconvenient if you died and left Gwyn and I all on our own." "You're just like your mother." "What's that supposed to mean?" "There's no deeper meaning to it. You're just like your mother. And as for me — don't worry about that; I'm just getting older. It happens to us all, but I can't die until you're a proper adult. I wouldn't be able to bear that shame, even in the grave... although with the kind of headway you're making, I suppose that means that I'll be living forever." "Ech. Living forever. You hear the stories of people who make stupid wishes like that. Never turns out well." "Then grow up if you want me to be able to die peacefully." "You're clearly well enough to throw jabs at me, so I'm not worried anymore. Don't worry about Gwyn, old man. I'll die before she does." "In that case, I've nothing else to say to you. Finish up with the rest of the rooms, and we can gather for Gwyn's cooking." "Boiled onions and turnips again..." That seems to be the end of the conversation, so you duck into your room before Garth can come out and catch you eavesdropping on him.
rows.translation: 当你走向自己的房间时，听到走廊尽头某间空置的客房里传来的声音，引起了你的注意。你现在已经非常熟悉加思的声音了，而另一个声音……没错，那就是加雷特。 又吵架了？嗯…… 老头，你到底想干什么？是来再训斥我一顿的吗？难道是我铺床铺得不好，还是窗台上还有灰尘？ 寂静。 嘿，如果你有什么话要说，就直说吧。别那样盯着我看。 不，不是这样的，加雷特。我是来告诉你的……无论发生什么，你都必须照顾好格温妮丝，好吗？ 加雷特哼了一声。哼，我是她的哥哥。 再等几分钟就好。 但这并不能改变事实。你永远都不需要提醒我这一点。那个责任？这到底是怎么回事？ 没什么，孩子。只要你答应我——无论发生什么——你必须一定要照顾好格温妮丝。她有着女战士般强健的身体，但心思却像只小狗一样单纯。事实就是如此——无论她将来选择如何生活，她始终都需要别人来照顾她。 当然……更加沉寂。你怎么了，老头？该不会是开始觉得自己年纪大了吧？ 哈……对自己撒谎也不会有什么好处。我现在比以前更加清楚地感受到了那种‘风在骨子里吹动’的感觉，但这个问题并不在于此。 那么到底是什么事情呢？是不是和城门外发生的那些奇怪的事情有关？比如那个女恶魔的事情？ 更重要的是，确实如此。这既不是篝火边的故事，也不是什么传说，加雷特。失败总是有可能发生的。你为什么认为我会允许[pc.name]可以免费在这里停留吗？ [pc.HeShe]这是我们目前拥有的最佳机会。如果萨瓦拉本身的安危都受到威胁，那么几枚硬币根本无关紧要。 哈，原来如此。你本应该说些诸如‘我完全相信你会获胜’之类的话，然后无论如何都要冲上去战斗。我看艾薇莉丝和奥格里斯这些人可不会白白付出努力，你为什么就要这么做呢？ 所以你是想收费的啊。 [pc.name]要留在这里吗？ 不，但原因并非如此。 [pc.heShe]是出去拯救世界之类的。主要是因为我欠他一个人情。 [pc.himHer]一个。 哼。 不过，老兄，你的身体还正常吧？如果感觉不舒服，就一定要说出来。毕竟，要是你突然死了，把格温和我丢在这里，那可就太麻烦了。 你和你妈妈真是一模一样。 这到底是什么意思？ 这其中并没有什么更深层的含义。你只是和你母亲一样而已。至于我——别担心这个；我只是年纪大了而已。这种事情每个人都会遇到，但在你真正长大成人之前，我是不能死的。那样的话，即使在我死后，我也无法承受那种羞耻……不过，看你现在的进步，我想这意味着我可能会永远活下去吧。 唉……永远活着。你肯定听说过那些人们许下这种愚蠢愿望的故事吧？结果从来都不会好起来。 那么，如果你想让我能够安详地离开这个世界，就成熟起来吧。 看你的样子已经恢复得不错了，居然还能跟我顶嘴，那我也就放心了。老兄，别担心格温，我肯定会在她之前死掉。 那样的话，我没有什么其他要说的了。你们把剩下的房间也检查完毕，然后我们就聚在一起吃格温做的饭吧。 又煮了洋葱和萝卜…… 看来这次谈话到此为止了，所以在加斯出来发现你在偷听他的谈话之前，你赶紧躲进了自己的房间。

rows.original: You're on your way upstairs and at the door to your room when you catch voices coming down the hallway once more. Feeling curious, you follow them until the hallway turns a corner, and spy Garth and Garret standing by a patch of open wall. The latter's got a pot of resin and a brush in his hands, and is busy caulking up the holes and cracks while the former supervises the process. "Garret." "Old man. What is it this time?" "I've been meaning to ask — why exactly did you take to fighting with your fists?" A grunt on Garret's part. "Is this a set-up for another of your lectures, old man?" "No, no. I'm truly curious." "Because it was something you couldn't do, and I could. There's nothing a blade or bludgeon can do that I can't with leather and studs." "Hrm. So at the end of the day, you were doing it just to rebel against my instruction. And here I thought it was something you loved." "Take up the sword and live in your shadow forever? No thanks, I'll pass. But there's no reason it can't be both." Garth chuckles. "You're just like your mother." "There you go again, just like last time. What's that supposed to mean?" "Again, there's no deeper meaning. You're just like your mother." "And how, exactly, am I like her?" "You prefer to be on top, just like she did. Wouldn't give up until she got on top. Guess that's what chafed you about being that elf witch's pet, wasn't it?" Garret's voice is considerably more subdued. "Speaking of Mom..." "Yes?" "When are you going to tell Gwyn what really happened to her?" Now it's Garth's turn to fall silent. "Not anytime soon. Maybe never. She wouldn't be able to take it." "That doesn't sound responsible, old man." "No, it isn't. But it's best for Gwyn that she never knows the truth. She's just a big puppy; it would break her. Or are you going to say otherwise?" "...No." "Then you understand." Garth coughs, flattening his ears against his head. "I only want the best for her." "Because she accepts anything you say without putting up a fight?" "Now, now, Garret — why the antagonism here?" "Gwyn was pleasant to be with when I was younger; I enjoyed playing with her even when we got older. What you put me through, though... just thinking about it makes me angry." "I pushed you harder than I did your sister because her spirit isn't suited to violence, even when it's necessary. Yours is, though. With your defiant attitude, I was never surprised that you were fuming all the while — your training involved a lot of hard work that I had to force you through. Turning you into a first-rate fighter was no easy task." Garret lowers his brush and grins triumphantly at his father. "Ha!" "What?" "You just called me a first-rate fighter, old man. You can't take that back." "Hmph." Garret closes his eyes and folds his hands. "I will give that you have some modicum of skill in what you've chosen to do. That, and you're capable of working hard when the mood takes you — which is far less often than it should. And you've still got a long way to go, judging by what happened at Westbank." "She was a witch, old man. She cast a spell to hold me in place." "As if that excuses anything. You think I didn't deal with any number of magicians in my day? What was it again — 'no matter how powerful the wizard, a knife between the shoulder blades will seriously cramp his style.' As things stand, I've still got a lot of painstaking work to do in the future." "You never give any ground, do you, old man?" Garth and Garret's voices slowly begin to fade away, and at length you hear them descend another set of stairs. Seems like that's the end of that... nothing left to do now but to head back to your room, it seems. Although, it must be said that the conversation has given you something to think about, even if you'll never be able to discuss it with Garret directly... not without admitting you've been listening in on his conversations, at any rate.
rows.translation: 当你正往楼上走，即将到达自己的房间门口时，又听到有声音从走廊里传来。出于好奇，你顺着声音走去，直到走廊拐了一个弯，然后看到了加斯和加雷特站在一片裸露的墙前。加雷特手里拿着一罐树脂和一把刷子，正在忙着修补那些孔洞和裂缝，而加斯则在一旁监督着这个过程。 加雷特。 老头，这次又有什么事？ 我本来就想问的——你究竟为什么喜欢用拳头打架呢？ 加雷特发出了一声低哼。老兄，这是不是又在为你的某个讲座做准备啊？ 不，不是的。我真的只是出于好奇而已。 因为那是你做不到的事情，而我能做到。没有任何武器能够做到的事情，我都能用皮革和钉子来完成。 嗯，说到底，你这么做只是为了反抗我的命令。而我还以为你是真的喜欢这样做呢。 拿起剑，永远活在阴影之中吗？算了，谢谢，我不要。不过，其实两者完全可以兼得啊。 加思轻声笑了起来。你和你妈妈真是一模一样。 又来这一套，和上次一样。这到底是什么意思？ 再说一次，这里并没有什么深层次的含义。你其实就是和你妈妈一样。 那么，我究竟在哪些方面和她相似呢？ 你就像她一样，总是喜欢占据上风。不达到目的绝不罢休。我想，正是因为这样，你才对成为那个精灵女巫的宠儿感到不满吧？ 加雷特的声音明显低沉了许多。说到妈妈…… 是吗？ 你到底什么时候才会告诉格温，她身上真正发生了什么？ 现在，轮到加斯保持沉默了。短期内不太可能。也许永远都不会。她根本无法承受。 这么说可不太负责任啊，老兄。 不，并非如此。但对格温来说，最好永远不要知道真相。她还只是个小孩子，知道这些会让她受到伤害的。难道你有什么不同的意见吗？ ……不。 那么你就明白了吧。加思咳嗽了一声，把耳朵贴在头上。我只是希望她能得到最好的。 就因为她从不反抗，总是毫无异议地接受你说的任何话？ 好了好了，加雷特——为什么要在这里闹矛盾呢？ 在我年轻的时候，和格温在一起很愉快；即使我们年纪大了，我也喜欢和她一起玩。不过你让我经历的一切……光是想到这些就让我感到愤怒。 我对你的要求比对你妹妹更严格，因为她的性格不适合使用暴力，即使在必要的情况下也是如此。而你的性格却适合。鉴于你那种反抗的精神，你一直处于愤怒状态也就不足为奇了——你的训练过程充满了艰辛，我不得不强迫你坚持下去。要把你培养成一名一流的战士，确实不是一件容易的事。 加雷特放下画笔，得意地朝父亲笑了笑。哈！ 什么？ 你刚才称我为一流的战士，老兄。这话可不能收回。 哼。加雷特闭上了眼睛，双手交叠在一起。我必须承认，你在自己选择做的事情上确实具备一定的能力。此外，当你决定努力的时候，你也确实能够全身心地投入其中——不过这种情况发生的频率其实远低于应有的水平。而且从西岸发生的事情来看，你还有很长的路要走啊。 她是个女巫，老人家。她施展了魔法。拼写把我固定在那里。 好像这样就能成为任何事情的借口似的。你以为我这些年来没有遇到过很多魔法师吗？好像是这么说的来着——‘无论那个巫师有多强大，只要在他背后插把刀，他的法术就根本无法施展了。’目前来看，我未来还有很多艰苦的工作要做呢。 你从来都不会退让半步，是吧，老家伙？ 加思和加雷特的声音渐渐消失了，最终你听到他们走下了另一段楼梯。看来这件事就这样结束了……现在似乎除了回到自己的房间，也没有别的事情可做了。不过，必须承认，这段对话确实让你有了很多思考的空间，尽管你永远也无法直接与加雷特讨论这些事情……至少，在不承认自己一直在偷听他的谈话之前，你是无法和他讨论的。

"Now, now, Garret — why the antagonism here?" "Gwyn was pleasant to be with when I was younger; I enjoyed playing with her even when we got older. What you put me through, though... just thinking about it makes me angry." "I pushed you harder than I did your sister because her spirit isn't suited to violence, even when it's necessary. Yours is, though. With your defiant attitude, I was never surprised that you were fuming all the while — your training involved a lot of hard work that I had to force you through. Turning you into a first-rate fighter was no easy task." Garret lowers his brush and grins triumphantly at his father. "Ha!" "What?" "You just called me a first-rate fighter, old man. You can't take that back." "Hmph." Garret closes his eyes and folds his hands. "I will give that you have some modicum of skill in what you've chosen to do. That, and you're capable of working hard when the mood takes you — which is far less often than it should. And you've still got a long way to go, judging by what happened at Westbank." "She was a witch, old man. She cast a spell to hold me in place." "As if that excuses anything. You think I didn't deal with any number of magicians in my day? What was it again — 'no matter how powerful the wizard, a knife between the shoulder blades will seriously cramp his style.' As things stand, I've still got a lot of painstaking work to do in the future." "You never give any ground, do you, old man?" Garth and Garret's voices slowly begin to fade away, and at length you hear them descend another set of stairs. Seems like that's the end of that... nothing left to do now but to head back to your room, it seems. Although, it must be said that the conversation has given you something to think about, even if you'll never be able to discuss it with Garret directly... not without admitting you've been listening in on his conversations, at any rate.'

rows.original: It's so easy, isn't it? The druidess' warg is out of the picture, but just to make sure it doesn't get up while and make trouble while you're having fun, you find a goodly-sized boulder by the riverside and pin the creature under its weight. Probably wouldn't last long, but it doesn't need to last long, just long enough. With the pet taken care of, that just leaves the mistress... Unsurprisingly, it looks like [pc.isDK |these hippies |druids ] aren't really into clothes. If not for the fact that she'd need to be around people, you doubt that she'd have even bothered with the simple shift to begin with — for all the quality of the fabric, perhaps some kind of spider silk that's cool to the touch like the boreal elf herself, it's notably light and sheer, perhaps even gauzy. That, and she hasn't bothered with underclothes — but does she need them with that kind of body to begin with. Lithe and slender, with narrow hips and petite, pointed tits, the druidess looks positively sylvan, built for running through the trees. All it takes is a flick of your wrist to send the shift fluttering through the air away from the riverbank, and then it's just you and her. It's then that the druidess slowly comes to, groaning and shifting on the ground under you. She's groggy at first, but that quickly fades as she realizes you're pinning her down onto the ground; still, she can't help but look an utter mess as she blinks back bleary eyes and curls her lip in an attempt to sneer. Has she noticed the lack of her bow? Of course she has, was it even a question? "I thought you'd have killed me already, [pc.ra elf |wyld-kin |[pc.race] ]." She could have done the same to the loggers, but she didn't. You only thought that it was fair to return the courtesy[pc.isDK |; after all, while you personally might not have cared that much, they would, and you have reason to give a shit about what they think ]. Now then, she can spread herself out, or you can do it for her. She doesn't look surprised as realization dawns, merely disappointed and angry. "You intend to -" Do no less to her than what she was perfectly willing to do others.[pc.isCunning | As they say down in the Belharan Heartlands, how does she like them apples? ] The druidess scowls at that, clearly weighing up her chances of fighting or fleeing and liking neither. "Two wrongs don't make a right." Oh, perhaps not. [pc.isDK |But you'll be the first one to confess that having a plausible, no, righteous pretext to do what you really wanted to do all along is extremely satisfying. She should know all about that, shouldn't she? For a moment, the druidess looks like she's going to argue the point anyway, then sullenly accepts the situation she's landed herself in |Perhaps the proper thing to do would be to bring her to Garret and the loggers, have her apologize to them and let them decide what to do with, or more likely, do her. Would that tickle her fancy instead? After all, it would be the wronged parties who'd decide the appropriate restitution, instead of someone more detached from this whole mess. For a moment, the druidess looks like she's actually going to accept that offer out of pure spite for you, then she realizes that it would simply take her out of the frying pan and into the fire ]. There's nothing left to say that the icy silence doesn't convey clearly. [pc.isDK |That pride of hers holds just the barest hint of fear, well-hidden under that facade... nature is red in tooth and claw, after all, and it's only your precious self that's standing between you disposing of her as you see fit given that she doesn't have the wherewithal to find that. Surely she knows as much... which is a little ironic, isn't it? You return the druidess' cold sullenness with a cheeky grin, acknowledging the truth of the situation, then carefully and unhurriedly divest yourself of your [pc.armor], followed by your other things |It's hard to believe that she thinks she's still in any kind of position to be all uppity — then again, you're not the one to invoke the mantra of nature red in tooth and claw when you're the one with the upper hand. No, you're civilized, and that means balancing being graceful in victory with, well, doing what you're doing. You return the druidess' cold sullenness with a shrug, acknowledging the truth of the situation before quickly stripping yourself of your [pc.armor] and other things. ]. Now then, the only question that remains is just what you're going to do with her...

Springing to attention, she snaps open her eyes and sits upright as if struck by lightning, lips puckered for a kiss. The moment her mind registers that it's you and realization dawns, though, she pulls away as if you'd slapped her, making a face that isn't convincing at all given her violet-flushed cheeks. Given how close your lips were to hers, though, you got just the tiniest taste of yourself in that moment, although it was mostly her. Just as things should be, really; it's impolite to take back presents you've already given.
    
    "H-hmph!"
    
    Why was she about to kiss you?
    
    "I thought it was Norathar come to save me from your clutches, nothing else."
    
    Just as you've come to save the loggers and yes, Garret from her.
    
    "So, I'm the villain now, aren't I?"
    
    She certainly seems to think you are, so it's not unreasonable to imagine that from your perspective, she is indeed the villain. And she kisses her warg?
    
    "I wouldn't expect people like you to have any affection for your pets."
    
    Tch, foreplay again already? Isn't she all out of breath from that last performance? Is she up for another round of tongue-lashing? You can keep going if she's that eager... 
    
    The druidess mumbles something under her breath, tries to sit up straighter, and promptly collapses back onto the rocky riverbank with a thud. You shrug, pick up your things, and prepare to leave. She still hasn't noticed that you're making off with her bow... and [pc.isDK
        |should probably be grateful that you're not stealing the clothes off her back either, not that a true-hugger like her would care about being naked in the first place
        |you really don't want to be in the vicinity when she realizes that fact
    ]. Pulling on your clothes, you totter away from the scene and make to catch up with Garret; you've had enough fun for now, and there're still loggers to save.

rows.original: Stepping into the Frost Hound, you take a moment to shake the dust and snow off your feet and savour the aroma of winterstem that's beginning to fill the common room. You don't have that long to make good your entrance, though, for it's quickly interrupted by Garth calling you from the bar. "Hey, [pc.name]. A moment?" [pc.isDK |This had better be worth your time. |Sure. What's up? ] You make a beeline for the bar, take a seat, and plant your elbows on the countertop. All right, what's got his fur all ruffled like this? Garth takes a couple moments to consider his answer, then pours you a drink — cheap ale — and slides it across to you. It's pretty typical, a dark brown mixture with seedy scum floating on the surface; not the best of drinks but not the worst either, sufficient to ease the stresses of daily living in the Frost Marches. [pc.isDK |You snort. You'd expected better. Well, you'll be magnanimous and let Garth off if his establishment is doing that badly. |Well, you're not going to look a gift centaur in the mouth. There's always worse — rotgut, sewer brew...[pc.bg slumrat | seven knows the things you've drunk to ease your sorrows back when you were living in the gutter. ] ] You pick up the mug, take a sip, and look up at Garth [party.som||as he pours out another drink for [companion1.name]|as he pours out drinks for [companion1.name] and [companion2.name]]. "Go ahead and wet your whistle," the old wolf-man says. "Think of it as a bonus for hearing me out." You take another swig of the cheap ale and motion for Garth to go on. "So you see, after that business with Westbank and my idiot son —" Garth glances around to make sure Garret isn't within earshot — "I've got to respect you for being willing to go after Garret and the loggers. I've got another job for you, if you're willing to take it." Since he's given you one on the house, you're obliged to at least hear him out. "You see, maybe that snowstorm wasn't all bad. Things got shaken around, things got unearthed. Things like an old lupine fortress I've been trying to find for some time now. Place dates back to the Godswar, and I've been talking to River there —" he jabs a finger out the door towards the town square — "to piece together where it might once have been." "Well, it's but a couple days ago when he comes up and tells me he's got a solid lead on the fort's whereabouts, that he's not just discovered that the snowstorm unearthed it, but he's actually managed to find the key to the place." And he wants you to go in there and... do what, again? "There's something in there that has sentimental value to my wife's side of the family. A jarl's medallion of office. That's where its bearer died — if you can get it for me, I'd be much obliged. I'd go myself, but I'm not as young as I once was." He gestures down at his bad leg for emphasis. [pc.ora lupine |Now that's interesting. How would Garth's wife be related to one of the pack jarls, for the medallion of office to have sentimental value to Garth — and by extent, her? Best not to directly question Garth about that, though. ] And to be upfront here, since he knows how this works, having been a mercenary and all — what's in it for you? Garth shrugs. "I'll be honest. Me, I don't really have anything on me that could adequately pay you for what I'm asking you to do. However, the medallion aside, you're more than welcome to keep anything else you find. Place's called Fort Marrok, somewhere out in the foothills; there's almost certainly going to be plenty of danger involved from what River's told me. "Well, are you up for it or not?" [party.has arona |Arona swills down the last of her cheap ale and cracks her mug on the table over where she's sitting. "Don't know about that, gray-fur. I'm not so good at digging around in old places, so the question is... are going to get to knock heads with anything interesting? What'd the catty fuckboy say about that; what sort of danger's hanging around that old ruin?" Garth shrugs. "River tells me there're spirits lingering about, ghosts, hauntings, that sort of thing. You'd have to ask him for the details, if you choose to take up the job." Arona rolls her eyes and makes an exasperated noise. "Ghosts. Bah..." Garth just gives her his practiced barman's shrug and takes her empty mug. "So, [pc.name]. How about it?"]
rows.translation: 走进寒霜猎犬酒馆，你花了一点时间抖掉脚上的尘土和雪花，同时尽情享受着开始弥漫在大厅中的冬日香气。不过，你并没有太多时间来享受这种宁静，因为加思很快从酒吧那边叫住了你。 嘿， [pc.name]等一下？ [pc.isDK |这件事绝对值得你花时间去做。 |当然可以。有什么事情吗？ ]你径直走向酒吧，找了个座位坐下，然后将肘部搁在柜台上。好吧，到底是什么事情让他这么心烦意乱呢？ 加思花了几秒钟思考该如何回答，然后给你倒了一杯酒——便宜的麦芽酒——推到了你面前。这种酒很常见，呈深棕色，表面漂浮着一些渣滓；虽然算不上上等饮品，但也不算太差，至少足以缓解在霜冻边境地区生活的种种压力。 [pc.isDK |你哼了一声，本以为会得到更好的结果。好吧，如果加斯的生意确实不错的话，你就大度一点，放他一马吧。那个很糟糕。 |嗯，你也不会觉得礼物中有什么不好的地方。总会有更糟糕的东西的——比如腐烂的内脏、下水道里的脏水……[pc.bg slumrat | 只有七个人知道，在你那些艰难的日子里，你是如何借酒来排解忧愁的。 ] ]你拿起杯子喝了一口，然后抬头看向加思。 [party.som||当他再为某人倒一杯酒时[companion1.name]|当他为众人倒酒时[companion1.name]以及[companion2.name]]。 尽管去解渴吧。老狼族说道。可以把这看作是对我耐心倾听你讲述的奖励吧。 你又喝了一口那廉价的麦芽酒，然后示意加思继续讲下去。 所以，你明白的，在那次与西岸的交易，以及我那个愚蠢的儿子之后——加思环顾四周，确保加雷特不在听力范围之内—— 我必须佩服你，愿意去追捕加勒特和那些伐木工。如果你愿意的话，我还有另一项任务要交给你。 既然他免费为你提供了这个机会，你至少也应该听他把话说完。 你看，也许那场暴风雪并非全是坏事。一些被埋藏的东西被翻了出来，比如那座我一直在寻找的古老狼族堡垒。它的历史可以追溯到神战时代，我还在那里和瑞弗聊过……他伸手指着门外的城镇广场——“试图拼凑出那里曾经是什么样子的。 嗯，就在几天前，他来找我，说他已经找到了关于那座堡垒位置的可靠线索。他不仅发现是暴风雪把堡垒暴露了出来，而且还真的找到了进入那里的钥匙。 他想让你进去那里，然后……再做什么来着？ 里面有一些对我妻子那一家人来说具有情感价值的物品。有一枚伯爵的官职徽章，持有者就是在那里去世的——如果您能帮我把它们取出来，我将不胜感激。我本来也想亲自去，但毕竟我已经不像从前那么年轻了。他指了指自己那条有问题的腿，以强调这一点。 [pc.ora lupine |现在那就是有意思。加斯的妻子与那些部落首领之间究竟有什么关系，才会让那枚象征职位的奖章对加斯来说具有如此特殊的意义——进而对她来说也同样重要呢？不过，最好还是不要直接去问加斯这个问题。 ]说实话，既然他了解其中的运作方式，而且他也曾经当过雇佣兵，那么这对你来说有什么好处呢？ 加思耸了耸肩。说实话，我身上确实没有什么东西能够用来充分补偿你为我所做的一切。不过，除了那枚奖章之外，你找到的其他任何东西都可以留着。那个地方叫马罗克要塞，位于山脚下；据瑞弗告诉我的，那里肯定充满了危险。 那么，你到底要不要参加呢？ [party.has arona |阿罗娜喝光了杯中剩下的廉价麦芽酒，然后将杯子重重地放在她坐着的桌子边上。那个我就不清楚了，灰毛。我不太擅长在旧地方翻找东西，所以问题就是……会不会遇到什么有趣的东西呢？那个讨厌的家伙是怎么说的；那片古老的废墟里到底隐藏着什么样的危险？ 加思耸了耸肩。瑞弗告诉我，那里有鬼魂在游荡，有幽灵，有各种超自然现象。如果你决定接受这份工作，就得去问他详细的情况。 阿罗娜翻了个白眼，发出一声无奈的叹息。鬼魂……呸…… 加思只是用他那套练就好的酒保式耸肩动作，接过了她那个空杯子。那么， [pc.name]怎么样？]

rows.original: You think about it for a moment, then give Garth a nod. Yeah, you're interested. Where do you sign up? Garth points out of the Frost Hound once more. "Like I said, River over there — he's got the details. I know this sounds awkward, but I don't really want to discuss it at length, even though I'm the one asking this favor of you." No, it's not awkward at all. By now, you know Garth well enough to know that he's reliably evasive whenever it comes to any topic remotely related to his wife. There's the slightest shift in Garth's expression — the lower lid of his left eye twitches, and the corner of his muzzle quirks downwards. "There's a reason old man Sanders and I don't like talking about her. People around these parts have long memories." And you're sure it's a good one, for all this secrecy. But it can't last forever. Even if you're not supposed to know, Gwyn and Garret — Now Garth looks absolutely sullen. "Yeah, yeah. I'll have to tell them someday. But not today, and definitely not in front of you. If you're just going to harangue me about my wife, then get your sorry ass to River over there and throw your annoying questions at him, not me."
rows.translation: 你想一想，然后向加斯点了点头。没错，你感兴趣。那在哪里报名呢？ 加斯再次指向了“霜犬酒馆”。就像我说的，那边的瑞弗掌握了所有细节。我知道这么说听起来有点奇怪，但我其实并不想详细讨论这个事情，尽管是我在请求你帮忙。 不，一点也不尴尬。到现在为止，你应该已经很了解加思了，知道每当涉及到与他的妻子有关的任何话题时，他总会巧妙地回避。 加思的表情有了一丝变化——他的左眼下眼睑微微抽搐，嘴角也向下撇了撇。我和桑德斯老人都不喜欢谈论她，这是有原因的。这一带的人记性都很好。 而且你确定这真的是个好主意，毕竟采取了这么多保密措施。但这种秘密状态不可能永远持续下去。即使你们本不该知道这些事情，格温和加雷特…… 现在，加斯看起来简直闷闷不乐。是啊，是啊。总有一天我得告诉他们。但不是今天，绝对不会在你面前说。如果你非得不停地问我关于我妻子的事，那就滚到那边的河边去，把你那些烦人的问题都抛到河里去吧。他不是我。
rows.raw: " You think about it for a moment, then give Garth a nod. Yeah, you're interested. Where do you sign up? Garth points out of the Frost Hound once more. "Like I said, River over there — he's got the details. I know this sounds awkward, but I don't really want to discuss it at length, even though I'm the one asking this favor of you." No, it's not awkward at all. By now, you know Garth well enough to know that he's reliably evasive whenever it comes to any topic remotely related to his wife. There's the slightest shift in Garth's expression — the lower lid of his left eye twitches, and the corner of his muzzle quirks downwards. "There's a reason old man Sanders and I don't like talking about her. People around these parts have long memories." And you're sure it's a good one, for all this secrecy. But it can't last forever. Even if you're not supposed to know, Gwyn and Garret — Now Garth looks absolutely sullen. "Yeah, yeah. I'll have to tell them someday. But not today, and definitely not in front of you. If you're just going to harangue me about my wife, then get your sorry ass to River over there and throw your annoying questions at him, not me." "

rows.original: After some consideration, you eventually shake your head. No, sorry. Not interested. Garth takes the news with his usual stoic demeanour, watching you finish the last of the cheap ale and taking your empty mugs. "It's what it is. You've got a crazy demoness to be chasing after all, right?" There is that, too. "Don't worry about it, there are enough glory-seekers passing through these parts that I'll find someone who'll bite. Thanks for hearing me out, though. If you change your mind, though, talk to the little catboy by the fire." [pc.isChamp|Nah, you should be the one thanking him for the drink. ]You stand, stretch, and wait for Garth to go back to his business at the bar before turning your back on him and leaving. What now?
rows.translation: 经过一番考虑，你最终摇了摇头。不，抱歉，我对这个没有兴趣。 加思以他一贯的冷静态度接受了这个消息，看着你喝完最后一杯廉价麦芽酒，然后收起了你空杯子。“事实就是如此。你毕竟是在追捕一个疯狂的女恶魔，对吧？” 也有这种情况。 “别担心，这一带总有那么多贪图功名的人经过，我一定能找到愿意帮忙的人。不过还是谢谢你听我讲这些。如果你改变主意了，就去火堆旁找那个小猫人吧。” [pc.isChamp|不，应该是你才应该感谢他请你喝东西呢。 ]你站起身，伸了伸腰，等到加斯回到酒吧继续他的事情后，才转身离开他。接下来该做什么呢？

"

rows.translation: 询问关于马罗克要塞的历史。

rows.original: What's the significance of the jarl's medallion?
rows.translation: 领主的勋章究竟有什么意义呢？
rows.raw: "What's the significance of the jarl's medallion?"

rows.original: "You suspect you'll be facing danger in there. Are you right?"
rows.translation: “你怀疑进去后会遇到危险，是这样吗？”
rows.raw: '"You suspect you\'ll be facing danger in there. Are you right?"'

rows.original: What can he tell you about the jarl's history?
rows.translation: 关于这位领主的历史，他能告诉你些什么呢？
rows.raw: "What can he tell you about the jarl's history?"

rows.original: You've asked River all the questions you want to. Time to move on.
rows.translation: 你已经向瑞弗问完了所有你想问的问题，是时候继续前进了。
rows.raw: "You've asked River all the questions you want to. Time to move on."

rows.original: [flags.RIVER_MET |River smiles as you approach him. "Well, if it isn't my dear old friend [pc.name]! What can I do for you today? A song? A tale? Or maybe you're so impressed with my boyish charm and natural good looks that you just want to buy me a tall, cold glass of fresh creamy milk?" No, you're here to talk business. The little bard-boy tortures forth a quick, dolorous chord from his lute. "Business. Business, eh. Oh well, business can't be helped, inasmuch as rainy days can't be helped. What did you have in mind?" |You approach the pint-sized catfolk bard by his usual spot at the statue, and he tilts his head upwards to regard you. At first, you're not quite sure that he's not a child — his looks are certainly very childlike — but considering the deep tenor voice that emerges from his mouth when he speaks, he's definitely no youngling. "Ah! A new face!" Well, at any rate, it is the first time that you're approaching him. The little catboy extends a hand which you take, and his fingers are surprisingly strong. "I'm River. River, the Singing Arrow, and it's a pleasure to see a new face around. It can get really dreary up here sometimes, especially about winter. But that's what Garth keeps me around here for — to liven things up and get people thirsty so they head into his establishment for a pint!" So, he's a musician of some sort? "Exactly. Although I do prefer the word 'bard.' It has a certain romantic feel to it, and a lot more finesse than something as bland as 'musician.' "Troubadour" is simply too flighty, and "minstrel" evokes a courtly connotation that really isn't present here. Don't you agree?" If he wants to be called a bard, fine, he can be one. "And you name, good [pc.mf|sir|madam]?" [pc.name]. "Mm-hm. Mm-hmmm... mmm-mmm-mmm." River flicks his fingers in a blur and jams out a quick series of chords on his lute. "I have the feeling that we will be the best of friends, [pc.name], whether we like it or not. Garth has told me much about you — alas, I was not here in the warmth and safety of the Hound on the day of the storm, but huddling in a hole by the road. Never mind, though, for we will be seeing much of each other, I think." If he's going to be hanging out at the Frost Hound, that's going to be a given. "Excellent! I shall see you around — if you want to hear something from me, don't be afraid to ask!" ] Well, there is the whole point of you being here talking to him in the first place. You draw up a seat next to River on the bench, and ask about the old lupine fortress. When you bring up the topic, the little bard-boy looks up and considers you. "Right, so you're the one who agreed to do it for Garth. He kept on saying that you'd leap at the opportunity, but I wasn't sure whether you'd follow through. Guess I've been proven wrong." [pc.isDK|He'd better be happy to be; you don't like being underestimated.|You aim to surprise.] Now, what's this all about? "You see," River says in a little sing-song voice, "I've heard tell that the snowstorm moved things about in the Foothills. Frightful things can send earth moving and boulders rolling, and things which were once buried can be brought to light that way. Fort Marrok was one of those things... but even so, getting in would be hard without this." The bard reaches into his poncho, and draws out a large brass key. The lock it fits must be pretty massive — it's as thick as his forearm, and the key's head has been shaped into the likeness of a snarling wolf. Flecks of greenish corrosion dot its surface, and there're a couple of what look suspiciously like claw marks running down its length. This thing's clearly seen some violence in its time. Now how did he get his little hands on such a thing? "Can't reveal my sources," River replies, raising a finger to his lips. "I make it my business to be in the know, and people won't confide in me if they knew I'd spill their names. Suffice to say that this key will open the gates to the fortress, and after the snowstorm, I know where said gates are. After all, I did say I weathered out much of that bit of bad weather in a hole." And he'll take you there? "There's a chasm just to the west of the Black Gate to Khor'minos, the one with the bridge that spans it. Quite hard to miss, really. At its bottom lie the now-exposed gates to Fort Marrok. I'll meet you there and open the gates for you, and you can waltz right in and find that medallion old Garth wants." And him? "I'll be staying outside, thank you very much. I may have a bow and quiver, but I'd rather not use them unless I absolutely have to. After all, I'm just a tiny little kitten; what can I do? Now then —" he takes a large swig of cream from a hip flask at his side— "I'm sure you have many questions for me, so ask away."
rows.translation: [flags.RIVER_MET |当你靠近他时，瑞弗露出了微笑。哎呀，这不是我亲爱的老朋友吗[pc.name]！ 今天我能为您做些什么呢？是一首歌吗？一个故事吗？还是说，您被我那孩子气的魅力和天生的英俊外表所吸引，想要买一杯冰凉的鲜奶油牛奶给我呢？ 不，你是来谈生意的。 那个小吟游诗人用他的鲁特琴弹奏出一段短小而哀伤的旋律。生意啊，生意……唉，总之，生意就是这样的，就像下雨天一样，是无法避免的。你到底有什么打算？ |你走到那个身材矮小的猫族吟游者常待的地方——那座雕像旁，他抬起头看着你。起初，你还有点不确定他是不是个孩子——他的外貌确实非常像小孩子——但当他开口说话时，从他口中发出的那低沉浑厚的声音，显然说明他绝不是一个幼童。 “啊！有新面孔来了！” 嗯，无论如何，总之是那是你第一次接近他的时候。那个小猫族伸出了手，你握住了他的手，发现他的手指出奇地有力。 “我叫瑞弗。瑞弗，歌箭，很高兴见到新面孔。这里有时候会变得非常沉闷，尤其是在冬天。但加斯正是为了这个才让我留在这里的——为了让气氛活跃起来，让人们产生喝东西的欲望，从而让他们走进他的酒吧喝上一杯！” 那么，他应该是某种音乐家吧？ 正是如此。虽然我更喜欢‘吟游诗人’这个词。它带有一种浪漫的气息，也比‘音乐家’这样的词语更加精致。‘游吟诗人’这个词太过轻浮，而‘吟唱者’则给人一种宫廷气息的联想，但实际上这里并不存在这种背景。你不同意吗？” 如果他想被称为吟游诗人，那好吧，他就可以这么称呼自己。 “至于你的名字，也不错。 [pc.mf|先生|夫人]？" [pc.name]嗯哼。嗯哼……嗯嗯嗯。”瑞弗快速地摆动手指，在鲁特琴上连续弹奏出一串音符。“我有种预感，我们一定会成为最好的朋友。 [pc.name]，无论我们是否愿意，事实就是如此。加思已经跟我讲了很多关于你的事情——可惜，在那场暴风雨来临的当天，我并不在“寒冰猎犬”那里，而是躲在路边的一个洞穴里。不过没关系，我想我们以后会经常见面的。 如果他打算经常去“寒冰猎犬”那里的话，那肯定是不可避免的。 “太好了！以后我们会经常见面的——如果你想听我讲些什么，尽管放心地问我吧！ ] 嗯，你之所以在这里和他谈话，不正是为了这个目的吗？你在河边的长椅上坐在瑞弗旁边，然后询问关于那座古老的狼族堡垒的事情。当你提到这个话题时，那个小吟游诗人男孩会抬起头，认真地注视着你。对了，原来就是你答应为加斯帮忙的。他一直说你会抓住这个机会的，但我其实不太确定你是否会真的去做。看来我错了。 [pc.isDK|他最好能乐意接受这一点；你可不喜欢被人低估。|你的目标就是制造惊喜。]现在，这一切到底是为了什么？ 你瞧，瑞弗用一种略带吟唱般的语调说道：我听说那场暴风雪在山脚地带把许多东西都搅得乱七八糟。那些可怕的天气现象能够引发地面震动，让巨石滚动，那些原本被埋在地下的事物也会因此暴露出来。马罗克要塞就是其中之一……不过，即便如此，如果没有这个东西，想要进入那里也依然非常困难。 吟游诗人从他的雨披里掏出一把巨大的黄铜钥匙。这把钥匙所配的锁肯定非常庞大——它的厚度几乎与他前臂相当，而钥匙的钥匙头被雕刻成了一只咆哮中的狼的形状。钥匙的表面布满了绿色的锈迹，上面还有几道看起来像是爪子留下的痕迹。显然，这把钥匙在它的使用过程中经历过不少“磨难”。 那么，他究竟是怎么用他那小小的双手拿到这样的钥匙的呢？ 无法透露我的消息来源。瑞弗抬起一根手指，放在嘴唇上回答道。我总是努力掌握各种信息，因为如果人们知道我会泄露他们的名字，他们就不会向我吐露秘密了。总之，这把钥匙能够打开通往那座堡垒的大门，而在暴风雪过后，我知道那些大门具体位于哪里。毕竟，我确实说过自己熬过了那场暴风雪那个不过是小范围的恶劣天气罢了。 他会带你去那里吗？ 在通往科尔米诺斯的黑门以西，有一道峡谷，那里有一座横跨峡谷的桥梁。其实很难错过这个地方。峡谷的下装，就是现在暴露出来的马罗克要塞的入口。我会在那里等你，为你打开大门，然后你就可以直接进去，找到加斯老先生想要的那个奖章了。 那他呢？ 我打算待在外面，非常感谢。虽然我有一把弓和一支箭袋，但除非真的有必要，否则我并不想使用它们。毕竟，我只不过是一只小小的小猫而已，又能做什么呢？现在，该……他从腰间的小壶中喝了一大口奶油—— 我敢肯定你们有很多问题想问我，尽管提问吧。

rows.original: River smiles at the question. "Let's go back a little over two hundred and fifty years ago, shall we? I'm sure you know all about the war which left Savarra in the current... reduced state that it's in right now. Tychris may teach of the histories which are relevant to it, but the peoples of these wilder lands prefer to tell the tales of their own past. "The Godswar was truly notable in that it marked the first time all of the various lupine packs unanimously agreed on a course of action, without need for squabbling or brokering. Not only did they agree to aid one another to resist the wraiths and their armies, but they also entered a — ahem — mutual defense agreement with the minotaur king of that time. Khor'minos would stand fast against any invaders approaching from the coast, while the lupines would guard the sparsely populated hinterlands with their numbers and knowledge of the land." River thinks a moment, closing his large, green eyes as he strums idly on his lute, creating a dolorous musical backdrop to his tale. "I'll spare you the details for another time. Suffice to say that in order to guard the passes through the foothills, the minotaurs lent their engineering genius to the building of a mighty fortress cut into the stalwart cliffs. It was a great task, but with minotaur efficiency and lupine enthusiasm applied in spades, the fortress was completed well ahead of schedule. "To say it was amazing would be quite the understatement, [pc.name]. The fortress boasted at least two wells, drawn from aquifers deep in the earth. It held quite a sizable garrison, with provisions to last a siege of months, perhaps even years. Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen, the poor bastard chosen to lead the garrison, wanted to make sure that no wraith-touched was going to cross the pass on his watch, and stocked the fortress with everything he could bring to bear; the minotaurs were equally proud of their handiwork, and helped him as much as they could. Fort Marrok was supposed to be the glorious gatekeeper of the passes, impenetrable, indomitable, unbreachable." What happened then, to wipe such a mighty bulwark from the face of Savarra? River smiles sadly, the tune he's strumming turning even more melancholy. "Events moved quickly. A mere two months after the fortress was fully garrisoned, creatures that used to be Belharan soldiers were sighted approaching from the south, near what we know today as Harvest Valley. They massed in the foothills like ants crawling through crevices, heading for the newly constructed fortress; everyone wanted to see it put to the test. "At last, the day came. The wraiths had massed their army of sorcerers and mindless thralls at the mouth of the pass; the lupines waited within Fort Marrok to join battle. Instead of marching forward, though, the wraiths created an earthquake, triggering a massive landslide. In the dead of winter, that in turn caused a handful of avalanches..." Oh. You see. A nod. "And that was that. Everyone and everything in Fort Marrok was buried under immense amounts of rock and snow, never to see the light of day again. With a single move, the wraiths made the lupines a non-issue in their invasion plans, and cost Khor'minos dearly in wasted time and resources. The lupines never recovered for the entire duration of the war, and with Gunvaldsen dead and buried, the jarls of the other packs held a vote of no confidence in light of his catastrophic failure. What remained of Galon Gunvaldsen's family was thrown out of their pack in disgrace once a new family was elected and raised up to the office by the remaining jarls." And that's the end to the story? "It is. A rather sad tale about learning about blind spots the hard way."
rows.translation: 河流对这个问题报以微笑。让我们回到大约250年前的那个时候，好吗？我相信你们都应该知道那场战争，正是那场战争让萨瓦拉落入了如今这种……衰败的境地。提克里斯可能会讲述与那场战争相关的历史，但这些荒野地区的人民更喜欢讲述他们自己过去的传说。 《神战》之所以如此引人注目，是因为这是所有不同的狼族部落首次达成一致，共同决定采取行动，而无需争吵或调解。他们不仅同意互相协助，共同抗性那些幽灵及其军队，还与当时的弥诺陶洛斯国王签订了——嗯——互防协议。科尔米诺斯人会坚决抗性任何从海岸方向入侵的敌人，而那些擅长在荒野中生存的族群则会利用他们的人数优势以及对这片土地的了解，来守护那些人口稀少的内陆地区。 瑞弗沉思片刻，闭上了那双绿色的大眼睛，随意地拨弄着琉特琴，为他的故事营造出一种充满忧伤的音乐背景。具体细节我就不详细说了，总之，为了守住那些穿过山脚的通道，弥诺陶洛斯人充分发挥了他们在工程建筑方面的才能，在坚固的悬崖上建造了一座巍峨的堡垒。这项工程规模庞大，但在弥诺陶洛斯人高效的工作方式以及他们那无比的热情的推动下，堡垒的建造进度远远超出了预期。 说它令人惊叹，其实还是轻描淡写了。 [pc.name]这座堡垒至少拥有两口井，这些水源来自地底深处的含水层。堡垒内驻扎着相当规模的守军，储备的物资足以支撑数月甚至数年的围攻。被指派领导这支守军的加隆·冈瓦尔德森领主竭力确保，在他负责守卫的这段时间里，不会有任何被“怨灵影响”的生物通过这条通道；他竭尽全力为堡垒配备各种所需物资。而那些弥诺陶洛斯也为自己的辛勤工作感到自豪，他们尽自己所能帮助加隆完成这些任务。马罗克要塞本应成为那些山口的巍然守护者——坚不可摧、无坚不摧、任何敌人都无法攻破的堡垒。 那么，究竟发生了什么，才会让萨瓦拉这片土地上消失如此强大的屏障呢？ 瑞弗悲伤地笑了笑，他弹奏的旋律变得更加忧郁了。事情发展得非常迅速。在堡垒完全驻军仅仅两个月后，人们就看到一些曾经是贝尔哈兰士兵的生物从南方赶来，它们出现在我们如今称之为“收获谷”的地方附近。这些生物像蚂蚁一样在山脚下聚集起来，朝着新建的堡垒方向前进——大家都想看看这座堡垒在真正的考验中会表现出怎样的实力。 终于，那一天到来了。那些幽灵们在山口集结了他们的法师军队以及那些没有思想的奴仆；而那些狼族则在马罗克堡垒内等待着加入战斗。然而，那些幽灵并没有向前进军，而是引发了一场地震，导致了一场大规模的山体滑坡。在严冬之中，这场山体滑坡又引发了数起雪崩…… 哦，你瞧…… 点了点头。就这样，福尔马罗克堡里的一切都被大量的岩石和积雪掩埋，再也无法见到阳光。那些幽灵仅仅用了一个动作，就使得那些狼族成为了他们入侵计划中无关紧要的因素，同时也让科尔米诺斯付出了巨大的代价——大量的时间和资源被白白浪费了。在整个战争期间，这些狼族始终未能恢复元气。而随着冈瓦尔德森的死亡，其他狼群的族长们鉴于他那灾难性的失败，决定对他不予以信任。当新的家族被其余族长们推选出来并执掌权力后，加隆·冈瓦尔德森的家族成员们便被羞辱地赶出了他们的狼群。" 故事就这样结束了？ 确实如此。这是一个关于通过惨痛的经历来认识到自己盲点的悲伤故事。
rows.raw: ' River smiles at the question. "Let's go back a little over two hundred and fifty years ago, shall we? I'm sure you know all about the war which left Savarra in the current... reduced state that it's in right now. Tychris may teach of the histories which are relevant to it, but the peoples of these wilder lands prefer to tell the tales of their own past. "The Godswar was truly notable in that it marked the first time all of the various lupine packs unanimously agreed on a course of action, without need for squabbling or brokering. Not only did they agree to aid one another to resist the wraiths and their armies, but they also entered a — ahem — mutual defense agreement with the minotaur king of that time. Khor'minos would stand fast against any invaders approaching from the coast, while the lupines would guard the sparsely populated hinterlands with their numbers and knowledge of the land." River thinks a moment, closing his large, green eyes as he strums idly on his lute, creating a dolorous musical backdrop to his tale. "I'll spare you the details for another time. Suffice to say that in order to guard the passes through the foothills, the minotaurs lent their engineering genius to the building of a mighty fortress cut into the stalwart cliffs. It was a great task, but with minotaur efficiency and lupine enthusiasm applied in spades, the fortress was completed well ahead of schedule. "To say it was amazing would be quite the understatement, [pc.name]. The fortress boasted at least two wells, drawn from aquifers deep in the earth. It held quite a sizable garrison, with provisions to last a siege of months, perhaps even years. Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen, the poor bastard chosen to lead the garrison, wanted to make sure that no wraith-touched was going to cross the pass on his watch, and stocked the fortress with everything he could bring to bear; the minotaurs were equally proud of their handiwork, and helped him as much as they could. Fort Marrok was supposed to be the glorious gatekeeper of the passes, impenetrable, indomitable, unbreachable." What happened then, to wipe such a mighty bulwark from the face of Savarra? River smiles sadly, the tune he's strumming turning even more melancholy. "Events moved quickly. A mere two months after the fortress was fully garrisoned, creatures that used to be Belharan soldiers were sighted approaching from the south, near what we know today as Harvest Valley. They massed in the foothills like ants crawling through crevices, heading for the newly constructed fortress; everyone wanted to see it put to the test. "At last, the day came. The wraiths had massed their army of sorcerers and mindless thralls at the mouth of the pass; the lupines waited within Fort Marrok to join battle. Instead of marching forward, though, the wraiths created an earthquake, triggering a massive landslide. In the dead of winter, that in turn caused a handful of avalanches..." Oh. You see. A nod. "And that was that. Everyone and everything in Fort Marrok was buried under immense amounts of rock and snow, never to see the light of day again. With a single move, the wraiths made the lupines a non-issue in their invasion plans, and cost Khor'minos dearly in wasted time and resources. The lupines never recovered for the entire duration of the war, and with Gunvaldsen dead and buried, the jarls of the other packs held a vote of no confidence in light of his catastrophic failure. What remained of Galon Gunvaldsen's family was thrown out of their pack in disgrace once a new family was elected and raised up to the office by the remaining jarls." And that's the end to the story? "It is. A rather sad tale about learning about blind spots the hard way."'

rows.original: [pc.ora lupine |You know something about such symbols of office, having heard of them in your youth, but is there anything particularly special about this medallion? Sure, it represented the jarl's authority over his pack, but how did Galon's differ, if it did? |You don't really know that much about lupine politics and customs. Is there something special about Galon's medallion that would peak Garth's interest in the object? ] The whole it-has-sentimental-value-for-my-wife thing aside, that is. River takes a sip of cream and considers the question. "Can't rightly say. Old Garth's the stoic kind; I've been with him for a while now, and he's hard to read some days. Might as well be talking to a stone wall. Not like me, of course." You suppose it has some value as a piece of jewellery, but there're easier ways than that to lay one's grubby hands on gold. "There is one problem, though." You can guess what it is, but you'll hear him out anyways. River nods. "As the symbol of the jarl's authority, it's almost certain that he died with it about his neck. Considering that the place is crawling with vengeful ghosts, it's more than likely you'll have to put the poor bastard to rest in order to retrieve it. You might want to give some thought to that little conundrum before heading on in." Nothing's ever as easy as it seems, is it? "Of course not. Where would be the fun in that?" Easy for him to say; he's not the one who has to go into that place. "But I am the one who has to write a song about it." Fine, fine. Either way, does he know what it's supposed to look like? A good, thorough description would make your job so much easier. "If I remember my lore, it should be hanging off a thick gold chain, long enough such that the medallion itself should be above one's heart. The jarl's pack insignia should be on one side, and a wolfshead with large sapphires for eyes on the other. Look, I know you'd like to be sure, but I believe it's one of those things you'll know when you see it; there'll be no mistaking the medallion for what it is."
rows.translation: [pc.ora lupine |你对这类象征权力的标志应该有所了解，因为在年轻时就听说过它们。但这个奖章究竟有什么特别之处呢？当然，它象征着酋长对其族人的统治权，但如果真有区别的话，加隆的这个奖章又有什么不同呢？ |你对狼人族的政制与习俗其实了解得并不多。难道加隆的那枚奖章有什么特别之处，才会引起加斯对它的兴趣呢？ ]先不说那套“对我的妻子来说具有情感价值”之类的说辞了。 瑞弗喝了一口奶油，然后开始思考这个问题。也说不准。老加斯是个性格内敛的人；我和他在一起有一段时间了，有时候他真的很难被说服或被影响。跟他说话简直就像在跟一堵石头墙说话一样。当然，这和我不一样。 你可能会认为，把它当作一件珠宝来收藏确实有一定价值，但其实还有更简单的方法可以让人轻易得到黄金。 不过，还有一个问题。 你可以猜到那是什么，但无论如何你都会听他把话说完。 瑞弗点了点头。作为酋长权威的象征，他去世时脖子上肯定戴着它。考虑到这个地方到处都是复仇的鬼魂，要想取回它，你很可能不得不让那个可怜的家伙安息才行。在继续前进之前，你或许应该好好考虑一下这个棘手的问题。 事情从来都没有看上去那么简单，对吧？ 当然不会。那样还有什么乐趣可言呢？ 他说得容易，毕竟不是他要去那个地方的人。 但是，我是那个必须为此写一首歌的人。 好吧，好吧。不管怎样，他知道它应该是什么样子吗？如果能给他一个详细、准确的描述，你的工作会容易很多。 如果我没记错的话，那枚奖章应该悬挂在一条粗金链子上，这条链子足够长，以至于奖章本身会位于佩戴者的胸前位置。链子的一侧应该刻有酋长的族徽，而另一侧则应该是一个眼睛里镶嵌着大颗蓝宝石的狼头图案。看，我知道你肯定想确认一下，但我相信，当你看到它的时候，你就会立刻认出来的——绝对不会把那枚奖章认错。

rows.original: River whistles and strums a discordant chord on his lute. "Yes, and I'm not surprised, considering the way they died. It must have been agonizing, being buried alive like that with no hope of escape; considering the numbers the jarl had amassed, they'd have suffocated long before they even began to starve. It's the ultimate in shameful straw-deaths, I'd say. "Given such a fate, is it really so strange that they would continue to haunt the ruin?" No, you suppose not. [party.has arona |Hearing this, Arona scowls viciously. "Of course, ghosts. It had to be ghosts." Now then, you didn't think [a] [pc.isDK|big strong girl|fearsome orc warrior] like her would have anything to fear from some spectres. [pc.isDK||Arona reaches around and smacks you upside the back of the head with a meaty palm. ]"It's not about being afraid of them, you moron. It's about what they are. You can't bash the innards out of ghosts. You can't hack them to pieces. You can't even throttle them with your bare hands. All someone like me can do is to send for Hretha or Infrith and skulk around while hoping they can deal with the problem. It's fucking frustrating!" |"Of course, they won't take kindly to your presence, as the restless dead are wont to do. It's likely you'll have to dispatch them." Oh, you've fought your share of stranger things in your time. There is a problem, though — aren't ghosts supposed to be incorporeal? Mundane weapons wouldn't be able to harm them, right?[pc.bg acolyte |While you saw enough exorcisms performed during your time as an acolyte, none of them really involved slicing up the offending haunt in combat... ] ] River considers that for a bit, stopping his playing to stroke his chin in thought. "Hmm. That's technically not true. Sure, it'd be harder to put down the ghosts with steel alone, but I wouldn't say it would be completely worthless. Remember, these are spirits caught up in the last moments of their lives; they remember they're supposed to so-called die if someone runs them through with a sword. You wouldn't be able to kill them, but you could prevent them from manifesting long enough for you to escape." [party.has arona |"Hah." Arona folds her arms under her ample chest. "Still sounds shit to me." ] Some kind of magical weapon would be better, then? "Oh, of course. Much more effective." River pauses a moment, then sighs. "If only we could just happen to find such weapons of great and legendary power lying around, but alas, the gods are not with us today. Hence, if your forte lies more in the martial and you'd like to give yourself an edge, I'd suggest nipping down to Ivriss' and see what she has in stock. There're any number of items she sells which could even the odds against such ghosts in a pinch." And magic? "Much more effective.[pc.cl whitemage| I believe you should already know a spell or two which would be rather efficient in putting them down.] As always, have a care as to what kind of magic you're throwing at them." [party.has cait |"I could help with that!" Cait pipes up. ] Isn't there some kind of way to put them all to rest? Some kind of ritual you can enact, or geas you can break? River shrugs, his face twisting into an oh-so-catlike expression of disaffection. "Putting the restless dead away en masse is trickier than it sounds — those things are highly circumstantial, I'm afraid, and often tied to the way they died. Given that the tales say there were as many as two thousand mustered within Fort Marrok in preparation for the wraiths' supposed siege..." All right, all right, you get the idea. "When I tried sneaking into the place, they were literally coming out of the walls and going for my throat. I wouldn't linger too long within those old hallways, if I were you. Go in, do what you need to, and get out. Folklore says that the best way to get rid of a lingering ancestor is to get him or her to realize the truth of his or her death — if you can get the jarl to realize that he's dead and should move on, that'll probably work, but I've got no idea as to how. You'll have to figure that one out on your own."
rows.translation: 河边的风儿吹动着，他的鲁特琴发出了不和谐的音符。是的，考虑到他们的死法，我并不感到惊讶。被活埋而且毫无逃脱的希望，那一定是一种极其痛苦的死法；考虑到那个酋长聚集了那么多人，他们在开始挨饿之前早就窒息而死了。我想，这简直就是最可耻的‘压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草’式的死亡方式。 面对这样的命运，他们依然继续在这片废墟中游荡，这真的有那么奇怪吗？ 不，你大概不会这么认为吧。 [party.has arona |听到这话，阿罗娜狠狠地皱起了眉头。当然是鬼魂了。肯定是鬼魂干的。 现在嘛，你该不会以为像她这样的[pc.isDK|强壮女孩|凶悍兽人战士]会害怕，哪怕是那些幽灵。 [pc.isDK||阿罗娜突然伸出手，用他那肉乎乎的手掌猛地拍在了你的后脑勺上。 ]并不是要害怕他们，你这个笨蛋。关键在于，你根本无法把鬼魂的内脏打出来，也无法把它们砍成碎片，甚至无法用双手扼住它们的喉咙。像我这样的人，所能做的就是去召唤赫蕾莎或因弗丽丝，然后躲在一边，满怀希望地等待着。他们根本解决不了这个问题，真是他妈的让人恼火！ |当然，他们不会对你们的出现持欢迎态度，因为那些不安宁的死者向来如此。很可能你们不得不将他们消灭掉。 哦，你在生活中肯定遇到过许多奇怪的事情。不过有个问题——鬼魂不应该都是无实体的吗？普通的武器应该不可能伤害到它们吧？[pc.bg acolyte |虽然你在担任学徒期间目睹过许多驱魔仪式，但其中并没有一次是真正通过战斗将那些邪灵彻底消灭的…… ] ] 瑞弗思考了一会儿，暂时停止了游戏，低头沉思起来。嗯，那个严格来说不对。当然，仅靠钢铁武器来对付这些鬼魂确实会变得更加困难，但我也不能说这样做完全没有意义。请记住，这些都是那些在生命最后时刻被困住的灵魂；它们清楚地记得，如果有人用剑刺穿它们，它们就应该“死去”。所以，你确实无法仅靠钢铁武器来解决这个问题。杀死你可以阻止它们显现出来，这样你就有足够的时间逃脱。 [party.has arona |哈。阿罗娜将双臂交叉抱在丰满的胸前。在我看来，这仍然听起来很糟糕。 ] 那样的话，某种具有魔力的武器会更好吧？ 哦，当然。效果要好得多。瑞弗停顿了片刻，然后叹了口气。要是我们能偶然找到这种拥有强大而传奇力量的武器该多好，可惜今天诸神并没有眷顾我们。因此，如果你更擅长战斗，想要让自己占据优势的话，我建议你去伊弗里斯那里看看她有什么存货。她出售的许多物品，在紧要关头甚至能够帮助我们战胜那些强大的敌人。 那么魔法呢？ 效果要好得多。[pc.cl whitemage| 我想你应该已经知道一两种在击败它们时会非常有效的法术了吧。]像往常一样，一定要注意以下几点。善良你对他们使出的那些魔法啊…… [party.has cait |这个我可以帮忙！凯特开口说话了。 ] 难道就没有什么办法能让它们都安息吗？难道不存在某种仪式可以举行，或者某种束缚可以打破吗？ 瑞弗耸了耸肩，他的脸上浮现出那种典型的、充满不满的、像猫一样的表情。将那些不安宁的死者集中处理起来，其实比听起来要困难得多——恐怕这些事情在很大程度上取决于具体的环境因素，而且往往与他们的死亡方式密切相关。根据那些传说，为了应对那些所谓的幽灵袭击，马罗克堡垒里甚至集结了多达两千名士兵…… 好吧，好吧，你明白我的意思了吧。 当我试图悄悄潜入那个地方时，那些东西简直就像从墙里冒出来一样，直接冲向我的喉咙。如果我是你，我绝对不会在那些古老的走廊里待太久。进去，做完你需要做的事，然后赶紧离开。传说中，摆脱那些缠人的祖先的最佳方法，就是让他们意识到自己其实已经死了——如果你能让那位领主明白他已经死了，应该放下这一切继续前进，那么这个方法可能会奏效……不过具体该怎么做，就得由你自己想办法了。

Now then, you didn't think [a] [pc.isDK|big strong girl|fearsome orc warrior] like her would have anything to fear from some spectres. [pc.isDK||Arona reaches around and smacks you upside the back of the head with a meaty palm. ]"It's not about being afraid of them, you moron. It's about what they are. You can't bash the innards out of ghosts. You can't hack them to pieces. You can't even throttle them with your bare hands. All someone like me can do is to send for Hretha or Infrith and skulk around while hoping they can deal with the problem. It's fucking frustrating!" |"Of course, they won't take kindly to your presence, as the restless dead are wont to do. It's likely you'll have to dispatch them." Oh, you've fought your share of stranger things in your time. There is a problem, though — aren't ghosts supposed to be incorporeal? Mundane weapons wouldn't be able to harm them, right?[pc.bg acolyte |While you saw enough exorcisms performed during your time as an acolyte, none of them really involved slicing up the offending haunt in combat... ] ] River considers that for a bit, stopping his playing to stroke his chin in thought. "Hmm. That's technically not true. Sure, it'd be harder to put down the ghosts with steel alone, but I wouldn't say it would be completely worthless. Remember, these are spirits caught up in the last moments of their lives; they remember they're supposed to so-called die if someone runs them through with a sword. You wouldn't be able to kill them, but you could prevent them from manifesting long enough for you to escape." [party.has arona |"Hah." Arona folds her arms under her ample chest. "Still sounds shit to me." ] Some kind of magical weapon would be better, then? "Oh, of course. Much more effective." River pauses a moment, then sighs. "If only we could just happen to find such weapons of great and legendary power lying around, but alas, the gods are not with us today. Hence, if your forte lies more in the martial and you'd like to give yourself an edge, I'd suggest nipping down to Ivriss' and see what she has in stock. There're any number of items she sells which could even the odds against such ghosts in a pinch." And magic? "Much more effective.[pc.cl whitemage| I believe you should already know a spell or two which would be rather efficient in putting them down.] As always, have a care as to what kind of magic you're throwing at them." [party.has cait |"I could help with that!" Cait pipes up. ] Isn't there some kind of way to put them all to rest? Some kind of ritual you can enact, or geas you can break? River shrugs, his face twisting into an oh-so-catlike expression of disaffection. "Putting the restless dead away en masse is trickier than it sounds — those things are highly circumstantial, I'm afraid, and often tied to the way they died. Given that the tales say there were as many as two thousand mustered within Fort Marrok in preparation for the wraiths' supposed siege..." All right, all right, you get the idea. "When I tried sneaking into the place, they were literally coming out of the walls and going for my throat. I wouldn't linger too long within those old hallways, if I were you. Go in, do what you need to, and get out. Folklore says that the best way to get rid of a lingering ancestor is to get him or her to realize the truth of his or her death — if you can get the jarl to realize that he's dead and should move on, that'll probably work, but I've got no idea as to how. You'll have to figure that one out on your own.""

rows.original: "A decent enough military mind, I'll grant you that," River replies after some thought. "The tales and songs from the period regarding him differ greatly depending on whether they were composed before or after the fall of Fort Marrok; I personally find it rather interesting how public opinion can be swayed so easily. He was, I suppose, out of his element — prior to the Godswar, the most anyone in his station ever had to deal with were smaller skirmishes between the packs, since the Belharan Empire never really got that much of a foothold in the Frost Marches. In that, the jarl was a magnificent strategist. The wraiths, however, were a different matter. "You must understand, [pc.name], that the lupines of the time had a clear delineation between the magical and the mundane. They had their own share of runes and totems, but actual arcane magic was not seen as a warrior's art, and to use it, especially in single combat, was considered cheating. The honor code did well by their society for generations, but it left them unprepared for wraiths who had no incentive to play by their arbitrary rules and every reason to cheat." Harsh. "It's easy to fall into the trap of imagining that everyone is, or with a little push, could be exactly like you are," River continues in a little sing-song voice. "It might be good to keep that in mind. The poor bastard was never really liked that much, even amongst his own." Why's that? "Remember what I said about that delineation between the magical and mundane? Galon, the poor bastard, he became enamored of a local white witch, a silly young thing from one of the backwater villages. Some say that she charmed him with a spell, stealing his heart with forbidden magic; other tales say that he seduced her and fucked her silly because he wanted to know how good a witch was in bed, then married the poor bitch to save face when she became too pregnant to hide it. Not that she was complaining, of course — making the jump from village witch to jarl's wife is nothing to sniff at. "Either way, while the Gunvaldsen bloodline was known to be strong, the pups she bore him — a brother and sister — were truly robust; it was clear to all that they would dwarf even their father when they reached full maturity. That sort of ostentatious overgrowth, it led to rumours that the jarl's wife was wraith-touched, that her children were half-demons, that sort of nonsense talk; it's little wonder they were quickly exiled once Galon perished along with Fort Marrok. What happened to them after, the songs and histories have nothing further to say."
rows.translation: 我得承认，你的军事头脑还算不错。 瑞弗思索片刻后回答道。 关于他的那些故事和歌谣，根据它们是在马罗克要塞陷落之前还是之后创作的，其内容会有很大的不同。我个人觉得，公众舆论竟能如此轻易地被左右，这一点相当有趣。我想，他当时确实感到很不适应——在“神战”之前，像他这样的职位上的人，所需要处理的最多也就是各个部落之间的小规模冲突，因为贝拉兰帝国在冰霜边境地区从来就没有真正建立起稳固的据点。在这方面，这位酋长确实是一位杰出的战略家。然而，那些幽灵却完全是另一回事了。 你必须明白， [pc.name]，在那个时代，狼族族对于魔法与世俗事物有着明确的区分。他们拥有属于自己的符文与图腾，但真正的奥术魔法并不被视为战士应有的技能；在单挑中使用魔法，甚至会被视为作弊行为。这种荣誉准则在他们社会中延续了数代，但却使他们完全无法应对那些根本不会遵守这些随意制定的规则、反而有着各种理由去作弊的幽灵族。 太苛刻了。 人们很容易陷入这样的误区：认为每个人都和你一样，或者只要稍加引导，就能变成和你一样的人。瑞弗用略带吟唱般的声调继续说道。记住这一点或许很有好处。那个可怜的家伙，就连在他自己的同伴中，也从来没真正受到过多少喜爱。 为什么会是这样呢？ 还记得我之前说的关于魔法与世俗之间的界限吗？那个可怜的加隆，他竟然迷上了一个当地的白女巫——一个来自偏远村庄的愚蠢少女。有人说她用咒语迷惑了他，用禁忌的魔法夺走了他的心；也有人说是他主动追求她、与她发生了关系，只是因为他想看看女巫在床上的表现究竟如何。后来，当她怀孕到无法隐瞒的时候，他为了保全面子才娶了她。当然，她并不是在抱怨——从乡村女巫变成领主的妻子，这可是件值得庆祝的事情。 无论如何，虽然冈瓦尔德森家族的血脉被认为非常强大，但她为他所生的那对兄妹确实体格健壮；大家都清楚，等到他们完全长大后，他们的体格甚至会超过他们的父亲。那种过分张扬的言行，引发了种种谣言——有人说领主的妻子被邪灵附身，说她的孩子们是半魔半人的怪物，诸如此类的无稽之谈；难怪在加隆与马罗克要塞一同覆灭后，他们很快就遭到了流放。他们之后发生了什么，那些歌曲和故事已经再也无法说明一切了。

rows.original: River looks you up and down. "I'd make sure you're prepared if I were you. The ghosts will be coming at you thick, so you won't have time to rest inside, and who knows how large the place is; I didn't get much further than the entry hallway before I had to back out. I'll open the gates for you, but don't come crawling out to me because you weren't ready. If you do come out without the medallion in hand, I'll take it that you don't want to ever go back in there. I know I don't." Yes, you're sure you're done. "All right, then. Head to the ravine in the eastern foothills, just west of the gates to Khor'minos. I'll meet you at its bottom, and we can get to work." And he'll just know when you've left town? River smiles. "Same as how I managed to get my hands on the key, friend. It's my business to know things. Don't worry, I only use this power for good, not evil." Hmm... "Oh, there's one more thing." River wags a finger at you. "Don't tell Garth that I told you this, but you might want to let Garret tag along on this little mission of yours. I get the feeling that he'd be quite interested." What? And get into Garth's bad books? "If I don't say anything, you don't say anything, and Garret doesn't say anything, who's to know? Seriously, though — I get the feeling that things might be different if you asked him to come along for the ride. Call it kitten's intuition. Besides, you know he'll be interested in anything that concerns his mother." And that's exactly why Garth didn't want him hearing this. "It's your call, [pc.name]. I'm only making you aware that the option exists. Whether you want to strike while the iron is hot — that's up to you, friend. With that, I bid you farewell and good luck — I'll be seeing you around." [party.has cait| As you turn to leave, though, River pauses in his playing long enough to snap his fingers. "Caitriss Zethra. A moment, if you please." Cait looks between you and the little bard-boy, then nods. "Go on, [pc.name]. I'll catch up with you later." Well, if she says so. You find an empty table, make yourself comfortable, and try not to appear too conspicuous as you spy on Cait out of the corner of your vision. Odd, the two of them aren't actually saying anything — instead, River has set his lute down on his lap, and is instead making a set of strange gestures at lightning speed with his nimble fingers. [pc.bg acolyte scholar|You're not completely sure, but you think... do some of the handsigns have anything to do with Mallach? You think you've come across them before, but you can't be sure in which tome... ] As Cait looks on, the usually bubbly catgirl's face blanches, her ears droop, and her pink tail curls about her legs. She looks like she's about to say something, then thins her lips and gives River a curt nod, a new hardness in her eyes. "I understand." "I'm sorry, but it is what it is." "All right, then." Cait tries to smile, but it doesn't go over very well. "I've got to head back to [pc.name]. [pc.mf|He|She]'ll worry if I'm away for too long." River nods, pulls his poncho up to shade his face, and goes back to playing. Within moment, Cait's back at your side, bouncing along as if nothing had ever happened. What was that all about? "Nothing much, just some old temple stuff." If she says so. ] Well, no point sitting around here wasting time, you've got an old fort full of ghosts to clean up.
rows.translation: 瑞弗上下打量了你一番。如果我是你，我会确保自己做好了充分的准备。那些鬼魂会大批地朝你袭来，你根本没时间在里面休息，而且谁也不知道那个地方到底有多大；我甚至还没走到入口大厅就不得不退回来了。我会为你打开大门，但如果你还没准备好就爬出来找我，那就说明你根本不想再回到那里去了。我知道，我自己也是这么想的。 是的，你确定已经完成了吗？ 好吧，那就这样吧。前往科尔米诺斯城门西侧的东麓峡谷，在那里的下装与你会合，然后我们就可以开始工作了。 那他怎么就会知道你离开小镇了呢？ 瑞弗笑了。就像我是怎么得到那把钥匙的那样，朋友。了解这些事情是我的事。别担心，我只会用这种能力做好事，而从不会做坏事。 嗯…… 哦，还有一件事。河流在向你摇手指。别告诉加斯是我告诉你的，但你或许可以考虑让加雷特陪你一起执行这次任务。我有种感觉，他会对此非常感兴趣的。 什么？还会被记在加斯的黑名单上？ 如果我什么都不说，你也不说什么，加雷特更不会说什么，那么谁会知道呢？不过说真的——我有种感觉，如果你邀请他一起来的话，事情可能会有所不同。就当是直觉吧。而且，你知道的，任何与他母亲有关的事情都会引起他的兴趣。 正因为如此，加斯才不希望他听到这些话。 这由你来决定。 [pc.name]我只是想让你知道这个选项是存在的。是否要趁现在机会行动，那就取决于你啦，朋友。话就说到这里，我再向你道别并祝你好运——以后还会再见面的。 [party.has cait| 然而，就在你转身准备离开的时候，瑞弗暂停了他的演奏，打了个响指。凯特·泽特拉。请稍等片刻。 凯特看了看你，又看了看那个小吟游诗人男孩，然后点了点头。继续吧， [pc.name]待会儿我再找你聊。 好吧，如果她这么说的话。你找一张空桌子坐下，放松下来，尽量别太引人注意，同时用眼角的余光偷偷观察凯特。奇怪，他们两个人其实什么都没说——相反，瑞弗把鲁特琴放在膝盖上，然后用他那灵活的手指以极快的速度做出了一连串奇怪的手势。 [pc.bg acolyte scholar|你并不是完全确定，但你觉得……这些手势中有些可能与马拉克有关吗？你认为自己之前见过它们，但却想不起来是在哪本书里看到的…… ] 眼睁睁看着这一幕，那个平时总是活泼开朗的猫娘脸色变得煞白，耳朵耷拉下来，粉红色的尾巴也蜷缩在她的腿边。她看起来像是要说些什么，但最终只是紧抿着嘴唇，向瑞弗简短地点了点头，她的眼中浮现出一种前所未有的坚毅。 我明白了。 很抱歉，但事实就是如此。 那好吧。凯特试图微笑，但效果并不理想。我得回去了。 [pc.name]。 [pc.mf|他|她]如果我离开太久，就会担心了。 瑞弗点了点头，拉起雨披遮住脸，继续玩游戏。不一会儿，凯特又回到了你身边，蹦蹦跳跳地走着，仿佛什么事情都没发生过一样。 刚才那到底是怎么回事？ 没什么特别的，只是些关于古老寺庙的资料而已。 如果她这么说的话…… ]好吧，坐在这里浪费时间也没什么意义，你有一座充满鬼魂的旧堡垒需要清理呢。
