rows.original: The door might be mighty, but it's weathered with age. Since you're a warrior, you might have a chance?
rows.translation: 这扇门虽然非常坚固，但经过岁月的侵蚀，也已经变得有些陈旧了。既然你是一名战士，或许你有办法打开它吧？
rows.raw: "The door might be mighty, but it's weathered with age. Since you're a warrior, you might have a chance?"

rows.original: Right. Why bother with keys and locks when you can just blast this stupid thing apart with a well-placed spell? Smiling, you gather power at your fingertips, feel the beginning of the spell begin to thrum in the air, and watch expectantly - — As the runes on the doorframe flash green, and your magic dissipates into nothingness. Oh. Guess you're not getting in that way, then. What was it River said about the wolves being distrustful of what they considered witchcraft? Either way, you'll have to find some other way to break down the door... or the key.
rows.translation: 没错。既然一个恰到好处的法术就能把这蠢东西炸成碎片，那还要钥匙和锁干什么？你微笑着，在指尖凝聚魔力，感到法术的起势开始在空气中嗡鸣，然后满怀期待地注视着—— ——可门框上的符文闪过一道绿光，你的魔法随即消散得无影无踪。 哦。 看来你是没法从那条路进去了。瑞弗不是说过什么吗，狼群不信任他们眼中的巫术？不管怎样，你都得另想办法破门而入……或者找到钥匙。
rows.raw: " Right. Why bother with keys and locks when you can just blast this stupid thing apart with a well-placed spell? Smiling, you gather power at your fingertips, feel the beginning of the spell begin to thrum in the air, and watch expectantly - — As the runes on the doorframe flash green, and your magic dissipates into nothingness. Oh. Guess you're not getting in that way, then. What was it River said about the wolves being distrustful of what they considered witchcraft? Either way, you'll have to find some other way to break down the door... or the key."

rows.original: Maybe you can blow it apart with a bit of magic...
rows.translation: 也许你可以用一点魔法把它炸毁……
rows.raw: "Maybe you can blow it apart with a bit of magic... "

rows.original: Resigned, you step back from the massive door and plan your next move. There must be some way to get past this barrier; you just have to find it. If the door was never meant to be opened from this side, there wouldn't even be keyhole, would there? Yes, yes. There's got to be a way, you just have to look around and find it, that's all.
rows.translation: 你认命地从那扇巨大的门前退开，盘算着下一步该怎么办。一定有某种办法能越过这道障碍；你只需要找到它而已。如果这扇门本来就不该从这一侧打开，那这里根本就不会有钥匙孔，对吧？ 没错，一定有办法的。你只需要仔细寻找一下，就能找到它，就是这么简单。
rows.raw: " Resigned, you step back from the massive door and plan your next move. There must be some way to get past this barrier; you just have to find it. If the door was never meant to be opened from this side, there wouldn't even be keyhole, would there? Yes, yes. There's got to be a way, you just have to look around and find it, that's all."

rows.original:
Grimacing, you set down your [var0] and send it away with a push. Sure, you could've just left it out in the halls instead of lugging it all the way back here, but you don't want to attract any attention than you already have and leaving large pieces of cookware out in the middle of the hallway is bound to raise some eyebrows.

            Well, time to make do with [a] [var1]. Let's just hope that this is the last time you have to return here and make a swap...
rows.translation:
你面带痛苦的表情，把东西放了下来。 [var0]然后轻轻一推，它就飞走了。当然，你本可以把那些东西直接放在走廊里，而不必费力地把它们搬回来，但你肯定不希望引起更多的注意——毕竟，把大件的炊具放在走廊里，肯定会引起别人的好奇和注意。

            好吧，现在只能用一个[var1]将就了。但愿这是你最后一次需要回到这里进行交换了……
rows.raw:
"
            Grimacing, you set down your [var0] and send it away with a push. Sure, you could've just left it out in the halls instead of lugging it all the way back here, but you don't want to attract any attention than you already have and leaving large pieces of cookware out in the middle of the hallway is bound to raise some eyebrows.

            Well, time to make do with [a] [var1]. Let's just hope that this is the last time you have to return here and make a swap..."

rows.original:
Time to make off with the dishes like some crazed, kleptomaniacal thief! Before you know it, you'll be lugging around fifty pounds of brooms because you have to... ha ha, not really. But you probably have your own reasons for wanting this [var0], right?

           Now that you're getting used to its weight, the [var0] is a bit hefty, but you can still move it around. Let's just hope you don't run into too much trouble in the interim before you find a use for this...
rows.translation:
是时候像个疯狂的盗窃癖小偷一样把这些碗碟顺走啦！不知不觉间，你就会扛着五十磅重的扫帚四处走动，因为你别无选择……哈哈，其实也不是真的。不过，你想要这个[var0]大概有你自己的理由，对吧？

           既然你已经渐渐习惯它的重量，这个[var0]虽然有点笨重，但你还是能把它搬来搬去。只希望在你找到它的用途之前，不会遇到太多麻烦……
rows.raw:
"
           Time to make off with the dishes like some crazed, kleptomaniacal thief! Before you know it, you'll be lugging around fifty pounds of brooms because you have to... ha ha, not really. But you probably have your own reasons for wanting this [var0], right?

           Now that you're getting used to its weight, the [var0] is a bit hefty, but you can still move it around. Let's just hope you don't run into too much trouble in the interim before you find a use for this..."

rows.original: On second thought, maybe you don't actually need this [var1]. Besides, you already have [a] [var0], right? Right? That should serve just fine, yes? Ugh, the [var1] looks like it'd be a right pain to heft around, too... yeah, you should just leave it behind and be done with it.
rows.translation: 仔细想想，也许你其实并不是这样。需要这个[var1]况且，你已经有一个[var0]了，对吧？对吧？这样应该就足够了，嗯？唉，真是的[var1]看起来带着它到处跑也会非常麻烦……没错，你干脆把它扔掉，这样就解决了。
rows.raw: "\n On second thought, maybe you don't actually need this [var1]. Besides, you already have [a] [var0], right? Right? That should serve just fine, yes? Ugh, the [var1] looks like it'd be a right pain to heft around, too... yeah, you should just leave it behind and be done with it."

rows.original: On second thought, maybe you don't actually need this [var0]. Ugh, the [var0] looks like it'd be a right pain to heft around, too... yeah, you should just leave it behind and be done with it.
rows.translation: 仔细想想，也许你其实并不是这样。需要这个[var0]呃，真讨厌[var0]看起来带着它到处跑也会非常麻烦……没错，你干脆把它丢掉，这样就解决了。
rows.raw: "\n On second thought, maybe you don't actually need this [var0]. Ugh, the [var0] looks like it'd be a right pain to heft around, too... yeah, you should just leave it behind and be done with it."

rows.original:
You give the assorted crockery and cookware lying over the dead hearths a look-over. They look hefty — enough that you could only carry one at a time, but if there were some reason you wanted to take one of them along with you, that would be possible — unlike the others tacked up against the walls, they're not so heavily corroded to be fused to the masonry.

    That being said, would you like to take one of them along with you? Who knows why you might want to do this, but the option remains.
rows.translation:
你仔细看了看那些堆放在废弃壁炉旁的各式各样的陶器与炊具。它们看起来相当笨重——一次只能携带一件，但如果你有特别的理由想要带走其中某件，也是完全可行的。与那些靠墙堆放的器具不同，这些器具并没有严重腐蚀到与墙壁粘连的程度。

    那么，你愿意带走其中某件吗？谁知道你为什么会想要这么做呢，但这个选择确实是存在的。
rows.raw:
"
    You give the assorted crockery and cookware lying over the dead hearths a look-over. They look hefty — enough that you could only carry one at a time, but if there were some reason you wanted to take one of them along with you, that would be possible — unlike the others tacked up against the walls, they're not so heavily corroded to be fused to the masonry.

    That being said, would you like to take one of them along with you? Who knows why you might want to do this, but the option remains."

rows.original:
You pick up one of the pots hanging from the spits and give it a good look-over. It looks large enough to hold a watermelon comfortably, just the right size for one person to heft around comfortably in their arms. Perhaps there was once a lid to this thing, but you can't find it, and upending the pot spills out a couple handfuls of dust but nothing else. There's some tarnish on the side, too, but nothing that makes its appearance too shabby.

        Well, is this what you want to take along with you?
rows.translation:
你拿起挂在架子上的其中一个锅，仔细端详起来。它看起来足够大，可以轻松容纳一个西瓜，大小正好适合一个人手持携带。也许这个锅曾经有一个盖子，但现在你找不到它了。把锅倒过来，里面只掉出了几把灰尘，除此之外什么也没有。锅的侧面也有些锈迹，但并不会让它看起来太破旧。

        那么，这就是你想要带在身边的东西吗？

rows.original: Pick up one of the pots.

You step over to one of the large kettles and examine it. It's a large, cylindrical thing, tall enough to reach your waist, and stands on a tripod over a long-dead fire pit. Two handles at its sides chafe uncomfortably at your fingers when you try to heft it off its stand, flakes of rust breaking away under the strain, and it lifts away with an audibly pained groan. On the bottom, a crust of age-old rot sits over a burnt-out bottom — looks like this kettle was left to burn with its contents. 

        There's a hole in the kettle's side which might have once been a spout, but as of now it's just a jagged edge which you need to be careful of, lest you cut your fingers on it. You take a few experimental steps, swing the kettle about for a bit — it's heavy, but not too unwieldy that you can't set it down quickly in case something untoward happens.
        
        Do you want to take the kettle with you?
rows.translation:
你走到其中一个大水壶旁仔细观察。它是一个巨大的圆柱形容器，高度足以达到你的腰部，被放置在一个三脚架上，而三脚架则架在一个早已熄灭的火坑上。当你试图把它从三脚架上搬下来时，两侧的手柄会让你手指感到不适；在用力拉扯的过程中，一些锈迹会脱落，而水壶也会发出令人听上去十分吃力的呻吟声，才终于被搬下来。在锅底，有一层积年累月的腐烂物覆盖在烧焦的部分之上——看起来这个水壶是带着里面的东西被留在火上烧着的。

        水壶的侧面有一个洞，那里原本可能是一个出水口，但现在只是一个参差不齐的边缘，使用的时候必须小心，否则很容易割伤手指。你先尝试着做几个动作，把水壶晃来晃去——它确实很重，但也不至于重到让你无法迅速把它放下，以免发生什么意外。
        
        你想把水壶带着一起走吗？

rows.original: Make off with one of the kettles.
rows.raw: "Make off with one of the kettles."

rows.original:
Cautiously, you draw close to one of the cast-iron cauldrons and peer over the edge. Whatever it used to hold has long since decayed into nothingness, leaving you with an ugly mess in the cauldron's recesses. Giving the handles a tug, then another, then a third, you finally manage to break the cauldron free of the firepit; it lifts up and away with a grisly tearing sound, leaving you holding a large, unwieldy burden.

        Huh. Considering it comes up to your chest, you'd have expected it to be even heavier; good thing this is empty, or else you wouldn't be able to so much as move it. You can kinda sorta lift it in short bursts, but it's much easier to just roll the thing along the ground. If the restless dead bother you on the way... well, it's not like they're going to nick the cauldron while your back is turned or anything, so you should be able to set it aside and defend yourself.
        
        Is the cauldron what you'd like to lug around with you?
rows.translation:
你小心翼翼地靠近其中一个铸铁大锅，探头往锅沿里看。它过去盛放的东西早已腐烂得无影无踪，只在锅的内壁留下一团难看的残渣。你拽了拽锅柄，再拽一次，又拽第三次，终于把大锅从火坑中弄了出来；它伴随着一阵令人毛骨悚然的撕裂声被抬了起来，留给你一个又大又笨重的负担。

        哈。既然它都高到你胸口了，你还以为它会更重一些；幸好它是空的，否则你连挪都挪不动它。你能勉强短促地把它抬起一下下，但直接在地上滚着走要轻松得多。如果路上那些不安分的亡灵来烦你……嗯，它们总不至于趁你转身时把大锅偷走吧，所以你应该能把它放到一边，腾出手来保护自己。
        
        这个锅就是你想拖着到处走的东西吗？

Looking at the assorted old cookware, you figure that you don't need any of this trash bogging you down. You're not that desperate that you need to steal plates and dishes — and you don't even have the excuse that you're some kind of archaeologist and these need to belong in a museum.

        Turning your heel on the dusty old heaps of junk, you consider your next move.
rows.translation:
看着那些各式各样的旧炊具，你心想自己根本不需要这些累赘。你也没穷到需要去偷盘子碗碟的地步——更何况，你也没有什么自己是考古学家，这些东西应该被送到博物馆去这样的借口。

        于是，你转身离开了那些积满灰尘的旧垃圾堆，开始思考下一步该做什么。
rows.raw:
"
        Looking at the assorted old cookware, you figure that you don't need any of this trash bogging you down. You're not that desperate that you need to steal plates and dishes — and you don't even have the excuse that you're some kind of archaeologist and these need to belong in a museum.

        Turning your heel on the dusty old heaps of junk, you consider your next move."

rows.original: You'd rather not pick up anything.

Unlike the other ghosts in the fortress, these ones don't seem to mind your presence, enraptured by the ongoing bouts in the makeshift ring. One after another, lupine soldiers enter, fight each other ferociously for the whole of five minutes, then leave laughing and clapping each other on their furry backs. There don't seem to be any kind of established rules in these bouts, either — but that's what no-holds-barred means, doesn't it? Swords, spears, bare fists, claws and teeth, fighting clean, fighting dirty, everything goes in this rough-and-tumble tournament, and yet no one seems to think any worse of the other for it. Quite a difference from your stereotypical honorable duel, that's for sure. The fighting goes on for a few more rounds as you watch on, and you begin to wonder if there's ever going to be an end to this tournament, or if the ghosts are just trapped in the final moments of their lives — and if these were the final moments of these poor sops' lives as they waited to die from asphyxiation, then what wills they must have had, to make merry till the end. Your musings are answered, though, when a tall lupine woman pushes the crowd aside and steps into the makeshift ring. Clearly, she's someone of importance, for the raucous cheering and yipping still as she looks around. Gracefully, she unclasps the fur-lined cloak from about her neck, folding it neatly in her hands, then undoes her leather cuirass and grins at the ensuing wolf whistles. Perhaps six and three quarters feet in height, the curvaceous amazonian wolfess basks in the adoration of the crowd, with all that she's wearing being a leather skirt and a strip of cloth that struggles to contain her huge bosom. "Well, I'm here. A bit late thanks to my uncle demanding my attentions, but I'm finally here. I see you've been about this for quite some time — when do we get started?" "Hey!" someone shouts from within the audience. "You know full well that you're a shoo-in for the top of the heap, Magna. Without Malachai or your uncle about to give your tail a good whupping, no one's going to best you one-on-one." Upon hearing this, the wolfess just shrugs, her grin growing wider. "All right, then. Let's make things a little more interesting and a little quicker, won't we? Why don't you come at me three, four at a time, and we'll see who comes out on top, eh? That should cut the chase quite a bit — Uncle says we should be saving our strength for fighting the wraiths, not each other." "But the Helm of Heroes —" A dismissive wave of her hand. "Yes, yes, I know, I know. You beat me, the winners get to fight it out amongst themselves as to who gets to wear the silly thing. You lot don't beat me, and I wear it into the fray, like always." "Like always," you hear one of the ghosts mutter from beside you. "Well! Any takers?" Magna's question is answered by a trio of overeager lupines who climb into the ring and rush her without so much as a care or thought. With a few easy twists and turns, she circles around them, grabs the pups by their scruffs and cracks their skulls together in quick succession, then leaves them dazed and stumbling off the mats. "Okay, then!" Magna cracks her knuckles. "Who's up next?" Several other groups make the attempt to take down the wolfess, with as much success as the first. Her weapons of choice are her bare fists, and they're a blur as she punches, claws, and wrestles her way to the top of the heap, leading her defeated opponents off the mats in an almost motherly fashion. The farce goes on for perhaps twenty minutes in all, and Magna isn't so much as winded at the end of it all. "Who's next?" she calls out to the crowd. "Anyone still hasn't had a go?" [party.has arona |"Can't say I like ghosts much in general, but this one rubs me the right way." Arona is actually smiling, the first time you've seen her in good cheer since entering Fort Marrok. "I don't know about you, but I'm of the mind that maybe we should take her up on her challenge." ] [party.has garret| A whimper at your side draws your attention. Garret? His usual bravado gone, Garret is visibly cringing, ears flat against his head, eyes fixed upon the apparition in the ring. He takes a half-step back, as if to flee, and clenches and unclenches his hands several times. "I..." [party.has brint|"What's wrong with you, Dogmeat? You look as if you've seen a gho- oh."|Is something the matter?] "Nothing's wrong with me, but I..." Garret steels himself, squaring his massive shoulders. "I'm going to go up there, alone if need be. Don't try and stop me." [party.has brint |Brint looks askance at you, his features creasing as he thinks. "I don't know about this. On one hand, it's stupid dangerous. On the other, I get the feeling that this is something he needs to do, and alone at that..." |[party.has cait |Cait swallows hard as she watches Garret push his way through the throng of ghosts towards the ring, elbowing and shoving as if he were in a marketplace crowd. "I... I'm not sure. This is something he needs to do alone, but it's so dangerous..." ] ] Given Garret's air of determination, there's no talking him out of this, but you could at least fight at his side. Will you do that? |Hmm... "Helm of Heroes", eh? You wonder what sort of thing this prize might be... and if so, whether it would be worth trying to compete in this tournament yourself. It's no fight to the death, and the ghosts here are pretty friendly as opposed to the ones prowling the corridors... would it be worth your time to match your strength against the jarl's niece to win it for yourself?]
rows.translation: 与堡垒里的其他幽灵不同，这些幽灵似乎并不在意你的存在，它们完全被那个临时搭建的擂台上的激烈战斗所吸引。一只又一只狼族士兵陆续进入擂台，疯狂地厮杀着，整整五分钟的时间里，他们不断地搏斗，最后却笑着离开，还互相拍打着自己毛茸茸的背部。在这些比赛中，似乎也没有任何既定的规则——但“不择手段”就是这个意思吧？刀剑、长矛、赤手空拳、爪子与牙齿，无论是正当手段还是卑鄙手段，这种激烈的比赛中什么手段都可能被使用，然而似乎没有人会因此而看不起对方。这确实与你们那种刻板印象中的光荣决斗有着很大的不同。 随着战斗的继续进行，你开始怀疑这场锦标赛究竟何时才能结束，还是说那些参赛者只是被困在了生命的最后时刻……如果对这些可怜的人来说，这些确实是他们等待窒息而死的最后时刻，那么他们究竟是怀着怎样的决心，才能坚持到最后依然欢笑不止呢？ 然而，当一位高个子的狼族女性推开人群，走进这个临时搭建的擂台时，你的疑问得到了解答。显然，她是个地位显赫的人物，因为当她环顾四周时，人群中依然响起了喧闹的欢呼声和尖叫声。她优雅地解开披在脖子上的毛皮斗篷，将其整齐地折叠在手中，然后脱下皮制胸甲，面对随之而来的狼族般的哨声，她露出了微笑。这只身高大约六英尺三四分的曲线优美的亚马逊女狼，正享受着人群的崇拜与赞美。她身上仅穿着一条皮裙和一条几乎无法遮住她那巨大胸部的布条。 嗯，我终于到啦。因为叔叔缠着我，所以来晚了些，不过现在总算到了。看你们准备这个已经有一段时间了——我们什么时候开始吧？ 嘿！观众中有人喊了起来。你心里很清楚，自己绝对是夺冠的热门人选，玛格娜。既然没有马拉凯，也没有你的叔叔来阻碍你，那么在一对一的对决中，根本没有人能打败你。 听到这话，那只母狼只是耸了耸肩，笑容变得更加灿烂了。好吧，那我们就让事情变得更有趣一点吧。以及快一点吧，好吗？你们为什么不一次来三四个对付我，看看谁会胜出，怎么样？这样应该能节省很多时间——叔叔说过，我们应该把体力留下来用来对抗那些幽灵，而不是互相争斗。 但是英雄头盔—— 她随意地挥了挥手。是的，是的，我知道的。你们赢了，所以胜者应该自己决定谁来戴那个傻乎乎的东西。但既然你们没有打败我，那我就像往常一样，戴着它去参加比赛吧。 像往常一样，你听到其中一个鬼魂在你身旁低声说道。 好了！有人愿意尝试吗？ 玛格娜的问题被三只急切的幼狼解答了——它们爬上擂台，毫不顾及任何后果地冲向她。她轻松地几个转身，就绕到了它们身边，抓住它们的脖子，迅速地将它们的头撞在了一起，然后让它们晕头转向地跌跌撞撞地离开了擂台。 好吧，那就这样吧！玛格娜活动了一下手指关节。下一个该谁上场呢？ 还有其他几组人也试图击败这位女战士，但他们的成功率都与第一组人一样低。她最常用的武器就是自己的赤手空拳，她在挥拳、抓挠以及搏斗的过程中动作快得让人看不清，最终她成功登上了擂台的顶端，以一种近乎母亲般的方式将那些被她击败的对手赶下了擂台。整个这场闹剧持续了大约二十分钟，而结束时，玛格娜却丝毫没有气喘吁吁的样子。 下一个是谁？她向人群喊话。还有人没试过吗？ [party.has arona |一般来说，我并不是很喜欢鬼怪之类的东西，但这个鬼怪却让我觉得挺有意思的。阿罗娜竟然在微笑，这是你自进入马罗克要塞以来，第一次看到她如此开心。我不知道你们怎么想，但我认为我们或许应该接受她的挑战。 ] [party.has garret| 你耳边传来一声呜咽，吸引了你的注意。 加雷特？ 他平时那种勇猛的样子早已不见，此刻明显显得非常害怕，耳朵贴在脑袋上，眼睛紧紧地盯着戒指中的那个幽灵。他向后退了半步，似乎想要逃跑，同时双手也不停地攥紧又松开。 我…… [party.has brint|你怎么回事，Dogmeat？你看起来好像看到了什么恐怖的东西……|出什么问题了吗？] 我没什么问题，只是……加雷特强作镇定，挺直了他那宽厚的肩膀。如果需要的话，我会独自上去。别试图阻止我。 [party.has brint |布林特侧目看着你，他的面部肌肉在思考时微微皱了起来。我不太明白这件事。一方面，这样做非常危险；另一方面，我又觉得这是他必须要做的事情，而且还是独自去做…… |[party.has cait |凯特艰难地咽下口水，看着加雷特在那一群幽灵中挤向擂台，他用肘部和肩膀推挤着前进，就像在拥挤的市场里一样。我……我不太确定。这是他必须独自完成的事情，但风险实在太大了…… ] ] 鉴于加雷特那坚定的态度，根本不可能劝他改变主意，但你至少可以站在他的一边与他并肩作战。你愿意这么做吗？ |嗯……“英雄头盔”，是吧？你一定在想这个奖品会是什么……以及是否值得自己参加这场锦标赛来争夺它。这毕竟不是生死搏斗，而且这里的“幽灵”们也相当友善，与那些在走廊里游荡的幽灵们可完全不同……花时间与酋长的侄女一决高下，只为赢得这个奖品，真的值得吗？]

"I don't know about you, but I'm of the mind that maybe we should take her up on her challenge." ] [party.has garret| A whimper at your side draws your attention. Garret? His usual bravado gone, Garret is visibly cringing, ears flat against his head, eyes fixed upon the apparition in the ring. He takes a half-step back, as if to flee, and clenches and unclenches his hands several times. "I..." [party.has brint|"What's wrong with you, Dogmeat? You look as if you've seen a gho- oh."|Is something the matter?] "Nothing's wrong with me, but I..." Garret steels himself, squaring his massive shoulders. "I'm going to go up there, alone if need be. Don't try and stop me." [party.has brint |Brint looks askance at you, his features creasing as he thinks. "I don't know about this. On one hand, it's stupid dangerous. On the other, I get the feeling that this is something he needs to do, and alone at that..." |[party.has cait |Cait swallows hard as she watches Garret push his way through the throng of ghosts towards the ring, elbowing and shoving as if he were in a marketplace crowd. "I... I'm not sure. This is something he needs to do alone, but it's so dangerous..." ] ] Given Garret's air of determination, there's no talking him out of this, but you could at least fight at his side. Will you do that? |Hmm... "Helm of Heroes", eh? You wonder what sort of thing this prize might be... and if so, whether it would be worth trying to compete in this tournament yourself. It's no fight to the death, and the ghosts here are pretty friendly as opposed to the ones prowling the corridors... would it be worth your time to match your strength against the jarl's niece to win it for yourself?]"

rows.original: No, this is not going to happen. You're here for each other; letting Garret walk into this alone is madness. Besides, Garth would never forgive you if you let something happen to his idiot son. "I..." Garret begins when you catch him by the arm, then his expression softens as he takes in your [pc.face]. He doesn't have to do this alone. You're here for him. [party.has brint |Brint takes Garret by his other arm. "I'm here for you too, Dogmeat. Remember that, okay?" ] You don't know what's shaken Garret about all this, but whatever it is, he doesn't have to face it alone. He doesn't have to tell you what it is, you're sure that he'll do so when he feels he's ready. "...All right." Together, you make your way into the ring where Magna is waiting. The gigantic wolfess gives your little group a look, then grins and waves you forward. "New challengers! What a surprise!" Garret doesn't say anything, but takes a step forward and nods. "Well then, I shan't hold back, and neither should you! Here I come!"
rows.translation: 不，不能让事情这样发展。你们本该相互扶持；让加雷特独自踏入其中简直是疯了。更何况，要是你放任那个傻儿子出事，加斯永远都不会原谅你。 你伸手抓住加雷特的胳膊，他刚说出“我……”，看清你的[pc.face]后，神情便缓和下来。 他不必独自面对这一切。你会陪着他。 [party.has brint |布林特抓住加雷特的另一条胳膊。“我也会陪着你，狗肉。记住了，好吗？” ] 你不知道这一切为何令加雷特如此动摇，但无论原因是什么，他都不必独自面对。他也不需要现在就告诉你；等他觉得自己准备好了，自然会开口。 “……好吧。” 你们一起走进玛格娜等候的擂台。高大的狼女扫了你们这一小群人一眼，随即咧嘴一笑，挥手招呼你们上前。 “新的挑战者！真让人意外！” 加雷特一言不发，只向前迈出一步，点了点头。 “那好，我不会手下留情，你们也别留力！我来了！”

rows.original: You're not going to let a friend walk into danger by himself.
rows.translation: 你总不会让朋友独自陷入危险之中吧。
rows.raw: "You're not going to let a friend walk into danger by himself."

rows.original: Your breath catches in your throat as you make the decision, but it has to be the right one. The way Garret is purposefully striding towards the ring, the set in his shoulders, the way his usually jovial demeanour has evaporated — there's more going on here than meets the eye. As you watch, Garret closes the last few steps to the ring, enters, and draws himself to his full height in front of the jarl's niece. "Oh my, aren't you a big one," Magna says with a chuckle as she looks up at Garret. "Haven't seen you around before — you'd stand out no problem. New recruit?" Garret is silent. He looks left and right, hands clenching and unclenching; even from where you are, you can hear his teeth grinding, so silent is the training hall. "Who are you? Why do you look like my mother?" Silence. The living locks eyes with the dead. And then Magna laughs, a huge belly laugh that sends her whole amazonian frame shaking. "Ha! Ha! Your mother? She must be quite a woman; I'd like to meet her someday! I'm too young to be your mother, and even if I weren't, I haven't had any pups yet. As for who I am... they call me the dark terror in Jassira, the savage barbarian in the east... "Here, though, I'm just the jarl's niece. No fancy titles, I'm afraid. And you? It's polite to get someone's name before you pound him into the floor." "I'm just a tavernkeeper's son." "Pah, no need to put yourself down like that." Magna throws her head back and spreads her arms in quite the melodramatic gesture. "If you can beat me, you'll be someone. How about that? You're afraid, I can tell. You reek of it." Garret looks away and cracks his knuckles. "Afraid? Of course I'm afraid. Would be stupid to not be afraid. But one of the last things my mom said to me was that courage isn't the absence of fear, but acting in spite of it." "I'm liking your mom more and more. Time for talking's over, though — you look like you might actually put up a decent fight. Have at you!" With that, Magna lunges straight for Garret with inhuman speed, poised to plant a solid right hook on him. The spectral wolfess' maniacal grin widens as Garret sidesteps the blow and plants a fist into her chiseled abs, sparks flying from the silver studs on his cestus. "Oof! Guess I wasn't wrong. Looks like I won't have to hold back, then!" From there, the fight erupts into a flurry of blows and more than a couple of attempted grapples and holds. Everything's moving so quickly, the two of them are but a blur; after a minute or two of this, though, it's clear that Garret isn't about to hold his ground. In terms of raw physicality, the two are evenly matched, but Garret simply doesn't have the training and experience that Magna has. He manages to get in a few more gut punches, slipping by his spectral opponent's defenses, but Magna locks him in an underarm hold and keeping him in place for a powerful straight to his jaw. Garret staggers back, clutching his muzzle, and that's all the opening Magna needs to sweep his legs out from under him and send him down to the mats. There're a few tense moments as he struggles to rise, and then collapses back down in a small cloud of dust. The massed lupines cheer, filling the training hall with howls and yips. They shut up well enough, though, when Magna shoots them a glare and crouches down besides Garret. Garret groans. "Mother, I am slain." "Oh, stop being so dramatic," Magna says as she reaches down and tries to lift Garret by the scruff of his neck. The poor bastard is too heavy for that, and she settles for grabbing him by the arm and hauling him to his feet. "You know, pup, where have you been all my life? Your talent's being wasted — I can tell that all you've ever fought are angry drunks and rowdy farmhands. At least here at Fort Marrok you'll get the training you need to actually improve — if you don't challenge yourself, you'll never get anywhere. I'll let Uncle know he has an uncut gem amongst his latest batch of recruits." "Ugh..." "It's odd that you called me Mother... do I really look that much like your old woman?" "She'd be older now. Quite some years..." Garret staggers to the edge of the ring, and the ghosts part to let him pass. "But... you remind me of her, my last memory..." "Oh. I'm sorry." "No. She's not dead. Just... gone." More silence. Somewhere behind them in the distance, a spectral lupine appears with a plumed, horned helm on a cushion, yelling for Magna to come back and claim her prize, but she ignores him and continues walking Garret back to you. "If I had a son... I wouldn't mind too much if he turned out like you. I get it, I've only known you for a handful of minutes, but I think I can say as much with certainty." Garret quirks up a corner of his muzzle. "I think that's one of the nicest things anyone's ever said about me, living or dead." "Oh, I never got your name, tavernkeeper's son..." "It's Garret." "I'll remember that." Magna pushes Garret into your arms, and snaps around at attention. "Okay, you lot! Uncle says fun's over and to get back to work, we've got wraiths and their beasties a-coming, and he wants you in shape, not all beaten up from biting each other. Come on, chop chop! You know what to do!" And they do indeed. The wolves quickly switch from rambunctious to orderly and disciplined, quickly falling into formation in preparation for drills and training. On your part, you get poor Garret back into some semblance of shape — he's still wobbly from the beating he took, but brushes you away after he's regained his bearings. "Don't worry about me. I just need to walk it off." Is he fine? "Not in the head, I think. But we should go on. There's nothing left for us here." [party.has brint |"You know, I'll admit I'm not the smartest. But even so, I think that our good old Dogmeat over there had one of those epiphany things." It's hard not to agree with that. ]
rows.translation: 当你做出这个决定时，呼吸几乎被堵在喉咙里，但这个决定必须是正确的。加雷特那坚定的步伐、他挺直的肩膀，以及他平时那欢快的神情此刻全都消失了——这里发生的事情远比表面上看起来的要复杂得多。当你看着加雷特一步步走向擂台，走进场地，在酋长的侄女面前站得笔直时，你不禁意识到 哦天，你该不会是个大人物吧？玛格娜轻笑着抬头看着加雷特说道。以前没见过你在这里——你肯定很容易就被注意到。是新来的吗？ 加雷特一言不发。他左右张望，双手不停地紧握又松开；即便在你所在的位置，也能听到他牙齿咬合的声音——训练室里实在太安静了。 你是谁？为什么你长得像我妈妈？ 寂静。生者与死者对视着。 然后，玛格娜笑了——那是一阵震天动地的笑声，让她那魁梧的身躯都开始颤抖。哈！哈！你的妈妈？她一定是个了不起的女人，我真希望能有朝一日见到她！我年纪太小，不可能成为你的妈妈，而且就算我年龄合适，我也还没有生过孩子呢。至于我到底是谁……在贾西拉，人们称我为‘暗影的恐怖’；在东部，人们则把我叫做‘野蛮的蛮族’…… 不过在这里，我只不过是酋长的侄女而已。恐怕没有什么华丽的头衔……那你呢？在把某人揍倒在地之前，先了解一下他的名字才是礼貌的做法吧。 我只不过是个酒馆老板的儿子罢了。 哼，没必要这样贬低自己。玛格娜将头向后一仰，双臂大张开，做出了一个相当夸张的姿态。如果你能打败我，那你就是个了不起的人。怎么样？我看你害怕了，这一点我看得出来，你的恐惧气息暴露无遗。 加雷特移开了视线，然后开始活动手指关节。害怕？当然害怕了。如果不害怕的话，那才傻呢。不是害怕吧。但我妈妈最后对我说的话之一就是：勇气并不是没有恐惧，而是在恐惧存在的情况下依然选择行动。 我越来越喜欢你妈妈了……不过，该说正事了——看样子你真的会奋起抵抗的。那我们就开始吧！ 说着，玛格娜以超乎常人的速度直冲向加雷特，准备用一记有力的右勾拳击中他。当加雷特侧身躲过这一击时，这位幽灵般的狼女露出了疯狂的笑容，而加雷特则一拳击中了她那结实有力的腹部，他手中铁链护手上的银色饰钉在撞击中迸发出火花。 哎哟！看来我猜对了。这样我就不用再克制自己了！ 从那一刻起，战斗迅速演变成一连串的攻击与几次试图擒抱的动作。一切发生得如此之快，以至于两人的动作都变得模糊不清；然而，一两分钟后，就很明显地看出，加雷特并没有打算坚守自己的防线。从纯粹的体力角度来看，这两人在这一方面势均力敌，但加雷特显然缺乏玛格娜所拥有的训练经验和技巧。他虽然设法打出了一些直拳，突破了自己对手的防御，但玛格娜很快就用锁臂技将他固定住，然后一记重拳击中了他的下巴。加雷特踉跄着后退，双手紧紧捂住自己的下巴，而玛格娜正是趁这个机会，猛地一推，使他失去了平衡，重重摔在了垫子上。在他挣扎着想要站起来的时候，有那么几秒钟令人紧张，最终他又在一片尘土中倒下了。 成群的狼族欢呼起来，他们的嚎叫声充满了训练厅。然而，当玛格娜瞪了他们一眼，然后蹲在加雷特旁边时，他们立刻安静了下来。 加雷特发出了呻吟声。妈妈，我被杀死了。 哦，别这么夸张了。玛格娜说着，伸手试图抓住加雷特的脖子将他拉起来。可惜那家伙太重了，她只好抓住他的手臂，把他拽了起来。你知道吗，孩子，这些年来你都去哪里了？你的天赋正在被浪费——我看得出，你以前打的那些对手都只是些愤怒的醉汉和吵闹的农夫。至少在马罗克要塞，你能够得到真正有助于提升自己的训练。如果你不挑战自己，永远也不会有所成就。我会告诉叔叔，他在新招募的这些人中，发现了一块未经雕琢的宝石。 呃…… 你叫我‘妈妈’，真是奇怪……我看起来真的有那么像你以前的妻子吗？ 她现在应该已经长大了吧……应该有好几岁了……加雷特踉跄着走到擂台的边缘，那些幽灵们纷纷退开，让他通过。但是……你让我想起了她，我最后的回忆…… 哦，对不起。 不，她并没有死。只是……离开了。 更深的寂静。在他们身后的远处，一个戴着羽毛装饰、角状头盔的幽灵般的身影出现了，它大声呼唤玛格娜回来领取属于她的奖品，但她无视了他的呼唤，继续带着加雷特朝你的方向走去。 如果我有一个儿子……他要是长得像你，我也不会太在意。我明白的，虽然我们才认识几分钟，但我敢肯定地说出这种话。 加雷特微微翘起了嘴角。我想，这是有人对我说过最中肯的话了，无论这个人是在世还是已经离世。 哦，我还没知道你的名字呢，酒馆老板的儿子…… 是加雷特。 我会记住的。玛格娜把加雷特推到你的怀里，然后立刻转过身来，要求你注意听她说话。好了，你们这些家伙！叔叔说玩闹的时间结束了，该回去工作了。那些幽灵和它们的怪物马上就要来了，他希望你们能保持良好的状态，而不是被互相撕咬得伤痕累累。快点，动作快点！你们知道该做什么的！ 他们确实做到了。那些狼群很快就从肆意妄为的状态转变成了井然有序、纪律严明的群体，迅速排成队形，准备开始训练和演习。而你这边，也终于让受伤的加勒恢复了些许行动能力——虽然他因为之前的撞击而仍然有些站不稳，但在重新找回平衡之后，他还是迅速地回应了你的指令。 别担心我，我只需要走一走就能好起来。 他没事吧？ 我想，不是脑子出了问题。但我们还是应该继续前进。在这里，我们已经无路可走了。 [party.has brint |你知道，我得承认自己并不是最聪明的人。但即便如此，我觉得我们那位老伙计Dogmeat刚才也经历了一次顿悟吧。 很难不同意这个观点。 ]

rows.original: Let Garret be. This is clearly something he needs to do alone.
rows.translation: 让加雷特自己去处理吧。这显然是他需要独自完成的事情。
rows.raw: "Let Garret be. This is clearly something he needs to do alone."

rows.original: You know what? There're several very good reasons why you shouldn't get involved in this tomfoolery — not exhausting yourself being one of them, especially when you've yet to achieve your main objective — but hey, there's a prize to be had, and you'll get to say you had a bout with ghosts! Not everyone gets to make that kind of boast truthfully, right? Faint chills prickle against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] as you push through the spectral throng and step into the ring to face Magna; the wolfess dusts off her thick gray-black fur, and gives you a nod. [pc.ra lupine |"Here to try your luck, [pc.mf|brother|sister]?[party.som|| I see you brought someone with you, too.| I see you brought plenty of backup with you, too.] I don't suppose you were waiting for me to tire out before having a go at the helm yourself, were you?" Best for last, as they say. You were just waiting for her to get warmed up so you could have a good fight! Magna smiles at you — or more accurately, shows you her teeth. "All right, then, [pc.mf|brother|sister]. Let's see you put your muscle where your mouth is!" The wolves are still giving you ample space, but their bodies are pressed tightly together as they vie to spy on this new challenger, preventing you from escaping the ring. Magna cracks her knuckles, sniffs the air, then drops down into a fighting stance before lunging at you. It's a fight! |"You're brave to step into this ring, [pc.race]. Others wouldn't even dream of doing so." You shrug, buying a little time while you cook up a plausible lie. Well, you'd heard that this pack of lupines were amongst the best in all of Savarra; when you mentioned this to the jarl, he told you to go to the training halls and see for yourself. Magna grins and cracks her knuckles. "Indeed. I'm between travels myself — the ancestral homeland needs us all in these times, and I answered Uncle's summons. If anything, getting about in the world taught me not to underestimate lowlanders." She looks around to the rest of the assembled lupines, and gives them an easy shrug. "A lesson the lot of you could take heed of. That's how they get you in the end, you know. Overconfidence." The lupines say nothing, but you feel the weight of a couple hundred intent gazes on the back of your neck, and surely there must be many more on Magna. Somehow, you get the idea that there's far more at stake here than the right to wear a helmet; if you're feeling pressured, Magna must be crushed. "Is the [pc.race] even allowed to do this?" someone shouts from the crowd. "The Helm of Heroes is reserved for —" "I invited any and all challengers forward. This one was brave enough to offer [pc.himHer]self up and rise to meet the challenge. Unless you're willing to come and take [pc.hisHer] place on the mats, I think you should shut up and watch." Silence. "Right. Any other comments? None? Then let's begin." Tensing her muscles, the wolfess throws you a quick salute, then lunges straight for you, fingers and knuckles ready to tear you apart. "Defend yourself!" It's a fight! ]
rows.translation: 你知道吗？其实有好几個很好的理由说明你不应该参与这种愚蠢的行为——其中之一就是避免让自己白白耗费精力，尤其是当你还没有实现自己的主要目标的时候。不过，话说回来，参与这次行动还是会有些收获的，而且你还可以声称自己与“鬼魂”打过交道！并不是每个人都能真正有这样的经历来吹嘘，对吧？此刻，一阵阵微寒正从你的[pc.skinFurScalesNoun]当你穿过那些幽灵般的群体，走进擂台与玛格娜对峙时，那只母狼抖了抖自己那浓密灰黑色的毛发，然后向你点了点头。 [pc.ra lupine |来这儿碰碰运气吧， [pc.mf|兄弟|姐姐]？[party.som|| 我看你也带了别人一起来啊。| 我看你也带了不少备用物资啊。]我猜你并不是在等我累垮了才打算自己来掌舵吧？ 正如人们所说，最后才展示最好的东西。你一直在等待她热身完毕，这样你们才能进行一场激烈的战斗！ 玛格娜对你笑了——或者更准确地说，她露出了她的牙齿。好吧，那么， [pc.mf|兄弟|姐妹]让我们看看你是不是只说不做！ 那些狼虽然仍然给你留出了足够的活动空间，但它们的身体却紧紧地挤在一起，争先恐后地想要观察这个新出现的挑战者，从而阻止你逃离那个圈圈。玛格娜掰了掰手指关节，嗅了嗅空气，然后摆出了战斗姿势，朝你扑了过来。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ |你能勇敢地走上这个擂台，真是令人钦佩。 [pc.race]其他人根本连想都不会想到这么做。 你耸了耸肩，暂时争取了一些时间，同时编造了一个看似合理的谎言。你知道，这批狼族绝对是整个萨瓦拉地区最上等的；当你把这件事告诉酋长时，他让你自己去训练场亲自看看。 玛格娜咧嘴一笑，然后活动了一下手指关节。确实如此。我现在正处于旅途之中——在这种时刻，故乡需要我们所有人的力量，所以我响应了叔叔的召唤。事实上，这些年的旅行经历让我明白了，千万不要低估那些生活在低地地区的人们。她环顾四周，看着其他聚集在一起的狼族，然后轻松地耸了耸肩。这是你们所有人都应该引以为戒的教训。要知道，他们最终就是利用这种过度自信来抓住你们的把柄的。 那些狼族们没有发出任何声音，但你能感觉到有数百道充满敌意的目光正紧盯着你的后颈；而在玛格纳岛上，这样的目光肯定更多。不知为何，你突然意识到，这里所面临的威胁远不止是是否能够戴头盔这么简单的事情；如果你感到压力巨大，那就意味着玛格纳岛必定会遭到毁灭。 像[pc.race]这样的存在甚至被允许这么做吗？人群中有人喊了起来。英雄头盔仅限—— 我邀请了所有愿意挑战的人前来。这个人竟然有足够的勇气站出来[pc.himHer]勇敢地站出来，迎接挑战。除非你愿意主动承担这个责任。 [pc.hisHer]让他们在擂台上对决吧，我觉得你最好闭嘴，好好观看就行了。 寂静。 好的。还有其他意见吗？没有吗？那我们就开始吧。狼女绷紧全身肌肉，向你快速敬了一个礼，然后猛地朝你扑来，手指和指关节都做好了将你撕成碎片的准备。保护自己！ 这是一场激烈的战斗！ ]

rows.original: Have a go at it. Who knows, you might actually win.
rows.translation: 试试看吧。谁知道呢，你说不定真的能赢呢。
rows.raw: "Have a go at it. Who knows, you might actually win."

rows.original: Given how Magna handled all those people by herself, you doubt that you'd have much of a chance against her[party.som||, even with [companion1.name] helping you|, even with [companion1.name] and [companion2.name] helping you]. She's fast as she is wiry, and besides, you have a mission here; you don't want to waste your strength unnecessarily on side pursuits like these. "Any more takers? No?" The training hall is silent as the massed lupines look amongst themselves, but there're no more who move to meet Magna's challenge. "Okie-dokie. I win, then. The prize, please." Fading into view, a ghostly lupine steps into the makeshift ring, a large, solid-looking helmet in between his hands. Without further ado, Magna steps up to him, plucks the helm from his hands with a little bow — it's one of those full-faced affairs, complete with a plume in the back and horns on its sides — and plonks it on her head. "We protect what we value," Magna intones solemnly to the crowd, her voice a little muffled by the helm. "To shield one's crown is to acknowledge the treasure that one's mind is, both on and off the field of battle." You get the feeling that there's some kind of ceremony or ritual going on here that you're not quite privy to, but it's over as quickly as it begun as Magna removes the helmet and gives the lot a dismissive wave. "Okay, you lot! Uncle says fun's over and to get back to work, we've got wraiths and their beasties a-coming, and he wants you in shape, not all beaten up from biting each other. Come on, chop chop! You know what to do!" And they do indeed. The wolves quickly switch from rambunctious to orderly and disciplined, quickly falling into formation in preparation for drills and training. Guess this is your cue to get out of here before someone notices that you aren't joining in — trying to remain as inconspicuous as the living can in a room full of lingering dead, you back off away from the mass and make for the door. Nothing left to see here, as they say. [party.has arona |Arona looks a little pensive as you leave. "Can't say I'm not disappointed with your decision, [pc.name]. But..." But you'll need all the strength you can get when facing down the jarl, instead of wasting it on something like this. She should know about pacing herself, after all. A sigh. Is it your imagination, or does Arona sound relieved? "Can't say you're wrong there. I just fucking hate ghosts." ]
rows.translation: 考虑到玛格娜独自应对了那么多人，你肯定会觉得，自己根本没有任何机会能与她抗衡。[party.som||即使如此，也依然[companion1.name]帮助您|即使如此，也依然[companion1.name]以及[companion2.name]帮助您]她身形瘦削，动作却异常敏捷。而且，你此刻有重要的任务要完成，总不能把体力浪费在这种无关紧要的事情上吧。 还有其他人愿意尝试吗？没有吗？ 训练厅里一片寂静，那些聚集在一起的狼族都在互相注视着，但再也没有人站出来接受玛格娜的挑战了。 好吧，那我就赢了。请把奖品给我吧。 渐渐消失在视线中，一个形如幽灵的狼族走入了这个临时搭建的擂台，他的双手中托着一只看起来十分坚固的大型头盔。没多做任何准备，玛格娜便走上前，轻轻一弯腰从他手中接过了那顶头盔——那是一顶全脸式的头盔，后部装饰着羽毛，两侧还长着角——然后她便将它戴在了自己的头上。 我们保护自己珍视的东西。玛格娜庄严地向人群致辞，她的声音因为戴着头盔而显得有些低沉。保护自己的王冠，其实就是承认自己内心所拥有的珍宝——无论是在战场上，还是在和平时期。 你会感觉到这里正在举行某种仪式或典礼，但你并不完全了解其中的具体细节。然而，这一切发生得如此迅速，就在玛格娜摘下头盔并随意地挥了挥手之后，这一切就结束了。 好了，你们这些家伙！叔叔说玩闹的时间结束了，该回去工作了。那些幽灵和它们的怪物马上就要来了，他希望你们能保持良好的状态，而不是因为互相打架而受伤。快点，动作快点！你们知道该做什么的！ 果然如此。那些狼群立刻从肆无忌惮的状态转变成了井然有序、纪律严明的群体，迅速排成队形，准备开始训练和演习。看来，现在是你们该离开这里的时候了——在别人注意到你们没有参与进来之前。在这个到处都是死者的房间里，你们要想尽可能不引起注意，就只能远离那群狼，朝着门口走去。正如人们所说，这里已经没有什么可看的了。 [party.has arona |当你离开时，阿罗娜看起来有些若有所思。不得不承认，你对这个决定的选择确实让我感到失望。 [pc.name]但是…… 但是当你面对那位酋长时，你需要用上自己所有的力量，而不是把它们浪费在这种事情上。毕竟，她应该知道如何把握自己的节奏。 叹了口气。是你的想象而已，还是阿罗娜的声音确实听起来松了一口气呢？你说得没错，我确实他妈的讨厌鬼魂。 ]

rows.original: It's not worth it. You'll be content to watch.
rows.translation: 这不值得。你在一旁看着就满足了。
rows.raw: "It's not worth it. You'll be content to watch."

rows.original: The Jarl's niece Magna is every bit as fearsome as she must have been in life: a big bear of a lupine woman, unarmed save for her claws and teeth. Her thick fur and long hair accentuate her muscular and bulky frame, and she's wearing nothing save for a loincloth and cloth bindings about her hefty chest.
rows.translation: 领主的侄女玛格娜，其凶猛程度无疑与她在世时一样：她是个体型庞大、如同熊一般的女子，除了爪子和牙齿外，没有任何武器。她浓密的毛皮和长发更加凸显了她结实粗壮的身材，身上仅穿着一条缠腰布，胸部则用布条固定着。
rows.raw: "\n    The Jarl's niece Magna is every bit as fearsome as she must have been in life: a big bear of a lupine woman, unarmed save for her claws and teeth. Her thick fur and long hair accentuate her muscular and bulky frame, and she's wearing nothing save for a loincloth and cloth bindings about her hefty chest."

rows.original: With a final blow, Magna's down onto the mats — and she doesn't get up this time. Panting heavily, her muzzle split in an open-jawed smile, the black-furred wolfess stares up at the ceiling, content to lie spread-eagled on the mats as she struggles to catch her breath. "Gods above," she mutters, then laughs raucously. "I lost! I admit that I completely and utterly lost!" The spectral wolves look between her and you, burning eyes open and staring. Magna groans, then manages to lift her head off the ground and shakes her mane. "...But why do I feel so refreshed? Do you know why that is, brothers and sisters?" Silence. "I fought with all my strength. I have no regrets. That's how they get you in the end, isn't it? Overconfidence, that's how it always is." A soft sigh escapes Magna's lips, and she shakily pushes herself to her feet. "Well, you earned it, friend. Bring forth the Helm of Heroes!" Fading into view, a ghostly wolf steps into the makeshift ring, a large, solid-looking helmet in between his hands. Without further ado, Magna steps up to him, plucks the helm from his hands with a little bow — it's one of those full-faced affairs, complete with a plume in the back — and plonks it in your hands. For something that came out of the hands of a ghost, it's surprisingly solid and corporeal; just looking at it, you're pretty sure they don't make helmets in this style anymore, either. "We protect what we value," Magna intones solemnly. "To shield one's crown is to acknowledge the treasure that one's mind is, both on and off the field of battle. The wraiths will be here in a few days. I hope to see the helm on the field of battle, perhaps by my side!" Perhaps. "Okay, you lot! Uncle says fun's over and to get back to work, we've got wraiths and their beasties a-coming, and he wants you in shape, not all beaten up from biting each other. Come on, chop chop! You know what to do!" And they do indeed. The lupines quickly switch from rambunctious to orderly and disciplined, quickly falling into formation in preparation for drills and training. As the mats are pulled away, Magna turns to you and clears her throat. "There is one more thing, friend..." Yes? "I didn't get your name. These days, not many save Gatekeeper Malachai and Uncle can best me... it was a thing to remember. I learned a few lessons and was reminded of even more in that short space. It'd be a shame if I didn't at least get your name." It's [pc.name]. "[pc.name]. It's a name I'll remember well." Magna claps you on the shoulder — her touch is practically freezing — and turns to leave. "Enjoy the honor while you have it; its sweetness is quick to pass." With that, Magna gathers up her cloak and disappears into the throng of wolves at training, leaving you with an awfully impressive plumed helmet in your hands and a strange sense of foreboding.
rows.translation: 随着最后一击，玛格娜倒在了垫子上——这一次，她再也没有站起来。她喘着粗气，张大嘴巴露出笑容，这只黑毛狼女仰望着天花板，满足地躺在垫子上，努力恢复呼吸。 天啊，她低声说了些什么，然后突然放声大笑起来。我输了！我承认，我真的彻底输了！ 那些幽灵般的狼兽在她和你之间来回注视，燃烧般的双眼死死地盯着你们。玛格娜发出一声呻吟，然后勉强将头从地上抬起来，摇晃着自己的鬃毛。……但为什么我会感到如此神清气爽呢？各位兄弟姐妹，你们知道这是为什么吗？ 寂静。 我付出了全部的力量去战斗，我没有任何后悔。最终，他们就是用这种方式打败你的，不是吗？过度自信，总是这样。玛格娜轻轻叹了口气，然后颤抖着站了起来。嗯，这是你应得的，朋友。把英雄头盔拿出来吧！ 一只幽灵般的狼缓缓走进临时搭建的擂台，手中捧着一顶看起来十分结实的大型头盔。玛格娜立刻走上前，轻轻从他手中取下那顶头盔——那是一顶全脸式头盔，后面还插着一根羽毛——然后将其递到了你的手中。尽管这顶头盔似乎是出自幽灵之手部，但它却出奇地结实、真实；光是看着它，你就会觉得这种风格的头盔应该已经不再被生产了。 我们保护自己珍视的东西。马格纳庄严地开口说道。保护自己的王冠，就意味着要认识到自己内心所拥有的宝藏——无论是在战场上，还是在生活中。那些幽灵几天后就会来到这里。我希望能在战场上看到那顶王冠，也许它会出现在我的身边！ 也许吧。 好了，你们这些家伙！叔叔说玩闹的时间结束了，该回去工作了。那些幽灵和它们的怪物马上就要来了，他希望你们能保持良好的状态，而不是因为互相打架而受伤。快点，动作快点！你们知道该做什么的！ 他们确实如此。那些狼犬立刻从顽皮的状态转变为守秩序、有纪律的样子，迅速排好队形，准备开始训练。当垫子被撤走后，玛格娜转向你，清了清嗓子。还有一件事，朋友…… 嗯？ 我还不知道你的名字。这些日子里，已经没有多少人能像Gatekeeper Malachai和叔叔那样击败我……这个事实值得记住。在那么短的时间内，我学到了很多东西，也意识到了更多问题。如果连你的名字都不知道，那就太遗憾了。 我叫[pc.name]。 “[pc.name]，这是一个我会永远铭记的名字。”玛格娜轻拍你的肩膀——她的触碰几乎让人感到刺骨的寒冷——然后转身离开了。趁现在还拥有这份荣耀，好好享受吧；它的甜蜜很快就会消逝的。 说完，玛格娜收拾起她的斗篷，消失在了训练场中那些狼群之中，只留下你手中那个令人印象深刻的羽饰头盔，以及一种莫名的不安感。

"Gods above," she mutters, then laughs raucously. "I lost! I admit that I completely and utterly lost!" The spectral wolves look between her and you, burning eyes open and staring. Magna groans, then manages to lift her head off the ground and shakes her mane. "...But why do I feel so refreshed? Do you know why that is, brothers and sisters?" Silence. "I fought with all my strength. I have no regrets. That's how they get you in the end, isn't it? Overconfidence, that's how it always is." A soft sigh escapes Magna's lips, and she shakily pushes herself to her feet. "Well, you earned it, friend. Bring forth the Helm of Heroes!" Fading into view, a ghostly wolf steps into the makeshift ring, a large, solid-looking helmet in between his hands. Without further ado, Magna steps up to him, plucks the helm from his hands with a little bow — it's one of those full-faced affairs, complete with a plume in the back — and plonks it in your hands. For something that came out of the hands of a ghost, it's surprisingly solid and corporeal; just looking at it, you're pretty sure they don't make helmets in this style anymore, either. "We protect what we value," Magna intones solemnly. "To shield one's crown is to acknowledge the treasure that one's mind is, both on and off the field of battle. The wraiths will be here in a few days. I hope to see the helm on the field of battle, perhaps by my side!" Perhaps. "Okay, you lot! Uncle says fun's over and to get back to work, we've got wraiths and their beasties a-coming, and he wants you in shape, not all beaten up from biting each other. Come on, chop chop! You know what to do!" And they do indeed. The lupines quickly switch from rambunctious to orderly and disciplined, quickly falling into formation in preparation for drills and training. As the mats are pulled away, Magna turns to you and clears her throat. "There is one more thing, friend..." Yes? "I didn't get your name. These days, not many save Gatekeeper Malachai and Uncle can best me... it was a thing to remember. I learned a few lessons and was reminded of even more in that short space. It'd be a shame if I didn't at least get your name." It's [pc.name]. "[pc.name]. It's a name I'll remember well." Magna claps you on the shoulder — her touch is practically freezing — and turns to leave. "Enjoy the honor while you have it; its sweetness is quick to pass." With that, Magna gathers up her cloak and disappears into the throng of wolves at training, leaving you with an awfully impressive plumed helmet in your hands and a strange sense of foreboding.'

rows.original: Just as you're beginning to wonder if you've bitten off more than you can chew, your question is answered as Magna plants her knuckles straight into the side of your head and sends you reeling. The world spins, teeters, and then you're on your back atop the mats, staring up at the ceiling, your face on fire. Ouch. "Good try," Magna says as she moves to help you up, tail wagging all the while. "But not good enough. And in the world out there, you're either good enough, or you're not." You take a few deep breaths, and push yourself upright. Standing is possible, but barely so — at this point, a stiff breeze would be enough to knock you back down onto the mats. "Feeling okay? Pretty sure I rattled about a few things in that head of yours back there." Yeah, you're fine; you just need a few moments to regain your bearings. Magna shrugs, smiles, and then turns to the watching wolves. "Well, guess I win." "Again." "Yes, again!" the wolfess claps her hands, and the crowd parts ever so lightly to admit a ghostly lupine into the makeshift ring, bearing a heavy-looking plumed, horned helmet on a cushion. You have to admit it looks quite imposing, what with all the gleaming and being engraved with plenty of swirly patterns. But the brunt of it, you guess, is how solid the thing it appears to be — most peoples' necks would be under severe strain with that thing on one's head, especially with all the adornments. "To be honest, never quite understood the whole hullabaloo. Sure, it makes you out to be some kind of big deal, but it also makes you a big target. Let's get this over with..." Breathlessly, you watch as Magna holds the helm in both hands and drops her voice to a serious intonation. "We protect what we value. To shield one's crown is to acknowledge the treasure that one's mind is, both on and off the field of battle. And now that that's out of the way, get back to work, you chumps! Playtime's over; the wraiths are going to be here in a couple of days, and we don't want to be caught with our pants down! Uncle wants you in shape, not beaten-down from playing rough with each other!" It's interesting how the entire pack immediately switches gear from rambunctious and rowdy to smart and disciplined; the circle has broken apart in the blink of an eye and reformed into neat ranks and rows, ready to be drilled. "I'll see you later, then." Magna grins and claps you on the back, her icy touch chilling you to the bone. "Hope I didn't hit you too hard."
rows.translation: 就在你开始怀疑自己是否能力不足、难以应对时，玛格娜突然用指关节猛击你的头部，让你整个人都晕头转向。世界开始旋转，摇摆不定，最后你仰面躺在垫子上，抬头望着天花板，脸上火辣辣的疼。 哎哟 想得美。玛格娜一边说着，一边走过来帮你站起来，她的尾巴一直欢快地摇个不停。但这还不够。在这个世界上，要么你足够优秀，要么你就不够好。 你深吸了几口气，用力站了起来。虽然能够站立，但实在很吃力——在这种情况下，哪怕是一阵微风，也足以把你重新吹倒在垫子上。 感觉还好吗？我敢肯定，我刚才把你脑子里的一些想法搅得乱七八糟的。 没关系的，你只需要几分钟时间来恢复一下状态就行了。” 玛格娜耸了耸肩，笑了笑，然后转向那些在一旁注视着的狼们。好吧，看来是我赢了。 再来一次。 没错，就是这样！女狼拍手示意，人群缓缓散开，让一位身披幽灵般白色狼皮的人走进临时搭建的擂台。她头戴一顶装饰着华丽羽毛与角状纹饰的重型头盔，头盔被放置在软垫上。不得不承认，这副头盔看起来确实十分威武，那些闪闪发光的纹饰以及复杂的雕刻图案更是增添了它的气势。不过，最重要的还是坚固的事实上，如果人们头上戴着那样的东西，尤其是还搭配了各种装饰品，他们的脖子肯定会承受巨大的压力。说实话，我一直都不太明白这一切大惊小怪是为什么。当然，这样会让你显得很重要，但同时也让你成了一个容易成为目标的人。我们还是把这件事尽快解决吧…… 你屏住呼吸，看着玛格娜双手紧握舵柄，将声音压低，语气变得严肃起来。 我们保护自己珍视的东西。保护自己的‘王冠’，其实就是承认自己内心所拥有的珍贵财富——无论是在战场上，还是在生活中。现在这个问题已经解决了，大家继续干活吧！游戏时间结束了，几天后那些怪物就会再来，我们可不能措手不及！叔叔希望你们保持良好的状态，而不是因为互相争斗而变得精疲力竭！ 有趣的是，整个团队竟然会立刻从吵闹无序的状态转变为安静有序、纪律严明的状态；原本混乱的队伍在瞬间就重新整编成整齐的队列，准备开始训练了。 那回头见吧。玛格娜咧嘴一笑，拍了拍你的背，她那冰冷的触感让你不寒而栗。希望我没有打你太重。

rows.original: You turn to leave, but after making your way through the milling ghost, you feel a cold ham-hand on your shoulder and turn about. Magna's back, and the jarl's niece has a softer expression on her face than she did moments ago. Is something the matter? You'd thought she'd just said her goodbyes. "Uh, well. I'm gonna ask you a question, you see, and it's better that I don't do it in front of my uncle's rabble. Morale, leading by example and all that, you know? It would, uh, negatively impact — ah, fuck it. People would laugh at me if I asked you out in the open. Not out of mockery or anything, but like I said, I kinda need to lead by example and we wouldn't get anywhere if everyone was screwing each other — damn it, I said it, didn't I?" You're seeing where this is going. She wants to smash, and it's not really proper to ask such things publicly, at least here and now. "Well, yeah. If I asked out in the open, too, you'd be put out on a spot and despite what I look like, I'm not really into that sort of thing. Still, you're the first person I've come across in a good while who's actually put up a bit of a fight, and I like you. Last time that happened, I was in a Jassiran gladiatorial pit, so you can imagine it's been a while. "So... yeah. Want to smash?" [party.comp cait brint garret |You turn to Cait and ask in a low whisper if Mallach has anything to say about sex with the undead; what did she learn during her time at the Temple? Is it forbidden or anything like that? "Um, uh." Cait's brows furrow as she desperately tries to dredge up what steadily becomes apparent as what little she knows on the subject. "Well, you're not supposed to do dead bodies, because that's a really good way to spread diseases. Ghosts, though... there are some tales. Generally, it's not a good idea because they can do things to you, but it can also be perfectly fine if they're friendly, which this one is." So, it's a gamble. Cait throws up her arms helplessly, a weak smile on her lips. "I seriously don't know. Although... if I were more sure of myself, I'd ask to join in. That's my answer." | "I'd be up for it," Brint adds. "Well, if not for the whole cold thing. Being frozen solid kind of kills my sex drive, no offense. Still, it'd be an interesting experience..." An interesting experience, huh. "I guess I'm not that brave to try and stick my thing into a freezing ghost, just saying. Being practical and all — we're not really with the task for Garth just yet, and it's a little too early to be lingering about these parts. None of these ghosts look like they're going to draw weapons and go for us, but I'd really not stay any longer than I need to." | Garret is just standing off to one side with his back to you, arms folded across his broad chest. One ear flicks towards you as you approach him and ask for his opinion. "Frankly... please don't touch her. She looks too much like what I remember my mom as." That was... direct, to put it lightly. "I just... don't want to have that kind of association stuck in my head," Garret continues with a sigh, rubbing his brow. "Do whatever you want, but I'm not going to be close by when you do it. Just so you know." You wouldn't expect him to be. ] Well, this appears to be the situation — even ghosts get horny and need a fuck every now and then, it looks like. Would you like the take the Jarl's niece up on her offer?
rows.translation: 你转身准备离开，但在穿过那些熙熙攘攘的人群后，突然感到有人用冰冷的手掌抓住了你的肩膀，于是你转过身来。看到的是玛格娜的背影，而那位伯爵的侄女脸上的表情也比刚才柔和了许多。 “出了什么事情吗？”你心想，她刚才不应该是只是说了句再见而已吗？ 呃，好吧。我有个问题想问你，不过最好不在我叔叔那些人面前问。毕竟，要以身作则嘛，你懂的吧？如果当着他们的面问你，只会带来负面的影响……哎，算了。如果我公开约你出来，大家只会嘲笑我，并不是出于嘲笑的意思，而是就像我说的，我需要以身作则，如果大家都乱来一通，那什么事情都办不成……该死，我说到这一步了，对吧？ 你应该已经明白事情会发展成什么样子了。她就是想发泄情绪，而在这种公开场合提出这样的要求，至少现在来说，确实不太合适。 嗯，没错。如果我直接当面提出邀请，你肯定会感到尴尬。虽然我看起来是这样，但实际上我并不喜欢那种方式。不过，你确实是我很久以来遇到的第一个真正反抗过我的人，我挺喜欢你的。上次发生这种事的时候，我还在贾西兰的角斗场里，所以你可以想象，那已经是很久以前的事了。 所以……嗯，想一起玩吗？ [party.comp cait brint garret |你转向凯特，低声问道：马拉克是否对与不死生物发生性关系有什么看法？她在神庙里学习到了什么？这种行为是被禁止的，还是有什么其他规定？ 嗯，呃。凯特皱起了眉头，她拼命地试图回忆起自己所知道的关于这个话题的那些零星信息。嗯，其实不应该接触尸体，因为那确实是传播疾病的一种方式。不过鬼魂……关于鬼魂也有一些传说。一般来说，与鬼魂打交道并不是个好主意，因为它们可能会对你做出一些不好的事情；不过如果它们怀有善意的话，那也没关系，就像这个鬼魂一样。 所以，这其实是一场赌博。 凯特无奈地举起双手，嘴角勉强挤出一丝微笑。我真的不知道。不过……如果我对自己更有信心的话，我就会要求加入的。这就是我的答案。 | 我愿意试试。布林特补充道。嗯，要不是因为天气太冷的话。被冻得动弹不得，确实会让人没了性欲，别见怪。不过，这样的经历也挺有意思的…… 一次有趣的体验，嗯。 我想，我并没有那么勇敢，愿意去尝试把我的东西塞进一个冰冷的鬼魂身体里吧，只是说说而已。毕竟现实点来说——我们目前还并没有接到关于加斯的任务，现在讨论这些事情还为时过早。这些鬼魂看起来也不会拔出武器来攻击我们，但我真的不会在这里待得比必要的时间更久。 | 加雷特只是站在一旁，背对着你，双臂交叉在宽阔的胸前。当你走近他并询问他的意见时，他的其中一只耳朵微微朝你的方向转动了一下。 说实话……请不要碰她。她太像我记忆中妈妈的样貌了。 这么说吧，那实在有点太直接了。 我只是……不想让那种联想留在我的脑海里。加雷特叹了口气，揉了揉额头，继续说道。你想做什么都行，不过当你做那些事情的时候，我肯定不会在附近。只是想让你知道这一点。 你绝对想不到他会是这种人。 ] 嗯，看来情况就是这样的——就连鬼魂也会产生性欲，偶尔也需要发泄一下。你愿意接受领主的侄女提出的邀请吗？

rows.original: Fucking a ghost isn't the kind of opportunity that shows up every day. Yeah, you'll take it.
rows.translation: 跟鬼上床这种机会可不是每天都会出现的。没错，你肯定会抓住这个机会的。
rows.raw: "Fucking a ghost isn't the kind of opportunity that shows up every day. Yeah, you'll take it."

rows.original: Given the situation[party.has brint cait garret| and hearing what your companion[party.manyCompanions|s have| has] to say,] you think you'll be turning this one down. You don't have the time to get jiggy in a fortress full of malevolent ghosts, and even if you did you're not too sure about this whole thing. Trying to be as tactful as possible, you explain to Magna that you're really not interested in a bout of smashing right now. It doesn't help that she doesn't seem to realize she's dead, so you can't point that out to her, but at last you get your denial through. "Oh. Pity." You're a bit surprised — you'd have expected more of a vigorous reaction from a big girl like her, but she seems to be taking it well. "A shame, but you can't have everything you want; Uncle taught me that. Well then, stay healthy, okay? We're going to be seeing a lot of action soon, the minotaurs say, and it'd be a shame to miss out on the fighting because of some stupid reason or the other." Same to her. "That's what I'm talking about!" Regaining some of her previous good humor, the wolfess claps you on the back hard enough to knock the wind out of your lungs. "I'll see you at the next muster!" With that, she clomps off, leaving you standing in a corner of the hall.[party.has garret| As you're pondering all of this, Garret sidles up and elbows you. "Look... I know this is awkward, but thanks for not fucking her. I know she's a ghost, I know she's dead and all, but when I said she looks like my mom, I really meant it. Thanks for not doing that to me." No problem. "Right, then. Let's move on before something weirder happens."]
rows.translation: 鉴于当前的情况[party.has brint cait garret| 以及听听你的同伴说了什么[party.manyCompanions|拥有| 拥有]也就是说，]你以为自己会拒绝这个邀请吧？你根本没有时间去一个充满邪恶幽灵的堡垒里冒险，而且就算你有时间，你也不太确定自己是否真的愿意参与这种事情。你尽量委婉地告诉玛格娜，现在你真的没有兴趣去参加任何冒险活动。更糟糕的是，她似乎根本没有意识到自己已经死了，所以你也无法跟她说明这一点，不过最终你还是成功地拒绝了她的邀请。 哦，真可怜。你有点惊讶——你本以为像她这样一个成熟的女孩会做出更激烈的反应，但她似乎对此表现得相当冷静。真遗憾，但人不可能得到自己想要的一切；叔叔就是这么教导我的。那么，一定要注意身体健康，好吗？据说很快就会有一场激烈的战斗发生了，如果我们因为一些愚蠢的原因而错过了这场战斗，那就太可惜了。 她也是同样的情况。 就是这个意思！狼女重新恢复了往日的幽默感，她用力拍了拍你的后背，那一拍简直让你喘不过气来。下次集合时见！ 说完，她一瘸一拐地走了，留下你独自站在大厅的角落里。[party.has garret| 就在你思考这些问题的时候，加雷特悄悄凑过来，用肘子轻推了你一下。 听着……我知道这有点尴尬，但真的谢谢你没有和她发生什么。我知道她只是个幽灵，已经去世了，但当我说她长得像我妈妈时，我是真心的。谢谢你没有让我遭受那样的事情。 没问题。 好吧，那我们继续吧，免得再发生什么更奇怪的事情。]

rows.original: You step up to the tomes in the library and marvel at how well they've been preserved, considering their age. Selecting one of them at random, you gingerly pick it up; it doesn't quite crumble into dust in your hands, but it's obvious that cover, spine and pages alike are frail. Slowly, you turn the pages and see what this one has to offer, a glimpse into the writer's mindset from more than two centuries ago, perhaps: [rand |The way of the Iron Poet It is the way of some lowlanders to devote their lives to either strength of arms or to pursuits of the mind. Perhaps it may work for them, safe in their warm homes, but such is not the path we tread. To do so is to be missing one half of the whole and needlessly hobble oneself. It is well-understood that exercising the body leads to greater invigoration of the mind; improved circulation of blood and breath to the head banishes ennui and promotes clear thinking. Straining the body leads to the development of one's will and tenacity, for the barriers to winning a bout are just as weighty in the mind as they are in the realm of the material. Similarly, by improving one's mind, one discovers better, more efficient ways to exercise one's body. By exercising the nerve pathways that lead from eye to limb, one becomes more dexterous and faster to react to the moves of one's opponents. By reading about the past victories and losses of others, one learns from the experiences of others without needing to suffer misfortune oneself. When a single person exercises both body and mind, their united power is greater than that of two who have trained one but neglected the other. It is such that we do not scorn books and learning, yet neither do we forget martial training: a man who only lives by the sword is a brute, while one who only lives by the pen is a fop. All warriors should be poets, and all poets should be warriors; if this burden is too much for you, then you are deserving of neither. A lupie of any pack should be able to sing a saga, to slaughter and butcher livestock, to put thoughts to paper, to make camp in the snow. He or she should experience wonder at the dawn over the mountains, drink deeply of both clean mountain springs and fresh-brewed mead, and to defeat enemies in pitched battle. Only then can one say that life has been lived to the fullest with a variety of wholesome experiences. Such is the way of the Iron Poet, the unbreakable tower of strength who nevertheless has the wits and spirit to move another to tears with words and writing. Such is the path the ideal lupine should tread. |The Cold The cold is here. Its teeth sink through my fur And gnaw at my flesh. The snow is here. It blankets the mountains and valleys Making passage impossible. The ice is here. It pelts down from above Uncaring of whom it strikes or kills. I am here. I have lived through cold, snow and ice. They have made me stronger. |Obedience and Discipline By Sirius Silvereye What is obedience? The simpleton will answer that it is the reverence one has for one's elders, for one's thane and jarl, for the Lore. That is not wholly incorrect, but it leaves out several vital nuances that without which lies and misinformation can be spread. The fool will answer that it is a yoke, a chain that evil rulers use to bind their subjects and keep them in their thrall; that it should be resisted at every turn. Such sentiments are the chief tools of those who sow dissent and sedition, hoping to appeal to the greed and avarice of those who hear them. When logic is applied to this train of thought, it soon falls apart, for the very essence of obedience decries such a simple and superficial interpretation. Allow me to elaborate: Obedience demands a person who is capable of putting others first and himself last. Putting others first demands discipline, the ability to finish a task without being distracted. Putting others first demands logic that will block the emotion that may ask one to do otherwise. Putting others first demands ethicality that makes one believe in and understand the benefits of abiding the rules of conduct. One cannot master the world around him without first mastering oneself, and a task left unfinished is a task failed. A wolf in service of the thane is obedient, that is to be sure. But the Thane is also obedient to the Lore, and hence also in service of his subjects. To not put others first and ask of obedience from others is wantonness, for then there are no rules or limits to what may be commanded; to free oneself from the so-called chains of obedience that bind oneself is to invite the very disaster that such fools claim to oppose! When obedience is realized by all within a pack, from lowest thrall to greatest thane, harmony prevails. That should be the goal of all lupines. |My exploits, volume one By Magna Hegan Hail, reader. I am Magna, but you know who I am by that name alone, for there is only one Magna. Uncle has asked me to pen some form of memoir, for though I am young, I have had many an adventure, and he wishes that others may learn and be inspired by my experiences. As his niece, I am only too pleased to acquiesce. From my youth, tournaments and duels have fallen in my favor, gaining me much fame within the pack. Hush, for these are but small glories compared to my actions later in life, although they did prepare — both good and ill — me for the first of my travels. Since I was of the jarl's family, I was well-cared for and trained as a pup, yet as his niece I had no claim to his position. Thus having few of the responsibilities which now burden my younger cousins, I was free to do as I wished; wanderlust overtook me as I tired of bouts and tournaments, and I decided to journey to put my skills to good use. Before I left, Aunt Thyri was kind enough to make me a gift of some very solid fur-lined boots, both to prevent blisters on the road and to keep my feet dry in the rain. After hearing countless tales of aching feet from others less prepared, here lies the first lesson I wish to impart to the reader: travel of any distance requires good footwear, and if possible, a walking stick or staff! You will be glad that you have had both. My first adventure took place when I had just left the ancestral lands and entered the plains to the south. Local farmers were complaining that thieves lurking in the forest were stealing their crop, and were willing to pay me to deal with them. I agreed to their request, but quietly resolved to extract proof of these thieves' guilt before laying my sword to them. Following the farmers' words, I guessed when the thieves would next strike and set up a prowl. On the second night, my patience was rewarded; humans approached from afar and slipped into the fields, making off with many melons in the sacks across their shoulders. I could have stopped them there and then, but resolved to root out the entire den of thieves; following their scent, I tracked them down to their forest hideout. Ten of them were cramped in one small shack; I was young and foolish, and my past victories had gone to my head — I roared a challenge and took them all on at once. This proved to be a mistake, for although they were no match for me, my overconfidence and their numbers led one of them to slip his knife between my ribs. Fortunately, I had slain enough of the wretches that the rest were disheartened enough to flee, and I collapsed to the ground, bleeding profusely from the grievous wound. For a moment, I thought I was going to die there in the most ignoble fashion, laid low by a common footpad's shiv! Fortunately, hours spent disciplining my mind against pain and panic served me well as my wits came back to me, and I remembered enough of my lessons in field dressing to bind the wound with clean cloth and staunch the bleeding with the help of one of my aunt's unguents before I lost too much of my vital essence. I was still weak, but no longer in mortal danger. The entirety of the farmers' reward was spent in the care of a proficient healer, where I recovered sufficiently over the course of a week and a half. Fortunately, no vital organs had been punctured, and I made a full recovery in time. Even though I came out no richer in coin than I had when I begun, I had learned two valuable lessons from this experience: the dangers of overconfidence, and the importance of a disciplined mind and body in the face of pain. ]

服从要求一个人能够将他人置于自己之前。将他人置于首位需要自律，需要具备在不被干扰的情况下完成任务的能力。将他人置于首位还需要运用逻辑，来抑制那些可能使人做出相反行为的情绪。将他人置于首位更要求一个人具备道德准则，能够相信并理解遵守行为规范所带来的好处。 一个人若不先掌握自己，就无法掌控周围的世界；而任何未完成的任务，都意味着失败。 当然，为一位领主服务的狼会是忠诚的。但这位领主本身也必须遵守古老的法则，因此他也在为他的子民服务。不把他人放在首位，却要求他人服从，这种行为才是肆无忌惮的；因为这样一来，命令的内容就再也没有任何规则或界限了。而摆脱那些所谓的“服从的枷锁”，其实正是招致那些愚蠢之徒所声称要反对的灾难啊！ 当一个狼群中的每一个成员，从最底层的仆从到最高位的领袖，都能做到服从命令时，和谐便得以实现。这应该是所有狼族成员追求的目标。 |我的辉煌事迹，第一卷 作者：玛格娜·希根 亲爱的读者，您好。我叫玛格娜，但只要听到这个名字，你们就应该知道我是谁了，因为世上只有一个玛格娜。叔叔让我写一些回忆录，因为虽然我还年轻，但我已经经历了许多冒险，他希望其他人能够通过我的故事学到东西，获得启发。 作为他的侄女，我当然非常乐意同意他的请求。 从我年轻的时候起，比赛和决斗就一直深受我的喜爱，这些经历让我在族群中获得了许多声誉。不过，这些都只是些微不足道的荣耀罢了，与我后来所做的事情相比，简直算不了什么。不过，这些经历确实为我后来的第一次冒险之旅做好了准备——无论是好是坏，都起到了一定的作用。由于我属于酋长的家族，从小就受到了悉心的照料和训练，但作为他的侄女，我并没有资格继承他的地位。因此，与我那些年纪较小的表兄弟们相比，我承担的责任要少得多，这让我可以随心所欲地做自己想做的事情。当我对那些不断的战斗和比赛感到厌倦时，旅行的渴望便占据了我的内心，于是我决定踏上旅途，将我的技能运用到实际中去。 在我离开之前，泰丽阿姨好心送了我一双质地非常厚实的毛皮衬里靴子，这样既可以在路上防止脚起水泡，也能在雨天保持双脚干燥。听过了太多关于那些没有做好充分准备的人脚部受伤的故事，因此我想向各位读者传达第一个重要经验：无论长途旅行还是短途出行，都必须准备合适的鞋具；如果可能的话，还最好准备一根拐杖或手杖！相信我，拥有这两样东西一定会让你感到非常方便。 我的第一次冒险发生在我刚离开祖籍之地，进入南方的平原之时。当地的农民们抱怨说，森林里潜藏的窃贼正在偷走他们的庄稼，他们愿意付钱让我去对付这些窃贼。我答应了他们的请求，但暗下决心要在采取行动之前找到证明这些窃贼有罪的证据。 按照农民们的提示，我推测小偷们下次会在什么时候行动，于是便埋伏了起来。到了第二个夜晚，我的耐心终于得到了回报——那些人类从远处悄悄接近，溜进了田地，把许多甜瓜装进袋子里带走了。我本可以当场阻止他们，但我决定要彻底捣毁这个贼窝。顺着他们的踪迹，我最终找到了他们藏在森林里的藏身处。 有十个人挤在一间小棚屋里；我当时年轻又愚蠢，过去的胜利让我变得骄傲自大——我大声挑衅，决定同时与他们所有人决斗。结果这成了一个错误，因为虽然他们根本不是我的对手，但我的过度自信加上他们的人数优势，让其中一个人趁机用刀刺中了我的肋骨。幸运的是，我之前已经杀死了足够多的那些混蛋，剩下的那些人吓得纷纷逃跑了。我倒在地上，伤口流出了大量的血。 有那么一刻，我以为自己会以最卑微的方式死在那里，被一个普通的盗贼用匕首刺死！幸运的是，我花了数小时强迫自己抑制疼痛和恐慌，这让我恢复了理智。我还记得一些关于野外包扎的基本知识，于是用干净的布包扎伤口，还借助我阿姨准备的一些药膏止住了出血，这才没有让我的生命之源流失太多。虽然我仍然很虚弱，但已经不再有生命危险了。 农民们获得的全部报酬都被用来聘请一位技艺高超的医治者，因此在一个半星期的时间里，我的身体状况得到了充分的恢复。幸运的是，我的内脏没有受到任何损伤，所以我最终完全康复了。虽然这次经历并没有让我获得任何额外的财富，但我从中吸取了两条宝贵的经验：一是过度自信的危险性，二是面对痛苦时，保持冷静与自律的重要性。 ]
rows.raw: " You step up to the tomes in the library and marvel at how well they've been preserved, considering their age. Selecting one of them at random, you gingerly pick it up; it doesn't quite crumble into dust in your hands, but it's obvious that cover, spine and pages alike are frail. Slowly, you turn the pages and see what this one has to offer, a glimpse into the writer's mindset from more than two centuries ago, perhaps: [rand |The way of the Iron Poet It is the way of some lowlanders to devote their lives to either strength of arms or to pursuits of the mind. Perhaps it may work for them, safe in their warm homes, but such is not the path we tread. To do so is to be missing one half of the whole and needlessly hobble oneself. It is well-understood that exercising the body leads to greater invigoration of the mind; improved circulation of blood and breath to the head banishes ennui and promotes clear thinking. Straining the body leads to the development of one's will and tenacity, for the barriers to winning a bout are just as weighty in the mind as they are in the realm of the material. Similarly, by improving one's mind, one discovers better, more efficient ways to exercise one's body. By exercising the nerve pathways that lead from eye to limb, one becomes more dexterous and faster to react to the moves of one's opponents. By reading about the past victories and losses of others, one learns from the experiences of others without needing to suffer misfortune oneself. When a single person exercises both body and mind, their united power is greater than that of two who have trained one but neglected the other. It is such that we do not scorn books and learning, yet neither do we forget martial training: a man who only lives by the sword is a brute, while one who only lives by the pen is a fop. All warriors should be poets, and all poets should be warriors; if this burden is too much for you, then you are deserving of neither. A lupie of any pack should be able to sing a saga, to slaughter and butcher livestock, to put thoughts to paper, to make camp in the snow. He or she should experience wonder at the dawn over the mountains, drink deeply of both clean mountain springs and fresh-brewed mead, and to defeat enemies in pitched battle. Only then can one say that life has been lived to the fullest with a variety of wholesome experiences. Such is the way of the Iron Poet, the unbreakable tower of strength who nevertheless has the wits and spirit to move another to tears with words and writing. Such is the path the ideal lupine should tread. |The Cold The cold is here. Its teeth sink through my fur And gnaw at my flesh. The snow is here. It blankets the mountains and valleys Making passage impossible. The ice is here. It pelts down from above Uncaring of whom it strikes or kills. I am here. I have lived through cold, snow and ice. They have made me stronger. |Obedience and Discipline By Sirius Silvereye What is obedience? The simpleton will answer that it is the reverence one has for one's elders, for one's thane and jarl, for the Lore. That is not wholly incorrect, but it leaves out several vital nuances that without which lies and misinformation can be spread. The fool will answer that it is a yoke, a chain that evil rulers use to bind their subjects and keep them in their thrall; that it should be resisted at every turn. Such sentiments are the chief tools of those who sow dissent and sedition, hoping to appeal to the greed and avarice of those who hear them. When logic is applied to this train of thought, it soon falls apart, for the very essence of obedience decries such a simple and superficial interpretation. Allow me to elaborate: Obedience demands a person who is capable of putting others first and himself last. Putting others first demands discipline, the ability to finish a task without being distracted. Putting others first demands logic that will block the emotion that may ask one to do otherwise. Putting others first demands ethicality that makes one believe in and understand the benefits of abiding the rules of conduct. One cannot master the world around him without first mastering oneself, and a task left unfinished is a task failed. A wolf in service of the thane is obedient, that is to be sure. But the Thane is also obedient to the Lore, and hence also in service of his subjects. To not put others first and ask of obedience from others is wantonness, for then there are no rules or limits to what may be commanded; to free oneself from the so-called chains of obedience that bind oneself is to invite the very disaster that such fools claim to oppose! When obedience is realized by all within a pack, from lowest thrall to greatest thane, harmony prevails. That should be the goal of all lupines. |My exploits, volume one By Magna Hegan Hail, reader. I am Magna, but you know who I am by that name alone, for there is only one Magna. Uncle has asked me to pen some form of memoir, for though I am young, I have had many an adventure, and he wishes that others may learn and be inspired by my experiences. As his niece, I am only too pleased to acquiesce. From my youth, tournaments and duels have fallen in my favor, gaining me much fame within the pack. Hush, for these are but small glories compared to my actions later in life, although they did prepare — both good and ill — me for the first of my travels. Since I was of the jarl's family, I was well-cared for and trained as a pup, yet as his niece I had no claim to his position. Thus having few of the responsibilities which now burden my younger cousins, I was free to do as I wished; wanderlust overtook me as I tired of bouts and tournaments, and I decided to journey to put my skills to good use. Before I left, Aunt Thyri was kind enough to make me a gift of some very solid fur-lined boots, both to prevent blisters on the road and to keep my feet dry in the rain. After hearing countless tales of aching feet from others less prepared, here lies the first lesson I wish to impart to the reader: travel of any distance requires good footwear, and if possible, a walking stick or staff! You will be glad that you have had both. My first adventure took place when I had just left the ancestral lands and entered the plains to the south. Local farmers were complaining that thieves lurking in the forest were stealing their crop, and were willing to pay me to deal with them. I agreed to their request, but quietly resolved to extract proof of these thieves' guilt before laying my sword to them. Following the farmers' words, I guessed when the thieves would next strike and set up a prowl. On the second night, my patience was rewarded; humans approached from afar and slipped into the fields, making off with many melons in the sacks across their shoulders. I could have stopped them there and then, but resolved to root out the entire den of thieves; following their scent, I tracked them down to their forest hideout. Ten of them were cramped in one small shack; I was young and foolish, and my past victories had gone to my head — I roared a challenge and took them all on at once. This proved to be a mistake, for although they were no match for me, my overconfidence and their numbers led one of them to slip his knife between my ribs. Fortunately, I had slain enough of the wretches that the rest were disheartened enough to flee, and I collapsed to the ground, bleeding profusely from the grievous wound. For a moment, I thought I was going to die there in the most ignoble fashion, laid low by a common footpad's shiv! Fortunately, hours spent disciplining my mind against pain and panic served me well as my wits came back to me, and I remembered enough of my lessons in field dressing to bind the wound with clean cloth and staunch the bleeding with the help of one of my aunt's unguents before I lost too much of my vital essence. I was still weak, but no longer in mortal danger. The entirety of the farmers' reward was spent in the care of a proficient healer, where I recovered sufficiently over the course of a week and a half. Fortunately, no vital organs had been punctured, and I made a full recovery in time. Even though I came out no richer in coin than I had when I begun, I had learned two valuable lessons from this experience: the dangers of overconfidence, and the importance of a disciplined mind and body in the face of pain. ]"

rows.original: You eye the small brass chest sitting in one of the library's cubbyholes. Ornate carvings of runes cover its lid, and the sides are decorated with yet more carvings, this time of a forest scene, complete with deer and rabbits running along its length. Given the bare and spartan conditions in which most of the garrison lived in, this has to be of some import — it certainly looks like something that'd fit in a noble's abode than in a border fort, even if this is the library. You try to pick it up, and it doesn't move. Brushing off the thick coat of dust that it's developed over the years, you quickly discover why: it's bolted to the stone bricks. Huh, so it's a permanent fixture... interesting. Guess you can't take the chest itself with you, but hopefully whatever's inside will be worth it. Oho. Now that the dust's off, you spy several lines of words etched into the lid — likely with acid of some sort — and a large lock with numerous tumblers, each one etched with letters. [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion courtesan|You've come across these before in your past — wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly|players|servants]. Each of these combination locks was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was, a riddle was often posed on the chest itself. If you could solve it and thereby rotate the tumblers into the right position, the chest would unlock and allow you to claim its contents.|[party.has cait|"Father used to tell Calla and I about these," Cait pipes up as she studies the chest. "They're wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly|players|servants]. Each combination lock was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was a riddle was often posed on the chest itself." So if you solved this thing, the lock would just pop open and you could just help yourself to anything inside. "Yep!"|Hmm, what can this all mean? It certainly seems like a thoroughly roundabout way to secure a container, but at least it isn't likely to be trapped in the bargain. ] ] Well, what now?
rows.translation: 你的目光落在图书馆某个书架角落里那个小小的黄铜箱子上。它的盖子上刻着精美的符文图案，箱身两侧也装饰着更多的雕刻，这次描绘的是一片森林场景，还有鹿和兔子在森林中奔跑。考虑到驻军中的大多数人所处的环境都是如此简陋粗糙，这一点显然相当重要——尽管这只是一个图书馆，但它看起来更像是适合贵族居住的地方，而不是边境要塞应有的模样。 你试图把它拿起来，但它一动不动。当你拂去那些多年来积在上面厚实的一层灰尘后，你很快就明白了原因：它被用螺栓固定在石砖上了。嗯，原来它是固定不动的……有意思。看来你不能把那个箱子本身带在身上，但希望里面的东西确实值得这个麻烦。 哦，现在灰尘已经被拂掉了，你发现箱子的盖子上刻有几行文字——很可能是用某种酸蚀刻上去的——还有一个带有许多小转盘的巨大锁，每个转盘上都刻着字母。 [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion courtesan|你在过去曾经见过这类东西——字锁箱。这种箱子曾是贝尔哈兰老贵族们的最爱，他们用它来保护贵重物品，防止那些不识字的[silly|玩家们|仆从们]偷走。这些组合锁每一把都需要输入密码才能打开，为了帮助主人记住密码，人们通常会在箱子本身上设置一个谜语。如果你能够解开这个谜语，将锁芯旋转到正确的位置，箱子就会打开，让你取走里面的物品。|[party.has cait|“父亲过去常给我和卡拉讲这些，”凯特在研究那个箱子时开口说道。“这些是字锁箱，是古老的贝尔哈兰贵族们非常喜爱的物品，它们的作用就是保护贵重物品免受那些不识字的[silly|玩家们|仆从们]侵害。每一把组合锁都需要输入正确的密码才能打开，而为了帮助主人记住密码，人们通常会在箱子本身上设置一个谜语来帮助记忆。” 所以，如果你解决了这个问题，锁就会自动打开，然后你就可以取走里面的任何东西了。 “没错！”|嗯，这一切到底意味着什么呢？这种方式获取一个容器似乎确实有些迂回，但至少它不太可能还附带什么陷阱。 ] ] 那么，现在该怎么办呢？
