rows.original: — And the jarl lets out a soft groan and slumps back in the throne, his sword clattering to the floor, blade as forlorn as the man. This looks like a good time to give him some space, so you step back and remain silent as Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen stares down at his ghostly hands, his fingers trembling. His breathing is even more pained than ever, and as you look on, he clenches and unclenches his fists into tight balls, thickset, furry fingers shimmering in the dim light. "I... I had thought it might happen. That when death did come... I would know. When I smelled death on the wind, I thought it came from you... but it was from myself, wasn't it?" You remain silent. At length, Galon Gunvaldsen collects himself as best as he can and raises his gaze to yours. "Tell me, [pc.race]. It has been more than two hundred years?" You remember River's tale, and nod. Thereabouts, since the Godswar. For the first time since you've met him, the jarl looks at his surroundings and seems to notice the dilapidated state his fortress is in. For something as simple as a mirror and a few words to have freed a ghost from the false reality he was trapped in... well, stranger things have happened. "If you are here, that means we eventually won, despite my failure..." It took much sacrifice, but the wraiths were beaten back, yes. Galon groans again, and bends over to pick up his sword off the ground before leaning his weight on it once more. "Then... why did you come here, to this place? What did you hope to achieve? Are you adventurers? Treasure hunters?" You... um, you were sent here to retrieve his medallion of office. "Ah. For the pack, no doubt. Gold does not decay with years, after all." The jarl closes his eyes and thinks for a few moments. "It was in front of my face all the time, but I could not see it. It's almost as if a veil had been draped over my eyes... until you forced me to face the truth. Perhaps it is... it is better this way. I would not have been allowed to remain jarl after what happened; the shame would have been too great." Silence. The fact that he might have been the last straw that broke the alliance between the packs and Khor'minos might just be too much for him to bear as he is. "Do the histories tell of my family and their fate?" You hesitate a moment, then decide that the jarl probably isn't going to shoot the messenger here. Still, you can't help but be a little hesitant when you relate River's tale to him. "I... am not surprised. Exile was the least of the fates which could have befallen them; at least, perhaps, my line still exists somewhere, and that is as much as I can ask for in my state. So, you are here for my medallion of office?" Yes. The lupines of today need it. "Then take it. It's not as if I can bring it with me, wherever it is that I'm fated to go when I pass. If it will restore some of our lost honor, then you're free to have it." The words spoken, Jarl Gunvaldsen bows his head and lifts both chain and medallion off his neck, placing them in your hands. Up close, you can see them in so much detail: the golden crossed swords with a burnished steel border, the heavy links of the chain, the sapphires in the wolfshead's eyes... hah, truly a wolf's adornment if there were ever one. He is most gracious. "Grace has nothing to do with it. Regret, perhaps... and a desire to right wrongs. And since I can't take them with me, either, let me make a gift to you of my sword and cloak." With that said, the jarl grasps his blade, still in scabbard, in both hands and solemnly passes it to you. Frost swirls about the scabbard as you take the basket-hilted bastard sword in hand, and you eye the jarl as he pulls off the spectral, fur-lined cloak from about his shoulders, wondering what has kept his possessions so well-preserved after all this time. He folds the cloak up into a neat square and presses it into your hands. It's thick and warm, garb meant for winter, and even given its nature it confers a thin thread of warmth into your fingers as you close your hands in about it. "That's all I have to give to you, [pc.race]," the jarl says at last, rolling his shoulders and looking about the empty audience chamber. "I suppose I should be leaving, but..." But? He looks sheepish. "Could you accompany me on the way out? I shouldn't have to ask you this, but to see what has happened to my fort in the intervening years... I fear it may be a match for my nerves. It must seem craven of me to ask this of you, but -" Oh, say no more. You'd be more than happy to go ahead and help him through this. You put him in this predicament after all, didn't you? You give the jarl a nod, and fall in at his side as he staggers out of the audience chamber and down the stairs into the ramparts. Odd. Wherever Galon Gunvaldsen passes, the spirits of his men start fading into view — lupines in ancient chainmail and livery slumped against walls, sprawled in alcoves, waiting for death. Bits of broken crockery lie on the floor amidst discarded weapons and fallen banners... it's as if the jarl himself was a torch, a beacon that allows you to see the last moments of Fort Marrok in spectral form. "Get up," he says softly to the massed lupines. "Our time is over." The garrison soldiers look up at him with uncomprehending eyes. "Lord, I don't understand -" "We are dead. We have been dead for a long time." He pauses, considering his words. "We failed, but the wraiths were defeated without us. The world has passed by without us. It's time for us to go." The ghosts look at their Jarl, at each other, then at you. As one, realization to dawn upon them, and their shoulders droop as they bow their heads. "Defeated warriors do not take their weapons with them to the beyond," one of them murmurs. Galon nods. "Do you see me with my sword? Weapon or no weapon, at last... an ending. I've failed in both my duty to lead you, and my duty to keep the pack's honor; I'll answer for both in my own time. But for now, onward and outward." Onward and outward indeed. The procession following the both of you is a sight to behold, a steadily growing stream of ghostly lupines limping and dragging themselves after you and the jarl. Dirty, disheveled, and dogged — but relieved in their own way, as if a huge spell that hung over their heads had been broken. It probably had. At last, the two of you reach the gates — now they are no longer dilapidated, but strong and gleaming, if translucent. The scent of fresh air wafts in from the canyon bottom, and the jarl closes his eyes and folds his hands for a moment, taking in the scent of freedom. "I remember now. The men had been trying to dig for hours, days, not knowing how deeply in the earth the wraiths had entombed us. I was on my throne waiting for the end, determined to die in as dignified a fashion as I could. To never see the light again..." It must have been harrowing. "For me, perhaps. And for the whole of the pack." He looks back at the garrison following him, and they manage a weak, if genuine cheer. "I owe you my eternal thanks," he says. "And I haven't even so much as asked your name." It's [pc.name]. "Well met then, [pc.name], and goodbye," Jarl Gunvaldsen salutes you crisply. "Day after day, one after the other, until we wake up and it turns out that's the day it all ends for you. You have to do what you can, when you can, because who knows if tomorrow is even happening?" That sounds deep. "It was what my father told me on his deathbed, before he had to go." The jarl looks away from you and squares his shoulders. "Make good use of my gifts, [pc.name]. May we one day meet again upon the peaks and snow. "Thyri... I'm sorry to have kept you waiting for so long." Without another word, he steps out into the canyon, through the gates — and the moment the jarl passes beyond the gates of his doomed fortress, he dissolves into a thousand spectral motes of glimmering radiance that, in their own time, wink out of existence. The wolves of Fort Marrok follow their lord, hundreds of specters pouring out from the gates and dissipating into nothingness, ranks upon ranks of livery-clad canines passing into the beyond until only emptiness is left, and the gates slowly revert to their old run-down state. "Wow." A soft tugging on your arms alerts you to River's presence. The fluffy kitten bard has finally deigned to make his presence known, stepping out from his hiding place between the rubble piles to gape at the exorcism you've just wrought. Hey, that was something, wasn't it? "Indeed, it was." River's attempt to remain solemn is made all the more comical by his ears and tail's constant twitching. "I mean, the sheer sight of all those spirits coming out of the fortress — just what did you do in there?" Oh, nothing much. Just a few shenanigans involving a hand mirror and a little smooth talking, that's all. River looks at you funny, then shakes his head and sighs. "You've got to tell me all about it on the way back, unless you want me making stuff up when I eventually do my composing. You don't want that, do you?" Haha, of course not. "Good, good." River peers up into your full hands and picks the jarl's medallion off the pile, giving it a long sniff and pressing his little fingers against its heavy surface. "Dusty and old. But it's the real thing, there's no doubt about that. Garth'll have a field day with this." You got some other things, too. Any idea about what you should do with the sword and cloak? "Don't throw it out, that would be my suggestion," he tells you. All right, then — you'll keep them on hand. Now, you don't think there's anything left for you here; perhaps you should get going back home. "Of course!" River replies as he starts off at a brisk walk. "And I want you to tell me everything that happened in there! No shirking now, got it?" The trip back to Hawkethorne is uneventful and thankfully so; you've had enough excitement for one day. River badgers you for the whole trip, getting down as many details as you're willing to give; you're not that inclined to talk at first, but the flask of brandy he offers you does smooth out your social graces somewhat. At length, though, the palisade walls of Hawkethorne draw into view. River gives you a nod, then steps away. "Well, this is it. I'm going to go ahead to the Frost Hound and get something to get those creative juices flowing. Maybe you'll be there shortly? Garth does want his little trinket, after all."
rows.translation: — 然后，这位酋长发出一声轻弱的呻吟，整个人瘫软在王座上，他的剑重重地落在地上，剑刃仿佛和主人一样充满绝望。此刻，似乎应该给他一些空间，于是你退后一步，保持沉默。加隆·冈瓦尔德森领主凝视着自己那双仿佛幽灵般的双手，手指在颤抖着。他的呼吸比以往任何时候都要艰难，你看着他一次次地将拳头握紧又松开，那些粗壮而多毛的手指在昏暗的光线下微微闪烁着。 我……我本来以为这种事会发生。当我感觉到死亡的气息来临时……我就能明白。当我闻到风中带着死亡的气息时，我以为那是你带来的……但其实，那是我自己带来的，对吧？ 你始终保持着沉默。最终，加隆·冈瓦尔德森竭力稳定了自己的情绪，然后将目光投向了你。 告诉我， [pc.race]已经过去两百多年了？ 你记得瑞弗的故事，于是点了点头。自那场神战之后，事情就是这样的。 这是你第一次见到他之后，这位酋长才真正注意到自己周围的环境，也注意到了自己的堡垒已经变得如此破败。仅仅因为一面镜子和几句话，就能让一个幽灵从它所被困住的虚假现实中解脱出来……嗯，其实更离奇的事情也发生过。 如果你在这里，那就意味着尽管我失败了，但我们最终还是赢了…… 确实，人们付出了巨大的牺牲，但这些怨灵最终还是被击退了。 加隆再次发出呻吟，弯下身子从地上捡起他的剑，然后再次依靠着这把剑站了起来。那么……你为什么来到这里，来到这个地方？你究竟想要达到什么目的？你是冒险家吗？还是寻宝人？ 你……嗯，你是被派到这里来取回他的官职徽章的。 啊，当然是为了那个包裹了。毕竟，黄金是不会随着时间的流逝而贬值的。领主闭上眼睛，沉思了片刻。它一直就在我眼前，但我却视而不见。就好像有一层面纱蒙在了我的眼睛上……直到你迫使我面对真相。或许这样……确实更好。发生了那些事之后，我本来就不可能继续担任酋长；那种耻辱实在太大了。 沉默。事实上，他或许正是那个导致各个族群与科尔米诺斯之间的联盟破裂的最后一根稻草——对于他目前的状况来说，这个事实或许实在太难以承受了。 这些历史记载中是否提到了我的家族以及他们的命运？ 你犹豫了片刻，然后认为这位酋长应该不会责怪传达消息的人。不过，当你把瑞弗的故事告诉他的时候，还是不禁有些忐忑不安。 我……并不感到惊讶。流放对他们来说已经是最好的结局了；至少，我的血脉或许还在某个地方延续着，对于我目前的处境来说，这已经是我所能期望的全部了。那么，你来这里是想要我的官职徽章吗？ 是的。如今的狼族确实需要它。 那就拿去吧。反正我去世后，无论会被带到哪里去，这些东西也不可能跟着我。如果这些东西能让我们失去的荣誉得到一些弥补，那你就尽管拿去吧。 听到这些话，冈瓦尔德森领主低下头，将脖子上的链条和徽章取下来，交到了你的手中。仔细观察，你可以看到它们上面的一切细节：那些带有镀铬钢边的金色交叉剑纹、链条上重型的环扣、以及狼头图案中镶嵌的蓝宝石……哈哈，如果真有什么东西能被称为“狼的装饰品”的话，那非这些莫属了。 他真是太慷慨了。 格蕾丝与这件事毫无关系。或许，只是有些遗憾……以及想要纠正错误的愿望。而既然我也无法将这些带走，那么就让我把我的剑和斗篷作为礼物送给你吧。 说着，这位酋长用双手握住了那把仍插在剑鞘中的刀，然后郑重地将它交给了你。当你接过这把剑柄呈篮子状的怪异剑时，剑鞘上弥漫着寒霜。你注视着酋长，看他脱下了那件覆盖着幽灵般毛皮的斗篷，不禁好奇：究竟是什么让他的这些物品在经历了这么漫长的时间后依然保存得如此完好无损。他将斗篷折叠成一块整齐的方形，然后递到你手中。这斗篷既厚实又保暖，是专为冬天准备的衣物。即便考虑到它的材质，当你将手握在它里面时，仍能感受到一丝暖意。 这就是我所能给你的全部了。 [pc.race]，”领主终于开口了，他耸了耸肩，环顾着空荡荡的观众厅。我想我应该离开了，但是…… 但是？ 他看起来有些尴尬。你能陪我一起去吗？其实我不应该这么麻烦你，但我想看看这些年来我的堡垒发生了什么变化……我担心看到那些景象会让我难以承受。向你提出这样的请求，或许显得我很懦弱，但是—— 哦，不用多说了。你肯定很乐意帮他渡过这个难关吧？毕竟是你把他弄到了这种境地，不是吗？你向酋长点了点头，然后跟在他身后，一起走出了会议厅，沿着楼梯来到了城墙边。 奇怪。无论加隆·冈瓦尔德森走到哪里，他的部下们的灵魂都会逐渐从视线中消失——那些穿着古老锁子甲、身着军服的灵魂，要么瘫软在墙壁旁，要么倒卧在壁龛里，等待着死亡。地板上散落着破碎的陶器，还有被丢弃的武器和掉落的旗帜。……仿佛那位酋长本身就是一支火炬，一座灯塔，让你能够以幽灵般的形态看到马罗克要塞的最后时刻。 起来。他轻声地对那些聚集在一起的狼尾草说道。我们的时间到了。 驻军士兵们用充满困惑的眼神望着他。大人，我实在不明白—— 我们死了。其实我们早就死了。他停顿了一下，仔细斟酌着自己要说的话。我们失败了，但那些幽灵在没有我们的参与下也被消灭了。这个世界继续向前发展，而我们却已经没有存在的意义了。是时候离开这里了。 那些鬼魂先是看着他们的首领，然后互相看了看，最后又将目光转向你。突然间，他们似乎都意识到了什么，肩膀一沉，低下了头。 战败的战士不会将他们的武器带往彼岸。其中一个人低声说道。 加隆点了点头。你们看到我手持宝剑了吗？无论有没有武器，最终……都只有一个结局。我在带领你们的职责上失败了，也在维护团队荣誉的使命上失败了；我会在自己合适的时候为这两件事负责。但现在，我们只能继续前进。 确实，队伍一路向前延伸。跟随在你们身后的这支队伍景象颇为壮观——那一群肮脏、衣衫褴褛却充满坚韧的家伙，一瘸一拐地跟在你们和那位酋长身后。他们虽然狼狈不堪，但内心却感到如释重负，仿佛头顶上那个重型的魔咒终于被打破了。 很可能确实如此。 最终，你们两人来到了那座大门前——如今它们已不再破败不堪，而是变得坚固而闪亮，尽管还略带半透明。来自峡谷下装的新鲜空气扑面而来，酋长闭上了眼睛，双手合十，静静地沉浸在这股自由的气息之中。 我现在想起来了。那些人们花了数小时、数天的时间试图挖掘，却不知道那些幽灵将我们埋在了地下多深的地方。我就坐在我的王座上，等待着终结的到来，决心以尽可能尊严的方式死去……再也不见天日了…… 那一定是非常痛苦的经历。 也许对我来说是这样，对整个团队来说也是。他回头望了一眼跟在后面的驻军，他们发出了一声虽然微弱，但却发自内心的欢呼声。 我永远感激你。他说。而我甚至还没有问过你的名字。 是[pc.name]。 那真是幸会啊， [pc.name]，再见了。冈瓦尔德森领主向您致以诚挚的问候。一天又一天，如此循环往复，直到我们醒来时，才发现那天正是你一切终结的时刻。你必须在你有能力、有时间的时候去做该做的事，因为谁也不知道明天是否还会到来。 这句话听起来很有深度。 这是我父亲在临终前告诉我的，就在他离开人世之前。那位酋长将目光移开你，然后挺直肩膀。好好利用我的天赋吧， [pc.name]但愿有朝一日，我们能再次在雪山之巅相见。 Thyri……很抱歉让你等待了这么久。 他一言不发地走进峡谷，穿过那些大门——而就在那位领主跨过他那注定毁灭的堡垒大门的那一刻，他化作了一千颗闪烁着微光的光点，随后这些光点也渐渐消失了。福特马罗克的狼群追随它们的首领，数百道幽灵从城门中涌出，随后消失得无影无踪；一排排身着统一服饰的犬类陆续离去，最终只剩下一片空旷，而城门也慢慢恢复了它那破败不堪的原状。 哇。 有人轻轻拉了拉你的手臂，提醒你河童的存在。这只毛茸茸的小猫吟游诗人终于决定现身了，它从废墟堆之间的藏身之处走出来，目不转睛地盯着你刚刚完成的驱魔仪式。 “嘿，那场面可真是够震撼的，不是吗？ 确实如此。瑞弗试图保持严肃的样子，但他的耳朵和尾巴不停地抽动，这让这一尝试显得更加滑稽可笑。我的意思是，看到那么多灵魂从那座堡垒中涌出来，这一幕本身就……真是太震撼了。你在里面到底做了什么？ 哦，没什么特别的。只不过是用小镜子耍了点小把戏，再加上些花言巧语而已。 瑞弗用奇怪的眼神看着你，然后摇了摇头，叹了口气。回程的路上你一定要把事情的来龙去脉都告诉我，否则等我开始创作的时候，就只能凭想象来编故事了。你肯定不希望这样吧？ 哈哈，当然不会了。 很好，很好。河流将罐子送入你的双手中，从那堆物品中取出了酋长的奖章，仔细地嗅了嗅，然后用他的小手指轻轻触碰那重型的奖章表面。破旧而陈旧，但确实是真品，这一点毫无疑问。加斯肯定会对此感到非常兴奋的。 你还有一些其他的物品。对于那把剑和那件斗篷，你有什么打算吗？ 别把它扔掉，这是我建议的。他告诉你的。 好吧，那么——你得把它们放在手边。现在，你该不会觉得这里还有什么事情需要你做的吧；或许你该回家去了。 当然！瑞弗边说边快步走了起来。我要你把里面发生的一切都告诉我！现在可不能逃避责任，明白吗？ 返回鹰棘镇的旅途十分顺利，谢天谢地如此；你一天之内已经经历了够多的刺激了。在整个旅途中，瑞弗不断向你询问各种细节，只要你愿意回答，他就会追问下去。起初你并不太愿意交谈，但他递给你的那瓶白兰地确实让你变得稍微愿意多说几句了。 终于，鹰棘镇的栅栏墙出现在眼前。瑞弗向你点了点头，然后便走开了。好吧，就是现在了。我打算去‘霜犬酒馆’那里找点东西，让创意的灵感涌现出来。也许你也会很快赶到吧？毕竟，加斯确实很想要他的那个小玩意儿。
rows.raw: ' — And the jarl lets out a soft groan and slumps back in the throne, his sword clattering to the floor, blade as forlorn as the man. This looks like a good time to give him some space, so you step back and remain silent as Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen stares down at his ghostly hands, his fingers trembling. His breathing is even more pained than ever, and as you look on, he clenches and unclenches his fists into tight balls, thickset, furry fingers shimmering in the dim light. "I... I had thought it might happen. That when death did come... I would know. When I smelled death on the wind, I thought it came from you... but it was from myself, wasn't it?" You remain silent. At length, Galon Gunvaldsen collects himself as best as he can and raises his gaze to yours. "Tell me, [pc.race]. It has been more than two hundred years?" You remember River's tale, and nod. Thereabouts, since the Godswar. For the first time since you've met him, the jarl looks at his surroundings and seems to notice the dilapidated state his fortress is in. For something as simple as a mirror and a few words to have freed a ghost from the false reality he was trapped in... well, stranger things have happened. "If you are here, that means we eventually won, despite my failure..." It took much sacrifice, but the wraiths were beaten back, yes. Galon groans again, and bends over to pick up his sword off the ground before leaning his weight on it once more. "Then... why did you come here, to this place? What did you hope to achieve? Are you adventurers? Treasure hunters?" You... um, you were sent here to retrieve his medallion of office. "Ah. For the pack, no doubt. Gold does not decay with years, after all." The jarl closes his eyes and thinks for a few moments. "It was in front of my face all the time, but I could not see it. It's almost as if a veil had been draped over my eyes... until you forced me to face the truth. Perhaps it is... it is better this way. I would not have been allowed to remain jarl after what happened; the shame would have been too great." Silence. The fact that he might have been the last straw that broke the alliance between the packs and Khor'minos might just be too much for him to bear as he is. "Do the histories tell of my family and their fate?" You hesitate a moment, then decide that the jarl probably isn't going to shoot the messenger here. Still, you can't help but be a little hesitant when you relate River's tale to him. "I... am not surprised. Exile was the least of the fates which could have befallen them; at least, perhaps, my line still exists somewhere, and that is as much as I can ask for in my state. So, you are here for my medallion of office?" Yes. The lupines of today need it. "Then take it. It's not as if I can bring it with me, wherever it is that I'm fated to go when I pass. If it will restore some of our lost honor, then you're free to have it." The words spoken, Jarl Gunvaldsen bows his head and lifts both chain and medallion off his neck, placing them in your hands. Up close, you can see them in so much detail: the golden crossed swords with a burnished steel border, the heavy links of the chain, the sapphires in the wolfshead's eyes... hah, truly a wolf's adornment if there were ever one. He is most gracious. "Grace has nothing to do with it. Regret, perhaps... and a desire to right wrongs. And since I can't take them with me, either, let me make a gift to you of my sword and cloak." With that said, the jarl grasps his blade, still in scabbard, in both hands and solemnly passes it to you. Frost swirls about the scabbard as you take the basket-hilted bastard sword in hand, and you eye the jarl as he pulls off the spectral, fur-lined cloak from about his shoulders, wondering what has kept his possessions so well-preserved after all this time. He folds the cloak up into a neat square and presses it into your hands. It's thick and warm, garb meant for winter, and even given its nature it confers a thin thread of warmth into your fingers as you close your hands in about it. "That's all I have to give to you, [pc.race]," the jarl says at last, rolling his shoulders and looking about the empty audience chamber. "I suppose I should be leaving, but..." But? He looks sheepish. "Could you accompany me on the way out? I shouldn't have to ask you this, but to see what has happened to my fort in the intervening years... I fear it may be a match for my nerves. It must seem craven of me to ask this of you, but -" Oh, say no more. You'd be more than happy to go ahead and help him through this. You put him in this predicament after all, didn't you? You give the jarl a nod, and fall in at his side as he staggers out of the audience chamber and down the stairs into the ramparts. Odd. Wherever Galon Gunvaldsen passes, the spirits of his men start fading into view — lupines in ancient chainmail and livery slumped against walls, sprawled in alcoves, waiting for death. Bits of broken crockery lie on the floor amidst discarded weapons and fallen banners... it's as if the jarl himself was a torch, a beacon that allows you to see the last moments of Fort Marrok in spectral form. "Get up," he says softly to the massed lupines. "Our time is over." The garrison soldiers look up at him with uncomprehending eyes. "Lord, I don't understand -" "We are dead. We have been dead for a long time." He pauses, considering his words. "We failed, but the wraiths were defeated without us. The world has passed by without us. It's time for us to go." The ghosts look at their Jarl, at each other, then at you. As one, realization to dawn upon them, and their shoulders droop as they bow their heads. "Defeated warriors do not take their weapons with them to the beyond," one of them murmurs. Galon nods. "Do you see me with my sword? Weapon or no weapon, at last... an ending. I've failed in both my duty to lead you, and my duty to keep the pack's honor; I'll answer for both in my own time. But for now, onward and outward." Onward and outward indeed. The procession following the both of you is a sight to behold, a steadily growing stream of ghostly lupines limping and dragging themselves after you and the jarl. Dirty, disheveled, and dogged — but relieved in their own way, as if a huge spell that hung over their heads had been broken. It probably had. At last, the two of you reach the gates — now they are no longer dilapidated, but strong and gleaming, if translucent. The scent of fresh air wafts in from the canyon bottom, and the jarl closes his eyes and folds his hands for a moment, taking in the scent of freedom. "I remember now. The men had been trying to dig for hours, days, not knowing how deeply in the earth the wraiths had entombed us. I was on my throne waiting for the end, determined to die in as dignified a fashion as I could. To never see the light again..." It must have been harrowing. "For me, perhaps. And for the whole of the pack." He looks back at the garrison following him, and they manage a weak, if genuine cheer. "I owe you my eternal thanks," he says. "And I haven't even so much as asked your name." It's [pc.name]. "Well met then, [pc.name], and goodbye," Jarl Gunvaldsen salutes you crisply. "Day after day, one after the other, until we wake up and it turns out that's the day it all ends for you. You have to do what you can, when you can, because who knows if tomorrow is even happening?" That sounds deep. "It was what my father told me on his deathbed, before he had to go." The jarl looks away from you and squares his shoulders. "Make good use of my gifts, [pc.name]. May we one day meet again upon the peaks and snow. "Thyri... I'm sorry to have kept you waiting for so long." Without another word, he steps out into the canyon, through the gates — and the moment the jarl passes beyond the gates of his doomed fortress, he dissolves into a thousand spectral motes of glimmering radiance that, in their own time, wink out of existence. The wolves of Fort Marrok follow their lord, hundreds of specters pouring out from the gates and dissipating into nothingness, ranks upon ranks of livery-clad canines passing into the beyond until only emptiness is left, and the gates slowly revert to their old run-down state. "Wow." A soft tugging on your arms alerts you to River's presence. The fluffy kitten bard has finally deigned to make his presence known, stepping out from his hiding place between the rubble piles to gape at the exorcism you've just wrought. Hey, that was something, wasn't it? "Indeed, it was." River's attempt to remain solemn is made all the more comical by his ears and tail's constant twitching. "I mean, the sheer sight of all those spirits coming out of the fortress — just what did you do in there?" Oh, nothing much. Just a few shenanigans involving a hand mirror and a little smooth talking, that's all. River looks at you funny, then shakes his head and sighs. "You've got to tell me all about it on the way back, unless you want me making stuff up when I eventually do my composing. You don't want that, do you?" Haha, of course not. "Good, good." River peers up into your full hands and picks the jarl's medallion off the pile, giving it a long sniff and pressing his little fingers against its heavy surface. "Dusty and old. But it's the real thing, there's no doubt about that. Garth'll have a field day with this." You got some other things, too. Any idea about what you should do with the sword and cloak? "Don't throw it out, that would be my suggestion," he tells you. All right, then — you'll keep them on hand. Now, you don't think there's anything left for you here; perhaps you should get going back home. "Of course!" River replies as he starts off at a brisk walk. "And I want you to tell me everything that happened in there! No shirking now, got it?" The trip back to Hawkethorne is uneventful and thankfully so; you've had enough excitement for one day. River badgers you for the whole trip, getting down as many details as you're willing to give; you're not that inclined to talk at first, but the flask of brandy he offers you does smooth out your social graces somewhat. At length, though, the palisade walls of Hawkethorne draw into view. River gives you a nod, then steps away. "Well, this is it. I'm going to go ahead to the Frost Hound and get something to get those creative juices flowing. Maybe you'll be there shortly? Garth does want his little trinket, after all." '

rows.original: — But it fades, and he rounds on you, snarling. Before you know it, a swipe from the flat of his blade has the mirror out of your hands, and it sails through the air, disappearing into the darkness before landing on the cold stone floor beyond. The tinkling of shattered glass echoes in the audience chamber. "I'll not fall for your vile witchcraft, whelp!" Gunvaldsen roars, and his sword cleaves through the air where you were standing a moment ago. "You mock... You mock me in my dying moments... I'll have none of it!" You try to reason with the enraged ghost for a few more seconds before finally being forced to admit that your attempt at parley has failed. For a moment there, you thought you had it, that Galon's mind was able to see clearly for a fraction of a second, but the fugue of undeath was simply too strong. If your words had been stronger, more forceful... The time for talk is over. Galon Gunvaldsen is bearing down on you, face and eyes alight with the burning flames of undeath. It's a fight!
rows.translation: — 但是镜面很快就会失去光泽，然后他就会转过身来，对着你咆哮着冲过来。在你还没反应过来的时候，他就会用刀刃的平面猛地一划，将镜子从你手中夺走，镜子会在空中飞出去，然后消失在黑暗中，最终落在那冰冷的石地上。 玻璃碎裂发出的清脆声响在观众厅中回荡着。 我才不会上你这种卑鄙把戏的当呢，小混蛋！冈瓦尔德森发出怒吼，他的剑划破了空气，正好是你刚才站立的地方。你在嘲笑我……你在我临终的时刻还在嘲笑我……我绝对不会容忍这种行为！ 你又尝试与那愤怒的幽灵进行了几秒钟的劝说，最终不得不承认，你的谈判尝试彻底失败了。有那么一瞬间，你以为自己成功了——以为加隆的那颗被死亡侵蚀的心灵终于在那一刹那恢复了清醒，但那股来自死界的力量实在太过强大。如果你的言辞能够更加有力、更加坚定一些…… 交谈的时间已经结束了。加隆·冈瓦尔德森正在朝你冲来，他的面容和双眼中燃烧着死亡之火。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: However, it's no use. Trapped in the veil of false reality as he is, the jarl's spirit is simply unable to hear reason; all your arguments fall on deaf ears. Angered by your prattling — or at least, what he perceives to be such — he picks up his greatsword and lurches out of the stone throne, intent on cutting you down. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 然而，这一切都是徒劳的。由于被虚假现实的迷雾所笼罩，这位酋长的灵魂根本听不进任何道理；你所有的辩解都对他来说毫无意义。被你的喋喋不休惹怒了——至少他是这么认为的——他拔出巨剑，从石制王座上冲了出来，决心将你斩杀。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: [pc.ra lupine |For a moment, the jarl looks like he's about to spring up and throttle you, but then he relaxes and sinks back into his throne. "I... I was not expecting petitioners today. Not when the wraiths are over the next hill." Petitioners? Oh. Oh. Your initial confusion fades quickly as you realize that because of your appearance, the jarl thinks you're one of his subjects. It doesn't really make complete sense — the way he's dressed does look like something you might expect from a two hundred years ago, as opposed to your current fashion sense — but then again, you suspect he isn't quite all there. One way or another, this is a lucky break. If Galon's spirit isn't immediately inclined to kill you like you were expecting, a number of additional options open up. Hmm... "If you have business, spit it out," the jarl commands, his ears folding back. "Otherwise, stop wasting my time. We don't have much of it left, and I don't suffer fools easily." As you close the distance, the jarl's eyes widen in horror as you whip out your [pc.weapon] and bring it to bear on him. Though he looks every bit worn and haggard, the winter wolf is quick on his feet and springs out of the throne, easily evading your blow and drawing his blade in one fluid movement. "Treachery! Murder!" he roars. The blue flames in his empty eye sockets blaze and writhe with the spirit's rage as Galon Gunvaldsen bares his fangs at you. "What did the wraiths promise you, to turn you against your own pack jarl?" Words from a ghost who's already dead. The jarl says nothing in reply, but rounds in on you with his greatsword, its serrated edge glinting in the dim light with his eyes. It's a fight! |As you close the distance to him, the specter of Galon Gunvaldsen twists his head to regard you for the first time, and his empty, flaming eyes flash in the dim light. "I smell death on the wind." It clearly takes him a good deal of effort, but he uncurls in a flash and springs to his feet. "Wraiths!" the tortured spectre roars, the scabbard falling to the floor as he draws his sword and brandishes it in the air. "Wraiths, in my keep! First that farce down by the coast, and now this — I'll slay you all if it's the last thing I do, and reclaim my honor!" Your protestations fall on deaf ears as you narrowly duck under a mighty cleave of his blade that sings through the air. The jarl's clearly caught in the last moments of his life as he suffocated in the darkness, and there's only one way to free his soul. It's a fight! ]
rows.translation: [pc.ra lupine |有那么一刻，那位酋长看起来像是要猛地站起来掐住你的脖子，但随后他又放松下来，重新坐回了王座上。 我……我本来没料到今天会有人来请愿。尤其是在那些幽灵还潜伏在附近的时候。 请愿者？哦。哦。当你意识到由于自己的外貌，那位领主以为你是他的子民之一时，最初的困惑很快就消散了。不过，这种想法其实并不完全合理——看看他的穿着，就知道了。确实这看起来确实像是两百年前才会出现的风格，与你们现在的审美观念完全不符——不过话说回来，你也不确定他是否真的神志清醒。 不管怎样，这确实是个幸运的机会。如果加隆的灵魂并没有像你预想的那样立刻想要杀死你，那么就会出现很多其他的选择。嗯…… 如果有事要说，就直说吧。酋长下达了命令，他的耳朵向后耷拉了下来。否则，就别再浪费我的时间了。我们的时间已经不多了，而我可不会轻易容忍蠢货。 当你逐渐靠近时，酋长看到你突然拔出武器，吓得眼睛都瞪圆了。 [pc.weapon]然后将这一攻击施加到他身上。尽管他看起来疲惫不堪、面容憔悴，但这头冬狼行动敏捷，从王座上猛地跃起，轻松避开了你的攻击，同时以流畅的动作拔出了他的剑。 背叛！谋杀！他咆哮着。当加隆·冈瓦尔德森露出獠牙向你袭来时，他空洞的眼眶中燃烧的蓝色火焰仿佛在随着怨灵的愤怒而扭曲、跳动。那些幽灵向你许下了什么承诺，让你背叛自己族群的首领？ 一个早已死去的鬼魂所说的话。 酋长没有回答什么，而是挥舞着他的巨剑朝你冲了过来，在昏暗的光线下，剑刃上的锯齿闪烁着光芒，他的眼睛也紧盯着你。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ |当你逐渐靠近他的时候，加隆·冈瓦尔德森的幽灵终于第一次转过头来注视你，他那空洞而燃烧着火焰的眼睛在昏暗的光线中闪烁着。我感觉到风中带着死亡的气息。 显然，这需要他付出相当大的努力，但他还是迅速恢复了动作，站了起来。 幽灵！那个受折磨的幽灵发出了咆哮，他拔出剑，将剑柄甩到地上，然后在空中挥舞着剑。幽灵们，快离开我的领地！先是海岸边的那场闹剧，现在又是这种事——如果这是我的最后手段，我一定会把你们全部消灭，重新夺回我的荣誉！ 你的抗议毫无作用，因为你刚刚才勉强躲过了他那划破空气的猛烈一击。这位酋长显然已经走到了生命的最后时刻，在黑暗中窒息而亡……而只有唯一一种方法，才能让他的灵魂得到解脱。 这是一场激烈的战斗！ ]

rows.original:
You're facing Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen!

    Some might call him old, others might say he's in the prime of his life. But there's no doubting the combat experience this gray-white lupine has that's earned him the moniker "The Winter Wolf." Wearing a drab surcoat over a chainmail shirt and skirts, an insignia of two crossed swords emblazoned on the former, the jarl moves with grace and purpose as his enchanted greatsword sings through the air, icy mist in its wake. Broad-shouldered and thickset, he definitely has the muscle to put power behind his strikes, and where his eyes once were, the flames of undeath burn.
    
    It's time to put this ghost to rest.
rows.translation:
你现在面对的是领主加隆·冈瓦尔森！

    有人也许会说他已经老了，也有人会说他正值壮年。但毫无疑问，这位灰白色的狼族拥有的战斗经验，为他赢得了“冬狼”的称号。他穿着一件土褐色的罩袍，里面是锁子甲上衣与甲裙，罩袍上绣着两把交叉长剑的纹章；这位领主举手投足既优雅又果决，他那把附魔巨剑在空中呼啸而过，剑锋后拖着一道冰冷雾气。他肩宽体壮，肌肉结实，每一击都绝对力量十足；而在他曾经双眼的位置，燃烧着亡者之火。
    
    是时候让这个幽灵安息了。

"You're facing Jarl Galon Gunvaldsen!

    Some might call him old, others might say he's in the prime of his life. But there's no doubting the combat experience this gray-white lupine has that's earned him the moniker "The Winter Wolf."     It's time to put this ghost to rest."

rows.original: The final blow lands, knocking the mighty lupine jarl off-balance and sending him to his knees as he tries to regain his footing. Sword point-down, its tip buried in the ancient mortar between the flagstones, he leans his weight on the crossguard and slowly levers himself upright again. It's clear that he's spent almost all of his strength fighting you and has no chance of snatching victory from the jaws of defeat, yet is determined to fight you to the bitter end. He sure is one tenacious ghost. You're not about to leave anything to chance — while Gunvaldsen is busy with righting himself, you dash forward and kick his blade out from under him. The mighty bastard sword flies from his hands with a loud clatter, skidding across the cold stone ground, and you watch as Galon collapses face down on the floor, panting and heaving, each breath pained and drawn out. "Thyri... Thyri... the wraiths... rouse our children..." Gunvaldsen's ghostly claws scrabble on the stones, gurgling noises rising from his throat, each breath coming harder than the last. He seems to have forgotten you completely now, fixated on something that you can't see, and raises his chin just high enough off the ground to peer with sightless eyes at the empty space beyond your feet. Grimly, you realize that you're viewing the last few moments of the jarl's life, the despairing exertions of a man facing an ignoble straw death. At last, though, it's over. Galon lets out a soft, whining sigh, twitches, and is still. Before your eyes, the translucent essence of the specter begins to dissolve away, motes of pale white light rising into the air as it gradually fades into nothingness. For a moment, the jarl's sword and medallion remain suspended in the air, hanging on nothing, then they clatter onto the flagstones with a ringing sound that echoes throughout the entire audience hall. Ringringringringring... Like a great collective sigh, the ringing radiates outwards from the buried tower, and the ghostly exhalation reverberates through stone and air alike. Ringringringringring... A sense of emptiness, and then a sense of lingering peace. Was Galon's determination, his force of will, his memories the only things that kept his men lingering in the mortal realm with him? You look back at the entrance that you came into the hall by, but there are no ghostly guards sprinting up the stairs or phasing through the walls to accost you for the murder of their lord. [party.has cait| "He's gone," Cait says, leaning on her staff and heaving a sigh of relief. The catgirl looks more than a little shaken by the violent exorcism that you've just performed, clutching her [cait.weapon] until her knuckles are white. "I felt him pass." She did, too? Cait says nothing, but bows her head and begins murmuring a small prayer for the recently departed. ] With that done, you kneel and pick the jarl's medallion of office off the floor. It's formed in the shape of a circle of solid gold with a tarnished steel boundary, crossed swords on one side and a wolfshead with gleaming sapphire eyes on the other, and is adequately weighty and cold in your hand as you examine it in the dim light. Guess the stories are right: you can't take it with you. Next things next: the jarl's bastard sword. It's heavier than it looks, and a little unwieldy in your hands, but feels like it could make a good weapon with a little practice. [party.has arona| Peering at the weapon, Arona makes a little thoughtful noise in the back of her throat. "Little too fancy for my tastes. Pretty good blade, though. Some might say a magic weapon's cheating, but I say I'll be taking every edge I can get when my life's on the line." ] And that seems to settle that. With Gunvaldsen's ghost gone, even the eerie glow in the air is slowly fading away, dimming ever so slightly by the moment. Retracing your steps isn't hard when there aren't any restless dead coming out of the walls at you, and before too long you're down the stairs and out through the gates. The scent of fresh air hits you as you step out into the canyon, and River peers out at you from his perch atop the rubble pile as he sees you emerge from the gates. "Thought you were never going to come out," he says. "Frankly, I was half-considering heading in myself and seeing if something had happened to you." Well, that won't be necessary. He nods. "Did you get it?" You hold out the medallion, and River steps forward to take it out of your hands. The little cat bard inspects it a moment, then raises it to his nose and gives it a sniff. He closes his eyes, murmurs to himself, then sighs contentedly and hands it back to you. "Yep, it smells like Gunvaldsen all right. This is the real deal." Just how does River know what the jarl smells like? "So... you want to tell me what happened back in there? Looking at how worn out you are, chances are it'd make a good story." Oh, it would indeed, it would. But it's a long one — you'll spill the beans on the way back. "Well, I've been getting pretty hungry sitting around here waiting for you to show your face; let's get back to Hawkethorne before I expire from starvation. Oh, and don't you forget to tell me the story now, and the whole story at that. You wouldn't want me to start making stuff up to fill in the blanks, would you?" Knowing him? Maaaybe... "Ha!" The walk back to Hawkethorne is uneventful; the harpies must be having an off day today. By and large, the village's palisade walls loom into view, and River gives you a small nod. "Guess this is where I get off. It's been a nice field trip with you lot — don't forget to see Garth and hand him the medallion, okay?" With that, River scampers off towards the gates, leaving you in the blink of an eye. [party.has garret| "Hmm." You turn, and realize that it's the first time that Garret has said anything since you struck down the jarl. For someone who's usually gregarious and jovial as all-out... yeah. Is he okay? Garret waves off your concern. "I'm fine, I'm fine. Still stings a bit, but I've lost more blood than that and lived. No, I'm just... thinking." A hawk for his thoughts? "I... I just..." His eyes cross for a moment as the gears turn in his head. "Originally, I wanted to come along for answers. I don't know what my mom did that got her thrown onto the Long Walk... and it's bad enough that my own old man won't say anything about the matter. But today... I left that Fort Marrok place with more questions than I came in with. "I don't know, [pc.name]. Maybe I should've tried talking to the jarl instead, but I didn't. Maybe I was scared of him; maybe I was scared of the answers he might give me. I... it's no good regretting it, I'll never know, and it's my own fault. I'll just have to live with that. "Well, either way I've got to head back, think up an excuse for coming home this early that my old man will buy. Fat chance of that. See you around, [pc.name]. Stay in one piece, okay?" With that, he's gone, hurrying after River through the village gates. ]
rows.translation: 最后一击命中，将那位强大的狼族伯爵击得失去平衡，使他跪倒在地，试图重新站稳。剑尖朝下，埋在石板间的古老灰浆中，他依靠剑柄慢慢站了起来。很明显，他已经耗尽了几乎所有的力量与你战斗，已经没有可能从失败的边缘夺回胜利，但他依然决心要将这场战斗进行到最后一刻。 他真是个不屈不挠的家伙。 你绝对不会让任何机会从手中溜走——当冈瓦尔德森还在努力恢复平衡时，你猛地冲上前去，将他的剑从他脚下踢飞。那把沉重的巨剑发出刺耳的声响，从他手中飞了出去，在冰冷的石地上滑行着。你看着加隆面朝下倒在地上，喘着粗气，每一次呼吸都充满了痛苦。 蒂莉……蒂莉……那些幽灵……正在迷惑我们的孩子……冈瓦尔德森那幽灵般的爪子在石头上抓挠着，他的喉咙里发出咕噜声，每一次呼吸都显得更加艰难。他似乎已经完全忘记了你，只专注于某个你看不见的东西，他将下巴微微抬高，用那双看不见的眼睛凝视着你脚下的空旷空间。你残酷地意识到，你正在目睹这位酋长生命中的最后时刻——一个面临卑鄙死亡的人在绝望中做出的最后挣扎。 终于，一切都结束了。加隆发出一声轻柔的叹息，身体微微颤抖了几下，然后静止了下来。在你眼前，那个幽灵的半透明身躯开始逐渐消散，淡白色的光点缓缓升向空中，最终彻底消失无踪。有那么一瞬间，酋长的剑和奖章还悬在半空中，仿佛没有任何东西支撑着它们，随后它们叮当作响地落在石板上，那声响彻了整个宴会厅。 叮叮叮叮叮…… 就像一声巨大的集体叹息，这种铃声从那座埋藏在地下的塔中向外辐射开来，这种幽灵般的回响在石头与空气中久久回荡。 一种空虚感，随后又是一种萦绕心头的宁静。难道只有加隆的决心、他的意志力，以及他的回忆，才能让他的部下们继续留在这个凡人世界中与他同行吗？你回头望向进入大厅的那道门，却看不到有任何幽灵般的守卫从楼梯上冲下来，也没有任何身影从墙壁中穿出来，因为你的行为而责备你杀害了他们的主人。 [party.has cait| 他走了。凯特靠在她的法杖上，长舒了一口气。那个猫女因为在你们刚才进行的激烈驱魔仪式中受到了不小的惊吓，她紧紧地抓着自己的法杖。 [cait.weapon]直到她的指关节都变白了。我感觉他过去了。 她也是这么做的吗？ 凯特什么也没说，只是低下了头，开始为那位刚刚离世的人默默祈祷。 ] 做完这些后，你跪下来从地上捡起了酋长的官印。这枚官印是由纯金制成的圆形物件，边缘镶着锈迹斑斑的钢边；其中一面刻着交叉的剑形图案，另一面则是一个有着闪烁蓝宝石般眼睛的狼头。在昏暗的光线下仔细端详时，你会感觉到它既沉重又冰冷。 看来这些说法都是对的：这种武器是带不走的。接下来是下一件物品——酋长的私生子之剑。它看起来比实际要重一些，拿在手里也有些笨重，但只要稍加练习，应该也能成为一把不错的武器。 [party.has arona| 阿罗娜仔细端详着那把武器，喉咙里发出了一声若有所思的低声。对我来说，这个武器有点太花哨了，不符合我的口味。不过，这把剑的质量确实不错。有些人可能会说魔法武器有点不公平，但我认为，当性命攸关的时候，任何能增加战斗优势的东西都是值得拥有的。 ] 这样似乎就把问题解决了。随着冈瓦尔德森的鬼魂消失，空气中那种诡异的光芒也在慢慢消退，每一刻都在变得暗淡一些。当没有那些从墙壁里冒出来的不安宁的死灵时，重新走回原路其实并不困难，不久之后，你就走下了楼梯，穿过了大门。当你走到峡谷外面时，清新的空气扑面而来，而河则从废墟堆顶上的位置看到了你从大门里走出来。 还以为你永远都不会现身呢。他说。说实话，我当时还在考虑是否应该亲自去看看你是不是出了什么事。 嗯，那没有必要。 他点了点头。你拿到它了吗？ 你递出那枚奖章，瑞弗走上前从你手中接过了它。那只小猫吟游诗人仔细地端详了一会儿，然后把它举到鼻子前闻了闻。他闭上眼睛，自言自语了几句，最后满意地叹了口气，又把奖章还给了你。没错，这确实有Gunvaldsen的味道。这才是真正的货。 究竟是如何确实河流知道这位酋长身上有什么气味吗？ 那么……你想告诉我里面发生了什么吗？看你现在的样子，这个故事应该会相当精彩吧。 哦，确实会这样，肯定会。不过这个过程有点长——你在回来的路上就会把秘密泄露掉啦。 嗯，坐在这里等你出现，我真是饿坏了；趁我还没饿死，我们赶紧回鹰棘镇吧。哦，对了，你可别忘了把整个故事都讲给我听。你总不希望我开始自己编故事来填补这些空白吧？ 认识他？也许吧…… 哈！ 返回鹰棘镇的途中一切顺利，那些鹰身女妖今天似乎没什么动静。渐渐地，村庄的栅栏墙映入眼帘，瑞弗还朝你微微点了点头。 看来我在这里就要下车了。和你们一起这次旅行真是太愉快了——别忘了去见加斯，把那枚奖章交给他，好吗？说着，瑞弗便飞快地跑向大门，转眼间就消失不见了。 [party.has garret| 嗯。 你转过身，才发现自从你击倒了那个酋长之后，加雷特竟然第一次开口说话。对于一个通常总是那么健谈、开朗的人来说……嗯，他没事吧？ 加雷特摆了摆手，表示你不必担心。我没事，真的没事。虽然还是有点刺痛，但我曾经流过更多的血，却依然活了下来。不，我只是在……思考而已。 言出必行吗？ 我……我只是……他的眼睛微微眯了起来，脑海中正在快速思考着各种可能性。起初，我是想弄清楚一些答案才来的。我不知道我妈妈做了什么才会被关进长路监狱……更糟糕的是，我的父亲对此事也只字不提。但今天……离开马罗克要塞后，我心中的疑问反而比来时更多了。 我不知道[pc.name]也许我应该试着去和那位领主谈谈，但我没有那么做。也许我是害怕他；也许我是害怕他会给出的答案。我……现在后悔也没用了，我永远也不会知道真相了，而且这确实是我的错。我只能接受这个事实，继续生活下去。 嗯，不管怎样，我都得回去了。得想个让我爸信服的借口，解释为什么这么早就回家……不过这可能性几乎为零吧。回头见吧。 [pc.name]一定要保持完整，好吗？ 说完，他就匆匆离开了，穿过村庄的大门，追着瑞弗而去。 ]
rows.raw: " The final blow lands, knocking the mighty lupine jarl off-balance and sending him to his knees as he tries to regain his footing. Sword point-down, its tip buried in the ancient mortar between the flagstones, he leans his weight on the crossguard and slowly levers himself upright again. It's clear that he's spent almost all of his strength fighting you and has no chance of snatching victory from the jaws of defeat, yet is determined to fight you to the bitter end. He sure is one tenacious ghost. You're not about to leave anything to chance — while Gunvaldsen is busy with righting himself, you dash forward and kick his blade out from under him. The mighty bastard sword flies from his hands with a loud clatter, skidding across the cold stone ground, and you watch as Galon collapses face down on the floor, panting and heaving, each breath pained and drawn out. "Thyri... Thyri... the wraiths... rouse our children..." Gunvaldsen's ghostly claws scrabble on the stones, gurgling noises rising from his throat, each breath coming harder than the last. He seems to have forgotten you completely now, fixated on something that you can't see, and raises his chin just high enough off the ground to peer with sightless eyes at the empty space beyond your feet. Grimly, you realize that you're viewing the last few moments of the jarl's life, the despairing exertions of a man facing an ignoble straw death. At last, though, it's over. Galon lets out a soft, whining sigh, twitches, and is still. Before your eyes, the translucent essence of the specter begins to dissolve away, motes of pale white light rising into the air as it gradually fades into nothingness. For a moment, the jarl's sword and medallion remain suspended in the air, hanging on nothing, then they clatter onto the flagstones with a ringing sound that echoes throughout the entire audience hall. Ringringringringring... Like a great collective sigh, the ringing radiates outwards from the buried tower, and the ghostly exhalation reverberates through stone and air alike. Ringringringringring... A sense of emptiness, and then a sense of lingering peace. Was Galon's determination, his force of will, his memories the only things that kept his men lingering in the mortal realm with him? You look back at the entrance that you came into the hall by, but there are no ghostly guards sprinting up the stairs or phasing through the walls to accost you for the murder of their lord. [party.has cait| "He's gone," Cait says, leaning on her staff and heaving a sigh of relief. The catgirl looks more than a little shaken by the violent exorcism that you've just performed, clutching her [cait.weapon] until her knuckles are white. "I felt him pass." She did, too? Cait says nothing, but bows her head and begins murmuring a small prayer for the recently departed. ] With that done, you kneel and pick the jarl's medallion of office off the floor. It's formed in the shape of a circle of solid gold with a tarnished steel boundary, crossed swords on one side and a wolfshead with gleaming sapphire eyes on the other, and is adequately weighty and cold in your hand as you examine it in the dim light. Guess the stories are right: you can't take it with you. Next things next: the jarl's bastard sword. It's heavier than it looks, and a little unwieldy in your hands, but feels like it could make a good weapon with a little practice. [party.has arona| Peering at the weapon, Arona makes a little thoughtful noise in the back of her throat. "Little too fancy for my tastes. Pretty good blade, though. Some might say a magic weapon's cheating, but I say I'll be taking every edge I can get when my life's on the line." ] And that seems to settle that. With Gunvaldsen's ghost gone, even the eerie glow in the air is slowly fading away, dimming ever so slightly by the moment. Retracing your steps isn't hard when there aren't any restless dead coming out of the walls at you, and before too long you're down the stairs and out through the gates. The scent of fresh air hits you as you step out into the canyon, and River peers out at you from his perch atop the rubble pile as he sees you emerge from the gates. "Thought you were never going to come out," he says. "Frankly, I was half-considering heading in myself and seeing if something had happened to you." Well, that won't be necessary. He nods. "Did you get it?" You hold out the medallion, and River steps forward to take it out of your hands. The little cat bard inspects it a moment, then raises it to his nose and gives it a sniff. He closes his eyes, murmurs to himself, then sighs contentedly and hands it back to you. "Yep, it smells like Gunvaldsen all right. This is the real deal." Just how does River know what the jarl smells like? "So... you want to tell me what happened back in there? Looking at how worn out you are, chances are it'd make a good story." Oh, it would indeed, it would. But it's a long one — you'll spill the beans on the way back. "Well, I've been getting pretty hungry sitting around here waiting for you to show your face; let's get back to Hawkethorne before I expire from starvation. Oh, and don't you forget to tell me the story now, and the whole story at that. You wouldn't want me to start making stuff up to fill in the blanks, would you?" Knowing him? Maaaybe... "Ha!" The walk back to Hawkethorne is uneventful; the harpies must be having an off day today. By and large, the village's palisade walls loom into view, and River gives you a small nod. "Guess this is where I get off. It's been a nice field trip with you lot — don't forget to see Garth and hand him the medallion, okay?" With that, River scampers off towards the gates, leaving you in the blink of an eye. [party.has garret| "Hmm." You turn, and realize that it's the first time that Garret has said anything since you struck down the jarl. For someone who's usually gregarious and jovial as all-out... yeah. Is he okay? Garret waves off your concern. "I'm fine, I'm fine. Still stings a bit, but I've lost more blood than that and lived. No, I'm just... thinking." A hawk for his thoughts? "I... I just..." His eyes cross for a moment as the gears turn in his head. "Originally, I wanted to come along for answers. I don't know what my mom did that got her thrown onto the Long Walk... and it's bad enough that my own old man won't say anything about the matter. But today... I left that Fort Marrok place with more questions than I came in with. "I don't know, [pc.name]. Maybe I should've tried talking to the jarl instead, but I didn't. Maybe I was scared of him; maybe I was scared of the answers he might give me. I... it's no good regretting it, I'll never know, and it's my own fault. I'll just have to live with that. "Well, either way I've got to head back, think up an excuse for coming home this early that my old man will buy. Fat chance of that. See you around, [pc.name]. Stay in one piece, okay?" With that, he's gone, hurrying after River through the village gates. ] "

rows.original: Closing in, the ghostly Jarl brandishes his blade and swings. You're too slow to react, and the great strike sends your [pc.weapon] clattering on the ground and out of reach. A small-minded man will want to gloat and make his victim squirm. A good man will kill you without another word. The Jarl's greatsword pierces your breast, and its blade of icy steel chills the life from your body. Your life and your adventure end here.
rows.translation: 幽灵般的酋长逼近而来，挥舞着他的刀刃猛力劈下。你反应太慢，这一记重击把你的[pc.weapon]打得叮当作响地落在地上，再也够不着了。 心胸狭隘的人会想要幸灾乐祸，让受害者痛苦挣扎；而善良的人则会二话不说地结束你的生命。酋长的巨剑刺入你的胸膛，那把由冰冷钢铁铸成的剑刃将生命从你体内抽走。 你的生命，以及你的冒险，就此结束。

A small-minded man will want to gloat and make his victim squirm. A good man will kill you without another word. The Jarl's greatsword pierces your breast, and its blade of icy steel chills the life from your body. Your life and your adventure end here."

rows.original: "You got it?" Sure do. You take the medallion out of your pack and plonk it down on the bartop, chain and all; the sight raises a few appreciative whistles from some of the other patrons. This is it, yes? Upon seeing the medallion, Garth swallows hard and sets down the glass in his hand. Picking up the medallion by its chain, he fingers it for a bit, then passes it from palm to palm as if testing its weight. You could be wrong, but you're pretty sure he's having a moment here and — are those tears in his big blue eyes? "Sorry," Garth says as he realizes you're staring at him, then wipes his eyes with the back of a hand. "I got something in my eye." Sure he did. Is he satisfied it's the real thing? "It is." Well, hope it was worth the trouble you went to in order to pry it off the ghostly jarl's neck. "It is. Trust me, it is. You have no idea how much this means to me." Garth pours out a large mug of honey mead before [party.som|setting it out in front of you|pouring another for [companion1.name]|pouring two more for [companion1.name] and [companion2.name]]. "Come, a drink on the house. It's the least I can do for you." If he wants to do more, he can start by explaining what this has to do with his wife, and why he won't tell Gwyn and Garret about their mother. A long, rueful sigh. "Fine, I owe you as much. Take a seat and get comfortable. "This symbol on the medallion, that's the banner my wife was flying the first day I joined up with her company. How do you think she got to be leader of one?" By fighting, clawing, and beating her way to the top, you presume. "Oh, that's not to say she didn't do plenty of that. But she also claimed to be descended from some supposedly dead lineage of the packs or somesuch. Back in the day, I could never tell when she was being serious, and when she wasn't — like Garret, my wife loved to make ludicrous boasts. She said she flew the insignia of that dead house on her banners, and all I thought of it at the time was that it was simply good advertising. But then as the years went by, I began to wonder-" And after she left, he began to search. Garth nods, a barely perceptible dip of his head. "I'd try to pry tales of the Gunvaldsen line from people who passed through the Frost Hound. So many false leads and pointless rumours — it's one of the reasons I keep River around, to sort through these for me. Then one day he comes up and tells me that Fort Marrok didn't just exist, but he'd gotten his hands on the key as well." All right, that explains that. You take a deep swig of mead and motion for Garth to continue. Why won't he tell Gwyn and Garret the truth about their mother? "Gwyn... she already hates her mother and doesn't want anything to do with her. I don't want to bring it up lest I break her heart again. And Garret..." Garth closes his eyes. "The choice my wife made wasn't an easy one. If I told him outright, it would poison him against her forever. I don't want that. But if he works to find the truth by himself, when he gets to that point, if he ever does, when he catches up with her... I'm hoping he'll be wise enough to understand why she had to do what she did, even if he doesn't agree with it." That sounds like a cop-out. "It does, but it's the truth. And no, I'm not going to tell you, because you'll just march straight up and spill it to Garret. Them's the breaks. Did you find anything good while in there to make the trip worth your time?" Could have. Doesn't have to be. "Playing coy, eh? Well, I owe you as much." He'd better, since you risked your neck to bring him a memento of his wife. "Look, I'm not saying that I'm not grateful. Let me pour you another drink, eh?" You spend the remainder of the day — and night — entertaining yourself at Garth's expense, recounting the tale of your adventure in the haunted fortress with Garth and anyone who'll listen. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_GARRET_RECRUITED |Of course, you leave out the bits about Garret coming along with you. Wouldn't do if Garth heard about it.] River's even composed a little tune about your exploits by now, and has the entire common room cheering and clapping at his music. It's well past midnight by the time you crawl into bed, stuffed and drunk, and are asleep before your head hits the pillow.
rows.translation: 明白了吗？ 当然可以。你从背包里取出那枚奖章，连链条一起放在吧台上；这一幕引得其他一些顾客发出赞赏的口哨声。就是这个吧？ 看到那枚奖章后，加斯猛地咽了口唾沫，然后将手中的杯子放下。他拿起奖章，用手指轻轻抚摸着它的链条，然后把奖章在双手之间来回传递，仿佛在测试它的重量。你可能弄错了，但你有种预感——他此刻肯定正在想着什么……那些声音，是不是泪水在他那双湛蓝的眼睛里？ 对不起。加斯注意到你在盯着他看，便用手背擦了擦眼睛，然后说道。我的眼睛里进东西了。 他确实这么做了。他确定这是真品吗？ 是的。 希望你费那么大劲把它从那个幽灵般的伯爵的脖子上取下来是值得的。 确实是这样。相信我，真的很重要。你根本无法想象这对我来说意味着什么。加斯先倒了一大杯蜂蜜酒出来。 [party.som|把它们摆在你的面前|再倒一杯给[companion1.name]|再倒两杯给[companion1.name]以及[companion2.name]]。 来，我请客喝一杯。这是我最起码能为你做的。 如果他想采取进一步的行动，那么他可以先解释这件事与他的妻子有什么关系，以及为什么他不愿意告诉格温和加雷特关于他们母亲的真相。 一声长长的、充满懊悔的叹息。好吧，我确实欠你这个人情。请坐，放松一下吧。 奖章上的这个标志，就是我加入我妻子的部队第一天，她所使用的旗帜。你猜她是怎么成为那个部队的领导的？ 你认为，她是通过战斗、拼搏和不懈努力才登上顶峰的。 哦，这并不是说她没有做过很多这样的事。但她还声称自己出身于那些据说已经灭绝的氏族之类的。过去，我从来分不清她什么时候是在说真话，什么时候是在开玩笑——就像我的妻子加雷特一样，她就喜欢说一些荒谬的自夸话。她说自己的旗帜上会印着那些已经灭绝的家族的徽章，而当时我只想，这不过是一种很好的宣传手段罢了。但随着时间的推移，我开始怀疑起来…… 在她离开后，他开始寻找起来。 加斯微微点了点头，那点头几乎看不出来。我曾经试图从那些路过‘寒霜猎犬’的人那里打探关于冈瓦尔德森家族的线索。但得到的都是虚假的信息和毫无意义的谣言——这也是我之所以让瑞弗留在我身边的原因之一，让他帮我梳理这些信息。直到有一天，他突然告诉我，‘马罗克要塞’确实存在，而且他还得到了那把关键的钥匙。 好吧，这就解释得通了。你深深地喝了一口蜂蜜酒，然后示意加斯继续说下去。为什么他不愿意告诉格温和加雷特关于他们母亲的真相呢？ 格温……她已经恨自己的母亲了，根本不想和她有任何瓜葛。我不想再提起这件事，以免再次伤害她的心。至于加雷特……加斯闭上了眼睛。我妻子所做的这个选择并不容易。如果我直接把真相告诉他，那会让他永远对她心生怨恨。我并不希望这样。但是，如果他能自己努力去寻找真相，当他真正了解到事情的真相时，如果他真的能理解她为什么会做出那样的选择……我希望他能有足够的智慧去理解她的决定，即使他并不认同她的选择。 那听起来像是在逃避责任。 确实是这样的，但这就是事实。而且，不，我不会改变这个事实。你因为你直接去告诉加雷特的话，一切就都暴露了。这就是其中的风险所在。你在那里有没有找到什么有价值的东西，让这次旅行没有白费时间呢？ 本可以。但不一定非得如此。 装傻卖萌呢，是吧？其实，我也欠你一个人情。 他最好这么做，毕竟是你冒着风险为他带来了他妻子留下的纪念品。 听着，我并不是说不感激你。让我再给你倒一杯吧，怎么样？ 你花了剩下的时间和夜晚，在加斯的资助下自娱自乐，向加斯以及任何愿意听的人讲述你在那座鬼屋中的冒险经历。 [flags.GARTH_QUEST_GARRET_RECRUITED |当然，你把加雷特跟你一起去的那些事给省略掉了。要是加斯知道了，那可就糟了。]此时，瑞弗甚至为你的事迹谱写了一小段曲子，整个公共休息室的人都为他的音乐欢呼鼓掌。而当你喝得酩酊大醉、吃得撑得不行，终于爬上床去时，早已过了午夜，你还没等枕头碰到头就睡着了。
rows.raw: " "You got it?" Sure do. You take the medallion out of your pack and plonk it down on the bartop, chain and all; the sight raises a few appreciative whistles from some of the other patrons. This is it, yes? Upon seeing the medallion, Garth swallows hard and sets down the glass in his hand. Picking up the medallion by its chain, he fingers it for a bit, then passes it from palm to palm as if testing its weight. You could be wrong, but you're pretty sure he's having a moment here and — are those tears in his big blue eyes? "Sorry," Garth says as he realizes you're staring at him, then wipes his eyes with the back of a hand. "I got something in my eye." Sure he did. Is he satisfied it's the real thing? "It is." Well, hope it was worth the trouble you went to in order to pry it off the ghostly jarl's neck. "It is. Trust me, it is. You have no idea how much this means to me." Garth pours out a large mug of honey mead before [party.som|setting it out in front of you|pouring another for [companion1.name]|pouring two more for [companion1.name] and [companion2.name]]. "Come, a drink on the house. It's the least I can do for you." If he wants to do more, he can start by explaining what this has to do with his wife, and why he won't tell Gwyn and Garret about their mother. A long, rueful sigh. "Fine, I owe you as much. Take a seat and get comfortable. "This symbol on the medallion, that's the banner my wife was flying the first day I joined up with her company. How do you think she got to be leader of one?" By fighting, clawing, and beating her way to the top, you presume. "Oh, that's not to say she didn't do plenty of that. But she also claimed to be descended from some supposedly dead lineage of the packs or somesuch. Back in the day, I could never tell when she was being serious, and when she wasn't — like Garret, my wife loved to make ludicrous boasts. She said she flew the insignia of that dead house on her banners, and all I thought of it at the time was that it was simply good advertising. But then as the years went by, I began to wonder-" And after she left, he began to search. Garth nods, a barely perceptible dip of his head. "I'd try to pry tales of the Gunvaldsen line from people who passed through the Frost Hound. So many false leads and pointless rumours — it's one of the reasons I keep River around, to sort through these for me. Then one day he comes up and tells me that Fort Marrok didn't just exist, but he'd gotten his hands on the key as well." All right, that explains that. You take a deep swig of mead and motion for Garth to continue. Why won't he tell Gwyn and Garret the truth about their mother? "Gwyn... she already hates her mother and doesn't want anything to do with her. I don't want to bring it up lest I break her heart again. And Garret..." Garth closes his eyes. "The choice my wife made wasn't an easy one. If I told him outright, it would poison him against her forever. I don't want that. But if he works to find the truth by himself, when he gets to that point, if he ever does, when he catches up with her... I'm hoping he'll be wise enough to understand why she had to do what she did, even if he doesn't agree with it." That sounds like a cop-out. "It does, but it's the truth. And no, I'm not going to tell you, because you'll just march straight up and spill it to Garret. Them's the breaks. Did you find anything good while in there to make the trip worth your time?" Could have. Doesn't have to be. "Playing coy, eh? Well, I owe you as much." He'd better, since you risked your neck to bring him a memento of his wife. "Look, I'm not saying that I'm not grateful. Let me pour you another drink, eh?" You spend the remainder of the day — and night — entertaining yourself at Garth's expense, recounting the tale of your adventure in the haunted fortress with Garth and anyone who'll listen. [flags.GARTH_QUEST_GARRET_RECRUITED |Of course, you leave out the bits about Garret coming along with you. Wouldn't do if Garth heard about it.] River's even composed a little tune about your exploits by now, and has the entire common room cheering and clapping at his music. It's well past midnight by the time you crawl into bed, stuffed and drunk, and are asleep before your head hits the pillow. "

rows.original: "Well?" Garth asks when you broach the subject. "I take it you didn't succeed, because you'd have the medallion if you did, right?" Well... in not so many terms... um... yes. There were simply too many ghosts for you to deal with. If not for River, you might never have come out of the fortress at all, let alone in one piece. "Oh well. River tells me that when Fort Marrok went down, the garrison housed within was about two thousand strong. There's no shame in admitting that you were defeated, going against those odds — there'll be other glory seekers in good time to get that medallion for me. Best to just be thankful that you escaped with your life." He sets down the glass he was wiping, and pours out a large mug of honey mead before [party.som|setting it out in front of you|pouring another for [companion1.name]|pouring two more for [companion1.name] and [companion2.name]]. "It's as much my fault for having too much confidence in your abilities too soon." [pc.isDK|Hey, what's that supposed to mean?|It's hard to argue with that, given the facts.] "Don't fret about it too much; enjoy your drink and think of this as a setback to be overcome. I'll have something else for you in the future, if you're willing."
rows.translation: 那么？当你提到这个话题时，加斯会问及具体时间。我猜你没有成功，因为如果成功了，你现在应该已经拿到那枚奖章了吧？ 嗯……用另一种说法来说……就是，有太多的鬼魂让你无法应对。如果没有瑞弗的帮助，你可能根本就无法从那座堡垒里出来，更别说还能安然无恙地逃出来了。 好吧。瑞弗告诉我，当马罗克要塞陷落时，驻守在那里的军队有大约两千人。承认自己在这种悬殊的形势下被击败，并没有什么可羞愧的——总会有其他追求荣耀的人有机会为我夺取那枚奖章。我们最好还是庆幸自己能够活着逃脱吧。他放下正在擦拭的杯子，然后倒了一大杯蜂蜜酒出来。 [party.som|把它们摆在你的面前|再给自己倒一杯吧[companion1.name]|再给[companion1.name]和[companion2.name]各倒一杯]。 我也应该为此负责，因为太早就对你们的能力过于信任了。 [pc.isDK|嘿，这到底是什么意思？|鉴于这些事实，确实很难反驳这一点。] 别太为此烦恼，好好享受你的饮品吧，把这次挫折当作需要克服的困难吧。如果你愿意的话，将来我还会为你准备其他东西的。

rows.original: Ah, another day well and done. You're about to turn in for the day, heading up the stairs to your room on the Frost Hound's second floor when you hear voices coming from one of the guest rooms. The doorway is open, so you can hear them well enough — it's Garth and Garret, presumably doing some housekeeping on the empty rooms. "Old man... that medallion you passed me the other day..." "I hope you understand what it means. You know more about the truth than your sister does, but it's because you earned it all yourself." "Then you shouldn't be so quick to try and shove the Frost Hound off on me. Look, old man, I know what you're trying to do here and I'm not saying that I don't appreciate it, but I take too much after Mom to be content with sitting down without at least getting that wanderlust out of my system." A snort. "Then understand, son, that someday I've got to let go of you. Until then, my job is to train you for the day that you'll no longer need me, and I get the feeling that day is coming up pretty soon. My only hope is that you won't go and get yourself killed the moment you break your leash." "And you know full well what I'm going to do." "I can't stop you from going after your mother, Garret. I don't believe she's dead — she's too wilful for that. But you'd better know what to do when you finally find her." "I damn well know what I'm going to do when I finally find Mom, old man." "Are you sure?" Silence hangs in the air for split second. "I gave you the medallion for a reason, Garret. Think about what you want to do, not just go for or against something just because I'm headed in the opposite direction." "...I'll think about it." "You do that, son." Their voices fade as father and son set about changing the mattresses on the beds, and you slip by on to your own room without too much trouble. Now that was an interesting conversation...
rows.translation: 啊，又一天顺利地过去了。当你准备上楼回到“寒霜猎犬”号二楼的房间时，突然听到其中一间客房里传来了声音。门是开着的，所以你能清楚地听到他们在说什么——应该是加斯和加雷特，他们大概正在这些空房间里打扫卫生吧。 老先生……前几天你递给我的那枚奖章…… 我希望你能明白这意味着什么。你比你姐姐更了解真相，因为这一切都是你自己努力争取来的。 那你就不该这么急着把‘霜犬酒馆’推给我。听着，老兄，我明白你的意思，我也不是说不感激你，但自从妈妈去世后，我承担了太多责任，如果不能至少消除一下自己内心的那份漂泊欲，我是无法安心下来的。 哼。那么，孩子，你要明白，总有一天我必须放开你。在那一天到来之前，我的职责就是训练你，让你准备好不再需要我的那一天——而我感觉，那一天已经不远了。我唯一的希望就是，当你终于摆脱束缚的那一刻，你不会去送命。 你非常清楚我打算做什么。 我无法阻止你去寻找你的母亲，加雷特。我不相信她已经死了——她太固执了，不可能那么轻易放弃。但当你最终找到她时，你最好知道该怎么做。 老兄，我一旦找到了妈妈，我到底要做什么，我心里可太清楚了。 你确定吗？ 空气中瞬间陷入了寂静。 我给你那枚奖章是有原因的，加雷特。仔细想想你自己真正想要做什么，而不是仅仅因为我的选择与你相反，就盲目地支持或反对某件事。 ……我会考虑一下的。 你就这么做吧，孩子。 当父子俩开始更换床上的床垫时，他们的声音渐渐消失了，你也就顺利地回到了自己的房间。那个那是一次非常有趣的对话……

rows.original:
A structure of stone juts up from the solid ice beneath your feet, just shy of 15 feet tall. It's clearly seen the worst of time's passing, with much of its upper reaches torn away by winds. There's a jagged gash where the roof once might have been, or perhaps even more floors, and where there were once windows there are now broken crags full of icicles. The door is still standing, though, a solid hulk of black iron that bars entrance from the ground.

    Even over the ever-present howl of the wind, you can hear a thunderous sound echoing from inside the tower: a clash of metal on metal, rhythmic and even. It sounds like... like a smith's hammer?
    
    [party.has etheryn|"This place... it's not elven," Ryn murmurs at your side, taking a knee and brushing her fingers through the snow. "And nobody's come this way in at least a day. Maybe much longer."]
    
    [party.has cait|"Spooky!" Cait laughs, clutching her cloak around herself. "But I'll risk ghosties or whatever just to get out of this wind!"]
    
    [party.has arona|"Yeah, don't care who's in there, I'm going in!" Arona declares. "Get me the fuck outta this cold!"
    
    [party.has etheryn|"This isn't even winter yet," Ryn snickers. "Just wait..."]]
    
    [party.has berwyn|"A tower, but not a wizard's," Berry comments from your side. "Too plain. Still, I sense magic..."]
    
    [party.has kiyoko|"Be careful, [pc.name]," Kiyoko says, taking your hand. "I smell a spirit close at hand."]
    
    [party.has azyrran|Your Hive Knight buzzes her wings and edges closer to the ruins. "Hopefully it's warmer in there!"]
    
    [party.has brint|"Look at that door!" Brint grins, gesturing ahead. "Big enough even for a fella my size! Come on, let's see who's home!"]
    
    You steel yourself to face whatever may lie inside...
rows.translation:
在你脚下的坚实冰层中，有一块岩石突了出来，高度接近15英尺。显而易见，它经历了漫长的岁月沧桑，其上部的大部分结构都被风蚀掉了。在那里，原本应该是屋顶的地方现在有一道参差不齐的裂口，或许还有更多的楼层被破坏；而那些曾经是窗户的地方，如今只剩下布满冰柱的破碎岩壁罢了。然而，那扇门依然矗立在那里，那是一扇由黑色铁块构成的坚固屏障，从地面开始就阻断了人们的进入之路。

    即便在风声持续不断的呼啸之中，你仍然能够听到从塔内传来的震耳欲聋的声音：那是金属与金属碰撞发出的声响，有节奏且整齐有序。听起来……就像铁匠的锤子一样？
    
    [party.has etheryn|这个地方……显然不是精灵们的居所，”小琳在你身旁低声说道，她单膝跪地，用手指拨开积雪。“至少已经有一整天没人来过这里了，或许更久。]
    
    [party.has cait|太可怕了！”凯特笑着说，一边把斗篷紧紧裹在身上。“但我宁愿面对鬼魂之类的东西，也不想再忍受这种风了！]
    
    [party.has arona|没错，我不管里面有什么人，我一定要进去！”阿罗娜坚定地说道，“快把我从这冰天雪地里弄出去！
    
    [party.has etheryn|现在甚至还没到冬天呢，”小琳冷笑道，“等着瞧吧……]]
    
    [party.has berwyn|一座塔，但不是巫师的塔，”贝里在你身旁评论道，“太普通了……不过，我感觉到其中蕴含着魔法……]
    
    [party.has kiyoko|小心点， [pc.name]，我感觉到有灵魂就在附近，”清子握着你的手说道。]
    
    [party.has azyrran|你的蜂鸟骑士振动着翅膀，逐渐靠近那些废墟。“希望里面会更暖和一些！]
    
    [party.has brint|看那扇门！”布林特咧嘴一笑，指向前方，“就算是我这种身材的人也能通过！来吧，让我们看看里面住着谁！]
    
    你鼓起勇气，准备面对里面可能存在的任何东西……

    [party.has berwyn|"A tower, but not a wizard's," Berry comments from your side. "Too plain. Still, I sense magic..."]
    
    [party.has kiyoko|"Be careful, [pc.name]," Kiyoko says, taking your hand. "I smell a spirit close at hand."]
    
    [party.has azyrran|Your Hive Knight buzzes her wings and edges closer to the ruins. "Hopefully it's warmer in there!"]
    
    [party.has brint|"Look at that door!" Brint grins, gesturing ahead. "Big enough even for a fella my size! Come on, let's see who's home!"]
    
    You steel yourself to face whatever may lie inside...'

rows.original: [flags.FRZ_SMITH |You enter the tower once more, once Brint has wrenched the door out of the way. The spectral smith is still inside, pounding away at her frigid scutum. She looks up with a snort, setting her hammer aside. [party.has arona|"Not a fucking GHOST," Arona grunts, grabbing her hammer. "Fuuuuuck!"] "You return," she observes sagely. "Tell me, child of the mountains... have you worked up the courage to face my trial? The legacy of my clan yet goes unclaimed, lost to time without one of our blood. One such as you." Brint glances at you, a smug grin on his lips. "I'm ready, [pc.name]. But I'd want you at my side..." |Brint grips the door as you approach, putting his back into it in a way that makes all those thick, sinewy muscles bulge and strain. The ancient metal squeals on rusted hinges, ice cracking loudly — but none of the sounds compare to the rhythmic striking coming from within the tower. Clang! Clang! Clang! When your minotaur [brint.fucked|lover|bro] finally wrenches the door open, you can see clearly the source of the clangor. Inside the tower is what could best be described as a blacksmith's workshop: an anvil sits in the center of the tower, surrounded by tools hanging from pegs, and a pair of tattered banners flank the door: one depicting a minotaur, and the other, a legion of serpents surrounding an empty throne. But that is all on your peripheral vision, as your attention is instantly focused on the tower's inhabitant: a massive woman, nearly Brint's own size, and just as covered in thick brown fur. Her muscles are nearly as impressive as his beneath it. The cow has a smaller snout and horns, but breasts so large that each time she brings her hammer down on the anvil, they sway so wildly that they could knock a man over. Yet... something about her is ethereal, spectral. You can see through her, if only barely. Fragments of ice fly like sparts from her heatless forge as her hammer strikes what must be a shield, a scutum made of solid frost. [party.has arona|"FUCKING GHOSTS! GAH!" Arona howls, grabbing at her hammer. "FuckfuckfuckFUCK."] Brint snorts loudly, eying the ghostly smith. "Northern mino. Or was. They're like us in Khor'minos, just backwards. Big furry women, little men." The smith strikes a final blow, and then her muscular arms relax. "I can still hear, you know. And smell... that wonderful scent of a mountain bull, so virile... almost overpowering. How long I've waited for one of our kind. Centuries beyond counting, perfecting this." She gestures to the shield laid out in the front of her, glistening blue. "What, you've been waiting for me?" Brint asks, scratching his head. "Come on, that-" "Not you!" she snorts. "But someone like you. Of our blood. My lost clan... we suffered so, enslaved by the icehewn giants for generations! And when they fell, there was no freedom for us, only a doom shared in dragonfire! But there was time enough for one last work, my masterpiece, the culmination of all the giants taught us — that we might serve them better. I have saved this all along, that our legacy would not be utterly lost, or worse... be carried off and lost by one unworthy! If I must bear the loss of my clan, I will not see all we learned forgotten! All we accomplished melt away like summer snow..." You glance between the cow-smith and Brint. "So you've been waiting for a minotaur like Brint?" [pc.ra minotaur cowgirl|You guess you don't count, not having been born one.] The ghost-woman nods slowly, rising to her full height — nearly as large as your companion, though her mammoth rack makes her look even wider around. "Not just any minotaur. A worthy minotaur. Are you one such, child of the mountains? Are you strong enough to wield elemental frost, a weapon far keener than that axe of yours; is your constitution great enough to gird yourself in armor of ice, that you may deflect any blow with the surety of a glacier?" "Sounds like a challenge if I ever heard one," Brint chuckles. "What do you say, [pc.name]?" To you, this sounds like an opportunity to help Brint learn some new tricks... but who knows what'll happen if you fail... ]
rows.translation: [flags.FRZ_SMITH |在布林特把门推开之后，你再次进入了那座塔。那位幽灵铁匠仍在里面，不停地敲打着她那冰冷的护甲。她哼了一声，停下了手中的锤子，抬头看着你。 [party.has arona|根本不是什么该死的鬼魂，”阿罗娜咒骂着，抓起了她的锤子。“真他妈见鬼了！] 你回来了，”她睿智地说道，“告诉我，山里的孩子……你是否已经鼓起勇气来面对我的考验？我们家族的遗产至今仍无人认领，随着时间的流逝而消失无踪，再也没有我们家族中的人来继承它。就像你这样的一个人。” 布林特瞥了你一眼，嘴角露出一丝得意的笑容：“我准备好了。 [pc.name]但我希望你能在我身边…… |当你靠近时，布林特紧紧抓住门框，用尽全力将身体压在门上，那些结实有力的肌肉因此而凸起、绷紧。古老的金属在生锈的铰链上发出刺耳的声响，冰面也伴随着巨大的裂裂声——但这一切声音，都远远比不上从塔内传来的那种有节奏的撞击声。叮当！叮当！叮当！ 当你的弥诺陶洛斯出现时[brint.fucked|恋人|兄弟]终于把门强行拉开，你终于能够清楚地看到那刺耳声响的来源了。塔的内部简直就是一个典型的铁匠作坊：一个铁砧被放置在塔的正中央，周围挂满了各种工具；门的两侧各挂着一面破旧的旗帜，一面上面画着弥诺陶洛斯，另一面则描绘着一群蛇围着一张空荡荡的王座。 但这些都只是你视野边缘所看到的，因为你的注意力立刻被塔中的居民吸引了——那是一个体型庞大的女人，几乎和布林特一样高大，全身也覆盖着厚厚的棕色毛皮。在毛皮之下，她的肌肉同样令人印象深刻。这头牛的鼻子和角都比较小，但乳房却大得惊人——每当它用“锤子”敲击铁砧时，那些乳房会剧烈晃动，甚至有可能把一个人撞倒。然而……它身上总有一种超脱尘世、仿佛来自幽灵世界的气质。你能够感受到这一点看穿她的伪装如果只是勉强能够做到的话…… 当她的锤子敲击那面由坚硬霜冻构成的盾牌时，冰块像碎片一样从她那毫无热量的“铁炉”中飞溅出来。 [party.has arona|该死的鬼魂！啊！”阿罗娜尖叫着，慌忙抓起她的锤子。“去他妈的……] 布林特大声哼了一声，盯着那个看起来像幽灵的铁匠。“北方米诺人。或者说，曾经是。他们和我们在科尔米诺斯一样，只不过生活方式完全相反——那些女人身材高大且毛发浓密，而男人则身材矮小。” 铁匠给了最后一下敲击，随后她那肌肉结实的双臂便放松了下来。我仍然能够听到那些声音，也能闻到……那种山野公牛散发出的美妙气味，如此雄壮有力，几乎让人无法抗拒。我等待着我们同类出现，已经等了数不清的世纪，只是为了不断完善这一技艺。” 她指了指放在自己面前的那面闪闪发亮的蓝色盾牌。 什么，你一直在等我吗？”布林特挠着头问道，“拜托，那……” “不是你在等！”她哼了一声，“但我等的是一个像你这样、与我们血脉相连的人。我那失落的氏族……我们遭受了太多的苦难，世代被那些冰雕巨人们奴役！当他们倒下之后，我们依然得不到自由，只能共同面对龙火带来的毁灭！但是，我们还有足够的时间来完成最后一项使命——创作我的杰作，将那些巨人们教给我们的所有知识融会贯通，从而能够更好地为他们服务。我一直保存着这一切，就是为了不让我们的传承彻底消失，更不会让某个不配的人把它们夺走并毁掉！如果我必须承受失去自己族群的痛苦，我也绝不会眼睁睁看着我们所学的一切被遗忘，看着我们所取得的一切像夏天的雪一样瞬间消融。你将目光在那个铁匠和布林特之间来回移动，说道：“原来你们一直在等待像布林特这样的弥诺陶洛斯啊？ [pc.ra minotaur cowgirl|你大概觉得自己不算数吧，毕竟你并不是天生就属于这一类的。] 那个女鬼缓缓点了点头，然后站直了身体——她的身高几乎与你身边的同伴相当，不过她那庞大的胸腔使得她的体型看起来更加魁梧。“不是普通的弥诺陶洛斯，而是一位真正配得上这个称号的弥诺陶洛斯。“你也是这样的山之子吗？你的力量是否足以驾驭元素寒霜这种比你的斧头更加锋利的武器？你的体魄是否强健到足以披上冰之铠甲，从而能够像冰川一样轻松挡住任何攻击？” “这听起来真像是一个挑战啊，”布林特笑着说，“你怎么看？ [pc.name]对你来说，这似乎是一个帮助布林特学习新技能的好机会……但谁又能知道如果你失败了会发生什么呢…… ]

rows.original:
"We accept!" Brint bellows, putting his hands on his weapon-hilts. "So what's the challenge?"

        The minotaur ghost takes up her ice-hewn hammer and sweeps it across the workshop, a gesture that brings with it a howl of shivering wind that tears through the ruined tower. "If you wish to command the powers of elemental ice, you must prove you can withstand the fury of the blizzard! Come and earn it, child of the mountains!"
        
        So it's a fight then!

我们接受！”布林特大声喊道，同时将双手放在武器柄上，“那么，挑战内容是什么呢？”

        原来是一场战斗啊！

rows.original:
You shake your head at Brint, and he lets our a tense breath — a bellows in his chest as his brawny arms cross. 

        "Khaak. Not yet, spirit," he grunts, "We need time to prepare."
        
        The smith sighs and picks up her hammer, returning to her work. "Do as you will. Or find one worthy of my clan's legacy. Every year, I feel myself growing fainter!"
        
        She strikes the ice, sending shards flying and as you and Brint turn to leave.

你朝布林特摇了摇头，他吐出一口紧张的气息——胸膛起伏如风箱，粗壮的双臂交叉抱在胸前。 

        “哈克。还不行，灵魂，”他咕哝道，“我们需要时间来准备。”
        
        铁匠叹了口气，拿起她的铁锤，回到工作中。“随你们的便吧。或者去找一个配得上我族传承的人。每一年，我都感觉自己变得更加虚弱！”
        
        她敲向冰面，冰屑四溅。你和布林特转身离开。

rows.original: The final blow strikes the spectral smith with boneshaking force, enough to rattle even her incorporeal form. The minotauress staggers to a knee, leaning on her anvil. "Worthy!" she bellows, throwing her head back with a ruckus laugh. "You are worthy indeed, son of stone! This shield, all the power I have kept safe within it for years beyond counting, it is yours! Take it, if you will, and show the world the skill of the Ljyarran clan." "So I will," Brint says with authority, stepping forward and grasping the scutum. The moment his meaty fingers touch its frigid surface, the wind howls anew, whirling through the tower — and into Brint. Ice and snow fly madly through the ruin, roaring like a dragon as the ghost-smith laughs and cheers, and slowly fades away to naught but cold mist. Brint grits his teeth and grabs the shield with his other hand, grasping it hard as the whirlwind flows around him, and through him. With a great grunt of effort, your minotaur [brint.fucked|lover|companion] hefts the shield up from the anvil and secures it on his arm. As he does so, the wind breaks — and frost erupts from the shield, spreading across his body like a suit of armor made from solid blue ice! Brint flexes his mighty muscles and rolls his broad shoulders as the ice encases his torso, arms, thighs... everywhere save his now thoroughly erect cock and his grinning face. "So much power!" he laughs, whirling his mace around his right hand and cracking it against his shield. "I feel like the glacier, alright, [pc.name]! Like I'm solid as a rock, but my blood's ice-cold! Feels good." The elemental chaos surrounding him finally abates, drawing itself into the shield and the minotaur both. He finally sighs and loosens his grip on the shield, and when he does so, the icy armor surrounding his body shatters, falling away to nothing. Only leather and fur remains. He feels colder than before, but even more solid, like he's put on even more muscle... and he's right, it feels good to be in his embrace. Like he could protect you from anything. |The minotaur grins and grabs Cait, giving her [cait.butt] a squeeze. "Thanks to you two." "Oh! B-Brint..."
