在这个房间里已经没有任何东西可以让你留下了，于是你转身准备开始漫长而艰辛的归程，返回鹰棘镇。
rows.raw: " "Goddess," Lia gasps. "Is he... there's no way he could've survived that, right?" Well, in your experience, especially given everything that happened in the Rift, demons can take real punishment. They can survive an awful lot of cold, after all; maybe that goes for lava, too. They can shapeshift, they can transform, and as far as you're concerned, unless you see a body, you can't be sure. Actually, given what happened with Gweyr and Leold, maybe you can't even be sure with a body. "Ugh. I think I get it." She nods slowly. "It's strange. He was a demon, he was absolutely insufferable, but... after seeing how he changed after the relic was parted from him, I'm not sure how much of his behavior was actually him. Even without the relic affecting his mind, someone as obsessive as he was having power of the likes that we saw slip from his grasp would have been a terrible blow. And speaking of that —" You look down at the Dawnsword in your hand, its blade [pc.isDK |pulsing with menacing red light. You still feel like yourself, for what it's worth. On a whim, you make an experimental swing through the air, and the blade of light makes a distinctive keening noise as it moves in a blurred arc of crimson.[var0| Oooooh! Pretty.] "Please be careful with it, [pc.name]. I don't know whether the demon did something to it or if it was already this twisted to begin with and it simply was seeking a like-minded wielder, but I can feel its malignancy even from here." [var0|Aww. It's really bright and shiny though... fiiiine. ]Someone's got to carry it back to Sanders. Does she want to hold it? "N-no. Not yet, at least. But you're right — we need to get the relic back to Dad and see if anything can be done about... about what's happened to it." You don't know about that; all this feels perfectly natural, as if the relic was made for you. But you aren't about to tell Liaden that to her face, and accept it with a nod. |shimmering with a faint golden sheen. Lia gazes at it in wonder. "Wow. Are you okay, [pc.name]? You sounded... well..." It was rough for a little bit, but you think you're fine. You don't feel an invasive presence in your mind, good or bad — if anything, the Dawnsword now appears far more placid in your hand than it did the incubus', content to rest until it's needed. On a whim, you make an experimental swing through the air, and the blade of light makes a distinctive keening noise as it moves in a blurred arc of radiance.[var0| Oooooh! Pretty.] She blows out a breath you hadn't realized she was holding. "I'm glad you're okay. Just — please be careful with it. Even if it doesn't reek of... malignancy like it did a moment ago, it[liaden.poly |'s still dangerous — it could maim you if you're not extra-attentive | deserves just a bit more respect than that ]." [var0|Aww. It's really bright and shiny though... fiiiine.|Fair enough.] With another little impulse of will, you close down the blade, then hold it up to her. Someone's got to carry it back to Sanders, see what he makes of all this. Does she want to hold it? "N-no. I don't think so. You're the one who saved it; it chose you. But you're right — we need to get the relic back to Dad and see about the next step. I... you know, after all this, after hearing you [pc.mascFem |yell |cry out ] when you purified it, I'm not sure whether I want to have been the one to claim it after all." You understand. It's not as though she spent the quest on the sidelines, though; she's the one who warned you to grab the sword before it fell over the edge — and who bull-rushed the demon instead of going for it herself. You're not sure whether you'd have been able to rescue the sword without that. "And you're the one who went for it even with a demon sitting on top of you," she laughs. "Maybe you've got to be a little crazy to be worthy, and if that's the case, I don't mind being the person who kept you safe long enough to purify the thing instead.[liaden.poly | Besides," she says, her eyes twinkling, "if the sword's with you, it's still staying in the family, isn't it?" Oooh. That's one way to think of it... She throws her arms around you in a fierce hug, holds your gaze for a heartbeat, and then brings you in close for a kiss. Even after smooching, she doesn't let go of the hug. "It's the only way." Wow. Y'know, if you'd known earlier that going on adventures with your girlfriend[party.has azyrran |s ] would be this fun... "We'll have to make more time to do more of 'em, right? Though I don't have any other swords that need savin'... ]" ] And speaking of which, is this supposed to be normal? Like, is it in the legends that the Dawnsword can fall, that it changes itself to suit its wielder, that it actually has — or at least had — a mind and will of its own? Sanders certainly didn't tell you anything about that when he was briefing the both of you; something like that would certainly have been pertinent information. "It... it wasn't. I mean, there were plenty of stories about the Dawnsword back in the keep that took its name from it, and while it had always been a powerful artifact that would only work for those worthy, it'd never had a true animus of its own." She shakes her head. "I'm way in over my head, [pc.name] — let's just see what Dad makes of all this." [pc.isDK |It's true. It's certainly a trend that Sanders has answers for questions — you can only hope that he hasn't been deliberately withholding them from you and Liaden all this time yet again. |She's right: he's the best person to ask about it all. You can't imagine that he left anything out of the story on purpose... ] [party.has etheryn |[pc.isDK |From your side, you hear Etheryn sigh. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I d-don't think so," she stammers |I don't think so," she says cautiously ]. "Maybe he has some guesses, though. At least we got it out of that d[etheryn.lowConfidence |-d ]emon's hands — I hate the idea of Princess Iveryn's sword, if that's what this really is, belonging to them." Far better for it to be in yours, yes; you've certainly proved as much. |[etheryn.highConfidence |"I don't know if he'll be able to say," Etheryn says from beside you. She gazes at the hilt with the same kind of reverence that Liaden did. "It doesn't sound like he had the experience you just did. Even if he doesn't know, though, you saved the sword — and got it back to normal again. If this really is Princess Iveryn's blade, I think she'd be proud." Does that go for her, too? "Of course!" Lia's grin is genuine: "Yeah[liaden.poly |. It's a great story, isn't it? The Champion of Frost rescuing the Dawnsword |, if it had to be somebody else, the Champion of Frost rescuing the Dawnsword isn't too bad ]. Kind of like you're bringing it back to the Winter City in a way." [etheryn.fucked |You wink at your royal [etheryn.married |spouse |lover ]: that's happening in more than just 'a way'. "Oh, Goddess." She swallows hard, in the best of ways. Heh. Romantically teasing your Ryn is one of the more fun things you get to do on a regular basis, and it works every time. |Kind of, yeah. Does that mean you have the royal assent? "The sword makes the choice, not me... but I'm happy it chose you as worthy." She gives you a cheerful, wobbly-eared grin. ] |"M[etheryn.lowConfidence |-m ]aybe he won't know," Etheryn says quietly. The elf hovers by your side, gazing at the hilt with genuine awe. "I don't... I don't think it matters that much, does it? The sword's [etheryn.lowConfidence |s- ]safe. If it really did belong to Princess Iveryn, maybe she'd be happy knowing you rescued it." Lia pats her on the shoulder and nods. "You're right. [liaden.poly |Who's a better person to rescue the Dawnsword than the woman who saved the Winter City? |If it had to be anybody other than me, I'm glad the [pc.manWoman] who saved the Winter City is also the one who saved the Dawnsword, too. ]" "Y-Yeah. You've done a lot for m[etheryn.fucked |e and m ]y people. I guess this is one more thing, right?" Ryn's smile is one of the broader ones you've seen on her. ] "Anyway. I'm sorry for interrupting. We're good to go, right?" ] ] With nothing left for you in this chamber, you turn back and prepare to make the long trek back to Hawkethorne. "

rows.original: "I've got this, Lia!" You manage to crack a punch straight into the demon's jaw. "Save the sword!" The demon howls; whether at the sound of your shout or the realization that its efforts were for naught, you don't know, but it's not important. What is important is keeping the bastard distracted. He bobs away from the next punch you throw, then reaches back with his talons to barely miss a swipe at your face. The punch after that, though — that gets him, rewarding you with another howl. You think fast, trying to press your advantage, but there's only so many places to follow up. His chest is well armored, he's got greaves, he's got — oh. You fire a knee right into his crotch and grin as his snarl turns into a high-pitched whine. But he's still wrestling with you, still grappling, holding on tight... ... and completely incapable of rising to meet Liaden as she streaks past him, dives for the Dawnsword, and comes up with the hilt in her hand. Another pulse thrums through the cavern, a pulse accompanied by Lia's wordless cry of pain. But she refuses to let go. Instead she grits her teeth, glaring at the vibrating, glowing hilt with an expression of sheer indomitable will. The ornamentation, the crimson gem, the light around the broken shard of a shaft itself all flicker red, then gold, then back again. She falls to her knees, digging into the ash and earth, but her fist tightens even further. The young paladin simply will not yield to whatever dark power animates the blade. "No!" The incubus tries to leap up, but you're prepared for it, knocking the demon right back to the ground with a devastating leg sweep. With the breathing space you've gained, with the distraction Lia's given you, with the [pc.weapon] you snatch from the ground[party.hasCompanions |, and with help from late-arriving [party.compNames true] ], you drive the fallen being back toward the ledge, giving Lia as much time as she needs to get the blade under control... She does. The demon tries another swipe at you, but before you even have a chance to block it, a golden blade flashes in front of him. Just like that, he howls with pain and draws his hand back, badly maimed. That gives you just enough of a breathing space to flick a glance to the blade's holder to make sure she's okay, and Lia, obviously in pain but still standing on her own two feet, gives you a fierce smile in return. You level your [pc.weapon] at the incubus once more. It's over.[silly | You have the... okay, come on, he knows how this goes. ] No longer the loquacious, borderline genteel opponent of before, he chokes out a "no" as he stumbles back toward the chasm, going further and further until he's only inches from the ledge. Precarious or not, though, he doesn't pay his footing any mind, instead focusing all his attention, his rage, his disbelief on you and Liaden. His hands flex, his legs tense, and he looks like he's working his way back up to one last attempt. "Not you. Not you." Liaden shakes her head. "Don't try it." He does. The demon, wobbling on unsteady legs, makes another lunge for Liaden, but the Dawnsword flashes and he crumples to the ground with a shriek of rage. That's the only sound he has time to make — because as soon as he hits the dirt, the outcropping that he was standing on separates from the rest of the ledge. Wordlessly, abruptly, both he and it plummet into the abyss. [party.CombatNames] edge forward carefully, alert for any further collapses, and manage to peer over the edge... just in time to see his black dot merge with the rest of the magma below and disappear. "Goddess," Lia gasps. "Is he... there's no way he could've survived that, right?" Well, in your experience, especially given everything that happened in the Rift, demons can take real punishment. They can survive an awful lot of cold, after all; maybe that goes for lava, too. They can shapeshift, they can transform, and as far as you're concerned, unless you see a body, you can't be sure. Actually, given what happened with Gweyr and Leold, maybe you can't even be sure with a body. "Ugh. I think I get it." She nods slowly. "It's strange. He was a demon, he was absolutely insufferable, but... after seeing how he changed after the relic was parted from him, I'm not sure how much of his behavior was actually him. Even without it affecting his mind, someone as obsessive as he was having power of the likes that we saw slip from his grasp would have been a terrible blow. Speaking of which." Yeah. The golden blade continues to glow in her hand as the [party.sizeText] of you back away from the edge, and you can't help but regard it with awe. [var0 |Actually... more than awe. It's... it's really super shiny. Hypnotizing, almost. You really want to just stare at it for a while. Gosh. She must be feeling really gooood. Like super good even. |She managed to save the weapon and purify it: very impressive. How is she feeling after that? ][liaden.poly | You were worried there for a little bit... ] [liaden.poly |She grins reassuringly. "Aw. Thanks for asking. It did take a little out of me... but I think I'm okay." |"It took something out of me," she admits. ] The young paladin breathes in and out slowly, fixes her eyes on the blade, and then manages to make it disappear into its hilt. Even after the golden glow vanishes, she continues to treat the weapon with care, even preciousness. "There was a presence, a want, in here. I don't know where it came from. It certainly isn't anything like the stories from before. It kind of... does what I want it to, now, though. It's calm now. Maybe calm 'again'." [party.has azyrran |Azzy steps forward with alarm. "Are you [azyrran.kdb |sure |certain |suuuuuure ] that's safe[azzy.liaden|, my flower]? What if...?" |Huh. Is that safe? She's not going to end up like your demonic foe, is she? ] Liaden nods. "[party.has azyrran |Thanks, [liaden.poly |you two |sweetie ], but I think ]I've got this — at least for now. But I'm definitely going to want to ask Dad plenty of questions about it when we get back." She pauses, then, with a smile, says, "[liaden.poly |I'm glad the three of us got to do this together. You two had my back, getting us going, fighting off the demon, giving me the chance to rescue the sword |[party.has azyrran |And I have to thank you, too, [pc.name] |Thanks, by the way ]. Thanks for getting us all going on this quest, for fighting off the demon, for giving me the chance to get the blade ]..." Hey, [liaden.poly|what are girlfriends for?|she did as much legwork as you did here.] And she was worthy; you figured the sword would be able to tell, too.[party.has etheryn | "Y[etheryn.lowConfidence |-Y ]eah," Etheryn adds. "You're a great Lumian paladin, Lia. If this really did used to be the sword of Princess Iveryn, I [etheryn.highConfidence |know |think ] she'd be really proud of you for saving it. And of you, [pc.name] — you gave up the chance to take it. M[etheryn.lowConfidence |-M ]aybe you'd have been worthy, too, but you helped Lia instead." It's all good; the sword went to somebody worthy all the same. ] Besides, you got to kick a demon right in the [silly |daddy bags |balls ], and how often does that chance come up? "Hopefully not very often," Liaden laughs. "Well, look. The first thing we should probably do is get back to Hawkethorne. And the second is figure out some way for the Order of the Oriflamme to show their appreciation to the hero[pc.mf | |ine ] who helped return the Dawnsword to us. I feel like being its wielder ought to give me a fair amount of pull, and you deserve more out of all this than a chance to boot a demon in the crotch."[liaden.poly | She winks. "Y'know, apart from the obvious thank-yous a girl like me might wanna give [party.has azyrran |you an' Azzy |a girl like you ]." | ] You won't say no to that. Time to head out, then.
rows.translation: 没问题的，莉亚！”你终于成功一拳击中了恶魔的下巴。“把剑收起来吧！” 恶魔发出了嚎叫；你是被你的喊声吓到了，还是因为它意识到自己的努力都是白费了，你并不清楚，但这也不重要。重要的是是关键是要让那个混蛋分心。他会躲开你接下来的攻击，然后伸出爪子，勉强避开对你脸部的攻击。但接下来的那一拳——就会击中他，让他再次发出惨叫。你必须迅速思考，努力利用自己的优势，但可进攻的位置其实并不多。他的胸部有厚重的护甲，他还穿着护腿……哦。 你用膝盖猛击他的裆部，看着他从怒吼变成了尖锐的哀嚎，不禁露出笑容。但他仍然在与你搏斗，紧紧抓住你不放…… ……而当他看到莉亚登从他身边飞掠而过，冲向晨曦剑并将剑柄握在手中时，他根本无力起身去阻拦她。 另一阵震动再次传遍整个洞穴，与此同时，莉亚发出了无声的痛苦呻吟。但她却丝毫没有松手的意思。相反，她紧紧咬住牙关，用一种充满不屈不挠的意志力，死死地盯着那根正在震动、发出光芒的剑柄。那些装饰物、那颗深红色的宝石，还有那块破碎的轴状物周围散发出的光芒，全都先是呈现出红色，然后变成了金色，随后又重新变回红色。她双膝跪地，在灰烬和泥土中摸索着，但她的拳头却握得更加紧了。这位年轻的圣骑士绝不会屈服于那些驱使这把剑发挥力量的暗影力量。 不！”那个梦魔试图跃起，但你早已做好了准备，用一记强有力的扫腿将这个恶魔重新击倒在地。多亏了你争取到的这一段时间，多亏了莉亚为你制造的干扰[pc.weapon]从地面抓起[party.hasCompanions |在那些后来才赶到的人的帮助下[party.compNames true] ]你将那个倒下的生物推向边缘，给莉亚足够的时间来控制那把刀…… 她做到了。那个恶魔再次朝你挥刀攻击，但在你还有机会挡住它的那一刻之前，一把金色的刀刃已经闪现在它的面前。就这样，他痛苦地嚎叫着，把手缩了回来，显然受了严重的伤。这一幕正好给了你片刻的喘息时间，让你能够瞥一眼那把刀的握把，确认她是否安然无恙。而莉亚，虽然明显在疼痛中，却依然自己站稳了脚跟，她回给你一个坚定的微笑。 你提升了自己的等级。 [pc.weapon]又一次陷入了这种困境。一切都结束了。[silly | 你已经有……好吧，快点吧，他知道该怎么做。 ] 他再也不是从前那个话多、近乎文雅的对手了。他艰难地挤出“不”这个字，踉跄着向深渊退去，越退越远，直到距离边缘只剩下几英寸的距离。尽管处境危险，他却完全不在意自己的脚步，而是将所有的注意力、所有的愤怒、所有的难以置信都集中在你和莉娅登身上。他的双手紧握，双腿绷得紧紧的，看起来他正在努力准备进行最后的尝试。“不是你。不是你。莉亚登摇了摇头：“别试了。” 他还是试了。那个恶魔摇摇晃晃地站不稳，又一次向莉亚登扑去，但晨光之剑一闪，它便在一声愤怒的尖叫中倒在地上。那也是它发出的唯一声音——因为它刚一触地，它原本站立的岩架就与其他部分分离了，于是它和那块岩架一起，无声无息地坠入了深渊。 [party.CombatNames]小心翼翼地向前挪动，时刻警惕着是否还会发生进一步的坍塌，终于设法从边缘处探出头来……正好看到那个黑点与下方的岩浆融为一体，消失不见了。 “女神啊，”莉亚惊呼道，“他……他真的消失了吗？……他不可能在那种情况下活下来，对吧？” 不过，以你的经验来看，尤其是考虑到在裂隙地区发生的一切，那些恶魔确实能够承受巨大的折磨。毕竟，它们能够忍受极度的寒冷；也许熔岩也对它们没有太大影响。它们能够变形，能够改变形态。而对你来说，除非你看到了实体，否则你根本无法确定它们的真实形态。事实上，考虑到格韦尔和利奥尔德所发生的事情，也许你甚至根本无法确定它们的存在。与一起呃，我想我明白了吧。”她缓缓点了点头，“真是奇怪……他本来是个恶魔，行为举止让人难以忍受，但是……在看到那件遗物与他分离后他的变化之后，我开始不确定他的那些行为，到底有多少是真正的本性，又有多少是受到了那件遗物的影响呢他即使这并没有影响到他的心智，对于一个如此执着的人来说，失去我们刚才所看到的那种力量，无疑会是一个巨大的打击。说到这里…… 是的，那把金色宝剑依然在她手中闪烁着光芒。你们[party.sizeText]从边缘退开时，不禁满怀敬畏地端详着它。 [var0 |其实……不仅仅是敬畏之情。它真的……闪闪发光，简直让人着迷，几乎让人无法移开视线。你真的会想要盯着它看上好一会儿。天啊，她现在肯定感觉非常非常开心，开心到极点吧。 |她成功救出了那件武器。以及净化它：真是令人印象深刻。经历那样的事情后，她现在感觉如何呢？ ][liaden.poly | 你有那么一会儿还挺担心的呢…… ] [liaden.poly |她露出安慰的笑容：“哎呀，谢谢你的关心。确实让我有点吃不消……不过我觉得我现在已经没事了。 |这真的让我失去了一些东西，”她承认道。 ]年轻的圣骑士缓缓地呼吸着，将目光紧紧地盯着那把剑，最终成功地将其收回到剑鞘中。即使那金色的光芒已经消失，她依然小心翼翼地对待着这把武器，仿佛它是一件无价之宝。“当时有一种存在想要在这里。我不知道它是从哪里来的。它肯定和以前的那些故事完全不同。不过，现在它确实能做到我想要它做的事情。现在它很平静。也许又恢复了平静吧。 [party.has azyrran rows.raw: " "I've got this, Lia!" You manage to crack a punch straight into the demon's jaw. "Save the sword!" The demon howls; whether at the sound of your shout or the realization that its efforts were for naught, you don't know, but it's not important. What is important is keeping the bastard distracted. He bobs away from the next punch you throw, then reaches back with his talons to barely miss a swipe at your face. The punch after that, though — that gets him, rewarding you with another howl. You think fast, trying to press your advantage, but there's only so many places to follow up. His chest is well armored, he's got greaves, he's got — oh. You fire a knee right into his crotch and grin as his snarl turns into a high-pitched whine. But he's still wrestling with you, still grappling, holding on tight... ... and completely incapable of rising to meet Liaden as she streaks past him, dives for the Dawnsword, and comes up with the hilt in her hand. Another pulse thrums through the cavern, a pulse accompanied by Lia's wordless cry of pain. But she refuses to let go. Instead she grits her teeth, glaring at the vibrating, glowing hilt with an expression of sheer indomitable will. The ornamentation, the crimson gem, the light around the broken shard of a shaft itself all flicker red, then gold, then back again. She falls to her knees, digging into the ash and earth, but her fist tightens even further. The young paladin simply will not yield to whatever dark power animates the blade. "No!" The incubus tries to leap up, but you're prepared for it, knocking the demon right back to the ground with a devastating leg sweep. With the breathing space you've gained, with the distraction Lia's given you, with the [pc.weapon] you snatch from the ground[party.hasCompanions |, and with help from late-arriving [party.compNames true] ], you drive the fallen being back toward the ledge, giving Lia as much time as she needs to get the blade under control... She does. The demon tries another swipe at you, but before you even have a chance to block it, a golden blade flashes in front of him. Just like that, he howls with pain and draws his hand back, badly maimed. That gives you just enough of a breathing space to flick a glance to the blade's holder to make sure she's okay, and Lia, obviously in pain but still standing on her own two feet, gives you a fierce smile in return. You level your [pc.weapon] at the incubus once more. It's over.[silly | You have the... okay, come on, he knows how this goes. ] No longer the loquacious, borderline genteel opponent of before, he chokes out a "no" as he stumbles back toward the chasm, going further and further until he's only inches from the ledge. Precarious or not, though, he doesn't pay his footing any mind, instead focusing all his attention, his rage, his disbelief on you and Liaden. His hands flex, his legs tense, and he looks like he's working his way back up to one last attempt. "Not you. Not you." Liaden shakes her head. "Don't try it." He does. The demon, wobbling on unsteady legs, makes another lunge for Liaden, but the Dawnsword flashes and he crumples to the ground with a shriek of rage. That's the only sound he has time to make — because as soon as he hits the dirt, the outcropping that he was standing on separates from the rest of the ledge. Wordlessly, abruptly, both he and it plummet into the abyss. [party.CombatNames] edge forward carefully, alert for any further collapses, and manage to peer over the edge... just in time to see his black dot merge with the rest of the magma below and disappear. "Goddess," Lia gasps. "Is he... there's no way he could've survived that, right?" Well, in your experience, especially given everything that happened in the Rift, demons can take real punishment. They can survive an awful lot of cold, after all; maybe that goes for lava, too. They can shapeshift, they can transform, and as far as you're concerned, unless you see a body, you can't be sure. Actually, given what happened with Gweyr and Leold, maybe you can't even be sure with a body. "Ugh. I think I get it." She nods slowly. "It's strange. He was a demon, he was absolutely insufferable, but... after seeing how he changed after the relic was parted from him, I'm not sure how much of his behavior was actually him. Even without it affecting his mind, someone as obsessive as he was having power of the likes that we saw slip from his grasp would have been a terrible blow. Speaking of which." Yeah. The golden blade continues to glow in her hand as the [party.sizeText] of you back away from the edge, and you can't help but regard it with awe. [var0 |Actually... more than awe. It's... it's really super shiny. Hypnotizing, almost. You really want to just stare at it for a while. Gosh. She must be feeling really gooood. Like super good even. |She managed to save the weapon and purify it: very impressive. How is she feeling after that? ][liaden.poly | You were worried there for a little bit... ] [liaden.poly |She grins reassuringly. "Aw. Thanks for asking. It did take a little out of me... but I think I'm okay." |"It took something out of me," she admits. ] The young paladin breathes in and out slowly, fixes her eyes on the blade, and then manages to make it disappear into its hilt. Even after the golden glow vanishes, she continues to treat the weapon with care, even preciousness. "There was a presence, a want, in here. I don't know where it came from. It certainly isn't anything like the stories from before. It kind of... does what I want it to, now, though. It's calm now. Maybe calm 'again'." [party.has azyrran |Azzy steps forward with alarm. "Are you [azyrran.kdb |sure |certain |suuuuuure ] that's safe[azzy.liaden|, my flower]? What if...?" |Huh. Is that safe? She's not going to end up like your demonic foe, is she? ] Liaden nods. "[party.has azyrran |Thanks, [liaden.poly |you two |sweetie ], but I think ]I've got this — at least for now. But I'm definitely going to want to ask Dad plenty of questions about it when we get back." She pauses, then, with a smile, says, "[liaden.poly |I'm glad the three of us got to do this together. You two had my back, getting us going, fighting off the demon, giving me the chance to rescue the sword |[party.has azyrran |And I have to thank you, too, [pc.name] |Thanks, by the way ]. Thanks for getting us all going on this quest, for fighting off the demon, for giving me the chance to get the blade ]..." Hey, [liaden.poly|what are girlfriends for?|she did as much legwork as you did here.] And she was worthy; you figured the sword would be able to tell, too.[party.has etheryn | "Y[etheryn.lowConfidence |-Y ]eah," Etheryn adds. "You're a great Lumian paladin, Lia. If this really did used to be the sword of Princess Iveryn, I [etheryn.highConfidence |know |think ] she'd be really proud of you for saving it. And of you, [pc.name] — you gave up the chance to take it. M[etheryn.lowConfidence |-M ]aybe you'd have been worthy, too, but you helped Lia instead." It's all good; the sword went to somebody worthy all the same. ] Besides, you got to kick a demon right in the [silly |daddy bags |balls ], and how often does that chance come up? "Hopefully not very often," Liaden laughs. "Well, look. The first thing we should probably do is get back to Hawkethorne. And the second is figure out some way for the Order of the Oriflamme to show their appreciation to the hero[pc.mf | |ine ] who helped return the Dawnsword to us. I feel like being its wielder ought to give me a fair amount of pull, and you deserve more out of all this than a chance to boot a demon in the crotch."[liaden.poly | She winks. "Y'know, apart from the obvious thank-yous a girl like me might wanna give [party.has azyrran |you an' Azzy |a girl like you ]." | ] You won't say no to that. Time to head out, then. "

rows.original: Tell Lia to save the Dawnsword while you defeat the demon. While you won't receive the Dawnsword as a quest reward, you will receive a different enchanted item instead.
rows.translation: 你去打败那个恶魔，让莉亚去拯救晨曦剑吧。虽然你不会通过完成任务来获得“晨曦剑”，但是会反而会收到一件不同的附魔物品。
rows.raw: "Tell Lia to save the Dawnsword while you defeat the demon. While you won't receive the Dawnsword as a quest reward, you will receive a different enchanted item instead."

rows.original: Thankfully, the trip back to Hawkethorne is as uneventful as it is tiring — climbing back out of the sinkhole is the hardest part of it all even with the rope, which is a small mercy.[pc.hasWings | Even someone with wings like you needs a few breaks on your way up. ] Eventually, you emerge into the cool air of the Marches, [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames] following closely behind |your limbs sore from the long climb ]. It's a relief to be able to breathe deep lungfuls of chill Marches air, especially after spending so long close to the sweltering heat so deep under the earth. Wasting no time, you head out of gnoll territory westward to the more familiar sight of homesteads and fields, and from there beat a quick trail straight to Sanders' chapel. [var1 |The man himself is at his usual spot at the altar, and has turned his head before [var0 |you and Liaden have |you've ] even set foot over the threshold. He takes one look at[var0 | the both of ] you, another at the Dawnsword in [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |her |your ] hand, then breathes deeply and gestures for you to take a seat in the pews. |The man himself has retired to the rectory for the night, but that isn't stopping [var0 |Liaden. She produces a small, weathered key, unlocks the door to the living quarters she and her father share, then marches straight up to Sanders' bedroom and starts pounding on the door with a fist. "Dad? Dad! Wake up! I know it's late, but this is really important! We need you up right now!" |you. The entrance to the chapel might be locked, but this isn't just important, it's time-sensitive. Balling a fist, you pound away at the old wood, calling for Sanders loudly enough for your voice to echo in the eaves of the weathered stonework. ] It doesn't take long for the man to show himself — the urgency of your summons combined with the fact that he was probably used to being suddenly awakened during the night in his youth has him at the door in a jiffy. He takes one look at you[var0 | and Liaden ], another at the relic in [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |her |your ] hand, then urges you into the pews, not even bothering to change out of his nightclothes. ] [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |"There it is," he murmurs. A gesture at the gentle golden glow of the Lumian icons on it, still shining faintly even though the blade's not extended: "You certainly found the right sword. And Lia... it chose you —" The old man's voice breaks, just the tiniest bit, and then he pulls his daughter into a powerful hug. "I am so proud of you." When the two of them separate, Lia's first gesture is toward you, with a grateful smile on her face. "Thanks, Dad. It feels amazing, but... I wouldn't have had the chance without [pc.name].[liaden.poly |" He grins and then, to your surprise, embraces you just as firmly. "Oh, [pc.name]. I never imagined I would have a daughter, a brave and valiant Lumian warrior. Now it seems I have two — three, in fact, counting[party.has azyrran | you, ] Azyrran. Thank you so much for being there for each other." Oh! Well[pc.isDK |, | — and here you hug him right back — ] you're glad you were. In fact, you're trying to make a habit of it. Lia's still wearing her own smile as she watches you and her dad disengage from your hug. "She actually took on a demon and told me to go for it. If she hadn't, well, it might be deep in a pool of magma." | [pc.HeShe] took on a demon and told me to go for the sword. Otherwise, it might be deep in a pool of magma." ] |[pc.isDK |Once you're all settled, he takes a closer look at the sword. "I... this looks like the Dawnsword, but I don't remember the sigils and gem being quite like this. Something seems very wrong." Casually, you ignite the blade and let him soak in the weapon's bloody, crimson appearance before closing it down again. As far as you're concerned, it works just fine. "It is the same weapon," he concedes. A worried frown furrows his brow as he speaks. "I... I don't know if you could feel it, but there was a feeling of something almost alive and very hungry when you activated it, and that wasn't there before. The sword... when I wielded it, it had sensations, maybe, a feeling of certainty you could immerse yourself in, but nothing like this. What on earth can have happened to it?" Who knows? It was like this when you got it — won it, actually, by right of conquest when defeating a demon who'd tried to claim it just before you. He was weak, though, and you weren't, which is why you've got the sword now. You're pretty sure it likes you, and if it doesn't, well, your will is stronger anyway. |"There it is," he murmurs. A gesture at the gentle golden glow of the Lumian icons on it, still shining faintly even though the blade's not extended: "You certainly found the right sword. And it chose you — you should be proud, [pc.name]." [var0 |You accept the compliment with the grace you figure a bearer of the sword ought to have. Well — and you say this with an ostentatious eye at Lia[party.has azyrran | and Azzy ] — you know that people claim that opposites attract, but in this case, you don't think that's true at all. "Ha. In that case, I'm very glad you're so alike — and that you're there for each other. Lia, [pc.name], Azzy... all three of you make me so proud." It's not my success at all, it's yours — but I'm happy to have seen it. It feels like I'm around for the beginning of something truly special." Smiling, you return the old man's handshake. You appreciate that, too. He wasn't wrong when he suggested that claiming the sword would involve trials, though. Hell, you ended up having to wrest it from a demon's grasp! ] ] ]

rows.raw: " Thankfully, the trip back to Hawkethorne is as uneventful as it is tiring — climbing back out of the sinkhole is the hardest part of it all even with the rope, which is a small mercy.[pc.hasWings | Even someone with wings like you needs a few breaks on your way up. ] Eventually, you emerge into the cool air of the Marches, [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames] following closely behind |your limbs sore from the long climb ]. It's a relief to be able to breathe deep lungfuls of chill Marches air, especially after spending so long close to the sweltering heat so deep under the earth. Wasting no time, you head out of gnoll territory westward to the more familiar sight of homesteads and fields, and from there beat a quick trail straight to Sanders' chapel. [var1 |The man himself is at his usual spot at the altar, and has turned his head before [var0 |you and Liaden have |you've ] even set foot over the threshold. He takes one look at[var0 | the both of ] you, another at the Dawnsword in [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |her |your ] hand, then breathes deeply and gestures for you to take a seat in the pews. |The man himself has retired to the rectory for the night, but that isn't stopping [var0 |Liaden. She produces a small, weathered key, unlocks the door to the living quarters she and her father share, then marches straight up to Sanders' bedroom and starts pounding on the door with a fist. "Dad? Dad! Wake up! I know it's late, but this is really important! We need you up right now!" |you. The entrance to the chapel might be locked, but this isn't just important, it's time-sensitive. Balling a fist, you pound away at the old wood, calling for Sanders loudly enough for your voice to echo in the eaves of the weathered stonework. ] It doesn't take long for the man to show himself — the urgency of your summons combined with the fact that he was probably used to being suddenly awakened during the night in his youth has him at the door in a jiffy. He takes one look at you[var0 | and Liaden ], another at the relic in [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |her |your ] hand, then urges you into the pews, not even bothering to change out of his nightclothes. ] [flags.LIADEN_LIGHTSABER |"There it is," he murmurs. A gesture at the gentle golden glow of the Lumian icons on it, still shining faintly even though the blade's not extended: "You certainly found the right sword. And Lia... it chose you —" The old man's voice breaks, just the tiniest bit, and then he pulls his daughter into a powerful hug. "I am so proud of you." When the two of them separate, Lia's first gesture is toward you, with a grateful smile on her face. "Thanks, Dad. It feels amazing, but... I wouldn't have had the chance without [pc.name].[liaden.poly |" He grins and then, to your surprise, embraces you just as firmly. "Oh, [pc.name]. I never imagined I would have a daughter, a brave and valiant Lumian warrior. Now it seems I have two — three, in fact, counting[party.has azyrran | you, ] Azyrran. Thank you so much for being there for each other." Oh! Well[pc.isDK |, | — and here you hug him right back — ] you're glad you were. In fact, you're trying to make a habit of it. Lia's still wearing her own smile as she watches you and her dad disengage from your hug. "She actually took on a demon and told me to go for it. If she hadn't, well, it might be deep in a pool of magma." | [pc.HeShe] took on a demon and told me to go for the sword. Otherwise, it might be deep in a pool of magma." ] |[pc.isDK |Once you're all settled, he takes a closer look at the sword. "It is the same weapon," he concedes. A worried frown furrows his brow as he speaks. "I... I don't know if you could feel it, but there was a feeling of something almost alive and very hungry when you activated it, and that wasn't there before. The sword... when I wielded it, it had sensations, maybe, a feeling of certainty you could immerse yourself in, but nothing like this. What on earth can have happened to it?" Who knows? It was like this when you got it — won it, actually, by right of conquest when defeating a demon who'd tried to claim it just before you. rows.original: As you step into the town square, you immediately notice the large crowd that's gathered about the statue[dayNight |. Something must be up for just about everyone in the village to be here and, well, that something becomes quite apparent soon: a pair of horse-riding paladins in literal shining armor. Their breastplates gleam [dayNight |with the brilliance of the reflected sun, resplendent in all its glory |even in the wan light of the moon, turning silver into gold ], and emblazoned upon their tabards is the symbol of a radiant flame, a sunflame, and once you see that... well, it doesn't take you long to figure out who they are. If your memory wasn't up to the task, though, River comes bounding up to remind you; the wide-eyed, excited kitten nimbly grabs you by the arm before you've even got time to react. "Hey! Hey! [pc.name], I don't think it's just me singing your praises anymore, not with big shots like these two showing up! Paladins of the Oriflamme the both of them, and they said they rode hard to get here. They've been all over town looking for you[silly| — well, not really, but c'mon, there's only so many places we can use to trigger these events]. They were with Sanders and Liaden, up to the castle, you name it... and when they came back here, they seemed antsy that they hadn't managed to locate you yet. I tried to reassure them that you'd be around eventually and, well, here you are!" You tell the kitten to slow down and take a breath. [pc.isDK |That's a lot of fuckin' words, and you want a little time to digest them first — and get a look at these paladins. Once you've given them the old once-over, you ask him whether they've been getting uppity or anything. |Even for someone like him who sings for a living and has pipes to spare, that's a lot of words in a very short time. They've been pretty restrained with their questions, and once they realized they'd have to wait for you to show up, they mostly just settled down to take care of their horses. As for the crowd, well, we're just here to get a decent look. Other than you and your friends and maybe those Tronarii folk, nobody this interesting's been to town in years." [pc.isDK |Ah, good. So you are going to get paid. Time to stop fucking around, then. |That bodes well. [pc.swornGod lumia |At the pause, he genuflects to you, as does the sister further back. "It's an honor to meet you, my lady. |He smiles faintly. We are here to reward you for service rendered — to an Order that usually prefers it the other way 'round. The Dawnsword, lost these twenty years, is once again in the hands of one of our own, and apparently rescued from a very grim fate. With his golden gauntlet, Brother Bastille gestures grandiloquently toward the chapel's steps, where the father-daughter pair stand, waving at you. "We have conferenced with both of them, and all is well." So there's no issue with Liaden being Sanders' daughter, or anything...? Baranian?[silly | no, French ] — accent really comes out when he says Sanders' first name, doesn't it? rows.raw: " As you step into the town square, you immediately notice the large crowd that's gathered about the statue[dayNight |. It's a little surprising to see so many people over here, rather than at the marketplace, especially at a time like this; not even River usually draws this much of a crowd[var1 |, and nobody here can use the Waystones except you ] | — especially odd given the time of night ]. Something must be up for just about everyone in the village to be here and, well, that something becomes quite apparent soon: a pair of horse-riding paladins in literal shining armor. Their breastplates gleam [dayNight |with the brilliance of the reflected sun, resplendent in all its glory |even in the wan light of the moon, turning silver into gold ], and emblazoned upon their tabards is the symbol of a radiant flame, a sunflame, and once you see that... well, it doesn't take you long to figure out who they are. If your memory wasn't up to the task, though, River comes bounding up to remind you; the wide-eyed, excited kitten nimbly grabs you by the arm before you've even got time to react. "Hey! Hey! [pc.name], I don't think it's just me singing your praises anymore, not with big shots like these two showing up! Paladins of the Oriflamme the both of them, and they said they rode hard to get here. They've been all over town looking for you[silly| — well, not really, but c'mon, there's only so many places we can use to trigger these events]. They were with Sanders and Liaden, up to the castle, you name it... and when they came back here, they seemed antsy that they hadn't managed to locate you yet. I tried to reassure them that you'd be around eventually and, well, here you are!" You tell the kitten to slow down and take a breath. [pc.isDK |That's a lot of fuckin' words, and you want a little time to digest them first — and get a look at these paladins. Once you've given them the old once-over, you ask him whether they've been getting uppity or anything. |Even for someone like him who sings for a living and has pipes to spare, that's a lot of words in a very short time. While he does that, you cast a weather eye over the paladins, then follow up with a question: that antsiness hasn't caused any problems, right? ] "No," he says bemusedly. "Does it look like it? They've been pretty restrained with their questions, and once they realized they'd have to wait for you to show up, they mostly just settled down to take care of their horses. As for the crowd, well, we're just here to get a decent look. Other than you and your friends and maybe those Tronarii folk, nobody this interesting's been to town in years." [pc.isDK |Ah, good. So you are going to get paid. Time to stop fucking around, then. |That bodes well. You're [pc.name], [pc.title]. [pc.isDK |They're here to see you, yes? |You don't suppose they're looking for you, are they? ] The paladins look at each other, then turn to you. One of them approaches, acknowledging you with a small nod, then removes his helmet — huh. A[pc.ra sheepfolk | fellow ] sheepfolk, as it turns out. "My name is Brother Bastille Shen and over there is Sister Joan Blanchet; we both hail from the Order of the Oriflamme. We've ridden hard from the Baranian chapter to meet you." [pc.swornGod lumia |At the pause, he genuflects to you, as does the sister further back. "It's an honor to meet you, my lady. |He smiles faintly. " ]Forgive the late arrival and the, mmm, confusion when searching for you; it has been some time since any of us has ventured up here to the roof of the world, as we call it. We're not exactly familiar with the area." [pc.isDK |Fine, whatever |That's all right ][silly |; it's not like they were able to text you the details of the meetup or anything |. A [pc.manWoman] like you might be anywhere in the Marches at any given time ]. You're here now, though. There's a bit of a guess percolating in your mind about why they're here, but if they wouldn't mind confirming it... "Of course. We are here to reward you for service rendered — to an Order that usually prefers it the other way 'round. The Dawnsword, lost these twenty years, is once again in the hands of one of our own, and apparently rescued from a very grim fate. Such a thing was very relieving to hear, even if some of our members initially blanched at the thought that our somewhat delinquent former comrade had already promised you a reward on our behalf. Sister Liaden's words, though, went rather farther to assuage those feelings[pc.swornGod lumia |, as the revelation of who you were ]." With his golden gauntlet, Brother Bastille gestures grandiloquently toward the chapel's steps, where the father-daughter pair stand, waving at you. "We have conferenced with both of them, and all is well." So there's no issue with Liaden being Sanders' daughter, or anything...? "Brother Riordan's actions two decades past did not sit well with everybody," he concedes. The — Yvennese? Baranian?[silly | no, French ] — accent really comes out when he says Sanders' first name, doesn't it? "One of the other sisters of the chapter was convinced that he was simply saving it for his daughter, and sent her off to it at the first opportunity. But our commander is seasoned enough..." "Old enough," chuckles Sister Joan from behind her helmet. "... old enough to have personal memories of his former comrade's integrity. Besides, we understand that he didn't even know his daughter existed until a short while ago. He can hardly have been saving it for someone he knew nothing of. At any rate, now that we're here, Sister Joan has seen the echoes of your struggle in the enchantment of the blade, and neither of us can deny that Liaden did prove worthy of it. That is the end of that. Or rather, we hope," he amends, casting a glance at his sister-in-arms on the chapel's steps, "a beginning to a long and fruitful career in Lumia's service. "But she has been congratulated in her turn. This gathering is for you." He nods to Joan, who withdraws a lacquered wooden casket from one of her saddlebags. "Liaden insists that you had a chance to claim the blade if you desired such, yet voluntarily sacrificed it. That sort of temptation is not the thing most can resist lightly. We believed that this gift would be appropriate for a [pc.manWoman] who has given up so much." With both hands, the sister opens the casket and presents its contents to you. Lying within the velveted interior is a small golden ring, but not a plain one; small curved spokes emerge along one side, a mirror of the icon on the paladins' armor. "Not quite a sword," she says, "but still quite powerful." You lift the golden ring out of the sun-carved casket, and Joan withdraws with a small bow. It feels heavy in your hand, heavier than it would've been even if it were solid gold. More than that, you can sense a thrum of power coming not just from the holy symbol of Lumia embossed along the top but from the runes etched along the inside as well — and that kind of power instinctively gives[pc.swornGod lumia | even a valkyrie like you ] pause. "The Guldring was formed from a sunshard in ages past, long before the Godswar; much like the Dawnsword, it's been passed down from one generation of the Order to the next." The sheepfolk's voice takes on a deeper timber, more intonation than speech, as he explains the artifact just bestowed upon you. "It may not have the same degree of symbolism and majesty as the Dawnsword does, but our commander insists that for anyone who conjures divine cleansing flames of their own, it is arguably more useful.[silly | And for someone who gave up a melee weapon, we figured a magical artifact would be reasonably appropriate. ] Hopefully you find it as appropriate a gift as we do, [pc.title]." "And hopefully more of our brothers and sisters will be able to fight by your side as you wear it," adds Sister Joan. "Or [pc.swornGod lumia |perhaps even your sisters. And, you know, if that's not your style, maybe you could marry someone with it |you know what? It looks more than nice enough to marry someone with ]." Marry someone, hmm? [brienne.married |She giggles, then flashes her own finger-bling. "Well, maybe someone else. I wouldn't trade this ring for the world. |"It is!" She flutters her eyelashes. "Although with the way the paladins described it, using it as a plain wedding ring would be a waste. Flattering! But a terrible waste. ]" [brienne.married |Awww. |True, true. ] She can hold it for a little while anyway. You pass the ring over to Brienne, and she runs her fingers along the edge, thinking to herself far more pensively than before; at length, her eyes widen, and she gives you a solemn nod. "Huh. Well, that's something. Yeah, you really wouldn't use this as a wedding ring. It's special in a different way." It certainly is. Those paladins certainly weren't kidding when they talked it up as a worthy reward for giving up the Dawnsword. |"Wow, that's pretty old," Atugia says, coming up to your side to study the ring. "Looks authentic, too." She knows? "Oh, Carmen's got a couple pieces like that locked away in some storeroom or the other, I'm pretty sure. Her dad loved collectin' antiques, and while Carmen didn't share that enthusiasm you don't just throw out your dad's stuff without thinkin', you know? It's not like there's any lack of space in the castle to put stuff like that. None of them were magical or anything like this one is and they were round instead of this funny shape, but the make's otherwise the same." Not that you were even considering the possibility that the paladins were going to pull a fast one on you, but it's good to know that there're other period pieces like this. "I'm not one for rings and their like, but if it's of any practical use then it's got to be at least a little magical. Looks kind of uncomfortable to wear, to be honest. Wouldn't the spikes keep pricking your other fingers? I wouldn't risk that kind of distraction in a fight, although I guess if you wore it all the time you might get used to it." |"Why, what a lovely period piece," [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ] purrs as she sashays forward and takes it in both hands for inspection. "Excellent workmanship, if I may say so — artifacts like these belong in a museum where everyone can appreciate their beauty and history. Of course, since there are no museums around for the gods know how far, it would appear that the ring is all yours, beloved." You really can't tell if she's being facetious here or not... "But I am being completely serious, am I not? The risk one runs in using a powerful relic, of course, is that of it being lost like your lovely Dawnsword was. Of course, in the long run that's not a problem; relics like these have a habit of turning up at the most convenient times — throw this ring into the ocean, beloved, and in a hundred years it will wash up on the shore to be found by some lucky fool. But since the paladins have been kind to present it to you as recompense for keeping their precious thing within the grasp of their order, we should make the most of this opportunity, should we not?" She's dissembling. When Kiyoko dissembles, she's really trying to say something that she'd rather not voice out loud. [kiyoko.married |Your fox-wife raises a dainty hand to her cheek. "Me? Dissemble and talk in circles? Over a trinket? Ah, have we been married so long already that you are able to pierce my words and decipher their hidden meaning? Ah, we truly have become so close in so short a time, my beloved |Kiyoko raises a dainty hand to her cheek. "Me? Dissemble and talk in circles? Over a Lumian trinket? Maybe I am. Maybe I am not. Wouldn't it be fun to figure out the difference? Or maybe I am just happy that your efforts are recognized, beloved ]. Come then, perhaps we will go on further adventures and give you an opportunity to try out your new toy, shall we not?" |Viviane hums idly while the crowd starts to disperse, and once you've got something close to privacy, she says, "Well. They weren't lying, you know. That ring's definitely from before the Godswar. Or, at least, in the style of it... but while fabricating a ring in the manner of the ancients isn't that difficult, endowing it with an enchantment like they once did is far harder. And this has a flame enchantment I've never seen before. May I?" Right, enchantments. That's her specialty, after all. You yield the Guldring into Viviane's careful hands. "They did say it had a storied history," she continues. The runes on the interior are what she focuses on most of all, and for several seconds her lips move silently, trying to get a handle on whatever ancient script and language they're written in. "Ah. Aha. Yes, definitely older." Is there something about the runes that makes it impossible to be a recent creation? "Yeah. The grammar's changed. We don't write like this anymore." Viv winks cheekily. "But yes, it's definitely much older than the Godswar in terms of enchantment, too, and the spiritual energy is... well, it's not exactly counting tree rings, but it just feels old, you know? Almost primordial." [pc.bg arcanist scholar |Come to think of it, you do know. You bring your hand close to the ring, concentrate on the energy, and... yep. This isn't anything like any of the artifacts you handled during your studies, let alone most of the things you've seen in your travels around the Marches. |You'll have to take her word for that. ] "So old... you know, now I'm curious about the rest of the story. What is a sunshard? Is it part of the binding, or just decorative — or just a word for a very old Lumian relic?" Sounds like a topic for further research. "Or a painfully tantalizing mystery. With my luck, I'll be down the[silly | archival ] rabbit hole for weeks, only to run into a dead end. Still: I think I'd like to trace out the runes[viv.isDemon | on this... precious thing ] next time we have a down moment, if I could. Might as well, you know? And then after that we can gather other data! Ideally we'll do it by using the ring to torch somebody who really ought to know better." |"Well, what a pretty piece," Agni says, whistling as she comes up to you to take stock of your new acquisition. "You don't see gold with that kind of luster anymore. That's how you know it's authentic." Was there a lot more of this sort of thing around back in her day? In one of her previous lives? "I... I think so. In one of my past lives, I was married with a ring much like this. Or at least, unless my memory's playing tricks on me..." Nah, you believe her. That, and it's not that big of a deal if she's misremembering. "Phew. Right, anyway. I don't know why exactly you don't see it that much these days, but sometime in the last century or so things gradually phased out over about a decade. Don't get me wrong, the old gold wasn't necessarily better — if anything, I think the stuff we have today is prettier — but it's a reasonable way to date pieces from the heartlands." Ah. Well, it's good to have her around to comment on your new gift, then. Even if her memory is spotty in some places, Agni always manages to surprise you with some piece of relevant trivia or the other at opportune times. "You're welcome." |You feel a presence draw close, and then Quin's peering over your shoulder at Guldring, his gaze boring into the ring's decor. "Hmm. Shiny." He doesn't sound impressed, but then, he's a somewhat understated guy. "I am impressed. You beat up a demon and got rewarded with a ring that lets you... what, set them on fire? Even better." Quin folds his arms and quirks a corner of his mouth upwards. "Whatever it does, it's just like Lumians to make their gifts all literally flashy. You should really test it out when you have the chance, just to see if you like it or not." Sure, thanks. "Yeah, no problem. Hey, worst comes to worst and it doesn't set Cult jerks on fire, it does make for a nice piece to wave in somebody's face if they're making problems for you." |[azyrran.kdb |"Oooh," Azyrran hums. "It's the color of honey! What a nice, shiny gold. And it's even got Lumia's sunburst on the side, too. What's that called? Relief? No, embossing! That's it." And enchanted, too, from the sound of things. Those runes on the inside glow even more than the rest of it. A fire enchantment, was it? "It'd be appropriate for those in Lumia's service, or those who use a lot of fire magic," the Hive Knight agrees. "And because it's, you know, holy, it's probably good for those in the habit of kicking demons in the balls, too. Not that either of us," she continues, winking, "knows anybody like that." [pc.isDK |Hah. Speaking of that, how's Lia doing with the sword you helped get her |No indeed. Speaking of, how's Lia taking to her new weapon ]? The mention of [azzy.liaden |her [var4 |other |paladin ] girlfriend |the Dawnsword's new bearer ] sends Azzy into a fiery blush. "She's... she's doing great. Practicing hard, you know? And she's standing taller, smiling broader[azzy.liaden |, going so much harder in bed ] — I — I m-mean, she's really something, [pc.name]. I'm glad she got the chance to prove her worth. I'm glad you gave it to her, too! You're wonderful, you know that?" |"Would you look at that," Azyrran says quietly. She leans down for a closer look at the ring, patting you on the shoulder in the process. "They really went all out for you, didn't they? Honey-bright gold, a Lumian symbol, some magical runes... that's really nice, [pc.name]. You should be proud." Those magical effects aren't just for show, of course. "Doesn't look like it. Probably fire magic, you know, what with the whole Lumia thing. Wouldn't mind seeing you make use of that — stand back a bit and hurl some fireballs while I keep anybody from getting to. You know how much [azyrran.fucked |it means to me, keeping my cute [pc.name] safe |I like to mix it up in close combat ]." You[azyrran.fucked | — whew, you ] definitely do. Something to try out, then. Speaking of [azyrran.fucked |members of her little harem getting used to their new gear |Lumians and holy enchanted equipment ], how's Lia doing with the Dawnsword? "Oh, she's adorable. You should drop by one of our little training things sometime." Azzy grins. "She's really taken to the whole thing. It's not just the fighting, either; her whole demeanor's changed. She's standing up straighter, smiling more broadly.[azzy.liaden | Hasn't stopped being a cute blushy sweetheart in bed, but I like her like that. ] You did a good thing, dear, helping [azzy.liaden |my little flower |her ] grow into her own." |The Hive Knight next to you bends down for a closer look. "Gosh, that's a cute ring. And it's really really Lumian, too! I think it makes it look that much prettier. What do you think? Does it make up for helping Lia?" You'll have to see how it performs in combat first, but at the moment, it doesn't seem too bad. "Awww, that's good!" Azzy sighs with relief and drapes her arms around your shoulders. "I was really worried — both of you should be as happy as possible with all this." That's very sweet of her... which is kind of her thing, isn't it? "Yipyup!" Still leaning close to you, she whispers conspiratorially: "We've been practicing with the sword already. She's already getting super good with it. And she's even more friendly and standing up straighter[azzy.liaden | and she is way hornier, I mean, wow, ] and just, like... it's all meant so much to her. Hopefully that's a little bit of payment for you too!" ] All's well that ends well, then. |"Damn," Arona says. She peers at the Guldring and lets out a long, low whistle. "A whole-ass ring." Sarcasm? She rolls her eyes. "I mean, yeah, but also no. Okay, it's tiny. Okay, it looks like magic bullshit. Okay, it's not a fuckin' flame sword, which, by the way, I think you're crazy for giving up. But a shiny Lumia ring ain't half bad." Which half of that was the more important to her? Shiny or Lumia? "Shiny's nice, but it doesn't do as much for me if it's in your hands, [arona.isSub |boss |beta bitch ]. Look, you picked up one of my goddess's holy relics and it's cool. Don't make any more out of it than that." Then a clever light comes into her blue eyes. "[arona.fucked |Then again... you know what Lumia's all about. You think that ring's just for fucking people up? Or you think it gives a little more oomph to breeding, too?" You're not sure about that. [var6 |The two of you are already expecting, though. What more help could she possibly need? [arona.isSub |"It's not about help, it's about more. C'mon," she says, patting [var7 |her |your ] belly. "You don't mind making this little orclet-to-be a big brother or sister a little further down the track, do you?" |She snorts. "I don't need help. I just want more. If you thought you had plans for the next few years..." ] |But, ah, it sounds like she wants more kids. [arona.isSub |"I mean, yeah? Was that news? Whenever you've got the time." |She snorts. "Damn straight I do." ] |Might be worth finding out sometime. [arona.isSub |"Hey, you know who's always up for shit like that." |Her big, meaty hand comes down hard on your shoulder. "You say that like you've got a choice." ] ] |Then again... y'know, I wonder if that does the other shit Lumia's known for. Maybe I could borrow it, show it to Hretha, see if she can figure out all the magic on it." And then what, keep it on during white week? "Did you have a better idea?" ] |"Wow," Ryn breathes. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |M-May |Do you mind if ] I take a look?" Yeah, that's fine. You bet she'd get a kick out of a genuine Lumian relic — well, another one. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |Th-thank you. |Thank you. |I would! Thank you. ]" Once it's in her hands, she runs her finger carefully over the sun-flare embossing, examines the runes on the inside closely, and even hefts it briefly in her hand, just like you did; she notices the weight, too. "Wow. It's something so simple-looking, but still... I've n[etheryn.lowConfidence |-n ]ever seen anything like it before. We've made plenty of Lumian art and even use this pattern, but we don't put it on rings, and the runes are so strange. We didn't even make these in Grandmother's time, I don't think." Just goes to show how diverse [pc.swornGod lumia |your |her ] goddess's worship is. People from all over the continent, making art and jewelry for the rest of the faithful in their own way. "I'd love to meet more of them," she says quietly. Between making diplomatic visits to lands in the south and receiving embassies from them at the Winter City, she'll probably be able to do just that. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I c-can't even imagine. Being a queen, m-meeting diplomats... that doesn't really sound like me. But m-maybe. |That's a nice thought. Just have to get to that point first, I guess! ]" Ryn hands the Guldring back to you, as carefully as when she took it. "It's a lovely gift. I think it just goes to show how much you gave up when you told Liaden to rescue the sword, and how much that sacrifice meant to them. They didn't j[etheryn.lowConfidence |-j ]ust loan the ring to you; they gave it. Wow. [pc.swornGod lumia |Then again... I guess it's only fair for Lumia's own Champion. If I didn't already have an idea about how southerners feel about valkyries, I do now. |If I had any doubts about how southern Lumians felt about hero[pc.mf | |in ]es like you, I don't anymore. ]" [var5 |Teasingly, you ask: what about her? How does she feel about people like you? "You know already!" she giggles delightedly. |Yeah. As far as good guys go, the Oriflamme warriors seem to be pretty high up there. ] ] One way or another, this should be the end of that little saga. It's been a long and bumpy road over years to get here, if you include both Sanders' and Gweyr's pasts as part of the story, but hopefully the final loose thread has been tied up.[silly | For good now. Definitely nothing else left to handle from this particular situation. You're all done. Completely. ] A job well done, as it were... "

rows.original:
As you step into the town square, you immediately notice the large crowd that's gathered about the statue[dayNight
        |. It's a little surprising to see so many people over here, rather than at the marketplace, especially at a time like this; not even River usually draws this much of a crowd
rows.translation:
当你踏入镇广场时，立刻注意到雕像周围聚集了一大群人[dayNight
        |。看到这么多人聚在这里，而不是在市场那边，多少有点让人意外，尤其是在这种时候；就连瑞弗通常也吸引不了这么多人
rows.raw: "\n    As you step into the town square, you immediately notice the large crowd that's gathered about the statue[dayNight\n        |. It's a little surprising to see so many people over here, rather than at the marketplace, especially at a time like this; not even River usually draws this much of a crowd"

rows.original: | — especially odd given the time of night ]. Something must be up for just about everyone in the village to be here and, well, that something becomes quite apparent soon: a pair of horse-riding paladins in literal shining armor. Their breastplates gleam [dayNight |with the brilliance of the reflected sun, resplendent in all its glory |even in the wan light of the moon, turning silver into gold ], and emblazoned upon their tabards is the symbol of a radiant flame, a sunflame, and once you see that... well, it doesn't take you long to figure out who they are. If your memory wasn't up to the task, though, River comes bounding up to remind you; the wide-eyed, excited kitten nimbly grabs you by the arm before you've even got time to react. "Hey! Hey! [pc.name], I don't think it's just me singing your praises anymore, not with big shots like these two showing up! Paladins of the Oriflamme the both of them, and they said they rode hard to get here. They've been all over town looking for you[silly| — well, not really, but c'mon, there's only so many places we can use to trigger these events]. They were with Sanders[liaden.atChapel | and Liaden ], up to the castle, you name it... and when they came back here, they seemed antsy that they hadn't managed to locate you yet. I tried to reassure them that you'd be around eventually and, well, here you are!" You tell the kitten to slow down and take a breath. [pc.isDK |That's a lot of fuckin' words, and you want a little time to digest them first — and get a look at these paladins. Once you've given them the old once-over, you ask him whether they've been getting uppity or anything. |Even for someone like him who sings for a living and has pipes to spare, that's a lot of words in a very short time. While he does that, you cast a weather eye over the paladins, then follow up with a question: that antsiness hasn't caused any problems, right? ] "No," he says bemusedly. "Does it look like it? They've been pretty restrained with their questions, and once they realized they'd have to wait for you to show up, they mostly just settled down to take care of their horses. As for the crowd, well, we're just here to get a decent look. Other than you and your friends and maybe those Tronarii folk, nobody this interesting's been to town in years." [flags.DARK_LIGHTSABER |Ah. Order of the Oriflamme, eh? They must be here to take a look at your sweet glowstick. Well, you don't mind showing it off for them. |Oh, okay. Well, if they're from the Order of the Oriflamme, you can only imagine that they're here to talk about the Dawnsword. Might as well, right? ] You [pc.hasWings |haven't got much of a chance of pushing through the crowd quickly, not when they're goggling at the Lumian warriors, but that's not a concern for someone like you. With the aid of your [pc.wings], you swoop over the onlookers, do a brief flourish in the air, and alight before |push through the throng — everybody's staring at the warriors, so they don't exactly think to part for you when you approach from behind — then come up to ] the pair of them with confidence and an easy smile. You're [pc.name], [pc.title]. They're here to see you, right? The paladins look at each other, then turn to you. One of them approaches, acknowledging you with a small nod, then removes his helmet — huh. A[pc.ra sheepfolk | fellow ] sheepfolk, as it turns out. "My name is Brother Bastille Shen[pc.swornGod lumia |, my lady ]. Over there is Sister Joan Blanchet. We both hail from the Order of the Oriflamme, and we've ridden hard from the Baranian chapter to meet you." [pc.swornGod lumia |He pauses, then solemnly genuflects before you, as does the still-helmeted sister further back. "It's an honor to meet the Champion of Lumia herself. |He offers you a faint, but quite real, smile, and a nod of respect. " ]We must offer an apology; we would have liked to have been here sooner, but it has been some time since any of us has ventured up here to the roof of the world, as we call it. Even though there is no closer chapter than Barania[liaden.atChapel | — save the one Sister Liaden has established here, of course — |, ] we're not exactly familiar with the area." [flags.DARK_LIGHTSABER |It's no skin off your nose if they think they're late. You certainly weren't expecting them. What exactly do they think they're late for, anyway? The paladin grimaces and rubs his nose. "We've had many tidings from this land of late. One of them is that the Dawnsword, lost these twenty years, has finally been found. Rescued from a... well, what [liaden.atChapel |Sister Liaden |Brother Riordan ] names a 'demon', even if apparently different from the Wraithkin I and my sworn brothers and sisters are used to. We came here to see for ourselves that the sword was safe and to congratulate its new bearer. Apparently, that [pc.manWoman] is you." Damn straight it is. Without waiting for the paladin to request proof, you provide it: the still-corrupted blade, Lumian engravings dark and glowing crimson. Casually, you activate it, and Hawkethorne's streets glow red. You bask in the shocked gasps from the onlookers as the powerful sword twists and twirls through the air, then as abruptly as you brought it to life, you close down the blade, presenting it to Bastille fully inert. "Well." He breathes in sharply. "That is not the way the Dawnsword was when it was last with our Order, but it is the same sword. Of that I have no doubt. It was corrupted by this demon, then?" Seems that way. You can still use it just fine — better than fine, actually. He's not going to start something about that, is he? Bastille's brow furrows. "No, certainly not. The sword, even in this condition, chose you, and that is simply that. Brother Riordan, I am sure, has already described how important it will be to cleanse it, and how one might go about doing so. Until then, though, if it is usable..." Despite the worried look on his face, he musters a shrug. "This land seems overrun by more demons than the one that crossed blades with you, and a wounded blade does as much against them as does a whole one." So people outside the Marches have finally noticed the demons, huh? "Slowly. Too slowly. I'm sure you've figured out that Sister Joan and I are some of the advance scouts, so to speak. In part, of course, we are here to congratulate you, but confirming the nature of the threat, what it means... those were some of our other purposes. That part, though, we have already done. How long it will take to set everything in motion, I cannot say, but thanks to us and a few others serving other codes and other gods, our Order and a dozen others have learned of the demons here." He can't say how long it'll take? "Marshaling warriors takes time. Settling affairs, marching... it will be many months before a host from the south can reach up here." This time Sister Joan speaks up, metallic behind her helmet. "We're getting here as fast as we can. But by the time we arrive, if there are still demons to fight, things are going to be grim." "Hence," Bastille adds, "why it's a good thing that you have the Dawnsword. Even in that state, it will serve well against those demons — certainly far better than it would have served in their hands." Huh. Okay then. Well, you don't mind if they hang around fucking the Cult up, but they'd better not get in your way. The ovine paladin opens his mouth as if to say something else, then thinks better of it, closing it again and cocking his head in a gesture of supreme self-control. Good for him. "Very well," he finally manages. "Just — do be careful, [pc.name]. Warrior's luck to you, and Lumia's light too, if you seek it." With that, the two paladins and their horses depart, and gradually, so too do the townsfolk. You're left in Hawkethorne's square with your sword and fewer questions than when you arrived. Right, then: time to stop wasting time and get back into the swing of things. |That's all right. You weren't exactly waiting for them or anything, so they've got nothing to apologize for. The paladin grins. "That's very gracious of you[pc.swornGod lumia |, my lady ]. Then to business, I suppose. We've had many tidings from this land of late. Some of them are disturbing, but to hear that the Dawnsword had been found — rescued from what [liaden.atChapel|Sister Liaden|Brother Riordan] names a 'demon', no less — was quite the bright light in the gloom. [pc.swornGod lumia |We should perhaps have expected that the woman Lumia named her Chosen would have been the one to do |You're quite the [pc.manWoman] to have done ] something so heroic." Now it's your turn to tell them that they're being gracious. Would they like to see the sword? "If we might — and at your convenience," Bastille says. Not a problem. You show them the hilt, to an audible gasp from the paladins, then, clearing a space in the middle of the crowd, you tease a little bit of your will into the blade. With its usual actinic flash, it ignites, and the broken hilt extends into a full golden blade to the oohs and aahs of all the collected onlookers — and then, after a brief pause, the square erupts in cheers. [var1 |It's just... it's sooo pretty that you just can't stop staring at it for a long, long time, but eventually you remember that (oops!) you actually were just showing it off, and reluctantly turn the super sparkly sunny sword into just a regular ol' hilt again. |A few careful moves through the air, without seeking to harm paladins or horses or people, suffice to prove the point and then, with a fresh exertion of will, you close the blade down and hold it up in your open palm. ] "There it is," breathes Sister Joan, sounding rather metallic through her helmet. "Indeed." Bastille bows again. "You truly are the worthy bearer of the Dawnsword. We can return to our fellows with good news — and leave you with our congratulations." You return the sword to your
rows.translation: |——考虑到现在是夜里，这就更奇怪了 ]。一定是出了什么事，村里几乎所有人才会聚到这里；而且，很快你就看清了那件事：两名骑马的圣武士，穿着字面意义上闪闪发光的铠甲。她们的胸甲[dayNight |反射着太阳的辉光，灿烂夺目 |即使在淡淡月光下，也把银色映成了金色 ]，外袍上则饰有一团辉耀火焰、一轮日焰的标志。你一看到那个标志……好吧，你很快就明白她们是谁了。 就算你的记忆一时没跟上，瑞弗也蹦蹦跳跳地跑来提醒你；这只睁大眼睛、兴奋不已的小猫在你还没来得及反应前，就灵巧地抓住了你的手臂。“嘿！嘿！[pc.name]，我觉得现在不只是我在唱你的赞歌了，连这种大人物都来了！她们两个都是圣焰骑士团的圣武士，而且她们说自己一路疾驰赶来。她们在镇上到处找你[silly|——好吧，也不是真的到处，但拜托，能触发这些事件的地方也就这么几个]。她们和桑德斯[liaden.atChapel | 还有莉娅登 ]一起待过，也去过城堡，能去的都去了……等她们回到这里时，看上去因为还没能找到你而有些焦躁。我试着安慰她们，说你迟早会出现，然后，瞧，你这不就来了嘛！” 你让这只小猫慢一点，先喘口气。[pc.isDK |这他妈是一大堆话，你想先花点时间消化一下——顺便打量这些圣武士。等你把她们上下看过一遍后，你问他她们有没有摆架子或者惹出什么事。 看起来是这样。你仍然能用它，用得还挺好——其实是非常好。他不会因此找茬吧？ Bastille 皱起眉。“不，当然不会。这把剑即使处于这种状态，也选择了你，事情就是如此。Riordan 修士，我相信，已经向你说明过净化它有多重要，以及可能该如何去做。不过在那之前，如果它还能使用……”尽管脸上仍有忧色，他还是勉强耸了耸肩。“这片土地似乎被比与你交锋的那一个更多的恶魔所侵扰；而一把受伤的剑，对付它们时也和完整的剑一样有用。” 所以 Marches 之外的人终于注意到恶魔了，是吧？ “慢慢地。太慢了。我想你已经看出来，Joan 修女和我算是先遣侦察的一部分。当然，我们来这里一方面是为了祝贺你，但确认威胁的性质、确认这意味着什么……也是我们的其他目的之一。而那部分，我们已经完成了。我不能说还要多久才能让一切运转起来，但多亏了我们以及其他侍奉不同准则和神祇的人，我们骑士团以及其他十几个组织都已经得知这里有恶魔。” 他不能说要多久？ “集结战士需要时间。安顿事务，行军……南方的军势要抵达这里，恐怕还需要许多个月。” 这时 Joan 修女开口了，声音从头盔后传出，带着金属感。“我们会尽快赶来。但等我们抵达时，如果还有恶魔要打，局势恐怕会很严峻。” “因此，”Bastille 接着说，“幸好你拥有晨曦剑。即使处于那种状态，它也能很好地对抗那些恶魔——至少远比落在它们手里要好。” 嗯。好吧。你不介意她们留下来狠狠干翻 Cult，但她们最好别挡你的路。
