rows.original:
[oma.freedomWishedFor
        |You ask Oma if she’d like to have a talk.
        
        At the question, she takes a long, drawn-out sigh through her nose. She tilts her head back, closes her eyes, and a wide smile spreads across her lips. "It’s wonderful that you’d ask," she replies. "I’d love to. I’d love nothing more than to talk. I’d love to choose to stop talking. I love that I can choose not to talk."
        
        You’re... getting a few mixed messages, here.
        
        "Yes, sorry," she says with a sheepish laugh. "Let’s talk. About anything. About everything, if we can! There’s so much for us to learn about each other."
        
        In that case, you’d like to go first....
        |Although you asked her this before, you ask again, just to be sure, if questions are considered ‘for free’ and you don’t need to use a wish when all you want is to talk a bit. As a genie, she probably has quite a lot to teach you.
        
        "You may ask your questions," she says with an impatient scowl. "And I will answer to the utmost of my abilities. Though you may be surprised at how much or how little I have to say."
        
        Well, that sounds cryptic. At least you know for sure that you can ask her whatever you want.
    ]
rows.translation:
[oma.freedomWishedFor
        |你问奥玛是否愿意聊一聊。
        
        听到这个问题，她从鼻子里长长地叹了口气。她仰起头，闭上眼睛，嘴角绽开一个灿烂的笑容。“你能提出这样的请求，真是太好了，”她回答道。“我愿意。我最想做的就是交谈。我想选择停止交谈。我喜欢自己可以选择不说话。”
        
        你在这里……收到了一些互相矛盾的信息。
        
        “是的，抱歉，”她带着一丝尴尬的笑容说道。“我们聊聊吧。什么都行。如果可以的话，什么都聊一聊！我们彼此之间还有太多可以了解的东西。”
        
        既然如此，你想先来……
        |虽然你之前已经问过她这个问题，但你还是又问了一遍，只为确认：如果只是想随便聊上几句，这些提问是否算‘免费’，而不必动用一次许愿。身为灯神，她大概有很多东西可以教你。
        
        “你可以提出问题了，”她不耐烦地皱着眉头说道，“我会尽我所能回答。不过，你可能会惊讶于我能说的有那么多——或者那么少。”
        
        嗯，这话听起来真有点神秘。至少你可以确定，你可以向她提出任何你想问的问题。
    ]

rows.original: Oma mentioned back when you first summoned her that she could grant you three wishes, but she also said that there were three rules that you needed to abide by. You ask her to list them again. "[oma.freedomWishedFor |Of course. ]The first rule is that I cannot directly harm any person or individual that does not wish for it." Could she elaborate? [oma.freedomWishedFor | |"Is it not obvious enough?" she asks with a nasally huff. ]"The potential exists to abuse the powers of the genie to injure, obstruct, debilitate, or even kill someone or something else," she explains. "I very specifically[oma.isCollared | |, even in my home pocket dimension, ] cannot use my magic to harm someone – there would be nothing preventing a Master from, for example, wishing for the death of someone, or even more than one person, to knowingly cause someone else harm. They could use the powers of the genie to commit horrible atrocities – everything from petty injuries to genocides." She could do that? Kill thousands of people with her magic? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |No, and I never could, specifically because of this limitation. But making a massive change on that sort of scale... was not out of the question." She turns her left hand over, looking at her own palm as she flexes her fingers. "If not for that one rule, the potential would have existed." What if, for instance, you asked her to transform into a sword, and you gripped her handle and you swung her at someone. It’s not her that’s knowingly attacking someone. Would she be unable to do that? "Yes," she answers immediately. "I cannot knowingly hurt someone else. That is the wording of my restriction. But if I were to transform into a sword, and you were to grip me by the handle and swing me at someone, and I were to make contact – that would be through no fault of my own." She crosses her arms and looks down in thought. "I wasn’t the one to discover this loophole. A previous, and... imaginative, and aggressive master of mine realized it first. I never told any of my other masters for fear of one of them being more imaginative and more aggressive. The powers of the genie could be terribly misused with a bit of creativity and some airtight wording." |I just said that I cannot," she responds with an impatient huff. "If you’re going to ask these questions, [pc.Master], you’ll need to pay attention when I answer. I cannot knowingly infringe upon any person’s well-being, whether it’s one person or a million or more." ] Okay, so, you [oma.freedomWishedFor |can’t |couldn’t ] wish for her to attack someone. Got it. What was the second rule? "The second rule is that I cannot impress upon another person, mentally, physically, or otherwise," Oma says. "For example, I cannot have someone fall in love with someone else[oma.freedomWishedFor |. Not that you’d need any help, if you’re as selfless with others as you have been with me, [pc.name]," she says with a lilting voice and a shy blush. " |. ]I likewise cannot make someone fall out of love. I also cannot make a person grow a tail, nor can I turn their skin to fur or to scales. And et cetera." You can imagine the sort of mayhem that could be caused if you wished for the world’s population to love and adore you. That’s a lot of power[pc.isDK |. | that nobody should have ]. "There’s that, of course," she answers with a nod. "I believe the actual intent, however, was to ensure that all people’s free will was not something that could be tampered with – at least, not directly, with powers like mine. Each person is an island, and the ground we live on is[oma.freedomWishedFor | |, metaphorically," she says haltingly, " ] the sea. A person could convince another person to grow a tree on their island – or to salt its dirt so that no trees may grow – but no person can never force them to do such things. And that includes me."[oma.isCollared | | Did that include you, when you were her [pc.Master]? If you had wished for it, could she had made it so? "In fact, no," she answers. "I could not and cannot make you love someone. I could not [pc.hasWings |remove your wings, even if you had wanted and even if you had wished |have you grow wings ]. Even if you had wished for it, I could not grant it." ] Would that have wasted one of your wishes? "No. If I [oma.isFree |could not |cannot ] grant it, you do not ‘lose’ it." Okay: the second rule is that you [oma.isCollared |can’t |couldn’t ] use her to change someone’s body or mind. Easy enough. What was the final rule? "The third and final rule is that, similar to how I cannot kill, I cannot raise someone from the dead," she explains. [oma.isCollared |Once the last word leaves her mouth, however, her normally stern and impeccable gaze breaks, for just the slimmest of moments. You ask her if what she just told you is the truth. Can she really not raise someone from the dead? "I cannot raise someone from the dead, [pc.Master]," she barks with the sudden indignation of a starving dog being cruelly teased of some food. "Not a word I’ve said is a lie." |"Although...." She stops suddenly, her eyes drifting downward as her right hand fidgets towards her abdomen. Her brow furrows in longing frustration, and her upper lip trembles, but she doesn’t continue. You tell her that she doesn’t have to finish that thought if she doesn’t want to. She pauses for a moment – and then her melancholy expression is broken with just the barest hint of a smile, playing at the edges of her mouth. "I want to," she says. "And I’m a free genie, now. And if I want to, that means that I can." Still, whatever joy she got from reminding herself of her freedom vanishes as quickly as it appeared. "It’s... more appropriate to say that the third rule is that I cannot grant life. Not that I can’t resurrect someone from the dead – although I can’t do that, either." [pc.isBimbo |You stare at Oma blankly, trying to parse what she just said. It’s not that she can’t... it’s that she... wait, what’s the difference? Oma’s fingers fidget, drawing your eyes to her stomach, and suddenly, the realization hits you. You gasp, covering your mouth with your splayed fingers. Does she mean that she can’t... have a baby? |From the way Oma is sadly patting her stomach, you hazard a guess – is she saying she can’t have a child? Is that what she meant when she said she ‘cannot grant life?’ ] "Yes, that’s correct," she says with a frown. "Returning old life or creating new life... both are beyond my near-infinite powers as a genie. Even if I were to ‘fashion’ a child, it wouldn’t truly be new life: it’d be a conscious extension of myself, sharing my thoughts, feelings, and emotions, and they would vanish the moment my concentration broke. A pale mockery of the true magic mortals possess." ] Well... you’ve learned everything you need to know about Oma’s wish-granting abilities. She can’t[oma.freedomWishedFor | purposefully ] attack anyone; she can’t change someone’s body or mind; and she [oma.isCollared |can’t resurrect someone from the dead |can’t grant life ]. Three fairly easy-to-remember rules.
rows.translation: 奥玛在你第一次召唤她的时候就提到过，她能赐予你三个愿望，但她也说过，有三条你必须遵守的规则。你请她再把这些规则列一遍。 “[oma.freedomWishedFor |当然可以。 ]第一条规则是，我不能直接伤害任何不希望受到伤害的人或个体。” 她能详细说说吗？ [oma.freedomWishedFor | |“这还不够明显吗？”她带着鼻音哼了一声问道。 ]“灯神的力量确实有可能被滥用来伤害、阻碍、削弱、甚至杀死别人或别的东西，”她解释道，“我特别[oma.isCollared | |，即使是在我自己的口袋维度里， ]不能用我的魔法去伤害别人——那样的话，就没什么能阻止一位主人，比方说，许愿让某个人，甚至不止一个人死去，从而故意让别人受到伤害。他们可以利用灯神的力量犯下可怕的暴行——从小小的伤害到种族灭绝，无所不包。” 她能做到那种事？用她的魔法杀死成千上万的人？ “[oma.freedomWishedFor |不能，我从来都做不到，正是因为这条限制。但在那种规模上做出巨大的改变……并非不可能。”她翻过左手，一边屈伸手指一边看着自己的掌心。“要不是有那一条规则，那种可能性本来是存在的。” 那么，比如说，你让她变成一把剑，你握住她的剑柄，拿她朝某个人挥去。故意攻击别人的并不是她。她难道就不能这么做吗？ “能，”她立刻回答。“我不能明知故犯地伤害别人。这就是我那条限制的措辞。但如果我变成一把剑，而你握住剑柄把我朝某个人挥去，而我碰到了对方——那就完全不是我的过错了。”她双臂交叉，低头沉思。“发现这个漏洞的不是我。我以前的一位……富有想象力、又咄咄逼人的主人最先发现了它。我从来没告诉过我其他的主人，因为我怕他们之中有人更有想象力、也更咄咄逼人。只要有一点创造力和一些滴水不漏的措辞，灯神的力量就可能被极其恶劣地滥用。” |我刚才就说了我不能，”她不耐烦地哼了一声回答。“如果你要问这些问题，[pc.Master]，我回答的时候你就得留心听。我不能故意损害任何人的福祉，无论是一个人，还是一百万人，或者更多。” ] 好吧，那么，你[oma.freedomWishedFor |不能 |不能 ]许愿让她去攻击别人。明白了。那第二条规则是什么？ “第二条规则是，我不能对另一个人施加影响，无论是精神上、身体上还是其他方面，”奥玛说。“比如说，我不能让某个人爱上另一个人[oma.freedomWishedFor |。倒不是说你需要什么帮助，如果你对别人也像对我这样无私的话，[pc.name]，”她用轻快的嗓音说道，脸上泛起羞涩的红晕。“ |。 ]我同样不能让某人不再爱上谁。我也不能让人长出一条尾巴，也不能把他们的皮肤变成毛皮或鳞片。诸如此类。” 你可以想象，如果你许愿让全世界的人都爱你、崇拜你，那会引发怎样的混乱。那可是很大的力量[pc.isDK | |，任何人都不该拥有 ]。 “那当然也是一部分原因，”她点点头回答。“不过我相信，真正的用意是确保所有人的自由意志都不是可以被篡改的东西——至少不能被像我这样的力量直接篡改。每个人都是一座岛，而我们生活在其上的大地是[oma.freedomWishedFor | |，打个比方，”她支支吾吾地说，“ ]大海。一个人可以说服另一个人在他的岛上种一棵树——或者往它的土里撒盐，让任何树都长不出来——但没有人能强迫他们做这种事。而这也包括我。”[oma.isCollared | | 那也包括你，在你还是她的[pc.Master]的时候？如果你许了愿，她能办到吗？ “事实上，不能，”她回答。“我不能，也无法让你爱上某个人。我不能[pc.hasWings |除去你的羽翼，即使你本来就想那样，即使你也许过愿 |让你长出羽翼 ]。即使你许愿要它，我也无法实现。” ] 那会浪费掉你一个愿望吗？ “不会。如果我[oma.isFree |无法 |无法 ]实现它，你并不算‘失去’它。” 好吧：第二条规则是，你[oma.isCollared |不能 |不能 ]用她改变某人的身体或心智。够简单。那最后一条规则是什么？ “第三条也是最后一条规则是，和我不能杀人类似，我不能让死者复活，”她解释道。[oma.isCollared |然而，最后一句话一离开她的嘴，她那平时严厉而无可挑剔的注视就破了功，只是极短暂的一瞬。 你问她，她刚告诉你的话是不是真的。她真的不能让死者复活吗？ “我不能让死者复活，[pc.Master]，”她吼道，突然愤愤不平，像一条饿狗被人残忍地拿食物逗弄。“我说过的没有一句是谎话。” |“不过……” 她突然停住，目光向下飘去，右手不安地朝自己的腹部摸索。她眉头因渴望而挫败地拧起，上唇颤抖着，但她没有继续说下去。 你告诉她，如果她不想，就不必把那个念头说完。 她停顿了片刻——随后，她忧郁的表情被一丝极淡的笑意打破，那笑意只在她的嘴角边缘游走。“我想说，”她说。“而且我现在是一个自由的灯神了。如果我想，那就意味着我能。” 然而，她从提醒自己自由这件事上得到的任何喜悦，都来得快去得也快。“更准确地说，第三条规则是我不能赐予生命。不是我无法让死者复活——虽然那个我也做不到。” [pc.isBimbo |你茫然地盯着奥玛，努力理解她刚说的话。不是她不能……而是她……等等，这两者有什么区别？ 奥玛的手指不安地动着，把你的目光引向她的肚子，突然间，你恍然大悟。你倒吸一口气，用张开的手指捂住了嘴。她的意思是，她不能……生孩子吗？ |从奥玛悲伤地拍着自己肚子的样子看，你大胆猜了一下——她是在说她不能生孩子吗？她说自己‘不能赐予生命’时，指的就是这个吗？ ] “是的，没错，”她皱着眉头说。“让旧生命回来，或者创造新生命……这两者都超出了我身为灯神近乎无限的力量。即使我‘拼造’出一个孩子，那也不是真正的新生命：那会是我自身一个有意识的延伸，分享我的思想、感受和情绪，而一旦我的注意力中断，它们就会消失。那不过是对凡人拥有的真正魔法的一种苍白模仿。” ] 嗯……关于奥玛实现愿望的能力，你已经了解了一切需要知道的。她不能[oma.freedomWishedFor | 刻意 ]攻击任何人；她不能改变某人的身体或心智；而她[oma.isCollared |无法让死者复活 |无法赐予生命 ]。 三条相当容易记住的规则。
rows.raw: ' Oma mentioned back when you first summoned her that she could grant you three wishes, but she also said that there were three rules that you needed to abide by. You ask her to list them again. "[oma.freedomWishedFor |Of course. ]The first rule is that I cannot directly harm any person or individual that does not wish for it." Could she elaborate? [oma.freedomWishedFor | |"Is it not obvious enough?" she asks with a nasally huff. ]"The potential exists to abuse the powers of the genie to injure, obstruct, debilitate, or even kill someone or something else," she explains. "I very specifically[oma.isCollared | |, even in my home pocket dimension, ] cannot use my magic to harm someone – there would be nothing preventing a Master from, for example, wishing for the death of someone, or even more than one person, to knowingly cause someone else harm. They could use the powers of the genie to commit horrible atrocities – everything from petty injuries to genocides." She could do that? Kill thousands of people with her magic? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |No, and I never could, specifically because of this limitation. But making a massive change on that sort of scale... was not out of the question." She turns her left hand over, looking at her own palm as she flexes her fingers. "If not for that one rule, the potential would have existed." What if, for instance, you asked her to transform into a sword, and you gripped her handle and you swung her at someone. It’s not her that’s knowingly attacking someone. Would she be unable to do that? "Yes," she answers immediately. "I cannot knowingly hurt someone else. That is the wording of my restriction. But if I were to transform into a sword, and you were to grip me by the handle and swing me at someone, and I were to make contact – that would be through no fault of my own." She crosses her arms and looks down in thought. "I wasn’t the one to discover this loophole. A previous, and... imaginative, and aggressive master of mine realized it first. I never told any of my other masters for fear of one of them being more imaginative and more aggressive. The powers of the genie could be terribly misused with a bit of creativity and some airtight wording." |I just said that I cannot," she responds with an impatient huff. "If you’re going to ask these questions, [pc.Master], you’ll need to pay attention when I answer. I cannot knowingly infringe upon any person’s well-being, whether it’s one person or a million or more." ] Okay, so, you [oma.freedomWishedFor |can’t |couldn’t ] wish for her to attack someone. Got it. What was the second rule? "The second rule is that I cannot impress upon another person, mentally, physically, or otherwise," Oma says. "For example, I cannot have someone fall in love with someone else[oma.freedomWishedFor |. Not that you’d need any help, if you’re as selfless with others as you have been with me, [pc.name]," she says with a lilting voice and a shy blush. " |. ]I likewise cannot make someone fall out of love. I also cannot make a person grow a tail, nor can I turn their skin to fur or to scales. And et cetera." You can imagine the sort of mayhem that could be caused if you wished for the world’s population to love and adore you. That’s a lot of power[pc.isDK |. | that nobody should have ]. "There’s that, of course," she answers with a nod. "I believe the actual intent, however, was to ensure that all people’s free will was not something that could be tampered with – at least, not directly, with powers like mine. Each person is an island, and the ground we live on is[oma.freedomWishedFor | |, metaphorically," she says haltingly, " ] the sea. A person could convince another person to grow a tree on their island – or to salt its dirt so that no trees may grow – but no person can never force them to do such things. And that includes me."[oma.isCollared | | Did that include you, when you were her [pc.Master]? If you had wished for it, could she had made it so? "In fact, no," she answers. "I could not and cannot make you love someone. I could not [pc.hasWings |remove your wings, even if you had wanted and even if you had wished |have you grow wings ]. Even if you had wished for it, I could not grant it." ] Would that have wasted one of your wishes? "No. If I [oma.isFree |could not |cannot ] grant it, you do not ‘lose’ it." Okay: the second rule is that you [oma.isCollared |can’t |couldn’t ] use her to change someone’s body or mind. Easy enough. What was the final rule? "The third and final rule is that, similar to how I cannot kill, I cannot raise someone from the dead," she explains. [oma.isCollared |Once the last word leaves her mouth, however, her normally stern and impeccable gaze breaks, for just the slimmest of moments. You ask her if what she just told you is the truth. Can she really not raise someone from the dead? "I cannot raise someone from the dead, [pc.Master]," she barks with the sudden indignation of a starving dog being cruelly teased of some food. Her brow furrows in longing frustration, and her upper lip trembles, but she doesn’t continue. You tell her that she doesn’t have to finish that thought if she doesn’t want to. She pauses for a moment – and then her melancholy expression is broken with just the barest hint of a smile, playing at the edges of her mouth. "I want to," she says. "And I’m a free genie, now. And if I want to, that means that I can." Still, whatever joy she got from reminding herself of her freedom vanishes as quickly as it appeared. "It’s... more appropriate to say that the third rule is that I cannot grant life. Not that I can’t resurrect someone from the dead – although I can’t do that, either." [pc.isBimbo |You stare at Oma blankly, trying to parse what she just said. It’s not that she can’t... it’s that she... wait, what’s the difference? Even if I were to ‘fashion’ a child, it wouldn’t truly be new life: it’d be a conscious extension of myself, sharing my thoughts, feelings, and emotions, and they would vanish the moment my concentration broke. A pale mockery of the true magic mortals possess." ] Well... you’ve learned everything you need to know about Oma’s wish-granting abilities. She can’t[oma.freedomWishedFor | purposefully ] attack anyone; she can’t change someone’s body or mind; and she [oma.isCollared |can’t resurrect someone from the dead |can’t grant life ]. rows.original: You ask Oma about the previous masters that she’s had over the course of her life. Actually... is that fair to say? Her ‘life?’ Is it correct to say that she has a ‘life’ in the same sense that a mortal does? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |Perhaps not," she replies with a lighthearted chuckle. "My life is not akin to a mortal’s, no." |No," she answers sternly and stiffly. And she doesn’t elaborate further. ] Okay, well, going back to the original question, then: what sort of masters has she had in the past? How many has she had up until you? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |I had |I have had ] exactly fifty-six masters before you, [oma.freedomWishedFor |and you [oma.isCollared |are |were ] my final [pc.master] at number fifty-seven |making you number fifty-seven ]," she answers. "The time between masters and mistresses [oma.isCollared |is |was ] difficult to calculate for certain; there [oma.isCollared |is |was ] a four year minimum gap between masters, and the largest drought between them [oma.isCollared |is currently |was ] thirty-two." There[oma.isCollared |’s | was ] a four year minimum gap between masters? Why is that? "[oma.isCollared |I am inexorably bound to this lamp," she answers, hefting the lamp in her palm once. " |Before you wished for my freedom, [pc.name], I was totally and absolutely bound to the lamp. ]Once a master [oma.isCollared |uses |used ] their allotted wishes, the lamp [oma.isCollared |will |would ] vanish, to reappear elsewhere within the realm of Savarra after four years’ time. It could be within a vault; it could be within a dense forest; a deep cave; under the ocean; buried in the desert; within a raging hurricane, to be blown across the world before finding its newest resting place. I [oma.isCollared |have |had ] no control over where it reappears and I [oma.isCollared |have |had ] no influence over who might find it next. The purpose of this eclectic system [oma.isCollared |is |was ] to prevent a family from hoarding the lamp – and me within it – so that the powers of the genie would be a privilege granted to a select few." That makes sense – if a particularly selfish person found the lamp, they could ensure that they and their lineage would control it and Oma for all eternity. That’s a lot of power for just one family to wield. "Indeed," she [oma.freedomWishedFor |says |grunts impatiently ]. "My first master was a petty soldier, marching in an army enlisted in an ancient kingdom where Tronarii now stands[oma.freedomWishedFor | |. Er... if it still stands ]. He was a simple, uneducated man that hardly understood the power of the genie: his first wish was for some softer boots to march in, and the second was to usurp the position of his commanding officer." Well... at least he didn’t seem so bad. "His third wish was for a sword that would instantly slay any person that it touched. His hope was to be such a ‘hero’ on the battlefield that any battle with him in it would be a decisive victory. He wanted ‘songs to be sung about him until the end of time.’" [pc.isBimbo |Now... you’re not... like, the smartest cookie in the jar, but, like, that doesn’t seem very smart. A weapon that defeated anybody by touching it? How’s he gonna get it out of the sca- the sca- the... the sword-holder thingie? |... And she said he was an ‘uneducated’ man? Because there’s a pretty obvious issue with a wish like that. ] [oma.freedomWishedFor |Oma looks at you with a mixed expression – one of regret for the future, but totally shameless of the past. "Don’t judge me harshly, [pc.name]," she says, her tone somewhat reserved. "I have no love for my previous masters. My wish, to their exact specifications, was my command. |"You have already proven yourself to be of sharper wit than more than half of my previous masters," Oma says humorlessly. " ]True to his wish, the weapon instantly slew anyone it touched – and he perished the moment he grabbed its hilt. I vanished into the lamp the moment his wish was granted; the sword fell where he last stood, and I imagine it’s rusted to nothing by now." [oma.isCollared |You’ll have to keep your phrasing in mind when you make your [oma.wishesLeftRange 2 |wishes |wish ] later |Well, at least you were a bit more attentive than that guy ]. You ask her to continue: does she remember every single master she’s ever had? "Yes." Isn’t that... a lot to keep track of? Especially over such a long period of time? "[oma.isCollared |I have nothing else better to do than to ruminate in between masters," she answers, her mouth curled downward into a I’m-quite-serious frown. |Up until recently, I’ve had very, very little to do, personally, then to ruminate, [pc.name]. Memorizing my previous masters, their wishes, and their follies, was just one of the ways I had available to me to pass the time." She smiles, like she had just told you a funny joke and you’re supposed to laugh. ] At the least, you’re enjoying Oma’s stories of her previous masters. You ask her to tell you about her second master, the one after the [pc.isDK |dumb |uneducated ] soldier. "My second master was a playwright: a learned upperclassman that owned a small, personal study. At first, he didn’t understand that what he possessed was a magic lamp housing a genie: he only thought it to be a simple oil-burning lamp that he had purchased from a peddler at the local market. It wasn’t until one cold, winter night, when he was rubbing his hand against the lamp’s cauldron for warmth, did he realize what he possessed." Uh oh... you hesitate to think what a smart person could do with the powers of the genie. [pc.isBimbo |That’s what makes you such a good candidate for holding onto the lamp! ] "In truth, his demands were fairly modest," she answers. For the first time since she began talking about her previous masters,[oma.freedomWishedFor |she regards the memory with some fondness |the borderline scowl on her face eases slightly – she doesn’t mind reminiscing about her second master, clearly ]. "His first wish was that he may never again be wanting for oil for the lamp, so that he may always have a light to read by night, and warmth from the cold." [pc.isBimbo |Aw, that’s a cute wish! But... wait. When you found the lamp, it was bone dry. So much for ‘endless oil,’ then! |She’s right, that’s a modest wish. But... when you found the lamp, the cauldron was bone dry. Shouldn’t the oil have been endless? ] "His first wish was that he may never again be wanted for oil for the lamp," she reiterates. "His wording may have been unintentional, but it was nonetheless very specific. His second wish was that his inkwell never ran dry – it was between that, and infinite parchment, and a quill that never dulled or snapped. These things I could have provided, of course, but only one at a time, and he reasoned that the ink was the most important." [pc.isBimbo |That sounds boring. You would have asked for something fun. Like... okay, it’s easy to think of something fun for you, but if you were a play write, you’d ask for... a stage! A big ol’ stage that belonged to you that you could have people act in! That sounds like fun. "He was fairly well-to-do, as I understand it," Oma continues. "He likely already had a stage – or, at least, easy access to one." Oh. In that case, you’d ask for [pc.hasCock |a bigger dick |the ability to take bigger dicks ] or something. |That sounds reasonable to you. Parchment and quills are fleeting things, but ink is difficult and expensive to obtain. If you had to choose between the three options, the ink would be the smartest choice. ] "His final wish, upon his deathbed, was for his written works to be published, and for his lineage to reap whatever royalties they’d accrue[oma.freedomWishedFor |. He never expounded his personal life to me all that much, but as I understand it, his plays were... not especially popular. No publishing house would take them ]." And did she grant that wish? [oma.freedomWishedFor |She winces. "Yes," she answers hesitantly. But? "I had only learned of this much later, with my eleventh master, but my second master’s plays were considered... subpar. Forgettable. Average." She frowns as she retells what she had learned. "And none of his children had children of their own. Their royalties were worth little and his family didn’t extend long enough to enjoy whatever they were worth." |"Of course," she answers snidely, like you had insulted her somehow. "Do not impugn my worth as a genie, [pc.master]. His wish was granted to his exact specifications." Despite her language and her powerful tone, her expression falters. But only slightly: a tremble of the upper lip and her normally-steely gaze breaking to flit between your eyes. It could be nothing. ] Well, at least her second master didn’t seem so bad. "[oma.freedomWishedFor |All in all, no; he was alright. He asked for simple, perhaps miniscule things that underutilized the powers of the genie, but I’ve had worse masters, that’s for sure. |Perhaps on the surface. But remember that each wish that he asked for – however miniscule they may be for the powers of the genie – were purely selfish in nature. He may not have been as witless as my first master, but he was just as self-serving. ]" On the one hand, you don’t really plan on sitting here and listening to her talk about all [pc.isBimbo |however-many |fifty-six ] of her previous masters, but on the other, you can’t help but be curious about the sorts of people that she served under as a genie of the lamp. So you skip ahead – you ask her to tell you about her[pc.isBimbo |, umm... the master she had three masters ago | fifty-fourth master ]. It’ll be [pc.isBimbo |neat |interesting ] to hear if people have changed that much between masters. "My fifty-fourth master was an orc woman," Oma answers. "A peasant for her tribe, as I understand it. She was one of the tribe’s seamstresses: she sewed clothing and leather armors for the warrior caste. rows.raw: ' You ask Oma about the previous masters that she’s had over the course of her life. Actually... is that fair to say? Her ‘life?’ Is it correct to say that she has a ‘life’ in the same sense that a mortal does? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |Perhaps not," she replies with a lighthearted chuckle. "My life is not akin to a mortal’s, no." |No," she answers sternly and stiffly. And she doesn’t elaborate further. ] Okay, well, going back to the original question, then: what sort of masters has she had in the past? How many has she had up until you? "[oma.freedomWishedFor |I had |I have had ] exactly fifty-six masters before you, [oma.freedomWishedFor |and you [oma.isCollared |are |were ] my final [pc.master] at number fifty-seven |making you number fifty-seven ]," she answers. "The time between masters and mistresses [oma.isCollared |is |was ] difficult to calculate for certain; there [oma.isCollared |is |was ] a four year minimum gap between masters, and the largest drought between them [oma.isCollared |is currently |was ] thirty-two." There[oma.isCollared |’s | was ] a four year minimum gap between masters? Why is that? "[oma.isCollared |I am inexorably bound to this lamp," she answers, hefting the lamp in her palm once. " |Before you wished for my freedom, [pc.name], I was totally and absolutely bound to the lamp. ]Once a master [oma.isCollared |uses |used ] their allotted wishes, the lamp [oma.isCollared |will |would ] vanish, to reappear elsewhere within the realm of Savarra after four years’ time. It could be within a vault; it could be within a dense forest; a deep cave; under the ocean; buried in the desert; within a raging hurricane, to be blown across the world before finding its newest resting place. I [oma.isCollared |have |had ] no control over where it reappears and I [oma.isCollared |have |had ] no influence over who might find it next. The purpose of this eclectic system [oma.isCollared |is |was ] to prevent a family from hoarding the lamp – and me within it – so that the powers of the genie would be a privilege granted to a select few." That makes sense – if a particularly selfish person found the lamp, they could ensure that they and their lineage would control it and Oma for all eternity. That’s a lot of power for just one family to wield. "Indeed," she [oma.freedomWishedFor |says |grunts impatiently ]. "My first master was a petty soldier, marching in an army enlisted in an ancient kingdom where Tronarii now stands[oma.freedomWishedFor | |. Er... if it still stands ]. He was a simple, uneducated man that hardly understood the power of the genie: his first wish was for some softer boots to march in, and the second was to usurp the position of his commanding officer." Well... at least he didn’t seem so bad. "His third wish was for a sword that would instantly slay any person that it touched. His hope was to be such a ‘hero’ on the battlefield that any battle with him in it would be a decisive victory. He wanted ‘songs to be sung about him until the end of time.’" [pc.isBimbo |Now... you’re not... like, the smartest cookie in the jar, but, like, that doesn’t seem very smart. A weapon that defeated anybody by touching it? How’s he gonna get it out of the sca- the sca- the... the sword-holder thingie? |... And she said he was an ‘uneducated’ man? Because there’s a pretty obvious issue with a wish like that. ] [oma.freedomWishedFor |Oma looks at you with a mixed expression – one of regret for the future, but totally shameless of the past. "Don’t judge me harshly, [pc.name]," she says, her tone somewhat reserved. "I have no love for my previous masters. My wish, to their exact specifications, was my command. |"You have already proven yourself to be of sharper wit than more than half of my previous masters," Oma says humorlessly. " ]True to his wish, the weapon instantly slew anyone it touched – and he perished the moment he grabbed its hilt. I vanished into the lamp the moment his wish was granted; the sword fell where he last stood, and I imagine it’s rusted to nothing by now." [oma.isCollared |You’ll have to keep your phrasing in mind when you make your [oma.wishesLeftRange 2 |wishes |wish ] later |Well, at least you were a bit more attentive than that guy ]. You ask her to continue: does she remember every single master she’s ever had? "Yes." Isn’t that... a lot to keep track of? Especially over such a long period of time? "[oma.isCollared |I have nothing else better to do than to ruminate in between masters," she answers, her mouth curled downward into a I’m-quite-serious frown. |Up until recently, I’ve had very, very little to do, personally, then to ruminate, [pc.name]. Memorizing my previous masters, their wishes, and their follies, was just one of the ways I had available to me to pass the time." She smiles, like she had just told you a funny joke and you’re supposed to laugh. ] At the least, you’re enjoying Oma’s stories of her previous masters. You ask her to tell you about her second master, the one after the [pc.isDK |dumb |uneducated ] soldier. "My second master was a playwright: a learned upperclassman that owned a small, personal study. At first, he didn’t understand that what he possessed was a magic lamp housing a genie: he only thought it to be a simple oil-burning lamp that he had purchased from a peddler at the local market. It wasn’t until one cold, winter night, when he was rubbing his hand against the lamp’s cauldron for warmth, did he realize what he possessed." Uh oh... you hesitate to think what a smart person could do with the powers of the genie. [pc.isBimbo |That’s what makes you such a good candidate for holding onto the lamp! ] "In truth, his demands were fairly modest," she answers. For the first time since she began talking about her previous masters,[oma.freedomWishedFor |she regards the memory with some fondness |the borderline scowl on her face eases slightly – she doesn’t mind reminiscing about her second master, clearly ]. "His first wish was that he may never again be wanting for oil for the lamp, so that he may always have a light to read by night, and warmth from the cold." [pc.isBimbo |Aw, that’s a cute wish! But... wait. When you found the lamp, it was bone dry. So much for ‘endless oil,’ then! |She’s right, that’s a modest wish. But... when you found the lamp, the cauldron was bone dry. Shouldn’t the oil have been endless? ] "His first wish was that he may never again be wanted for oil for the lamp," she reiterates. "His wording may have been unintentional, but it was nonetheless very specific. His second wish was that his inkwell never ran dry – it was between that, and infinite parchment, and a quill that never dulled or snapped. These things I could have provided, of course, but only one at a time, and he reasoned that the ink was the most important." [pc.isBimbo |That sounds boring. You would have asked for something fun. Like... okay, it’s easy to think of something fun for you, but if you were a play write, you’d ask for... a stage! A big ol’ stage that belonged to you that you could have people act in! That sounds like fun. "He was fairly well-to-do, as I understand it," Oma continues. "He likely already had a stage – or, at least, easy access to one." Oh. In that case, you’d ask for [pc.hasCock |a bigger dick |the ability to take bigger dicks ] or something. |That sounds reasonable to you. Parchment and quills are fleeting things, but ink is difficult and expensive to obtain. If you had to choose between the three options, the ink would be the smartest choice. ] "His final wish, upon his deathbed, was for his written works to be published, and for his lineage to reap whatever royalties they’d accrue[oma.freedomWishedFor |. He never expounded his personal life to me all that much, but as I understand it, his plays were... not especially popular. No publishing house would take them ]." And did she grant that wish? [oma.freedomWishedFor |She winces. "Yes," she answers hesitantly. But? "I had only learned of this much later, with my eleventh master, but my second master’s plays were considered... subpar. Forgettable. Average." She frowns as she retells what she had learned. "And none of his children had children of their own. Their royalties were worth little and his family didn’t extend long enough to enjoy whatever they were worth." |"Of course," she answers snidely, like you had insulted her somehow. "Do not impugn my worth as a genie, [pc.master]. His wish was granted to his exact specifications." Despite her language and her powerful tone, her expression falters. But only slightly: a tremble of the upper lip and her normally-steely gaze breaking to flit between your eyes. It could be nothing. ] Well, at least her second master didn’t seem so bad. "[oma.freedomWishedFor |All in all, no; he was alright. He asked for simple, perhaps miniscule things that underutilized the powers of the genie, but I’ve had worse masters, that’s for sure. |Perhaps on the surface. But remember that each wish that he asked for – however miniscule they may be for the powers of the genie – were purely selfish in nature. He may not have been as witless as my first master, but he was just as self-serving. ]" On the one hand, you don’t really plan on sitting here and listening to her talk about all [pc.isBimbo |however-many |fifty-six ] of her previous masters, but on the other, you can’t help but be curious about the sorts of people that she served under as a genie of the lamp. So you skip ahead – you ask her to tell you about her[pc.isBimbo |, umm... the master she had three masters ago | fifty-fourth master ]. It’ll be [pc.isBimbo |neat |interesting ] to hear if people have changed that much between masters. "My fifty-fourth master was an orc woman," Oma answers. "A peasant for her tribe, as I understand it. She was one of the tribe’s seamstresses: she sewed clothing and leather armors for the warrior caste. She was a dirty, malnourished, and neglected woman." [pc.isBimbo |Aww, that’s sad. But she used Oma’s genie powers to make herself better, right? Nobody would look down on her if she wished for bigger boobs or something! "As a matter of fact," Oma says[oma.freedomWishedFor |with a wry grin |with a dispassionate sigh ]. |A part of you hopes that this orc woman used her wishes to get herself a better life, or at least some respect among her peers... but if she was a peasant woman, that means she probably wasn’t any more farsighted than Oma’s first master, the soldier. "Perhaps. But then again, perhaps not," Oma says [oma.freedomWishedFor |with a wry grin |with a dispassionate sigh ]. ] "Her first wish was for larger breasts. She wasn’t considered conventionally beautiful – my words, not hers – so she wanted some way to attract the eyes of even the mightiest chieftain in the orc tribes. And she reasoned that having a large pair of breasts would do it." [pc.isBimbo |Yayyy! |Well... she probably wasn’t wrong. ] "Unfortunately for her, I cannot infringe on a person’s bodily autonomy, even if they wish for it. I could not grant her wish. So, instead, she wished for a longboat – an absolutely gigantic boat, requiring a crew of over thirty orcs just for the oars. I’m told that, in orcish culture, having a large boat is a status symbol, and gifting a boat to another is a gesture of love. The larger, the more romantic the gesture." "A year later, she was wed to her tribe’s warlord. I was told that she lived a happy life, full of plenty and security... but her husband was worried that marrying a frail seamstress over a proud warrior woman would be seen as weakness on his part, and he wanted to better establish his position among his people. So, she wished for a large monster for her husband to slay: a leviathan, a terror of the sea deep. Something of incredible size and ferocity, but a creature that her husband could slay single-handed." If her husband, an orc chieftain, was capable enough to slay a leviathan single-handedly, then it’s a surprise that he was worried about his outward appearances at all. "Orcs are, as I understand it, a fickle bunch, especially in the current year," Oma [oma.freedomWishedFor |laughs |sighs ]. "With his status confirmed as a rightful chieftain of his tribe, my mistress was happy as could be with her wishes, but she still had one remaining. So, she did the most romantic gesture she could think of." [pc.ra orc |That’d be an even larger longboat, then. That’d certainly win your heart several times over. "Correct," Oma says. " |[pc.isBimbo |Oooh, like what? A ring? Flowers? A ring with flowers on it?! "A larger longboat, of course," Oma says [oma.freedomWishedFor |with a laugh |with a sigh ]. [pc.ra orc |You tell Oma to stop; you can only get so [silly |[pc.hasCock |erect |wet ] |light-headed ]. She knew exactly what every orc could possibly wish for. |Sounds like she knew exactly what she wanted, at least. ] "[oma.freedomWishedFor |To this day, I wonder if that’s true," she hums |I doubt that," she replies dryly ]. "As I disappeared into the lamp upon granting her third wish, she and her husband were discussing the logistics of having a longboat that large. It’d require a crew larger than their tribe twice over. Its decks would need to be scrubbed at all hours of the day, from sunrise to sunset to sunrise. A single oar would be so long and heavy that even a typical orc could not row it. If one of the sheets was damaged, it’d require enough fabric to supply the sails of four average longboats, and over a season’s worth of effort." Oma [oma.freedomWishedFor |laughs to herself and averts her eyes |sighs through her nose ]. "Perhaps they learned their lesson on being careful what they wished for. But then again, perhaps not." rows.original: You ask Oma to talk a bit about herself. She’s a genie! She probably has one hell of a story to tell. [oma.isCollared |"There is nothing to tell," she answers sternly. You don’t believe that for a second. You rubbed an oil lamp and an entire... human? Elf? An entire genie popped out of it, saying she was going to grant you three wishes. There’s a backstory to that and you want to hear it. "Is that a wish?" she asks, crooking one eyebrow upward. You thought she said that talking was free. "What I said was that you may ask, and I will answer ‘to the best of my abilities,’" she responds. "And suddenly, my ‘abilities’ are feeling woefully inadequate. Unless, of course, you’d like to invoke the powers of the genie and utilize one of your wishes on my ‘story.’" She has unlimited, reality-warping powers, and she’s trying to coerce you into using one of your wishes into telling you her life’s story. And from the resistance you’re getting, you have a feeling that, even if you did use one of your wishes, she’d tell you as little as she can get away with. You acquiesce. You don’t want to hear her personal story that badly. "As you say," she says with a nasally sigh and a scowl on her lips. |She closes her mouth and sighs, her lips crooking diagonally as she considers her response. "It’s perhaps not as exciting as you probably hope it is," she answers. You’ll be the judge of that. She laughs once, lowering her eyes and taking a deep sigh through her nose. "Alright," she answers. "But I don’t know where to start." You have an easy place to start: are genies made? Or are they born? Again, Oma hesitates, unsure of how to answer the question. Or... from the expression on her face, it looks as if she’s trying to make a difficult decision. "I’m not certain of how much I’m at liberty to say," she responds. "There are restrictions for even a genie like myself." She laughs once again, although this time, it was less out of humor and more out of resigned frustration. "After all, I had rules to granting wishes. There are other rules I must abide by as well." But you wished for her freedom. Wouldn’t that mean that she doesn’t have rules to follow any more? "What you’ve given me, [pc.name], is the freedom to act of my own accord; to not need to answer to a master. That doesn’t mean I don’t have my limitations. You are a free [pc.manWoman]; that does not mean you can suddenly breathe underwater." Well... can she at least tell you who, or maybe what, is forcing her into these restrictions? "Who do you suppose?" she answers cryptically. "Who, or what, would have the authority to cow a genie?" ... One of the Seven. "Indeed." [flags.KEROS_MET|This is starting to sound awfully familiar. Oma’s been cursed with untold, unfathomable powers, but, ironically, also to an eternity of servitude and to a set of rules and regulations that she can’t break even with her own godly powers. You take a chance – you have a one-in-seven chance in guessing correctly, and it’s not like you can’t just list all of the names anyway – and ask if it was Keros that had put her in the position she’s in. Oma smiles genuinely, happy with having met something of a kindred spirit in you. "You two must be familiar," she says. "You are correct. It was Keros that had both given me the powers that I have, and had put me in the lamp." If anyone was going to create a wish-granting genie and if Oma was going to take the inspiration to take the very literal meaning of requests from someone, it would be Keros. Why would he do something like that to her, though? You’ve known Keros to be a trickster, and his punishments often fit the transgressions – he wouldn’t have done something like what he did to her just for his own entertainment. "Correct, he wouldn’t have," she answers bitterly.|Does she need you to list off all of their names until you say the correct one, or something? "No need," she answers with a flare of her nostrils. "It was Keros, the Trickster God, that had cursed me with the powers of the genie and had locked me within the lamp for all eternity." The Trickster God? That doesn’t seem like a very funny prank – to enslave an elf and trap her in an oil lamp forever. "Correct, it wasn’t a prank," she answers bitterly.] "In a past life, I was a Lady of a... reasonably sized province, overseeing a population of roughly one-hundred-thousand. ‘Events’ that had caused the fall of the past empire had brought the Seven to the world of Savarra, manifest in mortal forms to help with an invasion of Wraiths. Among them was Keros." Oma averts her eyes as she retells the story. Her sentences are occasionally broken with long pauses as she both reminisces on her past life, and considers what it is she can and can’t talk about. "I had beseeched Keros for the power to assist in what is now known as the Godswar," she continues. "As a Lady, I had considered myself just one step below beings like Keros – and thus, I should wield powers that were one step below the Seven. I had wanted to use the powers he would grant to assist in driving back the wraiths, and while that was the honest truth at the time... enough time has passed that I’ve learned to be more forthright with my intentions. I wanted the powers that I now wield for selfish reasons. To wield them for myself. To further my own status and elevate myself beyond the scope of what I could achieve on my own as a mortal." She pauses for longer than usual. "He granted my request," she says eventually. "I was granted powers that are one step below those of the Seven. But I had to sacrifice my privileges as a Lady in exchange. His phrasing – Gods, I can still hear his damn voice in my head, and that smug, cocksure look on his face – his phrasing was that ‘using the powers was my right; wielding them would be a privilege granted to me with the same leisure I granted my constituents.’" [pc.isBimbo |... Whazzat mean? |... Based on an answer like that, you take it to mean that she wasn’t a nice person before she was a genie. ] "I was an unkind Lady of my province, [pc.name]," she answers sadly. "I lived in opulence – in excess. I had more riches, more power, and more assets than any person would rightly require in their lives. And all the while, my people lived in squalor: disease was rampant; food was scarce; winters were harsh; and I would increase my tax rates every spring. The powers of the genie were mine, but they were not mine to wield; I was to be at the mercy of whoever possessed the lamp as a lesson in humility and empathy." And does she believe she’s learned them? Has Keros’ lesson gotten through to her? "That’s easy to answer now that I’m free," she says. "On the one hand, I believe that I have. Generations upon generations of being trapped in a lamp, waiting for another master to release me and make me their servant for whatever desire they want, has taught me everything from the avaricious greed that human- and other-kind is capable of, to their altruism. Seeing what sort of person I was, and seeing what sort of person I could have been, as reflected upon my many masters over the years, was a... sobering experience." And on the other hand? She pauses, her expression blanking. "On the other hand," she says sternly, fully committed to her own conviction. She stares at her open palm. "I wish I had never met Keros. I wish I had died in the Godswar." That’s very powerful phrasing for a genie. You decide not to push the subject any further – you’ve learned enough. ]
rows.translation: 你让奥玛讲讲她自己的事情。她可真是个“奇才”啊！她肯定有很多有趣的故事可以分享。地狱有一个故事值得讲述。 [oma.isCollared |没什么好说的，”她严肃地回答。 但你根本不相信这一点。你擦亮了油灯，结果一个……人类？精灵？还是一个精灵从灯里冒了出来，说她会满足你的三个愿望。这件事肯定有背后的故事，你肯定想知道。 “那也算一个愿望吗？”她挑起一条眉毛问道。 你还以为她是在说说话是免费的呢。 “我说过你们想问的其实就是这个，”她回答道，“我会尽我最大的能力来回答。但突然间，我觉得自己的‘能力’远远不够用了。当然，除非你们愿意动用精灵的力量，用其中一个愿望来帮助我讲述我的人生故事。” 她拥有无限的力量，能够扭曲现实，现在她正在试图迫使你们用其中一个愿望来帮助她讲述自己的故事。从你们的反应来看，你们似乎觉得，即使你真的使用其中一个愿望，”她会尽量少告诉你一些细节。 你同意了。你确实并不太想听她的个人故事。 “随你的便，”她带着鼻音叹了口气，嘴唇上露出一丝不悦的表情说道。 |她闭上嘴，叹了口气，嘴唇微微上扬，似乎在思考该如何回答。“也许并没有你想象中那么令人兴奋吧，”她说道。 不过，这还是要由你亲自来判断才行。 她轻笑了一声，低下头，然后通过鼻子深深地吸了一口气。好吧，”她回答道，“但我不知道该从哪里开始。” 其实有一个很简单的问题可以入手：精灵是后天被创造出来的，还是与生俱来的？ 然而，奥玛再次犹豫了，不知道该如何回答这个问题。或者说……从她脸上的表情来看，她似乎正在努力做出一个艰难的决定。 “我不太确定自己能说多少，”她回答道，“就连像我这样的精灵，也有一些限制。她再次笑了，但这一次，她的笑声中更多的是无奈与沮丧，而非幽默。“毕竟，我在实现愿望时是有自己的规则的。还有其他一些规则，我也必须遵守。” 但你希望她获得自由。难道这意味着她再没有任何规则需要遵守了吗？ “你给予我的这些东西， [pc.name]，自由，就是能够按照自己的意愿行事，无需向任何人负责。但这并不意味着我没有自己的局限。你也是自由的。 [pc.manWoman]那并不意味着你就可以立刻在水下呼吸了。” 那么……她至少能告诉你这个吧？谁那么，究竟是什么在迫使她遵守这些限制呢？ “你认为会是谁呢？”她神秘地回答道，“究竟是谁，或者是什么，才会有权力让一个精灵屈服呢？” …… 七人之一吧。 “确实如此。 [flags.KEROS_MET|这听起来简直太熟悉了。奥玛被赋予了无数、难以想象的力量，但具有讽刺意味的是，这也意味着她将永远处于奴役之中，必须遵守一系列规则和条例——即使拥有这些强大的力量，她也无法违背这些规定。 你不妨试一试——你有七分之一的机会猜对，而且反正你也可以把所有名字都列出来嘛——然后问问是不是凯洛斯让她陷入了现在的境地。 奥玛真诚地笑了，她很高兴在你身上找到了一个志同道合的人。你们两个肯定很熟吧，”她说。“没错，正是凯罗斯赋予了我这些能力，也是他让我被放进了那盏灯里。” 如果有人要创造一个能够实现愿望的精灵，如果奥玛想要从别人的请求中汲取灵感，并且严格按照这些请求的字面意思来行动的话，那个人肯定就是凯罗斯。但他为什么要那样对待她呢？你早就知道凯罗斯是个喜欢耍花招的人，他的惩罚往往与犯下的过错相匹配——他不会仅仅为了自己的娱乐而做出那样的事来。 没错，他肯定不会那么做的，”她苦涩地回答道。|她是需要你把所有名字都念一遍，直到你说出正确的那个名字，还是别的什么？ “没必要，”她回答道，鼻孔微微张开，“是恶作剧之神凯罗斯给我施加了精灵的力量，还将我永远囚禁在油灯里。” 恶作剧之神？这种把一个精灵囚禁在油灯里永世不得自由的把戏，似乎并不怎么好笑啊…… “没错，这根本不是什么恶作剧，”她苦涩地回答道。]在前世，我是一个管理着一个面积相当可观的省份的女士，那里的人口大约有十万。正是那些导致上一个帝国覆灭的‘事件’，让七位强者降临到了萨瓦拉世界，他们以凡人的形态出现，协助抵御那些幽灵的入侵。其中就有凯罗斯。 奥玛在重述这个故事时，会移开视线。她的句子常常会被长时间的停顿打断，因为她既在回忆自己前世的事情，也在思考哪些事情可以讲，哪些事情不能讲。 我曾恳求凯罗斯赐予我力量，以便能够帮助进行如今被称为‘神战’的这场战斗，”她继续说道，“作为一名女士，我一直认为自己与凯罗斯这样的存在仅相差一步之遥——因此，我也应该拥有仅次于‘七大强者’的力量。我一直想要利用他赋予我的力量来帮助驱赶那些幽灵，而事实上是说实话……如今时间已经过去了足够长的时间，我学会了更加坦率地表达自己的意图。当初，我追求现在所拥有的这些权力，是出于自私的原因。我想把这些权力据为己有，利用它们来提升自己的地位，让自己超越作为一个凡人所能取得的成就范围。她停顿了比平时更长的时间。 “他答应了我的请求，”她最终说道，“我获得了仅次于七大高人的力量。但为此，我不得不放弃自己作为贵族女士所享有的特权。他的那句话——天啊，我至今仍能听到他那该死的声音，在我脑海中回荡，还有他脸上那副自鸣得意的表情——他的说法是：“使用这些力量是我的权利；而运用它们，则是一种特权，我会像对待我的选民们一样，从容地行使这一特权。’" [pc.isBimbo |……你这是什么意思？ |……根据这样的回答，你可以理解为，在她变成精灵之前，她并不是一个善良的人。 ] 在我所在的那个地方，我曾是个冷酷无情的女子[pc.name]，我曾经过着极其奢华的生活，”她悲伤地回答，“拥有的财富、权力和资产远远超出了任何人一生中应有的需求。然而，我的子民却生活在贫困与苦难之中：疾病肆虐，食物匮乏，冬天严寒刺骨，而每年春天，我都会提高税收税率。精灵的力量原本属于我，但我并不能随意使用它们；只要拥有那盏灯的人愿意，我就会任由他们摆布——这就是一堂关于谦逊与同理心的课。 那么，她认为自己真的从中吸取了教训吗？凯洛斯给她的这个启示，她是否真正理解了呢？ 现在我自由了，这个问题就容易回答了，”她说，“一方面，我认为我明白了。世世代代被关在灯里，等待着另一个主人将我释放出来，让我成为他们实现各种欲望的工具，这种经历让我了解了人类以及其他生物所具备的各种特质——从贪婪自私到无私奉献，无一不让我有所领悟。看到我到底是怎样一个人，也了解到我真正的性格特质可以这些经历，正如这些年来我遇到的许多大师们所告诉我的，确实是一次……发人深省的体验。” 那么，另一方面呢？ 她停顿了一下，表情变得茫然。“另一方面，”她坚定地说道，完全相信自己的判断，“我希望自己从未遇到过凯罗斯。我希望自己在神战之中就死了。” 对于一个精灵来说，这样的表达确实非常有力。你决定不再继续这个话题了——你已经了解得够多了。 ]
