rows.original: Well, that was one of your companion’s thoughts on what to wish for from Oma. But [oma.isCollared|you’re not any closer to making any decisions on what you should wish for. You can still get a third opinion, though|there’s still at least one more opinion you could get].
rows.translation: 嗯，那只是你同伴对于该向奥玛许什么愿的一个想法。不过[oma.isCollared|你距离就自己该许什么愿做出决定还差得远呢。你还可以再征求第三种意见|你至少还能再听一种意见]。
rows.raw: " Well, that was one of your companion’s thoughts on what to wish for from Oma. But [oma.isCollared|you’re not any closer to making any decisions on what you should wish for. You can still get a third opinion, though|there’s still at least one more opinion you could get]. "

rows.original: You tell Oma that you think you’re ready. You have something in mind that you’d like to wish from her. [oma.freedomWishedFor |"Yes, by all means," Oma says, her back straightening. Her expression is still stony and difficult to get a real read on, but going by her tone and her sudden posture shift, she’s eager, if not excited, to grant you some wishes. |"They are my command," she drones, her expression and her posture unchanging. For you, this is an opportunity to have anything you could ask for, to bend reality to your very whimsy; for her, it’s just another day. ] You just have to keep in mind Oma’s three rules: She cannot knowingly hurt anyone, not without their permission, and she can’t kill anyone. She cannot change a person’s mind or body. And just as she cannot take life, she cannot grant it. You have options available to you: aside from those three limitations, you can wish for anything.
rows.translation: 你告诉奥玛，你觉得自己已经准备好了。你心里有件事，想要向她许个愿。 [oma.freedomWishedFor |“好的，当然可以，”奥玛说道，她的脊背挺直了。她的表情依然冷峻，很难读出她的真实想法，但从她的语气和突然改变的姿势来看，她还是很乐意的——即便算不上兴奋——愿意满足你的某些愿望。 |“它们听从我的号令，”她语气平淡地说道，表情和姿势丝毫未变。对你来说，这是一个可以求得任何东西、让现实屈从于你奇想的机会；而对她而言，这只不过是平凡的一天罢了。 ] 你只需要记住奥玛的三条规则即可： 她不能在未经他人允许的情况下故意伤害任何人，也不能杀死任何人。 她无法改变一个人的思想或身体。 正如她不能夺走生命一样，她也无法赋予生命。 你有多种选择：除了那三个限制之外，你可以许愿得到任何东西。

rows.original: While unimaginative, who doesn’t love money? More money, less problems, as the saying goes.
rows.translation: 虽然这种想法并不高明，但谁会不喜欢钱呢？俗话说，钱多烦恼少。
rows.raw: "While unimaginative, who doesn’t love money? More money, less problems, as the saying goes."

rows.original: One of the world’s most common fantasies is being able to live forever. And with Oma’s power, that fantasy could be realized.
rows.translation: 世界上最常见的幻想之一，就是能够永生。而凭借奥玛的力量，这个幻想真的有可能成为现实。
rows.raw: "One of the world’s most common fantasies is being able to live forever. And with Oma’s power, that fantasy could be realized."

rows.original: The world of Savarra is home to many different schools of magic, and a genie like Oma wields magic unlike anything you’ve seen before. It’s tempting to try and get a piece of that kind of power for yourself....
rows.translation: 萨瓦拉的世界里存在着许多不同的魔法流派，而像奥玛这样的灯神所掌握的魔法，绝对是你前所未见的。想要为自己弄到一份那样的力量，确实非常诱人……
rows.raw: "The world of Savarra is home to many different schools of magic, and a genie like Oma wields magic unlike anything you’ve seen before. It’s tempting to try and get a piece of that kind of power for yourself...."

rows.original: Oma gave you three very distinct rules on what you can and can’t wish for – but wishing for more wishes was, notable, not among them...
rows.translation: 奥玛给了你三条非常明确的规则，规定了你可以许什么愿，不能许什么愿——但值得注意的是，许下能够再许一个愿的愿望，并不在这些规则之中……
rows.raw: "Oma gave you three very distinct rules on what you can and can’t wish for – but wishing for more wishes was, notable, not among them..."

rows.original: Oma is a genie... but she’s also a person, cursed and enslaved to do the bidding of whomsoever possesses the lamp. There is only one way to break the curse, but she needs a master of strong enough character to wish for it. While that might be you, you’re not smart enough to phrase this wish in a way that keeps all your remaining wishes. Choosing this will use all of your remaining wishes at once.
rows.translation: 奥玛其实是个灯神……但她也是一个普通人，她被诅咒了，必须服从任何拥有那盏灯的人的命令。只有一种方法可以解除这个诅咒，但那需要一位品格足够坚定的主人来许下这个愿望。 而这个人，也许就是你。你还不够聪明，无法用一种既能实现这个愿望，又能保住你其余所有愿望的方式来许下它。选择这个选项将会让你一次性用掉所有剩余的愿望。
rows.raw: "Oma is a genie... but she’s also a person, cursed and enslaved to do the bidding of whomsoever possesses the lamp. There is only one way to break the curse, but she needs a master of strong enough character to wish for it.\n\nWhile that might be you, you’re not smart enough to phrase this wish in a way that keeps all your remaining wishes. Choosing this will use all of your remaining wishes at once."

rows.original: Oma is a genie... but she’s also a person, cursed and enslaved to do the bidding of whomsoever possesses the lamp. There’s only one way to break the curse, but she needs a master of strong enough character to wish for it. Is that going to be you...?
rows.translation: 奥玛是个灯神……但她也是一个人，被诅咒、被奴役，必须服从任何持有那盏灯的人的命令。要打破这个诅咒只有一个办法，但她需要一个品格足够坚强的主人来许下这个愿望。那个人，会是你吗……？
rows.raw: "Oma is a genie... but she’s also a person, cursed and enslaved to do the bidding of whomsoever possesses the lamp. There’s only one way to break the curse, but she needs a master of strong enough character to wish for it. Is that going to be you...?"

rows.original: You’ve already wished for Oma’s freedom and you’ve stipulated that it’s only to be granted after you’ve run out of wishes. But what if you can’t think of anything else to wish for...?
rows.translation: 你早已许下了让奥玛获得自由的愿望，并且规定只有当你的愿望全部用完之后，这个愿望才会实现。但是，如果你再也想不出其他什么愿望来许了……该怎么办呢？
rows.raw: "You’ve already wished for Oma’s freedom and you’ve stipulated that it’s only to be granted after you’ve run out of wishes. But what if you can’t think of anything else to wish for...?"

rows.original: Oma is certainly easy on the eyes, and she’s currently beholden to any wish you ask of her. There’s one in particular that comes to mind.
rows.translation: 奥玛确实非常赏心悦目，而且目前她愿意满足你提出的任何要求。其中有一个特别的请求让我想了起来。
rows.raw: "Oma is certainly easy on the eyes, and she’s currently beholden to any wish you ask of her. There’s one in particular that comes to mind."

rows.original: You do a lot of traveling on foot throughout Savarra, and it’s both time-consuming and physically taxing. Being able to be anywhere you want in the world with just a thought would be a huge boon to your daily routines.
rows.translation: 在萨瓦拉地区，你不得不经常进行长途步行旅行，这既耗时又十分耗费体力。如果能够仅仅通过一个念头就能到达世界上任何你想去的地方，那肯定会对你的日常生活带来巨大的便利。
rows.raw: "You do a lot of traveling on foot throughout Savarra, and it’s both time-consuming and physically taxing. Being able to be anywhere you want in the world with just a thought would be a huge boon to your daily routines."

rows.original: It’s easy to both under- and over-prepare when you’re beginning an excursion. Having a larger carry space would make your journeying so much simpler.
rows.translation: 在开始一次旅行时，人们很容易准备得不够充分，或者准备得过于充分。如果能有更大的携带空间，你的旅途将会变得轻松许多。
rows.raw: "It’s easy to both under- and over-prepare when you’re beginning an excursion. Having a larger carry space would make your journeying so much simpler."

rows.original: Oma sighs deeply through her nose and shuts her eyes, standing still for a moment and absorbing the ambience of the area around herself. She stands still as could be; if you didn’t know any better, you’d sooner think that she’s fallen asleep. "That is three wishes made, and that is three wishes granted," she says without opening her eyes. "My obligations are fulfilled. Our business has concluded, [pc.name]." Wait, that’s it? Oma told you that she would grant you three wishes, but none of them were to your liking or intent! With every wish she granted, your meanings were twisted and transformed until they were something you didn’t want! This can’t be it, you’re not satisfied! Oma, however, pays no attention to your ramblings. Silver smoke begins to seep from the lamp sitting on her upturned hand; as usual, the smoke wraps itself around Oma’s body, first sinking to the ground around her ankles and then coiling around herself like a snake, obscuring her legs, stomach, and chest as it climbs higher, rotating around her body with every new layer it adds to itself. She doesn’t make any attempt to stop the smoke from rising; she stands stock-still, her eyes closed all the while, and she simply lets it all happen. You lunge at her, trying to pull the lamp from her hands; this isn’t over, it can’t be over! She’s a genie with near-infinite powers, and you were promised that your wishes would be granted as long as she was beholden to you! None of your wishes were granted how you wanted; this can’t end like this! Your hand shoots into the smoke where you last saw the lamp, but your entire arm passes clean through the smokey pillar; you don’t even displace to shimmering-silver clouds when you do. You swing and claw at the smoke with both arms, trying to get it to disperse, but nothing works: the haze stubbornly stays in place, and your arms can’t find Oma or her lamp through the clouds anywhere. Eventually, the smoke starts to recede, but not back into the lamp: the pillar of smoke continues to spin, but the smoke slowly sinks into the ground, with the bottommost layer fanning out in every direction. The white cloud washes against your ankles before diffusing into the air, vanishing entirely. As the pillar sinks and sinks, you find that not only is Oma not standing where it was, but the lamp is missing as well. Finally, despite your attempts, the last of the smoke touches down on the ground, fanning away from you and disappearing into the air in a final red wisp. And there you are, on your knees, clawing at the ground where the smoke was in a desperate, vain attempt to reclaim the lamp and the genie within it so that you can get the power – and the satisfaction – you were promised. It takes some time, but after you’ve dug a sizeable hole with your bare hands in your crazy bid to find Oma’s lamp again, you finally admit defeat. Oma is gone. The lamp is gone. You were ‘granted’ three wishes, but you were so hubristic and vain that every wish you made was turned against you, and now, you’re left with nothing. Possibly less than nothing. In between bouts of flaring rage and frustration at Oma and her petulance over not giving you what the fuck you actually wanted, some part of you can’t help but think that maybe there’s a lesson to be taken, here. Whether or not you’ve learned anything is up to you, though.
rows.translation: 奥玛深深地吸了口气，闭上眼睛，静静地站立了一会儿，仔细感受着周围的环境。她一动不动地站在那里，如果你不了解内情，甚至会以为她已经睡着了。 “这样，三个愿望就都实现了，三个请求也都得到了回应，”她闭着眼睛说道，“我的责任已经履行完毕，我们的交易也到此结束了。 [pc.name]等等，就这样吗？奶奶明明说过会满足你的三个愿望，但结果没有一个符合你的意愿或要求！她实现的每一个愿望，都把你的原意歪曲得面目全非，最终变成了你根本不想要的东西！不可能吧，你肯定还不满意！” 然而，奶奶根本没有理会你的抱怨。那盏放在她手掌上的灯开始冒出银色的烟雾；像往常一样，这些烟雾缠绕在奶奶的身体上，先沉降到她脚踝周围的地面上，然后像蛇一样盘绕在她身上，遮住了她的双腿、腹部和胸部。随着烟雾不断叠加，这些层状结构还会继续在她身体周围旋转。她没有试图阻止烟雾上升；她只是站在那里，双眼紧闭，任由一切发生。 你冲向她，试图从她手中夺走那盏灯；这一切还没有结束不能完了！她可是个拥有近乎无限力量的精灵，而你承诺过希望你的愿望能够实现。当然只要她还受你的控制！你的任何愿望都没有得到如你所愿的结果；这样下去是不行的！ 你伸出手，试图去抓住上次看到那盏灯的地方，但你的整只手臂却完全穿过了那片烟雾；即便如此，你也没有感觉到有任何东西被触碰到。你用双手在烟雾中挥舞、抓挠，试图让烟雾散去，但一切都是徒劳的：那片迷雾依然固执地停留在原地，你的手臂在烟雾中根本找不到奥玛和她的灯。 最终，烟雾开始消散，但它并没有重新回到灯笼里：那股烟雾继续旋转着，却缓缓沉向地面，最底层的烟雾向四面八方扩散开来。那片白色的云雾先拂过你的脚踝，然后逐渐消散在空气中，彻底消失了。随着烟雾不断下沉，你发现，不仅奥玛不再站在原来的位置，那个灯笼也不见了。 最终，尽管你付出了种种努力，但最后一缕烟雾还是落在了地上，渐渐消散在空气中，留下一道红色的痕迹。此刻，你跪倒在地，拼命抓挠着那些烟雾曾经停留的地方，试图徒劳地夺回那盏灯以及其中的精灵，从而获得那些曾被承诺给你的力量与满足感。 这确实花费了一些时间，但当你用双手挖出了一个巨大的坑，却依然未能找到奶奶的灯时，你终于不得不承认失败。奶奶已经不在了，那盏灯也消失了。虽然你“得到了”三个愿望，但你的傲慢与自负让每一个愿望都反过来伤害了你，现在，你什么也没有了——甚至可能连什么都没有。 在那些因奥玛及其固执的行为而暴怒、感到沮丧的时刻里，你内心深处总会忍不住想：或许这其中确实蕴含着某种教训。 不过，你是否真的从中吸取了什么教训，那就取决于你自己了。

Oma, however, pays no attention to your ramblings. Silver smoke begins to seep from the lamp sitting on her upturned hand; as usual, the smoke wraps itself around Oma’s body, first sinking to the ground around her ankles and then coiling around herself like a snake, obscuring her legs, stomach, and chest as it climbs higher, rotating around her body with every new layer it adds to itself. She doesn’t make any attempt to stop the smoke from rising; she stands stock-still, her eyes closed all the while, and she simply lets it all happen. You lunge at her, trying to pull the lamp from her hands; this isn’t over, it can’t be over! She’s a genie with near-infinite powers, and you were promised that your wishes would be granted as long as she was beholden to you! None of your wishes were granted how you wanted; this can’t end like this! Your hand shoots into the smoke where you last saw the lamp, but your entire arm passes clean through the smokey pillar; you don’t even displace to shimmering-silver clouds when you do. You swing and claw at the smoke with both arms, trying to get it to disperse, but nothing works: the haze stubbornly stays in place, and your arms can’t find Oma or her lamp through the clouds anywhere. Eventually, the smoke starts to recede, but not back into the lamp: the pillar of smoke continues to spin, but the smoke slowly sinks into the ground, with the bottommost layer fanning out in every direction. The white cloud washes against your ankles before diffusing into the air, vanishing entirely. As the pillar sinks and sinks, you find that not only is Oma not standing where it was, but the lamp is missing as well. Finally, despite your attempts, the last of the smoke touches down on the ground, fanning away from you and disappearing into the air in a final red wisp. And there you are, on your knees, clawing at the ground where the smoke was in a desperate, vain attempt to reclaim the lamp and the genie within it so that you can get the power – and the satisfaction – you were promised. It takes some time, but after you’ve dug a sizeable hole with your bare hands in your crazy bid to find Oma’s lamp again, you finally admit defeat. Oma is gone. The lamp is gone. You were ‘granted’ three wishes, but you were so hubristic and vain that every wish you made was turned against you, and now, you’re left with nothing. Possibly less than nothing. In between bouts of flaring rage and frustration at Oma and her petulance over not giving you what the fuck you actually wanted, some part of you can’t help but think that maybe there’s a lesson to be taken, here. Whether or not you’ve learned anything is up to you, though. '

rows.original: [oma.freedomWishedFor |You’ll ask for an easy one: you want wealth. The modern world of Savarra revolves around money: kingdoms are raised and destroyed by it; fortunes are built on it; survivability depends on it. You never want to have to worry about money ever again, and with Oma’s powers, you can make that a reality. Oma hums, her hand stroking her chin as she considers it. "I was mortal once," she says to you. "And I was in a position of power before I became a genie. I understand the appeal for having more... and I understand better than you might realize the pitfall that comes with never feeling like you have enough." Does she mean that she’s not going to grant you your wish? So that you can learn a lesson in curbing your greed? "Explain to me what it is you want, first. But be very careful not to use the word ‘wish.’" You were just going to w – you were going to ask for money. A massive sum of it, all at once. You want to instantly have enough money to never worry about financial issues ever again. "I’ve granted this same wish many times in the past, and I’ll tell you right now: it’s foolhardy," she explains. "It pays no heed to the logistical challenges that come with it. Say you wish for a million coins – how will you carry them all? Do you have any idea how large one million of anything is?" "You could, alternatively, wish for the money as something else – gemstones, or metal ingots that you could melt or chip off at your leisure whenever you wanted. There’s still the issue of transport; of harvesting; of protecting your hoard against thieves. If you’re not careful, [pc.name], then the more money you might have, the more challenging it becomes to protect it, or to spend it. Wealth is a universal constant that everyone will always covet, but if you have too much of it, you’ll find that your daily challenges are not lesser like you had hoped." What does she recommend, then? "I can grant to you a boon," she continues. She extends her right hand, her palm facing upward, and from it, a wispy, translucent machination appears between her digits: a circular band, about the size of a ring to be fitted on a finger, appearing to be made of unpolished bronze and with no jewels, studs, or engravings upon it. For all the world, it looks like the plainest piece of jewelry imaginable. And it isn’t even real: you try to pinch it between your fingers, but they simply pass through the ring. "I could grant you a one-time surge of wealth. Or, I could grant you this ring: for as long as you wear it, you’ll find that your fortunes will find their way to you at an increased frequency. It’s not a one-time boon of wealth, but it will ultimately grant you more over the course of your life... provided it stays on your finger." While it’s not as immediately rewarding as you had hoped, you have to admit that Oma seems to know what she’s talking about, and she’s trying to give you the best result for your desire. You acquiesce and you follow her instructions: you wish for a ring that, when worn, will increase your wealth over time. Oma smiles wryly; her fist closes, the machination of the ring disappearing in her grip, and when she opens it again, the ring sits in her palm. She extends her hand to you, inviting you to take it, and when you try to pinch it again, this time, it’s real – and it’s perfectly sized to your digits. It could easily be slipped on or off. "Your wish is granted," she says. |You’ll ask for an easy one: you want wealth. The modern world of Savarra revolves around money: kingdoms are raised and destroyed by it; fortunes are built on it; survivability depends on it. You never want to have to worry about money ever again, and with Oma’s powers, you can make that a reality. "You must be more specific," Oma cautions. "Define ‘money.’" [bri.around |[bri.mf |"Hold on," you hear Brint say. You look over your shoulder to see him approach from the camp’s bonfire. "Did I just hear you right? You were about to wish for money?" You... were thinking about it, yeah. "Are we hurting for the cash?" he asks, tilting his head to one side. You wouldn’t say that you were in dire need of some extra float, no. But... well, he knows how it is: it’s always nice to have a little extra handy. Brint hums to himself as he considers what you just said. "Well, you know me," he says. "I prefer the simpler life. I think what we have right now is just perfect. And I know that you’re not me, but... I just worry about how this might end. If there is an end." You ask him what he means by that. "Well, I mean, wishing for a lot of money is going to come with its own problems," he answers "It’s going to be impossible to move and impossible to protect every hour of every day. And what happens if you run out? Will you wish for more?" ... This is getting awfully interrogative coming from a man that just asked if the group was hurting for funds. "There’s a difference between having enough and having more, [pc.name]," Brint cautions. "I just worry that asking to have more than what we need is going to get you started on something that doesn’t have an end." With that, he turns and walks away from you and Oma, saying no more. On the one hand, wishing for money is tempting. You’d never struggle financially again. But on the other, even ignoring all of the logistical issues... Brint is right. Wishing for more would inevitably have you pining for more again later. It might get you started on a path of indulgence and avarice that you might not be able to escape from. A massive – maybe infinite, if possible – pile of electrum coins that could be used to purchase any good or service you could ask for. But you think better of it: there are better, more valuable things than electrum in this world. Silver and gold both come to mind: a single gold coin is worth so much more than a single electrum coin. But you know that there’s even more valuable metals and minerals out there. You could wish for diamonds, but that might be going too far – diamonds are nearly impossible to break or cut, and nobody would want to buy, or even be able to afford, a gigantic diamond off of you. So... what about platinum? Platinum is worth more than gold. You tell Oma that you want enough platinum to solve any money issues you might have for the rest of your life. "You must use the magic word," she says, tilting her head and smiling at you. You say it again, then: you wish for enough platinum that you’ll never run out of money again. The jewel atop of Oma’s lamp, still sitting on her palm, begins to glow. Her irises begin to light up and sparkle, and her shimmering, butt-length white hair begins to levitate behind herself. With a grin, she lifts her free hand and snaps her thumb and middle finger; the sound hits your ears louder than you were expecting, and it seems to echo throughout the air, causing the very wind between you two to ripple and shift. You blink – and beside you, a fair distance from the camp, is a massive, gleaming, pristine and polished block of platinum. It’s larger than a house. It gently molds around the slight hills and dips in the area around your camp and it reaches several stories into the air. You can see the light of your nearby camp radiating off its perfectly smooth surface; you can see your reflection, and Oma’s, even from where you’re standing. You run your hands along its cool, perfectly smooth surface. It’s real. It’s a gigantic ingot of platinum. It’d be worth billions of electrum coins. If you could sell it. You search the ground for a rock that’s heavy enough to lift with both hands and pointed enough that you could try and chip off a piece of the platinum ingot. Your luck pays off and you find one, and you swing it with all your might onto the ingot – and the rock bounces clean out of your hands. You didn’t so much as scratch it.[party.randComp arona agnimitra | You call for Arona to join you at your side, although her eyes are entirely glued onto the gleaming slab of platinum just sitting there in the open field. "Holy shit!" she exclaims as she approaches. "What the fuck – where did this come from?!" Oma stands behind you, her expression unchanged and nonplussed. You ask Arona if she could swing her hammer onto the ingot to try and chip off a piece to sell. It’s made of pure platinum – she’ll need to swing it really hard. "Luckily, being really hard is my job," she says with a smug, confident laugh as she turns and heads back to the campfire to retrieve her hammer. When she returns, she spits into her palms and rubs them together for grip; she spreads her legs and bends her knees for stability; she lifts the hammer up and over her shoulder; and, with a deep, powerful grunt, she swings her hammer with all her might onto the corner of the ingot. The head of her hammer hits the ingot with a loud, echoing 'BONG!’; you can feel the vibration of the impact not just through the ground, but through the air as well. The sound of her hammer’s head hitting the ingot vibrates through the metal for some time. In the distance, whole flocks of birds take off from the trees, cawing into the [dayNight |day |night ] sky. Arona drops her hammer, her fingers locked open from the pain of hitting the ingot with such a huge amount of force. "Fuck!" she shouts, whipping her hands back and forth to try and shake out the shooting pain arcing up her wrists and forearms. Amid all the excitement, you nearly forget to take a look at the ingot. It’s solid. Not a dent on it. With a growl of frustration, Arona bends down to retrieve her hammer to make sure that it wasn’t damaged in the strike. Fortunately, the head of her hammer and its stem survived the impact intact, but you don’t know how much punishment it can take. "Fuck that, I’m not going to risk breaking my shit for this," Arona curses, hefting her hammer up and over her shoulder. "Figure it out yourself, [pc.name]." | You call Agnimitra to your side. With a ruffle of her feathers, she jumps from her spot at the campfire and glides just above the ground towards you, the embers in her feathers lighting up her silhouette as she travels – but she’s distracted by the incredible ingot behind you. "Holy cow!" she exclaims. "That wasn’t here when we got here, right? You don’t see that every day!" Oma stands behind you, her expression unchanged and nonplussed. You explain to Agnimitra that this is a giant obelisk made of pure platinum, and you ask her if she’d be able to use her flames to melt off a chunk of it into a bowl or something. If you can get even just a piece of this to a buyer, you and her and everyone else would be set on money for life. Agnimitra’s expression falls: her brow furrows and her face turns down slightly. "Pure platinum, you said?" she asks, and you confirm. "Do you have any idea what the melting point of platinum is? Especially for a block this size?" You admit that you don’t. She places her hand on the smooth, cold surface of the giant ingot. "I can do this if you really want, [pc.name]," she says, "but to give you an idea of how hot that’d get... try to imagine how hot magma, from a volcano, can get. That’s molten rock that’s come up from within the core of the planet. I’d have to get several magnitudes hotter than that. That’d melt your platinum, but that sort of uncontained heat would also incinerate any organic matter within a few hundred feet of me. Not to mention it’d turn the inorganic matter into, well, magma." ... What if you contained it? "You’d need to build a building larger than this ingot, and it’d have to be insulated several yards thick with material that could withstand my temperatures." She smiles and winks. "I know my stuff when it comes to heat. I’m sorry, [pc.name], but I think this one’s a wash." You hang your head in defeat and she pats you on the shoulder as she makes her way back to camp. ] You angrily turn to Oma. This wasn’t what you wanted! There’s no way you can make anything out of a gigantic ingot that you can’t break down or melt. It’s functionally worthless! "Perhaps you should have considered that." rows.translation: [oma.freedomWishedFor |你会选择一个再简单不过的目标：你想要财富。在萨瓦拉的现代世界中，金钱是一切的核心：王国因此而兴衰；财富由此而积累；生存本身也依赖于金钱。你一定再也不想为金钱而烦恼，而有了奥玛的力量，这个愿望完全可以实现。 奥玛轻声哼着，手托着下巴仔细思考着。“我也曾经是人类，”她对你说，“在变成精灵之前，我曾经拥有过权力。我理解人们渴望拥有更多东西的冲动……而且，比起你想象中的，我更清楚那种永远觉得拥有的东西还不够的陷阱究竟有多危险。她是这个意思吗？她不会满足你的愿望？这样你就能学会克制自己的贪婪了吧？ “先告诉我你到底想要什么。不过，一定要非常谨慎。不是用“希望”这个词来表达吧。询问为了钱。一大笔钱，而且要一次性得到。你希望立刻拥有足够的钱，从此再也不用为财务问题而烦恼。 “过去，我已经满足过很多人这样的愿望了，现在我可以告诉你们：这种想法简直太愚蠢了，”她解释道。它完全忽略了随之而来的物流问题。比如说，如果你想要一百万枚硬币，你该如何将它们全部携带呢？你有没有想过，一百万数量的任何东西到底会有多大呢？” “或者，你也可以选择将这些硬币想象成其他东西——比如宝石，或者金属锭，这样你就可以在需要的时候随时将它们熔化或切割成所需的形状。运输问题依然存在；收获问题也需要解决；此外，还得保护自己储存的物资，防止小偷偷窃。如果不小心的话[pc.name]，那么，你所拥有的金钱越多，保护它或支配它就会变得越困难。财富是一种普遍存在的东西，每个人都渴望得到它，但如果你拥有的财富太多，你会发现，日常生活中的种种挑战并不会像你期望的那样减少。 那么，她建议什么呢？ “我可以赐予你一份恩惠，”她继续说道。她伸出右手，手掌朝上，只见她的手指间出现了一个纤细、半透明的物件：一个圆形的饰物，大小大概与手指上的戒指相当，看起来是由未经抛光的青铜制成，上面没有任何宝石、装饰物或雕刻。从外表上看，它简直就是最普通、最不起眼的饰品了。而且它甚至都不是真正的珠宝：你试着用手指去捏它，却发现手指可以直接穿过这个戒指。 我可以赐予你一次性的财富暴增。或者，我可以赐予你这枚戒指：只要你一直戴着它，你就会发现财富会更加频繁地降临到你的手中。这不是某种一次性的财富恩赐，但只要你一直戴着它，它终将在你的一生中为你带来更多的财富……前提是你必须始终将它戴在手指上。 虽然这并没有带来你期望中的即时回报，但你不得不承认，奥玛似乎确实知道自己在说什么，而且她也在努力为你实现你的愿望而提供最好的结果。 于是你同意了她的建议，并按照她的指示行事。你渴望得到一枚这样的戒指：只要戴上它，你的财富就会逐渐增加。 奥玛苦笑着，握紧拳头，戒指在她的手中消失了，当她再次张开手时，戒指已经稳稳地落在她的掌心。她伸出手，邀请你接过它。当你再次试图捏它时，这次戒指确实是真实的——它的大小正好适合你的手指，可以轻松地戴上或取下。 “你的愿望已经实现了，”她说。 |等等，”你听到布林特说道。你回头一看，发现他正从营地的篝火旁朝你走来。“我听错了吗？你刚才不是在想方设法要钱吗？” 其实……我确实是这么想的，没错。 我们是缺钱了吗？”他歪着头问道。 嗯，你不会说自己急需一些额外的资金，对吧？但是……其实大家都明白：手头多些钱总是好的。 布林特低声自语着，思考着你刚才说的话。“嗯，你了解我的，”他说，“我更喜欢简单的生活。我觉得我们现在的生活状态已经很完美了。我知道你和我不一样，但是……我只是担心这件事最终会如何发展。如果有的话是就这样结束了。” 你问他这句话是什么意思。 “嗯，我的意思是，渴望拥有大量的金钱也会带来相应的麻烦，”他回答道，“这样一来，人们将无法正常生活，也无法保护自己每一天的每一刻。那么，如果你的资源用完了会怎么样呢？你会希望得到更多吗？” ……从一个刚刚询问过这个团队是否缺乏资金的人口中说出这样的话，未免显得太过追问了。“拥有与需要之间是有区别的。足够了并且拥有更多， [pc.name]，”我只是担心，如果要求得到超出我们实际需要的东西，就会让你陷入一个没有尽头的麻烦中，”布林特提醒道。说完，他就转身走开了，再也没有多说一句话。 一方面，渴望得到金钱确实很诱人——那样你就再也不会面临经济上的困扰了。 但另一方面，即使忽略所有这些实际问题……布林特说得对，如果总是渴望得到更多，那么以后你还是会不断地追求更多的东西。这可能会让你走上一条沉溺于享乐与贪婪的道路，而你可能再也无法摆脱它。 或许，你根本就不应该这么做。 |等等，”你听到布蕾妮的声音。你回头一看，发现她正从营地的篝火旁朝你走来。“我刚才听对了吗？你刚才不是在想方设法要钱吗？” “嗯……确实是这么想的。 rows.raw: ' [oma.freedomWishedFor |You’ll ask for an easy one: you want wealth. The modern world of Savarra revolves around money: kingdoms are raised and destroyed by it; fortunes are built on it; survivability depends on it. You never want to have to worry about money ever again, and with Oma’s powers, you can make that a reality. Oma hums, her hand stroking her chin as she considers it. "I was mortal once," she says to you. "And I was in a position of power before I became a genie. I understand the appeal for having more... and I understand better than you might realize the pitfall that comes with never feeling like you have enough." Does she mean that she’s not going to grant you your wish? So that you can learn a lesson in curbing your greed? "Explain to me what it is you want, first. But be very careful not to use the word ‘wish.’" You were just going to w – you were going to ask for money. A massive sum of it, all at once. You want to instantly have enough money to never worry about financial issues ever again. "I’ve granted this same wish many times in the past, and I’ll tell you right now: it’s foolhardy," she explains. "It pays no heed to the logistical challenges that come with it. Say you wish for a million coins – how will you carry them all? Do you have any idea how large one million of anything is?" "You could, alternatively, wish for the money as something else – gemstones, or metal ingots that you could melt or chip off at your leisure whenever you wanted. There’s still the issue of transport; of harvesting; of protecting your hoard against thieves. If you’re not careful, [pc.name], then the more money you might have, the more challenging it becomes to protect it, or to spend it. Wealth is a universal constant that everyone will always covet, but if you have too much of it, you’ll find that your daily challenges are not lesser like you had hoped." What does she recommend, then? "I can grant to you a boon," she continues. She extends her right hand, her palm facing upward, and from it, a wispy, translucent machination appears between her digits: a circular band, about the size of a ring to be fitted on a finger, appearing to be made of unpolished bronze and with no jewels, studs, or engravings upon it. For all the world, it looks like the plainest piece of jewelry imaginable. And it isn’t even real: you try to pinch it between your fingers, but they simply pass through the ring. "I could grant you a one-time surge of wealth. Or, I could grant you this ring: for as long as you wear it, you’ll find that your fortunes will find their way to you at an increased frequency. It’s not a one-time boon of wealth, but it will ultimately grant you more over the course of your life... provided it stays on your finger." While it’s not as immediately rewarding as you had hoped, you have to admit that Oma seems to know what she’s talking about, and she’s trying to give you the best result for your desire. You acquiesce and you follow her instructions: you wish for a ring that, when worn, will increase your wealth over time. Oma smiles wryly; her fist closes, the machination of the ring disappearing in her grip, and when she opens it again, the ring sits in her palm. She extends her hand to you, inviting you to take it, and when you try to pinch it again, this time, it’s real – and it’s perfectly sized to your digits. It could easily be slipped on or off. "Fuck!" she shouts, whipping her hands back and forth to try and shake out the shooting pain arcing up her wrists and forearms. Amid all the excitement, you nearly forget to take a look at the ingot. Fortunately, the head of her hammer and its stem survived the impact intact, but you don’t know how much punishment it can take. "Fuck that, I’m not going to risk breaking my shit for this," Arona curses, hefting her hammer up and over her shoulder. "Figure it out yourself, [pc.name]." | You call Agnimitra to your side. With a ruffle of her feathers, she jumps from her spot at the campfire and glides just above the ground towards you, the embers in her feathers lighting up her silhouette as she travels – but she’s distracted by the incredible ingot behind you. "Holy cow!" she exclaims. "That wasn’t here when we got here, right? You don’t see that every day!" Oma stands behind you, her expression unchanged and nonplussed. You explain to Agnimitra that this is a giant obelisk made of pure platinum, and you ask her if she’d be able to use her flames to melt off a chunk of it into a bowl or something. If you can get even just a piece of this to a buyer, you and her and everyone else would be set on money for life. Agnimitra’s expression falls: her brow furrows and her face turns down slightly. "Pure platinum, you said?" she asks, and you confirm. "Do you have any idea what the melting point of platinum is? Especially for a block this size?" You admit that you don’t. She places her hand on the smooth, cold surface of the giant ingot. "I can do this if you really want, [pc.name]," she says, "but to give you an idea of how hot that’d get... try to imagine how hot magma, from a volcano, can get. That’s molten rock that’s come up from within the core of the planet. I’d have to get several magnitudes hotter than that. That’d melt your platinum, but that sort of uncontained heat would also incinerate any organic matter within a few hundred feet of me. Not to mention it’d turn the inorganic matter into, well, magma." ... What if you contained it? "You’d need to build a building larger than this ingot, and it’d have to be insulated several yards thick with material that could withstand my temperatures." She smiles and winks. "I know my stuff when it comes to heat. I’m sorry, [pc.name], but I think this one’s a wash." You hang your head in defeat and she pats you on the shoulder as she makes her way back to camp. ] You angrily turn to Oma. This wasn’t what you wanted! "Is it not?" she asks you, her expression smooth as water. "You asked for ‘enough platinum that you’ll never run out of money again.’ Those were your precise words. I granted your wish exactly as you had specified it." You ask her how you’re meant to spend this platinum. There’s no way you can make anything out of a gigantic ingot that you can’t break down or melt. It’s functionally worthless! "Perhaps you should have considered that." Your fingers tense and you feel a knot in your throat – before you relax, your shoulders slumping in defeat. There’s nothing you can do about this. Next time, you’ll just have to be more careful about how you phrase your wishes. [lyric.around |Just as you turn away from Oma, you see a flash of green out of the bottom corner of your eye. "Um!" you hear Lyric say, [lyric.hisHer] undivided attention on the gigantic platinum ingot sitting away from the camp. [lyric.HisHer] pupils have dilated to the point of encapsulating [lyric.hisHer] whole eyeballs, and [lyric.hisHer] tail wags with enough force to drag [lyric.hisHer] whole ass back and forth with its momentum. [lyric.HisHer] hands are clasped together at [lyric.hisHer] chest, and a thick waterfall of drool drips from [lyric.hisHer] mouth, which [lyric.heShe] wipes away with the back of [lyric.hisHer] arm from time to time, but it doesn’t stop the slobber from coming. "Um," [lyric.heShe] says again, [lyric.hisHer] eyes going back and forth between you and the ingot again and again rapidly. "Um. Are you. Are you. You know. Um. Are. Are you. Gonna. Are you gonna. [pc.name]. Are you gonna eat that? Um. ‘cause. Um. You know. Kobolds. I’m a kobold. You know. Eating? The metals?" [lyric.HeShe] wipes away another layer of drool. "That’s a lot of metal. A lot of. A lot of delicious metal. I could, you know. If you had no plans or anything. That’s. I could. You know?" Hold on – if Lyric can just chew through platinum, then why doesn’t [lyric.heShe] bite off chunks of it for you to sell? "Oh," [lyric.heShe] says with a start, and it’s as if [lyric.heShe]’s instantly become someone else, just like that. "It’s because kobold saliva is corrosive towards metal. It’ll melt to nothing in our mouth once it’s in there. That’s how we can bite through them in the first place." And just like that, Lyric goes back to the trance-like, babbling kobold [lyric.heShe] was before. "So?" [lyric.heShe] asks, [lyric.hisHer] tail wagging a mile a minute behind [lyric.himHer]self. "The food? The eating? Of the platinum? That’s a thing that could happen. Could that happen?" You sigh. If you can’t make use of the platinum, then at least you can make Lyric’s day one to remember. You tell [lyric.himHer] to have fun. Although it’s a bit of an effort to keep yourself distracted from the sounds of a hungry, happy kobold eating more platinum than what could really be healthy for [lyric.hisHer] figure. ] ] ] '

rows.original: [oma.freedomWishedFor |Maybe Oma can’t empathize as much as a mortal can, since she isn’t one, but death is a common fear among the living. Once you cross that threshold, there’s no going back, and there’s a lot of uncertainty that comes with death: is there an afterlife? Is there any truth to the idea that ‘your life flashes before your eyes’ when you die? Is it simply... nothing? Is everything that you are, were, and could have been, simply lost to the ether once you pass away? While death is most certainly the most ‘known’ of the unknowns – everyone dies, it’s ironically a part of life – you nonetheless... want no part of it. You’d like to live forever, if you could.[party.has Agnimitra | Before Oma has the chance to open her mouth, you hear footsteps rapidly approaching from behind you. "No!" Agnimitra yells, rushing up beside you and slapping her hand across your mouth to keep you from talking. "No, no [pc.heShe] does not wish for immortality! Do not grant that wish!" "Luckily, [pc.heShe] did not use the word ‘wish,’" Oma says with a smirk, "so I am not beholden to grant it." You manage to pry Agnimitra’s hand from your mouth and push her away from you, but before you have a chance to talk, she cuts you off again. "[pc.name], I don’t know how to explain this to you any better than I can with words at their face value: immortality. Fucking. Sucks." She puts her hands together at their palms and bobs her hands with each word to emphasize her point. "Take it from me, someone that is immortal: if it were up to me, I’d wish for it to be gone. It’s a disease. I’m not going to stand here and let someone I care about ruin not just [pc.hisHer] life, but [pc.hisHer] eternity." [pc.isBimbo |Oh. Okay, then! Agnimitra’s eyes widen and her shoulders relax. "Wait, really?" she asks, tilting her head in surprise. "I was... I was kinda ready to argue about this with you." Nah, there’s no need for that. Agnimitra says that you shouldn’t wish for immortality, so you’re not gonna. That’s all you need to know. "Oh." Agnimitra turns to Oma, then to you. She reaches up to preen the base of her plumage on her head. "Well... alright, then." With that, she turns to leave – but she stays within earshot. |That doesn’t change the fact that... that you don’t want to die. It’s a pretty common thing to be afraid of! "Look, I get it," she continues. "I know what it’s like to die. I’ve seen other people die. I don’t know what’s waiting for us on the other side." She angrily points to the ground between you two. "But I also know what it’s like to not die; to keep living when you shouldn’t. I know what it’s like to outlive your family and friends; your home and your people; to watch everyone and everything wither away without you. Immortality sucks." She lifts her hand into the air, palm facing upward – and all five of her digits erupt into flames before she closes her fist, the fire engulfing her hand down to her wrist. "I’m ready to fight you over this, [pc.name]. It’s for your own damn good." You look into Agnimitra’s unflinching eyes beneath her furrowed brow, seeing the fire behind them; her eyes stay completely focused on yours, waiting for whatever it is you might do next. She looks like she’s ready to pounce if you try to pull a fast one and wish for immortality really fast. But... you concede. Agnimitra reels backward very slightly, her brow softening as you say that. Her fist remains raised and engulfed in flame, but her shoulders ease their tension slightly. Being afraid of something as intrinsic as death isn’t something that’s going to ‘go away’ with just a few sentences from someone that might know better like Agnimitra does, but... well, as the saying goes: ‘wise men learn from other’s mistakes; fools from their own.’ It takes Agnimitra a moment longer to finally relax. When she opens her hand, the flame surrounding it disappears. "That’s better," she says, her nostrils flaring as she gives a heavy enough nod that her plumage sways with the motion. "I’ll be sitting by the fire, [pc.name]. You better believe I’m listening in." With that, true to her word, she turns to leave for the campfire, still within earshot. ] | Oma raises her hand, her palm facing toward you. "If I may?" she asks. [pc.isBimbo |‘May’ what? "Speak freely," Oma clarifies. Oh! Yes of course! |You tell her that she can speak freely – you’ve already wished for her freedom. She doesn’t need to ask for permission to speak. ] She smiles as she lowers her hand. "Take it from someone that’s immortal," she says. "There are fewer worse fates in this world. I will grant this wish if you truly desire, [pc.master], but my advice is that you... really shouldn’t." [pc.isBimbo |Aww, why not? |... It’s easy for her to say. She has immortality. She can’t speak for others on their wants. ] "I know that death is an uncomfortable aspect of life, and that the fear of the unknown is a tangible thing that nobody can account for, [pc.name]. But it’s a part of life nonetheless. Imagine the world around you growing, aging, dying, but you remaining the same throughout it all: your friends, family, and loved ones perishing while you remain as you are for all eternity, unable to move on, forever stagnant in a world that’s constantly changing. It takes a certain mindset to watch the continued death and decay of the world around you and, at best, feel nothing." ] You sigh and cross your arms in thought. [party.has Agnimitra |You ask Oma what she suggests. |Then, what does she suggest? ] You’ll listen to what the immortal[party.has Agnimitra |s have | has ] to say about immortality, but that doesn’t change the fact that... that.... "I understand," Oma says soothingly as she turns her hand upward, her fingers splayed apart. "If not immortality, I can grant you something else: a boon of... something akin to invincibility. Which is significantly different." Suddenly, the center of Oma’s palm splits apart, revealing a bloody gash. The wound looks like a clean cut from a sharpened blade, and just as soon as the skin pulls apart, blood begins to pour from it. It’s surprising enough that you do a double-take. Oma, for her part, doesn’t flinch: maybe it’s just a trick that she’s doing for demonstrative purposes. "The body is a marvel in many different ways," she begins. "It takes quite a lot to kill a person, and if the person survives, the body has ways of mending nearly any wound and combatting nearly any disease. It’s easy to believe that life is a fragile thing since you only have one." Oma’s hand begins to glow from the wrist down as an orb of light appears above her fingertips, hovering in place a few inches above the wound. "Though... wounds take time to heal. Diseases require tremendous effort to fight off. These aren’t pleasant experiences and the less time we spend recovering from an injury or an illness, the better." The orb of light sinks into Oma’s palm, right on top of the still-bleeding open wound – and, just as suddenly as the wound appeared from nothing, the skin on her palm pulls and stretches until the gash seals itself shut once more. "The boon I can grant will accelerate your body’s natural healing. It won’t make you immortal or invincible, but any injury you take will heal faster than ever. A cut would be gone without a scar in hours; a bruise will be fully healed in minutes; so much as a headache will be gone before it has a chance to inconvenience you." Well, it’s not deathlessness... but it’s a good wish. You’re convinced. "You must use the magic word," Oma says with a smile and a wink. Taking a moment to consider how to phrase it, you make your wish official: you wish for a boon that will accelerate your ability to heal from any injury you take. The ball of light above Oma’s hand remains stationary as she moves her now-healed hand up and behind it: with a shove of her palm, the orb gently floats through the air before landing on your chest and sinking into your [pc.skinFurScales]. Your heart thumps a little harder for a moment, and you feel a gentle warmth radiate from your chest out to your limbs, and from there to your extremities – and then nothing more. "Your wish is granted," Oma says. New Perk: Semi-Invincibility HP will passively regenerate outside of battle. |You tell Oma that one of the world’s most common fantasies is being able to live forever. You want that. You want to be able to survive anything – you want to beat time itself and outlive your natural cycle. You want immortality: you want to see society advance to achieve their wildest dreams. You want to outlive the very ground you stand on. You want to never have to worry about food, or water, or disease, or injury, ever again. "Immortality is a common wish, yes," Oma says with her usual, practiced droll and her iron-smooth expression. |也许奥玛无法像人类那样产生深切的共鸣，因为她本身就不是人类，但死亡确实是所有生者共同畏惧的东西。一旦跨越了那道门槛，就再也无法回头了，而死亡也伴随着许多未知的因素：究竟是否存在来世呢？人死后，“生命中的种种片段会在眼前闪过”这种说法有没有事实依据呢？难道真的……什么都没有吗？当你离开人世后，你曾经拥有的一切、曾经经历的一切，以及你本来可能成为的一切，都会就这样消失得无影无踪吗？ 虽然死亡无疑是所有未知事物中最“为人所知”的那一部分——毕竟每个人最终都会死去，而这也恰恰是生命的一部分——但讽刺的是，人们却根本不希望面对它。如果有可能的话，谁都不想死去，谁都渴望永远活着。[party.has Agnimitra | 还没等奥玛有机会开口说话，你就听到身后有脚步声迅速靠近。“不行！”阿格尼米特拉大喊着，冲到你身边，用手捂住你的嘴，阻止你说话。“不行，绝对不行！ [pc.heShe]做不是渴望永生吧！不是那就实现那个愿望吧！” “幸运的是， [pc.heShe]我并没有使用‘愿望’这个词，”奥玛带着一丝笑意说道，“所以我也没有义务必须满足你的愿望。” 你好不容易才把阿格尼米特拉的手从自己嘴里拉开，把她推开了，但还没等你开口说话，她又打断了你。[pc.name]，我实在不知道该如何用更简洁明了的方式来向您解释这一点。只能用最直白的语言来说：永生？简直他妈的糟透了。她将双掌心相对，每说一个字就轻轻摆动双手，以此来强调自己的观点。“相信我，作为一个是 不朽者：如果由我来决定，我希望它能够消失。它真的太疾病。我不会坐在这里眼睁睁看着我在乎的人毁掉不仅[pc.hisHer]生命，但是[pc.hisHer] 永恒。” [pc.isBimbo |哦，好吧，那就这样吧！ 阿格尼米特拉的眼睛瞪得大大的，肩膀也放松了下来。“等等，真的吗？”她惊讶地歪着头问道，“我本来还准备和你争论这个问题的呢。 嗯，没必要那么做。阿格尼米特拉说过，你不应该渴望永生，所以你也不会这么做的。你就需要知道这些就行了。” “哦。”阿格尼米特拉转向奥玛，然后又看着你。她伸手轻轻整理了一下自己头上的羽毛。嗯……好吧，那就这样。” 说完，她转身准备离开——不过她还是留在了能听到对方说话的距离范围内。 |但这并不能改变一个事实……那就是你并不想死。害怕死亡是很正常的！”她继续说道，“我明白你的感受。我知道死亡是什么感觉，也见过别人死去；更何况谁知道另一边有什么在等着我们。”她愤怒地指着你们两人中间的地面，“但我也知道没有死去是什么滋味——在本该死去时依然活着。我知道那种比家人和朋友活得更久的感觉；知道那种离开自己的家园和亲人，看着周围的一切都在自己离开后逐渐消逝的滋味。而永生，就是这样的体验。太糟糕了她将手掌朝上举到空中，五根手指瞬间燃起了火焰，随后她握紧了拳头，火焰顺着她的手臂蔓延到了手腕。“我准备为此与你一战。 [pc.name]这是为了你自己的好。” 你凝视着阿格尼米特拉那双坚定的眼睛，她的眉头紧锁，但眼中燃烧着坚定的光芒；她的视线始终紧盯着你，等待着你接下来的举动。她看起来就像随时准备扑上来一样，只要你试图耍花招、过快地许下永生的愿望，她就会立刻行动。 但是……你还是选择了妥协。 当你这么说时，阿格尼米特拉微微后退了一步，她的眉头也放松了下来。她的拳头依然高高举起，周围环绕着火焰，但她的肩膀却稍微放松了一些。 对于死亡这样根本性的恐惧，仅仅依靠像阿格尼米特拉这样懂得道理的人说上几句话，是远远无法消除它的。嗯，正如俗话所说：“智者从他人的错误中学习，愚者则从自己的错误中学习。” 阿格尼米特拉又过了好一会儿才终于放松下来。当她张开手时，围绕在她手中的火焰也随之消失了。这样就好多了，”她说，鼻孔微微张开，用力点了点头，以至于她身上的羽毛都随着这个动作晃动起来。“我会坐在火堆旁[pc.name]你最好相信，我一直在听呢。” 说完，她果然没有食言，转身朝着篝火的方向走去，不过她的声音仍然在耳边回荡。 ] | 奥玛举起了手，手掌朝向你。“可以吗？”她问道。 [pc.isBimbo |May’什么？” “大胆说出来吧，”奥玛解释道。 哦！对了，当然可以！ |你可以告诉她，她可以自由地发言——你早就希望她能够拥有自由了。她根本不需要征求别人的许可才能说话。 ] 她微笑着放下了手，说道：“相信一个永生不灭的人的话吧。这个世界上，几乎没有比这更糟糕的命运了。如果你真心渴望得到这个愿望，我就会满足它。 [pc.master]但我建议你……真的不应该这么做。 [pc.isBimbo |哎呀，为什么不呢？ |…对她来说，说出来当然很容易。但她拥有永生。她无法代表其他人的意愿来表达他们的需求。 ] 我知道死亡是生活中令人不安的一部分，而对未知的恐惧也是一种真实存在、无人能够解释的情绪。 Is there any truth to the idea that ‘your life flashes before your eyes’ when you die? Is it simply... nothing? Is everything that you are, were, and could have been, simply lost to the ether once you pass away? While death is most certainly the most ‘known’ of the unknowns – everyone dies, it’s ironically a part of life – you nonetheless... want no part of it. "I understand," Oma says soothingly as she turns her hand upward, her fingers splayed apart. "If not immortality, I can grant you something else: a boon of... something akin to invincibility. Oma, for her part, doesn’t flinch: maybe it’s just a trick that she’s doing for demonstrative purposes. "The body is a marvel in many different ways," she begins. "It takes quite a lot to kill a person, and if the person survives, the body has ways of mending nearly any wound and combatting nearly any disease. The orb of light sinks into Oma’s palm, right on top of the still-bleeding open wound – and, just as suddenly as the wound appeared from nothing, the skin on her palm pulls and stretches until the gash seals itself shut once more. rows.original: You say it again, then: you wish for immortality. You want to live forever. "As you wish," Oma says, lifting her free hand from her behind her back. When it’s in the air between you two, she snaps her fingers, the sharp sound reverberating through the air. At first, nothing happens. You stand where you are, expecting something, anything – a feeling within you to change; a flow of strength to course through your arms and legs – but there’s nothing of that sort. Is there not supposed to be? Do you need to test out your newfound immortality? You’d rather not risk it.... The ground beneath your feet begins to rumble, the vibrations coursing up through your legs, almost knocking you off-balance. The seismic activity increases in intensity rapidly – it feels like it’s coming up from directly beneath you. Suddenly, the very ground splits apart as two, enormous, hollowed-out crystals, each slightly larger than you are, pierce the earth, one on either side of you, surrounding you like the pincers of a crab’s claw. And, just like a claw, once the two crystals are out of the ground, they snap shut around you, trapping you between them. Although they’ve been hollowed out to allow for your frame, it’s only just: you have no room to move even a fraction of an inch of any part of your body. Your fingers are locked; your arms are jammed; your legs are held still; you don’t even have any room to breathe. You’re absolutely encased within the two crystals – and, just as suddenly as they sprang from the earth, they recede once they’ve trapped you within them, pulling you into the darkness of the ground as they go. The last of the light above the surface of the world is cut off when the soil spills in from above you, burying you in your crystal tomb. The rumbling of the earth continues around you, and you can feel the vibrations through the walls, until they eventually stop as well – and all there is, is darkness and silence. At first, your heart races, and you try to panic... but you can’t move. You can’t even breathe. You can hardly blink. You’re trapped, completely and utterly, in the darkness of the earth and inside your crystalline coffin. Quickly, however, exhaustion overtakes you. You’re scared and confused – this isn’t what you wished for! – but... it gets harder and harder to worry as time goes by. Not because there’s nothing to worry about, but because you’re just... so sleepy. Even though your heart is racing, and even though it’s so tight inside the crystal that you can hardly blink, eventually, you drift to sleep, eyes still open. You aren’t sure how much time passes until that happens. It feels like a few seconds, but without the light of the sun, it could have been days, or months, or years. There you stay, within the depths of the earth, perfectly preserved: unaging, invulnerable to death, injury, or disease, for the rest of eternity. Or until someone digs and chisels you out.
rows.translation: 你说得对，那么就这样吧。你渴望永生，希望永远活着。 如你所愿，”奥玛说着，将背在身后的那只手抽了出来。当她的手悬在你们两人之间时，她打了个响指，清脆的声音在空气中回荡。 起初，什么也没有发生。你们依然站在原地，期待着什么——任何事情都行：体内有某种感觉发生变化；力量涌向你的四肢……但这一切都没有发生。难道不应该这样吗？你是想测试一下自己新获得的“永生”能力吗？不过你似乎并不愿意冒险…… 你脚下的地面开始震动，这些震动从你的双腿传向全身，几乎让你失去了平衡。地震活动的强度正在迅速增加——那种震动感觉就像是从你的正下方直接传来的。 突然间，地面裂开了，两颗巨大的、中空的晶体从地底钻了出来，每一颗都比你还要大一些，它们分别出现在你的两侧，将你包围在中间，就像螃蟹的钳子一样。而且，就像一只爪子一样，一旦这两块晶体从地面被挖出来，它们就会迅速闭合，将你困在中间。 虽然这些晶体已经被挖空，以便让你的身体能够穿过，但实际上只是你的身体没有任何部位可以移动半分。手指被锁住，手臂无法动弹，双腿也被固定住，甚至连呼吸的空间都没有。你完全被这两块水晶包裹住了——而就在它们从地面突然出现将你困住的同时，它们又突然消失了，将你拉入了地下的黑暗之中。 当土壤从上方倾泻而下，将你埋葬在这段水晶构成的墓穴之中时，世界上方最后一丝光线也被彻底切断。大地的震动持续不断，你能够通过墙壁感受到这些震动，直到它们最终也消失了——此时，只剩下黑暗与寂静。 起初，你的心跳加速，试图陷入恐慌……但却动弹不得。你甚至无法呼吸，几乎无法眨眼。你彻底被困在了大地的黑暗之中，也被困在了那具水晶制成的棺材里。 然而，很快，疲惫感就会笼罩你。你感到害怕和困惑——这根本不是你所期望的！——但是……随着时间的推移，继续担心反而变得越来越困难。并不是因为没有什么值得担心的，而是因为你 simply……已经无力再去担心了。……如此困倦。尽管你的心跳得飞快，尽管在那个水晶之中你感觉窒息得几乎无法眨眼，但最终，你还是睡着了，眼睛依然睁着。你也不清楚过了多久才睡着。虽然感觉上只过了几秒钟，但在没有阳光的情况下，那些时间也可能是几天、几个月，甚至几年的时间。 你就这样被埋藏在地球的深处，得到了完美的保存：永不衰老，既不会死亡，也不会受到伤害或疾病的侵袭，这样的状态会持续永恒。 直到有人挖出你，将你从那里带出来。

rows.original: [oma.freedomWishedFor |Oma has unique abilities that no other magician in Savarra could boast. It’s one thing to conjure a fireball or a bolt of lightning from your fingertips; it’s quite another to be able to create something with mass. A physical object that could be held and interacted with. The closest that any school of magic can get to that is polymorphization, and maybe conjuration, but Oma’s powers go beyond that. It’s risky, but you ask Oma if it’d be possible for you to have even a fraction of that kind of power. You imagine that it might be possible if you yourself were made into a genie, but that might mean being made a slave to a lamp, just like she is – or, was, very soon. Oma twists her mouth wryly as she considers the question. "In a sense, yes, I can grant this wish, but...." She pauses as she tries to consider how to finish the thought. "I’ve had masters that have wished for power before, but ‘power’ is a nebulous thing to ask for. Some of them referred to it as physical strength; some of them referred to it as magical aptitude; some of them referred to it as political power, or influence over others. And these are all things that I can grant, provided the wish is worded properly." So, is that the issue, then? You just need to phrase your wish as carefully as possible? "Well, no; there are specific limitations to what you are asking for," she continues. "You want power like mine; to essentially be able to grant your own wishes without the drawbacks of being enslaved to a lamp as I had. This is not within my capabilities. I can grant you power equal to my own, but that includes," she pauses, hefting the lamp in her hand for emphasis, causing the giant golden chain to rattle with its movements, "the deficits. And I cannot grant this wish in fractions; it is impossible to quantify what ‘one-tenth’ of my capabilities are." [pc.isBimbo |Well, dang. You were hoping you could do something like... drop anvils on the bad guys during a fight. Or make it sunny when it’s raining. Or make it rainy when it’s too hot and sunny. Oh! How about – and you tell Oma to follow along with you on this one – you’re in a fight against some bad guys, so you make it rain anvils on them! But only on them. You don’t want to be caught in the middle of an anvil storm. Oma smiles crookedly and brings a hand to her chin as she considers your fantasy. "Well, making it rain anvils would be within my power," she says with a laugh. "But playing with the fabric of reality like that is something that’s going to come with repercussions." She hefts the lamp in her hand once again. Oh. Lame. "But," she continues, her eyes wandering back and forth as she does some quick calculations in her head, "there may be an alternative." Oh. Yay! |That’s unfortunate, but you suppose it makes sense. You aren’t sure how you’d be able to quantify Oma’s abilities like that, either. And, on reflection, you aren’t even sure what you’d use powers like that for – it’s not like it’s difficult to use alchemy to [pc.hasRealCock |make your dick bigger |make your ass fatter ] or whatever. The only real application you could think of would be for combat, and she said herself that her powers can’t be used to hurt someone. Oma furrows her brow and rests her chin on her hand as she considers your options. "Well, there are two caveats to that, actually," she says. "The first is that the exact wording on my limitations is that I cannot directly harm someone. If, for example, I were to light a campfire for warmth, and then someone were to burn themselves on it, that would be through no fault of mine." ... What’s the difference between that and using a fire offensively? "The difference between lighting a campfire and throwing a fireball at someone is intent, [pc.master]," she says with a light chuckle. "The second caveat is that... you are not me. You are not bound by the same rules as I would be." Is that important? ] "What I could do is grant you the ability to perform one action specifically," she says. She turns her free hand over, palm facing upward, and from it, a tiny storm cloud forms about a foot away from her skin, hovering squarely above her hand. The occasional lightning bolt strikes from the cloud to one of her five digits. "Creating a storm cloud and having its bolts strike at your targets is not something that would stress the limits of reality[pc.isBimbo | like having it rain anvils would ]. It’s not the ‘fraction of my capabilities’ that you were initially hoping for, but it is nonetheless tangible power that could be summoned on your whimsy." And there are no drawbacks? "None as extreme as being beholden to a lamp and whomsoever possesses it." Well... it’s not quite what you had imagined when you started this line of thought. But you suppose it’s also going to be as close as you can get without wearing a golden choker with a massive chain on it. Oma stands still and upright, awaiting you to say the magic word so that she can grant it. So you put it to words: you wish for the power to summon lightning from the sky to strike your opponents. "Hold out your hand, palm upward," Oma says, and you follow her instruction. She hovers her hand above yours, her fingertips a few inches away – and then static bolts of electricity arc between her fingers and yours, zapping into your digits. Despite the suddenness and the intensity, it doesn’t hurt. In fact, you don’t feel much of anything at all. "Your wish is granted," she says, stepping back and resuming her posture. You flex your fingers a few times, trying to see if anything feels different, but nothing does. You ask her how it’s supposed to work. "It works similarly to how I utilize my own powers. You simply will it to be." ... Can you test it right now? "What, on me?" she asks, her mouth curling into a wry grin. You can’t tell if she’s okay with the idea and she’s goading you to trying it. Well.... "Go ahead," she says with a laugh. Now that you have her permission, you do as she instructed: you simply think about summoning lightning from the sky, trying to ‘will’ it into existence, to strike Oma right in front of you. You aren’t sure how much focus you’re meant to put into it, and you don’t know if you can control how intense the lightning is– While you’re fretting over the specifics, a bolt of lightning arcs through the air, landing directly on top of Oma. The air crackles with static, causing [pc.sfs |the hair on your arms to stand on end |the fur on your whole body to stand on end |the scales on your body to tingle from your head to your toes |your whole body to feel tingly, from your head to your toes ]; the boom of the strike rattles your ears and dazes your senses. It takes a while for your eyes to readjust and your ears to stop ringing. Oma stands where the lightning struck, completely nonplussed by the display. It’s as if she’s not even there. "Just like that," she says. Out of curiosity: could you have asked to be made into a genie like herself, and then have her possess your lamp and then wish for your freedom? Oma tilts her head and thumbs at her chin as she considers it. "I cannot, no," she answers. "A genie cannot be made in service to a genie, nor can a genie be made to master a genie. Nor can we communicate with each other: I’ve granted the ill-thought-out wish exactly once before, and I have no idea what became of my previous former master, and despite my occasional attempts, I cannot locate their lamp in the cosmos." She scratches at her neck as she continues to think. "You could, in theory, have a friend or family member do this... but your lamp will disappear into the ether for four years upon the wish being granted and will reappear anywhere in Savarra after one decade has passed. They would need to locate your lamp on their own." So much for that line of thought. |Oma wields powers unlike anything else the world of Savarra has seen. It’s one thing to conjure a fireball or shoot lightning from your fingers or something, but Oma is capable of creating real, tangible matter in the palm of her hand, or on scales of incomprehensible size. Reality is her plaything, and she is bound to whoever possess the lamp. Frankly, you want a piece of that for yourself. It’s hard to resist the temptation of [silly |phenomenal cosmic powers |reality-warping powers ] like hers. You don’t want the responsibilities and limitations of being a genie yourself, but... if it’d be possible to take even a fraction of that for yourself, there would be few in this world who would be able to challenge you. Oma takes a deep sigh through her nose, but otherwise remains totally stationary, as always. Back straight; the lamp resting on her upturned palm; her expression made of stone and impossible to read. [kiyoko.around |Before you have the chance to put your thoughts to words, however, you feel a hand gently place itself on your shoulder, gently-but-insistently pulling you backward for your attention. "Pardon me, beloved," you hear Kiyoko’s smooth voice say, "but I need your attention, if you do not mind." You tell her that you were in the middle of something. "Yes, precisely," she says with a smile. "I had been practicing my divinations by burning tea leaves in the bonfire just now. You were about to wish for power from Oma, correct?" That’s... yeah, that’s right. You wanted to wi– Kiyoko places her index finger on your [pc.lipsChaste]. "Do not say that word." You wanted to ask Oma for power not unlike hers. She’s a genie; the level of magic she’s capable of is a step beyond what even the most powerful sorcerers of Savarra can accomplish. You wanted a piece of that for yourself. "A tempting thing to wish for," she acknowledges, "but you must not." Why is that? "Because Oma will willfully twist your words against your intent," she explains. "I do not know what, specifically, she intends to do. All I know is that it will not end well for you." You turn back to Oma, trying to scan her expression for any sign that Kiyoko might be right or wrong. And, as usual, Oma stands totally stone-faced, her back straight, the lamp in her hand unmoving; she’s impossible to read – although you can see her brow furrowing as she stares directly at your kitsune. You ask Kiyoko if she’s sure. "I was right about you asking for power, was I not?" she asks, tilting her head and smiling, her ears perking just once above her head. "No matter how carefully you phrase the wish, the word ‘power’ is, by itself, obtuse and general. It could mean anything. She could grant you power by setting you on fire or zapping you with lightning, for all we know." You suppose those are fair points. Oma may be beholden you to as the possessor of her lamp, but that doesn’t mean you can relax around her: if you really want to make a wish, you need to be absolutely foolproof in your wording, and there’s no real way to wish for ‘power’ when the word itself could mean anything. "I am glad I could help," Kiyoko says, leaning in to give you a quick kiss. "Be sure to spend your wishes wisely, beloved. I would not want anything untoward to happen to you." With that, she turns back to her camp to practice her divinations once more. |After a moment of deliberation with yourself to make sure that this is, indeed, what you want, you steel your resolve and turn to face her. As concisely as you can, you say that you wish to Oma that you want power. You want to wield power not unlike hers: you want reality to bend to your whims just by thinking it. Oma closes her eyes for a moment as she inhales through her nose, and when they open again, her irises shimmer from silver to every color in the spectrum before settling down once again. "Your wish is granted," she says. You open your hands and look down at them, flexing your fingers a few times. You don’t feel any different.... Just as you look back up to Oma, an arc of lightning shoots down from the sky, landing directly on top of you. Electricity courses through your entire body, making every cell of your [pc.skinFurScales] light up with pain. A split second later, and the boom of a thunderclap rattles your ears loudly enough that it feels like your eardrums are about to burst. The electricity of the lightning bolt lasts only a fraction of a second, but the lingering pain and numbness through your body lasts for much, much longer than that. You sink to your knees, your arms and shoulder occasionally fidgeting from the leftover static still tensing your muscles involuntarily. It takes a long moment for the pain to subside to numbness, and that’s only marginally better. When you can finally feel your tongue in your mouth again – and you have the strength to move your jaw – you shout at Oma that this obviously wasn’t what you wished for. You wanted power like hers! She can conjure materials from nothing; she can warp the very reality around herself with a thought! "As can you, now," she responds. "There is a rock the size of your hand to your right. Touch it." You glance to your right, and, sure enough, there’s a rock, just a few inches away from your hand. The pain still has your fingers acting jittery and unsteady, but you do as she says and you reach for the rock – and, just as your fingers glance its surface, a tiny bolt of static electricity jumps between you and it, giving you one last bite and forcing you to yank your hand away in surprise. "And with that, reality has been forever altered," Oma says. What – that’s – that’s not what you wanted at all! Not even a little! You wanted to be able to do that on command, on a much larger scale, using powers similar to her own! You wanted to be able to conjure something from nothing with just a thought! "Then let this be a lesson in specificity," she responds, completely deadpan and stone-faced. You look down at your hands and flex your fingers once again. Now that the static is wearing off, the feelings in your digits are slowly starting to return. As a test, you reach out to the same rock once more, tepidly touching its smooth surface with the tip of your index finger – and nothing happens. In some small, imperceptible way, reality has been forever altered. Just not the way you had envisioned. ] ]

It’s one thing to conjure a fireball or a bolt of lightning from your fingertips; it’s quite another to be able to create something with mass. A physical object that could be held and interacted with. The closest that any school of magic can get to that is polymorphization, and maybe conjuration, but Oma’s powers go beyond that. It’s risky, but you ask Oma if it’d be possible for you to have even a fraction of that kind of power. You imagine that it might be possible if you yourself were made into a genie, but that might mean being made a slave to a lamp, just like she is – or, was, very soon. Oma twists her mouth wryly as she considers the question. "In a sense, yes, I can grant this wish, but...." She pauses as she tries to consider how to finish the thought. "I’ve had masters that have wished for power before, but ‘power’ is a nebulous thing to ask for. Some of them referred to it as physical strength; some of them referred to it as magical aptitude; some of them referred to it as political power, or influence over others. And these are all things that I can grant, provided the wish is worded properly." So, is that the issue, then? You just need to phrase your wish as carefully as possible? "Well, no; there are specific limitations to what you are asking for," she continues. "You want power like mine; to essentially be able to grant your own wishes without the drawbacks of being enslaved to a lamp as I had. This is not within my capabilities. I can grant you power equal to my own, but that includes," she pauses, hefting the lamp in her hand for emphasis, causing the giant golden chain to rattle with its movements, "the deficits.
