The pain still has your fingers acting jittery and unsteady, but you do as she says and you reach for the rock – and, just as your fingers glance its surface, a tiny bolt of static electricity jumps between you and it, giving you one last bite and forcing you to yank your hand away in surprise. "And with that, reality has been forever altered," Oma says. What – that’s – that’s not what you wanted at all! Not even a little! You wanted to be able to do that on command, on a much larger scale, using powers similar to her own! You wanted to be able to conjure something from nothing with just a thought! "Then let this be a lesson in specificity," she responds, completely deadpan and stone-faced. You look down at your hands and flex your fingers once again. Now that the static is wearing off, the feelings in your digits are slowly starting to return. As a test, you reach out to the same rock once more, tepidly touching its smooth surface with the tip of your index finger – and nothing happens. In some small, imperceptible way, reality has been forever altered. Just not the way you had envisioned. ] ] '

rows.original: You think back to the three rules that Oma had laid out for you when it comes to wishing for something from her. The first was that she cannot harm anyone that doesn’t already want it – that’s an odd caveat, but you suppose there could be any circumstances where someone might want, or need, to be injured for something, like wishing for a wound to be cauterized or whatever. The second is that she cannot infringe upon anyone’s personal autonomy: you can’t wish for [pc.hasRealCock |a bigger dick, or ]bigger muscles, or longer hair, or anything like that. And the third was that she cannot create or grant life: she can’t bring back anyone from the dead, nor can she create life from whole cloth. [oma.freedomWishedFor |There’s a pretty distinct loophole in the rules that she’s laid out for you, but, well... you don’t want to try and take advantage of her good mood by trying to lock her into granting you more wishes. Although, you did wish for her to be free ‘after she granted [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |your next wish |your next two wishes | ],’ so, maybe even if you asked for more wishes, it wouldn’t matter? Well, in any case, you ask Oma: for your own curiosity, would it have been possible for you to wish for more wishes? You don’t intend to; you just want to know. Oma laughs. "It’s one of the most common wishes from all my previous masters," she says. "Every other master wishes for more. Three just isn’t enough. It’s refreshing to finally meet someone that not only wished for my own freedom, but is okay with just [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one |two | ]!" "To answer your question, no, it is not possible to wish for more wishes," she answers, her mouth crooking diagonally into a wide smirk. "When I first appeared from the lamp, I very specifically said ‘whomsoever possesses the lamp is entitled to three wishes.’ Wishing for more wishes is such a common thing that I’ve taken up the habit of messing with any master that wishes for it with specificities and word plays – things like ‘it takes one wish to grant one wish,’ so they just wind up back to where they started[var0 |. You are one of the few masters that took is so far and tried to game my restrictions so much that it actually cost you a wish." You ask if you wishing for her freedom afterward changes her opinion of you. "Somewhat. You’re definitely the only one that ever actually learned from their hubris, but on the other hand, you had that kind of hubris to start with. Whether overcoming your greed is better than not having greed at all is a philosophical question that, frankly, I just don’t feel like answering ]." She laughs again. At the very least, you didn’t lose any wishes asking that question. Now you know for sure that you only have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 |one wish |two wishes ] left, and no amount of proper phrasing or word-twisting is going to get around that. |There’s... a pretty distinct loophole here. You ask Oma what’s stopping you from wishing for more wishes. "Nothing," she answers flatly. ... Wait, really? "Wishing for more wishes is a common wish. One of the most common, in fact." Her face is completely smooth and her eyes are deadlocked on yours – she’s serious as could be. "There is nothing preventing you from wishing for it." Uh... in that case... you wish to have four wishes. Oma’s eyes close for a short moment, and when she opens them again, the colors of her irises swirl across every color in the spectrum before settling on silver once again. "Granted," she says. "You now have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one wish |two wishes |three wishes ] remaining." Wait, that’s not how that works. "It requires one wish to grant you one wish," she explains. "With every new wish I grant you, one wish is expunged from your allowance. You have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one wish |two wishes |three wishes ] remaining." You [pc.isBimbo |kinda |already ] figured where this is going, but: you wish for ten thousand wishes. Again, Oma’s eyes close for a moment, and when she opens them again, her silver irises go through the whole rainbow before settling back to normal. "Granted. You now have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one wish |two wishes |three wishes ] remaining."[pc.cunningRange 0 40 | Well, damn, you’re out of ideas. You thought you had found a pretty clever loophole in her ‘contract,’ but in the end, you’re back where you started. At least you didn’t lose any wishes. | Hmm. There has to be a way around that limitation of hers somehow. If it weren’t possible to wish for more wishes, she would have said so with her rules. What if... what if you could grant your own wishes? You’d have no need for Oma. If you had the sort of power that she has, to be able to grant your own wishes, you’d have everything that you could want right then and there. You’d be set for life – maybe for eternity! Still, though, before you jump to conclusions, you ask Oma if that were possible. Can you wish to become a genie and grant your own wishes? "Yes," she answers plainly, "I can grant your wish for you to become your own genie. No; you cannot grant your own wishes." With her free hand, she grips onto the golden chain connecting her choker to her lamp. "I would not still be wearing this if that were the case." So, wait, she’s suggesting that– "To grant you your wish of becoming a genie would mean being consigned to a prison of your own, cursed to an eternity of servitude," she answers for you. "How do you believe I became a genie myself?" She raises her right hand, her fingers flexed and pointed upward; a dim green light begins to glow from the tips of each of her digits, followed by an orb of light hovering just a few inches above her palm. "I am prepared to grant this wish, [pc.master], if you’d simply use the magic word." ][pc.cunningRange 0 60 | You tell her that that’s quite alright; the message has been received. You’re not about to wi – you’re not about to ask for that. Maybe you should stop trying to dig for loopholes while you’re ahead. | You grunt in frustration and wave your hand at Oma, wordlessly signaling for her to forget the idea. What’s the point in wielding ultimate power if you can’t use it for yourself? Still, you’re undeterred. All this has done is bring you back to the basics: you’re determined to figure out the loophole to Oma’s rules. You’re onto something; you just need to hone in a little bit. Maybe... well, Oma is one genie. One genie equals three wishes. Maybe the solution is to wish for more genies? Could that work? You haven’t burned [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |your last wish |all of your wishes |any of your wishes ] yet, so, might as well give it a try: you tell Oma that you wish for more genies to grant you wishes. Oma closes her eyes again, and silver smoke begins to pour from the lamp’s spout at an incredible rate. The smoke falls to the ground and begins to pile up on itself over and over, circling around itself as if it was wrapping around a tall pillar. By the time the smoke cloud reaches as high as Oma is standing, just as suddenly as it started, all of the smoke begins to recede back into the lamp – and, standing where the smoke once was, is a second Oma, taking a similar posture as the original one, lamp and golden choker and all. When the smoke fully recedes, both of the Omas open their eyes, their irises a shimmering rainbow of colors before settling back on their normal silver sheen. "Your wish has been granted," they both say at the exact same time. Before you open your mouth to at least ask how many wishes you have, the first, original Oma closes her eyes again. "My duty has been fulfilled," she says, and, as before, silver smoke flows from the spout of the lamp sitting on her hand. The smoke falls to her feet and quickly wraps around her body, making its way up her legs, her torso, her head, obscuring her entirely – and after rotating in place for a moment, the smoke appears to vanish back into what you’d presume is the lamp once again, but when the smoke dissipates, there’s simply nothing remaining at all. The silver smoke simply turns to air, leaving nothing behind. The second Oma, seemingly nonplussed by the situation, takes a quick sigh through her nose, her expression otherwise stoic. "I am at your command, [pc.master]," she says. "I am Oma. I am a denizen of the lamp. I am here to grant you [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one wish |two wishes |three wishes ]." You ask her what her justification is for not giving you more wishes this time. "The same as before," she replies matter-of-factly. "I am indeed still bound to grant you [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one wish |two wishes |three wishes ]. It required one wish to grant you one wish." ][pc.cunningRange 0 90 | You could probably think of other ways to try and work this supposed loophole that you think you found, but you’re pretty sure you’re seeing a pattern here. It’s not worth the headache of trying to finagle the rules the way you want them. | You snort through your nose – you’re smarter than this. There’s a loophole here somewhere and you’re pretty sure you’re getting close to finding it. Having more wishes is a thing that you can have, you’re certain of it. [arona.around |Just as you close your eyes to really put some long, hard thought into how to phrase your wish so that you can get more, you hear Arona’s voice booming through the air, hitting your ears like a drum. "Hey, [pc.name]!" she shouts jovially, laughing once, apparently proud of something. "Check this out!" You turn back towards the campfire, and there is Arona, her war hammer held tightly in her grip – with its head set ablaze, the fire wicking off its metal, although the flame is weak. You doubt the flame would survive a swing. "Fuck yeah, right?!" she laughs, hefting it up a bit. "I got the idea to cover my hammer in booze, and now I can do this!" She spins the hammer in her grip. "It’s not a very strong flame, though. It’ll only last for a little bit. But still, fuck yeah!" She smiles at you widely enough to show you her molars. "Can you imagine? I’d really bring the heat to the heat of the battle!" To demonstrate her apparent mastery of alchemy, she swings the hammer once, the weapon battering through the air with a low, heavy thrum. Just like you had guessed, the flame dies out after one swing – and the alcohol that had been clinging to her hammer flicks off in multiple directions with her swing, causing embers to fly as they go. One of them hits your tent. "Oh, shoot," Arona grunts, dropping her hammer and turning her attention to the tent. You rush to help her; if you don’t get that under control in a hurry, you’ll have a serious problem on your hands. ... Some time later, you have the growing fire under control and doused, and, bonus, with minimal damage to your tent and belongings. It’s a few minutes later until your adrenaline starts to wane and your heart starts to settle in your chest. Now that your head is starting to clear from all of the excitement, you get back to what it was that had your attention beforehand: wishing for more wishes from Oma. And... ... Frankly, Oma’s gone through all this trouble to prevent you from wishing for more wishes. Maybe there’s a way to circumvent all of her wordplay and bullshittery, but now that things have calmed down, you’re starting to think that it’s probably not worth the effort to keep trying. And if you did keep trying, there’s no doubt that Oma would just find some way to cheat you out of what you really wanted again. You’ll give this one a pass. There are better things you could be spending your energy on. |You think back to each of your attempts so far and why they might have failed. You asked for more wishes; you asked to be a genie yourself; you asked for more Omas to grant you more wishes; but each of these lines of thought have failed. What’s the commonality between them? What’s the thing that’s making them all fail collectively? The one thing that immediately comes to mind is... Oma herself. She’s a genie, and she’s capable of granting wishes, but she did not say that wishing for more wishes was against the rules. In fact, she explicitly said that wishing for more wishes was an option! Maybe she’s just being difficult, to try and get out of doing more work? Is that even possible for someone as bound as she is? You try and think – how can you remove Oma from the equation, but still get infinite wishes, without becoming a genie yourself? Maybe... maybe you could wish that something else could grant you wishes. Take the powers that Oma has and move it into something that still obeys you, but is willing to obey your commands. Something like a pet? No, it needs to be something with great enough intelligence to infer your meaning behind words and contexts. You could try wishing for, like, a magic rock, or a staff, or something, but they’d be objects; not something that is capable of executing your will, even if you specified that they could. Oh, wait: how about a book? A book that always had one more page than you needed, and anything that you – you, specifically – write in it will become real. If you wrote in it that you had a lump of gold in your pocket, that reality would suddenly become real. You run the scenario over and over in your head, refining the exact wording that you’d use to wish for it to be real, to make sure that Oma can’t try and twist this one around on you. You’re not sure how she could: the onus of the wishes would be going from her to the book, but she wouldn’t be able to try and twist your words and meanings around. The book wouldn’t be bound by a curse to disappear after three wishes. As long as you word it properly, it should be foolproof.... After another moment to yourself to rehearse exactly how you want to phrase it, you turn to Oma and you try again: you wish for a book filled with pages that never run out, and anything you write in it comes true. Normally, Oma is quick to grant you your wish, even if it’s her twisting your intention around to make it backfire on you somehow. This time, though, she hesitates: it’s a few seconds before she acknowledges that you said anything at all. Eventually, she closes her eyes and lifts her free hand, her palm facing upward. From the very air between you, material spawns from nothing at all: first, a long, thick sheet of leather that makes for the book’s binding; then the fine, black twine that comprises the book’s spine; and then, a single piece of parchment, fastened to the inside of the book. All of the materials pull from the space above her hand like they were being forced through a small hole, and when they unfurl, they’re in perfect, pristine condition, as if they were freshly created right then and there. When she opens her eyes, her irises shimmer through every color in the rainbow before settling back onto their normal silver sheen. "Your wish has been granted," she says. The book continues to hover in the air above her hand; when you reach out and grab it, it’s real. It’s fairly light, as you expected it to be, but the leather is firm-but-not-unforgiving, as you expected leather to be, and the parchment is soft and twists between your fingertips as you’d expect parchment to. You didn’t wish for a quill with ink to write in it with, but that’s okay: you turn to the fire going at the camp and you pull out a small, thin branch. After extinguishing the flame at its tip and dipping it into the fire’s soot, you have a makeshift quill with ink. That seems like a fairly easy thing to write into the book, to test out its powers. You open the leatherbound book and press the sooty stick to the parchment, and you write that you wish you had a quill with ink to write with. As soon as you dot the period at the end of the sentence... the whole sentence disappears. The paper doesn’t retain any indentations from you pressing the stick against it. It’s as if you hadn’t written anything in there at all. You look around yourself to see if the quill with ink had suddenly appeared next to you, or on your person, or within the book’s leather or something, but there’s no such luck. The quill with ink that you specifically wish for is nowhere to be found. You write the sentence in the book again, but the same thing happens: the words disappear; the parchment is as perfect as ever; and you still don’t have a quill with you. You try writing that you wish for a single gold coin, but the same thing happens: there are no words on the page and there is no gold coin. You ask Oma how to work the book. You wished for a book where anything you wrote in it would come true, and yet nothing you write in it is coming true. Is there some trick to it or something? "I have granted your wish to your exact specifications, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ]," she responds. Well, clearly, she didn’t. "Try writing a sentence that uses the word ‘anything.’" Immediately, a cold pit forms in the bottom of your chest as you look back to the book in your hand. You tried to be as specific as you could with your phrasing, but the word ‘anything’ is, by its own definition, as broad as can be. With hesitant fingers, you write the sentence 'I wish for anything to come true’ – and, just as you feared, every word in the sentence evaporates into the parchment... except for the word ‘anything.’ You write more sentences into the parchment, each of them containing the word ‘anything,’ only for every sentence to vanish but the word ‘anything’ remains. No matter what you try, nothing works as you want it to: the only thing that stays on the page is that one word, which you can write as often as you like. What you have is a book that will literally grant you anything, and only anything. "Most of my masters would have understood that wishing for more wishes is impossible before you, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ]," Oma says. Her normally stony expression breaks; the corners of her lips lift into a cheeky smirk. "It is not a wish I can actually grant, but you, in your greed, had to push it further. And now you have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |no wishes |one wish |two wishes ] remaining." You shout in frustration and hurl the book at Oma; the book passes right through her, as if she were made of smoke. It’s up to you if you learned something about your greed and hubris from this exchange. ] ] ]
rows.translation: 你回想起了奶奶曾经为你制定的三条规则，这些规则是关于向她许愿时需要遵守的。第一条是：她不能伤害那些本来并不希望受到伤害的人——这个规定听起来有点奇怪，但你想，也许在某些情况下，有人确实会希望或需要因此受到伤害，比如希望某处的伤口能够得到处理之类的。第二条是：她不能侵犯任何人的个人自主权：你不能许愿要求别人违背自己的意愿去做某事。 [pc.hasRealCock |一个更大的家伙，或者 ]更结实的肌肉，或者更长的头发，诸如此类的东西。第三，她无法创造生命或赋予生命：她既不能让死者复生，也不能凭空创造新的生命。 [oma.freedomWishedFor |她为你制定的规则中其实存在一个相当明显的漏洞，不过……你肯定不会想趁她心情好的时候，试图迫使她答应你更多的请求吧。虽然，你确实希望在她做出让步之后，她能够获得自由。 [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |你的下一个愿望 |你的下一个两个愿望 | ]所以，也许甚至如果你要求得到更多的愿望，这有什么关系吗？ 嗯，无论如何，你可以问问奶奶：只是出于好奇，你是否有可能希望获得更多的愿望呢？你并不是真的想要这样做，只是想了解一下而已。 |你是为数不多的几位大师之一，你们竟然试图如此巧妙地利用我的限制条件，以至于最终让自己失去了一个愿望。 你接着询问，之后你为她祈求自由，是否改变了她对你的看法。 有点吧。你确实是唯一一个真正从他们的傲慢中吸取了教训的人，但另一方面，你本身也具备那种傲慢的性格。至于克服贪婪是否比完全没有贪婪更好，这其实是一个哲学问题……坦白说，我并不想回答这个问题。 ]她又笑了起来。 The first was that she cannot harm anyone that doesn’t already want it – that’s an odd caveat, but you suppose there could be any circumstances where someone might want, or need, to be injured for something, like wishing for a wound to be cauterized or whatever. The second is that she cannot infringe upon anyone’s personal autonomy: you can’t wish for [pc.hasRealCock |a bigger dick, or ]bigger muscles, or longer hair, or anything like that. And the third was that she cannot create or grant life: she can’t bring back anyone from the dead, nor can she create life from whole cloth. Although, you did wish for her to be free ‘after she granted [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |your next wish |your next two wishes | ],’ so, maybe even if you asked for more wishes, it wouldn’t matter? Well, in any case, you ask Oma: for your own curiosity, would it have been possible for you to wish for more wishes? You don’t intend to; you just want to know. Oma laughs. "It’s one of the most common wishes from all my previous masters," she says. "Every other master wishes for more. Three just isn’t enough. It’s refreshing to finally meet someone that not only wished for my own freedom, but is okay with just [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |one |two | ]!" "To answer your question, no, it is not possible to wish for more wishes," she answers, her mouth crooking diagonally into a wide smirk. "When I first appeared from the lamp, I very specifically said ‘whomsoever possesses the lamp is entitled to three wishes.’ Wishing for more wishes is such a common thing that I’ve taken up the habit of messing with any master that wishes for it with specificities and word plays – things like ‘it takes one wish to grant one wish,’ so they just wind up back to where they started[var0 |. You are one of the few masters that took is so far and tried to game my restrictions so much that it actually cost you a wish." You ask if you wishing for her freedom afterward changes her opinion of you. "Somewhat. You’re definitely the only one that ever actually learned from their hubris, but on the other hand, you had that kind of hubris to start with. Whether overcoming your greed is better than not having greed at all is a philosophical question that, frankly, I just don’t feel like answering ]." She laughs again. "Hey, [pc.name]!" she shouts jovially, laughing once, apparently proud of something. "Check this out!" You turn back towards the campfire, and there is Arona, her war hammer held tightly in her grip – with its head set ablaze, the fire wicking off its metal, although the flame is weak. You doubt the flame would survive a swing. "Fuck yeah, right?!" she laughs, hefting it up a bit. "I got the idea to cover my hammer in booze, and now I can do this!" She spins the hammer in her grip. "It’s not a very strong flame, though. It’ll only last for a little bit. But still, fuck yeah!" She smiles at you widely enough to show you her molars. "Can you imagine? I’d really bring the heat to the heat of the battle!" To demonstrate her apparent mastery of alchemy, she swings the hammer once, the weapon battering through the air with a low, heavy thrum. Just like you had guessed, the flame dies out after one swing – and the alcohol that had been clinging to her hammer flicks off in multiple directions with her swing, causing embers to fly as they go. One of them hits your tent. "Oh, shoot," Arona grunts, dropping her hammer and turning her attention to the tent. You rush to help her; if you don’t get that under control in a hurry, you’ll have a serious problem on your hands. ... Some time later, you have the growing fire under control and doused, and, bonus, with minimal damage to your tent and belongings. It’s a few minutes later until your adrenaline starts to wane and your heart starts to settle in your chest. Now that your head is starting to clear from all of the excitement, you get back to what it was that had your attention beforehand: wishing for more wishes from Oma. And... ... Frankly, Oma’s gone through all this trouble to prevent you from wishing for more wishes. Maybe there’s a way to circumvent all of her wordplay and bullshittery, but now that things have calmed down, you’re starting to think that it’s probably not worth the effort to keep trying. And if you did keep trying, there’s no doubt that Oma would just find some way to cheat you out of what you really wanted again. You’ll give this one a pass. There are better things you could be spending your energy on. |You think back to each of your attempts so far and why they might have failed. You asked for more wishes; you asked to be a genie yourself; you asked for more Omas to grant you more wishes; but each of these lines of thought have failed. What’s the commonality between them? What’s the thing that’s making them all fail collectively? The one thing that immediately comes to mind is... Oma herself. She’s a genie, and she’s capable of granting wishes, but she did not say that wishing for more wishes was against the rules. In fact, she explicitly said that wishing for more wishes was an option! Maybe she’s just being difficult, to try and get out of doing more work? Is that even possible for someone as bound as she is? You try and think – how can you remove Oma from the equation, but still get infinite wishes, without becoming a genie yourself? Maybe... maybe you could wish that something else could grant you wishes. Take the powers that Oma has and move it into something that still obeys you, but is willing to obey your commands. Something like a pet? No, it needs to be something with great enough intelligence to infer your meaning behind words and contexts. You could try wishing for, like, a magic rock, or a staff, or something, but they’d be objects; not something that is capable of executing your will, even if you specified that they could. Oh, wait: how about a book? A book that always had one more page than you needed, and anything that you – you, specifically – write in it will become real. If you wrote in it that you had a lump of gold in your pocket, that reality would suddenly become real. You run the scenario over and over in your head, refining the exact wording that you’d use to wish for it to be real, to make sure that Oma can’t try and twist this one around on you. You’re not sure how she could: the onus of the wishes would be going from her to the book, but she wouldn’t be able to try and twist your words and meanings around. The book wouldn’t be bound by a curse to disappear after three wishes. As long as you word it properly, it should be foolproof.... After another moment to yourself to rehearse exactly how you want to phrase it, you turn to Oma and you try again: you wish for a book filled with pages that never run out, and anything you write in it comes true. Normally, Oma is quick to grant you your wish, even if it’s her twisting your intention around to make it backfire on you somehow. This time, though, she hesitates: it’s a few seconds before she acknowledges that you said anything at all. Eventually, she closes her eyes and lifts her free hand, her palm facing upward. From the very air between you, material spawns from nothing at all: first, a long, thick sheet of leather that makes for the book’s binding; then the fine, black twine that comprises the book’s spine; and then, a single piece of parchment, fastened to the inside of the book. All of the materials pull from the space above her hand like they were being forced through a small hole, and when they unfurl, they’re in perfect, pristine condition, as if they were freshly created right then and there. When she opens her eyes, her irises shimmer through every color in the rainbow before settling back onto their normal silver sheen. "Your wish has been granted," she says. The book continues to hover in the air above her hand; when you reach out and grab it, it’s real. It’s fairly light, as you expected it to be, but the leather is firm-but-not-unforgiving, as you expected leather to be, and the parchment is soft and twists between your fingertips as you’d expect parchment to. You didn’t wish for a quill with ink to write in it with, but that’s okay: you turn to the fire going at the camp and you pull out a small, thin branch. After extinguishing the flame at its tip and dipping it into the fire’s soot, you have a makeshift quill with ink. That seems like a fairly easy thing to write into the book, to test out its powers. You open the leatherbound book and press the sooty stick to the parchment, and you write that you wish you had a quill with ink to write with. As soon as you dot the period at the end of the sentence... the whole sentence disappears. The paper doesn’t retain any indentations from you pressing the stick against it. It’s as if you hadn’t written anything in there at all. You look around yourself to see if the quill with ink had suddenly appeared next to you, or on your person, or within the book’s leather or something, but there’s no such luck. The quill with ink that you specifically wish for is nowhere to be found. You write the sentence in the book again, but the same thing happens: the words disappear; the parchment is as perfect as ever; and you still don’t have a quill with you. You try writing that you wish for a single gold coin, but the same thing happens: there are no words on the page and there is no gold coin. You ask Oma how to work the book. You wished for a book where anything you wrote in it would come true, and yet nothing you write in it is coming true. Is there some trick to it or something? "I have granted your wish to your exact specifications, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ]," she responds. Well, clearly, she didn’t. "Try writing a sentence that uses the word ‘anything.’" Immediately, a cold pit forms in the bottom of your chest as you look back to the book in your hand. You tried to be as specific as you could with your phrasing, but the word ‘anything’ is, by its own definition, as broad as can be. With hesitant fingers, you write the sentence 'I wish for anything to come true’ – and, just as you feared, every word in the sentence evaporates into the parchment... except for the word ‘anything.’ You write more sentences into the parchment, each of them containing the word ‘anything,’ only for every sentence to vanish but the word ‘anything’ remains. No matter what you try, nothing works as you want it to: the only thing that stays on the page is that one word, which you can write as often as you like. What you have is a book that will literally grant you anything, and only anything. "Most of my masters would have understood that wishing for more wishes is impossible before you, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ]," Oma says. Her normally stony expression breaks; the corners of her lips lift into a cheeky smirk. "It is not a wish I can actually grant, but you, in your greed, had to push it further. And now you have [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |no wishes |one wish |two wishes ] remaining." You shout in frustration and hurl the book at Oma; the book passes right through her, as if she were made of smoke. It’s up to you if you learned something about your greed and hubris from this exchange. ] ] ] '

rows.original: [oma.freedomWishedFor |You deliberate with yourself on what you could use your wish on. You have the near-infinite powers of the genie at your disposal; you could use them to make your life easier, or to make the world a better place. Whatever you want, it’s up to you to decide. When you think back to the journey you’ve had up to this point, there’s one commonality to all of the places you’ve visited and all of the things you’ve done: it can get pretty exhausting. Constantly walking from one place to another, all day, every day, is difficult enough: sometimes the terrain is difficult and sometimes you have to defend yourself from rowdy wildlife, or highwaymen, or the occasional demon or whatever[pc.hasWings |. And having wings doesn’t make your life easier: even if you used them to regularly fly, you’d just be moving all of that exhaustion from your feet to your [pc.wings]. And that’d probably be much worse ]. It'd be simpler if you could just be wherever it is that you wanted to be. No more long-winded traveling; no need to lug heavy resources here and there. You just think about your destination, and poof, there you’d be. ... Is something like that possible? You assume so, but you ask Oma just in case. "There are few things that are impossible for me," she answers, though her tone is a bit more serious: she tilts her head to one side and frowns as she strongly considers your wish. "Your phrasing must be precise. If your phrasing is too weak, then you could teleport whenever an image of a location comes to your mind – if someone were to say that they got caught in a storm out in the ocean, for example, your thoughts would naturally turn to the ocean, and then you’d be teleported there." "And there are other considerations as well: when traveling, do you maintain momentum? If you were to accidentally teleport into the sky and start falling, and you imagine yourself back onto safe ground, would all of your momentum carry? What if you try to teleport somewhere that’s already occupied, by, say, a rock, or a person? What would happen then?" There are a lot of technicalities to wish like that. Maybe it’s a pointless line of questioning. "It is not," she says again, her eyes narrowing in determination on you. "But you would have to phrase every nuance into a single grammatically-correct sentence. It’d certainly be challenging, and you only get one opportunity[oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 | |... unless you’re willing to spend your final wish on undoing your mistake | ]." Well... while that’s disappointing, it’s not like things are all bad. You pull out your Waystone Charm and dangle it in the air between yourself at Oma, saying that the Ways Between is pretty convenient as far as traveling goes. "Oh!" Oma starts, her eyes widening at the sight of the crystal dangling from your hand. "You know of the Ways Between?" ... Yeah, most people do in the modern world. There’s a portal to there in the middle of Hawkethorne. "Ah, this changes things slightly," she says, cupping her hands underneath your charm. You acquiesce and drop it into her palms; she twists it around and holds it up to the sky as she examines it. "I can improve this charm of yours so that you can enter the Ways Between from anywhere in Savarra, if you’d like. It’s not true teleportation, like you had been hoping for, but it’s a modest runner-up: from anywhere in Savarra, to the Ways Between, and from there, any portals that you’ve been attuned to." Is it possible to teleport from the Ways Between to anywhere you want in Savarra? "Unfortunately, no," she responds, her eyes going from the charm back to you. "Time and space are contorted within the Ways Between; it’s not as simple as going there, seeing a spot in Savarra within the crystalline ‘floor,’ and then willing yourself to be there. The charm would be able to place you within the Ways Between, but the journey would be one-way; you must use a portal to leave." On the one hand, you’re still being served limitations and disappointments with everything that she says. You could have exactly what you want, but the line between getting exactly what you want, and getting something that could be catastrophic, is razor-thin; it’s a pretty risky wish to go for something like that. On the other, being able to travel directly to the Ways Between without the need of a portal, at any time, and going anywhere you like from there, is still a powerful tool. You’d have to find future portals, but if you ever got hungry, lost, or tired, you could abandon your current excursion and head straight to the Ways Between, and from there, to Hawkethorne, or to any other safe haven you’d want. You deliberate with yourself on the issue for a moment before deciding that, while it’s a compromise, and you weren’t expecting to have to compromise on your own wishes, it’s nonetheless still a powerful option. Without taking the charm from Oma, you tell her that you wish for the ability to travel to the Ways Between from anywhere in the world. Oma smiles and shuts her eyes for a moment; when she opens them, her irises have gone from their normal, shimmering silver to shifting between every color in the spectrum, one after the other. She closes her palms together, your charm in between her hands as a wispy, pale-blue light glows around her wrists, traveling up her hands before focusing in on the space between them; the light seeps from the spaces between her fingers and out the sides of her palms. After a moment, the light subsides, and, with another blink, her shifting irises return to their normal silver coloration. She hands you back your Waystone Charm... and it doesn’t look any different from normal. Has she really done something to it? "Hold it in your hand and think of the Ways Between, and you’ll find out," she says. The charm sits in your palm, looking totally normal as before. It’s almost as if Oma hadn’t taken it from your hands in the first place. Well, if you want to give it a try, there’s only one way to test it out for sure.... |You deliberate with yourself on what you could use the near-infinite powers of the genie on. It could be anything from power to wealth to infinite life, but... if there’s any one thing that you’ve learned ever since you began your journey across the lands of Savarra, it’s that walking for long periods of time is, well, it’s exhausting[pc.hasWings |. You’d think having wings would help alleviate that, but they’re not as effective at mitigating exhaustion as it might seem ]. It’d be useful, bordering on fantastical, if you could simply... be wherever it is you want to be with just a thought. If you wanted to go home and sleep in a nice bed at the Frost Hound Tavern, you’d be there. If you wanted to return to this spot right here once you’re rested, you could do that in the blink of an eye. Wandering like you do is as dangerous as it is difficult, because if you’re caught by anyone or anything looking for a fight, you’d be exhausted and unprepared to fight for your life. [lyric.around |The more you think about it, the more you convince yourself that this is a power you’d like to have. Instantly be anywhere, at any time, just by thinking about it. You turn to Oma– And, suddenly, beside you is Lyric, taking a particularly keen interest in what it is that you’re doing. "Heya, [pc.name]," [lyric.heShe] says, [lyric.hisHer] hands behind [lyric.hisHer] back and [lyric.hisHer] tail wagging gently from side to side as [lyric.heShe] rocks on [lyric.hisHer] heels, watching you deliberate with yourself on what to wish for from Oma. "You looked like you were trying to figure something out. Can I help? I'm good at figuring things out!" Oh, [lyric.heShe] things so, does [lyric.heShe]? "Yeah!" [lyric.heShe] continues with a wide smile. "I don’t know what I would do with three whole wishes from a genie, but you look like you were in the middle of figuring out what it was that you were after. You had every look on your face from concentration to constipation!" [lyric.HeShe] laughs out loud at [lyric.hisHer] own little joke. "Figuring things out is fun! Learning to work with a genie can't be that much harder than channeling electricity through a copper wire." ... Lyric has always had a penchant for the sciences. Maybe [lyric.heShe] could help you figure it out. "Sock it to me!" [lyric.heShe] says, [lyric.hisHer] tail wagging even harder behind [lyric.himHer]self. You were just thinking about how walking the world of Savarra – while it’s good exercise and the sights are beautiful – is, well, it’s hard. You were thinking that it’d be amazing if you could simply be wherever it is that you wanted to be with just a thought: if you could imagine yourself in a place, you’d be there instantly. No walking; no need to carry heavy camping supplies; no worrying about combating the elements. Just, one thought, and suddenly, you’re there. "Ooh, that does sound useful," [lyric.heShe] says, placing the chin of [lyric.hisHer] scaly snout on the crux of [lyric.hisHer] thumb. "But I could think of a few ways it could go wrong." Such as? "Well, based on the language you used, how would you differentiate between an errant thought about Hawkethorne from a place you actually wanted to visit?" [lyric.heShe] asks. "If I said, ‘I’m thirsty; I can’t wait to go back to the Frost Hound for a drink,’ your mind would think of the tavern, even if you didn’t mean to. Would you suddenly find yourself there?" Well– "And where in the Frost Hound would you appear?" [lyric.heShe] continues. "In the very spot you imagined, maybe, but what if you misremembered it? What if you imagined yourself just a bit too short – would your feet sink into the floor? What if someone or something was at the exact spot you imagined yourself as; would one of you be obliterated? Would you, I dunno, mix yourselves together? If Garth had set down a crate on the spot you imagined, would you be half [pc.race] and half crate?" That doesn’t– "Or maybe the opposite issue – what if you misremembered some detail, and then the magic wouldn’t function properly? What if you remember the bar as you last saw it, down to the very details, but one of the stools was slightly misaligned since last you had gone? The place in your mind would technically not exist. Would the magic still work?" With a bit of clever phrasing, you could get Oma to– "And then there are other spatial concerns to keep in mind as well. What if–" You know what? Never mind. You’ll think of something else. Lyric looks up at you with [lyric.hisHer] big, round, golden eyes. "Did I help?" In one sense or another, yes. You tell [lyric.himHer] that [lyric.heShe] was a tremendous help. [lyric.HeShe] steps into you to give you a quick, tight hug before turning back to the campfire. "Let me know if there’s anything more I can do!" |[var0 |Still, though, there are a handful of ways that this line of thinking could go wrong. It’ll come down to how well it’s phrased, and even then, you’ll be playing with fire: even if Oma granted your wish to your exact specifications, you could still inadvertently use it to, say, teleport straight into the ground, or off a cliff, or something. Those are restrictions and challenges that you’d have to overcome, but... if you can overcome them, then you’d have a powerful skill at your disposal. The more you think about it, the more you convince yourself that this is a power that you’d like to have. Instantly be anywhere, at any time, just by thinking it. You turn to Oma and you tell her that you wish you could be anywhere that you wanted in an instant. Oma closes her eyes in response: her body begins to glow slightly, with a light-blue aura surrounding her skin and her hair as she focuses on channeling the powers of the genie within her. When she opens her eyes, her irises have changed from shimmering silver to a radiant rainbow, her eyes displaying every color of the spectrum– But only for an instant. In another, the world around you has disappeared – and, in its place, you’re in the Ways Between. Familiar territory to you now, but... this is hardly what you had wished for! When you look around the plain of nothingness, you see that all of your effects are still with you – including Oma’s lamp, tucked into your pack. You angrily pull it out and summon her again by rubbing the lamp’s side; she goes through the whole show of appearing through a cloud-silver cloud of smoke, ending with both of you standing in the infinite expanse of the Ways Between. You ask her what the hell that was all about. You wished for the ability to teleport; you didn’t wish to be teleported! "What you wished for, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ], was ‘to be anywhere you wanted in an instant.’" She turns her heads and looks out across the flat nothing of the Ways Between. "There already exists a system to allow even anyone without the powers of the genie to accomplish this very goal. I simply pointed you towards it." You already knew about the Ways Between and how to utilize it; you wanted to skip using it altogether! To be anywhere you wanted on a whim, directly, without having to jump between dimensions; without having to put any further effort into it than a thought! "[oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |I would tell you to be more specific next time, but I do believe that is your third wish of three," she says, the corner of her mouth curling into the faintest smirk. |Then specify that next time," she says. |Then specify that next time," she says. ] Well, shit. |Still, though, there are a handful of ways that this line of thinking could go wrong. It’ll come down to how well it’s phrased, and even then, you’ll be playing with fire: even if Oma granted your wish to your exact specifications, you could still inadvertently use it to, say, teleport straight into the ground, or off a cliff, or something. Those are restrictions and challenges that you’d have to overcome, but... if you can overcome them, then you’d have a powerful skill at your disposal. That’s up to you, though: do you take that risk? Do you wish for the ability to teleport? ] ] ]
rows.translation: [oma.freedomWishedFor |你仔细思考着自己应该用这个愿望来实现什么。你拥有精灵赋予的近乎无限的力量，你可以利用这些力量让自己的生活变得更舒适，或者让这个世界变得更好。无论你想要什么，最终的决定权都在你手中。 当你回顾迄今为止所经历的一切时，你会发现你到过的所有地方以及做过的所有事情都有一个共同点：这些经历往往会让人感到精疲力竭。每天整天不停地从一个地方走到另一个地方，本身就已经非常辛苦了；有时候地形环境十分恶劣，有时候你还得保护自己，免受那些吵闹的野生动物、强盗的袭击，甚至偶尔还会遇到恶魔之类的东西。[pc.hasWings |而且，拥有翅膀并不会让你的生活变得更容易：即使你经常用它们来飞行，你也只是把那些疲劳从腿部转移到了翅膀上而已。 [pc.wings]那样情况可能会更糟。 ]如果你能直接这样做的话，会简单很多。是无论你想要去哪里，都不再需要漫长的旅途，也不必费力地搬运重型的物资。你只需要想着目的地，然后，砰的一下，你就到了那里。 ……这样的事情真的可能吗？你心里认为是可以的，但还是忍不住去问了奥玛。 “对我来说，没有什么是不可能的，”她回答道，不过肌肉度显得有些严肃。她把头偏向一边，皱着眉头仔细思考你的请求。“你的说法应该精确。如果你的表述不够清晰明确，那么每当你脑海中浮现某个地点的影像时，你就可以立即传送到那里。例如，如果有人告诉你他们在海洋中遭遇了风暴，你的思绪自然会转向海洋，而你也会立刻被传送到那里。此外，还有其他需要考虑的因素：在旅行过程中，你是否能够保持原有的运动状态？如果你不小心传送到空中开始下落，而你试图让自己重新回到安全的地面上，那么你之前的运动状态还会保留吗？如果你试图传送到某个已经被其他物体，比如一块石头或一个人占据的地方，会发生什么呢？那时会怎么样？” 其实，对于这样的问题，存在很多技术上的细节需要考虑。也许，这个问题本身就没有实际意义。 不是这样的，”她再次说道，目光坚定地注视着你，“但你必须把所有的细微差别都用一句语法正确的句子表达出来。这肯定很有挑战性，而且你只有一次机会。[oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 | |……除非你愿意用自己最后的愿望来纠正这个错误。 | ]嗯……虽然这确实令人失望，但事情也不至于发展到那种地步吧。所有太棒了！”奥玛看到你手中悬挂着的那块水晶，眼睛立刻亮了起来。你拿出你的道路石魔法饰品，在自己和奥玛之间悬着它，说道：“道路石在旅行方面确实非常方便。你知道那些‘通道’的存在吗？” “……嗯，在现代社会，大多数人都知道。在鹰棘镇的中心，有一扇通往那里的入口。” “啊，这样情况就有点不同了。”她说着，将双手放在你的饰品下方。你同意了，便将它放在她的手掌中；她仔细地端详着，然后将它举到空中。“我可以改进你的这个护身符，这样你就能进入‘道路之间’了任何地方在萨瓦拉地区，你可以使用这种传送方式。虽然它并不是你期望中的那种瞬间传送，但也已经算是相当不错的替代方案了：你可以从萨瓦拉的任何地方传送到“道路之间”，然后再从那里前往你已经调谐好的任何传送门。 那么，是否可以从“道路之间”传送到萨瓦拉的任何地方呢？ 很遗憾，不行，”她回答道，目光再次从那枚护身符上移回到你身上。“在‘道路之间’，时间和空间都是扭曲的；并不是简单地前往那里，在萨瓦拉的晶体‘地面’上找到某个位置，然后就立刻到达那里那么简单。那枚护身符确实能将你送到‘道路之间’，但那次旅行是单程的——你必须通过传送门才能离开。 一方面，她说的每一句话都在给你带来种种限制和失望。你本可以得到你想要的一切，但得到你想要的东西与得到可能带来灾难性后果的东西之间的界限其实非常微妙；追求这样的东西实在是一件风险极大的事。 When you think back to the journey you’ve had up to this point, there’s one commonality to all of the places you’ve visited and all of the things you’ve done: it can get pretty exhausting. Constantly walking from one place to another, all day, every day, is difficult enough: sometimes the terrain is difficult and sometimes you have to defend yourself from rowdy wildlife, or highwaymen, or the occasional demon or whatever[pc.hasWings |. You just think about your destination, and poof, there you’d be. ... Is something like that possible? You assume so, but you ask Oma just in case. "There are few things that are impossible for me," she answers, though her tone is a bit more serious: she tilts her head to one side and frowns as she strongly considers your wish. "Your phrasing must be precise. If your phrasing is too weak, then you could teleport whenever an image of a location comes to your mind – if someone were to say that they got caught in a storm out in the ocean, for example, your thoughts would naturally turn to the ocean, and then you’d be teleported there." "And there are other considerations as well: when traveling, do you maintain momentum? If you were to accidentally teleport into the sky and start falling, and you imagine yourself back onto safe ground, would all of your momentum carry? What if you try to teleport somewhere that’s already occupied, by, say, a rock, or a person? What would happen then?" There are a lot of technicalities to wish like that. Maybe it’s a pointless line of questioning. "It is not," she says again, her eyes narrowing in determination on you. "But you would have to phrase every nuance into a single grammatically-correct sentence. You pull out your Waystone Charm and dangle it in the air between yourself at Oma, saying that the Ways Between is pretty convenient as far as traveling goes. "Oh!" Oma starts, her eyes widening at the sight of the crystal dangling from your hand. "You know of the Ways Between?" ... Yeah, most people do in the modern world. There’s a portal to there in the middle of Hawkethorne. "Ah, this changes things slightly," she says, cupping her hands underneath your charm. You acquiesce and drop it into her palms; she twists it around and holds it up to the sky as she examines it. "I can improve this charm of yours so that you can enter the Ways Between from anywhere in Savarra, if you’d like. It’s not true teleportation, like you had been hoping for, but it’s a modest runner-up: from anywhere in Savarra, to the Ways Between, and from there, any portals that you’ve been attuned to." Is it possible to teleport from the Ways Between to anywhere you want in Savarra? "Unfortunately, no," she responds, her eyes going from the charm back to you. "Time and space are contorted within the Ways Between; it’s not as simple as going there, seeing a spot in Savarra within the crystalline ‘floor,’ and then willing yourself to be there. The charm would be able to place you within the Ways Between, but the journey would be one-way; you must use a portal to leave." On the one hand, you’re still being served limitations and disappointments with everything that she says. You could have exactly what you want, but the line between getting exactly what you want, and getting something that could be catastrophic, is razor-thin; it’s a pretty risky wish to go for something like that. On the other, being able to travel directly to the Ways Between without the need of a portal, at any time, and going anywhere you like from there, is still a powerful tool. You’d have to find future portals, but if you ever got hungry, lost, or tired, you could abandon your current excursion and head straight to the Ways Between, and from there, to Hawkethorne, or to any other safe haven you’d want. You deliberate with yourself on the issue for a moment before deciding that, while it’s a compromise, and you weren’t expecting to have to compromise on your own wishes, it’s nonetheless still a powerful option. Without taking the charm from Oma, you tell her that you wish for the ability to travel to the Ways Between from anywhere in the world. Oma smiles and shuts her eyes for a moment; when she opens them, her irises have gone from their normal, shimmering silver to shifting between every color in the spectrum, one after the other. She closes her palms together, your charm in between her hands as a wispy, pale-blue light glows around her wrists, traveling up her hands before focusing in on the space between them; the light seeps from the spaces between her fingers and out the sides of her palms. After a moment, the light subsides, and, with another blink, her shifting irises return to their normal silver coloration. She hands you back your Waystone Charm... and it doesn’t look any different from normal. Has she really done something to it? "Hold it in your hand and think of the Ways Between, and you’ll find out," she says. The charm sits in your palm, looking totally normal as before. It’s almost as if Oma hadn’t taken it from your hands in the first place. Those are restrictions and challenges that you’d have to overcome, but... if you can overcome them, then you’d have a powerful skill at your disposal. That’s up to you, though: do you take that risk? Do you wish for the ability to teleport? ] ] ] '

rows.original: The more you think about it, the more you convince yourself that this is a power that you’d like to have. Instantly be anywhere, at any time, just by thinking it. You turn to Oma and you tell her that you wish you could be anywhere that you wanted in an instant. Oma closes her eyes in response: her body begins to glow slightly, with a light-blue aura surrounding her skin and her hair as she focuses on channeling the powers of the genie within her. When she opens her eyes, her irises have changed from shimmering silver to a radiant rainbow, her eyes displaying every color of the spectrum– But only for an instant. In another, the world around you has disappeared. Where you stand, the sky is dark: the ‘ground,’ if it could be called that, is glassy, and beneath it, you can see what you vaguely understand is Savarra – or, at least, something that looks like it. The place you’re in is a large, dark, otherwise-featureless void, with the exception of the occasional pillar of light beaming straight up from the glassy ground beneath you, stretching infinitely into the dark sky. There are hundreds of them, each of them stretching over the ‘map’ of Savarra beneath you, seemingly situated over important locations – towns, villages, and other places of society and interest. One of them you recognize is Hawkethorne. But nothing you do gets the beams of light to react to you: simply walking into one isn’t enough for them to respond to your presence, nor do they react to any bodily gestures that you make. You’re missing something – something important. Panic starts to set in before long: this isn’t what you wished for! You have no idea where you are; you don’t know how to get out; you still have your clothes on your back and your effects, but nothing you’re carrying is of any help to you and your current predicament, and notably absent is Oma and her lamp, since she was the one last carrying it. How are you meant to escape this? What little provisions you happened to be carrying won’t last you for long. Are you meant to wait until someone comes to rescue you? Help! Somebody, help! —- Back at the camp, Oma continues to stand, the lamp sitting in her upturned right palm, as she stares into nothing in front of her. The rainbow sheen of her irises had reverted back to their normal silver some time ago. [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 |"Ah," she says after a long moment, her stance jolting upright. "That was [pc.hisHer] final wish." |Oma hums to herself, her lips crooking to one side as she chews on nothing. "It will be some time before [pc.heShe] expires," she says, "and then my cycle will begin anew." ] The silver smoke begins to billow from the spout of her lamp; the heavy smoke falls to the ground, wrapping around Oma’s body again and again, starting at her ankles and working its way up her legs. When the smoke fully encapsulates her body, the cloud rapidly spins in place again and again for a few moments – and when it dissipates, Oma, and the lamp she was carrying, have vanished completely. The only way you’re getting out of this predicament is if someone comes to rescue you, and soon. Your hope of that ever happening extinguishes fairly quickly.
rows.translation: 你越仔细思考，就越会确信这种能力正是你想要的——只要心中想着，就能立刻出现在任何地方、任何时刻。于是你转向奥玛，对她说：“你一定希望自己能够瞬间出现在任何你想去的地方。 奥玛闭上眼睛，她的身体开始微微微发光，皮肤和头发周围浮现出淡蓝色的光环，她正专注于引导体内精灵的力量。当她再次睁开眼睛时，她的虹膜已经从闪烁的银色变成了绚丽的彩虹色，她的双眼仿佛蕴含了光谱中的所有色彩—— 但这种感觉只持续了一瞬间。下一刻，你周围的世界便消失了。 你站立的地方，天空一片漆黑；那所谓的“地面”呈现出玻璃般的质地，而在它的下方，你能看到一些东西——那些东西让你隐约觉得它们应该就是萨瓦拉，或者至少看起来很像萨瓦拉。你所处的这个地方是一个巨大而暗影的空洞，除了偶尔有光线从下方那玻璃般的地面上直射而出，无限延伸进暗影的天空之外，这里没有任何其他特征。 有成百上千这样的光束，每一道都延伸覆盖着你脚下的萨瓦拉“地图”，似乎都位于一些重要的地点上——城镇、村庄，以及各种具有社会意义或吸引人的地方。其中有一道光束你认得，那就是鹰棘镇。但是，无论你做什么，这些光束都不会对你产生反应：仅仅走进其中一道光束的范围并不能让它们察觉到你的存在，你做出的任何身体动作也同样不会引起它们的反应。显然，你遗漏了什么——某个非常重要的东西。 不久之后，恐慌开始蔓延：这根本不是你所期望的！你不知道自己现在在哪里，也不知道该如何离开这里；你身上的衣服和物品虽然还在，但没有任何一样东西能帮助你摆脱目前的困境。尤其是，奥玛和她的灯也不见了她就是他最后一个背着它。你究竟要怎么逃出去呢？你身上那些为数不多的补给根本撑不了多久。难道你要一直等到有人来救你吗？ 救命啊！有人救救我！ ——— 回到营地，奥玛依然站在那里，右手掌心托着那盏灯，呆呆地望着前方。她虹膜上的那道彩虹光芒早已恢复了正常的银色。 [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 |啊，”过了好一会儿，她终于站直了身子，说道，“原来是这样[pc.hisHer]最后的愿望。 |奥玛自言自语地哼着小曲，嘴唇微微上扬，却什么也没嚼。“还得等上一段时间呢[pc.heShe]会过期，”她说，“然后我的周期就会重新开始。 ] 银色的烟雾开始从她的灯嘴中袅袅升起；这些浓重的烟雾缓缓落向地面，一次又一次地缠绕在老奶奶的身上，从她的脚踝开始，逐渐向上蔓延到她的双腿。当烟雾完全将她的身体笼罩起来时，这片烟雾云会快速地在原地旋转几秒钟——而当烟雾散去时，老奶奶以及她手中的灯，就已经彻底消失了。 摆脱这种困境的唯一办法就是有人来救你，而且要尽快。 然而，你对这种事情会发生抱有的希望很快就破灭了。

rows.original: [oma.freedomWishedFor |You have the near-infinite powers of the genie at your disposal, and you could use it to wish for anything you want. You could use that wish on something immediately pragmatic[pc.isBimbo | or awesome ], like a weapon of some kind. You could try wishing for something more altruistic, like ending world hunger. But you need to look after yourself: the world is a dangerous and unforgiving place, and even something as mundane as the elements can be dangerous if you’re not prepared. Every time you leave a safe haven like Hawkethorne, you’re putting a lot of trust in the fact that you’ve adequately prepared yourself for whatever trial lies ahead of you. It’s not enough to have a sturdy shield, a strong sword, and some warm clothes: even something like not packing your lunch adequately could have disastrous effects down the line. How could you wish for something like ending world hunger if you can’t even feed yourself? If there’s any one thing that you’ve learned since you’ve started this journey, it’s that having a properly prepared pack can make the difference between life and death. And even with a large pack and proper knowledge on how to make the most efficient use of your pack space, it’s often all too easy to run out of room for anything long before you’re prepared for that. Having more space in your pack would be a godsend – you ask Oma if she could give you a larger pack to store your items in. In response, she frowns in confusion, tilting her head to one side and raising an eyebrow. "You could simply purchase a larger pack," she offers. That’s true, you could. But that’s not what you asked. Oma clicks her tongue as she considers your question. "I mean, yes, granting you a larger pack is obviously within my power," she continues, "but that seems like a terrible use of a wish. A larger pack is something that you could purchase. You could make one yourself with some materials, skill, and time." Oma crosses her arms and rests her chin on her free hand as she considers the wish. "And there’s the logistics. A larger pack would allow you to store more items – but a larger pack would also sag down closer to the ground, reducing your mobility. And more items mean more weight, and a heavier pack could be a death trap for harsher environments and terrains." It sounds to you like she’s trying to talk you out of making this wish. "Not at all," she answers. "I’m trying to help you not waste a wish. Like I said, a larger pack is within my power, but there are practical challenges to overcome – all of which are also within my power; they simply need to be addressed and specified in the wish." Okay, so: you need to wish for a pack that is larger– Oma interrupts you before you can even get your first thought out. "I don’t think a ‘larger’ pack is the correct route to take." Then... what? Can she somehow make the space inside of your pack larger without making the pack itself any bigger? "Yes, actually." ... Wow. You weren’t serious. Is there a limit? Can she only double the ‘space’ within your pack? "No, there is no limit," she answers. "Imagine a house that’s small on the outside, but is larger on the inside. I can do that to an infinite degree: there would be an entire dimension of limitless space within the pockets of your pack, all without making the pack itself any larger." [pc.cunningRange 0 50 |That sounds incredible! There’s no limit to what a pack like that could achieve – you could put yourself into that pack and live a warm, comfortable life. You could assemble an entire house in there[lyric.around |! You’d know just what it’d be like for Lyric living in your pack, too ]! "You don’t want that," Oma cautions. |That’s– Wait, that sounds like a bad thing. Oma smiles a toothy, genuine smile. "You’re quick," she congratulates. ]"Having a pack with infinite space means you’d never be able to find anything you place inside of it. If you dropped a rock into the pack’s pocket, it’d simply fall forever; there would be no ground for it to hit. There needs to be some form of moderation." So... what you want is more space, but not an infinite amount. You want space in your pack that you can reach within arm’s length. And you want your pack to remain the same weight as it is now. Oma hums, her eyes wandering as she runs the scenario through her head again and again. "I think that should work," she eventually says. "I can’t think of any other reasons why that could fail." In that case, you make it official: you wish for double the amount of space within your pack, and for your pack to not gain any additional weight when you place things in it. Oma’s eyes blink, and her irises, and the entirety of her long, flowing ponytail, go from slate silver to a radiant rainbow of colors. She snaps her fingers on her left hand, itself glowing a pale blue from her fingers to her wrist, before everything settles back down and her body returns to the way it was. "Your wish has been granted." You set down your pack. Sure enough, it doesn’t look any different, nor does it weigh any more than it just did. When you open up its main pocket, though, you see that its inner lining doesn’t match with its outer lining: the space within the pack has been increased, the dimensions of the interior being mismatched with the exterior.[lyric.around | Inside your pack is a very surprised kobold, laying flat on [lyric.hisHer] back now that there’s so much space inside. "What just happened?" [lyric.heShe] asks in bewilderment. You tell it to [lyric.himHer] honestly: you wished for Oma the genie to make the inside of your pack bigger so that– "So that I could have more living space?!" [lyric.heShe] interrupts, [lyric.hisHer] eyes wide with joy. ... Yep. [lyric.HeShe]’s got it. Lyric sits up, [lyric.hisHer] hands reaching up through the mouth of the pack, and [lyric.heShe] gently grips onto your cheeks. Pulling [lyric.himHer]self to [lyric.hisHer] knees, [lyric.heShe] closes the gap between you two and leans in, kissing you on the mouth. It’s a quick peck, but the appreciation is apparent. "You’re the best," [lyric.heShe] says, nuzzling [lyric.hisHer] nose against yours, before settling back down into the pack’s main pocket, appreciating just how roomier it is in there. ] You can now hold twice as many stackable items. |You try and rack your mind on things that you could use the near-infinite powers of the genie to make your life easier. Life is full of little inconveniences that you have to put up with, but you’ve gotten so used to it that it’s difficult to think of them on the spot. Sure, your feet get tired when you walk for a long time, but is wishing for ‘no pain when you walk’ a waste? Can you not think of something better? If you can’t, would wishing for something like that even be wise? When you cross your arms, you heft your pack so that you can get your hand into a more comfortable position against its strap. It’s a small action that you do unconsciously, and you almost ignore it completely – when, suddenly, inspiration strikes. Having a pack to keep all of your adventuring gear in is an absolute necessity for your survival. It carries everything from food, to temporary shelters, to survival gear[lyric.around |, and even living creatures ]. You’d have been dead a few times over without your pack by now... which only serves to remind you of how limited it can be sometimes. There are times when you wish you had more space for more items. You’ve already convinced yourself, given how naturally you just thought of the word ‘wish’ for your inventory space. You ask Oma if it’d be possible to somehow grant you more space in your pack; if it’d be possible to store more things with you while you travel. "You could simply obtain a larger pack," Oma offers humorlessly. Sure, you could – but that’s not what you asked. "Manipulating the space within your pack to grant you more space than it can outwardly carry is within my power, yes." Is there a limit? Can she only, say, double the ‘space’ within your pack? "There is no limit, no." ... Wow. You have to be careful about this, though: there are lots of logistical challenges that go into having a pack with infinite space. Infinite space would also mean infinite weight. [etheryn.around |Just as you start to put some real thought into how to phrase the question, though, your train of thought is interrupted by the sound of wings flapping through the air – it’s a quiet sound, and you barely picked it up, but it contrasts against the quiet ambience just enough to stand out. And before you have a chance to turn your head and see what it is, something large lands on the pack you had set down nearby. It’s Harrick, Etheryn’s hunting hawk – and he’s got something in his talons. A [rand |lizard |rabbit ], its body having been gored through with his sharp claws and beak, the blood dripping off different parts of his body. Harrick gives you one look before he starts trying to hide his fresh kill in the open main pocket of your pack[lyric.around | – and causing Lyric, still inside, to shriek in surprise and kick [lyric.hisHer] legs to try and get Harrick to leave before dropping a dead animal onto [lyric.himHer] ]. "Harrick, no, not in there!" Etheryn shouts, running up to the pack to retrieve Harrick. He fusses, his wings spreading and flapping, and he makes a loud ‘caw’ in indignation that Etheryn is interrupting his meal, but, ultimately and begrudgingly, he concedes to letting her pick him up – but not to dropping his kill. "I’m sorry about that," Etheryn says sheepishly as she sets Harrick down on the ground, standing between him and your pack. "He gets all fussy and independent if I take too long to feed him, and he can be a bit of a hoarder over food. I hope we’re not interrupting anything." You tell her that it’s fine; you were just– Well... now that you think about it, you were going to wish for more carrying capacity from Oma. Maybe a larger backpack, or more pockets, or something. But, if anything, this whole ordeal has taught you that maybe less pockets would be the better move, if things like this are going to happen. "No, please, don’t reconsider on my sake," Etheryn implores you. "This shouldn’t happen again; I’ll be sure to stay on top of looking after Harrick." You tell her that it’s alright. Honestly, knowing Oma, she’d try to mess up your wish on purpose if your phrasing wasn’t absolutely airtight anyway. It just means you have other options to consider. |You take a moment to think about how you want to phrase your wish. After some time deliberating with yourself, you turn to Oma and you wish for a new pocket on your pack, with a mouth as large as your main pocket, that contains infinite space to store infinite items, and that your pack does not gain or lose weight when items are added to the pocket. It’s a meticulously-worded wish, and you can see Oma’s brow flutter as she tries to wrangle with the language of your wish, but only for a moment. She raises her left hand, all five digits glowing an off-blue, before she brings her middle finger and thumb together – and she snaps them, the sharp sound of skin-on-skin echoing in your ears. "Granted." You set down your pack, excited to see what your wish has gotten you. Sure enough, your pack’s depth has increased slightly to make room for the second mouth, just as large and wide as the pack’s main pocket. Anything you could fit into your pack normally would also fit in there. When you open it, all you see is the interior fabrics; there’s nothing in it. You search your immediate surroundings, looking for something to test the supposed ‘infinite’ space within this second pack. At your foot is a particularly sturdy stone, roughly the size of your hand, with a considerable amount of weight to it: you pick it up, set it inside the new pocket, and close it. You lift your pack with one hand, testing its weight. True to your instructions, you can’t feel the difference; it’s like the rock isn’t in there at all. You set the pack down and open the pocket again, reaching in to retrieve the stone– But you can’t find it. Your hand swings back and forth, left and right, swinging around in the infinite space within the pocket. You reach far enough down that you should be wrist-deep into the ground, but you can’t find the rock you just put in there. It’s gone. You ask Oma where the rock went. Your hand can’t find it. "Oh, it’s in there," she confirms, her face as stoic as ever. You know it’s in there. You asked how to find it. "Just keep looking," she answers. "Though it may take a bit of time." You shove your arm into the pack shoulder-deep, your fingers grasping for anything inside of it. Your hand doesn’t brush against the interior fabrics of the pack; in fact, despite you being on your knees and pushing the outer fabrics of the pack against the ground, your hand makes contact with absolutely nothing inside of there. It’s like you’ve shoved your arm into empty air. Eventually, you withdraw your arm and pull the pocket of the pack open, hoping to spot the rock with your eyes. But you don’t: all you see is the interior fabrics of the pack – something you couldn’t feel when you were shoulder-deep in there. It’s like the rock just disappeared. "Your wish has been granted to your exact specifications," Oma explains. "Within that pocket is an infinite amount of space. Adding anything to it will not increase the weight of the pack. Your stone is in there, [oma.wishesLeftRange 1 2 3 |[pc.name] |[pc.master] |[pc.master] ] – you simply need to find it." How are you supposed to do that? It’s infinite! "Perhaps you should have specified," Oma answers, her nostrils flaring. Perfect. What you have isn’t infinite storage space in your pack; what you have is an ordinary pack, but one of its pockets is an endless, infinite, yawning void of nothing. ... Maybe you should sew that pocket shut. ] ]
rows.translation: [oma.freedomWishedFor |你拥有精灵赋予的近乎无限的力量，可以利用它来许任何你想要的东西。你可以马上把那个愿望应用到一些实际的事情上吧。[pc.isBimbo | 或者非常棒 ]就像某种武器一样。你可以试着许下一些更有益于他人的愿望，比如消除世界上的饥饿问题。 但是你也需要照顾好自己：这个世界充满了危险，而且非常无情；即使是一些看似平常的事物，如果你没有做好准备，也可能会带来危险。每次当你离开像鹰棘镇这样的安全庇护所时，你都在很大程度上依赖自己已经为即将面临的任何挑战做好了充分的准备。仅仅拥有一个结实的盾牌、一把锋利的剑以及一些保暖的衣服是远远不够的；甚至像没有妥善准备午餐这样的小事，也可能在未来带来严重的后果。如果你连自己的肚子都填不饱，又怎么可能去期望解决世界饥饿这样的问题呢？ 如果说从开始这段旅程以来你学到了什么，那就是：一个准备得当的背包真的能决定你的生死。即便你拥有一个容量较大的背包，并且也掌握了如何最有效地利用背包空间的方法，往往还是会在你还没做好充分准备之前，就发现背包空间已经不够用了。如果背包能有更多的储物空间，那简直就是天赐之物——你甚至可以请求奥玛再给你一个更大的背包，用来存放你的物品。 作为回应，她困惑地皱起了眉头，把头偏向一边，挑起了眉毛：“你完全可以购买一个容量更大的包装啊，”她建议道。 确实，那样做也是可以的。但那并不是你最初提出的问题。 奥玛思考着你的问题，轻轻吐了吐舌头。“我的意思是，没错，给你一个更大的包裹显然在我能力范围之内，”她继续说道，“但这样使用愿望似乎有点太浪费了。更大的包裹你完全可以通过购买来获得啊。你可以利用一些材料、技巧和时间自己制作一个。 奥玛双臂交叉，将下巴搁在空闲的手上，仔细思考着这个愿望。“还有物流方面的问题。如果背包更大，就能装下更多的物品——但同时，背包也会变得更重，下垂得离地面更近，从而影响行动自由。而携带的物品越多，重量自然也会增加，在环境恶劣或地形复杂的地区，过重的背包反而会成为致命的隐患。 在你听来，她似乎是在试图劝你放弃这个愿望。 “绝对不是这样，”她回答道，“我是想帮你避免浪费一个愿望。正如我所说，推出更大的包装版本是在我的能力范围之内的，但也需要克服一些实际困难——所有这些挑战都还有只要在我能力范围之内，这些问题完全可以得到解决；只需要在愿望中明确提出来即可。” “好的，那么你需要许一个得到更大包裹的愿望……” 然而，你还没来得及把想法说完整，奥玛就打断了你。我认为，增加背包的容量并不是正确的解决办法。”
