rows.original: Tie them up. Demons or not, these women are still Etheryn's subjects. The Crown can figure out something to do with them later.
rows.translation: 把她们绑起来。不管这些女人是不是恶魔，她们终究还是伊瑟琳的子民。王室以后再想办法处理她们吧。
rows.raw: "Tie them up. Demons or not, these women are still Etheryn's subjects. The Crown can figure out something to do with them later."

rows.original:
You push Ryn aside and do what she lacks the courage to: putting these corrupted traitors to the sword. The elven princess gasps, reaching out to grab at your wrist before you can do it, but she has no power to stop you. 

        Etheryn covers her mouth, looking away at the last moment. For her part, Daliza gives you the slightest of nods, lips tight, before climbing the stairs to examine the runework on the platform. She takes Etheryn with her, guiding the princess by the hand. 
        
        "It looks like some kind of lift," the bailiff calls down once you're done. "There's an activation rune here, I think."
        
        That's your ticket upwards, then.
rows.translation:
你将小琳推到一边，做了她没有勇气去做的事——将这些堕落的叛徒处决。精灵公主惊呼出声，在你动手之前试图抓住你的手腕，但她根本无力阻止你。 

        伊瑟琳在最后一刻捂住了嘴，将视线移开了。而达莉莎则微微点了点头，嘴唇紧闭，随后走上楼梯去检查平台上的符文。她牵着伊瑟琳的手，带着这位公主一起前往。 
        
        看起来像是某种升降装置，”等你们完成后，法警往下喊道，“这里应该有一个激活符文。”
        
        那么，这就是通往上层的途径了。

rows.translation: 因此，总是如此，面对恶魔也是如此。

rows.original: The sound of hammer-blows echoes through the tower from this floor, each strike on the anvil rattling your teeth with its awesome power. The main chamber has several large windows overlooking the keep far, far below — a necessary adaptation, considering how much black smoke is billowing through the room from a tremendous bronzesmithing apparatus that surrounds the walls, with bellows and burning coals liquifying the metal and sending it running through purifying filters made of strange crystal lattices. Uncounted hundreds of swords, spears, maces, and axes have piled up in the armory, overflowing from their storage racks and into piles on the floor. You've found where all those weapons are coming from. And from whom, too. Or rather, what. A titan made of stone stands at the heart of the forge, heaving up a tremendous crystal hammer and slamming it down on the anvil. It's a monstrous reflection of the human form, too top-heavy and with great sweeping horns and a tail that must be necessary to stabilize its massive form. To your eyes, though, the thing looks more demonic than draconic. Each time it raises its immense arms, chains of gold linked to gilded manacles drag across the floor. "Goddess, what have you wrought...?" Daliza murmurs, watching the stone-and-crystal behemoth work. She takes a cautious step closer, disembarking the lift platform. The moment her boot touches the floor of the forge, the golem freezes, hammer suspended in the air mid-swing. Dal gasps, hand tightening around her sword's hilt, as the sound of stone grinding on stone fills the forge. The golem slowly rotates its head around to stare her down, crystal eyes flaring with an inner light. You shout a desperate "Watch out!" as the golem's crystalline muscles flex, and its hammer begins to raise again. The cudgel comes down in the blink of an eye, but Daliza's just a little bit faster, drawing her blade and lunging in quick enough that the hammer crashes into the ground where she'd been standing while she slashes her kitsune-forged blade across the golem's chest. Sparks fly wildly, scattering across the floor, but as the behemoth lumpers around again, you can see there's hardly a scratch on it. Daliza snarls, swinging her blade back up into a high guard. "A little help, [wayfort.hasDaliza |m'[pc.mf |lord |lady ]? |please! ]" You and Ryn exchange a look and ready your weapons.
rows.translation: 铁锤的敲击声从这一层传遍整座高塔；每一次砸上铁砧的巨响，都以惊人力量震得你的牙齿颤动。主厅开着几扇宽大窗户，可以俯瞰远在下方的要塞——这是不可或缺的改造，因为环绕墙壁的巨型青铜锻造装置正让滚滚黑烟充斥房间；风箱与燃烧的煤炭将金属熔为液体，使其流经奇异水晶晶格制成的净化滤器。数百柄难以计数的刀剑、长矛、钉锤与战斧堆满兵工厂，从储物架一直溢出，在地板上堆成小山。 你找到了那些武器的来源，也找到了铸造者。或者更准确地说，铸造它们的东西。 一名石头构成的泰坦伫立在锻炉中心，举起巨大的水晶锤，狠狠砸上铁砧。它是人类形态的怪物倒影：上身过于沉重，生有巨大而弯曲的犄角，还有一条大概用于稳定庞大身体的尾巴。但在你眼中，这东西更像恶魔，而非巨龙。每当它抬起硕大双臂，连在镀金镣铐上的金色锁链便会拖过地板。 “女神啊，你们究竟创造了什么……？”达莉莎注视着石头与水晶构成的巨兽工作，低声说道。她谨慎地靠近一步，离开升降平台。靴子接触锻炉地面的瞬间，魔像便停住动作，铁锤悬在半空。石头摩擦石头的声音充满锻炉；达莉莎倒吸一口气，握紧剑柄。魔像缓缓转过脑袋，直直盯着她，水晶双眼燃起内在光芒。 魔像的水晶肌肉绷紧，铁锤再度开始抬起；你绝望地大喊：“小心！”重锤转瞬间砸落，但达莉莎仍然快了一点；她拔剑扑出，速度之快，让铁锤只砸中刚才站立的地面，同时狐妖锻造的剑刃则斩过魔像胸膛。火花疯狂飞溅，洒满地面；可巨兽再次笨重转身时，你能看出它几乎没有留下半点伤痕。达莉莎怒吼着，把剑重新举到上段架势。 “来帮个忙，[wayfort.hasDaliza |我的[pc.mf |大人 |女士 ]？ |拜托了！ ]” 你和小琳交换一道目光，纷纷备好武器。

rows.original:
One of the golem's tremendous fists crashes into your chest, sending you flying back against the far wall. Stars of darkness explode across your vision, and your ears ring with the sound of your breaking bones. You slump down, drooling blood, barely aware of somebody shouting your name.

    It doesn't matter, though. You're so tired after all the fighting that you just can't keep your eyes open anymore.
    
    You never open them again.
rows.translation:
其中一个魔像巨大的拳头狠狠击中你的胸膛，将你猛地撞向远处的墙壁。一片黑暗的星芒在眼前闪烁，你的耳边回荡着骨头断裂的声响。你瘫软在地，口中不断流着鲜血，几乎听不见有人在呼唤你的名字。

    不过，这些都已经无关紧要了。经过这么激烈的战斗，你已经累得再也睁不开眼睛了。
    
    你再也没有睁开过眼睛。
rows.raw:
"
    One of the golem's tremendous fists crashes into your chest, sending you flying back against the far wall. Stars of darkness explode across your vision, and your ears ring with the sound of your breaking bones. You slump down, drooling blood, barely aware of somebody shouting your name.

    It doesn't matter, though. You're so tired after all the fighting that you just can't keep your eyes open anymore.
    
    You never open them again."

rows.original:
The golem staggers back under the force of your party's assault, straining against the enchanted manacles binding its wrists and ankles. "Keep the pressure on it!" Daliza barks, leaping in and bringing her sword down on the golem's head, shearing across one of its horns. Shattered crystal scatters across the floor, but the behemoth remains standing — and if stone could look furious, the monstrosity's slashed-up face is damned close. It groans, the sound of gravel pouring, and lunges against its chains. The golden links strain, creaking and bending, giving way to the golem's bulging crystal muscles.

    "Get back!" Ryn yelps, ducking down behind one of the work benches just a moment before the chains snap entirely. You follow her lead and hit the deck as shrapnel goes flying everywhere, accompanied by a ringing echo that sets your teeth to aching. The floor trembles beneath you, and suddenly the golem, once ponderously sluggish, leaps across the forge and slams its hammer down into the workbench on its way sailing past. You and Ryn both yelp in shock, diving across the floor to escape the attack. 
    
    The golem roars, throwing its head back and pounding its chest. Embers of flame drool from its fingertips, searing the ground beneath its stony feet. 
    
    "Etheryn!" Daliza shouts, vaulting the bench to return to your side. "Stay back! It's gone berserk!"
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |"And what about me?" you complain,
        |You groan,
    ] getting up and leveling your [pc.weapon]. "We've got to stop this thing!"
rows.translation:
在你们的团队发起猛攻之下，那个魔像踉跄着后退，拼命挣扎着想要挣脱束缚着它手腕和脚踝的魔法手铐。“继续施加压力！”达莉莎大喊着，冲了上去，用剑砍向魔像的头部，将其的一只角砍掉了。破碎的水晶碎片散落在地板上，但那个巨大的怪物依然屹立不倒——如果石头也能表现出愤怒的话，那么这个怪物那布满伤痕的脸庞，简直就是愤怒的化身。它发出低沉的呻吟声，仿佛有碎石正在从它的体内倾泻而出，然后它拼命地挣扎着，试图挣脱那些锁链。那些金色的链条在承受压力时发出吱嘎声，不断弯曲，最终被魔像那凸出的水晶肌肉所撕裂。

    “快躲开！”小琳惊叫着，立刻躲到了其中一张工作台后面。就在这时，链条彻底断裂了。你顺着她的动作迅速趴倒在地，只见碎片四处飞溅，同时那震耳欲聋的回声让你的牙齿都感到刺痛。你脚下的地面开始震动，那只原本行动迟缓的魔像突然跃过熔炉，在飞驰而过的同时将铁锤猛地砸在工作台上。你和小琳都吓得大叫起来，急忙跳到地面以躲避这一攻击。 
    
    魔像发出怒吼，将头向后仰，不断捶打自己的胸膛。它的指尖迸发出火焰，灼烧着它那石质脚掌下方的地面。
    
    “伊瑟琳！”达莉莎喊道，她跳过长凳，迅速回到了你的身边。退后！它已经失控了！
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |那我呢？”你抱怨道，
        |你发出了呻吟声。
    ]站起来，提升自己的水平吧。 [pc.weapon]我们必须阻止这件事发生！

    The golem staggers back under the force of your party's assault, straining against the enchanted manacles binding its wrists and ankles. "Keep the pressure on it!" Daliza barks, leaping in and bringing her sword down on the golem's head, shearing across one of its horns. Shattered crystal scatters across the floor, but the behemoth remains standing — and if stone could look furious, the monstrosity's slashed-up face is damned close. It groans, the sound of gravel pouring, and lunges against its chains. The golden links strain, creaking and bending, giving way to the golem's bulging crystal muscles.

    "Get back!" Ryn yelps, ducking down behind one of the work benches just a moment before the chains snap entirely. You follow her lead and hit the deck as shrapnel goes flying everywhere, accompanied by a ringing echo that sets your teeth to aching. The floor trembles beneath you, and suddenly the golem, once ponderously sluggish, leaps across the forge and slams its hammer down into the workbench on its way sailing past. You and Ryn both yelp in shock, diving across the floor to escape the attack. 
    
    The golem roars, throwing its head back and pounding its chest. Embers of flame drool from its fingertips, searing the ground beneath its stony feet. 
    
    "Etheryn!" Daliza shouts, vaulting the bench to return to your side. "Stay back! It's gone berserk!"
    
    [pc.isCunning
        |"And what about me?" you complain,
        |You groan,
    ] getting up and leveling your [pc.weapon]. "We've got to stop this thing!"'

rows.original: Blow after blow lands against the golem before it finally starts to falter, shedding stone and crystal across the floor like a living thing might lose blood. Its swings are becoming more sluggish with every arrow and sword-stroke that shatters its outer layers, until finally, it takes a last couple of steps forward, groans, and slumps to its knees. The great stone hammer falls from its fingers, clattering across the floor. Ryn breathes a sigh of relief, lowering her [ryn.weapon] and slumping against the wall. "Lumia's breath. What... who made this thing?" "The better question is: who put these chains on it?" you ask, poking one of the gilden links with your [pc.foot]. Daliza nods, striding closer to the fallen golem. "The chains bound it, but also seemed to be driving the thing mad," she says. The bailiff's sword comes to rest on one of the manacles around its wrist. "Strange. These don't seem to be part of its original design. Just bolted on after the fact." Ryn looks between the stone and her subject. "[ryn.lowConfidence |W-W-Wait, you're not thinking of- |You're not thinking of cutting them off? ]" The bailiff half-smirks, and sweeps her blade across the golden cuff. Sparks fly, but the magic within the manacles is so strained from the fighting that even her mundane iron can slice through. The chain falls to the side, joined soon by the other three in as many deft strikes. When the last of them is sundered, there's a release of pressure in the air so monumental that your ears pop. The golem's stony limbs grind as new life floods through it. The fell glow in its eyes recedes, replaced by a pair of dim red embers. You tense when one of its hand reaches for a rack of weapons against the wall, but its rocky fingers close around another flat-faced smithing hammer, and the golem silently, ponderously turns its attentions back to the forge. It does not begin to smith, however. Once it has resumed its original position, the construct simply falls still, quietly waiting for... something. A command, perhaps. Daliza finally sheathes her blade and runs a hand through her hair. "I am... glad that worked. It would have been a shame to have to destroy something capable of this kind of work." She gestures to the room around you, overflowing with weapons. "Perhaps now it can be bent to the realm's service." Ryn blinks. "You think now it'll make us weapons?" "That would appear to be its purpose. Perhaps the chains were what allowed the demons to coerce the golem into doing their bidding? Either way, it seems docile for now. We can investigate it's abilities another day."
rows.translation: 一次又一次攻击落在魔像身上，它终于开始踉跄；石块和水晶洒落地面，如同活物失去鲜血。每一支箭矢和每一次剑击都震碎它的外层，使挥击愈发迟缓。最终，它向前迈出最后几步，发出呻吟，跪倒在地。巨大的石锤从指间滑落，哐当一声砸在地板上。 小琳松了口气，放下[ryn.weapon]，靠着墙壁瘫下。“卢米娅之息。什么……是谁造了这个东西？” “更好的问题是：谁给它戴上这些锁链？”你一边问，一边用[pc.foot]戳了戳一枚镀金链环。 达莉莎点点头，大步靠近倒下的魔像。“锁链束缚着它，但似乎也在逼它发疯，”她说道。女管事的剑刃停在套住魔像手腕的一枚镣铐上。“奇怪。这些似乎并非原始设计的一部分，只是事后用螺栓固定上去的。” 小琳在石头与自己的臣民之间来回看着。“[ryn.lowConfidence |等、等、等等，你该不会是想—— |你不会想把它们砍掉吧？ ]” 女管事露出一半坏笑，挥剑斩过金色镣铐。火花飞溅；但镣铐中的魔力已经因战斗而不堪重负，甚至她的普通铁剑也能将其斩断。锁链落向一旁，随后另三条也在同样数量的灵巧斩击下断裂。最后一条锁链分开的瞬间，空气中的压力得到释放，声势之大，令你的耳膜啪的一响。新的生机涌入魔像，石头四肢摩擦移动。双眼中的邪恶光芒逐渐退去，化作两点黯淡红色余烬。它一只手伸向墙边的武器架，令你绷紧身体；可岩石手指只是握住另一把平头锻造锤，魔像随即沉默而缓慢地把注意力重新转向锻炉。 不过，它并未开始锻造。构装体恢复原来的位置后便纹丝不动，只是安静等待着……某样东西。或许是一道命令。 达莉莎终于收剑入鞘，用一只手梳过头发。“我很……庆幸它奏效了。要是不得不摧毁能够完成这种工作的东西，那会很可惜。”她指向四周堆满武器的房间。“或许现在，可以让它为王国效力了。” 小琳眨眨眼。“你觉得它现在会为我们打造武器？” “那的确像是它的使命。或许正是这些锁链让恶魔能够强迫魔像替自己效命？无论如何，它现在似乎很温顺。我们可以改日再调查它的能力。”

rows.original: You approach the dormant golem, still cautious after your previous fight. The thing does not so much as move to acknowledge you, staring blankly down at the empty anvil in front of it. "D-did we break it?" Ryn asks. Daliza shakes her head. "I don't think so. Without the chains to bind it to a task, perhaps it's simply waiting for commands..." You take the shattered remnants of Njorhaalt's former royal crown and set them on the anvil: a circle imbued with golden light, and a shard of glacial ice that never melts. "Can you fix this?" you ask the stone construct. It stares, unmoving. Daliza steps up beside you, placing her hand on the golem's arm. "Do as [pc.heShe] says. Repair the crown." Stone grinds noisily as the golem's head slowly turns to regard the hand on its crystal-veined bicep. A tense moment passes as its hand curls around its new smithing hammer, before slowly hefting it up and picking up the pieces in its other hand. Where once it had hammered away with earthshaking force, now it taps away with almost delicate care, gently resetting the icy shard into the circlet and crimps the metal down around it, rebinding it into place. The whole process takes the golem just over a minute, after which it relaxes its grip on its hammer again and sets the crown down in your hands. It then goes stock-still once again. Ryn gasps as you hold the crown aloft, covering her heart with her hands. "Amazing. It looks exactly the same as- as with the ghost of grandmother we saw!" "It does," you say, running your fingers across the chill shard that makes up the crown's fore. "Should you be wearing this, as queen?" Your elven [ryn.fucked |lover |companion ]'s ears twitch. "I, well, we have another crown, made for my mother after grandmother passed. Alissa left it behind, s-so I'd planned on wearing that...[ryn.fucked | P-perhaps my consort should, um, wear this one... ]"
rows.translation: 你小心翼翼地靠近那个处于休眠状态的魔像，毕竟之前那场战斗还是让你心有余悸。那个怪物甚至没有丝毫反应，只是呆呆地望着它面前的空铁砧。 “我们……我们把它弄坏了吗？”小琳问道。 达莉莎摇了摇头：“我不这么认为。如果没有那些束缚它的任务，或许它只是在等待指令……” 你将恩乔哈尔特那顶破碎的王冠残片放在铁砧上：一个散发着金色光芒的圆环，以及一块永远不会融化的冰块碎片。 你能修好这个吗？”你问那座石制构造物。它只是呆呆地望着你，没有丝毫反应。 达莉莎走到你身边，将手放在那个魔像的手臂上。“动手吧。 [pc.heShe]修好那顶王冠吧。” 石块在研磨中发出刺耳的声音，与此同时，那个魔像的头缓缓转动，将目光投向它那布满水晶脉络的二头肌上。在紧张的片刻之后，它的手握住了新打造的铁锤，然后缓缓地将它举起来，同时用另一只手捡起了那些碎片。曾经，它以震天动地的力量猛力敲击，而现在，它却以近乎小心翼翼的动作轻轻敲打，将那块冰冷的碎片重新安置回环状结构中，然后把金属边缘压紧，将其牢牢固定回原位。整个过程耗时略超过一分钟，之后，这个魔像就会松开手中的锤子，将那顶王冠交到你的手中。然后，它再次静止不动了。 当你将王冠高高举过头顶时，小琳倒吸了一口凉气，双手捂住自己的心脏：“太神奇了……它看起来和我们看到的祖母的幽灵一模一样！” “确实如此，”你说道，手指轻轻抚过构成王冠前部的那片冰冷的碎片。作为一位女王，你真的应该穿这个吗？” 你的精灵族[ryn.fucked |恋人 |伴侣 ]他的耳朵微微一动。“我，嗯，我们拥有另一顶皇冠，是在祖母去世后为我的母亲制作的。艾莉莎把它留了下来，所以我本来打算戴上它……[ryn.fucked | 或许我的妻子应该……嗯，穿上这件吧…… ]"

rows.translation: 这样，伊瑟琳将会获得“冬之王冠”这件物品，同时她的各项属性也会得到永久性的提升。你确定要这样做吗？
rows.raw: "\n This will give Etheryn the Crown of Winter item along with a permanent stat boost. Are you sure you want to do this?"

rows.original: You heft up the crown and set it upon Etheryn's head, smiling as it fits perfectly atop her golden mane. She draws in a muted breath, eyes closing for a moment before her arms fly around your shoulders, and she pulls you into a tender hug. "Y-you're right. This is... this feels right." She runs her hands across the frigid icon now resting atop her head. "Thank you, [pc.name]. I don't know that I'd have had the courage to put this on without you." You catch a fleeting glimpse of Daliza smiling behind the princess as you let her go. Ryn takes another deep breath, nods, and gathers up her weapon from where she'd let if fall. "I... I still have to earn this crown, though. Alissa can't be far..."
rows.translation: 你将王冠举起来，轻轻戴在伊瑟琳的头上，看到它如此完美地镶嵌在她金色的长发中，你不禁露出了微笑。她轻轻吸了一口气，闭上眼睛片刻，然后双臂环绕着你的肩膀，将你紧紧拥入怀中。 “你……你说得对。这真的……真是太合适了。感觉起来……好的。” 她将双手放在那颗此刻正位于她头上的冰冷图标上。“谢谢。 [pc.name]如果没有你，我不知道自己是否有勇气戴上这顶王冠。” 当你放开她时，你瞥见了达莉莎在公主身后微笑的身影。小琳深吸一口气，点了点头，然后将掉在地上的武器捡了起来。“不过……我仍然必须赢得这顶王冠。艾莉莎应该就在附近吧……

rows.original: You spend a few minutes rifling through the drawers of the workshop tables, swiftly joined by your elven companions — they're as curious as you are as to what secrets the place might hold. "Tsk. I've never seen half of these tool designs before in my life," Daliza murmurs. "What were all these used for? Repairing that stone behemoth outside?" Ryn nods. "Maybe. These look like artificing tools. Magical. Look at all the runes engraved on them." You hold up a long metal rod as thick around as ten hairs and squint at it. Sure enough, there are runes on it... though they aren't in any spell-script you've ever come across before. [pc.bg scholar |They look like dragon-marks, though there's no way a drake could possibly have etched something so minute. ]Strange, but oddly beautiful, whatever they are. "I've no mind for magic, m'lady, so I'll take your word for it." Daliza takes a knee next to one of the chests and flicks the dust off it with the back of her hand. "Var Dracias have always been warriors. This tower was built by the mages of Estelore when the college was at its peak, and sent its wizards here to learn of our dragons' ancient sorcery. Why they needed a tower this big, though..." "It's certainly a wonder, though," Ryn says. "I've never seen anything half as big before." [var0 |"Except my dick," you tease. The princess's cheeks turn crimson. "That... is also pretty impressive." |"Almost as big as my dick." Your orc laughs from where she's sat picking her teeth with a splinter from the desk Ryn's trying to search. When the little elf glances up, it's to a face-full of bulge aimed at her. [ryn.lnhConfidence |"I... I guess..." |"It's... pretty close, yeah." |"In your dreams, big green." "Big's right," Arona leers. ] ] Your attention turns to the last of the chests, and the only one actually sitting up on a shelf — at least one that hasn't collapsed with age-rot. This one's got a lock on it, too, though a hesitant test shows it was never engaged. You lift up the box's wooden lid, vaguely aware of Ryn and Daliza peeking around either of your shoulders as you do so. It's not all that big, perhaps a foot on the long end and half as much deep, and it unleashes a puff of stale old air when you crank it open. [silly |"Nice hiss," you murmur. ]The inside is padded with blue velvet, and plays host to but a single, tiny artifact. "A ring," Daliza says, breathing shakily. [pc.isCunning |Her powers of observation never fail to impress. ]It is indeed a ring, or at least, part of one — it looks to have been made of whitewood, the same as Ryn's bow, but was shattered into perhaps a dozen different pieces, only half of which remain. The shards have been bound back by strands of red crystal, thin and opaque, pulsing faintly with an inner light to a rhythm that can't help but to evoke a slow, steady heartbeat. Pulse-pulse... pulse-pulse... pulse-pulse... "Njorhaalt whitewood," Daliza whispers, "inlaid with gold. It's just like in the tales: Jarl Eldred's ring, given to his draconic bride. It must be! Or what is left of it anyway. But what is that redness holding it together?" You reach in, tentatively scooping up the velvet pillow the ring rests on so that you can examine it more closely. The ring has no scent to it, but up close, the red crystal has a distinctly sanguine hue to it. Dried blood comes to mind. "Beautiful, though, isn't it?" the bailiff says. You can't disagree. Hesitantly, Daliza plucks it up, holding the ring up to the faint rays of [dayNight |sun |moon ]light spilling through the glassless windows. "I never heard of the ring shattering so. Perhaps when Jarl Talraed fell? But then... who would have repaired it? And with what?" "I [pc.isBimbo |dunno that anybody's left to ask |doubt you'll find your answers here ]," you say, looking around the abandoned workshop. You've just taken the only thing of immediate value here, as far as you can tell. She nods, closing her hand around the ring. "Of course. Still. Thank you, [daliza.fucked |love |Champion ], [party.compNames true] too, for helping me to recover this. It is... it is a precious thing, indeed." [pc.isBimbo |"Almost as precious as you!" you tell her. |You [daliza.fucked |give Dal a kiss on the cheek |clap the elf's shoulder ]. "Come on. [pc.isDK |I need you focused, now. No more distractions. |What are friends for? ]" ] "O-of course. Let's make haste, then. We've still a demon to lay low."
rows.translation: 你花了几分钟时间翻找工作台上的抽屉，你的精灵同伴也迅速加入了你的行动——他们和你一样，都对这个地方可能隐藏的秘密感到好奇。 “啧，这些工具的设计，有半数我都是第一次见到呢，”达莉莎低声说道。这些都是用来做什么的？是用来修理外面那个巨大的石像的吗？” 小琳点了点头：“也许吧。这些看起来像是某种魔法工具。上面刻满了符文。” 你拿起了那根粗细只有十根头发那么长的金属棒，仔细地端详起来。果然，那里是上面刻着一些符文……不过这些符文与你以前见过的任何法术咒语都不一样。 [pc.bg scholar |它们看起来像龙纹，不过一只小龙绝对不可能刻出如此精细的图案。 ]奇怪，但却有一种奇异的美丽，无论它们究竟是什么。 “我对魔法没什么兴趣，小姐，所以我相信您的话。”达莉莎在其中一个箱子旁边跪了下来，用手背轻轻拍去上面的灰尘。达拉西亚人历来都是战士。这座塔是由埃斯托洛尔的法师们在学院鼎盛时期建造的，他们将巫师们送到这里，是为了学习我们龙族古老的魔法。不过，他们究竟为什么需要这么一座巨大的塔呢……不过，这确实是个奇迹，”小琳说道，“我以前从未见过这么大的东西。 [var0 |除了我的阴茎……”你开玩笑道。 公主的脸颊顿时变得通红：“那…… 是也相当令人印象深刻。 |差不多有我的阴茎那么大。”那个兽人一边笑着，一边用桌子上的一根木刺剔牙。而当那个小精灵抬起头时，看到的却是一张满脸肌肉、鼓鼓囊囊的脸正对着她。 [ryn.lnhConfidence |我……我想…… |已经……很接近了，没错。 |在你的梦里吧，大绿色的东西。” “‘大’这个描述没错，”阿罗娜咧嘴笑道。 ] ] 你的注意力被最后一个箱子吸引了——它是唯一一个真正放在架子上的箱子，至少没有因为年久而腐烂倒塌。这个箱子上也有一把锁，不过尝试了一下后发现，锁从来都没有被上过。你掀开了箱子的木盖，这时你隐约感觉到小琳和达莉莎正从你的肩膀后面偷看里面。这个箱子并不是很大，长度大概有一英尺，深度则是它长度的一半。当你打开箱子时，一股陈旧的空气扑面而来。 [silly |真好听，”你轻声说道。 ]内部衬着蓝色天鹅绒，里面只放着一件极其微小的文物。 “一枚戒指，”达莉莎颤抖着说道。 [pc.isCunning |她的观察能力总是令人印象深刻。 ]这确实是一枚戒指，或者至少是戒指的一部分——它看起来是由白木制成的，和小琳的弓是用同样的材料打造的，但现在已经碎成了十几块，现在只剩下其中的一半。这些碎片被细长的红色水晶丝线固定在一起，这些水晶丝线既薄又不透明，会发出微弱的光芒，其闪烁的节奏让人不禁联想到缓慢而稳定的心跳声。脉冲…脉冲…脉冲…” “白木制成的戒指，上面镶嵌着黄金，”达莉莎轻声说道，“就像故事里描述的那样：埃尔德雷德伯爵送给他的龙族新娘的那枚戒指。一定是这样！至少现在剩下的部分应该是吧。但究竟是什么力量让这种红色保持住了它的形态呢？” 你小心翼翼地伸出手，将戒指所在的那个天鹅绒垫子取了出来，以便能更仔细地观察它。这枚戒指没有任何气味，但仔细看的话，那些红色水晶确实呈现出一种类似血液的颜色。干涸的血液浮现在脑海中。 “不过，真的很漂亮，不是吗？”执达官说道。你确实无法反驳这一点。 达尔扎犹豫了一下，最终拿起了那枚戒指，将它举到微弱的光线中[dayNight |太阳 |月亮 ]光线从没有玻璃的窗户中透了进来。“我从未听说过那枚戒指会碎裂。也许是在塔尔拉德领主倒下的时候？但那样的话……谁会去修理它呢？又用什么材料来修理呢？” “我[pc.isBimbo |不知道是否还有人愿意提出这个问题了…… |我怀疑你在这里找不到你想要的答案。 ]你说得对，”你环顾着那间废弃的车间说道。据你所见，你刚刚拿走了这里唯一有价值的东西。 她点了点头，将手指紧紧握住那枚戒指。“当然。不过，还是谢谢你。 [daliza.fucked |爱 |冠军 ]， [party.compNames true]太感谢你了，帮助我找回了这个。这确实是一件非常珍贵的东西。 [pc.isBimbo |几乎和你一样珍贵！”你对她说。 |你[daliza.fucked |轻吻达尔的脸颊 |轻拍精灵的肩膀 ]来吧。 [pc.isDK |现在，我需要你全神贯注，不要再有任何干扰了。 |朋友到底是用来做什么的？ ]" ] 哦，当然。那我们赶紧行动吧，还有个恶魔需要被消灭呢。
rows.raw: ' You spend a few minutes rifling through the drawers of the workshop tables, swiftly joined by your elven companions — they're as curious as you are as to what secrets the place might hold. "Tsk. I've never seen half of these tool designs before in my life," Daliza murmurs. "What were all these used for? Repairing that stone behemoth outside?" Ryn nods. "Maybe. These look like artificing tools. Magical. Look at all the runes engraved on them." You hold up a long metal rod as thick around as ten hairs and squint at it. Sure enough, there are runes on it... though they aren't in any spell-script you've ever come across before. [pc.bg scholar |They look like dragon-marks, though there's no way a drake could possibly have etched something so minute. ]Strange, but oddly beautiful, whatever they are. "I've no mind for magic, m'lady, so I'll take your word for it." Daliza takes a knee next to one of the chests and flicks the dust off it with the back of her hand. "Var Dracias have always been warriors. This tower was built by the mages of Estelore when the college was at its peak, and sent its wizards here to learn of our dragons' ancient sorcery. Why they needed a tower this big, though..." "It's certainly a wonder, though," Ryn says. "I've never seen anything half as big before." [var0 |"Except my dick," you tease. The princess's cheeks turn crimson. "That... is also pretty impressive." |"Almost as big as my dick." Your orc laughs from where she's sat picking her teeth with a splinter from the desk Ryn's trying to search. When the little elf glances up, it's to a face-full of bulge aimed at her. [ryn.lnhConfidence |"I... I guess..." |"It's... pretty close, yeah." |"In your dreams, big green." "Big's right," Arona leers. ] ] Your attention turns to the last of the chests, and the only one actually sitting up on a shelf — at least one that hasn't collapsed with age-rot. This one's got a lock on it, too, though a hesitant test shows it was never engaged. You lift up the box's wooden lid, vaguely aware of Ryn and Daliza peeking around either of your shoulders as you do so. It's not all that big, perhaps a foot on the long end and half as much deep, and it unleashes a puff of stale old air when you crank it open. [silly |"Nice hiss," you murmur. ]The inside is padded with blue velvet, and plays host to but a single, tiny artifact. "A ring," Daliza says, breathing shakily. [pc.isCunning |Her powers of observation never fail to impress. ]It is indeed a ring, or at least, part of one — it looks to have been made of whitewood, the same as Ryn's bow, but was shattered into perhaps a dozen different pieces, only half of which remain. The shards have been bound back by strands of red crystal, thin and opaque, pulsing faintly with an inner light to a rhythm that can't help but to evoke a slow, steady heartbeat. Pulse-pulse... pulse-pulse... pulse-pulse... "Njorhaalt whitewood," Daliza whispers, "inlaid with gold. It's just like in the tales: Jarl Eldred's ring, given to his draconic bride. It must be! Or what is left of it anyway. But what is that redness holding it together?" You reach in, tentatively scooping up the velvet pillow the ring rests on so that you can examine it more closely. The ring has no scent to it, but up close, the red crystal has a distinctly sanguine hue to it. Dried blood comes to mind. "Beautiful, though, isn't it?" the bailiff says. You can't disagree. Hesitantly, Daliza plucks it up, holding the ring up to the faint rays of [dayNight |sun |moon ]light spilling through the glassless windows. "I never heard of the ring shattering so. Perhaps when Jarl Talraed fell? But then... who would have repaired it? And with what?" "I [pc.isBimbo |dunno that anybody's left to ask |doubt you'll find your answers here ]," you say, looking around the abandoned workshop. You've just taken the only thing of immediate value here, as far as you can tell. She nods, closing her hand around the ring. "Of course. Still. Thank you, [daliza.fucked |love |Champion ], [party.compNames true] too, for helping me to recover this. It is... it is a precious thing, indeed." [pc.isBimbo |"Almost as precious as you!" you tell her. |You [daliza.fucked |give Dal a kiss on the cheek |clap the elf's shoulder ]. "Come on. [pc.isDK |I need you focused, now. No more distractions. |What are friends for? ]" ] "O-of course. Let's make haste, then. We've still a demon to lay low." '

rows.original: You step up to the writing desk beside the bed[party.has arona |, grimacing as Arona flops herself into the latter with gusto ]. When you get within about two feet of of the crystal sat ensconced atop it, the gem flares with an enchanted light deep within that grows into a luminescent glow. A quartet of runes flicker to life above it, hovering on threads of light projected from the heart of the gem, each bearing a draconic numeral — a clawmark, then two, then three side by side, and a fourth that's a single clawmark and a V-shape. [first RQ2_STONE |"A memory crystal," Daliza gasps. "These are sacred to Nareva. [pc.swornGod nareva |I believe your gothic Order goes to great lengths to collect these, don't they, [pc.name]? |Her holy Order Astrida goes to great lengths to recover these all over the world. ] They're said to contain the living memories of those attuned to them. What a treasure they are, a true and incorruptible glimpse into the past." "C-can we see those memories?" Ryn asks, glancing between the crystal and the bailiff. Daliza nods. "Press your hand to one of the runes. It should show you the memory imprinted within." ] What do you do?

rows.original:
The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of an elf. She's extremely curvy, though nowhere near as statuesque as most boreal elves you've seen, perhaps five foot six at most. A Wyld Elf, then? You can hardly make out any details besides body shape, though, as if she's seen through a thick black fog. Her voice, however, carries clearly and with just enough of a western Belharan accent to be noticeable. 

        "Be it recorded in the third year of Queen Atheldred var Ridell's reign, and the seventeenth of Her Holy Majesty the Empress Julianna Harasii. Construction has finally finished on the highest floors of Cloudreach Tower, and the enchantments that will make my new abode livable are all in place. It is now possible to breathe up here without assistance, most importantly. So let it be recorded that on this, the forty-fourth day of spring, does the Collegia Magisterium of Estelore take receipt of this tower from the Skal'noria Clan who have long labored to ensure that it lives up to its name."
        
        Though the image hardly moves, you can hear the elf woman sigh. A chair scrapes the stone floor. "Given the several chests of gemstones we've just transferred from the Imperial coffers to the horde of Lady Senasthrelle, I do hope this tower proves half as sound an investment as the Archmagister seems convinced it will be. Our frosty cousins have only barely learned to tolerate Belharan presence on their borders, and already we're conspiring with their allies to build enormous fortifications on their islands. I fear the political cost of this tower may well outmatch the financial one. Yet Duchess Iveryn has once more assured me that the new queen wishes for a lasting peace, and... given said queenly sister has just married a Belharan lord and publicly given herself to the Lumian church, perhaps it's more than just posturing. I've done more than most to fight for peace, including more than my share of half-truths and cloaked daggering, but getting plowed by the Empress's cousin would be a step too far even for me. Seven help her, she might actually love him!"
        
        The elf-mage laughs dryly. "I suppose big-hearted, strong, and stupid has an appeal. Speaking of pretty men, with the tower finished off I ought to send a mage-missive back home to Marius. My husband's been chomping at the bit to come up and join me ever since the Collegia sent me to this northern frost-hell. Ah, yes, I should make sure he brings as many blankets as he can stuff into the ship. No amount of enchantment seems capable of shaking off the cold up here entirely."
rows.translation:
当你触碰到第一个符文时，那些光点便会闪烁着消散，它们的光芒汇聚成了一位精灵的朦胧身影。她的身材极为曲线优美，不过远没有你见过的那些极北精灵那样魁梧高挑，身高大概也就五英尺六英寸左右。那么，她应该是一位野精灵吧？不过，除了她的体型之外，你几乎无法分辨出她的其他特征，就好像她被一层浓重的黑雾所笼罩一样。然而，她的声音却清晰可闻，其中带着一丝明显的贝拉兰西部口音，让人很容易就能听出来。 

        谨记录于阿瑟尔德雷德女王统治的第三年，也是朱莉安娜·哈拉西女皇在位的第十七年——云达塔的最高层终于竣工了，那些能让我的新居变得宜居的魔法也都已经设置完毕。最重要的是，现在在这里呼吸已经不再需要任何辅助了。因此，让我们正式记录下来：在这个春天的第四十四天，埃斯特洛尔的法师学院正式接收了这座塔——正是斯卡尔诺里亚家族长期以来不懈的努力，才确保了这座塔名副其实。"
        
        虽然那幅图像几乎没有任何动静，但你可以听到那位精灵女子在叹息。一把椅子在石地上刮出了刺耳的声音。“考虑到我们刚刚把几箱宝石从皇室的金库中转移到了塞纳斯特蕾尔夫人的手中，我真心希望这座塔能像大法师所坚信的那样，成为一笔值得的投资。我们的那些冰冷的邻居才刚刚学会容忍贝尔哈兰人在他们边境的存在，而我们却已经与他们的盟友密谋在他们的岛屿上建造巨大的防御工事。我担心，建造这座塔楼所带来的政治代价可能会远远超过其经济成本。然而，艾薇琳公爵夫人再次向我保证，新女王确实渴望实现长久的和平……而且，考虑到这位女王的妹妹刚刚嫁给了贝尔哈兰的一位贵族，并且公开皈依了卢米安教会，这种表态或许并非只是表面功夫而已。我为争取和平付出了比大多数人更多的努力，甚至不惜使用一些半真半假的信息和隐晦的攻击手段。但被女皇的表亲所伤害，这对我来说也实在是太过分了。有七个人在帮助她，说不定她真的会爱上他呢！"
        
        那位精灵法师干笑道：“我想，慷慨大方、力量强大却又有点傻乎乎的人，确实会有一种吸引力吧。说到帅气的男人……等这座塔建好了，我应该给马略斯寄一封法师信回去。自从学院把我派到这个北方的冰冻之地以来，我丈夫就一直迫不及待地想过来陪我呢。啊，对了，我得让他带上尽可能多的毯子，因为这里的寒冷似乎根本无法用任何魔法来驱散。

rows.original: The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of an elf, seated across from a woman that might be a salamander save for her prodigious rack of horns and a pair of small wings sprouting from her shoulders. Almost reminds you of Kasyrra, actually, complete with a rather blatant bulge in the front of her kilt. Both women are shadowed, seen only in grayscale outlines that blur their features. The elf speaks first, her arm receding from the desk. "I promise, my lady, no one will see this recording without your express consent. What you say is between you, me, and the gods." The other woman nods slowly. "I will hold you to that, Magister. Your entire bloodline, if it comes to it." "It won't. Memory stones have more use than just recording voices, my lady. They take... a burden of memory. Sometimes all of it, if you wish it. Though your psyche is a bit too powerful for that, I'm afraid. You'd likely shatter the crystal with a thought if we tried entirely emptying your mind. Still, just talking about it will... it may ease the weight on your mind. So. Tell me about these dreams, my lady." The winged salamander exhales slowly. "It has been months now of the same dream every night through which I can manage to sleep. It begins here, in your study, with you and your husband. There are children; twins. The jarl is present as well. A shadow rises over the horizon from the south, full of such evil that it shatters the mind of all that it touches, reduces them to madness. I take wing, rushing headlong to fight this wickedness among the clouds, but it is strong. Stronger than even I. Every night that I dream, Magister, I dream of a thousand daggers of wickedness-given-form piercing my breast and driving at my heart. A death that bites deeper than death. I slept rarely, before. Now? Now I am... I am afraid to." "It's difficult to imagine you being afraid of anything, Lady Senasthrelle." Daliza cuts her eyes to you, widening. "You see why I don't want this recorded, Magister?" "There's no shame in fear. During the war, Marius would always tell our men 'It is not fear I hate, but cowards. Fear can make you strong. It can keep you alive. Heroes feel fear as much as any of you. It is what you do with that fear that makes you a coward, or a hero.' I always thought there was some merit to that." The other woman's wings stretch out as she leans back in her seat. "Your husband is entirely too pretty to have been saying such things. I knew the dragon that gave him those handsome scars on his legs, but I still cannot picture such a small elf-boy leading a warhost of mage-knights. Much less slaying my kin." "We're talking about your dreams, Lady Senasthrelle. Please. Tell me: why do you keep charging into battle against this, this great shadow? You seem certain you can't defeat it." "How does one fight a shadow?" Senasthrelle says. "I am still trying to understand, myself. But even in my dreams, I know that if I cannot defeat it, there is no way Jarl Talraed and his men can. I fight so that they can flee — so that they can live. I have watched over the people of this island since I was a hatchling, as my mother did before me when the pale elves first landed here. If my death buys one Dracian life, it will have been worth it." The Magister pauses. "Do you truly believe that? That a dragon's life is worth an elf's?" "Life has no greater or lesser worth if you are born in an egg or from a mother's womb; from an empress or from a farmer's daughter. I swore on my mother's tomb to protect the people of this island from any who would do them harm, be they Belharan or from Beyond. And besides: like you, now, I plan to raise a family here of my own." "How did you-" The memory fades as the Magister reaches for the crystal.
rows.translation: 当你触碰到第一个符文时，那些符文会闪烁着光芒消散开来，它们的光芒汇聚成了一道朦胧的身影——一个精灵。这个精灵坐在一位女性的对面，而这位女性，如果她没有那一对巨大的角以及从肩膀上长出来的小翅膀的话，简直就像是一条蝾螈。其实，这两人几乎让人联想到卡希拉——尤其是那位女性，她的裙摆前部明显隆起。两位女性的身影都被阴影笼罩，只能看到模糊的灰度轮廓，无法辨认出她们的面容。 首先开口说话的是那位精灵女性，她的手臂从桌子上收回了。我向您保证，夫人，没有您的明确许可，没有人会看到这段录像。您所说的话，只会在您、我以及众神之间流传。” 另一位女士缓缓点了点头。“我会要求您遵守这个承诺的，大师。如果有必要的话，甚至会动用您整个家族的力量来确保这一点。不会的。夫人，记忆石的作用可不仅仅是记录声音，它们还能承载……记忆的负担。有时候，如果您愿意的话，它们甚至可以承载所有的记忆。不过，恐怕您的精神力量太过强大，这样的负担对它们来说也有些难以承受吧。如果我们试图彻底清空你的思绪，你很可能会仅仅通过一个念头就使那块水晶碎裂。不过，仅仅是谈论这件事……也可能会产生同样的效果。轻松你心中所忧之事，不妨告诉我吧，我的女士。” 那只长着翅膀的蝾螈缓缓吐了口气：“已经有好几个月了，每晚我都会做同一个梦，而也只有在这个梦里，我才能真正入睡。这个梦的一切，都始于你的书房，始于你和你的丈夫。那里有一些孩子，还有双胞胎。那位酋长也在场。从南方地平线上升起了一道阴影，那阴影充满了邪恶的力量，凡是它触及的东西，都会被其摧毁，使人陷入疯狂。我立刻振翅飞起，冲向云层中去与这种邪恶力量战斗，但它实在太强大了…… 甚至比我还要强大。每晚当我入睡时，大师，我都会梦见上千把邪恶之刃刺穿我的胸膛，直击我的心脏。那种痛苦，比真正的死亡还要深刻。以前，我很少能够入睡。而现在呢？现在我……我害怕这样做。 真难以想象你竟然会害怕任何事情，塞纳斯特雷尔女士。” 达莉莎睁大了眼睛看着你。 “现在您应该明白为什么我不想让这件事被记录下来了吧，大师？” “害怕并没有什么可羞耻的。在战争期间，马略总是对我们士兵们说：“我憎恨的并不是恐惧，而是懦夫。恐惧能够使人变得坚强，能够让人活下去。英雄们也会像你们一样感到恐惧。真正决定一个人是懦夫还是英雄的，是这个人如何面对恐惧。我一直认为这其中确实有些道理。 另一个女人向后靠在椅子上，她的翅膀展开了。“你丈夫长得实在太帅了，不可能会说出那种话来。我知道是那条龙在他腿上留下了那些漂亮的疤痕，但我还是无法想象一个这么小的精灵男孩能够率领一支由法师骑士组成的军队。更别说还能杀死我的族人了。 我们谈论的是你的梦想，塞纳斯特雷尔女士。请告诉我：为什么你总是执意要与这个巨大的阴影战斗？你似乎很清楚自己无法战胜它。” “那么，该如何与一个阴影战斗呢？塞纳斯特雷尔说道，‘我仍在努力理解这一切。但即使在梦中，我也明白：如果我无法战胜它，那么塔尔拉德领主和他的部下也绝无可能成功。我战斗，只是为了让他们能够逃脱——为了让他们能够活下来。从我还是个幼崽的时候起，我就一直在守护着这个岛上的人民。我的母亲在淡色精灵第一次来到这里时，也是这样做的。如果我的死亡能够挽救一个达拉西亚人的生命，那么这一切都是值得的。 大师停顿了一下。“你真的这么认为吗？认为一条龙的性命就比一个精灵的性命更重要？” “无论一个人是诞生在蛋中，还是通过母亲的子宫出生；无论他是皇室成员，还是农民的女儿，他们的生命都没有高低贵贱之分。我在母亲的墓前发誓，要保护这个岛上的人民，让他们免受任何伤害——无论是来自贝尔哈兰的人，还是来自其他地方的人。而且，就像你现在一样，我也打算在这里建立一个属于自己的家庭。 你是怎么做到的……” 随着法师伸手去拿那块水晶，那些记忆渐渐消失了。
rows.raw: ' The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of an elf, seated across from a woman that might be a salamander save for her prodigious rack of horns and a pair of small wings sprouting from her shoulders. Almost reminds you of Kasyrra, actually, complete with a rather blatant bulge in the front of her kilt. Both women are shadowed, seen only in grayscale outlines that blur their features. The elf speaks first, her arm receding from the desk. "I promise, my lady, no one will see this recording without your express consent. What you say is between you, me, and the gods." The other woman nods slowly. "I will hold you to that, Magister. Your entire bloodline, if it comes to it." "It won't. Memory stones have more use than just recording voices, my lady. They take... a burden of memory. Sometimes all of it, if you wish it. Though your psyche is a bit too powerful for that, I'm afraid. You'd likely shatter the crystal with a thought if we tried entirely emptying your mind. Still, just talking about it will... it may ease the weight on your mind. So. Tell me about these dreams, my lady." The winged salamander exhales slowly. "It has been months now of the same dream every night through which I can manage to sleep. It begins here, in your study, with you and your husband. There are children; twins. The jarl is present as well. A shadow rises over the horizon from the south, full of such evil that it shatters the mind of all that it touches, reduces them to madness. I take wing, rushing headlong to fight this wickedness among the clouds, but it is strong. Stronger than even I. Every night that I dream, Magister, I dream of a thousand daggers of wickedness-given-form piercing my breast and driving at my heart. A death that bites deeper than death. I slept rarely, before. Now? Now I am... I am afraid to." "It's difficult to imagine you being afraid of anything, Lady Senasthrelle." Daliza cuts her eyes to you, widening. "You see why I don't want this recorded, Magister?" "There's no shame in fear. During the war, Marius would always tell our men 'It is not fear I hate, but cowards. Fear can make you strong. It can keep you alive. Heroes feel fear as much as any of you. It is what you do with that fear that makes you a coward, or a hero.' I always thought there was some merit to that." The other woman's wings stretch out as she leans back in her seat. "Your husband is entirely too pretty to have been saying such things. I knew the dragon that gave him those handsome scars on his legs, but I still cannot picture such a small elf-boy leading a warhost of mage-knights. Much less slaying my kin." "We're talking about your dreams, Lady Senasthrelle. Please. Tell me: why do you keep charging into battle against this, this great shadow? You seem certain you can't defeat it." "How does one fight a shadow?" Senasthrelle says. "I am still trying to understand, myself. But even in my dreams, I know that if I cannot defeat it, there is no way Jarl Talraed and his men can. I fight so that they can flee — so that they can live. I have watched over the people of this island since I was a hatchling, as my mother did before me when the pale elves first landed here. If my death buys one Dracian life, it will have been worth it." The Magister pauses. "Do you truly believe that? That a dragon's life is worth an elf's?" "Life has no greater or lesser worth if you are born in an egg or from a mother's womb; from an empress or from a farmer's daughter. I swore on my mother's tomb to protect the people of this island from any who would do them harm, be they Belharan or from Beyond. And besides: like you, now, I plan to raise a family here of my own." "How did you-" The memory fades as the Magister reaches for the crystal.'

rows.original: The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of an elf. She's extremely curvy, though nowhere near as statuesque as most boreal elves you've seen, perhaps five foot six at most. She's quite heavily pregnant, gravid with child such that she has dragged the memory crystal to the desk's edge in order to activate it from her chair. "Be it recorded in the seventh year of Queen Atheldred var Ridell's reign, and the second of His Holy Majesty the Emperor Claudio the Second Harasii. It has been six months since Lady Senasthrelle first confided in me about her dark dreams. They continue unabated, once a week when the dragoness becomes too tired to avoid sleeping — and gods but she does avoid it as much as possible. These premonitions of death worry my husband to no end; Marius may be a learned scholar of the highest renown, but he's as religious as they come. Nobody's perfect. He insists on reminding me that the Holy Belharan Empire was founded from an oracle's mad ramblings, and that the legends tell of a goddess founding Estelore, so what do I know? According to Marius: 'If you have half the brain left that I fell in love with, Viona, you'll investigate.' Bah." "I've delved the issue as much as I can from here. Tried hypnosis, dream-diving, even letting the dragon's mighty psyche crack my only spare memory crystal trying to off-load her dream into it. That was a right mess. But it's all been fruitless. I have no scrolls here laden with the wisdom to treat a war-traumatized lizard and her recurring nightmares of endless shadows consuming the world." The elf groans wearily, resting a hand on her stomach. "Gods. I'm entirely too big for this early into a pregnancy. Didn't Senasthrelle say something about my having twins in her nightmare? Mmm. Maybe there's truth in dreams. Nothing much we can do about it at the moment, though. I failed utterly to convince the Lady Senasthrelle to debase herself enough that she'd fly down to Estelore and actually talk with a specialist. Sigismund would probably — no, absolutely — cream his robes at the chance to peer through the dreams of a dragon. Heh. Senasthrelle might have the right idea, actually. Still and all, I'm entirely out of commission, and Marius hasn't walked ten paces without his cane and brass braces since the war. Neither of us is going on some grand adventure of lore-seeking." The Magister turns to a figure out of sight of the crystal and waves a hand. You hear the squeak of old hinges from the direction of the door, to the beat of bootfalls on stone. "Yes, I was just talking about you... yes, only good things, my knight. Always." You catch the faint trace of a smile on the shadow's features as she returns her attention to the crystal. "At the behest of my extremely handsome, boundlessly affectionate, and utterly brilliant husband I have sent a mage-missive to the most prolific expert on dreams I know outside Estelore. Thyri Hegansdottir — sorry, Jarlessa Gunvaldsen now, I keep forgetting — has been publishing some remarkable works among the collegia arcana on the connection between dreams and magic. Fascinating stuff, actually. Truth be told, I'm mostly hoping that Thyri's mixed blood will be a convincing argument for Senasthrelle to forgive my reaching for outside help. I'm entirely sure she'd just step on me if I tried roping Arch-Magister Sigismund or any of my colleagues back at Estelore into this mystery." She sighs at something said beyond the crystal's ken. "You've been stepped on by a dragon, Marius. Contain yourself."
rows.translation: 当你触碰到第一个符文时，那些符文的光芒便会熄灭，汇聚成一位精灵的朦胧身影。她的身形极为曲线优美，不过远没有你见过的那些极北精灵那样魁梧高挑，身高大概也就五英尺六英寸左右。她已经怀孕很久了，胎儿的重量使得她不得不将记忆水晶拖到桌边，才能从椅子上操作它来激活它。 谨记录于阿瑟尔德雷德·瓦·里德尔女王统治的第七年，也是克劳迪乌斯二世·哈拉西皇帝在位的第二年。自从塞纳斯特蕾尔小姐第一次向我倾诉她那些可怕的梦境以来，已经过去了六个月。这种事情每周都会发生一次，每当那位女龙太疲惫而无法避免入睡时——不过她其实会尽最大努力避免这种情况发生。这些关于死亡的预感让我的丈夫忧心忡忡；尽管马略是一位声名显赫的学者，但他却是个极其虔诚的宗教信徒。没有人是完美的。他总喜欢提醒我，神圣贝拉兰帝国其实是建立在一位先知疯狂的预言之上的；而传说中也有一位女神创立了埃斯托洛尔，所以我又能知道什么呢？按照马略斯的说法：“薇奥娜，如果你还有一半我当初爱上你的那份头脑的话，你就应该去调查一下的。呸。 我已经尽我所能去研究这个问题了。尝试过催眠、梦境探索，甚至让那条龙的强大精神力破坏了我唯一剩下的记忆水晶，试图将它的梦境转移到那块水晶上。结果一片混乱，但这一切都毫无成效。我这里可没有什么充满智慧的卷轴，能帮助我治疗这只深受战争创伤的蜥蜴，以及她那些关于无尽阴影吞噬世界的噩梦。”精灵疲惫地呻吟着，将手放在自己的肚子上。“天啊，才怀孕这么早，我的体型就已经变得这么大啦…… 塞纳斯特蕾尔不是在她的噩梦中说过我可能会生双胞胎吗？嗯……也许梦里说的都是真的。不过目前我们也无能为力，我完全没能说服塞纳斯特蕾尔女士放下架子，专程飞到埃斯托洛去咨询专家。西吉斯蒙德很可能会——不，其实并不会。绝对地 — 一有机会就能窥探龙的梦境，他简直乐不可支。呵呵，其实Senasthrelle的想法或许挺有道理的。不过，我现在完全无法行动了，而自战争以来，Marius走路时如果没有拐杖和铜制支撑装置，就连十步都走不了。我们俩都没有打算去进行什么寻找古老传说的冒险。” 法师转向水晶后面看不见的地方，挥了挥手。这时，你听到门的方向传来旧铰链发出的吱吱声，紧接着是靴子踩在石头上的声响。 是的，我刚才说的就是你……嗯，当然都是些好话，我的骑士。永远都是。”当她将注意力重新转向水晶时，你可以隐约看到她的身影中带着一丝微笑。“应我那位英俊潇洒、充满爱心且才华横溢的丈夫的要求，我给埃斯托洛之外我所认识的最擅长研究梦境的专家寄去了一封魔法信函。 泰丽·赫甘斯多蒂尔——抱歉，现在应该称她为贾勒萨·冈瓦尔德森，我总是忘记——最近在奥术学界发表了几篇关于梦境与魔法联系的杰出论文。这个课题确实很有意思。说实话，我更希望泰丽的混血身份能成为说服塞纳斯特雷勒原谅我寻求外界帮助的有力理由。如果我试图让大法师西吉斯蒙德或我在埃斯托洛的任何同事参与这个谜团，我敢肯定她肯定会拒绝我的请求。 她听到水晶之外传来的某些话语，叹了口气：“你已经马略斯，被一条龙踩到了。冷静点吧。

rows.original: The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of a pair of wyld elves: a short, effete male with motherine feelers sprouting from his brow who's standing with the help of a cane, and an extremely curvy woman dressed in figure-hugging robes. The woman's reached her hand onto the crystal, though it appears they're already deep mid-discussion — you're not sure if turning the memory crystal on was intentional or not. The man's already speaking: "-not abandon you, Viona. I did not earn these scars in battle just to leave my wife and soil my knickers at the first sight of a shadow on the sea." "Listen to me you boar-skulled buffoon," the woman snarls. "This is exactly what happened in Senasthrelle's dreams. A shadow from the south, like a twisting worm that stretches from the sea to the clouds. You're the one that believed it from the outset, and now it's happening for real. We have to act! I need you to take the children and-" "We have servants. Your apprentices; my squire. Any of them can take the children. Or we both can. You choose. But no matter what, I will not leave your side, Viona. I meant every word of what I swore on Nareva's altar." The woman's shoulders fall. "Damn you, Marius. You have to tell Estelore-" Before she can continue, the shadows are both shaken as if by an earthquake. By the time they've regained their footing, clutching each others' shoulders for support, another two shadows have strode into the crystal's aura from the direction of the balcony: a scaly woman with horns and wings, and a tall, sharp-featured boreal elf man buckled into full armor and carrying a brace of swords at his hip. The tall man speaks first, softly but with the confidence of absolute authority: "Arch-Magister Viona var Este. Ser Marius en Errion. I call upon the oaths you have both sworn to the Jarldom of Dracia. It is time." Both wyld elves straighten their backs, ears perking. "Aye, lord," Viona says. Marius raps a fist against his bicep. "What would you have of us, Jarl Talraed?" "Lady Senasthrelle means to meet whatever this creature on the horizon is," the Jarl says, inclining his head to the winged woman at his side. "And if need be, do battle with it. The creature is so large that I doubt our walls will hold it for more than a few minutes. She will delay its advance until my warriors are assembled and ready to face it. Magister, I will need your spells to support us. Our onagers won't be able to hit the thing once it gets over the walls; you're the only heavy hitter we'll have." The elf-woman bows her head. "Aye, Lord." "And what of me, Lord?" Ser Marius asks. He's produced a long, silvery sword of his own from somewhere, though even in featureless shadow you can see he struggles with its weight in one hand. "I can still fight." "Marius," the Jarl sighs. "This isn't the time for bravado. You earned your reputation in the war; I've felt Maidenscythe's sting myself. But those days are long past you. I need your mind more than your muscles now. Go, coordinate the evacuation." "Evacuate? Lord! It's a single creature, and we've a dragon!" The dragon herself finally speaks. "One dragon, thanks in no small part to that blade, Ser Marius. You of all people should know we are not invulnerable. I... I do not believe I will survive my encounter with this beast. But I will buy enough time for your children and the Jarl's to escape. For you to save as much of the island's people as you can." "This is madness! You order me into cowardice!" Marius protests. "This is necessity," the dragon says evenly, turning back towards the balcony. "Take the long way down, Talraed. I fly for the endless meadows." "Senasthrelle!" the Magister gasps, taking an unsteady step after her. The dragoness pauses, glancing over her shoulder. "For the gods' sake, don't do this. Don't die." The Jarl takes the Magister's hand and lowers it. The dragon departs without another word, and the shadows are shaken again by her departure. "Get all of our children to safety on the mainland, Marius. Goddess willing, we'll slay this beast and recall you in a day's time." He steps past the married pair, heading for the elevator. The wyld elves exchange a wary glance, but the Magister takes up a crescent-headed staff from beneath the bed and gives her husband a firm nod. "Gods be good. We're running out of time. I will see you on the other side, Marius." "The other side of the strait," he insists, hefting his sword onto a shoulder. "Break the world and sunder the heavens if you must, but I beg you... come back to me, Viona." "Always," she says. The two of them walk after their Jarl, and the memory fades. Daliza takes a shuddering breath when the light reconstitutes its original runes. Her hand rests heavy on the side of the desk; you wonder if that's all that's keeping her upright after all that.
rows.translation: 当你触碰到其中第一个符文时，那些符文会瞬间熄灭，它们的光芒汇聚成了一道朦胧的身影——那是一对野精灵：一个身材矮小、看起来有些柔弱的男子，他的额头上长着类似母亲触角的突起，他拄着拐杖站立着；另一个则是身材曲线极为优美的女子，她穿着紧身长袍。那位女士将手放在了那块水晶上，不过看起来他们当时正在深入讨论中——你不确定她是否故意打开了那块记忆水晶。 那位男士已经开口说道：“——不会抛弃你的，维奥娜。我身上的这些伤痕并不是在战斗中获得的，我可不想仅仅因为海面上出现一个阴影，就抛弃我的妻子，让自己陷入混乱。” “听好了，你这个头脑简单的蠢货，”女人怒斥道，“在塞纳斯特雷尔的梦境中，恰恰发生了这样的事情。一道来自南方的阴影，如同一条蜿蜒的蠕虫，从大海延伸到云端。从一开始，就是你相信了这一预言，而现在，它真的正在发生。我们必须采取行动！我需要你带着孩子们离开—— 我们有人手可以帮忙。你的学徒们，还有我的侍从，他们中的任何一个人都可以照顾这些孩子。或者，我们两者皆然你可以选择。但无论如何，我都不会离开你身边，薇奥娜。我在娜瑞瓦的祭坛前许下的每一句话都是真心话。 那个女人的肩膀垂了下来。“该死的，马略斯。你必须告诉埃斯特尔洛…… 她还没来得及继续说话，那些阴影突然像遭遇地震一样剧烈摇晃起来。当它们重新稳住身形，互相抓住肩膀以保持平衡时，又有两个阴影从阳台的方向走了进来，进入了那水晶散发出的光环之中：一个长着角和翅膀、皮肤覆满鳞片的女人，以及一个身材高大、五官轮廓分明的极北精灵男子，他全身穿着重甲，腰间还别着两把剑。 高个男子首先开口，声音轻柔，却带着绝对权威的自信：“大法师维奥娜·瓦尔·埃斯特。马里乌斯·恩·埃里恩。我现在要求你们履行当初向达拉西亚伯爵领地立下的誓言。时候到了。” 两位野精灵立刻挺直身子，耳朵竖得老高。“遵命，大人，”维奥娜说道。马里乌斯则用拳头敲了敲自己的二头肌。“塔尔拉德伯爵，您需要我们做什么？ 塞纳斯特蕾尔女士的意思是，无论地平线上出现的那个怪物是什么，我们都必须迎击它，”酋长说道，同时将头偏向身旁的这位有翅膀的女性。“如果有必要的话，甚至要与之战斗。那个怪物实在太大了，我怀疑我们的城墙根本无法抵挡它太久——她必须延缓它的进攻速度，直到我的战士们集结完毕、准备好与之对抗。法师，我们需要您的法术来支援我们。一旦那个怪物冲过了城墙，我们的投石机根本无法击中它；您才是我们手中唯一的强力武器。 那位精灵女子低下了头：“遵命，主人。” “那我呢，主人？”马略斯爵士问道。他从某个地方取出一把银轻型闪闪的长剑，尽管在昏暗的光线下也能看出，他单手握住这把剑显得有些吃力。“我仍然可以战斗。 马吕斯，”酋长叹息道，“现在不是逞勇的时候。你的名声是在战场上赢得的；我一直以来都很欣赏这一点…… 梅登西斯我真该自讨苦吃……但那些日子早已过去。现在我需要的不是你的力量，而是你的智慧。去，负责协调疏散工作吧。” “疏散？大人！那不过是一只怪物而已，而我们这里可有一条龙啊！” 这时，那条龙终于开口说话了。一条龙……在很大程度上要归功于那把剑，马略斯爵士。您最应该明白，我们并非无懈可击。我……我认为自己无法在这场战斗中存活下来。但我一定会为您的孩子们以及领主的家人争取足够的时间来逃脱。目的是为了让你们尽可能拯救岛上的居民。 这太疯狂了！你这是在逼我成为懦夫！”马略斯抗议道。 “这是必要的，”龙平静地说道，然后转身朝阳台走去，“塔拉德，你从另一条路下去吧。我会飞往那片无边无际的草原。” “塞纳斯特雷尔！”法师惊呼着，踉跄着跟了上去。龙女停下了脚步，回头看了他一眼：“看在诸神的份上，不要这样。不要死。 酋长握住了法师的手，将其放了下来。巨龙没有再说一句话便飞走了，它的离去再次扰乱了周围的阴影。“马略斯，把我们的孩子们都带到大陆上安全的地方去。如果女神愿意，我们一天之内就能消灭这只怪物，然后把你接回来。 他从那对已婚夫妇身边走过，朝着电梯走去。那些野精灵互相交换了警惕的目光，但那位女法师从床底下拿出一根新月形的法杖，坚定地点了点头对她的丈夫说：“愿诸神保佑。我们的时间不多了。马略斯，我们在另一边见吧。 海峡的对岸，”他坚定地说，将剑扛在肩上，“即使需要打破世界、分裂苍穹，我也恳求你……回到我身边来，薇奥娜。” “我一定会的。”她回答道。两人跟随他们的酋长继续前行，那些回忆也逐渐淡出了他们的记忆。 当光芒重新显现出那些原始的符文时，达莉莎不禁打了个寒颤。她的手重重地搭在桌子上；你不禁怀疑，在经历了这一切之后，是否只有这把桌子还在支撑着她，让她没有倒下。
rows.raw: ' The runes flicker away when you touch the first of them, their light coalescing into the shadowy figure of a pair of wyld elves: a short, effete male with motherine feelers sprouting from his brow who's standing with the help of a cane, and an extremely curvy woman dressed in figure-hugging robes. The woman's reached her hand onto the crystal, though it appears they're already deep mid-discussion — you're not sure if turning the memory crystal on was intentional or not. The man's already speaking: "-not abandon you, Viona. I did not earn these scars in battle just to leave my wife and soil my knickers at the first sight of a shadow on the sea." "Listen to me you boar-skulled buffoon," the woman snarls. "This is exactly what happened in Senasthrelle's dreams. A shadow from the south, like a twisting worm that stretches from the sea to the clouds. You're the one that believed it from the outset, and now it's happening for real. We have to act! I need you to take the children and-" "We have servants. Your apprentices; my squire. Any of them can take the children. Or we both can. You choose. But no matter what, I will not leave your side, Viona. I meant every word of what I swore on Nareva's altar." The woman's shoulders fall. "Damn you, Marius. You have to tell Estelore-" Before she can continue, the shadows are both shaken as if by an earthquake. By the time they've regained their footing, clutching each others' shoulders for support, another two shadows have strode into the crystal's aura from the direction of the balcony: a scaly woman with horns and wings, and a tall, sharp-featured boreal elf man buckled into full armor and carrying a brace of swords at his hip. The tall man speaks first, softly but with the confidence of absolute authority: "Arch-Magister Viona var Este. Ser Marius en Errion. I call upon the oaths you have both sworn to the Jarldom of Dracia. It is time." Both wyld elves straighten their backs, ears perking. "Aye, lord," Viona says. Marius raps a fist against his bicep. "What would you have of us, Jarl Talraed?" "Lady Senasthrelle means to meet whatever this creature on the horizon is," the Jarl says, inclining his head to the winged woman at his side. "And if need be, do battle with it. The creature is so large that I doubt our walls will hold it for more than a few minutes. She will delay its advance until my warriors are assembled and ready to face it. Magister, I will need your spells to support us. Our onagers won't be able to hit the thing once it gets over the walls; you're the only heavy hitter we'll have." The elf-woman bows her head. "Aye, Lord." "And what of me, Lord?" Ser Marius asks. He's produced a long, silvery sword of his own from somewhere, though even in featureless shadow you can see he struggles with its weight in one hand. "I can still fight." "Marius," the Jarl sighs. "This isn't the time for bravado. You earned your reputation in the war; I've felt Maidenscythe's sting myself. But those days are long past you. I need your mind more than your muscles now. Go, coordinate the evacuation." "Evacuate? Lord! It's a single creature, and we've a dragon!" The dragon herself finally speaks. "One dragon, thanks in no small part to that blade, Ser Marius. You of all people should know we are not invulnerable. I... I do not believe I will survive my encounter with this beast. But I will buy enough time for your children and the Jarl's to escape. For you to save as much of the island's people as you can." "This is madness! You order me into cowardice!" Marius protests. "This is necessity," the dragon says evenly, turning back towards the balcony. "Take the long way down, Talraed. I fly for the endless meadows." "Senasthrelle!" the Magister gasps, taking an unsteady step after her. The dragoness pauses, glancing over her shoulder. "For the gods' sake, don't do this. Don't die." The Jarl takes the Magister's hand and lowers it. The dragon departs without another word, and the shadows are shaken again by her departure. "Get all of our children to safety on the mainland, Marius. Goddess willing, we'll slay this beast and recall you in a day's time." He steps past the married pair, heading for the elevator. The wyld elves exchange a wary glance, but the Magister takes up a crescent-headed staff from beneath the bed and gives her husband a firm nod. "Gods be good. We're running out of time. I will see you on the other side, Marius." "The other side of the strait," he insists, hefting his sword onto a shoulder. "Break the world and sunder the heavens if you must, but I beg you... come back to me, Viona." "Always," she says. The two of them walk after their Jarl, and the memory fades. Daliza takes a shuddering breath when the light reconstitutes its original runes. Her hand rests heavy on the side of the desk; you wonder if that's all that's keeping her upright after all that.'

rows.original: You glance at the bailiff, giving her a moment to regain her composure before you ask your question. "Did we just see what I think that was?" "The... the first hours of the Godswar," Daliza confirms. "Just before the first Wraith in recorded history made landfall on Dracia, killing Jarl Talraed and Senasthrelle — killing the last lord of Dracia and its last draconic guardian. All the stories were true, down to the last word. Even Ser Marius being a dragonslayer! The she-drake said as much." "They were all so brave," Etheryn says quietly. "[etheryn.lnhConfidence |I could n-never do what they did." "Nonsense," Daliza says immediately. "You're here, fighting evil, of your own volition. Do not be so hard on yourself, my liege." |T-they knew they were going to die, didn't they? And still, they gave their lives to protect as m-many people as they could." Daliza nods. "They did. Like you, they recognized evil, and put everything on the line to defeat it." |They knew they were going to die, but they did their duty without hesitation... they gave everything to protect the innocent. I can only hope to be as selfless a leader as your ancestor someday, Daliza." The bailiff smiles softly. "You already are, my queen." ] "What happened to Ser Marius and the evacuees?" you ask. Daliza indicates herself. "I'm standing here, so clearly they made it to land, hmm? Marius Wyrmsbane did as Jarl Talraed commanded and commandeered every boat but one on the island, bringing thousands of Dracians to the mainland. Most of them participated in the long foot-slog all the way from the coast to Njorhaalt that warned as many settlements as it could of the coming danger. They saved a lot of lives, even if Ser Marius himself never abandoned the shore. The Jarl's wife and children escaped, as did Arch-Magister var Este's twins. I believe their daughter married into the Odain family; as for their son... I know there was a mage-knight, Lucian var Este, who was a minor hero in the latter days of the Godswar, after the Seven incarnated and turned the tide. He led forces from Maidenbridge to help pacify the Wraith-blighted imperial heartlands, if I recall." "And the Arch-Magister?" Ryn asks. Dal shakes her head. "She doesn't appear in any of the legends beyond being the reason Ser Marius refused to follow the evacuees inland: heartbroken for his Estelorean wife, determined to stay and greet her when she arrived on the last boat to bring them all the good news. He perished protecting the port town the refugees landed at, buying time for more people to escape. Brave man. Magister Viona, though, must have died with Talraed. Consumed by the first Wraith." She sighs, shaking her head in disbelief. "Every story my parents told me as a child was true, I'm realizing. The tower that reached the heavens. The first Wraith. Dragons that loved my lineage like their own kin.[flags.RQ2_MURAL | Even the notion that Nareva herself blessed our line seems at least part-true. Jarl Eldred laid with a dragon that may well have been kin to the goddess, and got his faith from her. Imagine! ]" "I wish I could do more than just listen to them," Daliza adds, casting a glance towards the balcony. "The questions I would ask Talraed. And, goddess, a living, breathing dragon! Did you see that she was shapeshifted down, looking like a winged salamander? Another legend borne out by this remarkable crystal. I wonder if there are any dragons out in the world, hidden among us mortals using that power? Could that be where they've all gotten off to, after the Godswar? I always had a hard time imagining all the dragons died off in it. There must have been thousands, in those days." [pc.isCunning |"That would imply they're hiding from us, wouldn't it?" you say. "Not a lot of Wraiths around these days." [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED|Except the Seven, but even dragons probably wouldn't know that secret... right?] Dal and Ryn exchange a glance, and both elves shrug. "Perhaps they are recovering their numbers?" Daliza suggests. ]
rows.translation: 你瞥了瞥法警，给了她一点时间让自己恢复镇定，然后才问道：“我们刚才看到的，真的是我所认为的那样吗？” “那是……是‘神战’开始后的最初几个小时，”达莉莎确认道，“就在有记录以来第一个‘幽灵’降临达拉西亚之前——那个幽灵杀死了塔尔拉德领主和塞纳斯特雷尔，也就是达拉西亚的最后一位领主和最后的龙族守护者。所有这些故事都是真实的，每一个字都是真的。就连马略斯爵士也是屠龙者！那条雌性巨龙也是这么说的。 “他们全都那么勇敢，”伊瑟琳轻声说道。[etheryn.lnhConfidence |我永远不可能做到他们所做的事情。” “胡说八道，”达莉莎立刻说道，“你是自愿来到这里，与邪恶作斗争的。不要这么苛责自己，我的主人。 |他们明明知道自己会死，对吧？然而，他们还是献出了自己的生命，只为保护尽可能多的人。 达莉莎点了点头。“没错。就像你一样，他们认清了邪恶，并不惜付出一切代价去战胜它。 |他们明知自己会死，却毫不犹豫地履行了自己的职责……他们倾尽全力去保护无辜的人们。我只希望有朝一日，自己也能成为像你这位祖先那样无私的领导者，达莉莎。 执事温柔地笑了笑：“你现在已经做到了，我的女王。 ] 马略斯爵士和那些被疏散的人们后来怎么样了？”你问道。 达莉莎指了指自己：“我就站在这里，所以很明显他们成功登陆了，对吧？马略斯·沃姆斯贝恩按照塔尔拉德伯爵的命令，占用了岛上的所有船只，只留下了一艘，从而将成千上万的德雷西亚人带到了大陆上。他们中的大多数人都参与了那场从海岸一直持续到Njorhaalt的漫长行军，目的是尽可能多地提醒其他定居点即将到来的危险。他们拯救了许多人的生命，尽管塞尔·马略斯本人始终没有离开海岸。领主的妻子和孩子们逃走了，大法师瓦尔·埃斯特的双胞胎也一样。据我所知，他们的女儿嫁入了奥丹家族；至于他们的儿子……我记得有一位名叫卢西恩·瓦尔·埃斯特的法师骑士，在神战后期，也就是在七神降临并扭转战局之后，他曾经是一位小有名气的英雄。如果我没记错的话，他带领着来自梅登布里奇的部队，协助平定了那些受到“幽灵灾祸”影响的帝国核心地区。 那大法师呢？”小琳问道。 达尔摇了摇头：“在所有的传说中，她都没有被提及。唯一与她有关的信息，就是马略斯爵士之所以拒绝跟随撤离人群前往内陆，正是因为他为自己的埃斯特洛丽安妻子心碎，决心留下来，等待她乘坐最后一艘船归来，带来好消息。他在保护那些难民登陆的港口小镇时牺牲了，为更多的人争取了逃生时间。真是一位勇敢的人。不过，维奥娜大师肯定也是和塔尔拉德一起死去的——被第一个“幽灵”吞噬了。 她叹息着，难以置信地摇了摇头。“我终于意识到，我小时候父母告诉我的每一个故事都是真实的。那座直通天际的塔楼，第一个幽灵，还有那些将我的血脉视为与自己同族的巨龙[flags.RQ2_MURAL | 就连“娜雷瓦亲自保佑了我们的血脉”这一说法，似乎也至少有一部分是真实的。埃尔德雷德领主与一条很可能与这位女神有亲缘关系的巨龙发生了关系，也正是因此而获得了她的庇护与信仰。想象一下吧！ ]我真希望能做更多，而不仅仅是倾听他们的诉说，”达莉莎说道，同时朝阳台的方向瞥了一眼。“我有很多问题想要问塔拉德……而且，女神啊，那可是一条活生生的龙啊！你们看到她变形成那只长着翅膀的蝾螈了吗？这一块非凡的水晶再次印证了一个传说。我在想，世界上是否真的存在一些龙，它们隐藏在我们这些凡人之中，利用着那种力量生活着？或许在神战之后，它们就是躲到了那里去的吧？我一直很难想象这一点所有那些龙在那里灭绝了。在那个时候，它们的数量肯定有成千上万。 [pc.isCunning |这意味着他们正在躲着我们，对吧？”你说道，“最近这些地方几乎见不到幽灵了。 [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED|除了七人之外，恐怕就连龙们也不会知道这个秘密……对吧？] 达尔和小琳对视了一眼，然后两人都耸了耸肩。“也许他们的数量正在恢复吧？”达莉莎提出了这个猜测。 ]

rows.original:
You exchange a look with Etheryn as the bailiff lights a torch, angling the nascent flames down the curling stone stairs. They go down and down far out of sight, but you can hear... something, a faint laughter on the air, echoing up from the depths. 

    "This leads to the family crypt, doesn't it?" Ryn asks. "At least back home, it would."
    
    Daliza nods, frowning. "Any boer'alvar castle would have its crypt and vaults down below. Do you hear that, though? What degenerate is down there giggling over the bones of my ancestors?"
    
    "It's not Alissa's voice, at least."
    
    Dal tightens her lips and takes the first step down. You follow her closely, hand on your [pc.weapon], expecting each step to take you face to face with some ravening demoness... but these steps go far, far deeper down than those in the Palace of Ice. You exchange another wary look with Ryn as you pass what feels like fifty feet of new depth, and still see no evidence of a bottom floor. 
    
    The stone walls of the palace have given way to solid, packed earth down here, accompanied by a deeply damp smell tinged with sea-salt. At least the stairs are still stone, though many of them are in poor shape after the centuries, cracked and loose underfoot. More than once you have to gab the back of Daliza's breastplate when she catches bad footing, or feel Ryn have to steady herself on your shoulder from behind. 
    
    And more than once, Daliza pauses to rub at her temples, complaining about a growing headache.
    
    The unnerving laughter certainly doesn't make it any easier. 
    
    It's definitely a woman's voice, and just the one, carrying madly up the winding stairs. She's hysterical, laughing herself hoarse to the point of coughing fits before starting up against with wailing howls of glee. Daliza inches her sword from its scabbard, growing more tense with every step. You ready yourself to have to restrain the swordswoman from rushing in the moment she sees the source of all this noise.
    
    At just past a hundred feet down, you finally see her.

女管事点燃一支火把，将初生火光斜斜照向盘旋的石阶；你和伊瑟琳交换一道目光。阶梯一路向下，远远伸出视野以外，可你能听见……某种声音。微弱的笑声飘在空气中，从深处回荡而上。

    “这里通往家族墓穴，对吧？”小琳问道。“至少在故乡，这里会通往墓穴。”
    
    达莉莎皱眉点头。“任何布尔阿尔瓦城堡都会把墓穴和金库设在下方。不过，你听见了吗？什么堕落之徒正在我祖先的尸骨上咯咯发笑？”
    
    “至少那不是艾莉莎的声音。”
    
    达莉莎抿紧双唇，踏出向下的第一步。你紧跟在她身后，一手按着[pc.weapon]，预感每迈一步，都可能与某个饥渴恶魔女面对面……但这些台阶向下延伸得远比寒冰宫殿中的阶梯幽深。你们向下走了仿佛足有五十英尺，却仍看不见底层的迹象；你又一次与小琳交换警惕的目光。
    
    到了这里，宫殿的石墙已经被坚实紧密的泥土取代，还伴着混有海盐气味的浓重潮气。至少阶梯仍由石头筑成；不过历经数百年，其中许多已经破败不堪，在脚下松动开裂。达莉莎踩空时，你不止一次需要抓住她胸甲背部；小琳也不止一次从后方扶住你的肩膀，以稳住身体。
    
    达莉莎还数次停下脚步揉着太阳穴，抱怨头痛越来越严重。
    
    那令人不安的笑声当然不会让事情变得轻松。
    
    那绝对是一个女人的声音，而且只有一人；疯狂的笑声沿蜿蜒阶梯向上飘荡。她歇斯底里地大笑，嗓音哑到剧烈咳嗽，随后又以欢喜的哀号重新笑了起来。每走一步，达莉莎便愈发紧张，长剑也从鞘中又抽出一寸。你做好准备，一旦剑士看见所有噪声的源头，便立刻拦住她，免得她冲上前去。
    
    向下刚过一百英尺，你终于看见了她。

rows.original:
The narrow stairs let out into a chamber that puts the largest halls of the Palace of Ice to shame, with arches of stone so white they could pass for rib bones supporting slabs of stone like gateways a hundred feet above. The smell of wet earth and sea-salt is overpowering, but it's the raucous, hysterical laughter that grates your senses the most.

        Finally, you step into the chamber at Daliza's back. The last features to come into sight are the most impressive: a titanic, arched stone door at the far side of the crypt, engraved from the roof to the bedrock floor with the images of skeletal dragons lording over countless prostrated salamanders and boreal elves. The stone is etched with glittering blue leycrystal, forming swirling runic patterns between the chiseled figures. Standing at the foot of the door is a lone, living individual with her head thrown back and motherine wings spread out, howling with laughter as she clutches her horned, befeelered head. She's wearing flowing black robes adorned with blue starlight patters visible through the cuts up her legs and the interior of a tremendously wide-brimmed hat. [party.has viv
            |Viv clicks her tongue on the back of her teeth, quirking her head to the side. "Hmm, she must have found one of my old outfits lying around. I wonder how much of that cleavage my magic's responsible for."
            |[flags.VIVIANE_MET
                |That looks damnably familiar.
            ]
        ]
        
        Daliza's sword clears its scabbard before Ryn's even down the steps. "Damnable demon! What's so funny about the graves of good and righteous folk, huh?"
        
        The fiendish moth-witch wheels around on a high heel, a rictus grin of pure insanity stretched across her lips. Her gold-hued eyes burn with mad, wild magic, and her ashen hair whips wildly around her beneath the great brim of her black hat. "You're here! Oh, radiant and serpentine goddess, do you finally mean to bless me?"
        
        At your side, Daliza spreads her feet and aims the silvery tip of her blade towards the witch's heart. There's a snarl on her lips far fiercer before, almost draconic in its furor. "Let me just kill her," she growls, barely audible. "I'm gonna fucking kill her." 
        
        The demon's knife-like ears wiggle. "No! I am unworthy to die here, with no soul to give to the grave. But you... your souls will feed the great queen. Come! Come and-"
        
        Daliza breaks ranks and charges, sweeping her sword for a killing cut across the chest. The witch is damnably fast, though, pirouetting to the left and deflecting Daliza's blade with a small rune-etched sword drawn from a sleeve in the blink of an eye. Dal recovers before the witch can capitalize, coming back around to parry a thrust at her kidney. Sparks fly as iron and bronze clash, almost to fast to follow. Ryn shouts the bailiff's name, trying to recall her, but the battle is already joined. The witch produces a crystalline orb from between her breasts, thrusting it in your direction alongside a shouted word of power that builds into a thunderous shockwave that pushes all but Daliza back. You skid to a stop on your knee, braced on your [pc.weapon].
        
        "Come then, serpent. Show me your fangs!" the moth-demon hisses. "SHOW ME!"

rows.original:
You spend a moment just taking in the grim majesty of the chamber you've found yourself in: the huge arched ceilings and earthen walls would make any druid salivate in admiration, but it's the grand doors of the tomb that really draw your attention. The artistry on the relief is exquisite, truly masterful in its detail of godlike dragons and supplicating elves and salamanders surrounding them. There are hundreds of individuals rendered on solid stone, with sweeping inlays of what you suspect must be once-liquified ley crystal that's been poured through chiseled lines. 

    "Incredible, isn't it?" Daliza murmurs, still rubbing at the side of her head. "To see something wrought not by mortal hands at all... This structure predates elven settlement here by centuries, I believe. The stories said it was in the middle of an inland lake, but I suppose the years have changed things. Dried the water up, or buried it."
    
    "What's inside?" you ask. "Just a tomb?"
    
    She cants her head to the side, looking up. "I don't know. Nobody does. The dragons kept their secrets close to their chest."
    
    [ashe.around
        |Ashe murmurs to you, "Yes, Champion, there is a tomb within. And galleries, and monuments, and memorial art. All our commemorations for those that died in the great war against the giants. I hate to see it so cold and lonely, now. Once it was beautiful and inviting, a place to bask in our history."
    ]
    
    "I hate to see it so... so abandoned," Daliza murmurs to herself, drawing a little closer to the door. "This ground was sacred to the dragons that my clan called their bondmates. A memorial to their dead from a war long ago. Even when Jarl Eldred married his dragon-bride, my kin weren't permitted entry."
rows.translation:
你花了一刻时间来欣赏自己所处的这个厅室的庄严与宏伟：巨大的拱形天花板以及土墙足以让任何德鲁伊都为之倾倒，但真正吸引你注意力的，却是那扇宏伟的墓门。这些浮雕的艺术水准堪称精湛，对那些神一般的巨龙以及围绕在它们周围的卑微精灵和火蜥蜴的细节刻画实在令人叹为观止。在整块坚硬的石头上，工匠们雕刻出了数百个生动的形象，同时还运用了那些显然曾经被熔化过的秘银晶体，将这些晶体按照精心设计的线条浇铸进去，从而形成了这些精美的装饰图案。 

    真是不可思议，不是吗？”达莉莎轻声说道，一边仍在揉着自己的太阳穴。“看到这样的建筑竟然完全不是人类手工建造的……我认为，这个遗迹的出现时间比精灵们在这里定居要早几个世纪。传说中，它原本是位于一个内陆湖泊中的，但想必这些年来，环境已经发生了变化。把水都抽干，或者把水埋藏起来。”
    
    “里面有什么？”你问道，“只是一座坟墓而已吗？”
    
    她把头偏向一边，抬头看着你：“我不知道。没人知道。那些龙把他们的秘密守得严严实实。
    
    [ashe.around
        |阿什轻声对你说：“是的，冠军，里面有一座陵墓，还有走廊、纪念碑以及纪念艺术品。这些都是我们为那些在对抗巨人的伟大战争中牺牲的人们设立的纪念场所。现在看到它如此冷清、寂寞，我真的很难过。曾经这里是多么美丽、多么令人向往，是我们缅怀历史的地方啊。
    ]
    
    我真不愿意看到它变得如此……如此荒废，”达莉莎低声自言自语，同时慢慢靠近那扇门。“这片土地对我的族人来说曾是非常神圣的，因为我的族人将那些龙视为他们的伙伴。这里其实是为了纪念那些在很久以前的一场战争中牺牲的龙而建立的。即使埃尔德雷德领主娶了他的龙新娘，我的族人也不被允许进入这里。

rows.original:
"The dragons buried here... what can you tell me about this war they fought in?"

        "Not much," Daliza admits. "It was long before the elves arrived on Dracia. There's only bits and pieces that come down from my family's stories; I know more from what we've learned from those few giantish traders I've spoken with. They say their ancestors fought a great and terrible war against dragonkind, and lost bitterly. A jotun once told me that his many-greats-grandfather felled the first dragon of the war, with one of the first bronze arrows ever smithed. I don't know that I believe that, but I've been to the Rift and seen the fallen fortresses peeking up from the snow. There used to be a civilization up there, grander than our own. Nothing's left of it now, and there wasn't much more of it back when Queen Atheldred was alive." 
        
        [ashe.around
            |You feel a sad pang from the mace at your side. "Even I am far too young to have been present when that war was fought. It's hard for me to put into perspective how long ago that was — centuries before the Belharan Empire or the Kingdom of Njorhaalt were even founded, before humans and elves had learned to work flint into tools. 
            
            The world was much colder then, and giants roamed further afield than they have ever since. Understand that the giants back then weren't the simple nomads you're familiar with today: they had a complex kingdom, with strong castles and brave soldiers and a vast hierarchy of shamans. They had every right to think they would be a match for any foe. But they had never fathomed facing dragonfire before. We burned every scrap of their culture to the ground and sunk their sprawling cities into the boreal sea. My ancestors' judgment against them was truly terrible. The sagas say that the giants had butchered the dragons they met and ate them, as if we were common animals... but I often wonder just how true that tale is."
            
            Daliza arches a brow at you. "Deep in thought, hmm?"
            
            "... Something like that."
        ]
rows.translation:
这里埋葬的那些龙……你们能告诉我关于它们参与的这场战争些什么吗？”

        “知道的并不多，”达莉莎承认道，“那是在精灵们来到达拉西亚很久之前发生的事了。我只能从家族的故事中了解到一些零星的信息；而更多细节，则是通过与我遇到的那些体型庞大的商人交谈后才得知的。人们说，他们的祖先曾与龙族进行过一场惨烈而可怕的战争，最终以失败告终。有一位巨人曾告诉我，他的高祖父用当时最早制造的青铜箭之一，击杀了那场战争中的第一条龙。我不确定自己是否真的相信这一点，但我确实去过裂谷，看到那些被积雪覆盖的废弃堡垒。那里曾经存在过一个文明，它的规模甚至比我们的文明还要庞大。然而现在，那里已经什么也不剩了；在阿塞尔德雷德女王在世的时候，那里的情况也并没有好到哪里去。" 
        
        [ashe.around
            |你感到身边那柄长矛让你心中涌起一阵悲伤。“就连我，也还太年轻了，那时那场战争还没有发生。对我来说，很难真正理解那究竟是多久以前的事——那是在贝尔哈兰帝国和尼乔哈尔特王国建立之前的几个世纪，也是在人类和精灵还不知道如何将燧石制成工具之前的时代。 
            
            那时的世界要寒冷得多，巨人们的活动范围也比现在要广阔得多。要知道，那时的巨人们并不是你们今天所熟知的那种简单的游牧民族：他们拥有复杂的王国，有坚固的城堡、勇敢的士兵，还有严密的萨满等级制度。他们完全有理由认为自己能够与任何敌人抗衡。但他们从未想过会遇到龙火这样的威胁。我们将他们所有的文化遗迹都烧成了灰烬，也将他们那些庞大的城市沉入了北冰洋之中。我的祖先对他们的评价确实非常严厉。传说中，那些巨人会将遇到的龙宰杀后吃掉，把我们当作普通的动物……但我常常在想，这个故事到底有多真实。
            
            达莉莎挑了挑眉毛看着你：“在沉思什么呢，嗯？”
            
            “……差不多吧。
        ]
