rows.original:
No sooner have you set foot into the chaos of the old Wayfort that an overwhelming wave of disorientation and despair washes over you — far too sudden to be anything but a deliberate attack upon your mind. [pc.willpowerRange 70
        |However, your formidable willpower is enough to quickly shrug off these psionically-induced sensations, giving the finger to whoever — or whatever — is trying to mess with your head
        |It takes you several moments of gasping and shuddering for you to get ahold of yourself, fending off the psionically-induced sensations and telling your body that this isn't real. Perhaps if you'd had better willpower you'd be capable of brushing it off like nothing, but at least you weren't reduced to a blubbering mess of nerves
    ].
    
    Still, even discounting the psionic attack, the maze that lies before you is daunting enough by itself. Time doesn't flow. Space isn't stable. On the edge where existence of a sphere frays and gradually becomes the non-existence of the void, only dreams remain.
    
    Will you reach the exit if you press forward? In this place, is there an up or down, let alone a forward or backward?
    
    "Like... if I really try, I can keep it somewhat sensible," Nina replies, as if reading your thoughts. She probably did. Her voice is strained, her teeth gritted as she focuses furiously; the poor bird really sounds like she could use a drink or half-dozen. "Leastways, I think I can keep it such that the hallways don't change on us while we're walking down them. If I didn't have the mind for it, we could be trapped here forever."
    
    Well then, thanks. You don't want to be faced with this chaos for any longer than what's necessary, especially if it's going to try and directly assault your mind. And the maze changing on you while you try and make it through... yeah, that's evil. Good thing you have her, eh?
    
    "Oh, don't worry, I'm not the one taking all the credit here. Without you pressing down on the fabric and making it all wibbly-wobbly timey-wimey, I wouldn't have the leeway to set us straight, man. You're the champ, after all. We make a good team, don't we?"
    
    Nina isn't messing with you — as you pace down these stairs and hallways, [pc.weapon] in hand, they straighten themselves out, becoming less of a tangled mess. It's still a chaotic jumble of dust and brickwork, but at least you aren't expected to walk up walls or hang from the ceiling.
    
    How long can she keep this up for?
    
    "I don't know. Just keep moving." Nina frowns, thinking. "If there weren't something opposing us, we could just think of somewhere and be there instantly, but them's the breaks. There's an exit somewhere, I'm sure of it; that's how mazes work."
rows.translation:
你才刚踏入旧驿堡的混乱之中，一股压倒性的迷失与绝望便席卷而来——如此突兀，只可能是有人蓄意攻击你的心智。[pc.willpowerRange 70
        |然而，你强大的意志足以迅速摆脱灵能诱发的感觉，还能朝试图扰乱你思绪的人——或东西——竖起中指
        |你喘息、颤抖了好一会儿才重新掌控自己，抵挡住灵能诱发的感觉，告诉身体这一切并不真实。或许意志力更强的话，你便能若无其事地甩开影响；但至少你没有崩溃成一团哭哭啼啼的紧张废物
    ]。
    
    即使撇开灵能攻击不谈，眼前的迷宫本身也足够令人畏惧。时间不会流动，空间并不稳定。在世界球体的存在开始磨损、逐渐化作虚空中非存在的边界，只余梦境尚存。
    
    继续前进就能抵达出口吗？在这片空间里，是否存在上下之分，更遑论前后？
    
    “就是……只要我真心努力，应该能让这里勉强保持合理，”妮娜回答道，仿佛读到了你的想法。她大概真的读到了。她的声音紧绷，牙齿紧咬，全神贯注得近乎凶狠；这只可怜的小鸟听起来真该来上一杯，或者半打酒。“至少，我觉得自己能让走廊在我们穿行时别突然变化。要是我没有这份精神力量，我们可能会永远困在这里。”
    
    那么，多谢了。你一点也不想面对这片混乱超过必要的时间，特别是它还会直接攻击心智。而且当你试图穿过迷宫时，迷宫本身还会变化……对，这实在邪恶。幸好有她，对吧？
    
    “哦，别担心，我可没打算独占全部功劳。要不是你压住现实的织物，让时间和空间变得摇摇晃晃，我也没有余地把方向理顺，伙计。毕竟你才是勇士。我们是支很棒的队伍，对吧？”
    
    妮娜没有逗你——你手持[pc.weapon]，沿着这些阶梯与走廊前进时，它们会自行拉直，不再像纠缠的乱麻。这里依旧是灰尘与砖石组成的混乱杂物堆，但至少你不必沿墙行走或吊在天花板上。
    
    她能坚持多久？
    
    “我不知道。继续走就好。”妮娜皱着眉思考。“要不是有什么东西在阻挠我们，我们本可只需想象一个地点，立刻就能抵达；可惜事情就是这样。某处肯定有个出口，我很确定；迷宫就是这么运作的。”
rows.raw:
"
    No sooner have you set foot into the chaos of the old Wayfort that an overwhelming wave of disorientation and despair washes over you — far too sudden to be anything but a deliberate attack upon your mind. [pc.willpowerRange 70
        |However, your formidable willpower is enough to quickly shrug off these psionically-induced sensations, giving the finger to whoever — or whatever — is trying to mess with your head
        |It takes you several moments of gasping and shuddering for you to get ahold of yourself, fending off the psionically-induced sensations and telling your body that this isn't real. Perhaps if you'd had better willpower you'd be capable of brushing it off like nothing, but at least you weren't reduced to a blubbering mess of nerves
    ].
    
    Still, even discounting the psionic attack, the maze that lies before you is daunting enough by itself. Time doesn't flow. Space isn't stable. On the edge where existence of a sphere frays and gradually becomes the non-existence of the void, only dreams remain.
    
    Will you reach the exit if you press forward? In this place, is there an up or down, let alone a forward or backward?
    
    "Like... if I really try, I can keep it somewhat sensible," Nina replies, as if reading your thoughts. She probably did. Her voice is strained, her teeth gritted as she focuses furiously; the poor bird really sounds like she could use a drink or half-dozen. "Leastways, I think I can keep it such that the hallways don't change on us while we're walking down them. If I didn't have the mind for it, we could be trapped here forever."
    
    Well then, thanks. You don't want to be faced with this chaos for any longer than what's necessary, especially if it's going to try and directly assault your mind. And the maze changing on you while you try and make it through... yeah, that's evil. Good thing you have her, eh?
    
    "Oh, don't worry, I'm not the one taking all the credit here. Without you pressing down on the fabric and making it all wibbly-wobbly timey-wimey, I wouldn't have the leeway to set us straight, man. You're the champ, after all. We make a good team, don't we?"
    
    Nina isn't messing with you — as you pace down these stairs and hallways, [pc.weapon] in hand, they straighten themselves out, becoming less of a tangled mess. It's still a chaotic jumble of dust and brickwork, but at least you aren't expected to walk up walls or hang from the ceiling.
    
    How long can she keep this up for?
    
    "I don't know. Just keep moving." Nina frowns, thinking. "If there weren't something opposing us, we could just think of somewhere and be there instantly, but them's the breaks. There's an exit somewhere, I'm sure of it; that's how mazes work.""

rows.original: You're just about to come up with a reply when more sensations scrape against your mind, sending your nerves screaming. At first, you think it's just another psychic attack, but this stimulus is very real; with a sensation reminiscent of a file being dragged against metal, inhuman blobs of writhing cosmic matter spill from rents in the masonry. Before your eyes, they rapidly coalesce into shapes recognizable as boreal elves — if they were missing parts of themselves. Some headless, some limbless, others spindly and deformed, they bear antiquated arms and armor of the sort you've seen around Ryn's palace as decorative pieces. All of it silhouettes, motes of light suspended within inky emptiness, outlined by a membrane of shimmering iridescence. No flesh here, only star-stuff held together by memories. You cast a quick glance at Nina, and point at your [pc.weapon]. "It'll work, man. It's just light and dust, held together by memories. Rightly speaking, it shouldn't do anything to them, but they remember that weapons hurt and they can die, and that's what really matters this close to the edge." Once more: time doesn't flow. Space isn't stable. With the deathly forces of the void so near, will alone can influence reality. So long as you really, really believe your [pc.weapon] can hurt these shattered shades, so long as they remember that weapons can hurt and kill, it might just work. Like Nina said, this isn't part of any vision... so you'll just have to choose your own fate. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 你正要开口回答，更多感触却刮过心智，令神经发出尖锐悲鸣。起初，你以为这又是一场精神攻击，可这股刺激无比真实；伴随着锉刀刮过金属般的感触，一团团非人的蠕动宇宙物质从砖石裂隙间涌出。它们在你眼前迅速凝聚成依稀可辨的极北精灵轮廓——只是身体残缺不全。有的没有头颅，有的缺少四肢，还有的瘦长畸形；它们手持古旧的兵器、身披古老盔甲，与小琳宫殿里作为装饰品陈列的样式相同。所有形体都只是剪影，是悬浮在墨色虚无中的点点微光，外缘包裹着一层闪耀的虹彩薄膜。 这里没有血肉，只有被记忆聚合在一起的星辰物质。你飞快瞥了妮娜一眼，指向自己的[pc.weapon]。 “会有用的，伙计。它们只是光与尘，由记忆维系在一起。严格来说，武器根本不该伤到它们；但它们记得武器会造成伤害，也记得自己会死。离边界这么近，真正重要的就是这一点。” 再强调一次：时间不会流动，空间并不稳定。虚空中的致命力量近在咫尺，单凭意志便足以影响现实。只要你真正、真正相信自己的[pc.weapon]能够伤到这些破碎的幽影，只要它们还记得武器能够伤害、能够杀戮，或许就真的可行。 正如妮娜所说，这并非任何预知的一部分……所以你只能选择自己的命运。 战斗开始！

rows.original: [rand |You're walking down the twisted, crumbling hallways when suddenly the air feels taut, a sensation familiar to you at this point. Barely have you readied your [pc.weapon] that a shimmering rend tears asunder in the ether, blobs of shimmering star-stuff disgorging from the rift before it seals itself. Within the blink of an eye, they've shifted through several forms as massed memories vy for dominance over matter, eventually resolving themselves into [rand |a pair of minotaurs |a pale elf outrider and her warg |Tychrisian frostmanders garbed in ancient livery |pale elves from the Wayfort's old garrison ]. Bits and pieces are missing from their star-spawned bodies, but there's more than enough coherency despite the gaps in memory to pose a threat. |Passing through the ruined wayfort, you hear a wet squelch echo along the old masonry. Nothing good can come of such a viscous noise — and your suspicions are confirmed as star-stuff drips from the ceiling just up ahead, ethereal motes of light dancing in the darkness. Grimacing, you tell Nina to ready herself, and tighten your grip on your [pc.weapon]. Now that it's been noticed, the animated mass abandons all stealth and rips itself from the ceiling, scattering stone brick in all directions. Before your eyes, it shapes itself into two of the Wayfort's elven garrison, memories passing through several iterations before settling on a suitable form. |You're making your way through the familiar-yet-alien Wayfort of old when a sudden wave of intense emotion ripples through the air from some unknown origin, pounding against both Nina and you. While you mentally brace yourself and manage to weather the blow without too much trouble, sibilant whispers ring in your ears as the air itself grows thicker about you. Before your eyes, two of the Wayfort's old garrison take shape from nothingness, shades wrought from a jumble of broken memories. Their origin makes the duo no less dangerous as they move to attack, star-stuff dripping from their weapons as they move with single-minded purpose. ] It's a fight!
rows.translation: [rand |当你走在那些蜿蜒曲折、摇摇欲坠的走廊中时，突然间，空气似乎变得紧张起来——这种感觉对你来说已经再熟悉不过了。你还没来得及做好准备[pc.weapon]在那片虚空中，一道闪烁的光芒突然撕裂了空间，一些闪烁的星尘从裂口中喷涌而出，随后裂口又重新闭合了。 在转瞬之间，它们经历了多种形态的变化——那些庞大的记忆碎片不断争夺着对物质形态的控制权，最终它们才稳定下来，形成了某种特定的形态。 [rand |一对牛头人 |一位皮肤苍白的精灵骑手与她的战兽 |身着古老服饰的提克里斯安霜冻巨兽 |来自荒废驿堡旧驻军的苍白精灵们 ]它们的身体虽然缺失了一些零部件，但尽管记忆中存在空白，整体而言依然足够协调一致，因此依然具备威胁性。 |穿过那座已被毁坏的哨所，你听到一阵湿漉漉的声响在古老的砖石结构中回荡。这种黏腻的声音绝不会带来什么好事——而你的怀疑很快就得到了证实：前方不远处，星尘正从天花板上滴落下来，那些微小的光点在黑暗中闪烁着。 你皱着眉头，让妮娜做好准备，同时也紧紧抓住了手中的武器。 [pc.weapon]现在既然已经被发现了，那个会移动的物体便放弃了所有的隐蔽行动，从天花板上猛地冲了下来，将石块和砖块向四面八方抛洒开来。在你们眼前，它逐渐变形成了两架荒废驿堡家族的精灵守卫机甲，其形态经过多次变化后才最终定型。 |当你正在这片既熟悉又陌生的旧日荒废驿堡地区穿行时，突然有一股强烈的情绪波动从某个未知的地方传了过来，冲击着你和尼娜。虽然你在心理上做好了准备，也顺利地熬过了这一阵冲击，但周围的气氛却变得越来越浓重，耳边也不断传来低语声。 在你眼前，瓦伊福特的两名老卫兵从虚无中浮现出来，他们的身影是由零散的记忆碎片凝聚而成的。正因为这样的起源，这两名卫兵在发起攻击时显得更加危险——他们的武器上还挂着星尘，他们行动时充满了坚定的决心。 ] 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: That looks to be the last of the maze of looping stairs and corridors — your feet feel like they've walked anywhere between five to ten lengths of the Wayfort you know, but at least the chaotic atmosphere has faded to the point where it's bearable once more, as it was in the storeroom. Hopefully you won't have to deal with that nonsense again, although at this point you're a seasoned enough adventurer to know such hopes are usually empty. Nevertheless, the brief respite is welcome, and you're returning to familiar territory, the Wayfort you know. This looks like the entrance of your vault — look, there's even the portcullis and winch. Good thing the former's raised, otherwise you'd have a problem; Nina can't quite blink through the portcullis — — Nina? Your harpy companion's been decidedly silent for the last several minutes, a most unsettling state of affairs given that in the time you've been together, she usually bounces between inebriation and hysteria. Turning around, you find the silly bird-brain completely frozen up, her one good eye staring into space. She's not petrified with fear — no, she very definitely lacks that, given that she's lacking everything as her mind and body simply disassociate from each other. The world in which dreamwalkers operate is still [pc.isDK |a whole load of bullshit |all rather opaque ] to you, but inasfar as it follows any kind of guidelines, let alone rules, you're pretty sure this isn't supposed to happen. She is caught in her own web. Your ears swear they didn't hear a sound, but your mind registers the words anyway, right down to the direction they're supposed to have originated from. Speaking, by someone or something unused to needing to lower oneself to such a menial task. To be able to see a future you cannot change, where all your efforts to fight it merely help realize it. To be able to see the alternatives that could have been, and yet personally be unable to change the flow of time. Seeing and realizing the futility of action. You see it now. A decidedly avian entity born of a nightmare, a peril of the void given shape from the recesses of Nina's own mind; perhaps this is what she drinks to avoid having to face in her quiet moments. How can you tell it's her? Simple enough — it has two scaly legs, two wings dusted with star-stuff... and twenty-two unblinking, crimson eyes, all of them trained on you. A fitting if warped image of a silly bird constantly plagued by visions. This is Nina, right? Antonina? Both yes and no are correct and incorrect. [pc.isDK |All right, that's just fucking bullshit. You don't have time to deal with this kind of mind game, and most definitely not from a big ball of feathers with twigs for wings and legs. |Now it's just being obtuse on purpose. You don't have the patience for such games, the only reason you're entertaining this is because it's presumably some part of Nina in the same way all these shattered shades are bits and pieces of the old garrison's minds. ] The star-spawned bird ignores you and continues, delivering its monologue right into your mind within the blink of an eye. But you don't have any fate. You have a measure of freedom — not overly much, but more than the vast majority of people will ever have. Your decisions matter, within boundaries. You create perturbations. This cannot be allowed.
rows.translation: 看来这就是那片由循环楼梯和走廊组成的迷宫的尽头了——你的双脚感觉好像已经走了相当于五到十段荒废驿堡那么长的距离，不过至少，那种混乱的氛围已经减弱到可以忍受的程度了，就像在储藏室里的时候一样。希望你不会再遇到那些烦人的事情了，不过以你现在的经验，应该也知道这种期望往往只是空想罢了。 不过，这次短暂的休息确实让人感到欣慰，而且你即将回到熟悉的地区——那个你熟悉的荒废驿堡。这看起来像是你藏宝处的入口——看，那里甚至还有吊闸和绞盘。幸好吊闸是升起来的，否则就会出麻烦了；尼娜的眼睛实在太小了，根本无法从吊闸下面穿过…… ——尼娜？ 你那只女妖同伴在过去的几分钟里一直保持着惊人的沉默，这种情况实在令人不安——因为在你们共处的这段时间里，她通常总是处于醉酒或歇斯底里的状态之中。你转过身，发现这只愚蠢的家伙完全愣住了，她那唯一的一只眼睛正呆呆地望着前方。她并没有被恐惧吓得动弹不得——不，她显然没有这种感觉，因为她的意识与身体已经完全分离了，她已经失去了一切。 那些能够进行梦游的人所生活的世界，依然[pc.isDK |一堆废话 |相当不透明 ]对你来说，或许这并没有什么不妥，但既然这种行为遵循了某种准则，更不用说规则了，那你肯定应该知道，这种事情本就不应该发生。 她陷入了自己设下的陷阱之中。 你的耳朵坚称自己没有听到任何声音，但你的大脑却确实接收到了那些话语，甚至还能判断出它们应该来自哪个方向。有人在说话——某个不习惯需要做这种卑微事情的人或东西在说话。 能够预见一个你无法改变的未来，在那里，你所有试图改变它的努力，反而只是加速了它的实现。能够看到本可能存在的其他发展路径，但却无力改变时间的流逝。意识到自己的行动其实是徒劳的。 你现在看到了。这是一个明显的鸟类生物，诞生于噩梦之中，是虚无中的危险在尼娜内心深处凝聚而成的形态；或许，这就是她之所以喝酒的原因——为了在宁静的时刻避免面对这个怪物。你怎么能认出它就是她呢？其实很简单——它有着两条长满鳞片的腿，两只布满星星斑点的翅膀……还有二十二只一眨不眨的深红色眼睛，所有这些眼睛都在注视着你。这确实是一个恰如其分的形象，一个总是被各种幻象所困扰的愚蠢生物是妮娜，对吧？安东妮娜？ 既是也不是”这种说法既正确又不正确。 [pc.isDK |好吧，这完全是一派胡言。你根本没有时间去应付这种心理游戏，更何况这种游戏还是来自一个长着树枝当翅膀和腿的家伙。 |现在，他们纯粹是在故意装傻。你根本没有耐心去玩这种游戏，你之所以还在继续玩下去，只是因为这些碎片可能代表着尼娜的某些方面，就如同这些破碎的残片代表着那座旧要塞中人们的思想一样。 ] 这只由星星孕育而生的鸟无视了你，继续它的独白，而这一切都在转瞬之间直接传入了你的脑海之中。但你并没有真正的命运。你拥有一定程度的自由——虽然不是太多，但确实比绝大多数人都要多。在一定的范围内，你的选择确实会产生影响，你会引发一些变化。 然而，这种情况是不能被允许的。

rows.original: "Screw that. I create my own fate." You do have that power. With it comes the knowledge that you are responsible for your failures. In due time, you may even glimpse their true extent. If you can create your own fate, then you don't have to fail. If you are the author of your destiny, then you can overcome the odds. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 去他的。我要自己创造属于我的命运。 你确实拥有那种力量。但随之而来的，也是这样一种认识：你必须为自己的失败负责。假以时日，你甚至可能会看清这些失败的真正程度。 如果你能够自己创造自己的命运，那么你就不会失败。如果你是自己命运的创造者，那么你就能够战胜一切困难。 真是太遗憾了——你本来希望在这个支离破碎的现实世界中遇到的第一个有智慧的生命也会是神志清醒的。那只全视之鸟展开了翅膀，它体内散发着点点光芒和五彩斑斓的羽毛，然后便向你扑了过来。 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " "Screw that. I create my own fate." You do have that power. With it comes the knowledge that you are responsible for your failures. In due time, you may even glimpse their true extent. If you can create your own fate, then you don't have to fail. If you are the author of your destiny, then you can overcome the odds. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!"

rows.original: Screw that. I create my own fate.
rows.translation: 去他的。我要自己创造属于我的命运。
rows.raw: "Screw that. I create my own fate."

rows.original: "Who's going to stop me? You?" No. You will. That doesn't make any sense regardless of how you interpret those words, but at this point, it doesn't matter. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 谁能阻止我？你吗？ 不，你会的。 无论你如何解读那些话，这都毫无意义……但在这个时候，这也已经无关紧要了。 真是太遗憾了——你本来希望在这个支离破碎的现实世界中遇到的第一个有智慧的生物也是个神志清醒的人吧。那只全视之鸟展开了翅膀，它体内散发着点点光芒和五彩斑斓的羽毛，然后便扑向了你。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!"

rows.original: Who's going to stop me? You?

So be it, then. You grit your teeth and ready your [pc.weapon] — if it can hurt the broken shades that wander the Wayfort past, it can hurt this caricature. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 那就这样吧。你咬紧牙关，做好准备。 [pc.weapon] — 如果它能够伤害那些在荒废驿堡道路上徘徊的破碎幻影，那么它也同样能够伤害这个滑稽可笑的仿制品。 真是太遗憾了——你本来希望在这个支离破碎的现实世界中遇到的第一个有智慧的生命也会是神志清醒的。那只全视之鸟展开了翅膀，它体内散发出的光芒与色彩如同羽毛一般闪烁着，然后它就扑向了你。 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " So be it, then. You grit your teeth and ready your [pc.weapon] — if it can hurt the broken shades that wander the Wayfort past, it can hurt this caricature. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!"

rows.original: You can see where this is going.
rows.translation: 你应该能猜到这会走向何方。
rows.raw: "You can see where this is going."

rows.original: You simply fold your arms, tilt your chin up, and stare down all of the star-spawned bird's twenty-two eyes. This lasts for about a second. Your defiance has the potential to make a difference. That's odd. You'd have thought it would talk up the futility of your actions. No. I see much, but I do not see you. That makes you unpredictable. Dangerous. An anomaly that needs correction. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 你只需双臂交叉，微微仰起下巴，凝视着那些布满星星的鸟儿那二十二只眼睛。这个动作持续大约一秒钟而已。 你的反抗有可能带来改变。 真奇怪。你本以为它会指出你的行为是多么徒劳无功才对。 不。我看得很多，但却看不到你。这种特性让你变得难以预测，也充满危险——你就是一个需要被纠正的异常现象。 真是太遗憾了——你本来希望在这个支离破碎的现实世界中遇到的第一个有智慧的生物也是个神志清醒的人吧。那只全视之鸟展开了翅膀，它体内散发着点点光芒和五彩斑斓的羽毛，然后便向你扑了过来。 这是一场激烈的战斗！
rows.raw: " You simply fold your arms, tilt your chin up, and stare down all of the star-spawned bird's twenty-two eyes. This lasts for about a second. Your defiance has the potential to make a difference. That's odd. You'd have thought it would talk up the futility of your actions. No. I see much, but I do not see you. That makes you unpredictable. Dangerous. An anomaly that needs correction. It really is a pity — you'd have hoped that the first sapient being you met in this fractured reality would be sane as well. The all-seeing bird spreads its wings, pinpricks of light and plumes of color shining from within its body, and then is upon you. It's a fight!"

rows.original: Keep your silence and don't say anything.
rows.translation: 保持沉默，什么都不要说。
rows.raw: "Keep your silence and don't say anything."

rows.original: The anomaly has been corrected. This outcome was not inevitable, but I am glad it happened anyway. You had the potential to cause trouble. It doesn't hurt, for you need a mind to perceive pain. Your body might keep going for a while longer inasmuch as that has any meaning in a place where time doesn't flow, but your self shatters into dozens of fragments, blowing away into the void between the stars. Your [silly |heart may go on, but your ]adventure ends here.
rows.translation: 该异常已被修正。这个结果并非必然，但我还是很高兴它发生了。你本来有可能惹出麻烦。 这并不疼，因为你需要心智才能感知疼痛。在一个时间并不流动的地方——如果这还有任何意义的话——你的身体或许还能继续运转一阵子，但你的自我会碎成几十块碎片，飘散到群星之间的虚空里。 你的[silly |心脏或许还会继续跳动，但你的 ]冒险就此结束。
rows.raw: " The anomaly has been corrected. This outcome was not inevitable, but I am glad it happened anyway. You had the potential to cause trouble. It doesn't hurt, for you need a mind to perceive pain. Your body might keep going for a while longer inasmuch as that has any meaning in a place where time doesn't flow, but your self shatters into dozens of fragments, blowing away into the void between the stars. Your [silly |heart may go on, but your ]adventure ends here."

rows.original: As the final blow lands true on the feathered fiend, it shatters like glass — physicality melting away as it warps from three dimensions into two and falls to the old flagstones of the Wayfort. The pieces dissolve into motes of starlight, and then it's gone. You breathe a sigh of relief, then turn back to Nina. While the prospect of imminent harm was enough to jolt her into action aiding you, she clearly isn't in good shape as she huddles on the ground, knees between her elbows as she holds her head in her hands. Is she okay? "Dude. Like, what just happened, man?" Does she remember anything of what just happened? "I think I did, like I had a vision, but I'm pretty sure I didn't. I'd know if that were the case." Well, as to what happened, her guess is as good as yours. That being said, you think the immediate danger's over. Can she stand? Nina takes your hand, tries to take several steps, and ends up collapsing into your [pc.chest] with a muffled groan. Eventually, her one good eye comes into focus, and she pushes herself off you unsteadily. Heaving ragged breaths, she summons a spark of life into her too-wide eye and a weak, stupefied smile forms on her lips; as her thoughts and sense of self assemble themselves into some kind of coherency, so does her sense of humor. "I can't stand it, man. Keeping it together while facing that thing took more out of me than I realized I had. Like, this is totally not cool — I feel like there's some part of me that's missing, and while that isn't anything super-new I don't have drink to fill in the hole with." Any visions? "I've got a couple ongoing, man, but they're not like, useful at all." Swallowing hard, Nina paces slowly in a small circle to find her feet again, flapping at the air with her wings. "Like, don't worry about me. But first, I've got to get my head back into shape, man. This sense of emptiness is bugging me to no end, it's totally not cool at all. It's like something got knocked loose in my head, and I don't like it one bit." The area up ahead looks safer and is at least recognizable as the Wayfort you know; you don't want to remain here so close to the chaos you just left. She can recover while the two of you take a look around — maybe you'll even find something to drink in this miserable place. Nina's smile widens marginally. "Now wouldn't that be a treat. Man, if the elves kept the Wayfort this miserably stocked back in the day then maybe they deserved what was coming. You're a much better [pc.mf |lord |lady ], at any rate. Lead the way, then."
rows.translation: 最后一击准确落在羽翼怪物身上，它顿时像玻璃一样粉碎——实体性逐渐消融，从三维扭曲成二维，飘落到驿堡古老的石板上。碎片溶解成点点星光，随后彻底消失。 你松了口气，转身看向妮娜。迫在眉睫的伤害虽然足以惊得她采取行动协助你，但她显然状态很差；她蜷缩在地上，双膝夹在两肘之间，双手抱着脑袋。 她没事吧？ “老兄。就是，伙计，刚刚发生什么了？” 她还记得刚刚发生的任何事吗？ “我感觉自己好像看见了预知，可又很确定自己没有。要真是预知，我肯定知道。” 好吧，对于发生了什么，她和你一样毫无头绪。不过，你觉得眼前的危险已经过去了。她能站起来吗？ 妮娜握住你的手，试着迈出几步，结果闷哼一声倒进你的[pc.chest]。终于，她那只完好的眼睛重新聚焦；她摇摇晃晃地推开你。她急促地喘着气，过于圆睁的眼中唤回一丝生机，嘴唇也勾起虚弱而茫然的笑容；当思绪与自我认知重新拼凑出几分连贯，她的幽默感也随之回归。 “我受不了，伙计。面对那东西时勉强保持清醒，消耗了我自己都没意识到还有的精力。就是，这实在太不够意思了——我感觉自己缺了一部分；这也不算什么特别新鲜的事，可我现在没酒填上那个洞。” 有什么预知吗？ “有几段还在继续，伙计，但就是，完全派不上用场。”妮娜用力咽了口唾沫，在一个小圈里缓慢踱步，试着重新站稳，翅膀也不断拍打着空气。“就是，别担心我。但首先，我得把脑袋整理好，伙计。这股空虚感快把我烦死了，一点也不够意思。就好像有什么东西在脑子里被震松了，我一点也不喜欢。” 前方区域看起来更安全，至少还能认出是你所熟悉的驿堡；你不想继续停留在刚刚离开的混乱附近。你们两人查看四周时，她可以慢慢恢复——或许你甚至能在这个悲惨地方找到酒喝。 妮娜的笑容微微扩大。“那可真是件美事。伙计，如果当年的精灵把驿堡储备得如此寒酸，那么或许他们活该遭遇后来的一切。无论如何，你都是一位好得多的[pc.mf |领主 |女领主 ]。那么，你带路吧。”

rows.original: [rand |A piece of the southern gate, complete with a chunk of dirt attached to its underside. That's all that keeps you from falling into the lightless void below — you're not even sure if you're actually upright, given the twisting of the roads that lead away from this chunk of semi-reality... Being sundered aside, the poor gate looks even worse for wear than you remember it being when you entered the Wayfort for the first time. Looks like this place isn't kind to the reality of things that wind up here... |A segment of bridge that spans a mockery of the River Ridell, dark oily liquid flowing under it with no seeming start or end. The bridge itself is set on an incline, something that makes no sense given the so-called river's span, but space and physicality have no hold on this place. It's survived better than some of the other ruins in this shattered, twisted version of the Wayfort, but even so there're several loose stones here and there in its otherwise sturdy build. The bridge seems to go on forever... until it doesn't. |A section of garden, or the packed dirt road that passes through it — distinguishing where one begins and the other ends is nigh-impossible. Choked with weeds and fallen into full disrepair, one can only wonder how weeds manage to thrive in this place when everything else is ruined. Well, perhaps thrive is being a bit too generous, but they're certainly proliferating, animated by whatever forces pervade this place. |A long stretch of tiled path that winds about itself and twists like a ribbon — following the same surface as it slants ever so slightly to the right has you upside-down at points, but here there doesn't seem to be any down to fall to, or at least that which isn't redefined by your senses from moment to moment. It's not like the path is supported by anything to refer direction to by, anyway, so up can be whatever you need it to be. Several stone lanterns stay planted by the side of the path, still lit and flickering away — you don't look at them too closely, especially considering that despite their light, they don't illuminate any of the path at all. You don't remember these; maybe they crumbled away by the time you first entered the Wayfort. |An island of packed dirt with a single solitary well and little else. You don't remember there being a well in your Wayfort — at least, not one as notable as this — but it's there nevertheless. Maybe it collapsed in on itself in the centuries that came after? The sight, it's almost normal. Mundane. There's something about the juxtaposition of the humdrum and everyday, complete with an old cart and piles of straw, and the utter chaos that lies beyond the borders of this floating chunk of rock in the Ways — it disquiets the spirit, to put it lightly. ]
rows.translation: [rand |南门的一块残骸，其底部还粘着一块泥土。正是这块残骸才阻止你坠入下方那片无光的虚空——由于通往这片半真实空间的道路蜿蜒曲折，你甚至不确定自己是否真的处于垂直状态…… 被强行拆开的南门，如今看起来比你第一次进入荒废驿堡时记忆中的还要破败不堪。看来，这个地方对那些被抛到这里来的物品来说，实在是个残酷的地方…… |一段横跨里德尔河的桥梁，河底流淌着黑色、黏稠的液体，那液体似乎没有起点，也没有终点。这座桥梁本身呈倾斜状，考虑到这条所谓的河流的宽度，这种设计实在令人费解——但在这个地方，空间与物理规律似乎都不再起作用了。尽管在这片被破坏、扭曲的荒废驿堡一带，它的状况比其他一些废墟要好，但即便如此，它的结构中还是有一些石块松动脱落。 这座桥看起来仿佛没有尽头…… 直到它不再能那样做为止。 |那片花园，或是穿过它的那条布满碎石的小路——要区分它们的起始与终点，几乎是不可能的。那里杂草丛生，一片荒废，人们不禁会想：在一切都已经毁坏的情况下，这些杂草究竟是如何在那里繁茂生长的？嗯，或许用“繁茂生长”来形容它们有点夸张了，但它们确实正在迅速蔓延，而推动它们生长的力量，恐怕就是弥漫在这个地方的那些无形因素吧。 |一条由瓷砖铺成的长路，蜿蜒曲折，如同丝带般缠绕着同一片地面，同时微微向右倾斜，因此在某些地方会让你感到仿佛处于倒立的状态……不过在这里，似乎并没有这样的情况发生。向下落入其中，或者至少是那种不会被你的感官时刻重新定义的东西。反正，这条路并没有任何可以用来确定方向的参照物，所以“向上”这个方向，完全可以由你自行定义。 小路旁竖立着几盏石灯，灯光依然闪烁着——但你不会仔细去观察它们，尤其是考虑到，尽管这些灯还在发光，但实际上它们并没有照亮小路的任何一部分。你可能不记得这些了；也许当你第一次进入荒废驿堡的时候，它们就已经消逝不见了。 |这是一片布满泥土的岛屿，上面只有一口孤零零的井，除此之外什么也没有。你不记得你的荒废驿堡一带有这样一口井——至少没有这么显眼的井——但它确实存在。也许在之后的几个世纪里，这口井逐渐塌陷了？这一景象，其实相当普通，平凡无奇。然而，当那些单调而日常的事物——比如一辆旧马车、几堆稻草——与这片漂浮在道路上的岩石边界之外所呈现的彻底混乱形成对比时，这种反差确实会让人感到不安，至少可以说是如此。 ]

rows.original: You investigate the section of wall more closely, and as it happens there's a small storeroom set in an alcove like the one you started off in, only smaller and still full, it seems. There might be something useful in the pots and barrels, if you could get to the other side — at the very least, it'd make wandering about in this chaotic web of stairs and halls less of a waste, especially since you've arrived at a dead end. Of course, it's closed off with a grate, and set into the wall by its side is a very boreal elven mechanism — a wheel that's no doubt attached to the raising mechanism. You give it an experimental turn and it clicks: well, at least it still works. You don't remember this being in your wayfort, but as discrepancies go this is pretty small. "Oh. It's one of these again. Used to have a mechanism like this in one of my old houses — the boreal elves built them all over the place. Easier than losing your key, at any rate. Guess someone had these on his or her mind when the poor bastard died." You may remember that from last time. Or you may not. Everything about that episode passed by in a drunken haze, really... "If it's like the old sluice gate..." Nina taps her chin, thinking. "How you lift the gate is through this wheel over here: you can turn it left, right, or just hold it in place for a bit. You've got to do this five times, and it's got to be in the correct sequence; for each action in the sequence that you perform correctly, the mechanism will click." So if you got three out of five correct, there'd be three clicks? "That's right. What we want to hear is five clicks from the portcullis mechanism." Always good to have her around to explain things. So, no helpful visions as to the answer? "None at all, man. I can feel them trying to get to me, but whatever's stopping us from going out is also stopping them from coming in; that's a good thing because I'm pretty sure my head would explode otherwise with all the bad vibes surrounding us. We're on our own here, man." Always at the worst possible times, huh? All right, maybe you'll give this a go.
rows.translation: 你更仔细地调查这段墙壁；原来，壁龛里设有一间小储藏室，与起初所在的房间相似，只是规模更小，而且似乎仍堆满物品。只要能抵达另一侧，坛坛罐罐和木桶里或许藏着有用的东西——至少能让你们在这片楼梯与厅堂构成的混乱网络中游荡得不算毫无收获，特别是现在已经走进了死路。 当然，储藏室被一道铁栅封闭；旁边墙内嵌着一套极具极北精灵特色的机械——一只无疑连接着升降装置的转轮。你试探着转了一下，机械发出咔嗒声：好吧，至少还能运转。你不记得自己的驿堡里有这东西，但在各种差异中，这一点实在微不足道。 “哦，又是这东西。我以前的一栋房子里也有这种机关——极北精灵把它们造得到处都是。不管怎么说，总比把钥匙弄丢方便。估计那个可怜虫死时，脑子里正惦记着这种东西。” 你可能还记得上次见到的机关，也可能不记得。那段经历全都在醉醺醺的迷雾中一晃而过…… “如果它和旧水闸门一样……”妮娜点着下巴思考。“要升起闸门，就得使用这里的转轮：你可以向左转、向右转，或者保持原位一会儿。你必须操作五次，而且顺序必须正确；顺序中每正确完成一个动作，机关都会发出一声咔嗒。” 所以，要是五步中正确了三步，就会听到三声咔嗒？ “没错。我们想听见的是闸门机关发出的五声咔嗒。” 有她在身边解释总是很方便。那么，有没有预知能提示答案？ “完全没有，伙计。我能感觉到预知试图传给我，但阻止我们出去的东西，也在阻止它们进来；这倒是好事，因为四周都是糟糕透顶的气息，不然我的脑袋肯定会爆炸。这里只能靠我们自己了，伙计。” 总在最糟糕的时候失灵，对吧？好吧，或许你该试上一试。
rows.raw: " You investigate the section of wall more closely, and as it happens there's a small storeroom set in an alcove like the one you started off in, only smaller and still full, it seems. There might be something useful in the pots and barrels, if you could get to the other side — at the very least, it'd make wandering about in this chaotic web of stairs and halls less of a waste, especially since you've arrived at a dead end. Of course, it's closed off with a grate, and set into the wall by its side is a very boreal elven mechanism — a wheel that's no doubt attached to the raising mechanism. You give it an experimental turn and it clicks: well, at least it still works. You don't remember this being in your wayfort, but as discrepancies go this is pretty small. "Oh. It's one of these again. Used to have a mechanism like this in one of my old houses — the boreal elves built them all over the place. Easier than losing your key, at any rate. Guess someone had these on his or her mind when the poor bastard died." You may remember that from last time. Or you may not. Everything about that episode passed by in a drunken haze, really... "If it's like the old sluice gate..." Nina taps her chin, thinking. "How you lift the gate is through this wheel over here: you can turn it left, right, or just hold it in place for a bit. You've got to do this five times, and it's got to be in the correct sequence; for each action in the sequence that you perform correctly, the mechanism will click." So if you got three out of five correct, there'd be three clicks? "That's right. What we want to hear is five clicks from the portcullis mechanism." Always good to have her around to explain things. So, no helpful visions as to the answer? "None at all, man. I can feel them trying to get to me, but whatever's stopping us from going out is also stopping them from coming in; that's a good thing because I'm pretty sure my head would explode otherwise with all the bad vibes surrounding us. We're on our own here, man." Always at the worst possible times, huh? All right, maybe you'll give this a go."

rows.original: There's something set in the wall here...
rows.translation: 这里的墙里似乎有什么东西……
rows.raw: "There's something set in the wall here..."

rows.original: You take one last look at the stash in the alcove and shrug. Whatever's behind that grate, it can't be more important than finding a way forward in this twisting maze of madness, which is what you really should be doing at the moment. "Sour grapes is fine, man. No shame in it," Nina says, patting you on the shoulder. "That's what Rumie says half the time when she gets around to serving me my drinks — no idea what she means by it." She's not exactly helping or making you feel better. "Tough. Let's be on our way, yeah? We can circle around back if you discover that you can suddenly turn into mist or something and float through the grate. Man, that'd be really cool." You frown. Does she know lots of people who can do that? "Just the one, but people discover all sorts of funky things about themselves under pressure. It could happen, man."
rows.translation: 你最后看了一眼壁龛中的储藏物，耸了耸肩。无论栅栏后面藏着什么，都不可能比在这座扭曲疯狂的迷宫中找到前进道路更重要，而这才是你此刻真正该做的事。 “吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸也没事，伙计，没什么好丢脸的，”妮娜拍着你的肩膀说道。“露米有一半时间都是这么说的，尤其是她终于肯给我上酒的时候——我完全不懂她是什么意思。” 她既没有帮上忙，也没让你好受多少。 “管他的。我们上路，好吗？要是你突然发现自己能变成雾气什么的，从栅栏间飘过去，我们还可以绕回来。天啊，那肯定酷毙了。” 你皱起眉头。她认识很多能做到这种事的人吗？ “只认识一个，不过人在压力下会发现自己身上各种稀奇古怪的能力。说不定真会发生，伙计。”

rows.translation: 你输入到该系统中的序列是：<b>
rows.raw: "\n        The sequence you fed into the mechanism was: <b>"

rows.original: [var0 |You finish your sequence of turns, and let go of the wheel to see what happens with the grate. Nope, nothing, not even a single click. "Hey, it's fine," Nina says, patting you on the shoulder. "At least you know what not to do next." There is that, you suppose. Given that there're only so many combinations of wheel turns to be had, having a complete dud ought to teach you something about what the correct sequence ought to be. It's not like there's anyone here judging you for guessing wrong or anything. "I forgot the combination all the time when I lived in that old sluicehouse up north," Nina chirps happily. "Of course, I always had a vision or two to remind me what it was whenever it was handy. Man, I really miss them. At least you have something to go on, unlike me." It's not as if the mechanism will stop clicking or anything if Nina's the one turning the wheel, will it? "Might be. You never know with the machine spirits — sometimes they just don't like people. I don't know what I did to earn their enmity, but there're also plenty of other things I don't know." |You finish the sequence of turns and wait for something to happen. After what feels like an eternity, you hear a single click from the gate mechanism. Better than nothing... or perhaps maybe worse, given that you've no way of telling exactly which turn of the wheel was the right one. Or maybe you do, and just have to think about it a little. "For what it's worth, I think we're pretty safe here," Nina chirps. "So long as we don't move about too much, I think we can't be found when in this very specific section of the maze. Kind of like the eye of the storm, man, the center of calm when you're all conflicted. Deep. "Anyways, just keep at it, okay?" |You finish the sequence of turns and wait for the gate's response. Before too long, two clicks sound from within the mechanism, the gate itself still unmoving. Not completely cold, perhaps, but still some ways off from the correct sequence. "Take your time, man," Nina says, patting you on the shoulder. "Not as if it's flowing in here while we all slowly go crazy." That's a thought: can someone like Nina actually get any crazier than she already is? Well, in the same fashion, anyway. In fact, does her absolutely batshit insane mind have any helpful suggestions as to getting this thing open? She used to live in a place which had one of these, after all. "I'd turn the wheel all the way to one side once, then to the other, then hold it. Figure out how many of each are in the correct sequence; that's a good starting point that everyone can use, man." Nina shrugs. "That knowledge would help narrow down the potential number of sequences quite a bit, wouldn't it? You'd still have to figure out what goes where, but the kinds of turns that you have to do with the wheel wouldn't be a mystery any more." Hmm... "Like, it'd matter if you were limited in how many times you could try, but since we aren't there's nothing to lose, man. Just keep at it." |You finish the sequence of turns and wait to see if anything happens; sure enough, after a few seconds, you hear three clicks from the gate's internal mechanisms. More than halfway there, then — that's got to be good, right? "Getting warm," Nina says, patting you on the shoulder. "You'll figure it out before too long. I believe in you, man — you've already brought us this far." Yeah well, that's little comfort when she's just standing there watching you figure it out while dishing out helpful advice. "See? Man, I sure am helpful. Feels great to be as good a helper as I am. Now, for my next bit of great advice — just turning the wheel randomly and hoping to strike upon the sequence by chance isn't going to get you anywhere. Like, you've got to have a —" she frowns, gears turning in her head — "strategy to figure it out. Approach it all methodically-like, you know?" Would she mind sharing such a strategy, then? "What works for me might not work for you. Besides, you're at three out of five. Might as well keep on doing what you're doing, right?" |You finish the sequence of turns and wait for the gate's response, which comes almost immediately: a series of four loud clicks and several grinding noises from the grate, which sends specks of dust floating down from the ceiling. Unfortunately, the last click doesn't come — close, but not close enough. "Almost there," Nina says. "Just got one of them wrong. Question is: which one?" Does she have any idea? "To be perfectly honest, no. You're so much more interesting than a silly old grate, I've been watching you all this time, man. Why would I spend any of my limited head-space on that when you're doing it already? Won't go any faster with two people doing it." Actually, it might, but arguing the point with Nina's going to waste more time than actually getting this done. Just one more — but which one is it? |No sooner have you finished with the wheel that five clicks sound from within the old stone wall, and the grate swings wide open. It functions surprisingly well for being so ancient — maybe you should look within your own Wayfort for false walls and the like when you get back. But now, the contents of the storeroom lie before you, ripe for the taking. Nina and you spend the next several moments searching through the old containers — while most of them are sundries like grain and dusty linens, you do find several jars of vulneraries and a sealed package of dried winterstem. Nina, on the other hand, continues to have absolutely no luck in the search for a cure for her sobriety. You gain 5x vulnerary. You gain 5x winterstem. "Gods, what is this? Don't soldiers need drink to function, even if they were elves?" Actually[pc.bg soldier |, you're a soldier and ] — "Well, at least they liked to smoke enough to put some of that away. Wonder if a smoke would even do anything in this place." Well, at least coming all this way wasn't completely pointless. Now it's time to turn away from this dead end and find the actual way out of this maze... ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你完成了一系列操作后，松开了操纵杆，想看看栅栏会发生什么变化。结果，什么也没有发生。甚至没有点击一下嘿，没关系的，”妮娜轻拍着你的肩膀说，“至少你现在知道发生了什么。不是接下来该做什么。是嗯，你这么认为吧。既然车轮转动的组合方式有限，那么一次完全失败的尝试应该能让你明白正确的顺序是什么。毕竟这里没有人会因为你猜错而批评你什么。 我在北方那座老水闸屋里住的时候，总是忘记那个密码组合，”妮娜开心地说道，“不过每次需要的时候，我总会突然想到一些线索来提醒自己该是什么。唉，我真的挺想念那些地方的。至少你还有事情可做，不像我。” 就算是由妮娜来转动那个轮子，这个机器应该也不会停止运转吧？ “也许会吧。谁知道这些机器精灵会怎么反应呢——有时候它们就是不喜欢人类。我不知道自己做了什么才会招致他们的敌意，但还有很多其他的事情我也并不清楚。 |你完成了这一系列的操作，然后等待着某种事情的发生。在仿佛过了漫长的时间之后，你终于听到了只需轻轻点击门控装置即可。总比什么都没有好……不过，也许情况会更糟，因为你根本无法确定究竟是哪一次尝试才是正确的。 又或者，你其实心里清楚，只是需要再仔细思考一下而已。 不管怎么说，我觉得我们在这里应该挺安全的，”妮娜轻声说道，“只要我们不要到处乱动，就应该不会被找到。在这个迷宫的特定区域里，我们简直就像风暴中的平静中心，在周围一切都很混乱的时候，这里却是宁静的所在。不管怎样，坚持下去就好，好吗？ |你完成了一系列操作后，等待着大门的回应。不久之后，机械内部传来了两次点击声。大门本身依然纹丝不动。或许还没有完全冷却，但距离达到正确的状态还有一段距离。 “慢慢来吧，伙计，”妮娜轻拍着你的肩膀说，“总不会在我们都慢慢发疯的时候，液体突然流进这里来的吧。这个想法挺有意思的：像尼娜这样的人，还能变得比现在更疯狂吗？嗯，至少在某种程度上应该是可以的吧。其实，她那完全疯狂的头脑，会不会有什么有用的建议，能帮助我们打开这个东西呢？她曾经住在一个有这种东西的地方，毕竟。 “我会先把方向盘转到一边，然后再转到另一边，然后保持这个位置。弄清楚每种东西按照正确的顺序应该放在什么位置上；这是一个大家都可以使用的好方法，真的。尼娜耸了耸肩：“这样的知识确实能大大缩小可能的序列组合范围，不是吗？虽然你仍然需要弄清楚各个部分应该放在什么位置，但使用转盘时该选择哪些选项，就再也不会成为谜团了。嗯……” “比如说，如果尝试的次数有限的话，那确实会很重要，但既然我们现在没有这种限制，那就没什么可失去的，继续努力吧。 |你完成了这一系列的行动，然后等待看是否会发生什么；果然，几秒钟后你会听到三声咔嗒声。从大门的内部机制来看，已经进行到一半以上了——这样应该已经很不错了吧？ “慢慢来，”妮娜轻拍着你的肩膀说，“你很快就会掌握方法的。我相信你，伙计，你已经带领我们走到了这一步。是啊，不过当她站在那里，一边给你提供有用的建议，一边看着你自己想办法解决问题的时候，这种‘帮助’也就没什么意义了。” “看吧？我确实是个很乐于帮忙的人。能够成为一个这么有用的帮手，感觉真是太好了。现在，我来给大家提供另一个很重要的建议——仅仅随意转动转盘，指望偶然找到正确的序列，是根本不会有什么结果的。也就是说，你必须得有一个……”她皱起眉头，开始在脑海中思考，“策略要想弄清楚这个问题，就得有条不紊地来处理，你懂我的意思吧？” 那么，她会不会愿意分享这样的策略呢？ “对我有效的方法，对你可能并不适用。而且，你现在已经取得了三胜两负的成绩，继续坚持你现在的做法或许才是最好的选择，对吧？ |你完成了一系列操作后，等待着大门的反应，而这个反应几乎立刻就到来了：一连四声清脆的咔嗒声栅栏处传来几声刺耳的摩擦声，那些声音使得天花板上的灰尘开始飘落下来。不幸的是，最后的那个动作并没有成功——差一点，但还不够。 “快成功了，”妮娜说道，“只是有一个步骤做错了而已。问题是：哪一个？” 她知道答案吗？ “说实话，不知道。你可比那个愚蠢的老铁栅栏有趣多了，我一直都在观察你呢，伙计。既然你已经在做了，我为什么还要把有限的精力浪费在这件事上呢？两个人一起做的话，速度并不会更快啊。 其实，也许会更快一些，但和妮娜争论这个话题，只会浪费更多的时间，而根本无法真正把这件事完成。就再最后一个吧——但到底是哪一个呢？ |你刚把那个轮子弄完，五次点击从那古老的石墙内部传来了声响，栅栏也随之大敞开来。尽管这东西如此古老，但它运作起来却出奇地顺畅——也许你回去后，应该在自己的荒废驿堡基地里也找找类似的假墙之类的东西。 现在，储藏室里的东西就摆在你的面前，任你取用。尼娜和你一起花了接下来的几分钟时间翻找那些旧容器——虽然其中大部分里面装的都是谷物或者积满灰尘的亚麻布之类的杂物，但你们还是找到了几罐治疗伤药的药材，以及一包密封好的干冬茎。另一方面，尼娜在寻找让自己能够保持清醒状态的方法时，仍然一无所获。 你的脆弱性会增加5倍。 你将获得5倍的冬茎。 天啊，这是什么？就算是精灵士兵，不也需要喝水来维持正常活动吗？[pc.bg soldier |你是一名士兵，因此…… ]嗯，至少他们很喜欢抽烟，抽烟的频率高到那个走了。不知道在这地方抽烟到底有没有用……” “好吧，至少一路走来并没有完全白费。现在该离开这个死胡同，找到真正离开这个迷宫的路了…… ]

Why would I spend any of my limited head-space on that when you're doing it already? Won't go any faster with two people doing it." Actually, it might, but arguing the point with Nina's going to waste more time than actually getting this done. Just one more — but which one is it? |No sooner have you finished with the wheel that five clicks sound from within the old stone wall, and the grate swings wide open. It functions surprisingly well for being so ancient — maybe you should look within your own Wayfort for false walls and the like when you get back. But now, the contents of the storeroom lie before you, ripe for the taking. Nina and you spend the next several moments searching through the old containers — while most of them are sundries like grain and dusty linens, you do find several jars of vulneraries and a sealed package of dried winterstem. Nina, on the other hand, continues to have absolutely no luck in the search for a cure for her sobriety. You gain 5x vulnerary. You gain 5x winterstem. "Gods, what is this? Don't soldiers need drink to function, even if they were elves?" Actually[pc.bg soldier |, you're a soldier and ] — "Well, at least they liked to smoke enough to put some of that away. Wonder if a smoke would even do anything in this place." Well, at least coming all this way wasn't completely pointless. Now it's time to turn away from this dead end and find the actual way out of this maze... ] "

rows.original: Compared to the Wayfort that you know, the grand hall of Wayfort past exudes an air of melancholy — an easy task when just about every piece of furniture lies in splinters save for the long table, which itself is ruined by bloodstains long soaked into the grain of the wood. Another discrepancy from the state the Wayfort was in when you found it — the long table was smashed as well... "Careful, man. There's something here. Reckon it's pretty big too, if the traces I'm seeing are right." No helpful visions? "Sorry, man, haven't had any. Dunno why, but they've been, like, in really short supply ever since we ended up in this place. Funny, that." Remembering the feathered fiend that awaited you by the exit of your vault, you tighten your fingers about your [pc.weapon] and proceed into the great hall, edging around the chamber with your back against the walls. Not that it ought to matter given that the broken minds of the old garrison are more than capable of phasing through stone, but it makes you feel better and in this place that does count for something. As you inch closer to the middle of the room, Nina taps your shoulder and points. You squint, and then see it too — a faint white mist starting to gather near the bloodstained table, something materializing and taking shape. Instincts taking over, you [pc.isMage |ready a spell, hoping to get a first strike off on whatever this is before it can fully manifest and threaten you. As it turns out, the magic is consumed mid-flight, the spell fizzling and failing [pc.swornGod nareva |in a fashion that's distinctly familiar to you |before your eyes ] |step forward and swing with your [pc.weapon], hoping to strike first against whatever broken psyche this is before it can fully manifest. Unlike your previous encounters, though, your [pc.weapon] doesn't hurt it at all, passing through the apparition without so much as slowing ]. That would have hurt quite badly, a voice echoes in your head. [pc.isMage |[pc.swornGod nareva |On the other hand, it's good to know that my faculties are still in order. Gods, it's been so long... |I suppose it's good to know that at least some of my faculties are still in order. ] |[pc.swornGod nareva |Is that how they're greeting people in Tychris these days? It used to be more of a friendly clap on the shoulder, even amongst close friends. |But I've retained enough of my wits to know that I'm dead and ought to be immaterial. ] ] The apparition finally coalesces into greater definition — though largely drained of color, you can make out a dark tint to the salamander's scales, and a long chain of glass beads about her neck holds a medallion in the shape of an ouroboros, Nareva's holy symbol. Though her clothes certainly are long out of fashion, the tell-tale signs are still the same: [pc.swornGod nareva |she's an Astrida just like you are. Nareva be praised, the spirit mumbles, melancholy and a little dazed all at once. Sane, living people, and one of them is of the Order, too. I'd hoped... |she's a gothmander right out of Tychris. Nareva be praised, the spirit sighs. Living, sane people. I had almost given up hope. ] Holding out her hands palms forward as she steps forward, the Astrida probably intends to mean you no harm, but what her hands are sending is a rather different message. Heavy, clawed hands adorned with thick scales and hooked tips, not to mention the horns... now that she's more clearly defined, she looks just a tinge more draconic than most salamanders do. Nina shrinks back behind you, and you give her a reassuring pat on the wing. Ahem. If she doesn't mind, introductions please? [pc.swornGod nareva |You're just as glad to see another of Nareva's godsworn in this place, but even so being familiar usually means knowing the other party's name |While it's good to find another sane soul in this ever-changing madhouse, you'd like to know who you're speaking to ]. You'll begin — you're [pc.name], and this here by your side is Antonina. Now, she would be? Sorry, sorry. I... I'm Thalia Galanis, but when I was inducted into the order I shed my last name and took up that of Star-Viewer. [pc.swornGod nareva |That's... hm. Thalia frowns at your confusion. Do they not do this any more for those inducted into the Order? Your clothes are a little strange — how long has it been? No, Nareva's godsworn don't change their names when inducted into the order, because none are these days — it's something one's born to. You were the first recruitment in a long, long time, and the goddess certainly didn't bring up any such requirement or custom. And as for her second question, it's been about two and a half centuries since the Godswar. Since the Godswar. We won, then. At great cost, but yes. Remnants exist and need to be constantly suppressed. ...They don't change their last names, because there's no need to. Maybe... maybe it's better this way. |That's... well, you don't know any Astrida who have last names in that manner. Thalia frowns at your confusion. Do they not do this any more for those inducted into the Order? Your clothes are a little strange — how long has it been? No, Nareva's godsworn don't change their names when inducted into the order, because none are these days — it's something one's born to. Everyone knows that; they're pretty famous all over Savarra and aren't shy about making who and what they are known to the people at large. Known all over Savarra. Ah... if only I could see it. Well, infamous to the wrong people. And as for her second question, it's been about two and a half centuries since the Godswar. Since the Godswar. We won, then. At great cost, but yes. Remnants exist and need to be constantly suppressed. ] Thalia slowly closes her spectral eyes and shakes her head. There is so much I need to ask you, [pc.name]. Funny, you could say the same. But perhaps she should go first, and answer some of your questions...
rows.translation: 与你所熟知的荒废驿堡相比，那里的宏伟大厅如今弥漫着一种忧郁的气息——这种氛围很容易营造出来，因为几乎所有的家具都已经破碎成碎片，只有那张长桌例外，而那张长桌也被血迹侵蚀得面目全非，血迹早已渗入木纹之中。这与你发现荒废驿堡时它的状态又有所不同——那张长桌子也被砸坏了…… “小心点，这里面好像有什么东西。如果我看到的痕迹没有弄错的话，那东西应该相当大。 没有任何有用的预感吗？ “抱歉，伙计，我一点预感都没有。不知道为什么，自从我们来到这个地方之后，这种预感就变得非常稀少了。真是奇怪。” 回想起那个在你的地窖出口处等着你的有羽毛的怪物，你紧紧握住了手中的[pc.weapon]然后你走进大厅，沿着墙壁小心翼翼地移动。虽然考虑到那些老驻军们混乱的思维完全有可能穿透石头，这其实并不重要，但这样做会让你感觉更安心——而在这个地方，这种安全感确实很重要。 当你慢慢靠近房间的中央时，妮娜轻拍你的肩膀并指向某个方向。你眯起眼睛，然后也看到了——一片淡淡的白色雾气开始在那张沾满血迹的桌子附近聚集，某种东西正在形成、逐渐显现出来。本能占据了上风，你[pc.isMage |准备好了咒语，希望能在这东西完全显现出来并威胁到你之前，先发制人。结果却是在咒语释放的过程中，魔力就被消耗殆尽了，咒语也就失效了。 [pc.swornGod nareva |以一种你非常熟悉的方式 |就在你眼前 ] |上前一步，然后挥动你的[pc.weapon]你希望能在这种扭曲的心理状态完全显现之前，先发制人加以阻止。不过，与之前的遭遇不同，这一次[pc.weapon]这样做完全没有任何坏处，甚至可以在穿过那个幻影的时候毫不减速 ]。 那肯定会非常疼的。有一个声音在你脑海中回荡。[pc.isMage |[pc.swornGod nareva |另一方面，知道自己的各项机能仍然正常运作，这也是一件好事。天啊，真是过了太久的时间了…… |我想，知道自己的某些能力仍然正常运作，也算是件好事吧。 ] |[pc.swornGod nareva |现在在提克里斯，人们就是用这种方式打招呼的吗？过去，即使是亲密的朋友之间，也会用友好的方式拍拍对方的肩膀来表示问候。 |但我还算保持着足够的清醒，明白自己已经死了，应该不再关心这些事情了。 ] ] 这个幻影终于变得清晰可辨了——虽然它的颜色已经大部消失，但仍然可以分辨出那条蝾螈鳞片上淡淡的暗色，而它脖子上戴的那串玻璃珠里，悬挂着一枚象征着娜瑞瓦的圣物——环形图案的奖章。尽管她的衣服早已过时，但这些特征依然清晰可见。 [pc.swornGod nareva |她和你一样，也是一名阿斯特里达。 赞美娜瑞瓦吧，那灵魂开始低语，语气中充满了忧郁，同时还带着一丝恍惚。都是神志清醒的活人，其中还有一个人属于那个组织。我原本还抱有希望…… |她简直就是从提克里斯世界中走出来的哥特曼德。 赞美娜瑞瓦吧，灵魂在叹息。活着的、神志清醒的人们啊……我几乎已经放弃了希望。 ] 当她向前迈步时，双手掌心朝前，阿斯特里达大概是想表示自己没有恶意，但她的双手所传递的信息却截然不同。那些布满厚厚鳞片、指尖呈钩状的重型爪子，更不用说那些角了……现在她的形象已经更加清晰明了，与大多数蝾螈相比，她确实显得更具龙类的特征。尼娜吓得缩到了你身后，你轻轻拍了拍她的翅膀，以安慰她。 嗯，如果她不介意的话，能不能介绍一下你们呢？ [pc.swornGod nareva |看到娜瑞瓦的这位信徒出现在这里，你同样感到高兴；不过，熟悉对方通常也意味着知道对方的名字。 |虽然在这个变化无常的疯狂世界里找到另一个理智的人确实是一件好事，但你还是想知道自己正在和谁交谈。 ]你将会开始——你就是[pc.name]，而站在你身边的这位就是安东妮娜。那么，她现在应该……？ 对不起，对不起。我……我是塔莉娅·加拉尼斯，但当我加入这个组织时，我放弃了自己的姓氏，改用了“星之观察者”这个称号。 [pc.swornGod nareva |那……嗯。 塔莉娅看到你一脸困惑，皱起了眉头。对于那些被纳入这个组织的人来说，他们不再这样做了吗？你的穿着有点奇怪……这都已经过去多久了？ 不，娜瑞瓦的神圣骑士们在加入这个组织时并不会更改自己的名字，因为如今已经没有人会这样做了——这种身份本就是与生俱来的。你是很久很久以来第一次有新人被招募进来，而女神也确实没有提到过任何这样的要求或习俗。至于她的第二个问题，自从那场神战以来，已经过去了大约两个半世纪了。 自从那场神战之后，我们就赢了。 虽然代价高昂，但确实如此。那些残余势力仍然存在，必须不断加以遏制。 ……他们没有更改自己的姓氏，因为没有必要这么做。也许……也许这样反而更好。 |那……嗯，你应该不认识任何姓氏是那样的阿斯特丽达吧。 塔莉娅看到你一脸困惑，皱起了眉头。对于那些被纳入这个组织的人来说，他们不再这样做了吗？你的穿着有点奇怪……这都已经过去多久了？ 不，娜瑞瓦的神之誓士们在加入这个组织后并不会改变自己的名字，因为如今已经没有人会这么做——这是与生俱来的身份。所有人都知道这一点；他们在整个萨瓦拉地区都很有名，也从不隐瞒自己的身份。 在整个萨瓦拉地区都是众所周知的。啊……要是我能亲眼看到它该多好。 嗯，对某些人来说，这个名字确实声名狼藉。至于她的第二个问题，自从那场神战之后，已经过去了大约两个半世纪了。 自从那场神战之后，我们就赢了。 虽然代价高昂，但确实如此。那些残余势力仍然存在，必须不断加以遏制。 ] 塞莉亚缓缓闭上她那幽灵般的眼睛，然后摇了摇头。有太多事情我想问你。 [pc.name]。 有趣，你也可以这么说。不过，或许她应该先来，回答你的一些问题……

rows.original: Several moments later, both Nina and you have filled Thalia in on what happened to you — Nina's visions, you going out into the Ways and being torn away from your original destination into this twisted image of the Wayfort. The broken spirits of the old boreal elf outriders garrisoned here and a bunch of Belharan stragglers, their psyches shattered. The many-eyed bird that you're certain was a manifestation of Nina's self. The wayfort, it still exists in your world. To be sure, the one on the River Ridell? Yes. Is that so strange? It's now your home and you're it's [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Certainly no one's about to challenge your claim, so there's that. There are some discrepancies between this Wayfort and the one you remember, differences that can't be explained by the mere ravages of time, but otherwise it's recognizable as the Wayfort. Hmm. Something the matter? Just thinking for now.[pc.swornGod nareva | I'll admit, when I first realized you were an Astrida, I'd hoped that the goddess had mustered a force to deal with the situation cleanly and thoroughly. Nevertheless, even one of us is a force to be reckoned with — perhaps it is fate that led you to this place. ] All right, then. Now it's Thalia's turn to explain what's going on here. In brief, if she doesn't mind — you get the feeling that dithering isn't going to help, and you can always ask for the details if need be. I understand; well, here's the abridged version: I am Thalia Star-Viewer, one of the first Astrida. The Godswar was raging, sweeping northwards from beyond the Greyvale Ranges. We'd just finished defending Tychris when a missive arrived from Njorhaalt; they'd heard of our successful defense of Tychris thanks to the newly-formed Order Astrida and begged us to help. The Belharans led by Victor Reverra were folding fast, with the marcher-baron himself dead and his daughter holed up in her castle; the village's inhabitants had either fled to the surrounding lupine tribes, northward towards the Wayfort in the hopes of sailing downriver to the safety of Khor'minos, or were dead. Okay, you follow her so far. Presumably, Nareva was willing to send reinforcements. Not too many. Me and a couple junior godsworn, with about a dozen of the prince's guard — the wraith host was slow-moving but numerous, and we had to go around them in order to reach the River Ridell before they did. That sounds like hardly enough to make a difference in holding back an advancing host. [pc.swornGod nareva |A dangerous mage might warrant a duo, a monstrosity unearthed in the heartlands half a dozen. A single Astrida and her retinue against an entire wraith-host — it's the stuff of legends, but the thing about legends is that they tend to grow in the telling. |The Astrida of your time are brave but aren't suicidal — you understand that the Godswar was a time of heroes, but even so. ] Oh, believe me, it was a price I paid later. But you must remember that we'd just held Tychris against all odds, even if the victory was a little pyrrhic. In that moment, it felt like there was nothing we newly minted godsworn couldn't do — we simply weren't as jaded as our descendants apparently now are. Hmph. We circled around the host's flanks and reached the River Ridell before they did, and the commander took us in, having received orders from Njorhaalt to expect our arrival. I'd never left Tychris or its surrounding lands before — it was quite the experience for me.
rows.translation: 几分钟后，尼娜和你都向塔莉娅讲述了发生在自己身上的事情——尼娜所看到的幻象，你进入那些通道后却被强行带到了这个扭曲的荒废驿堡景象中。这里驻扎着那些古老的极北精灵骑兵，他们的灵魂早已破碎；还有一些贝拉兰人的散兵游勇，他们的精神也受到了极大的伤害。而那只多眼鸟，你确信它就是尼娜自身的某种体现。 那个路标，它仍然存在于你的世界里。当然，就是那座位于里德尔河边的路标吧？ 是的。有那么奇怪吗？现在这里已经是你的家了，你才是这里的主人。 [pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]当然，没有人会质疑你的说法，这一点是肯定的。这个荒废驿堡与你记忆中的那个确实存在一些差异，这些差异无法仅仅用时间的侵蚀来解释，但除此之外，它确实可以被认出就是那个荒废驿堡。 嗯。 怎么了？ 只是暂时想想而已。[pc.swornGod nareva | 我得承认，当我第一次意识到你其实是阿斯特里达的时候，我原本希望这位女神能够召集一支力量，来彻底解决这个问题。不过，即便是我们中的一个人，也足以构成一股不容小觑的力量——或许，正是命运将你引到了这里。 ] 好吧，那么现在轮到塔莉娅来解释这里发生了什么。简而言之，如果她不介意的话——你们应该能感觉到，含糊其辞并不会有什么帮助，如果有需要，随时可以询问详细情况。 我明白了；那么，简短来说就是这样的：我是塔莉娅·星望者，也是最早的一批阿斯特拉达成员之一。当时神战正在肆虐，战火从灰谷山脉以北地区蔓延开来。我们刚刚完成对提克里斯的防御，就收到了来自Njorhaalt的求援信——他们听说由于新成立的阿斯特拉达组织，我们成功守住了提克里斯，因此恳请我们伸出援手。 在维克托·雷维拉的率领下，贝尔哈兰人正在迅速溃败：那位领主本人已经阵亡，他的女儿则躲在城堡里不肯出来；村庄的居民要么逃到了周边的狼族部落，要么向北前往荒废驿堡，希望能顺流而下，到达安全的科尔米诺斯地区，要么已经死了。 好吧，到目前为止你都是跟着她的节奏走的。想必，娜瑞瓦也是愿意派遣援军的。 不算太多。我和几个初级神誓者，还有大约十几名王子的护卫——那些幽灵军队行动缓慢，但数量庞大，我们必须绕开它们，才能在他们之前赶到里德尔河。 这样的力量显然远远不足以阻止敌军的进攻。 [pc.swornGod nareva |一个危险的法师或许需要两个人来对付；而那种在内陆地区发现的怪物，更是需要两人才能将其消灭。仅仅靠一个阿斯特里达和她的随从去对抗整个幽灵军团，这样的故事简直就像是传说中的情节。但传说嘛，往往在流传的过程中会被夸大其词。 |你们这个时代的阿斯特里达们虽然勇敢，但并不会选择自杀——你们明白，神战时期确实是英雄辈出的时代，但即便如此…… ] 哦，相信我，这是我后来不得不付出的代价。但你们必须记住，当时我们是在种种艰难险阻中才战胜了提克里斯，尽管这场胜利代价沉重。在那一刻，我们觉得没有什么是我们这些新诞生的、被神明诅咒的战士做不到的——至少我们还没有像我们的后代现在这样变得麻木不仁。 哼。 我们在敌军之前绕到了主力的侧翼，抢先抵达了里德尔河。指挥官接到了Njorhaalt的命令，让我们务必在此等候，因此他热情地接待了我们。我此前从未离开过蒂克里斯及其周边地区，因此这次经历对我来说确实是一次全新的体验。
rows.raw: " Several moments later, both Nina and you have filled Thalia in on what happened to you — Nina's visions, you going out into the Ways and being torn away from your original destination into this twisted image of the Wayfort. The broken spirits of the old boreal elf outriders garrisoned here and a bunch of Belharan stragglers, their psyches shattered. The many-eyed bird that you're certain was a manifestation of Nina's self. The wayfort, it still exists in your world. To be sure, the one on the River Ridell? Yes. Is that so strange? It's now your home and you're it's [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. Certainly no one's about to challenge your claim, so there's that. There are some discrepancies between this Wayfort and the one you remember, differences that can't be explained by the mere ravages of time, but otherwise it's recognizable as the Wayfort. Hmm. Something the matter? Just thinking for now.[pc.swornGod nareva | I'll admit, when I first realized you were an Astrida, I'd hoped that the goddess had mustered a force to deal with the situation cleanly and thoroughly. Nevertheless, even one of us is a force to be reckoned with — perhaps it is fate that led you to this place. ] All right, then. Now it's Thalia's turn to explain what's going on here. In brief, if she doesn't mind — you get the feeling that dithering isn't going to help, and you can always ask for the details if need be. I understand; well, here's the abridged version: I am Thalia Star-Viewer, one of the first Astrida. The Godswar was raging, sweeping northwards from beyond the Greyvale Ranges. We'd just finished defending Tychris when a missive arrived from Njorhaalt; they'd heard of our successful defense of Tychris thanks to the newly-formed Order Astrida and begged us to help. The Belharans led by Victor Reverra were folding fast, with the marcher-baron himself dead and his daughter holed up in her castle; the village's inhabitants had either fled to the surrounding lupine tribes, northward towards the Wayfort in the hopes of sailing downriver to the safety of Khor'minos, or were dead. Okay, you follow her so far. Presumably, Nareva was willing to send reinforcements. Not too many. Me and a couple junior godsworn, with about a dozen of the prince's guard — the wraith host was slow-moving but numerous, and we had to go around them in order to reach the River Ridell before they did. That sounds like hardly enough to make a difference in holding back an advancing host. [pc.swornGod nareva |A dangerous mage might warrant a duo, a monstrosity unearthed in the heartlands half a dozen. A single Astrida and her retinue against an entire wraith-host — it's the stuff of legends, but the thing about legends is that they tend to grow in the telling. |The Astrida of your time are brave but aren't suicidal — you understand that the Godswar was a time of heroes, but even so. ] Oh, believe me, it was a price I paid later. But you must remember that we'd just held Tychris against all odds, even if the victory was a little pyrrhic. In that moment, it felt like there was nothing we newly minted godsworn couldn't do — we simply weren't as jaded as our descendants apparently now are. Hmph. We circled around the host's flanks and reached the River Ridell before they did, and the commander took us in, having received orders from Njorhaalt to expect our arrival. I'd never left Tychris or its surrounding lands before — it was quite the experience for me."

rows.original: So, the wraith-host descended upon them then? Not immediately. It could have been days, weeks, I don't remember how long exactly — but nothing of note happened. The wraith-host was caught up around Hawkethorne for an inordinate amount of time — I don't know if the imperials put up that good a fight, or if there was something else at play there. One night, though, we all saw it: a beam of light engulfing Castle Hawkstone in the distance, illuminated against the night sky. The next day, the wraith-host started moving again. I was sent to the Wayfort to fight, but as it turned out I ended up playing surgeon for most of my stay. This hall was where I did most of my work; it wasn't as if there were going to be any feasts in the near future. Imperial stragglers, the local lupines, minotaur legionnaires who'd gotten separated — one by one they found their ways to our gates, and I sent them on towards the Frostwood and Njorhaalt. We couldn't keep them here, save for those few who could fight and would warrant us stretching our supplies. Eventually, the enemy came — at first the outriders and their wargs came in with gashes from encounters with thralls, then by and large the host began filtering in through the southern forest over weeks. There were several clashes — I was finally able to leave the great hall to actually fight and show these elves what an Astrida could do. Then the wraiths arrived, surrounded by their sycophantic mages. We were prepared for a long, bitter siege, [pc.name]. We were ready to collapse the bridge if need be, to hold out for weeks or even months. Whatever Victor Reverra did in order to stall the host for that long before his demise, we were ready to outdo it. He didn't have divine power on his side. We did. Thalia's voice halts here, the Astrida mulling over her words, and you motion for her to continue. We were on the walls, arrayed with grim determination — even the Belharan stragglers who'd thrown their lot in with us found sudden inspiration in our ragtag group. We'd have given them a long, protracted fight had we the chance to... which we didn't. I guess whatever happened at Hawkethorne, at Castle Hawkstone, it had exhausted whatever patience those monsters had. We'd loosed the first volley of arrows from the ramparts and were preparing for another when someone shouted and pointed up at the sky. They'd opened a portal, [pc.name] — they'd torn open the sky, something that only happened as a result of the confluence of great supernatural powers. Something that took the mages of Estelore great effort to accomplish, the wraiths and their minions achieved with ease. For a moment, I saw what was beyond the portal, [pc.name]. It was beautiful and terrible at the same time — I knew I had to react, to fight, but couldn't tear my eyes away from the wondrous horror even as I gathered the goddess' power in myself. That was my undoing. A meteorite came out of the portal the wraiths had torn in reality — a massive chunk of dark, gleaming material from beyond our world, a raw bundle of terrible power. It smashed straight into the courtyard — I knew I had to do something and I did... I did something... What did she do? There was a lot of power there, I recall. The meteorite wasn't just death, it was life of a sort that was antithetical to our own. The inverse of ley-crystals, as it were. And... and then... And then what? I don't remember. It was thoroughly unpleasant, a sensation of being torn asunder, and then my next concrete recollection is of coming to next to the table on which I'd treated the many casualties this wayfort's garrison suffered. My best guess is that so many of my recent memories had been made in this hall that my spirit was drawn here. And she's been in this hall ever since? I can't leave, [pc.name]. Believe me, I've tried. Be it the main doors or those leading to the throne room, I... just can't. Everything just fades — maybe I didn't have enough of a connection to the rest of the Wayfort in life, maybe whatever's keeping you here is also hemming me into this hall. The reason may be unclear, but the end result is very real. You can only wonder at the things that Thalia's forgotten. They're all quite specific... narrow and deep. Conveniently placed to prevent her from giving critical information. I've wondered what ties them together, but there we have it. I can't leave.
rows.translation: 所以，那些被怨灵附身的生物当时就袭击他们了？ 并没有立即发生什么。可能过了几天、几周，我记不清具体用了多长时间——但总之没有任何值得注意的事情发生。那股幽灵军团在鹰棘镇附近停留了很长时间，我不知道帝国军队是否进行了激烈的抵抗，还是还有其他原因在起作用。然而有一天晚上，我们都看到了：一道光芒在远处笼罩了霍克斯通城堡，将其映照在夜空中。第二天，那股幽灵军团又开始移动了。 我被派往荒废驿堡参加战斗，但实际上，在那里的大部分时间里，我都在担任外科医生的工作。我大部分手术都是在这个大厅里完成的——因为在短期内，这里不可能会有任何宴会举行。那些帝国军队的散兵游勇、当地的狼族，以及那些与队伍走散的弥诺陶洛斯军团士兵，他们一个接一个地找到了我们这里，而我则把他们送往霜木之地和Njorhaalt。我们无法把他们留在这里，只有那些能够战斗、并且值得我们耗费资源来养活的人才能留下。最终，敌人来了——起初是那些先锋部队和他们的狼族战士，他们在与奴仆们的战斗中受了伤；随后，在接下来的几周里，敌军的主力部队开始从南边的森林中陆续涌入。发生了几起冲突——最终，我终于得以离开大厅，真正离开了那里。战斗让这些精灵们看看，一个真正的阿斯特丽达究竟能做到什么。 然后那些幽灵出现了，它们身边围绕着那些阿谀奉承的法师们。 我们做好了长期、艰苦的围攻准备的。 [pc.name]如果有必要，我们甚至准备拆毁那座桥，也要坚持数周甚至数月。无论维克托·雷维拉采取了什么手段来拖延时间，直到自己最终失败，我们都准备做得比他更彻底。他没有任何神力相助，而我们则有。 塔莉娅的话在这里停住了，阿斯特里达陷入了沉思，你示意她继续说下去。 我们全员士气高昂，斗志昂扬——就连那些原本独自行动、后来加入我们行列的贝尔哈兰人，也从我们这个临时组成的团队中找到了力量。如果有机会的话，我们一定能够与他们展开一场持久而激烈的战斗……可惜，我们并没有这样的机会。 我想，无论在鹰棘镇，还是在霍克斯通城堡发生了什么，那些怪物们的耐心已经耗尽了。我们刚刚从城墙上射出了第一波箭矢，正准备再次发动攻击时，突然有人大喊着指向天空——他们打开了一个传送门。 [pc.name] ——他们撕裂了天空，而这种景象只有在强大的超自然力量汇聚之时才会出现。对于埃斯特洛尔的法师们来说，要实现这一目标需要付出巨大的努力；而对于那些幽灵及其爪牙们来说，却轻而易举就能做到。 有那么一瞬间，我看到了传送门另一侧所呈现的景象。 [pc.name]那景象既美丽又恐怖——我知道自己必须做出反应，必须反抗，但当我将那位女神的力量凝聚在体内时，我却无法将视线从那令人毛骨悚然的景象上移开。而这，正是我失败的原因。 一颗陨石从那些幽灵在现实中撕开的裂缝中飞了出来——那是一块来自我们世界之外的巨大而漆黑的、闪烁着光芒的物质，蕴含着极其可怕的能量。它直接坠入了庭院……我知道自己必须采取行动，于是我就这么做了……我确实这么做了。某个东西…… 她做了什么？ 我记得，那里蕴含着巨大的能量。那颗陨石带来的不仅仅是死亡，还有一种与我们截然不同的生命形式。可以说，它是莱晶的相反存在。然后……然后…… 然后呢？ 我不记得了。那种感觉极其难受，就像身体被撕裂一样。接下来我清楚地记得自己走到了那张桌子旁——正是在那张桌子上，我以这种方式处理了fort’s驻军中那些受伤的士兵。我猜测，因为我最近很多记忆都是发生在这个大厅里的，所以我的灵魂被吸引到了这里。 从那以后，她就一直待在这个大厅里吗？ 我不能离开。 [pc.name]相信我，我试过了。无论是那些主门，还是通往王座厅的门，我都……就是进不去。所有东西都仿佛消失了——也许我在生前与荒废驿堡这个地方的联系不够紧密，也许就是某种力量将你困在这里，也将我束缚在这个大厅里。原因可能并不清楚，但结果却是显而易见的。 人们只能不禁猜测，塔莉娅究竟忘记了哪些事情。那些事情都相当具体……范围狭窄却内涵深刻，而且被巧妙地隐藏起来，从而阻止她透露出那些关键的信息。 我一直想知道是什么将他们联系在一起，现在终于明白了。我无法离开。

rows.original: Hmm. You're no expert on spirits and dreamwalking, but you do have one here. Hey, Nina... "Yeah? Don't mind me, man, just being all quiet and listening to this great story. I'd totally take this over some old lupine storyteller's drawl out in the woods." Yeah well, you need her opinion, being the psychic expert and all. Has she seen anything like this before? "Oh, all over the place. Thalia's not wrong in that she's likely bound here because it was where she spent most of her time in the Wayfort, man. Hearing her say it, she had the most intense — not necessarily painful, but just intense — memories impressed upon her in this place, and if she didn't care for the rest of the Wayfort and just treated it as a place to eat and sleep, then yeah, it makes sense. If you just don't care about anything, man, it becomes invisible to you, might as well not exist. That's just basic headology." Headology? "Don't sweat it, man. Turn of phrase." Is there any way that she could leave? "Depends. Was there something she gave a damn about? Like, felt really strongly towards?" As one, the both of you turn towards Thalia, who fidgets uncomfortably under your gaze. There were my juniors and the prince's guard sent with me, but I can't be sure they're even around in this memory of the Wayfort. I... I don't remember where they were supposed to be at the time the wraiths opened the portal and summoned the meteorite down on us, but I hope they made it out. Perhaps they were accompanying the outriders when it all happened. Yeah, that's not very helpful. Anything... wait a minute. You're pretty sure you know something that Thalia would feel strongly about — not necessarily in a good way, but certainly self-conscious with a bit of pride to boot. Oh? Her Astrida self. Throughout this conversation, you've had the feeling that... well, she certainly takes pride in being amongst the first to serve the goddess, and that the changes to her body weren't an unfortunate deformity, but a mark of devotion to Nareva. Yeah, you'd say she feels pretty strongly about the matter, moreso than her attachment to the grand hall. ...You aren't wrong. Well, Nina? Could Thalia leave that way? "If it were real enough to her, yeah. Man, that'd be a sight to see." There's the matter of actually finding Thalia's remains, assuming they're still around in the Wayfort, but if you do find them, Thalia would be able to leave the great hall by hitching a ride on them. Here where one's beliefs and memories are made uncomfortably real, it would be nice to have this mess work in your favor for once. I... I'm not sure if I should dare to hope. But all this has been a lot — seeing [pc.swornGod nareva |not just living souls here, but one of them being a fellow Astrida in the bargain |two living souls here when I'd given up all hope ] — and now a way out of this predicament? I... I need a moment to take it all in, please. That's fine, this introduction has run on overlong anyway. You'll be back to talk about it in a bit, or as long as she needs.
rows.translation: 嗯，你虽然不是灵界与梦游方面的专家，但你自己就拥有这样的能力。嘿，妮娜…… “嗯？别介意我这么说，我只是想安静地听这个精彩的故事而已。比起那些在森林里用拖长声音讲述故事的狼族讲述者，我更喜欢这个故事呢。嗯，你确实需要她的意见，毕竟她可是通灵方面的专家。她之前见过类似的情况吗？ “哦，这种事情到处都有。塔莉娅说得对，她很可能被束缚在这里，因为她在荒废驿堡的时候大部分时间都是在这里度过的。听到她这么说，那些发生在这个地方的回忆突然涌上心头——这些回忆并不一定令人痛苦，只是格外鲜明。如果她对荒废驿堡的其他地方毫不在意，只是把它当作一个用来吃饭和睡觉的地方，那么，嗯，这样想确实也挺合理的。如果你就是不愿意的话关心关于任何事情，伙计，它都会在你眼中变得毫无意义，简直就像不存在一样。这就是基本的‘心理认知原理’。” “心理认知原理？” “别担心，伙计，这只是个表达方式而已。 她有没有什么办法可以离开呢？ “这得看情况。有没有什么事情是她真正在乎的？也就是，她对某件事有着非常强烈的感情吧？” 你们俩同时转向了塔莉娅，而她在你们的注视下显得很不自在，坐立不安。 我的那些学弟们，还有随我一同前往的王子卫队成员们……但我不确定在荒废驿堡的这段记忆中，他们是否还存在于那里。我……我不记得当那些幽灵打开传送门、将陨石引向我们的时候，他们应该在哪里；但我希望他们能够成功逃脱。也许在这一切发生的时候，他们正在跟随那些先头部队行动吧。 是啊，这没什么帮助。有没有什么……等等，你应该是确定知道某些事情，这些事情会让塔莉娅感到非常在意——不一定是好的方面，但肯定会让她感到有些尴尬，甚至还会让她感到一丝自豪吧。 哦？ 她的阿斯特里达自我。在整个对话过程中，你一定感受到了……嗯，她确实为自己能够成为最早侍奉这位女神的人之一而感到自豪，而且她身体发生的那些变化，并不是什么不幸的畸形，而是对娜瑞瓦虔诚的象征。没错，你可以说，她对这件事的感受非常强烈，甚至超过了她对那座宏伟大厅的眷恋之情。 …你说的没错。 那么，妮娜？塔莉娅能从那边离开吗？” “如果这对她来说真的是真实存在的，的话，应该可以。天啊，那场面肯定很壮观。” 当然，前提是必须真正找到塔莉娅的遗骸，前提是它们还在荒废驿堡那里。但如果你真的找到了，塔莉娅就可以借助那些遗骸离开大厅了。在这个信念与记忆都被赋予了超乎寻常真实感的地方，要是这些因素能有一次反过来为你服务，那该多好啊。 我……我不确定是否应该敢于抱有希望。但这一切发生得太突然了——实在让人难以置信。 [pc.swornGod nareva |这里不仅仅有有生命的生物，其中还有一个还是我们的同伴——阿斯特丽达。 |当我已经彻底放弃希望的时候，这里还有两个活生生的人。 ] — 那现在有没有办法摆脱这种困境呢？我……我需要一点时间来消化这些信息，拜托了。 没关系，这个介绍本来就讲得太长了。过一会儿你们还会再讨论这个话题的，或者等她需要的时候再谈也行。
rows.raw: " Hmm. You're no expert on spirits and dreamwalking, but you do have one here. Hey, Nina... "Yeah? Don't mind me, man, just being all quiet and listening to this great story. I'd totally take this over some old lupine storyteller's drawl out in the woods." Yeah well, you need her opinion, being the psychic expert and all. Has she seen anything like this before? "Oh, all over the place. Thalia's not wrong in that she's likely bound here because it was where she spent most of her time in the Wayfort, man. Hearing her say it, she had the most intense — not necessarily painful, but just intense — memories impressed upon her in this place, and if she didn't care for the rest of the Wayfort and just treated it as a place to eat and sleep, then yeah, it makes sense. If you just don't care about anything, man, it becomes invisible to you, might as well not exist. That's just basic headology." Headology? "Don't sweat it, man. Turn of phrase." Is there any way that she could leave? "Depends. Was there something she gave a damn about? Like, felt really strongly towards?" As one, the both of you turn towards Thalia, who fidgets uncomfortably under your gaze. There were my juniors and the prince's guard sent with me, but I can't be sure they're even around in this memory of the Wayfort. I... I don't remember where they were supposed to be at the time the wraiths opened the portal and summoned the meteorite down on us, but I hope they made it out. Perhaps they were accompanying the outriders when it all happened. Yeah, that's not very helpful. Anything... wait a minute. You're pretty sure you know something that Thalia would feel strongly about — not necessarily in a good way, but certainly self-conscious with a bit of pride to boot. Oh? Her Astrida self. Throughout this conversation, you've had the feeling that... well, she certainly takes pride in being amongst the first to serve the goddess, and that the changes to her body weren't an unfortunate deformity, but a mark of devotion to Nareva. Yeah, you'd say she feels pretty strongly about the matter, moreso than her attachment to the grand hall. ...You aren't wrong. Well, Nina? Could Thalia leave that way? "If it were real enough to her, yeah. Man, that'd be a sight to see." There's the matter of actually finding Thalia's remains, assuming they're still around in the Wayfort, but if you do find them, Thalia would be able to leave the great hall by hitching a ride on them. Here where one's beliefs and memories are made uncomfortably real, it would be nice to have this mess work in your favor for once. I... I'm not sure if I should dare to hope. But all this has been a lot — seeing [pc.swornGod nareva |not just living souls here, but one of them being a fellow Astrida in the bargain |two living souls here when I'd given up all hope ] — and now a way out of this predicament? I... I need a moment to take it all in, please. That's fine, this introduction has run on overlong anyway. You'll be back to talk about it in a bit, or as long as she needs. "

rows.original: Is there something you need to discuss with Thalia?
rows.translation: 有什么事情你需要和塔莉娅讨论吗？
rows.raw: "Is there something you need to discuss with Thalia?"

rows.original: As you approach the dusty tables, the shape of Thalia fades into view, weary but putting up a hopeful front. You're back, [pc.name]. Is there something I can do for you? At least, that falls within the reach of the chains I find myself bound by? There might be some topics that you'd like to pick her mind on to better understand the Wayfort as it was in the past and what happened here, perhaps have her retell some of the sections to see if there was anything you missed the first time around. Please, ask away. Ask as many times as you'd like — when all one has for company this last eternity are the broken minds of the Wayfort's old garrison, one gets a little lonely. There are some things that I cannot, or may not speak of, but I'll do my best. There's not much I can do in this state save hold a conversation...
rows.translation: 当你走近那些布满灰尘的桌子时，塔莉娅的身影逐渐清晰起来——她显得疲惫不堪，但却努力保持着乐观的表情。你回来了。 [pc.name]有什么我可以为您做的吗？至少，这些事情是否在我能力范围之内，能否通过我现有的能力来帮助您呢？ 或许有一些话题你可以跟她探讨，以此更深入地了解过去的荒废驿堡以及这里发生的事情。或许可以让她重新讲述其中的一些章节，看看你是否有什么之前遗漏的地方。 请随时提问吧，想问多少次就问多少次——当一个人在这段漫长的时间里唯一的陪伴只有荒废驿堡老驻军那些精神失常的人时，确实会感到有些孤独。有些事情我无法或可能不愿意谈论，但我会尽力回答的。在这种状态下，我所能做的也就只有进行对话而已了……

At least, that falls within the reach of the chains I find myself bound by? There might be some topics that you'd like to pick her mind on to better understand the Wayfort as it was in the past and what happened here, perhaps have her retell some of the sections to see if there was anything you missed the first time around.
