There are some things that I cannot, or may not speak of, but I'll do my best. There's not much I can do in this state save hold a conversation..."

rows.original: That question is easy and difficult to answer. As the numbers of the dead mounted, one of the southern storerooms was converted into a makeshift morgue. It was the commander's hope that the dead could be afforded a proper funeral once the fighting eased, as opposed to mass graves or cremation... preserving bodies, at least for a while, was easy to do, so it was done. At the very least, it helped morale for what it was worth. If she would keep to the topic, please... Y-yes. The morgue that my subordinates set up is in the southern end of the Wayfort — you'll recognize it when you see it. That's the easy part. The difficult part is that there must be about a hundred bodies lying in repose, if not more, and all of them must be bones by now. Discovering which set of remains is mine is likely to be an impossible task without additional information. Thalia smiles ruefully. I'm afraid I wasn't alive to see exactly where my body was dragged after being pulverized by the impact. Nor, I must say, am I familiar with how my bones look — can't quite study them while they're in use. You see. So, theoretically, if this information were to be recorded somewhere in this Wayfort, where might it be? Thalia thinks a moment. The commander was responsible for creating reports to be sent back to Njorhaalt every month; the watchtower lookouts were also required to keep logs of their shifts. That lot were the only ones in the entire Wayfort who had any love or need of writing... if anyone wrote down what happened to me after my demise, then it'd have been either of them. The wayfort's archives were kept in the base of the watchtower, so you might want to start there. The watchtower, as well as any places that the commander might have frequented. Got it. By helping you, I'm also helping myself. Consider it a selfish motive, so thanks are not needed. Anything else?
rows.translation: 这个问题既容易回答，又难以回答。随着死亡人数的不断增加，南边的一个储藏室被临时改成了停尸房。指挥官希望，等到战斗缓和后，能够为这些死者举行适当的葬礼，而不是将他们埋进集体坟墓或进行火化……至少暂时保存这些尸体是可行的，所以人们就这么做了。至少，这样做在某种程度上有助于维护士气。 如果她能紧扣主题的话，那就太好了…… 是的。我的下属们设置的停尸房位于荒废驿堡城的南端——你看到它就能认出来。这部分工作还算简单。真正困难的是，那里应该有大约一百具尸体，甚至可能更多，而现在这些尸体都应该已经变成骨头了。如果没有额外的信息，要找出哪一组遗骸是属于我的，几乎是不可能完成的任务。塞莉亚无奈地笑了笑。恐怕我当时已经不在人世了，因此无法亲眼看到自己的身体在撞击中被粉碎后被拖到了哪里。同样，我也无法确定自己的骨头现在是什么样子——毕竟在它们还在发挥作用的时候，我根本无法仔细观察它们。 你看，从理论上讲，如果这些信息被记录在荒废驿堡的某个地方，那么它可能会被保存在哪里呢？ 塔莉娅思考了一会儿。这位指挥官负责每月编写报告并发送回Njorhaalt；而瞭望塔上的守卫们也必须记录下他们值班期间的情况。在整个荒废驿堡，只有这两个人真正懂得如何书写，也真正有写作的需求……如果有人记录下了我死后发生的事情，那肯定就是他们中的某一个。荒废驿堡的档案资料被保存在瞭望塔的基地里，所以你或许应该从那里开始查找。 瞭望塔，以及指挥官可能经常光顾的任何地方。明白了。 通过帮助你，我也在帮助自己。可以把这看作是一种自私的行为，所以不需要感谢。还有其他事情吗？

rows.original: Has she any idea where her body might be?
rows.translation: 她知道自己的尸体可能被丢在什么地方吗？
rows.raw: "Has she any idea where her body might be?"

rows.original: Thalia's expression becomes guarded. What exactly would you like to know? Well, more of their history, for one. What it was like back then. How this order of mage-hunters was founded, and where their unique physical forms came from. Is this relevant to our predicament at hand? Well, as an Astrida, she's the only mind left in this place that hasn't been utterly broken with the passage of... well, time doesn't have much meaning here, does it? Still, she understands what you mean. It is because of my acceptance of Nareva's teachings, and the transformation of my body through the infusion of her blessings of magic and knowledge that I have been able to keep myself together all this while. The reply is definitely curt, with a warning in there. It's not something that you can use to your advantage, I'm afraid. [pc.isGodsworn |The essence and teachings of your own deity should protect you, should that not be the case? |If we get out of here, perhaps you can pledge yourself to her cause should you be interested, but it's not something that should be discussed overmuch right now. ] All right, you understand. Moving on...
rows.translation: 塔莉娅的表情变得警惕起来。你究竟想了解些什么呢？ 首先，我们需要了解更多关于他们的历史。了解那段时期的情况，了解这个法师猎手组织是如何成立的，以及他们那些独特的身体形态是从何而来的。 这与我们目前面临的困境有关吗？ 嗯，作为一位阿斯特里达，她是这个地方上唯一一个没有在时间的流逝中彻底崩溃的精神。虽然在这里，时间本身并没有太大的意义，但她还是理解你的意思的。 正是因为我接受了娜瑞瓦的教诲，而且通过她赐予我的魔法与知识的力量，我的身体也发生了变化，因此我才能够一直保持自己的理智与稳定。这个回复确实很简短，其中还隐含着一种警告意味。恐怕，这并不能被你用来为自己谋利。 [pc.isGodsworn |你自己信仰的神灵的精髓与教义应该能够保护你，难道不是这样吗？ |如果我们能离开这里，或许如果你感兴趣的话，可以承诺支持她的事业，但现在还不是讨论这个问题的时候。 ] 好的，你明白我的意思了。继续吧……

Moving on..."

rows.original: Thalia smiles bitterly. As a member of our most divine order, shouldn't you know this already? The groundwork for our future was being laid out when I left Tychris — does the order not teach its own history? Yeah, about that... well, your membership was considerably expedited. Most Astrida are born and raised to the task for all of their childhood... you've been one for far less time, roped into the ranks during a crisis. Suffice to say that you haven't had the time to jump through the hoops and sit through lessons; [pc.bg scholar acolyte arcanist |while the prospect of academia in what's arguably the most secretive and elite of institutions is exciting, ]you were recruited for your ability to deal with the demon threat. So, a situation much like the one under which the Order was formed. Not as terrible as the Godswar, but still a threat. To be frank, prior to joining the Order Astrida and receiving the goddess' blessing, you've never met anyone who actually knows the details of the order's founding. Most people vaguely understand that they came into existence during the Godswar because that's when these things happened, but as far as the practical side of things is concerned they may as well have been around forever. It all happened with the Prince of Tychris, Telandros. When his children, the half-siblings Philander and Phyria, failed to return from a magical convocation Philander had arranged, the mages of Estelore whom his son had invited were the first suspects. That is, until Telandros received word that not only had the mages attending the convocation disappeared as well, but the entire island of Estelore itself was lost to some peril. Oh, and his son's pet jotun was also gone in the bargain. Of course, Philander hadn't earned the nickname Philander for nothing, and had deliberately neglected to tell his father where his grand Convocation of Mirrors was being held; retrieving his childrens' remains from their secret gathering was quite impossible even discounting the perils of the Godswar. That... does match up with what you know about the time period, yes. It was then that Nareva revealed herself to Telandros in his grief. Magic is not intrinsically evil, but there is much power in it, and power tends to attract a certain character of person. The mages of Estelore had brought the Godswar down upon the heads of people by calling in creatures from beyond, and that had taken his children from him. With the help of Telandros and his people, Nareva would build a grand order of scholars and knights to ensure that this would never happen again.
rows.translation: 塔莉娅苦涩地笑了。身为我们最神圣教团的一员，你难道不该早就知道这些吗？我离开提克里斯时，我们未来的根基已经开始铺设——教团难道不教授自己的历史？ 是啊，关于这件事……嗯，你的入会流程被大幅加快了。大多数阿斯特里达从小便为了这份职责出生、长大……你成为其中一员的时间短得多，是在危机中被拉入教团。简而言之，你根本没有时间跨过重重门槛、坐下来听课；[pc.bg scholar acolyte arcanist |虽然在这个堪称最神秘也最精英的机构里求学令人兴奋， ]但教团招募你，是为了你处理恶魔威胁的能力。 所以，与教团成立时的情况十分相似。 虽没有神战那么可怕，却仍是一场威胁。坦白地说，在加入阿斯特里达教团并得到女神赐福以前，你从未遇见真正了解教团创立细节的人。大多数人大概知道它诞生于神战期间，因为那正是这些事情发生的年代；但若论实际情况，它仿佛从古至今一直存在。 一切都始于提克里斯王子泰兰德罗斯。他的孩子——同父异母的菲兰德与菲莉亚——没有从菲兰德组织的魔法集会归来，于是受他儿子邀请而来的埃斯托洛尔法师首先受到怀疑。直到泰兰德罗斯收到消息：不仅出席集会的法师同样失踪，整个埃斯托洛尔岛也陷入某种灾难。哦，他儿子饲养的约顿也一并消失了。当然，菲兰德赢得“菲兰德”这个名号不是毫无缘由；他故意没有告诉父亲，盛大的镜像集会究竟在何处举行。即便不考虑神战的危险，想从秘密集会地点找回孩子们的遗骸也完全不可能。 这……确实与你了解的那个时代相符。 正是在那时，娜瑞瓦向悲痛的泰兰德罗斯显现。魔法本身并不邪恶，但其中蕴藏着巨大力量，而力量总会吸引某一类人。埃斯托洛尔的法师召来界外生物，使神战降临在人们头顶，也夺走了他的孩子。在泰兰德罗斯及其子民的帮助下，娜瑞瓦将建立一个由学者与骑士组成的伟大教团，确保这种事永不重演。

To be frank, prior to joining the Order Astrida and receiving the goddess' blessing, you've never met anyone who actually knows the details of the order's founding. Most people vaguely understand that they came into existence during the Godswar because that's when these things happened, but as far as the practical side of things is concerned they may as well have been around forever. It all happened with the Prince of Tychris, Telandros. When his children, the half-siblings Philander and Phyria, failed to return from a magical convocation Philander had arranged, the mages of Estelore whom his son had invited were the first suspects. That is, until Telandros received word that not only had the mages attending the convocation disappeared as well, but the entire island of Estelore itself was lost to some peril. Oh, and his son's pet jotun was also gone in the bargain. Of course, Philander hadn't earned the nickname Philander for nothing, and had deliberately neglected to tell his father where his grand Convocation of Mirrors was being held; retrieving his childrens' remains from their secret gathering was quite impossible even discounting the perils of the Godswar. That... does match up with what you know about the time period, yes. It was then that Nareva revealed herself to Telandros in his grief. Magic is not intrinsically evil, but there is much power in it, and power tends to attract a certain character of person. The mages of Estelore had brought the Godswar down upon the heads of people by calling in creatures from beyond, and that had taken his children from him. With the help of Telandros and his people, Nareva would build a grand order of scholars and knights to ensure that this would never happen again."

rows.original: No doubt Prince Telandros agreed, because the two of you are here right now. A wisp of a smile plays over Thalia's ethereal features. Much of my memory has been eroded by this place, but these recollections are inviolate. The first candidates were drawn from Philander' understudies and the remnants of Phyria's personal command. All of us were given the offer of the goddess' blessing, her essence, her power, at a potentially terrible and unknown cost. Since it was untested, we could not be sure that the process to infuse our bodies with the goddess' essence and the resultant transformations would be wholly safe or precise. Risks were involved. Despite that, everyone volunteered to form the first generation of the Order Astrida. Was she with Philander or Phyria? The latter. I remember that day... the prince himself, getting up in years, abdicated the throne to his nephew. He was insistent on being the first to receive the goddess' essence, refusing to subject anyone else to anything he wasn't willing to experience himself. That's what happened to you, too. Astrida these days are born, but you were changed — the first in a while, if you're not wrong. Divine power the world had never seen before, at a potentially great price. What a choice... but in truth, there was none. Who amongst us would say no? Thalia raises her heavy, clawed hands. I got off lightly — losing my fingers and thumbs and having to relearn all of the simplest tasks from holding a spoon, to not accidentally tearing apart everything I touched was a small price to pay in the scheme of things. No one outright perished as a result of the transformations thanks to the goddess' oversight, but people paid terribly to be a part of the goddess' new militant order. We all knew the unknowns, we all volunteered freely, and even so... blindness. Irregular heartbeats. Twisted limbs. Misaligned organs and more, all because the need was great. We loved her, we did it all for her, and we'd do it again unquestioningly. Even though you understand the situation was different with the Godswar raging on, it's hard to imagine your average Astrida these days bursting with so much fanatical zeal. Has the passing of centuries really turned the order more practical, to put it kindly, or jaded if one would rather be blunt about it? Out of curiosity, what price did Prince Telandros pay for Nareva's divine powers? Tumors. ...Gods.
rows.translation: 毫无疑问，泰兰德罗斯王子也是同意的，因为你们俩现在就在这里。 塔莉娅那如精灵般美丽的面容上浮现出一丝微笑。这个地方已经侵蚀了我大部分的记忆，但这些回忆却依然完好无损。最初的候选人是从菲兰德的副手部们以及菲莉亚原来的亲信中挑选出来的。我们所有人都被赋予了女神的祝福、她的力量与本质，但为此可能需要付出极其可怕且未知的代价。由于这一过程尚未经过测试，我们无法确定将女神的力量注入我们的身体以及由此带来的变化是否完全安全或准确。其中确实存在风险。尽管如此，所有人都自愿成为了“阿斯特里达秩序”的第一代成员。 她是和菲兰德在一起，还是和菲莉亚在一起呢？ 后者。我记得那天……那位年事已高的王子主动放弃了王位，将王位传给了他的侄子。他坚决要求自己第一个获得女神的力量，拒绝让任何人经历他自己都不愿意尝试的事情。 你也是这样。这些天，阿斯特丽达这类人不断出现，但你的情况却发生了变化——如果我没弄错的话，你是最近第一个遇到这种变化的。 这种神力是世间前所未见的，但代价可能也非常巨大。这真是一个艰难的选择……但实际上，我们根本没有其他选择。在我们当中，有谁会拒绝呢？塞莉亚举起了她那双布满爪子的重型双手。我的遭遇还算轻微的——失去手指和拇指，以及不得不重新学习从握勺子这样的最基本动作，再到避免不小心弄坏自己触碰的任何东西，这些在整体来看都算是微不足道的代价。多亏了女神的庇护，没有人会因此而直接丧命，但那些选择加入女神新建立的军事组织的人，却付出了重型的代价。我们都知道其中隐藏着未知的风险，但所有人都是自愿加入的。即便如此，后果依然令人痛心。失明、心律不齐、肢体扭曲、内脏错位……这一切都是因为需求太过迫切。我们爱她，我们做这一切都是为了她，而且我们会毫不犹豫地再次这么做。 尽管你明白在“神战”爆发期间，情况确实有所不同，但如今很难想象普通的阿斯特里达会展现出如此狂热的热情。几个世纪的发展，究竟是让这个组织变得更加务实了——用委婉的说法——还是说，如果直截了当地说，它反而变得变得麻木不仁了呢？ 出于好奇，坦德罗斯王子究竟付出了什么代价，才得到了娜瑞瓦的神圣力量呢？ 肿瘤。 ……天啊。

rows.original: Virulent tumors in his body that resisted all suppression. In spite of the palace physicians' best efforts, he was given three years to live at most. He was the first and took as much of the goddess' essence into himself as he could — no, more than he could contain. The power he wielded as an Astrida was immense, but it burned his life like a candle from both ends. Do not look so aggrieved, [pc.name]. The prince was a dead man walking after the deaths of Philander and Phyria; if not for the existential danger to Tychris, he might have given up before then. As it turned out, the perils of the Godswar killed him before the tumors did, but not before he had achieved much in Nareva's name. It was... it was but two weeks before I left to reinforce Njorhaalt. Why do I suddenly remember that? Despite the knowledge that Nareva's had centuries more to perfect the process, the nightmares still creep in; before you manage to catch yourself, your hands have unconsciously wondered over to your [pc.chest] and [pc.belly], wondering if there's something horrible within you that's just waiting to malfunction or burst or — No. This place is made of nightmares, it's what's speaking, not you. But... now you understand why new Astrida are born these days, as opposed to being directly reshaped like you were. Even if she can do it perfectly well, there're just too many bad memories attached to a people she loved. I think that suffices for a brief history of our order's origins, [pc.name]. Is there something else you'd like to discuss?
rows.translation: 他体内的恶性肿瘤对任何抑制手段都表现出强烈的抗性。尽管宫廷御医们竭尽全力，他也最多只能再活三年。他是第一个将女神的力量尽可能多地吸收到自己体内的人——不，其实是吸收了远超他身体所能承受的量。作为阿斯特里达，他所拥有的力量确实强大无比，但这种力量却像蜡烛一样，从两端同时燃烧着他的生命。 别摆出那么委屈的表情来。 [pc.name]在菲兰德和菲莉亚去世后，这位王子简直就是活死人一般；如果不是因为提克里斯面临的生存危机，他可能早就放弃了。事实上，正是这场神战带来的危险在肿瘤杀死他之前就夺去了他的生命，但在此之前，他确实为娜瑞瓦的事业做出了许多贡献。啊……就在我离开去支援Njorhaalt之前的两周……为什么我突然想起了这件事呢？ 尽管知道娜瑞瓦家族还有几个世纪的时间来完善这一工艺，但这些噩梦依然会不时浮现；在你意识到之前，你的双手就已经不自觉地伸了过去[pc.chest]以及[pc.belly]我在想，你是否内心藏着什么可怕的东西，只是等待着出故障、爆发出来…… 不。这个地方本身就充满了噩梦，是这些噩梦在说话，而不是你。但是……现在你明白为什么新的阿斯特丽达会出生这些天，与你们当初被直接改造成现在的样子不同。即使她能够把这件事做得非常完美，但对于一个她曾经深爱过的人来说，其中还是伴随着太多痛苦的回忆。 我认为，这些已经足以简要介绍我们这个组织的起源了。 [pc.name]还有其他你想讨论的事情吗？

rows.original: Can she tell you more about the first generation of the Order Astrida?
rows.translation: 她能告诉你更多关于阿斯特里达教团第一代的事情吗？
rows.raw: "Can she tell you more about the first generation of the Order Astrida?"

rows.original: Thalia frowns, thinking; you wonder what gaps in her memory she's trying to put together. At last, though, she speaks: It was about eighteen months since the order's founding, I believe. We'd beaten back several incursions into the lands surrounding Tychris and attempts upon the city itself, and news of the order of salamanders bearing the goddess' blessing had begun to spread beyond our city-state. We received word that the Belharans led by Victor Reverra in Hawkethorne were facing the prospect of being overrun, and the Wayfort was next in line. Given our order's mission, fighting the wraiths and their mages wherever we found them, the boreal elf queen — I don't remember her name — appealed to us for any help we could send. Prince Telandros — well, he hadn't been prince for more than a year at that time, his nephew was — had recently perished in order to secure Tychris from the wraiths. I... I wanted to get away from all the mourning, so I volunteered to lead several of Tychris' finest to lend what aid we could. There weren't many of us — less than a dozen — but there didn't need to be, already talk was running loose than one Astrida was worth several dozen mundane troops. And how true was that gossip? [pc.swornGod nareva |Thalia sighs wistfully, a haunting note in this ruined hall. "Are our kind really so common in your time to be considered unworthy of note, [pc.name]? Ah, but I jest |A little overblown, but I'd like to think it was mostly true ]. At the time we, and we alone, actually had the capability to harm more than the simplest flesh-and-blood thralls the wraiths commanded. The boreal elf queen's missive indicated that she was up to something along the same lines with Lumia, but I never found out what it was. [pc.swornGod lumia |If by that she means valkyries, there's one standing in front of her right now. I see. Something similar to us Astrida, then, but aligned with your own goddess. Certainly the aesthetics match what one would expect of the goddess of the sun. ] You see. Well, it does match up with what you know. The Wayfort used to mark the border of boreal elf lands with Belharan territory to the south. Things must've gotten pretty desperate for them to ask for external help. Everyone was desperate in those times, [pc.name]. When I arrived at this place there wasn't just the garrison of boreal elves to be had; there were several Belharans who'd been fleeing northward instead of joining the apparently doomed Hawkethorne, even a couple minotaur legionnaires who'd gotten separated from their own and were planning to build a rowboat to try head downriver and home. The elves were quite accommodating, given that Njorhaalt had problems of its own. Muscle was muscle. I'd like to think that I made a good impression on them before the end. I'd ask, but the shattered and insane remnants of their selves who wander the halls aren't up to much in the way of conversation.
rows.translation: 塔莉娅皱着眉头思考着，不知道她正在努力填补自己记忆中的哪些空白。最终，她还是开口说道： 我想，从该组织成立的那一刻起，已经过去了大约十八个月。我们成功击退了多次针对蒂克里斯周边地区的入侵，也挫败了那些针对这座城市的进攻。而关于这个受到女神庇佑的蝾螈组织的好消息，也开始在我们这个城邦之外传播开来。我们得到消息，由维克托·雷维拉领导的贝尔哈兰人在鹰棘镇正面临被敌人攻陷的危险，而荒废驿堡也紧随其后。考虑到我们这支队伍的任务——无论在何处遇到那些幽灵及其法师，都必须予以打击——那位极北精灵女王（我记不起她的名字了）恳请我们能提供任何可能的帮助。 泰兰德罗斯王子——其实那时他称得上王子已经有一年多了，他的侄子为了保护提克里斯免受那些幽灵的侵害，刚刚牺牲了。我……我想远离这一切哀伤，所以主动提出带领提克里斯手下的几名精英，尽我们所能提供帮助。我们的人数并不多，还不到十几人，但这也足够了。因为据说，一个阿斯特丽达的力量，相当于几十名普通士兵的力量。 而那些流言蜚语，又有多少是真实的呢？ [pc.swornGod nareva |塞莉亚黯然叹息，这一声叹息在这座破败的大厅中回荡着。“在我们的时代，我们这样的种族真的如此常见，以至于根本不值得被重视吗？ [pc.name]啊，不过我只是在开玩笑而已。 |有点言过其实了，但我也愿意相信其中大部分内容都是真实的。 ]在那个时候，只有我们才真正拥有能力，去伤害那些被怨灵控制的、最普通的血肉奴仆之外的目标。极北精灵女王的信中提到，她也在与卢米娅一起策划着类似的行动，但我始终没有弄清楚具体是什么。 [pc.swornGod lumia |如果她指的是女武神，那么现在就有一位女武神站在她面前。 我明白了。那么，这应该和我们的阿斯特里达类似，只不过是与你们自己的女神相呼应的。当然，其外观设计也完全符合人们对太阳女神的期待。 ] 你看，这确实与你所知道的相符。过去，荒废驿堡人总是用贝尔哈兰领土来标记极北精灵领地的边界。他们之所以会寻求外部帮助，肯定是情况已经变得非常危急了。 在那些日子里，每个人都陷入了绝望。 [pc.name]当我来到这个地方时，那里不仅有极北精灵的驻军，还有几名原本应该加入似乎注定失败的鹰棘镇军队的贝拉尔人，他们选择了向北方逃亡；甚至还有几名与自己的部队走散了的小弥诺陶洛斯军团士兵，他们打算划船顺流而下，回家去。考虑到Njorhaalt自己也面临着一些问题，这些精灵们表现得相当通情达理。毕竟，力量就是力量。 我希望在事情结束之前，我给他们留下了良好的印象。不过，那些已经支离破碎、精神错乱的自我残余，那些在走廊里游荡的灵魂，其实根本无法进行什么有效的对话。

rows.original: How did a delegation from Tychris come to be at the Wayfort?
rows.translation: 提克里斯的一个代表团是如何出现在荒废驿堡的？
rows.raw: "How did a delegation from Tychris come to be at the Wayfort?"

rows.original: I don't know, and not just because I can't remember the events that immediately led up to me ending up here; I've had a long time to think about it, but without evidence all I have is conjecture. Nevertheless, your news that the Wayfort still exists back in Savarra and that you've taken up residence there has given me reason to rethink my assumptions. I used to think that the material aspect of the Wayfort had been warped into the Ways after the fashion of the Estelorean mages building holdings in our dreams, but that clearly is wrong. What's her new theory, then? Well... [pc.bg scholar acolyte |There, there. As someone who's dabbled in academia you're well acquainted with hesitance to forward a theory for fear of being wrong, but no one's going to judge her. |No need to be shy about it. What's the worst that could happen? She's wrong? ] This Wayfort isn't material, but still very real in the sense that it's made up of what the garrison remembered it as. It's what our collective memories are... it wasn't like this when I was first here. I think. I thought the place was physically falling apart as an eternity stretched on, but now that I know there's still a wayfort back on Savarra, I can only guess that the deterioration is of a different nature. You nod and motion for Thalia to continue. The spirits, these broken memories who have free run of the halls — they used to be more coherent, some of them even sane. But as their selves have fragmented and the power that resides in this place grows ever stronger, this Wayfort is remade into something that's less suited to the former and more suited to the latter. If allowed to continue, the original memories and selves will fall apart completely, and who knows what will have taken shape then? "Yeah, man. That's pretty much what I figured, man." Nina reaches for a drink from her stash, finds none, then sighs and rubs her face. "Like, this place isn't real real, but um, it's still real where it matters. It's all in your head, man, and that makes it even more dangerous than it would be otherwise, because what's sloshing about in that brain-soup of ours? That's potentially limitless in the nightmares we can have." You still need to think it over a bit, but the theory doesn't sound too off. You've already spotted several discrepancies between the Wayfort as you know it and the Wayfort past — discrepancies that simple deterioration can't explain, but haywire memories can. That, and the utterly chaotic mazes that should have been simple hallways are also no doubt a product of the growing entropy as this place falls into chaos. Whatever the reason, this place is unstable; eventually, it will be nothing but the dust of memories, absorbed into the void that lies beyond the Ways and the creatures that exist there. Which is why I am so desperate to leave... and it is to be your fate should you fall here, too. A sour note on which to end a topic, to be sure, but a honest one. Is there something else you need to know?
rows.translation: 我也不清楚，不仅仅是因为我记不起那些直接导致我来到这里的事情；我已经有很长时间来思考这个问题了，但如果没有证据，我所能做的也只是猜测而已。不过，你告诉我的那个消息——荒废驿堡仍然存在于萨瓦拉，而且你已经在那里定居了——这让我有理由重新审视我之前的假设。我曾经以为，荒废驿堡的物质形态在经历了类似埃斯托洛尔人法师们在我们的梦境中建立据点的那种过程之后，就已经发生了变化，变成了那些“Ways”了，但显然这种想法是错误的。 那么，她的新理论是什么呢？ 嗯…… [pc.bg scholar acolyte |别担心，别担心。作为一个曾经涉足学术研究的人，你应该很清楚那种因为害怕犯错而不敢提出理论的心理吧？不过没人会评判她的。 |没必要为此感到羞愧。最坏的结果又能怎样？她错了而已，不是吗？ ] 这个传送站本身并没有实体存在，但它确实非常真实——因为它是由驻军们对它的记忆构成的。这就是我们共同的记忆……我第一次来到这里的时候，这个地方并不是这样的。我原以为随着时间的流逝，它的物理结构会逐渐毁坏，但现在我知道在萨瓦拉上仍然存在另一个传送站，所以我只能推测，这种破坏其实属于另一种性质。 你点了点头，示意塔莉娅继续说下去。 那些幽灵，那些在走廊中肆意游荡的破碎记忆——它们曾经更加连贯，其中一些甚至还算理智。但随着这些记忆与自我的逐渐破碎，而这个地方所蕴含的力量却日益增强，这个“荒废驿堡”已经变成了一个不再适合那些原始记忆与自我存在的地方。如果让这种趋势继续下去，那些最初的记忆与自我将会彻底消失，而到时候，又会形成什么呢？ 是啊，兄弟。我差不多也是这么想的。”妮娜伸手去拿自己的储藏物，却发现什么都没有，于是叹了口气，揉了揉脸。“说真的，这个地方真的不太真实的确实如此，但嗯，在关键问题上，它依然是真实的。这一切都只存在于你的脑海中，而这就使得它比实际情况更加危险，因为在我们的大脑中究竟在酝酿着什么呢？这些想法可能会让我们陷入无边无际的噩梦之中。你还需要再仔细考虑一下，不过这个理论听起来倒也不太荒谬。你已经发现，你现在所认知的荒废驿堡与过去的荒废驿堡之间存在一些差异——这些差异无法用单纯的退化来解释，但混乱的记忆却可以说明这些差异的存在。除此之外，那些本该是简单走廊的地方却变成了混乱不堪的迷宫，这一切无疑也是这个地方逐渐陷入混乱、熵值不断增加的结果。 无论出于什么原因，这个地方都是不稳定的；最终，它只会变成记忆的尘埃，被吸收进那些存在于“道路”之外的虚无之中，以及那里存在的生物们之中。正因为如此，我才如此迫切地想要离开……而如果你也在这里坠落，同样的命运也会降临到你身上。 虽然这个结尾有点扫兴，但至少是诚实的。还有其他你需要了解的事情吗？
rows.raw: " I don't know, and not just because I can't remember the events that immediately led up to me ending up here; I've had a long time to think about it, but without evidence all I have is conjecture. Nevertheless, your news that the Wayfort still exists back in Savarra and that you've taken up residence there has given me reason to rethink my assumptions. I used to think that the material aspect of the Wayfort had been warped into the Ways after the fashion of the Estelorean mages building holdings in our dreams, but that clearly is wrong. What's her new theory, then? Well... [pc.bg scholar acolyte |There, there. As someone who's dabbled in academia you're well acquainted with hesitance to forward a theory for fear of being wrong, but no one's going to judge her. |No need to be shy about it. What's the worst that could happen? She's wrong? ] This Wayfort isn't material, but still very real in the sense that it's made up of what the garrison remembered it as. It's what our collective memories are... it wasn't like this when I was first here. I think. I thought the place was physically falling apart as an eternity stretched on, but now that I know there's still a wayfort back on Savarra, I can only guess that the deterioration is of a different nature. You nod and motion for Thalia to continue. The spirits, these broken memories who have free run of the halls — they used to be more coherent, some of them even sane. But as their selves have fragmented and the power that resides in this place grows ever stronger, this Wayfort is remade into something that's less suited to the former and more suited to the latter. If allowed to continue, the original memories and selves will fall apart completely, and who knows what will have taken shape then? "Yeah, man. That's pretty much what I figured, man." Nina reaches for a drink from her stash, finds none, then sighs and rubs her face. "Like, this place isn't real real, but um, it's still real where it matters. It's all in your head, man, and that makes it even more dangerous than it would be otherwise, because what's sloshing about in that brain-soup of ours? That's potentially limitless in the nightmares we can have." You still need to think it over a bit, but the theory doesn't sound too off. You've already spotted several discrepancies between the Wayfort as you know it and the Wayfort past — discrepancies that simple deterioration can't explain, but haywire memories can. That, and the utterly chaotic mazes that should have been simple hallways are also no doubt a product of the growing entropy as this place falls into chaos. Whatever the reason, this place is unstable; eventually, it will be nothing but the dust of memories, absorbed into the void that lies beyond the Ways and the creatures that exist there. Which is why I am so desperate to leave... and it is to be your fate should you fall here, too. A sour note on which to end a topic, to be sure, but a honest one. Is there something else you need to know?"

rows.original: Just... what happened to the Wayfort?
rows.translation: 只是……荒废驿堡号到底发生了什么？

rows.original: [var0 |I don't think there's much left to say, Thalia replies, regarding you with a smile. I could feel it from the throne room from here — if nothing else, you've bought us all more time. There is still something left of the old garrison in the shattered spirits, and you were able to bring it out in them long enough for them to recognize you on the throne. [pc.swornGod nareva |Truth be told, you're not entirely sure that you did it all by yourself. A lot of the spirits' reverence came from the fact that you were an Astrida — you were simply building upon the foundation which Thalia had laid. Without her actions making such an impression on the garrison back in the day, you doubt that you'd have had as hearty a welcome as you did. |It's a little embarrassing being adored like that, but you have to admit that it felt really, really good. If they recognized you, then you deserved it. There isn't enough left of their selves to be deceitful, for better or for worse. Enjoy your laurels, [pc.name], just don't rest on them. Oh, not to worry. You haven't forgotten the mortal peril that Nina and you are currently entrapped in, and being [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of a crumbling Wayfort trapped in the Ways is not in your long-term plans. ] Well. Now that most of the garrison acknowledges you as their ruler, they should not harass you any further; they're simple creatures like that. There might be a few who are more unhinged and might not have received the message, or if you do something to anger them it might still trigger their instincts, but otherwise you should have the run of the Wayfort unimpeded. Good work on that. Aww, now she's really laying it on thickly. The wayfort's old commander is not here with her garrison, so she must have survived the meteorite's devastation; who knows what happened afterwards? But that's all dust now — who better to fill her shoes than the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort's future? |They rejected you, Thalia replies flatly. Don't take it too hard — most of them are not themselves any longer. Yes, you understand that. Even so... there's that nagging doubt in the back of your mind as to whether you're fit to be ruler of the Wayfort. [pc.bgMulti noblescion slumrat scholar |You may have the lineage, perhaps, but you were always the spare's spare. That's why you were allowed to leave to seek your fortune in the first place; no one would have cared if you simply vanished and saved your house the trouble of arranging some kind of vocation for you down the line. Maybe if you'd been trained better, had a few more chances to show yourself, had more lessons in exerting your presence, you might've gotten through to the garrison. If the Wayfort garrison of old feels that you're not worth respecting, how many in the garrison of today thinks similarly, even though it would never be said to your face? |If someone had ever told you, street rat that you were, that you would own property, let alone rule, you'd have laughed, cried and cursed all at once. Even after the impossible has happened, the feeling that you're not good enough still surfaces from time to time... Maybe the saying is true: you can take the rat out of the slums, but you can't take the slums out of the rat. Broken and half mad, the spirits of the old garrison weren't capable of deceit, so they simply acted as they felt. A damning judgement, if there was one. |A life in academia — well, you were never high enough in the pecking order to exert any kind of leadership over your fellow bookworms and eggheads, and even if you were that kind of cat-corralling is vastly different from gaining the respect of a garrison. Broken and half mad, the spirits of the old garrison weren't capable of deceit, so they simply acted as they felt; the brutal honesty just makes it worse. You'd like to think that you've proven yourself enough times over, but while valor and skill in combat is part of it, there's clearly still more to getting the respect of a bunch of dead outriders. |Before you came to this part of the Marches, you were just a [pc.background] — hardly of special note in the scheme of things. And even though you ought to have proven yourself plenty times over, there's a difference between skill in arms and ruling a wayfort. Are you really qualified for this? ] Please, [pc.name]. I would urge you to not dwell upon it too much. You're here, you've come this far, and this is not the time to doubt yourself. Like I said, I really would not put too much weight on the opinions of a bunch of fragmented memories. Isn't that what she is? Should you ignore her, then? While I've kept better than most, I don't claim to be wholly myself at this point. That being said, I would really rather you not join me in my predicament, and I'm sure you and your harpy friend agree. All that being said, since the garrison refuses to acknowledge you as [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort, I'm afraid you'll have to continue contending with them. Once, I might have asked you to be merciful... but now they are beyond even pain. Do what you need to. |The garrison are not what they used to be, that much is obvious, Thalia says with a sigh. It's what will happen to me, too, given long enough. It's also what will happen to you and your harpy friend should you fall here. You figured as much — the spirits are so fragmented that even their manifestations are missing parts of themselves. That being said, that doesn't stop them from being a nuisance while you're trying to make your way through the Wayfort, nipping at your heels especially in the more chaotic sections. Hmm, I'm not sure. It would take a pretty big impetus, something extremely meaningful to them as a whole in order to get through their fugue state to begin with. Anything at all would be helpful. They just keep coming out of the walls, and constantly keeping them off you is starting to get tiring. Hmm. Anything come to mind? There is one thing. You said that you are the ruler of the Wayfort in your time? The commander of the garrison? Well, what you have in your Wayfort may or may not be called a garrison, but you've taken up residence there and call it yours, yes. So far, no one has contested your claim, [flags.WAYFORT_OFFER 1 2|especially since it was granted to you by Njorhaalt, ]so there's that. The old commander must have survived the meteorite's impact — either that, or her sundered spirit hasn't passed through the grand hall or throne room once in all these aeons, which I strongly doubt. The throne is open, but it still possesses much of its symbolic power to the garrison; I would wager that it has much meaning to it. The throne? Power? You glance across the hall and through the open doors into the distant throne room — as far as you can tell, it's just a mundane throne. You can't see it? No. Feel, perhaps? No... "I can," Nina pipes up. "It's like, a bunch of fuzz about the throne, man. Like thick fog or cotton wool, that kinda stuff. Looks like it'd pretty comfortable if you could sit in it." Maybe it'll become more evident when you get closer, or perhaps you need external aid to be able to perceive it. But dreams and memories are what the garrison and this Wayfort are made of, and so they have much power here. If you manage to find a way to tap into the throne's power, you could attempt to impose your will upon what remains of the garrison, convince them that you belong here as their [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. That should put a stop to them. That sounds like a pretty tall order, but if it's the only idea Thalia can come up with then you'll keep it in mind. Feel free to try any other ideas you think will work; I certainly am not an exhaustive authority on the matter. Is there anything else I can help you with? ]
rows.translation: [var0 |我想没什么好说的了。塞莉亚微笑着回答，目光中充满了对你的关注。从这里，我就能从王座厅感受到那种气息——至少，你为我们争取到了更多的时间。在那些破碎的精神中，仍然残存着一些昔日的驻军力量，而你成功地将它们唤醒，让它们有足够的时间来认出你坐在王座上的身影。 [pc.swornGod nareva |说实话，你并不完全确定这一切都是自己独自完成的。那些精灵们的尊敬，很大程度上是因为你身为阿斯特里达——你只是在塔莉娅所打下的基础上继续前进而已。如果她当初没有在驻军中留下如此深刻的印象，你怀疑自己是否能够获得如今这样的热烈欢迎。 |被那样崇拜确实有点尴尬，但你必须承认，这种感觉真的非常、非常美好。 如果他们认出了你，那么你确实当之无愧。他们已经没有足够的自我去欺骗别人了，无论是出于好意还是恶意。好好享受你的荣耀吧。 [pc.name]，只要别把它们当成依靠就行了。 哦，别担心。你肯定没有忘记尼娜和你目前所面临的致命危险，对吧？ [pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]一个逐渐崩溃的、被困在那些通道中的荒废驿堡，并不在你的长期计划之中。 ] 嗯，既然驻军中的大多数人都承认你是他们的统治者，他们应该不会再骚扰你了——他们就是这样的简单生物。可能还会有一些人思想比较偏激，或者没有收到这个消息；另外，如果你做了什么让他们生气的事情，他们的本能反应仍可能会发作，但除此之外，你应该可以毫无阻碍地在荒废驿堡地区自由行动了。干得不错。 哎呀，现在她真是做得太过了。 韦弗堡的那位老指挥官并没有带着她的部队来到这里，所以她肯定是在那场陨石灾难中幸存了下来；但之后发生了什么，谁又知道呢？不过，这一切都已经成为过去式了——还有谁比身为驿堡未来[pc.mf |领主 |女领主 ]的你更适合接替她呢？ |他们拒绝了你。塞莉亚冷淡地回答道。别太往心里去——他们中的大多数已经不再是原来的他们了。 是的，你明白这一点。即便如此……你内心深处仍然会萦绕着一个疑问：自己是否真的有资格成为荒废驿堡的统治者。 [pc.bgMulti noblescion slumrat scholar |你或许拥有那血脉传承，但实际上你从来都是那个被舍弃的人。正因如此，你才被允许离开去寻找属于自己的命运；如果你干脆消失不见，反而会省去大家日后为你安排某种职业的麻烦。 也许，如果你接受过更好的训练，有更多机会展示自己的能力，也学过如何更好地展现自己的存在感，你或许就能进入驻军行列了。如果过去的荒废驿堡驻军认为你不值得被尊重，那么如今的驻军中，又有多少人会持有同样的看法呢？尽管他们永远不会当面这么说吧？ |如果有人曾经告诉你，像你这样一个街头混混，竟然也会拥有自己的财产，更不用说还能掌权了，你肯定会又笑又哭，还会破口大骂。即使那些看似不可能的事情真的发生了，那种“自己还不够好”的感觉仍然会时不时地浮现出来。也许这句话是真的：你可以把老鼠从贫民窟里赶出去，但却无法消除贫民窟本身。那些古老驻军的灵魂已经支离破碎、近乎疯狂，他们已经没有了欺骗他人的能力，所以只能按照自己的内心感受去行动。如果非得用一个词来形容的话，那就是“毁灭性的评价”。 |在学术界的生活啊——说实话，你的地位从来都不高，根本不可能对那些同样热衷于读书和研究的同僚们发挥任何领导作用。而且，即便你真的具备这种能力，这种领导方式也与赢得他人的尊重是完全不同的。 这些古老驻军的灵魂早已支离破碎、近乎疯狂，他们根本无法伪装自己的真实情感，所以就只能按照自己的内心感受去行动；这种赤裸裸的诚实反而让情况更加糟糕。你可能会认为自己已经多次证明了自己的价值，但尽管勇气和战斗技巧确实是其中的重要因素，然而要想赢得这些早已死去的游骑兵们的尊重，显然还有其他更多的条件。 |在你来到这片边境地区之前，你只不过是一个[pc.background] — 在整个大局来看，这其实并没有什么特别的意义。虽然你早就应该证明自己的能力了，但掌握武艺与管理一个商队之间，还是存在着很大的区别的。 你真的有资格担任这个职务吗？ ] 请， [pc.name]我建议你不要过分纠结于此。你已经来到了这里，已经走了这么远，现在不是怀疑自己的时候。就像我之前说的，我真的不认为那些零散的记忆所代表的意见有什么分量。 她不就是这样的吗？那么，你应该忽略她才对吧？ 虽然我比大多数人表现得都要好，但我也必须承认，目前我并没有完全做回自己。因此，我真心希望你们不要加入我的困境中，我相信你和你的那位“泼妇”朋友也会同意我的看法。 话虽如此，但由于驻军拒绝承认你的存在[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]对于韦弗特家族的人，恐怕你还得继续与他们作对。从前，我或许会请求你手下留情……但现在，他们已经连痛苦都感受不到了。你想怎么做就怎么做吧。 |很明显，现在的驻军已经不复从前了。塞莉亚叹了口气说道。如果时间足够长，同样的事情也会发生在我身上。如果你也掉到这里，你和你的那位“女妖朋友”也会遭遇同样的命运。 你早就猜到了——那些灵魂已经分裂得如此严重，以至于它们的显现形态也缺少了原本的一部分。不过，这并不会阻止它们在你试图穿越荒废驿堡通道时给你带来麻烦，尤其是在那些更加混乱的区域，它们会不断缠住你。 嗯，我不太确定。要想让他们摆脱这种恍惚状态，需要某种巨大的推动力，某种对他们整个群体来说具有极其重要意义的因素才行。 任何帮助都是可行的。那些东西不断地从四面八方出现，要想一直阻止它们攻击你，真的开始让人感到疲惫了。 嗯。 有什么想法吗？ 有一件事。你说过，在你那个时代，你是荒废驿堡的统治者，是驻军的指挥官，对吧？ 嗯，你在荒废驿堡建立的那个据点，或许可以被称为驻军基地，或许也不能；但你自己已经在那里安了家，并且认为那是属于你的地方，没错。到目前为止，还没有人对你的这种主张提出异议。 [flags.WAYFORT_OFFER 1 2|尤其是因为这是由Njorhaalt赐予你的。 ]就是这样。 那位老指挥官肯定在陨石撞击中幸存了下来——要么就是她的灵魂在漫长的岁月里从未穿过那座宏伟的大厅或王座室，而我对此表示强烈怀疑。王座虽然空缺，但它对驻军来说依然拥有巨大的象征意义；我敢打赌，这对他们来说肯定意义重大。 王座？权力？你望向大厅的对面，透过敞开的门望去，远处的王座室里——就你所能看到的，那只是一个普通的王座而已。 你看不见吗？ 不。 或许，你能感受到吧？ 我可以，”妮娜抢着说，“就是那种覆盖在王座上的绒毛，就像浓雾或者棉花糖一样。看起来坐在上面应该会很舒服吧。 也许当你靠近时，这些现象会变得更加明显；又或许你需要外界的帮助才能察觉到它们。但梦想与记忆，正是这座要塞以及这个荒废驿堡的根基，因此它们在这里拥有巨大的力量。如果你能找到某种方法来利用王座的能量，或许就能迫使剩下的守军接受你的意志，让他们相信你才是属于这里的人。 [pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]那样应该就能阻止他们了。 这听起来要求相当高，但如果这是塔莉娅能想出的唯一办法，那你还是可以考虑一下吧。 你可以随时尝试任何你认为可行的其他方法；我当然也不是这个领域的权威专家。还有其他什么事情需要我帮忙的吗？ ]

If they recognized you, then you deserved it. There isn't enough left of their selves to be deceitful, for better or for worse. Enjoy your laurels, [pc.name], just don't rest on them. Oh, not to worry. You haven't forgotten the mortal peril that Nina and you are currently entrapped in, and being [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of a crumbling Wayfort trapped in the Ways is not in your long-term plans. ] Well. Now that most of the garrison acknowledges you as their ruler, they should not harass you any further; they're simple creatures like that. There might be a few who are more unhinged and might not have received the message, or if you do something to anger them it might still trigger their instincts, but otherwise you should have the run of the Wayfort unimpeded. Good work on that. Aww, now she's really laying it on thickly. The wayfort's old commander is not here with her garrison, so she must have survived the meteorite's devastation; who knows what happened afterwards? But that's all dust now — who better to fill her shoes than the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort's future? |They rejected you, Thalia replies flatly. Don't take it too hard — most of them are not themselves any longer. Yes, you understand that. Even so... there's that nagging doubt in the back of your mind as to whether you're fit to be ruler of the Wayfort. [pc.bgMulti noblescion slumrat scholar |You may have the lineage, perhaps, but you were always the spare's spare. That's why you were allowed to leave to seek your fortune in the first place; no one would have cared if you simply vanished and saved your house the trouble of arranging some kind of vocation for you down the line. Maybe if you'd been trained better, had a few more chances to show yourself, had more lessons in exerting your presence, you might've gotten through to the garrison. If the Wayfort garrison of old feels that you're not worth respecting, how many in the garrison of today thinks similarly, even though it would never be said to your face? |If someone had ever told you, street rat that you were, that you would own property, let alone rule, you'd have laughed, cried and cursed all at once. Even after the impossible has happened, the feeling that you're not good enough still surfaces from time to time... Maybe the saying is true: you can take the rat out of the slums, but you can't take the slums out of the rat. Broken and half mad, the spirits of the old garrison weren't capable of deceit, so they simply acted as they felt. A damning judgement, if there was one. |A life in academia — well, you were never high enough in the pecking order to exert any kind of leadership over your fellow bookworms and eggheads, and even if you were that kind of cat-corralling is vastly different from gaining the respect of a garrison. Broken and half mad, the spirits of the old garrison weren't capable of deceit, so they simply acted as they felt; the brutal honesty just makes it worse. You'd like to think that you've proven yourself enough times over, but while valor and skill in combat is part of it, there's clearly still more to getting the respect of a bunch of dead outriders. |Before you came to this part of the Marches, you were just a [pc.background] — hardly of special note in the scheme of things. And even though you ought to have proven yourself plenty times over, there's a difference between skill in arms and ruling a wayfort. Are you really qualified for this? ] Please, [pc.name]. I would urge you to not dwell upon it too much. You're here, you've come this far, and this is not the time to doubt yourself. Like I said, I really would not put too much weight on the opinions of a bunch of fragmented memories. Isn't that what she is? Should you ignore her, then? While I've kept better than most, I don't claim to be wholly myself at this point. That being said, I would really rather you not join me in my predicament, and I'm sure you and your harpy friend agree. All that being said, since the garrison refuses to acknowledge you as [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort, I'm afraid you'll have to continue contending with them. Once, I might have asked you to be merciful... but now they are beyond even pain. Do what you need to. |The garrison are not what they used to be, that much is obvious, Thalia says with a sigh. It's what will happen to me, too, given long enough. It's also what will happen to you and your harpy friend should you fall here. You figured as much — the spirits are so fragmented that even their manifestations are missing parts of themselves. That being said, that doesn't stop them from being a nuisance while you're trying to make your way through the Wayfort, nipping at your heels especially in the more chaotic sections. Hmm, I'm not sure. It would take a pretty big impetus, something extremely meaningful to them as a whole in order to get through their fugue state to begin with. Anything at all would be helpful. They just keep coming out of the walls, and constantly keeping them off you is starting to get tiring. Hmm. Anything come to mind? There is one thing. You said that you are the ruler of the Wayfort in your time? The commander of the garrison? Well, what you have in your Wayfort may or may not be called a garrison, but you've taken up residence there and call it yours, yes. So far, no one has contested your claim, [flags.WAYFORT_OFFER 1 2|especially since it was granted to you by Njorhaalt, ]so there's that. The old commander must have survived the meteorite's impact — either that, or her sundered spirit hasn't passed through the grand hall or throne room once in all these aeons, which I strongly doubt. The throne is open, but it still possesses much of its symbolic power to the garrison; I would wager that it has much meaning to it. The throne? Power? You glance across the hall and through the open doors into the distant throne room — as far as you can tell, it's just a mundane throne. You can't see it? No. Feel, perhaps? No... "I can," Nina pipes up. "It's like, a bunch of fuzz about the throne, man. Like thick fog or cotton wool, that kinda stuff. Looks like it'd pretty comfortable if you could sit in it." Maybe it'll become more evident when you get closer, or perhaps you need external aid to be able to perceive it. But dreams and memories are what the garrison and this Wayfort are made of, and so they have much power here. If you manage to find a way to tap into the throne's power, you could attempt to impose your will upon what remains of the garrison, convince them that you belong here as their [pc.mf |lord |lady ]. That should put a stop to them. That sounds like a pretty tall order, but if it's the only idea Thalia can come up with then you'll keep it in mind. Feel free to try any other ideas you think will work; I certainly am not an exhaustive authority on the matter. Is there anything else I can help you with? ] "

rows.original: About the broken psyches who wander the Wayfort's halls...
rows.translation: 关于那些在荒废驿堡的大厅中游荡、精神失常的人们……
rows.raw: "About the broken psyches who wander the Wayfort's halls..."

rows.original: While your original plan as formulated by Nina and yourself was to distract whatever was holding you here long enough for you to slip its grasp and escape, the more you hear about the meteorite that emerged from the portal, the more it sounds like something that would be dangerous to leave unattended in the Ways. Is there any means by which it can be taken care of in a more permanent fashion before it finds a way to escape this pocket of the Ways? [pc.isAstrida |... Thalia? It is possible, but I don't know if I would be sending you to a fate worse than death. When it first emerged from the portal and crashed in the Wayfort courtyard, I tried and was found wanting. The life of an Astrida can be short and fraught with peril; Nareva was very clear on that when she made you her champion. Now then, you'll ask again: is there anything that can be done about this shadowlith thing? You are Nareva's godsworn. You already know the answer. Only your unique godsworn abilities as an Astrida can harm it, then. Before the gods descended and lent us their aid, there was no way to harm wraiths or their kin. We... we were made for this purpose, [pc.name]. So is she sure about this? That weapons and spells won't harm it, but only powers granted to you by virtue of being an Astrida will? I... I think so. She thinks so. I... I don't remember. I should when it comes to something as great and important as this, but... With the very specific way certain parts of her memories and personality have been torn from Thalia, one would imagine agency and malice behind these gaps in her mind. I'm sorry, I can't be completely sure. I have this feeling that it should, but I can't be certain. Well, if there's anything that could work against a chunk of rock from beyond that stars that might have some sort of agency of its own, it'd be god-granted powers. All right, thanks for trying anyway. Once more, I apologize. Do you have any other questions? |[pc.isGodsworn |I... I don't think so. You may be godsworn — it's true that before the gods descended and lent us their aid, there was no way to harm wraiths or their kin. At the same time, I don't think you possess the particular abilities required to be able to harm it. She tried to and sort of managed, didn't she? I am an Astrida. You are not. Our colors of divine power are different; I would be exceedingly cautious about deriving your chances from my experiences. I don't mean to be rude, but I don't want to send you off to your demise, either. Death is better than joining me in my fate. So there is no reasonable course of action but to find a way out and retreat. Well... Ah, here comes the %"but." [pc.isDK |Out with it, then |If she'd be so kind as to tell you ]? I may be able to do something if I were present. If you were to find my remains so I can leave this hall and travel with you, there's a chance I may be able to bring what strength I have left to bear while you fend it off. A chance. May. That's a lot of uncertainty there. Then from one godsworn to another, take it in stride and assess your risks, Thalia snaps, clearly growing irritated — though it's more with herself than with you. I'm sorry, I really don't know. I'd only heard that Njorhaalt was doing something with Lumia before I left Tychris, and as for the other gods... there's so much I've lost, and there's what I never had to begin with. You're welcome to do as you please, [pc.name], but I won't speak in concrete certainties where I don't know if there any. All right, maybe you needled her just a bit too much, but on your side, you desperately need to figure out what's going on here and good information is in short supply. With the very specific way certain parts of her memories and personality have been torn from Thalia, one would imagine agency and malice behind these gaps in her mind. I'm sorry, I can't be completely sure. I have this feeling that I've lost something and should know more, but I can't be certain. Do you have any other questions? |No. She sounds pretty certain about that. Before the gods descended and lent us their aid, there was no way to harm wraiths or their kin. That's one of the reasons why Astrida, and by extrapolation, other godsworn, were made. Only the divine power that we were lent was any proof against powers from beyond the Ways; weapons were worthless even against the lesser creatures, arcane magic was absorbed harmlessly. Before I arrived at the Wayfort, the garrison were only capable of dealing with the least of the enemy's thralls. So what she's saying is that you should stick with your plan of escaping. Well... Ah, here comes the %"but." [pc.isDK |Out with it, then |If she'd be so kind as to tell you ]... If you're really bent on doing something about it, I may be able to do something if I were present. If you were to find my remains so I can leave this hall and travel with you, there's a chance I may be able to bring what strength I have left to bear while you fend it off. [pc.isDK |Under normal circumstances, you'd suspect something so out of the blue to be a ploy to encourage you to go along with her plan, but frankly that would be overkill at this point |Were you a more cynical [pc.mf |man |woman ], you'd think this a ploy to encourage you to help her out, but that would be just pushing it ]. But is she sure she can actually do that? Everyone knows stories of the Order Astrida's exploits, but they're always in the context of rogue mages and the like and less about unfathomable psychic horrors from beyond. If defeating it was in her power, why is she a spirit chained to this hall? That is, alas, a risk that you'll have to take — I won't say for sure that it's certain, but at least the attempt can be made, as opposed to you having no chance to begin with. When it comes to certainties, I'm afraid I have few to share — there's so much I've lost, and there's what I never had to begin with. You're welcome to do as you please, [pc.name], but I won't speak in concrete certainties where I don't know if there are any. You'll keep that in mind, then. Let's not get ahead of ourselves; there's still much to be done before any of us even approach that point. Are there any other questions I can answer? ] ]
rows.translation: 虽然尼娜和你最初制定的计划是，设法转移那些阻碍你们离开的力量，让你们有足够的时间逃脱，但当你听到越来越多关于从那个通道中出现的陨石的信息时，你就越来越觉得，如果让这个陨石继续留在那里而不加以处理，它很可能会对“通道”系统造成严重的威胁。有没有什么办法可以彻底解决这个问题，防止它找到机会逃离这个“通道”的区域呢？ [pc.isAstrida |…… 塞莉亚？ 它是这是可能的，但我不知道这样做是否会让你陷入比死亡更可怕的境地。当它第一次从传送门中出现并坠落在荒废驿堡的庭院里时，我尝试过阻止它，但却失败了。 阿斯特里达的生命往往短暂且充满危险；娜瑞瓦在任命你为她的勇士时，已经明确指出了这一点。现在，你可能会再次问：对于这种“暗影石”物质，究竟有没有什么办法可以解决呢？ 你是娜瑞瓦的神之选民。你早已知道答案。 那么，只有作为阿斯特里达所拥有的那些独一无二、受神明庇佑的能力，才能伤害到它。 在众神降临并赐予我们力量之前，人们根本无法伤害那些幽灵及其同类。我们……就是为这样的使命而存在的。 [pc.name]。 那么，她真的确定这一点吗？也就是说，武器和法术不会对它造成伤害，只有那些因为你是阿斯特里达而获得的能力才会有效吗？ 我……我想是的。 她也是这么认为的。 我……我不记得了。对于这么重要的事情，我应该记得的，但是…… 由于她的某些记忆和性格特征是以一种非常特殊的方式从塔莉娅身上分离出来的，因此人们很自然地会认为，她脑海中这些空白之处背后存在着某种故意的行为或恶意。 很抱歉，我并不能完全确定。我有这种感觉，应该可以，但我还是不能确定。 嗯，如果说有什么东西能够阻碍那些来自遥远星辰、或许拥有自身力量的巨石的话，那肯定就是神赐的力量了。好吧，无论如何还是感谢你的尝试。 再次为我的失误道歉。您还有其他问题吗？ |[pc.isGodsworn |我……我不这么认为。你或许受到了神的庇佑——的确，在众神降临并帮助我们之前，确实没有任何方法能够伤害那些幽灵及其同类。但同时，我也认为你并不具备伤害它们所需要的特殊能力。 她尝试过了，而且还算是成功了吧？ 我是阿斯特里达，而你不是。我们身上所蕴含的神圣力量是不同的；因此，我绝不会根据自己的经验来判断你的命运。我并非有意冒犯，只是也不希望你因此而走向灭亡。死亡总比与我共同面对命运要好。 因此，除了寻找出路并撤退之外，没有其他合理的行动方案了。 嗯…… 啊，那个“但是”又要出现了[pc.isDK |那就直说吧。 |如果她能好心地告诉你的话…… ]如果我在场的话，或许能做些什么。如果你能找到我的遗体，让我离开这个大厅，与你一同前行，那么我就有可能尽我最后的力量来帮助你抵挡那些威胁。 只是个机会而已。也许吧……这其中其实充满了不确定性。 那么，从一个誓言到另一个誓言，冷静地面对这一切，认真评估你所面临的风险吧。塔莉娅突然发怒了，显然她自己也很恼火——不过这种愤怒更多是针对她自己，而不是针对你。很抱歉，我真的不知道。我只能听到了在我离开提克里斯之前，我就知道尼奥尔哈尔特正在和卢米娅一起做些什么。至于其他神明……我失去了太多，也有些东西本来就从未属于我。你们想怎么做都行。 [pc.name]，但我也不会在那些我不确定是否存在的情况下给出具体的结论。 好吧，也许你确实有点太过分了，但从你的角度来看，你确实迫切需要弄清楚这里到底发生了什么，而目前可用的有用信息却非常有限。鉴于她记忆中的某些部分以及她的性格特征是以如此特殊的方式从塔莉娅身上分离出来的，人们很自然会认为，她脑海中这些空白之处背后必定存在着某种人为的干预或恶意行为。 很抱歉，我也不能完全确定。我有种感觉，好像自己丢失了什么，应该了解更多信息，但我确实无法确定。你还有其他问题吗？ |不。 她听起来对此非常确信。 在众神降临并赐予我们力量之前，人们根本无法伤害那些幽灵及其同类。正因为如此，才创造了阿斯特里达，以及其他被神明眷顾的存在。只有神赐的力量，才能对抗那些来自异界的力量；武器对那些低等生物来说毫无作用，而秘术则会被它们毫无伤害地吸收掉。在我来到荒废驿堡之前，那里的驻军根本无力对抗敌人派来的那些低级奴仆。 所以她的意思是，你应该坚持你的逃跑计划。 嗯…… 啊，那个“但是”又要出现了[pc.isDK |那就直说吧。 |如果她能好心地告诉你的话…… ]…… 如果你真的决心要采取行动的话，如果我在场的话，或许能够帮上忙。如果你能找到我的遗体，让我能够离开这个大厅，与你一起踏上旅途，那么我就有可能尽我最后的力量来帮助你应对那些困难。 [pc.isDK |在正常情况下，遇到这样突如其来的事情，你可能会怀疑这是她为了让你同意她的计划而设下的圈套。但坦白说，在这种情况下，这种怀疑未免有些过分了。 |你是不是本来就更加愤世嫉俗一些呢？ [pc.mf |男人 |女性 ]你可能会认为这是某种诱使你帮助她的手段，但那样的话就有点太牵强了。 ]但是，她真的是这样吗？当然可以。她真的能做到吗？大家都听说过阿斯特里达骑士团的英勇事迹，但这些故事通常都是关于那些叛逆的法师之流的，而很少提到那些来自异界的、令人难以想象的灵能恐怖存在。如果击败那些怪物真的在她的能力范围之内，那她为什么还会成为被锁在这座大厅里的幽灵呢？ 唉，这确实是一个你必须去承担的风险——我不能肯定地说这种尝试一定会成功，但至少你可以尝试一下，而不是从一开始就没有任何机会。至于那些可以确定的事情，恐怕我没什么可以分享的……我失去了太多，也有一些东西从来就从未拥有过。你可以随心所欲地做你想做的事。 [pc.name]，但我也不会在那些我不确定是否存在某种情况的时候，给出具体的肯定答复。 那你可要记住这一点。 我们先不要急着下结论，在我们任何人达到那个目标之前，还有许多事情需要去做。还有其他问题需要我回答吗？ ] ]

rows.original: The meteorite that fell... is there anything that can be done about it?
rows.translation: 那颗坠落的陨石……我们能采取什么措施来应对它吗？
rows.raw: "The meteorite that fell... is there anything that can be done about it?"

rows.original: [pc.isAstrida |I don't think this is relevant to our predicament right now. Not exactly, but you're interested in the matter. What happened at Estelore is exactly what the Order Astrida was founded to prevent — she should know that. I... hm. To be honest, I don't really know much more than what was common knowledge at the time. If you're interested in the secrets of the mages of that island or the like, I can't help you there. Even common knowledge would be helpful. A lot has been lost to history over the centuries, and what remains is largely garbled half-truth. All that I know is second-hand, but all right. Estelore was the Belharan Empire's mage-capital, so to speak. The central hub of learning, research, experimentation — so long as it pertained to the arcane, they had it. They were just off the east coast of the Marches, right on the border of the coastal reaches claimed by the boreal elves. A bit far from Belhar itself, for such an important part of the empire. It's because they were so far from the imperial center that they were able to exert a considerable amount of autonomy. No imperial lord ruled it; Estelore governed the adjoining college town that sprung up at its foot as it pleased, and even levied its own taxes. Just about all the students lived in the town and stayed there for the duration of their educations, unless they had relatives nearby like Baron Reverra was to his nephew who studied there. Thalia seems to know a lot about the Marcher-Baron and his family. Not firsthand, as I said; I never personally knew the man. I spent several evenings in conversation with the Wayfort's commander, who was quite intimately acquainted with him — all my knowledge comes from her. What was the relationship like between Hawkstone and Estelore? Both represented the extreme northern reach of Belharan power, and Estelore seems to have been something of a rogue agent. The barony and the college lived in mutual distrust. Estelore was suspicious of the Reverra family, because Baron Victor's wife was said to be practising magic esoteric even by their standards — not anything forbidden or evil per se, but they just didn't like her doing something they weren't. The baron's daughter Carmen was brilliant, but refused a scholarship at the academy because, as the commander said, %"she decided that they had nothing to teach her." His nephew Michael took far better to academia than his cousin did, and spent his student breaks at his uncle's castle. The commander was quite emphatic in telling me that if not for the boy, relations between his uncle and Estelore would be even worse. That doesn't matter now, though; the island's completely obliterated. Is there anything else you'd prefer to ask? |I don't think this is relevant to our predicament right now. Not exactly, but you're interested in the matter. A lot has been lost to history over the centuries, and what remains is largely garbled. Perhaps when we're out of here and after I've had the goddess' blessing, I can speak more freely about such matters with you. For now, though, I must insist on drawing us back to the imminent peril we — well, more you — are in. It's clear that Thalia doesn't want to talk about this. Perhaps after all this is over, maybe. ]
rows.translation: [pc.isAstrida |我认为这与我们目前的处境并没有关联。 不完全是，但你对这件事很感兴趣。在埃斯托洛尔发生的事情，正是阿斯特里达组织成立的初衷就是为了防止这类事情的发生——她应该明白这一点。 我……嗯，说实话，我所知道的也不比当时大家普遍了解的信息多多少。如果你对那个岛上法师们的秘密之类的东西感兴趣，那我可帮不上你的忙。 即使是常识也会很有帮助。几个世纪以来，许多信息已经消失在历史的长河中，而留存下来的大多是些被篡改过的半真半假的内容。 我所知道的都是道听途说，不过也好吧。可以说，埃斯泰洛尔是贝尔哈兰帝国的魔法中心——那里是学术研究、实验探索的聚集地，凡是与魔法相关的活动，都在那里进行。它位于边境地区东海岸，正好与北方精灵所宣称的沿海领地接壤。 距离贝尔哈尔本身还有些远，但考虑到这是帝国中如此重要的一个地区，这样的布局也是情有可原的。 正是因为它们距离帝国中心太过遥远，才能够享有相当大的自治权。没有任何帝国贵族来统治这些地区；埃斯特洛尔可以随心所欲地管理那些在其脚下兴起的大学城，甚至可以自行征收税款。几乎所有的学生都居住在这些城镇里，并且会在那里完成他们的学业，除非他们身边有亲戚——就像雷维拉男爵和他的侄子那样，侄子就是在那里学习的。 塞莉亚似乎对那位步兵男爵及其家族了解很多。 正如我所说，这些并不是第一手资料；我本人从未真正认识过那个人。我有几个晚上与荒废驿堡的指挥官进行了交谈，她与那个人关系非常密切，所以我所知道的一切都来自她。 霍克斯通与埃斯托洛之间的关系是怎样的？他们两者都代表着贝拉兰势力的最北端边界，而埃斯托洛似乎更像是一个独立行动的特工。 这个男爵家族与那所学院之间始终存在着互不信任的关系。埃斯托洛对雷维拉家族充满怀疑，因为据说维克托男爵的妻子所从事的魔法研究，即便是按照他们的标准来看，也属于深奥神秘的范畴——这些行为本身并不违法，也不邪恶，但他们就是不喜欢她去做那些他们自己也不了解的事情。男爵的女儿卡门才华横溢，但却拒绝了学院提供的奖学金，因为正如那位指挥官所说：“她认为那些学院里没有什么东西是能教给她的。”他的侄子迈克尔则对学术学习表现得远比他的表妹好得多，每次放假他都会去叔叔的城堡里度过。那位指挥官非常坚决地告诉我，如果不是因为那个男孩，他叔叔和埃斯特尔尔之间的关系会更加糟糕。 不过现在这些都无所谓了，那座岛屿已经彻底被毁掉了。还有其他你想问的问题吗？ |我认为这与我们目前的处境并没有关联。 不完全是，但你对这个话题确实很感兴趣。几个世纪以来，许多信息已经消失在历史的长河中，而剩下的那些内容也大多已经变得混乱不堪了。 或许等我们离开这里，等我得到了女神的庇佑之后，我就可以更自由地与你讨论这些事情了。不过现在，我必须坚持让我们先回到我们——或者说，主要是你——所面临的迫在眉睫的危险之中。 很明显，塔莉娅并不想谈论这件事。也许等这一切都结束了，她才会愿意开口吧。 ]

rows.original: Thalia mentioned Estelore before — given that she was around at the time, what can she tell you about it?
rows.translation: 塔莉娅之前提到过埃斯托洛尔——既然她当时也在场，她能告诉你关于那里的什么情况呢？
rows.raw: "Thalia mentioned Estelore before — given that she was around at the time, what can she tell you about it?"

rows.original: That's all you have for the moment. It's nice to be able to talk to someone sane in this place. And the same here. "Hey, man." Nina grumps. "I'm not totally crazy." The both of you will eventually be if you don't hop to it. Time may not have any hold on this place, but I would not linger overlong. With that, Thalia's spirit dissipates and fades from view, leaving the two of you to contemplate your next move.
rows.translation: 目前就这些了。能在这个地方遇到一个神志清醒的人交谈，真是太好了。 这里也是如此。 “嘿，伙计。”妮娜抱怨道，“我可没完全疯掉。” 如果你们不抓紧时间，最终还是会变成那样的。时间或许对这个地方没有任何影响，但我建议你们不要拖延太久。随着这句话落下，塔莉娅的灵魂消散了，从视野中淡去，只留下你们两人去思量下一步该怎么走。

With that, Thalia's spirit dissipates and fades from view, leaving the two of you to contemplate your next move."

rows.original: Sit in the throne. This may or may not be a good idea.
rows.translation: 登上王位吧。这个主意或许不错，或许也不行。
rows.raw: "Sit in the throne. This may or may not be a good idea."

rows.original:
You brush off a bit of dust from the throne — it's held up surprisingly well under the gritty gray coating. It's a whim all right, but you slowly ease yourself into the throne's embrace, half-expecting the ancient furniture to give way under you any moment. It doesn't, but the furs have thinned and the bone frame prods at your rear most insistently. It's a throne from a different age for a people who no longer exist, a reminder that leadership should be uncomfortable.

        Despite the residual aura that lingers about the throne, though, nothing happens. You bide a little while longer, taking in the ruined, dreary view that's so different from the Wayfort and throne room you know, then sigh and stand. This chamber may be infused with memories strong enough to be palpable, but they're not yours. Maybe it's for the best that nothing happened as a result of your sudden whim.
rows.translation:
你拂去王座上的一层灰尘——在那层灰蒙蒙的覆盖物之下，王座竟然依然完好无损。虽然这只是一时兴起，但你还是缓缓坐了下去，心中不免有些担心：这古老的家具会不会随时在你坐下的一刹那崩塌呢？并没有，但那些毛皮已经变得稀疏，骨制的框架则更加明显地刺在你的后背。这其实是一把属于另一个时代的王座，属于一个早已消失的民族，它提醒着我们：领导者的位置本就应该让人感到不适。

        然而，尽管这把王座周围仍然萦绕着某种残留的气息，却什么也没有发生。你再稍等片刻，凝视着这片破败而阴郁的场景——它与你所熟悉的荒废驿堡宫以及王座厅截然不同。然后，你叹了口气，站了起来。这个房间里或许充满了那些强烈到几乎可以触摸得到的回忆，但它们并不属于你。也许，正因为你一时兴起做出了那个决定，所以最终什么事情都没有发生，这反而是件好事。

rows.original: A shiver runs up your spine as you approach the throne — not of fear, but an inexplicable thrill that may not even have been yours to begin with. With Nina's Juice coursing through your veins, the commanding aura emanating from the throne is overwhelming; you have to focus on every step just to keep your feet moving forward. Part of you wonders if this might be a good idea, to which the rest replies with a unanimous yes. Being [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort back home would be so much more appealing if you felt like this when you sat on your throne... Speaking of which, you're right up against it. You brush off a bit of dust from the throne — it's held up surprisingly well under the gritty gray coating. Heart clenching and pulse racing, you slowly ease yourself into the throne's embrace, half-expecting the ancient furniture to give way under you any moment. It doesn't, but the furs have thinned and the bone frame prods at your rear most insistently. It's a throne from a different age for a people who no longer exist, a reminder that leadership should be uncomfortable. Yes, it's undeniable — something's going to happen if you remain seated, and whatever happens next it's not likely that you're going to get another chance at it. Knowing this, will you remain seated on the throne?
rows.translation: 当你走近王座时，一阵寒意从脊背涌上——并非恐惧，而是一种难以解释的兴奋，这种兴奋或许从一开始就不属于你。当尼娜的能量在你的血液中流淌时，王座散发出的强大气场令你几乎无法抗拒；你必须集中全部注意力才能让脚步继续向前移动。内心有一部分在质疑这样做是否明智，但其余部分却一致地给出了肯定的答案。毕竟[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]在韦弗特回家的路上所以如果你在登上王座时就有这样的感受，那么这一切就会显得更加吸引人了…… 说起来，你现在就处于这样的境地。你轻轻拂去王座上的一些灰尘——在那层灰蒙蒙的外壳之下，王座竟然依然保存得相当完好。心惊胆战、脉搏加速，你缓缓坐上王座，心中暗自担心这些古老的家具随时会坍塌。然而它们并没有倒下，只是那些毛皮垫子已经变得稀薄，而木质框架则从你的背后不断刺来，让人感到格外不适。这是一把属于另一个时代的王座，为早已消失的民族而打造，它提醒人们：担任领导者其实是一件令人不适的事情。 没错，这一点毋庸置疑—— 有些事情……如果你继续坐在王位上，那么某些事情就会发生，而无论接下来发生什么，你很可能不会再有机会重新选择。知道了这一点，你还会继续坐在王位上吗？

rows.original: [pc.isDK |Tch. You've already faced so much madness that this shattered image of your own home has thrown at you, a piece of furniture with an imperious air about it is nothing by comparison. Feisty, but you'll show it who's boss soon enough. Whoever once sat in this throne before you, he or she clearly abandoned the post — finders keepers, losers weepers. |Steeling yourself, you redouble your resolve to remain seated — if this is some kind of test, then by the gods you're going to pass it. Sure, you already own the Wayfort of the future, but there'd be a whole lot of shame involved if you didn't manage to win the approval of whoever it was who sat in this throne before you. ] With that thought in mind, you tighten your fingers about the armrests and redouble your determination to remain seated. Even so, you cast a glance over at Nina — she surprisingly doesn't have much of a reaction to what you're doing, instead watching with arms akimbo and what can only be called a half-drunk expression on her face. Not approving, but not against the idea either... Just as the psychic pressure within the throne's glimmering aura reaches a zenith, it snaps out of existence, and the broken shapes of the Wayfort's garrison start filtering into the throne room through the walls. Twisted images of boreal elves, imperials, even a minotaur or two — recognizable as people, but wrong as if viewed through one of those gag mirrors that Tychris used to make. Too tall, too spindly, bent in shapes that should not be possible, all with gaps in their bodies where holes in their memories and psyches exist — all of them form up in ranks with military precision, waiting, expectant.
rows.translation: [pc.isDK |啧，你已经经历了太多疯狂的事情，而这种将自己家园的破碎景象呈现在你面前的行为，与一件摆出威严姿态的家具相比，简直微不足道。你虽然脾气火爆，但很快就会让那些人知道谁才是真正的主人。无论在你之前谁坐过这个王位，显然他们都已经放弃了这个位置——谁抢到就归谁，失去的人只能自认倒霉罢了。 |你强压住自己的恐惧，更加坚定了要坐下去的决心——如果这是某种考验的话，那么凭着神明，你一定会通过它。当然，你早已掌握了未来的发展方向，但如果你无法赢得坐在这个王位上的人的认可，那未免太可惜了。 ] 怀着这样的想法，你紧紧抓住扶手，更加坚定了要坐下去的决心。不过，你还是瞥了尼娜一眼——出乎意料的是，她对你所做的并没有太大的反应，只是双臂交叉地站在那里看着你，脸上带着一种只能被形容为“微醉”的表情。并不赞同这个想法，但也不反对…… 就在王座那闪烁的光环中蕴含的精神压力达到顶点的时候，它突然消失了，而荒废驿堡驻军的残破身影开始透过墙壁渗入王座厅堂。那些扭曲的图像中出现了极北精灵、帝国士兵，甚至有一两个弥诺陶洛斯——它们看起来仍然像人类，但错误仿佛是通过提克里斯曾经制作过的那些搞笑镜子来看待这些景象一样。它们太高了，太纤细了，身体呈现出本不该存在的弯曲形态，它们的身体上还有些缝隙，那些缝隙正是它们记忆与精神中缺失的部分……所有这些生物都以军事般的精准度排成队列，静静地等待着，充满期待。

rows.original: Just as you're wondering how to win acceptance from what remains of the Wayfort's old inhabitants, they solve the problem for you. Barely has the old garrison assembled in the throne room that a hushed whisper ripples through the mental echoes of the dead, rushing from back to fore like a wave gathering strength and speed before breaking upon the shore. Astrida. Once they realize what you are, what's sitting in the throne, a complete change comes over the apparitions' demeanor. Warped and twisted as they may be, the broken mental echoes set down their weapons and get on their knees — or at least, what you think are their knees. Those with helmets remove them, those with missing limbs and other parts are helped by their fellows. Astrida. [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion |As far as you know, this isn't any kind of ceremony or rite you've read of as a [pc.background] |You could be wrong, but you don't think they're putting on a show for you ]. No, even if it's eerily coordinated and executed with ceremonial precision, it's merely the desire of all these combined wills. In a way, it's pretty solid proof that these apparitions are wholly genuine about their feelings... Astrida. The wave of worshipful reverence that smacks straight into you is overwhelming and dizzying, throwing you back into the throne as if you'd been physically struck. In this place, you may as well have been. Even so, the sight of every single shattered psyche with arms laid down and repeatedly kowtowing to you, foreheads pressed to the floor — to say that you've earned their approval would be a great understatement. Because you're an Astrida, they love you with fanatical fervor — whatever else filled the last days of their lives, it's clear that this desperate love and admiration for the godsworn of Nareva dominated so much of their thoughts and emotions to leave so deep a mark that even the void could not take it from them. It's beautiful. [var0 |Of course, you're well aware that you're riding on Thalia's coattails here — the worshipful adoration these shattered shades have for you is because of her deeds in their final moments, and the respect she garnered amongst the garrison by giving them hope. [pc.isDK |How nice of her to leave this kind of legacy for a fellow Astrida to pick up — don't mind if you do, then. It feels really, really good to have everyone groveling before you like this; if only the present-day inhabitants of the Wayfort would do the same for you. rows.translation: 就在你还在思考如何赢得荒废驿堡老居民们的认可时，他们已经为你解决了这个问题。几乎就在老驻军们聚集在王座厅的那一刻，一阵低语声在死者的精神回响中荡漾开来，那声音如同海浪一样，不断积蓄力量和速度，最终冲向岸边。
