当那些幻影继续吟诵着咒语时，你的脸上露出了笑容；看到所有人都在你面前卑躬屈膝，这种感觉真是太美妙了。你很清楚过分膨胀自己的虚荣心会带来危险，但坐在那古老的王座上，享受众人的崇拜与尊敬，稍微放纵一下自己，应该也不会有什么坏处吧？这个是比你通常所获得的尊重还要多一些。 |嗯……你真是[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]这无疑与未来的韦弗特家族有着紧密的联系，同时也以自己的方式与过去的韦弗特家族产生了关联。如果即将取代现任王位的王位不属于你，那么这一切无疑会变得更加艰难。当然，受到神明的加冕也起到了一定的作用，但单凭这一点可能还不够。 ] ] 好了，够了。 那些曾经隶属于荒废驿堡的人全都服从命令，站起身来收拾武器，然后离开了王座厅。不久之后，你就只剩下自己和妮娜在这个布满灰尘的房间里了——既然王座已经完成了它的使命，围绕着它产生的那种灵力压力也就消失了。 “哼，”妮娜说道，“这才像样嘛。看来你真的注定要统领所有荒废驿堡家族，对吧？无论是过去的、现在的，还是未来的 [var0 |考虑到塔莉娅为他们所做的一切，这并不奇怪；到最后，她实际上已经成为了驻军指挥官。然而，如果没有塔莉娅，或者没有另一位像阿斯特里达这样的存在，那么一个被神明祝福的人——也就是你——也足以填补他们心中那个空缺。 |嗯，即使这种荣誉感觉来得并不理所应当，但它确实是一种荣誉。 ] 嗯，好的，当然。我确实觉得既然他们已经接受了你，我们在这个地方活动时应该会少遇到一些麻烦了。当然，肯定还有一些人顽固到根本意识不到荒废驿堡现在有了新的领导，但至少我觉得，既然他们认为你属于这里，大多数人应该不会再来打扰我们了。不过，奇怪的是，直到你坐上了王位，这种效果才显现出来。你本以为，如果他们一开始就能弄清楚你的真实身份，那么无论何时，他们都应该能认出你才是那个被神明选中的人才对。 来吧，伙计，”妮娜一边说，一边帮你从王座上下来。你在里面待的时间应该不超过十五分钟，但你的关节却像是坐了很久很久一样在嘎吱作响。“这个地方的内部面积比外部看起来要大得多，你居然还在担心这里的东西会不会合乎常理吗？你就按你自己的想法去做吧。感受到 —事实证明，这是目前最明智的选择，因为整个荒废驿堡其实就是这些受伤心灵的写照。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我们得走了。
rows.raw: " Just as you're wondering how to win acceptance from what remains of the Wayfort's old inhabitants, they solve the problem for you. Barely has the old garrison assembled in the throne room that a murmur ripples through the mental echoes of the dead, rushing from back to fore like a wave gathering strength and speed before breaking upon the shore. You don't know exactly why, but with so many of these apparitions in one place, these fragmented memories given shape, you feel some kind of kinship with them. Maybe it's because you're [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort in the future, maybe it's something deeper, but it's there nevertheless. What's changed? Maybe it's because you're sitting in the throne that allows them to feel it as you do. Once that connection is made, a complete change comes over the apparitions' demeanor. Warped and twisted as they may be, the broken mental echoes set down their weapons and get on their knees — or at least, what you think are their knees. Those with helmets remove them, those with missing limbs and other parts are helped by their fellows. [pc.bg scholar acolyte noblescion |As far as you know, this isn't any kind of ceremony or rite you've read of as a [pc.background] |You could be wrong, but you don't think they're putting on a show for you ]. No, even if it's eerily coordinated and executed with ceremonial precision, it's merely the desire of all these combined wills. In a way, it's pretty solid proof that these apparitions are wholly genuine about their feelings... The wave of worshipful reverence that smacks straight into you is overwhelming and dizzying, throwing you back into the throne as if you'd been physically struck. In this place, you may as well have been. Even so, the sight of every single shattered psyche with arms laid down and repeatedly kowtowing to you, foreheads pressed to the floor — to say that you've earned their approval would be a great understatement. Because you gave yourself over to service of one of the Seven, they love you with fanatical fervor — whatever else filled the last days of their lives, it's clear that this desperate love and admiration dominated so much of their thoughts and emotions to leave so deep a mark that even the void could not take it from them. It's beautiful. You're not one of Nareva's, of course, but that reverence nevertheless transfers to you. [var0 |Of course, you're well aware that you're riding on Thalia's coattails here — the worshipful adoration these shattered shades have for you is because of her deeds in their final moments, and the respect she garnered amongst the garrison by giving them hope. [pc.isDK |How nice of her to do a favor for the godsworn of another of the Seven — don't mind if you do, then. It's not like she's going to be claiming her laurels anytime soon, and it feels really, really good to have everyone groveling before you like this; if only the present-day inhabitants of the Wayfort would do the same for you. As the apparitions continue chanting, a smile spreads over your face. You're well aware of the dangers of inflating your ego too much, but just a little indulgence while sitting on an ancient throne and being acknowledged can't hurt, can it? This is a little more than the respect you usually enjoy from your own as a godsworn. |You may not some from the same line, but no doubt the other godsworn worked just as hard during the Godswar, so there's no shame in accepting what Thalia's left. It would be more proper for an Astrida to claim it, but you're the one who happened to be in the right place at the right time. Heh. Despite you sitting in the throne, despite the powerful aura of command and imperiousness that pervades these ancient furs and bones, the gravity of the situation strikes you amidst having your ego warmed over by such unadulterated adoration. You're only getting this from these broken apparitions because of whatever memories they have of Nareva's godsworn order, and not of you. And while it might feel good to have the present-day inhabitants of the Wayfort grovel in the same way, it'd probably get old fast. Many of them are your friends, after all, not your subjects. For now, though, a little indulgence in exerting your godsworn presence over these shattered shades can't hurt too much... ] |But there's more there. That kinship you felt earlier... it might be wholly imaginary, but what matters in this place is that the broken shades believe that it's real. So close to the edge of reality, these dreams are all that's truly needed to give it power. And if it's not imaginary? [pc.isDK |Does it matter? You're [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort in the future, and it's only natural that you assert the same authority in the Wayfort of the past. That should be enough to subdue these apparitions to begin with, let alone the fact that you're a godsworn. As the apparitions continue chanting, a smile spreads over your face; it feels really, really good to have everyone groveling before you. You're well aware of the dangers of inflating your ego too much, but just a little indulgence while sitting on an ancient throne and being acknowledged can't hurt, can it? This is a little more than the respect you usually enjoy. |Well... you're [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort in the future, and clearly that it ins own way reaches out to the Wayfort of the past, too. No doubt this wouldn't have been so easy if the throne that would replace this one wasn't yours. No doubt being godsworn also helped, but it might not have been enough on its own. ] ] All right, that's enough. As one, the former garrison of the Wayfort's past obey, standing and gathering their weapons before marching out of the throne room. Before too long, you're left alone with Nina in the dusty chamber, the psychic pressure about the throne gone now that its purpose has been fulfilled. "Huh," Nina says. "Now that's something. Guess you really are meant to lord it over all the Wayforts there are, aren't you? Past, present, future and all." [var0 |It's not surprising, given what Thalia did for them; she was the de facto garrison commander by the end. Without Thalia or another Astrida, though, a godsworn — you — sufficed to fill that empty space in their psyches. |Well, it's most certainly an honor even if it feels unearned. ] "Yeah, okay, sure. What I do think is that now that they've accepted you, we'll be harassed less getting around this place. I'm sure there're a few stragglers too far gone to realize that there's new command in the Wayfort, but at least I get the feeling most of them won't be bothering us now that they think you belong." Odd that it took you sitting in the throne for that to kick in, though. You'd have thought you would be recognizable as a godsworn anytime if they were going to figure out what you were to begin with. "C'mon, man," Nina replies as she helps you out of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." "

rows.original: Sure, you weren't the heir — not even the spare, but the spare's spare — yet as a noble scion, you ought to have absorbed some of the lessons your siblings got on exerting one's noble presence. Besides, that sort of thing should come naturally to you, right? Right? Of course, impressing yourself upon a bunch of half-insane apparitions is bound to be harder than folks who're mostly your friends to begin with, but in essence being the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort past shouldn't be fundamentally different than being that of the Wayfort present. The psychic emanations surrounding the throne resonate with your focused will as you concentrate on filling your ego with that sense of grandiose command... This Wayfort is yours. Your blood is noble. [pc.isDK |They will recgonize you |By every means, you ought to be qualified ] — [pc.ra elf | |even if you aren't a boreal elf, ]you're the Champion of Frost and in good with the Var Ridells. You have every right to sit in this throne. By degrees, you feel your sense of self slipping out from the dais, crawling over the crumbling walls and floor, encircling the throne room with your noble presence. This is the sort of thing you might've been expected to do, had you been born earlier... and now by some quirk of fate, you've been given the chance to impress yourself upon a captive audience. Whether it's the throne itself or some fragment of the Wayfort's previous commander lodged within the fur and bone, the dreamlike emanations serve as a conduit for yourself; the remainder is up to you... [var1 |Just when you feel you're stretched impossibly thin over the floor and walls, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. But it doesn't. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Half of them are fading in and out of existence at this point, but even so your presence has stirred something within them; meeting your gaze, the garrison of Wayfort past stands at attention and salutes you. It worked, it actually worked. They recognize you. You think. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the shattered shades march out of the throne room with as much military precision as they can muster, as opposed to the way they arrived. [pc.isDK |Finally, someone actually respects your authority. Not the highest bar to clear, but it's a starting point from which to work your way up |It makes you a little emotional, the way they instinctively recognized you... no speeches, no words, just you and your raw presence ]. A dream, perhaps, of your lineage should be self-evident regardless of you being a so-called spare's spare. Not so surplus to requirements now, eh? Before too long, you're left alone with Nina in the dusty chamber, the aura about the throne gone now that its purpose has been fulfilled. "Huh," Nina says. "Now that's something. Guess you really are meant to lord it over all the Wayforts there are, aren't you? Past, present, future and all." Oh, come on. Now even she's laying it on thickly. But... it does feel gratifying to [pc.isDK |finally have your inherent nobility recognized and finally good for something. Others might call it unearned, but you know better |be accepted in this fashion, even if you had to leverage your noble lineage and training to get it done. It feels a little unearned, but you'll take every advantage you can get in this madhouse ]. "Yeah, okay, sure. What I do think is that now that they've accepted you, we'll be harassed less getting around this place. I'm sure there're a few stragglers too far gone to realize that there's new command in the Wayfort, but at least I get the feeling most of them won't be bothering us now that they think you're their boss." And all it took was you sitting in the throne for that to kick in. It makes sense in a way, there has to be a formal handing over of authority when it comes to these things, but here in this place there's just a little too much emphasis placed on the appearance of things to the point where it becomes the substance. "C'mon, man," Nina replies as she helps you out of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." |Just when you feel like you're being torn apart, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched, your head spinning from the impossible madness of this world. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. And that's exactly what it does, collapsing into a miserable pile of shards and ruined furs underneath you. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Their faces straight, they focus their attention solely on you. And then they turn their backs. Before then, you thought it might have worked despite the mishap, but this makes it clear they've found you lacking by whatever criteria half-mad shades use to acknowledge authority. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the garrison of Wayfort past scatters, disappearing into the walls and floor as quickly as they arrived. In the blink of an eye, there's nothing left of them but a chill across the length of your spine and a heaviness in your heart. [pc.isDK |Well, if they won't acknowledge your authority, you'll just have to do this the hard way. In fact, maybe it's better that these ghosts are recalcitrant — this will be just as satisfying, albeit in a different fashion |If this is how things turn out when your noble presence is put to the test, maybe it's better that you left to seek your fortune than scrabble for what scraps your family could spare you ]. "Huh," Nina says. "Don't take it too hard — they're not right in the head. I mean, at least they didn't outright attack us there and then. As great as you and I are, man, I don't think we're capable of standing up to an entire garrison. We're already being harassed getting around this place, so..." Please don't say that it can't get worse, because it always can get worse. "Don't get too sour about it, man," Nina replies as she helps you up and out of what remains of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." ]
rows.translation: 当然，你并不是继承人——甚至都不是备选继承人，而是备选继承人中的“备选者”……但作为贵族的后裔，你本应该从你的兄弟姐妹们身上学到一些如何展现贵族风范的知识才对。而且，这种事情对你来说应该也是理所当然的吧？ 对吧？ 当然，要让一群行为古怪、近乎疯狂的人对你刮目相看，肯定比让那些本来就是你朋友的人认可你要困难得多……但说到底，身为[pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]，管理过去的驿堡与现在的驿堡在本质上并无区别。当你专注于用那种威严感来充实自己的自我时，王座周围散发出的灵能会与你集中起来的意志产生共鸣…… 这个韦弗特属于你。你的血脉是高贵的。 [pc.isDK |他们会认出你了 |你必须具备相应的资格，这样才能胜任这项工作。 ] — [pc.ra elf | |即使你并不是北方精灵…… ]你是霜之冠军，也与瓦里德尔家族关系融洽。你完全有资格坐上这把王座。 渐渐地，你感觉到自己的自我意识正在从王座上脱离，缓缓爬过那些摇摇欲坠的墙壁和地板，以你高贵的存在感环绕着整个王座厅。如果你出生得再早一些，或许本来就应该去做这样的事情……而现在，由于命运的某种安排，你得到了这个机会，在这些被你“俘获”的观众面前展示自己的能力。无论是那把王座本身，还是那些蕴含在瓦福特前任指挥官遗骸中的力量，这些梦境般的能量，都在为你本人提供实现目标的途径。剩下的就由你来决定了…… [var1 |就在你感觉自己已经被拉伸得几乎透明、无处不在的时候，王座内部的压力突然消失了，你就像一块被拉伸后的黏液橡胶一样，又被猛地拉回了自己的身体里。你喘着粗气，拼命抓住一切可以依靠的东西，身体被猛地推向椅背，那把王座发出吱嘎声，仿佛随时都会在你重量之下坍塌。 但它并没有。当你缓过气来，抬起头，看到眼前聚集的那些人——他们都是那些只剩下情感与支离破碎的记忆的人，他们的身影扭曲而凄惨。此刻，它们有一半已经渐渐消失在现实中，但即便如此，你的存在依然触发了它们内心的某种反应；当它们与你的目光相遇时，那些曾经驻守在荒废驿堡的军队便会立正敬礼，向你致意。 真的有效，真的奏效了。他们认出了你，你猜？ 他们并没有等你将他们驱赶出去——那些破碎的阴影以它们所能展现出的最大军事纪律性，从王座厅里走了出来，与它们进来时的样子截然不同。 [pc.isDK |终于，有人真正尊重你的权威了。这虽然不是最高的标准，但至少是一个可以让你逐步前进的起点。 |他们的这种本能反应，让你不禁感到有些感动……没有演讲，没有言语，只有你，以及你真实的存在。 ]或许，你这一家族的使命应该是显而易见的，无论你是不是所谓的“多余之人”。现在，你已经不再被需要了，对吧？不久之后，你就会和妮娜一起待在那个布满灰尘的房间里，而王座周围的那股气息也会随着它的使命完成而消失。 “嗯，”妮娜说道，“这倒真是有点意思。看来你真的注定要统领所有荒废驿堡家族，对吧？无论是过去的、现在的，还是未来的。 哦，得了吧。就连她现在也在夸大其词了。但是确实让人感到很有成就感[pc.isDK |终于，你与生俱来的高贵品质得到了认可，终于能够有所作为了。别人可能会认为这是你应得的，但你知道事实并非如此。 |以这样的方式获得认可，即使你必须借助自己高贵的血统和所受过的训练才能做到这一点，也让人感觉这种认可有点来之不易。但在这个混乱的环境中，你会抓住一切可以利用的机会的。 ]嗯，好的，当然可以。我确实觉得既然他们已经接受了你，我们在这个地方活动时应该会少遇到一些麻烦了。当然，肯定还有一些人顽固到根本意识不到荒废驿堡现在有了新的领导，但至少我觉得，既然他们认为你是他们的上司，大多数人应该不会再来打扰我们了。而这一切，只需要你坐在王位上就可以了。从某种意义上来说，这种做法确实合情合理——在涉及这类事务时，必须要有正式的权力交接仪式。但在这个地方，人们过于注重形式上的东西了，甚至让形式本身取代了实质内容。 来吧，伙计，”妮娜一边说，一边帮你从王座上下来。你在里面待的时间应该不超过十五分钟，但你的关节却仿佛已经坐了很久很久一样在嘎吱作响。“这个地方的内部面积比外部看起来要大得多，你居然还在担心这里的东西会不会合理吗？你就按你自己的想法去做吧。感受到 —事实证明，这是目前最明智的选择，因为整个荒废驿堡其实就是这些受伤灵魂的情感寄托。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我们得走了。 |就在你感觉自己快要被撕裂成碎片的时候，王座内部的压力突然消失了，你就像一块被拉伸后的黏液橡胶一样被猛地拉回自己的身体里，头晕目眩，完全无法理解这个世界的疯狂与不可思议。你惊呼着，拼命抓住一切可以抓住的东西，身体被猛地推向椅背，那把王座发出吱嘎声，仿佛随时都会在你重量之下坍塌。 而事实上，它确实坍塌了——在你脚下，变成了一堆碎片和毁坏的毛皮。当你喘过气来，你抬起头，看着眼前聚集的那些人——他们都是那些只剩下情感与支离破碎的记忆的人。他们的面容严肃，全部注意力都集中在你身上。 然后他们就转身离开了。 在此之前，你或许还以为，尽管发生了那些意外，事情还是有可能成功的；但现在很明显，他们认为你并不符合那些疯狂的家伙们用来认可权威的标准。它们不会等你将它们驱散——荒废驿堡要塞的守卫们迅速散开，就像来时一样快地消失在墙壁和地面之中。转瞬间，它们就消失得无影无踪，只留下你脊背上的寒意和心中沉重的感觉。 [pc.isDK |嗯，如果他们不愿意承认你的权威，那你只能采取强硬的手段了。事实上，这些顽固的人反而更好对付——虽然方式不同，但结果同样令人满意。 |如果当你的高贵身份面临考验时，事情会变成这样，那么或许你当初离开去追求自己的命运，反而比在这里为家里能给你的那点残羹剩饭而挣扎要好得多。 ]哼，”妮娜说道，“别太往心里去——他们确实有点不正常。至少他们没有当场直接攻击我们。虽然你和我都很厉害，但我觉得我们根本无法对抗整个驻军。光是在这个地方活动就已经让我们遇到了很多麻烦，所以……” 请别说情况还会更糟，因为总是情况可能会更糟。 “别太往心里去，伙计，”妮娜一边说，一边帮你从残余的王座上站起来。你在里面待的时间应该不超过十五分钟，但你的关节却像是坐了很久一样在嘎吱作响。“这个地方的内部面积比外部看起来要大得多，你还在担心这些会不会有什么不合理的地方吗？顺其自然就好。感受到 —事实证明，这是目前最明智的选择，因为整个荒废驿堡其实就是这些受伤心灵的写照。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我们得走了。 ]
rows.raw: " Sure, you weren't the heir — not even the spare, but the spare's spare — yet as a noble scion, you ought to have absorbed some of the lessons your siblings got on exerting one's noble presence. Besides, that sort of thing should come naturally to you, right? Right? Of course, impressing yourself upon a bunch of half-insane apparitions is bound to be harder than folks who're mostly your friends to begin with, but in essence being the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort past shouldn't be fundamentally different than being that of the Wayfort present. The psychic emanations surrounding the throne resonate with your focused will as you concentrate on filling your ego with that sense of grandiose command... This Wayfort is yours. Your blood is noble. [pc.isDK |They will recgonize you |By every means, you ought to be qualified ] — [pc.ra elf | |even if you aren't a boreal elf, ]you're the Champion of Frost and in good with the Var Ridells. You have every right to sit in this throne. By degrees, you feel your sense of self slipping out from the dais, crawling over the crumbling walls and floor, encircling the throne room with your noble presence. This is the sort of thing you might've been expected to do, had you been born earlier... and now by some quirk of fate, you've been given the chance to impress yourself upon a captive audience. Whether it's the throne itself or some fragment of the Wayfort's previous commander lodged within the fur and bone, the dreamlike emanations serve as a conduit for yourself; the remainder is up to you... [var1 |Just when you feel you're stretched impossibly thin over the floor and walls, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. But it doesn't. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Half of them are fading in and out of existence at this point, but even so your presence has stirred something within them; meeting your gaze, the garrison of Wayfort past stands at attention and salutes you. It worked, it actually worked. They recognize you. You think. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the shattered shades march out of the throne room with as much military precision as they can muster, as opposed to the way they arrived. [pc.isDK |Finally, someone actually respects your authority. Not the highest bar to clear, but it's a starting point from which to work your way up |It makes you a little emotional, the way they instinctively recognized you... no speeches, no words, just you and your raw presence ]. A dream, perhaps, of your lineage should be self-evident regardless of you being a so-called spare's spare. Not so surplus to requirements now, eh? Before too long, you're left alone with Nina in the dusty chamber, the aura about the throne gone now that its purpose has been fulfilled. "Huh," Nina says. "Now that's something. Guess you really are meant to lord it over all the Wayforts there are, aren't you? Past, present, future and all." Oh, come on. Now even she's laying it on thickly. But... it does feel gratifying to [pc.isDK |finally have your inherent nobility recognized and finally good for something. Others might call it unearned, but you know better |be accepted in this fashion, even if you had to leverage your noble lineage and training to get it done. It feels a little unearned, but you'll take every advantage you can get in this madhouse ]. "Yeah, okay, sure. What I do think is that now that they've accepted you, we'll be harassed less getting around this place. I'm sure there're a few stragglers too far gone to realize that there's new command in the Wayfort, but at least I get the feeling most of them won't be bothering us now that they think you're their boss." And all it took was you sitting in the throne for that to kick in. It makes sense in a way, there has to be a formal handing over of authority when it comes to these things, but here in this place there's just a little too much emphasis placed on the appearance of things to the point where it becomes the substance. "C'mon, man," Nina replies as she helps you out of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." |Just when you feel like you're being torn apart, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched, your head spinning from the impossible madness of this world. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. And that's exactly what it does, collapsing into a miserable pile of shards and ruined furs underneath you. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Their faces straight, they focus their attention solely on you. And then they turn their backs. Before then, you thought it might have worked despite the mishap, but this makes it clear they've found you lacking by whatever criteria half-mad shades use to acknowledge authority. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the garrison of Wayfort past scatters, disappearing into the walls and floor as quickly as they arrived. In the blink of an eye, there's nothing left of them but a chill across the length of your spine and a heaviness in your heart. [pc.isDK |Well, if they won't acknowledge your authority, you'll just have to do this the hard way. In fact, maybe it's better that these ghosts are recalcitrant — this will be just as satisfying, albeit in a different fashion |If this is how things turn out when your noble presence is put to the test, maybe it's better that you left to seek your fortune than scrabble for what scraps your family could spare you ]. "Huh," Nina says. "Don't take it too hard — they're not right in the head. I mean, at least they didn't outright attack us there and then. As great as you and I are, man, I don't think we're capable of standing up to an entire garrison. We're already being harassed getting around this place, so..." Please don't say that it can't get worse, because it always can get worse. "Don't get too sour about it, man," Nina replies as she helps you up and out of what remains of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." ] "

rows.original: Sure, you may not have been anyone of note when this adventure started, but you daresay that's changed by now. Not only are you [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort in the present day, but you're also the Champion of Frost — that gives you all the authority you need here, given that this was a boreal elf holding. Of course, impressing yourself upon a bunch of half-insane apparitions is bound to be harder than folks who're mostly your friends to begin with, but in essence being the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort past shouldn't be fundamentally different than being that of the Wayfort present. The psychic emanations surrounding the throne resonate with your focused will as you concentrate on filling your ego with that sense of grandiose command... The Wayfort is yours. You [flags.WAYFORT_OFFER 1 2 |were granted it from the var Ridells |took it fair and square — ownership is nine-tenths of the law, after all ]. That's all that's needed for this garrison to owe fealty to you in the lack of their original commander. You have every right to sit in this throne. You don't just deserve it, you earned it. They must recognize that. By degrees, you feel your sense of self slipping out from the dais, crawling over the crumbling walls and floor, encircling the throne room with your presence. You may not have been great, but greatness starts somewhere, and you've achieved far more in this short time than the vast majority of so-called bluebloods. Whether it's the throne itself or some fragment of the Wayfort's previous commander lodged within the fur and bone, the dreamlike emanations serve as a conduit for yourself; the remainder is up to you... I'm sure there're a few stragglers too far gone to realize that there's new command in the Wayfort, but at least I get the feeling most of them won't be bothering us now that they think you're their boss." |他们的认出你的方式，真的会让人感到一阵触动……没有演讲，没有言语，只有你，以及你真实的存在。曾经，这样的场景简直是不可思议的，但就像荒废驿堡所说，过去的你，已经不再是现在的你了。 ]伟大总得从某个地方开始，为什么不是从你这里呢？不久之后，你就只剩下自己和妮娜在那个布满灰尘的房间里了——既然王座的用途已经达成，它周围散发出的那种气息也早已消失了。 “哼，”妮娜说道，“这才叫有点意思呢。看来你真的注定要统领所有荒废驿堡家族，对吧？无论是过去的、现在的，还是未来的。 哦，得了吧。就连她也在故意夸大其词了。但是确实这种感觉很令人满足，即使你知道不应该因此而骄傲自满。这证明了，尽管一开始[pc.background]你真是混得越来越好了啊。 “嗯，好吧，当然。我确实觉得既然他们已经接受了你，我们在这个地方活动时应该会少遇到一些麻烦了。当然，肯定还有一些人顽固到根本意识不到荒废驿堡现在有了新的领导，但至少我觉得，既然他们认为你是他们的上司，大多数人应该不会再来打扰我们了。而这一切，只需要你坐在王位上，就能得以实现。从某种角度来看，这是合情合理的——在这种事情上，必须要有正式的权力交接仪式。但在这个地方，人们过于注重形式了，甚至让形式本身取代了实质内容。 来吧，伙计，”妮娜一边说，一边帮你从王座上下来。你在里面待的时间肯定不超过十五分钟，但你的关节却像是坐了很久很久一样在嘎吱作响。“这个地方的内部面积比外部看起来要大得多，你居然还在担心这里的东西会不会合乎常理吗？你就按你自己的想法去做吧。感受到 —事实证明，这是目前最明智的选择，因为整个荒废驿堡其实就是这些受伤灵魂的情感寄托。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我们得走了。 |就在你感觉自己快要被撕裂成碎片的时候，王座内部的压力突然消失了，你就像一块被拉伸后的黏液橡胶一样被猛地拉回自己的身体里，头晕目眩，完全无法理解这个世界的疯狂与荒谬。你喘着粗气，拼命抓住一切可以抓住的东西，身体被猛地撞在椅背上，王座也在你的重量下发出吱嘎声，仿佛随时都会坍塌下来。 事实也正是如此——在你脚下，那些碎片和毁坏的毛皮会塌成一堆凄惨的残骸。当你喘过气来，抬头望去，你会看到那些聚集在你面前的守卫们。他们的身影扭曲而残破，这些人已经失去了一切，只剩下情感和支离破碎的记忆。他们的目光直直地盯着你。 然后他们就转身离开了。 你可能会想，情况本可能更糟。他们本可以嘲笑你的尝试，或者因为你试图表达自己的观点而大发雷霆；但当你清楚地意识到自己并不具备所需的条件时，这种冷漠、无情的拒绝已经算是最好的结果了。无论那些半疯狂的生物使用什么标准来认定权威的存在，昔日的荒废驿堡驻军都会认为你不符合这些标准。他们甚至没有等你下令离开——荒废驿堡的驻军们迅速散开，就像他们出现时一样，瞬间消失在了墙壁和地面之中。转瞬间，它们便消失无踪，只留下一阵寒意顺着你的脊椎蔓延，以及心中沉重的压抑感。 [pc.isDK |好吧，如果他们不愿意承认你的权威，那你只能采取强硬的手段了。事实上，这些顽固的人反而更好对付——虽然方式不同，但结果同样令人满意。你会让他们知道，他们是无法小看你的。 |像你这样的无名小卒，显然必须达到更高的标准才能真正赢得别人的尊重；无论你在当今世界获得了什么样的荣誉，对于那些被囚禁在时空之中的幽灵们来说，这些都毫无意义。 ]哼，”妮娜说道，“别太往心里去——他们确实有点不正常。至少他们没有当场直接攻击我们。虽然你和我都很厉害，但我觉得我们根本无法对抗整个驻军。光是在这个地方活动就已经让我们受到了骚扰，所以……” 千万别说情况还会更糟，因为真的有可能的。总是情况可能会更糟的。 “别太往心里去，伙计，”妮娜一边说，一边帮你从残余的王座上站起来。你在里面待的时间应该不超过十五分钟，但你的关节却像是坐了很久一样在嘎吱作响。“这个地方的内部面积比外部看起来要大得多，你还在担心这些会不会有什么不合理的地方吗？顺其自然就好。感受到 —事实证明，这是目前最明智的选择，因为整个荒废驿堡其实就是这些受伤灵魂的情感寄托。现在，如果你们不介意的话，我们得走了。 ]
rows.raw: " Sure, you may not have been anyone of note when this adventure started, but you daresay that's changed by now. Not only are you [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort in the present day, but you're also the Champion of Frost — that gives you all the authority you need here, given that this was a boreal elf holding. Of course, impressing yourself upon a bunch of half-insane apparitions is bound to be harder than folks who're mostly your friends to begin with, but in essence being the [pc.mf |lord |lady ] of the Wayfort past shouldn't be fundamentally different than being that of the Wayfort present. The psychic emanations surrounding the throne resonate with your focused will as you concentrate on filling your ego with that sense of grandiose command... The Wayfort is yours. You [flags.WAYFORT_OFFER 1 2 |were granted it from the var Ridells |took it fair and square — ownership is nine-tenths of the law, after all ]. That's all that's needed for this garrison to owe fealty to you in the lack of their original commander. You have every right to sit in this throne. You don't just deserve it, you earned it. They must recognize that. By degrees, you feel your sense of self slipping out from the dais, crawling over the crumbling walls and floor, encircling the throne room with your presence. You may not have been great, but greatness starts somewhere, and you've achieved far more in this short time than the vast majority of so-called bluebloods. Whether it's the throne itself or some fragment of the Wayfort's previous commander lodged within the fur and bone, the dreamlike emanations serve as a conduit for yourself; the remainder is up to you... [var1 |Just when you feel you're stretched impossibly thin over the floor and walls, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. But it doesn't. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Half of them are fading in and out of existence at this point, but even so your presence has stirred something within them; meeting your gaze, the garrison of Wayfort past stands at attention and salutes you. It worked, it actually worked. They recognize you. You think. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the shattered shades march out of the throne room with as much military precision as they can muster, as opposed to the way they arrived. [pc.isDK |Finally, someone actually respects your authority. All the effort you spent clawing your way up into being someone, and finally others have no choice but to see the you that you've worked so hard to become |It makes you a little emotional, the way they recognized you... no speeches, no words, just you and your raw presence. Once, this would have been beyond impossible, but like the Wayfort, past you is no longer present you ]. Greatness has to start somewhere, and why not with you? Before too long, you're left alone with Nina in the dusty chamber, the aura about the throne gone now that its purpose has been fulfilled. "Huh," Nina says. "Now that's something. Guess you really are meant to lord it over all the Wayforts there are, aren't you? Past, present, future and all." Oh, come on. Now even she's laying it on thickly. But... it does feel gratifying, even if you know you shouldn't let it get to your head. It's proof that despite starting off as a [pc.background], you've really come up in the world. "Yeah, okay, sure. What I do think is that now that they've accepted you, we'll be harassed less getting around this place. I'm sure there're a few stragglers too far gone to realize that there's new command in the Wayfort, but at least I get the feeling most of them won't be bothering us now that they think you're their boss." And all it took was you sitting in the throne for that to kick in. It makes sense in a way, there has to be a formal handing over of authority when it comes to these things, but here in this place there's just a little too much emphasis placed on the appearance of things to the point where it becomes the substance. "C'mon, man," Nina replies as she helps you out of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." |Just when you feel like you're being torn apart, the pressure from within the throne suddenly fades, and you're flung back into your body like a piece of slime-latex snapping back from being stretched, your head spinning from the impossible madness of this world. Gasping, you hold on for dear life as you're thrown against the backrest, the throne creaking like it might collapse under your weight any moment. And that's exactly what it does, collapsing into a miserable pile of shards and ruined furs underneath you. As you catch your breath, you raise your eyes to the garrison assembled before you, those twisted, broken echoes of people with nothing left but emotions and half-torn memories. Their faces straight, they focus their attention solely on you. And then they turn their backs. It could've been worse, you suppose. They could've mocked your attempt, or flown into a rage at your attempt to assert yourself; cold, stony rejection is about the best you could've hoped for once it became clear you didn't have what it took. Whatever criteria half-mad shades use to acknowledge authority, the former Wayfort garrison finds you lacking by those standards. They don't wait for you to dismiss them — the garrison of Wayfort past scatters, disappearing into the walls and floor as quickly as they arrived. In the blink of an eye, there's nothing left of them but a chill across the length of your spine and a heaviness in your heart. [pc.isDK |Well, if they won't acknowledge your authority, you'll just have to do this the hard way. In fact, maybe it's better that these ghosts are recalcitrant — this will be just as satisfying, albeit in a different fashion. You'll teach them to look down on you |Guess a nobody like you needs to clear a higher bar to actually earn some respect; whatever accolades you may have earned in the present-day world, they mean nothing to these shades caught in time and space ]. "Huh," Nina says. "Don't take it too hard — they're not right in the head. I mean, at least they didn't outright attack us there and then. As great as you and I are, man, I don't think we're capable of standing up to an entire garrison. We're already being harassed getting around this place, so..." Please don't say that it can't get worse, because it always can get worse. "Don't get too sour about it, man," Nina replies as she helps you up and out of what remains of the throne. You can't have been in there longer than fifteen minutes, but your joints creak like you've been seated for an eternity. "This place is bigger on the inside that it is on the outside, and you're worried about anything making sense? Just go with what you feel — that's turned out to be the best bet so far, given that this entire Wayfort is literally the feelings of all these broken souls. Now, if you don't mind, we've got to go." ]"

rows.original:
You're not quite prepared for whatever's about to happen. Focusing furiously, you wrench yourself off the throne with a concerted effort — your limbs feel leaden and your body resists you, but the throne itself is ambivalent about the entire thing and doesn't stop you as you stand and totter away from it. No, that was all you...

        Still, it remains there, inviting you to return when you're ready, if you ever will be.
rows.translation:
你还没有为即将发生的事情做好充分的准备。你集中全部力量，拼命地将自己从王座上拽了下来——你的四肢仿佛被铅块绑住般沉重，身体也在极力抵抗你的动作，但王座本身似乎对这一切无动于衷，也没有阻止你站起身来，摇摇晃晃地离开那里。不，那全是你自己做到的……

        然而，王座依然留在那里，仿佛在邀请你：当你准备好了——如果真的有一天你准备好的话——随时都可以回来。

        Still, it remains there, inviting you to return when you're ready, if you ever will be."

rows.original: Examine the chest in the corner.
rows.translation: 去角落里的那个箱子看看吧。

rows.original:
While the old watchtower has been frozen in a state of utter chaos, a stash set into several shelves catches your eye. Its metal bandings glistening in the otherworldly glow that suffuses this twisted ruin, it's a small bastion of order amidst this sea of chaos.

    [pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte
        |You've come across these before in your past — wordlock chests, a favorite of the old Belharan nobility, meant to safeguard valuables from illiterate [silly
            |players
            |servants
        ]. Each of these combination locks was secured by a password, and to help the owner remember what it was, a riddle was often posed on the chest itself. If you could solve it and thereby rotate the tumblers into the right position, the chest would unlock and allow you to claim its contents.
        
        "Oh, a wordlock," Nina muses. "Pawned off a couple of them for drinking money before. They're good for two whole weeks to a month, depending on how well preserved they are. Good times, man."
        
        Huh, is she sure? These things are relics at this point and would be worth more in themselves to a collector than the contents they'd be holding. Where did she get said wordlocks to cash in?
        
        "Oh. Here and there — things get lost in all kinds of corners. They weren't owned by anyone when I picked them up, so if that's what you're worried about you can rest easy. People lose all kinds of things all the time, and the visions tell me where to find them, man. It doesn't make me rich or anything, but is just enough to keep body and spirit together in this cold, hard world."
        |Hmm, what can this all mean? It certainly seems like a thoroughly roundabout way to secure a container, but at least it isn't likely to be trapped in the bargain. You test the mechanism a few times, turn the tumblers, but nothing happens.
        
        "Oh, a wordlock," Nina muses. "Pawned off a couple of them for drinking money before. They're good for two whole weeks to a month, depending on how well preserved they are. Good times, man."
        
        Can she open it up?
        
        "Never bothered to try." Nina's good eye goes out of focus, as if she's lost in thought. Or drunk, but that's not likely given the circumstances. "The chests themselves are usually worth more than the stuff they hold these days; most of those I've come across were nailed down.
        
        "Aanyway. If you want it open, that's simple. There's a riddle on the chest... solve it and it opens. A silly novelty, man, but like, you've got to respect rich peoples' quirks, that's how it goes."
    ]
    
    Well, given that this memory of the Wayfort's past dates to the Godswar, at least the time period matches up. You could have a go at opening it up, if you like.
rows.translation:
虽然那座古老的瞭望塔早已陷入一片混乱之中，但架在几层架子上的那些物品却吸引了你的注意。它们的金属带在笼罩着这片荒废之地的那种超凡光芒中闪闪发光，在这片混乱之中，它们仿佛是一片秩序的象征。

    [pc.bg noblescion courtesan scholar acolyte
        |你在过去曾经见过这类东西——词锁箱。这种箱子曾是贝尔哈兰老贵族们的最爱，他们用它来保护贵重物品，防止那些不识字的人偷走它们。 [silly
            |玩家们
            |仆从们
        ]这些组合锁每一把都需要输入密码才能打开，为了帮助主人记住密码，人们通常会在箱子上设置谜语。如果你能够解开这个谜语，将锁芯旋转到正确的位置，箱子就会打开，让你取走里面的物品。
        
        哦，原来是字谜啊，”尼娜若有所思地说，“之前我卖掉过几个来换酒喝。这些字谜能使用两星期到一个月，具体时长取决于保存得怎么样。那些日子真是美好啊。”
        
        “哈，她确定吗？这些东西现在都已经成了古董，对收藏家来说，它们本身的价值远比里面装的东西要高。她是从哪里得到这些密码锁来兑换现金的？
        
        “哦，到处都是——这些东西总会掉在各种角落里。当我捡到它们的时候，它们根本不属于任何人，所以如果你是在担心这个问题的话，可以放心了。人们总是会丢失各种各样的东西，而那些幻象会告诉我该去哪里找到它们。这些东西虽然不能让我变得富有，但至少足以让我在这个寒冷而艰难的世界里维持生计。"
        |嗯，这一切到底意味着什么呢？这种方式看起来确实有些迂回，但至少不会让人陷入不必要的麻烦。你试了几次这个装置，转动了那些旋钮，但什么反应也没有发生。
        
        哦，是一个字谜锁，”尼娜喃喃道，“之前为了买酒，我把其中几个卖掉了。这些字谜锁能使用两到一周的时间，具体时长取决于它们的保存状况如何。那些日子真是美好啊。”
        
        她能打开它吗？
        
        从来都没想过要试试。”尼娜的目光渐渐变得恍惚，仿佛陷入了沉思。或者说是喝醉了，但考虑到当时的情况，这种可能性似乎不大。“如今，这些宝箱本身的价值通常都比里面装的东西要高；我见过的那些宝箱，大多数都被钉住了。
        
        不管怎样，如果你想打开它，其实很简单。箱子上有个谜题……解开谜题就能打开它。虽然有点无聊又新奇，但嘛，你总得尊重富人的怪癖，就是这么回事。
    ]
    
    嗯，既然这段关于荒废驿堡过去的记忆可以追溯到“神战”时期，那么至少时间上是吻合的。如果你愿意的话，可以试着打开它看看。

rows.original: You rub your temples and sigh. The riddle's right there in front of you, but its words might as well have been unscalable walls. Whatever's in the chest is going to have to stay inside until you figure this out.
rows.translation: 你揉了揉太阳穴，叹了口气。这个谜题就摆在你的眼前，但它的答案仿佛就是一道无法逾越的墙。直到你解开这个谜团，箱子里的东西才会被取出。
rows.raw: "\n    You rub your temples and sigh. The riddle's right there in front of you, but its words might as well have been unscalable walls. Whatever's in the chest is going to have to stay inside until you figure this out."

rows.original: Something within the chest clicks, followed by a loud thump as the mechanisms within disengage. Instinctively, you step back, fearing a trap, but your fears are soon allayed as the spring-loaded lid pops open, revealing the chest's contents. Within are several bottles which Nina shuffles over to inspect, only to have her dismay make clear as she realizes it's not booze. "Aw. Man, I could use a drink." Now, now, just because she can't get at her own stash doesn't mean she has to raid other peoples'. No, you're raiding this stash because you're adventurers. "That joke was like, totally flat, man." Yeah, everyone's a critic. Nevertheless, you pull out the dusty bottles and examine the stash — the labels are written in antiquated Belharan, but you figure the lot's a bunch of alchemical concoctions, several decanters of conjuror's concoction amongst them. You gain 3x Vulnerary, 2x Naphtha and 2x Conjuror's Concoction. You're putting the find away when you hear a grunt from Nina. The silly bird-brain has her hands on the lid and is trying to lift the wordlock chest out of its resting place, only to find that it's screwed down where it stands. "Oh, come on!" she groans after yet another failed attempt to make off with the chest. "This is totally not cool, man." After realizing the value of the chest itself? Nah, every wordlock you've come across has been nailed or screwed down tight. Come on, there's no point in wasting one's strength — there's still the rest of the Wayfort to explore.
rows.translation: 箱内传来一声咔嗒，随后内部机械脱开，发出响亮的砰声。你本能地后退，担心触发了陷阱；但弹簧驱动的箱盖猛然打开，露出里面的东西，很快便打消了你的忧虑。箱中摆着几只瓶子，妮娜凑过去查看；发现里面装的不是酒，她顿时毫不掩饰地露出失望之色。 “唉，伙计。我真想喝一杯。” 好啦，好啦，就算她拿不到自己的存货，也不代表该洗劫别人的酒藏。你们来洗劫这批东西，是因为你们是冒险者。 “伙计，这笑话简直逊爆了。” 是啊，人人都是评论家。尽管如此，你仍取出那些落满灰尘的瓶子，检查起这批存货——标签由古贝尔哈兰文字写成，不过你推测这些都是炼金调配物，其中还有几瓶术士的调配药剂。 你获得了3份伤药、2份石脑油和2份术士的调配药剂。 你正在收起找到的东西，忽然听见妮娜发出一声闷哼。那个脑袋空空的傻鸟正抓着箱盖，试图把词锁箱从安放的位置搬走，却发现它早已被螺钉固定在原地。 “哦，拜托了，真是的！”她又一次试图搬走箱子失败后呻吟道。“这太不够意思了，伙计。” 她是发现箱子本身的价值了？不，你遇见的每一只词锁箱都被钉死或牢牢拧在地上。行了，没必要白费力气——驿堡里还有其余地方等待探索。

rows.original:
Carefully, you make your way amongst the wrecked bookshelves — at a glance, most of the space is filled by archives of the Wayfort's everyday activities, with one corner dedicated to more private reading material. Even discounting the ravaged volumes frozen mid-fall, there's more than what you could ever get through stashed away in the old watchtower. Paradoxically, you don't have the luxury of dithering in a place where time doesn't flow... not if you want to get out of here in one piece, anyway.

    Come to think of it, the shelves and books weren't here by the time you found the Wayfort in the present day, not even rotted wood and crumbled scraps. It may have been a couple of centuries, but where did this all go?
    
    [pc.hasPerk SecondSight
        |Something at the edge of your vision catches your eye, though — a faint purple glow that vanishes when you try to look at it directly. Peering out the corner of your eye, you note that the collapsed bookshelf by the far western wall gives off a faint light when you're not focusing on it — maybe that's your mind's way of telling you that it's important. It may be worth investigating and making note of what information's to be had in there.
    ]
rows.translation:
你小心翼翼地穿过那些损毁的书架——一眼望去，大部分空间都存放着关于荒废驿堡日常活动的档案资料，而其中一个角落则专门用来放置一些更为私人的阅读材料。即便不计算那些在坠落过程中被损坏、还停留在半空中未能掉落的书籍，这个旧瞭望塔里储存的资料数量也远远超过了你能够在短时间内阅读完的量。具有讽刺意味的是，在这样一个时间流逝根本不存在的地方，你根本没有犹豫的余地……至少，如果你想平安离开这里的话，是绝对没有这样的机会的。

    仔细想想，当你在这个现代世界找到荒废驿堡的时候，那些书架和书籍根本就不存在，甚至连腐烂的木头和碎屑都没有。虽然可能已经过去了几百年，但这一切究竟都去了哪里呢？
    
    [pc.hasPerk SecondSight
        |然而，你的视线边缘突然有 something 吸引了你的注意——那是一种淡淡的紫色光芒，当你试图直接注视它时，它又会消失不见。你用眼角的余光观察，发现位于最西侧墙边的那个倒塌的书架，在你没有刻意注视它的时候，会发出微弱的光芒。也许，这是你的大脑在告诉你，这个书架很重要，值得你去探究一下，看看里面究竟藏着什么信息。
    ]

rows.original: With a plethora of volumes to choose from in the archives, you pick one of the tattered scraps out at random and briefly flip through it, hoping to gain any kind of useful information... ...Nothing can be seen from our position due to the thick black and green smoke coming from the direction of Castle Hawkstone, but plenty can be heard still. The imperials retreating north from their settlements bring with them news of Victor Reverra's death, and one can only assume the explosion we saw was his daughter's demise as well. We're obligated by the treaty to house the imperials along with the rest of the garrison, and they look like they can fight. With any luck, we'll all be dead before we have time to starve. It looks like the besiegers will eventually arrive on our doorstep, and though the River Ridell and its bridge make for a natural funnel and chokepoint we can't overrely on it. The imperials speak of their experiences with these demons from beyond — even though their forces are capable of neutralizing the thralls and willing servants, the primary threat stems from the demons themselves. Although the imperials are quite unnerved and hysterical, I feel that their claims of the demons being impervious to conventional attacks has the ring of truth to it. Their accounts all match up on the important points, especially the claim that enormous amounts of ley-crystal are the only thing capable of even hurting the monsters. Needless to say, we don't have that kind of luxury. Despite the fact that several straggling groups of thralls have already been dispatched before even reaching the river, the garrison is more than aware that these are advance scouts. Sightings of ceaseless combat activity to the south has everyone on edge; reports say that the southern valley and forest have had their population centers decimated. The only hope is potential reinforcements promised from Tychris, but even if those do arrive in time people are unsure if that will change anything. Needless to say, morale is low. I have no active outriders to spare, only a few remain to garrison the keep while the others evacuate anyone who can't fight to the Winter City. Surprisingly, no one bemoans the loss of so-called camp followers at this juncture... (The log is missing several pages. By the time the writing is legible again, the narrative's moved on to another entry.) ...Some minor skirmishes have been reported in the southern forest, but nothing more has happened here since yesterday's bombardment. It appears that all the siege engines are grouped up with the renegade mages in order to effect a coordinated attack, with the exception of two engines to the west. The aid from Tychris is supposed to arrive tomorrow, but I can't fathom what sort of help they can send at this point. The principality, the imperial settlement of Hawkethorne, and the luxury resort the imperials built atop the mountain have been the main centers of heavy fighting so far; the minotaurs have retreated into their mountain and the lupines simply scatter and vanish about any concentrated force brought against them. Such tactics won't last of course, but for now they avoid fighting and take few casualties. Unfortunately, large exposed structures like Castle Hawkstone and this wayfort are easy targets, and so they move to pick low-hanging fruit first. So far the undermountain is safe, but the stories from the imperials of the use of gaseous miasma during the assault on Castle Hawkstone leaves me in doubt as to their long-term survival. I never imagined such a thought would even appear let alone coalesce in my mind, but there is no hope. It is over. When the demons from beyond the veil do finally annihilate everything on the surface, they will flush out survivors with miasma to be eliminated; events up to this point have given me no reason to believe otherwise. Estelore is so close to the Marches... if only we had hanged all those wizards before they could have caused this calamity and revealed our existence to these demons beyond the veil, but the past can't be changed. Who am I writing this final report to? If you are reading this I am already dead. If you threw your lot in with the demons, I hope you and your kind burns until the end of time for what you've done. If not, then know that there used to be a whole world here, and that its inhabitants fought bravely to preserve it. ...No, this is silly. Now isn't the time to wax poetical. I think the reinforcements from Tychris are at the gate...
rows.translation: 在档案中有大量卷册可供选择，你随意拿出一本破旧的书页，快速翻阅了几下，希望能从中获得一些有用的信息…… 由于从霍克斯通城堡方向飘来了浓重的黑烟和绿烟，我们从当前的位置根本无法看到任何景象，但仍然能够听到许多声音。那些从定居点向北撤退的帝国军队带来了维克托·雷维拉死亡的消息，因此我们可以推测，我们所看到的那场爆炸，也是他女儿的死亡。根据条约的规定，我们有义务为这些帝国军队以及其他驻军提供住宿，而他们看起来也具备作战能力。如果运气好的话，我们可能还没等饿死，就已经全部死了。 看来围攻者最终会来到我们的门前。虽然里德尔河及其桥梁构成了天然的屏障和要塞，但我们不能过分依赖这一点。帝国军队谈到了他们与这些来自异界的恶魔打交道的经验——尽管他们的军队有能力消灭那些被恶魔控制的奴仆和忠实追随者，但真正的威胁仍然来自于这些恶魔本身。尽管那些帝国人士表现得非常慌乱和歇斯底里，但我认为他们关于那些怪物对常规攻击具有抗性的说法确实有一定的真实性。他们的描述在关键点上是一致的，尤其是那种认为只有大量的 ley-crystal 才能真正伤害到那些怪物的说法。 不用说，我们根本没有这样的奢侈条件。尽管在那些散落的奴役者队伍甚至还没到达河边时，就已经有好几支队伍被派了出去，但驻军非常清楚，这些其实只是先遣侦察队而已。据报道，南部地区持续不断的战斗活动让所有人都感到忧心忡忡；有消息称，南部的山谷和森林地区的居民中心已经遭受了严重破坏。目前唯一的希望就是来自提克里斯的援军，但即便这些援军能够及时赶到，人们也不确定这是否真的能够改变当前的局势。毫无疑问，大家的士气都很低落。 我手头上已经没有可派出的骑兵了，只剩下少数人留守要塞，而其他骑兵则把那些无法参战的人都疏散到了冬城。令人惊讶的是，在这个节骨眼上，竟然没有人为失去这些所谓的“随军人员”而抱怨…… 这本日志缺失了几页。等到剩下的内容再次变得可以辨认时，故事情节已经发展到了另一页了。 据报道，南部森林发生了一些小规模冲突，但自昨天的轰炸之后，这里再没有发生任何事情。看来，所有的攻城器械都已经与那些叛变的法师们集结在一起，准备发动协同攻击，只有西边的两台器械除外。 提克里斯方面的援助应该会在明天到达，但我实在想不明白他们此时能提供什么样的帮助。到目前为止，这个公国、鹰棘镇帝国定居点，以及帝国在山上建造的豪华度假村，一直都是战斗的主要发生地；那些弥诺陶洛斯已经退回了他们的山区，而那些狼族一旦遇到任何规模的敌军，就会四散逃窜、消失无踪。这样的策略当然无法长久持续，但眼下它们避免了战斗，也因此减少了人员伤亡。不幸的是，像霍克斯通城堡这样的大型暴露建筑，以及这些交通要道，都很容易成为攻击目标，因此它们暂时选择先攻击这些容易得手的对象。到目前为止，地下山域还算安全，但那些帝国军队在进攻霍克斯通城堡时使用了有毒气体这一事实，让我对他们能否长期生存产生了怀疑。 我从未想过这样的想法会出现在我的脑海中，更别说它还会逐渐成形。但已经没有希望了，一切都结束了。当那些隐藏在幕后、邪恶的力量最终摧毁地表上的一切时，它们会用瘴气将幸存者驱赶出来，然后将其消灭；到目前为止发生的一切，都让我没有理由相信情况会有所不同。埃斯托洛尔距离边境地区如此之近……要是我们能在那些巫师造成这场灾难、让那些隐藏在迷雾之外的恶魔发现我们的存在之前就把他们全部处死该多好，但过去的事情已经无法改变了。 我究竟是在给谁写这份最终报告呢？如果你正在读这些文字，那么我早已死去。如果你选择了与恶魔为伍，那么我希望你和你的同类会因为自己的所作所为而永远受到惩罚。但如果并非如此，那么请记住：这里曾经存在着一个完整的世界，它的居民们也曾为守护它而英勇战斗。 ……不，这样太愚蠢了。现在不是搞文艺抒情的时候。我觉得来自提克里斯的援军应该已经到门口了……
