rows.original: ...Victor Reverra's gift of a lupine statue is a veiled snub, I'm sure of it. The Wayfort sits on the River Ridell and has marked the domain of the var Ridell line since the treaty with the empire, and yet the statue was that of a lupine rather than a boreal elf. He knows full well that the lupines still lay claim to parts of the Frostwood as their ancestral territory, this wayfort included. Yet I can't refuse without appearing petulant myself. The statue is undoubtedly masterwork, complete with a protective glaze made to order in Tychris such that the gem set into the stone might be displayed prominently without fear of theft or damage from the elements. I won't put it in the southern courtyard — surely there's a dignified corner out of the way where I can hide it while plausibly showing it respect or something. I'll have to call the archivist over this evening — he knows more about imperial customs than I do. Surely there's some kind of loophole we can use to snub him right back without making fools of ourselves. I'm most suspicious about the gem, though. I know I'm not warranted something like that... I need to send for a druid from the palace, have it looked over. Nothing about this sits right... (Several pages are missing from the log) ...I'm not sure why Victor Reverra has asked if he can use the Wayfort as a venue to host his demonstration. It's true that Castle Hawkstone is remote and we sit right here on the River Ridell, but these are supposed to be wizards that he's hosting. Surely imperials would be more comfortable on imperial land? I've asked the archivist and his answer is that it's likely to be imperial politics; that the territory of the boer'alvar is seen as natural territory free of imperial squabbles. Thank the Wyld that we don't have anything like that; everyone loves and respects the var Ridells. I'd rather not him drag us into petty human squabbles, but he is paying a lot. Maybe those rumors about him sitting on a literal mountain of gold in the crags beneath his castle are real. I recognize none of these names on the guest list, but all of them are wizards from Estelore and there are a lot of them. I'll have to source all the mirrorwine I can somehow — given that it's the only true luxury our lands produce that the imperials really want, I'm sure the wizards will take to it well. Still, so many wizards in one place... if something were to happen, no one would really miss us, would they? Well, the var Ridells would, but what are they going to do against the Belharans? Send a strongly-worded letter? Maybe I can take a few bottles of mirrorwine for myself... (More missing pages) Now I know why Victor wants us to host his demonstration. All the platitudes about cooperation between Belhar and the pale elves — at least, that's what he calls us — aside, the man arrived with his daughter Carmen and nephew Michael to deliver the subjects of the event. Stone constructs fashioned with the same dreary aesthetic that pervades his entire castle, no doubt some inside joke that we're not privy to. Though inactive at the time of delivery, he was rather proud of them, saying that they were indistinguishable from the average person with all relevant faculties. Ordinarily, there should be nothing strange about this — my time with the druids at the temple of terrestrial flame has made me familiar with elemental spirits of varying degrees of sapience. But Victor claims that his %"gargoyles" are fully constructs, that he fashioned their intelligences himself. That has to be a lie — you can't create something like that out of thin air, it goes against everything we know. No doubt every wizard at the meet he's called will be trying to disprove his claim in every imaginable fashion, magical and mundane. My head hurts. I should never have agreed to this — we'll be getting off lightly if they merely turn the Wayfort upside-down. And am I going to be the one to say no to a bunch of imperial wizards? Michael's a new one — I understand he's being tutored at Estelore itself, and is only here because the students are dismissed in the spring so their teachers can get drunk for the entire season and retire to their bathouses. Still, the fellow's more likeable than his uncle and possesses a curiosity about the world that his cousin lacks. Unlike every single imperial wizard I've met, he's open to experience and the path less traveled, which is rare amongst his kind given that they live and die by their spells and theories. Not too unlike our druids, if you look at it the right way... I spoke with Michael some, and he confessed that since his cousin had other interests Victor had requested his help with these %"gargoyles", and that made his uncle and him the only two people privy to the secrets of their creation — if it's not all a fraud to begin with, which I think increasingly likely. No doubt he intends to ride Victor's coattails to wizardly fame at a young age.
rows.translation: 我敢肯定，维克托·雷维拉赠送的那座狼族雕像其实是一种隐晦的嘲讽。荒废驿堡家族世代居住在里德尔河沿岸，自与帝国签订条约以来，这片土地一直属于里德尔家族的领地。然而，他赠送的雕像却是狼族的形象，而不是极北精灵的…… 他非常清楚，那些狼族仍然将弗罗斯特伍德的某些地区视为他们的祖传领地，包括这个地方在内。 然而，如果我拒绝，反而会显得自己很任性。这座雕像无疑是一件杰作，其表面还涂有一层特别制作的保护涂层——这种涂层是在提克里斯专门定制的，这样一来，镶嵌在石头中的宝石就能得到妥善保护，既不会被偷走，也不会受到自然环境的影响而受损。我不会把它放在南院里——肯定有某个不显眼、体面的角落可以把它藏起来，同时还能显得我是在尊重它之类的。今晚我得把档案管理员叫过来，他对宫廷礼仪的了解比我多。肯定存在某种漏洞，我们可以利用它来回击他，而不会让自己出丑。 不过，我最怀疑的还是那颗宝石知道我并没有理由要求那样的事情……我需要去宫殿请一位德鲁伊来检查一下。这件事有些地方明显不对劲…… 日志中缺少了几页内容。 我不太明白为什么维克托·雷维拉会询问是否可以使用荒废驿堡作为举办演示活动的场所。的确，霍克斯通城堡地处偏远地区，而我们所在的地点也靠近里德尔河，但毕竟他邀请来的是巫师们啊。在帝国的土地上，帝国主义者们肯定会更加自在吧？ 我询问过档案管理员，他的回答是，这很可能是出于帝国政治的考虑；在人们看来，布尔人的领地是属于自然领土，不应该成为帝国之间争斗的对象。幸好我们没有遇到那样的事情；大家都喜爱并尊重里德尔一家。我真不希望他把我们卷入那些无聊的人际纷争之中。是花费可真不小啊。也许那些关于他城堡下方山洞里堆满了黄金的传闻是真的。 名单上的这些名字我一个都不认识，但他们全都是来自埃斯托洛的巫师。而且人数众多。我得想办法弄到尽可能多的镜像酒——毕竟这是我们这片土地上唯一真正能让帝国人士垂涎的奢侈品，我相信巫师们也会很欢迎这种酒的。不过，这么多巫师聚集在同一个地方……如果发生了什么，其实也没人会真正想念我们，对吧？嗯，里德尔一家会想念我们的，但他们又能对贝拉尔人做什么呢？难道就寄一封措辞严厉的信吗？ 或许我可以自己拿几瓶镜像酒…… （还有更多缺失的页面） 现在我明白为什么维克托希望我们来举办他的演示活动了。那些关于贝尔哈尔与苍白精灵之间应该合作的陈词滥调——至少他是这么称呼我们的——其实都无关紧要。这个人带着他的女儿卡门和侄子迈克尔来到了现场，为这次活动准备所需的参与者。这些石制构造物同样秉承着他整个城堡所特有的那种单调、乏味的审美风格，想必这是某种只有内部人才懂的幽默吧。虽然在这些构造物被交付过来的时候它们已经处于闲置状态，但他对此还是感到相当自豪，他说这些构造物与那些具备所有正常功能的人相比，根本没有任何区别。 通常来说，这件事并没有什么奇怪的——我在大地之火神庙与德鲁伊们共度的时光，让我对各种智慧程度的元素精灵有了了解。但维克多声称，他的那些“石像鬼”完全是人造的，是他亲自赋予了它们智慧的。那肯定是在撒谎——不可能凭空创造出这样的东西，这与我们所知道的一切都相违背。毫无疑问，被他邀请来的每一位巫师都会想尽一切办法，无论是用魔法还是普通的手段，来反驳他的说法。 我的头好疼。我当初真不该同意这件事的——如果他们只是把荒废驿堡彻底搞得乱七八糟，我们还算运气好的了。真是的我难道要由我来拒绝那一群帝国巫师吗？ 迈克尔是个新人——我知道他正在埃斯托洛尔接受指导，他之所以来到这里，只是因为学生们会在春天放假，这样他们的老师就可以整个季节都喝得酩酊大醉，然后去浴室休息了。不过，这个家伙比他的叔叔更讨人喜欢，而且他对这个世界充满了好奇心，这是他的表弟所没有的。与我遇到的所有帝国巫师不同，他愿意去体验那些少有人走的道路，而在他的同类中，这种态度实在是非常罕见的——毕竟他们的一生都是围绕着魔法和理论来度过的。如果从某个角度来看的话，这与我们的德鲁伊们其实并没有太大区别…… 我和迈克尔聊过一些，他承认，因为他的表弟有其他兴趣爱好，维克多便请求他帮忙制作这些“滴水嘴兽”，因此他和他的叔叔成为了唯一了解这些装置制作秘密的人——当然，如果这一切从一开始就是一场骗局的话，那情况就另当别论了……而我觉得，这种可能性正在逐渐增加。毫无疑问，他打算借助维克托的名声，在年纪尚小的时候就一举成名。
rows.raw: " ...Victor Reverra's gift of a lupine statue is a veiled snub, I'm sure of it. The Wayfort sits on the River Ridell and has marked the domain of the var Ridell line since the treaty with the empire, and yet the statue was that of a lupine rather than a boreal elf. He knows full well that the lupines still lay claim to parts of the Frostwood as their ancestral territory, this wayfort included. Yet I can't refuse without appearing petulant myself. The statue is undoubtedly masterwork, complete with a protective glaze made to order in Tychris such that the gem set into the stone might be displayed prominently without fear of theft or damage from the elements. I won't put it in the southern courtyard — surely there's a dignified corner out of the way where I can hide it while plausibly showing it respect or something. I'll have to call the archivist over this evening — he knows more about imperial customs than I do. Surely there's some kind of loophole we can use to snub him right back without making fools of ourselves. I'm most suspicious about the gem, though. I know I'm not warranted something like that... I need to send for a druid from the palace, have it looked over. Nothing about this sits right... (Several pages are missing from the log) ...I'm not sure why Victor Reverra has asked if he can use the Wayfort as a venue to host his demonstration. It's true that Castle Hawkstone is remote and we sit right here on the River Ridell, but these are supposed to be wizards that he's hosting. Surely imperials would be more comfortable on imperial land? I've asked the archivist and his answer is that it's likely to be imperial politics; that the territory of the boer'alvar is seen as natural territory free of imperial squabbles. Thank the Wyld that we don't have anything like that; everyone loves and respects the var Ridells. I'd rather not him drag us into petty human squabbles, but he is paying a lot. Maybe those rumors about him sitting on a literal mountain of gold in the crags beneath his castle are real. I recognize none of these names on the guest list, but all of them are wizards from Estelore and there are a lot of them. I'll have to source all the mirrorwine I can somehow — given that it's the only true luxury our lands produce that the imperials really want, I'm sure the wizards will take to it well. Still, so many wizards in one place... if something were to happen, no one would really miss us, would they? Well, the var Ridells would, but what are they going to do against the Belharans? Send a strongly-worded letter? Maybe I can take a few bottles of mirrorwine for myself... (More missing pages) Now I know why Victor wants us to host his demonstration. All the platitudes about cooperation between Belhar and the pale elves — at least, that's what he calls us — aside, the man arrived with his daughter Carmen and nephew Michael to deliver the subjects of the event. Stone constructs fashioned with the same dreary aesthetic that pervades his entire castle, no doubt some inside joke that we're not privy to. Though inactive at the time of delivery, he was rather proud of them, saying that they were indistinguishable from the average person with all relevant faculties. Ordinarily, there should be nothing strange about this — my time with the druids at the temple of terrestrial flame has made me familiar with elemental spirits of varying degrees of sapience. But Victor claims that his %"gargoyles" are fully constructs, that he fashioned their intelligences himself. That has to be a lie — you can't create something like that out of thin air, it goes against everything we know. No doubt every wizard at the meet he's called will be trying to disprove his claim in every imaginable fashion, magical and mundane. My head hurts. I should never have agreed to this — we'll be getting off lightly if they merely turn the Wayfort upside-down. And am I going to be the one to say no to a bunch of imperial wizards? Michael's a new one — I understand he's being tutored at Estelore itself, and is only here because the students are dismissed in the spring so their teachers can get drunk for the entire season and retire to their bathouses. Still, the fellow's more likeable than his uncle and possesses a curiosity about the world that his cousin lacks. Unlike every single imperial wizard I've met, he's open to experience and the path less traveled, which is rare amongst his kind given that they live and die by their spells and theories. Not too unlike our druids, if you look at it the right way... I spoke with Michael some, and he confessed that since his cousin had other interests Victor had requested his help with these %"gargoyles", and that made his uncle and him the only two people privy to the secrets of their creation — if it's not all a fraud to begin with, which I think increasingly likely. No doubt he intends to ride Victor's coattails to wizardly fame at a young age."

rows.original: ...This %"godsworn" from Tychris is efficient. Infuriating and imposing, no doubt, but also extremely efficient. Thalia Star-Viewer, she calls herself — I note she hides her Tychrisian last name from us with this moniker — and the powers she wields are extremely effective at slaying the first waves of wraith-thralls sent at us. I would expect that to be the case, given that by her own admission she was reshaped by her goddess into a weapon tailored to destroy everything linked to the demons from beyond the veil. Well, that and now that the southern roads have been cut off, the Tychrisian reinforcements will share the same fate we do. The effect that Thalia and her retinue of frostmanders have had on the remaining outriders is unmistakable: where the Wyld and our druids have failed, the gods of the imperials succeed. Why these gods allowed things to come to this point and only intervene when the entire world lies in ruin is beyond me, but anything that aides the garrison is welcome. While I can't bring myself to believe in these southern gods the way Thalia clearly does, it's clear that some of the garrison are overawed at what this so-called godsworn is capable of. The changes wrought upon her body have disfigured her, but she wears that crippling as a mark of pride and devotion. ...What has happened to Tychris? What has happened to Njorhaalt? A terrible calamity engulfs the world, and these southern gods the imperials worship manifest and step in to save it in the nick of time. People are grateful, overawed; they kneel before these gods for having saved them. If I were any more cynical than I am, I would have suspected a ruse; yet gods with these powers would not need to concoct a crisis to gather followers. For all its failures in defending us, I feel that the Wyld deserves more, that we shouldn't just throw away the beliefs and spirits that sustained us just because of a single failure. But maybe the archivist is right, and I'm just nostalgic for a better age. Whatever my private thoughts, there's now hope for this wayfort, something I thought lost; I'm not so petty as to try and take it from my outriders. (Several pages are missing from the log) I feel like a failure. Before Thalia's arrival, the situation seemed hopeless; even I was in half a mind to save the lives of the garrison and call for a retreat to Njorhaalt. Now, even the imperials who've taken shelter with us have glimpsed hope and want more. It's not my fault that I don't have these godsworn powers that the Tychrisians have — the Wyld simply never worked that way, the capability to wreak wrath in its name not something that can be bestowed on a whim. And yet... that's exactly what's needed at this juncture. As far as things are concerned, this mutant frostmander is the garrison's de facto commander now. It would be so much easier if she were hateable — but she isn't. In fact, she's respected my position at every opportunity, going over her plans and clearing them with me, but all I can do is nod for the simple reason that I don't understand half of what she's saying. It's all religious terminology that I haven't even heard the imperials use before. At this point, it doesn't take a genius to figure out that I'm largely defunct here. Since she gave them hope, the garrison has taken to not just Thalia herself, but the Tychrisians as a whole, others are openly talking about wanting to learn more or what's been happening with Queen Atheldred back up north. Maybe, like the Wyld, I'm not needed any longer, that someone better has come to take my place and the gracious thing to do for the sake of the garrison is to simply give way, overtly or otherwise... (More missing pages) Thalia died today. The demons from beyond the veil brought everything they had to bear against the Wayfort — the chanting from the other side of the River Ridell continued for days. Then, a terrible rift in the air opened; those who looked directly into it were stricken by an infectious madness that claimed their minds. From this gash in reality came a boulder, a fallen star that warped the world about it and struck Thalia directly; for all the powers her goddess had granted her, she did not survive. What was left was thrown clean across the courtyard where the fallen star still remains, pulsating menacingly... I suppose in her last moments, that frostmander got to see a star up close. She certainly saw it coming and was working some spell, but didn't manage to get it off. We have to retreat. The demons from beyond the veil are taking us seriously, and without this godsworn we don't have any way of so much as hurting them. That's not to mention the fallen star — even being close to it is unsettling. The brave souls who retrieved Thalia's remains were driven half-mad by simply being close for a few moments; no one will even entertain the thought of attempting to move the star-shard. It's not alive, and yet it is in a way that I can't put into words but turns my stomach... Whatever the case, the dead have been added to the makeshift morgue. [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |We put Thalia in the [var0|top|middle|lower] chamber on the [var1|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] column and [var2|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] row; at least we know which one she is if Tychris ever wants her back. |We put Thalia in the [var0|top|middle|lower] chamber on the [var1|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] column and [var2|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] row; at least we know which one she is if Tychris ever wants her back. ] The imperials and surviving Tychrisians agree with us that a retreat to Njorhaalt is for the best; everything south of the River Ridell is considered lost. But it's got me thinking while I muster what stragglers we have: instead of being required to sacrifice for these gods, these gods — or at least their most devout followers — sacrifice for us. To be sure, they receive much from their worshippers, but that by all appearances is given and not compelled. Of course, I only have Thalia as an example, but that has... a certain undeniable appeal. The temple village system is far more complex than that, but the average boer'alvar only sees the tithes they pay, and the shipments of mirrorwine coming out of the druidic vineyards while their moral guides clothe themselves in finery and enjoy the patronage of royalty. As much as I don't want to, I'm not sure I can say that any of the druids I know would have had the whole-hearted fanaticism to do what Thalia did for us. Whatever spell she wove in her last moments — or at least, was interrupted in doing — it's bought us time to retreat. I don't have any evidence of this save for the fact that we're still alive, but I believe that's the case. While everyone's demoralized with Thalia's abrupt end, it hasn't turned into a rout like I would've expected. I don't know. Maybe the star-shard has affected my mind, and I'm going mad. Maybe we all are. There — (The writing abruptly ends here)
rows.translation: ……这个来自提克里斯的、“该死的”存在确实非常高效。它既令人愤怒，又充满压迫感，但同时也极其高效。她自称塔莉娅·星之观察者——我注意到，她用这个称呼来隐藏自己提克里斯的姓氏——而她所拥有的力量极其在我们遭遇的第一波幽灵奴仆的攻击中，这些武器确实发挥了巨大的作用。考虑到她自己也曾承认，是她的女神将她重塑成了这种专门用来摧毁与那些来自幽暗领域的恶魔有关的一切事物的武器，我完全预料到会这样。 嗯，再加上南方的道路已经被切断，提克里西亚的援军也将和我们遭遇同样的命运。 塔莉娅以及她那些由霜冻巨魔组成的随从对剩下的骑兵们所产生的影响是显而易见的：在荒野之地以及我们的德鲁伊们失败的地方，帝国诸神却取得了成功。我实在不明白，为什么这些神明会任由事情发展到这种地步，直到整个世界陷入毁灭才出手干预。不过，任何能够帮助驻军的事情都是值得欢迎的。虽然我无法像塔莉娅那样相信这些南方的神明，但很明显，驻军中的一些人确实对这种所谓的“神明之力”感到敬畏。这些变化虽然毁掉了她的容貌，但她却将这种残缺视为自豪与忠诚的象征。 ……提克里斯发生了什么事？Njorhaalt又遭遇了什么？一场可怕的灾难席卷了整个世界，而那些帝国人们所崇拜的南方诸神现身了，他们在最后关头拯救了世界。人们心存感激，敬畏之情油然而生；他们跪在这些神明面前，感谢他们拯救了自己。如果我再愤世嫉俗一些的话，或许会怀疑这其中隐藏着什么阴谋；然而，拥有这样的力量的神明，根本不需要通过制造危机来吸引信徒。 尽管它在保护我们方面屡次失败，但我认为“荒野”应该得到更多的尊重。我们不应该仅仅因为一次失败，就抛弃那些曾经支撑我们的信念与精神。不过，也许档案管理员说得对，我只是怀念那个更美好的时代罢了。无论我内心有何想法，现在这条道路终于重新燃起了希望——这是我原本以为已经失去的东西。我也不会小气到去抢走那些为这条道路付出努力的人们的成果。 日志中有几页内容缺失了。 我觉得自己是个失败者。在塔莉娅到来之前，形势似乎已经毫无希望了；就连我也在考虑是否应该拯救驻军的生命，然后撤往Njorhaalt。而现在，那些与我们一起避难的神圣帝国士兵们，也重新看到了希望，他们想要更多的东西。我没有那些提克里斯人拥有的神奇力量，这并不是我的错——毕竟“荒野”本身的运作方式就不是这样的，以它的名义来施加惩罚，这种能力也不是可以随意赋予别人的。然而，事实就是如此…… 这正是目前所需要的。 事实上，这个变异的霜冻巨兽现在已经是驻军的实际指挥官了。如果她是个让人讨厌的角色的话，事情会简单很多——但事实并非如此。相反，她每次都会尊重我的地位，会事先与我讨论她的计划并征求我的意见，而我所能做的，也只是点头表示同意，因为其实我根本听不懂她在说什么。那些都是一些宗教术语，我甚至从未听帝国的人使用过。 在这种情况下，任何人都能看出我在这里已经基本上没什么作用了。既然她给了他们希望，驻军们就开始不再把目光仅仅放在塔莉娅个人身上，而是把整个提克里西亚族群都视为目标。其他人也公开表示想要了解更多情况，或者想知道北方那位阿塞尔德雷德女王最近发生了什么。 也许，就像在荒野中一样，我已经不再被需要了；肯定有其他人更适合来取代我的位置。为了驻军的利益着想，最体面的做法就是主动让路，无论是明示地还是暗中地…… （还有更多缺失的页面） 塔莉娅今天去世了。 那些来自幽暗领域的恶魔使出了他们所有手段来攻击荒废驿堡——里德尔河对岸传来的诵经声持续了好几天。随后，天空中出现了一道可怕的裂隙；凡是直视那裂隙的人，都会陷入一种会侵蚀他们心智的疯狂之中。从这个现实中的裂口中，一块巨石飞了出来——那是一颗坠落的星辰，它扭曲了周围的一切，直接击中了塔莉娅；尽管她的女神赋予了她种种力量，她还是没能活下来。剩下的那块巨石被抛到了院子的另一边，至今仍然在那里，不断散发着威胁性的光芒。我想，在她生命的最后时刻，那个冰霜巨魔一定有机会近距离地观察那颗星星。她肯定察觉到了它的到来，也尝试施展了一些法术，但却没能成功将其驱散。 我们必须撤退。那些隐藏在帷幕之后的恶魔已经将我们视为威胁，而没有这件神赐之物，我们根本无法伤害它们。更不用说那颗坠落的星辰了——哪怕只是靠近它也会让人感到不安。那些勇敢地去取回塔莉娅遗骸的人，仅仅是因为在附近待了短短几分钟，就几乎精神崩溃了；没有人会考虑去尝试移动那颗星辰碎片。它并没有生命，但却有一种让我无法用语言形容的诡异力量，那种力量会让我感到恶心…… 无论如何，那些死者已经被安置在了临时设立的停尸房里。 [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |我们把塔莉娅安置在[var0|上层|中层|下层]墓室，即[var1|第一|第二|第三|第四|第五|第六]列、[var2|第一|第二|第三|第四|第五|第六]排；至少如果提克里斯想要她回来，我们就知道该找哪一格了。 |我们把塔莉娅安置在[var0|上层|中层|下层]墓室，即[var1|第一|第二|第三|第四|第五|第六]列、[var2|第一|第二|第三|第四|第五|第六]排；至少如果提克里斯想要她回来，我们就知道该找哪一格了。 ]帝国势力以及幸存下来的提克里西亚人也都认同，撤退到恩乔哈尔特才是上策；里德尔河以南的地区，已经注定无法挽救了。 但这一点让我陷入了思考：既然我们不必为这些神明牺牲，那么这些神明——或者至少是他们最虔诚的追随者——应该为我们牺牲才对。的确，他们从信徒们那里获得了很多，但这一切看起来都是自愿给予的，而非强迫所得。当然，我这里只是以塔莉娅为例，但她的魅力确实无可否认。寺庙村落系统的运作方式要复杂得多，但普通的布尔阿尔瓦尔们所看到的，只有自己缴纳的什一税，以及德鲁伊葡萄园里出产的镜像酒；而那些被他们视为道德导师的人们，却穿着华丽的服饰，享受着王室的赞助与支持。 尽管我很不愿意承认，但我不确定我认识的那些德鲁伊中，有谁会像塔莉娅那样全心全意地为我们付出一切。她在最后时刻施展的那些法术——或者至少，是在施展过程中被中断的那些法术——为我们赢得了撤退的时间。我没有任何证据能够证明这个存档的存在，除了我们仍然活着这一事实之外，但我相信确实如此。虽然大家都因为塔莉娅的突然离世而感到沮丧，但情况并没有像我预想的那样变得一团糟。 我不知道……也许那颗星碎片影响了我的思维，让我产生了幻觉。也许我们所有人都是这样。看—— （文字在这里突然中断了）
rows.raw: " ...This %"godsworn" from Tychris is efficient. Infuriating and imposing, no doubt, but also extremely efficient. Thalia Star-Viewer, she calls herself — I note she hides her Tychrisian last name from us with this moniker — and the powers she wields are extremely effective at slaying the first waves of wraith-thralls sent at us. I would expect that to be the case, given that by her own admission she was reshaped by her goddess into a weapon tailored to destroy everything linked to the demons from beyond the veil. Well, that and now that the southern roads have been cut off, the Tychrisian reinforcements will share the same fate we do. The effect that Thalia and her retinue of frostmanders have had on the remaining outriders is unmistakable: where the Wyld and our druids have failed, the gods of the imperials succeed. Why these gods allowed things to come to this point and only intervene when the entire world lies in ruin is beyond me, but anything that aides the garrison is welcome. While I can't bring myself to believe in these southern gods the way Thalia clearly does, it's clear that some of the garrison are overawed at what this so-called godsworn is capable of. The changes wrought upon her body have disfigured her, but she wears that crippling as a mark of pride and devotion. ...What has happened to Tychris? What has happened to Njorhaalt? A terrible calamity engulfs the world, and these southern gods the imperials worship manifest and step in to save it in the nick of time. People are grateful, overawed; they kneel before these gods for having saved them. If I were any more cynical than I am, I would have suspected a ruse; yet gods with these powers would not need to concoct a crisis to gather followers. For all its failures in defending us, I feel that the Wyld deserves more, that we shouldn't just throw away the beliefs and spirits that sustained us just because of a single failure. But maybe the archivist is right, and I'm just nostalgic for a better age. Whatever my private thoughts, there's now hope for this wayfort, something I thought lost; I'm not so petty as to try and take it from my outriders. (Several pages are missing from the log) I feel like a failure. Before Thalia's arrival, the situation seemed hopeless; even I was in half a mind to save the lives of the garrison and call for a retreat to Njorhaalt. Now, even the imperials who've taken shelter with us have glimpsed hope and want more. It's not my fault that I don't have these godsworn powers that the Tychrisians have — the Wyld simply never worked that way, the capability to wreak wrath in its name not something that can be bestowed on a whim. And yet... that's exactly what's needed at this juncture. As far as things are concerned, this mutant frostmander is the garrison's de facto commander now. It would be so much easier if she were hateable — but she isn't. In fact, she's respected my position at every opportunity, going over her plans and clearing them with me, but all I can do is nod for the simple reason that I don't understand half of what she's saying. It's all religious terminology that I haven't even heard the imperials use before. At this point, it doesn't take a genius to figure out that I'm largely defunct here. Since she gave them hope, the garrison has taken to not just Thalia herself, but the Tychrisians as a whole, others are openly talking about wanting to learn more or what's been happening with Queen Atheldred back up north. Maybe, like the Wyld, I'm not needed any longer, that someone better has come to take my place and the gracious thing to do for the sake of the garrison is to simply give way, overtly or otherwise... (More missing pages) Thalia died today. The demons from beyond the veil brought everything they had to bear against the Wayfort — the chanting from the other side of the River Ridell continued for days. Then, a terrible rift in the air opened; those who looked directly into it were stricken by an infectious madness that claimed their minds. From this gash in reality came a boulder, a fallen star that warped the world about it and struck Thalia directly; for all the powers her goddess had granted her, she did not survive. What was left was thrown clean across the courtyard where the fallen star still remains, pulsating menacingly... I suppose in her last moments, that frostmander got to see a star up close. She certainly saw it coming and was working some spell, but didn't manage to get it off. We have to retreat. The demons from beyond the veil are taking us seriously, and without this godsworn we don't have any way of so much as hurting them. That's not to mention the fallen star — even being close to it is unsettling. The brave souls who retrieved Thalia's remains were driven half-mad by simply being close for a few moments; no one will even entertain the thought of attempting to move the star-shard. It's not alive, and yet it is in a way that I can't put into words but turns my stomach... Whatever the case, the dead have been added to the makeshift morgue. [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |We put Thalia in the [var0|top|middle|lower] chamber on the [var1|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] column and [var2|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] row; at least we know which one she is if Tychris ever wants her back. |We put Thalia in the [var0|top|middle|lower] chamber on the [var1|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] column and [var2|first|second|third|fourth|fifth|sixth] row; at least we know which one she is if Tychris ever wants her back. ] The imperials and surviving Tychrisians agree with us that a retreat to Njorhaalt is for the best; everything south of the River Ridell is considered lost. But it's got me thinking while I muster what stragglers we have: instead of being required to sacrifice for these gods, these gods — or at least their most devout followers — sacrifice for us. To be sure, they receive much from their worshippers, but that by all appearances is given and not compelled. Of course, I only have Thalia as an example, but that has... a certain undeniable appeal. The temple village system is far more complex than that, but the average boer'alvar only sees the tithes they pay, and the shipments of mirrorwine coming out of the druidic vineyards while their moral guides clothe themselves in finery and enjoy the patronage of royalty. As much as I don't want to, I'm not sure I can say that any of the druids I know would have had the whole-hearted fanaticism to do what Thalia did for us. Whatever spell she wove in her last moments — or at least, was interrupted in doing — it's bought us time to retreat. I don't have any evidence of this save for the fact that we're still alive, but I believe that's the case. While everyone's demoralized with Thalia's abrupt end, it hasn't turned into a rout like I would've expected. I don't know. Maybe the star-shard has affected my mind, and I'm going mad. Maybe we all are. There — (The writing abruptly ends here) "

rows.original:
You flip through the damaged volume — this is an accounting of the taxes collected by the Wayfort over several years. Some of it is written in Belharan, primarily entries pertaining to dealings with the empire; the rest is written in the pale elf tongue and indecipherable to you. Ryn would be able to read it, but she's not here with you.

        Still, the information is detailed, if sundry. Travelers consisted of not just those crossing the bridge, but also those under it; Khor'minos was a lot more open before the Godswar. Naturally, a toll was paid by those passing over or under the bridge, and a small tax was levied on any trade conducted within the Wayfort; given that it was a crossroads of a sort there was a surprising amount of it. Imperials paid well for boreal elf mirrorwine — also known as ice wine — and exports from Khor'minos.
        
        By all accounts, the Wayfort of centuries past was fairly prosperous, capable of not just supporting itself comfortably, but also producing a reasonable surplus in revenue to send back to the crown. A little oddly, it oversaw no lands — perhaps no one wanted to settle on the border with the empire, but that didn't seem to diminish its importance any.
        
        That's about all the information you can glean from these records. You pick up several more and flip through them, but they're much the same, just from previous years.
rows.translation:
你翻阅着这本破损的书册——其中记录了荒废驿堡多年来征收的税款情况。其中一部分是用贝尔哈兰语写成的，主要是与帝国有关的交易记录；其余部分则用淡色精灵语书写，对你来说根本无法理解。小琳或许能够看懂这些内容，但她现在并不在你身边。

        尽管这些信息相当详尽，但内容也有些杂乱无章。旅行者并不只是那些穿过桥梁的人，还包括那些在桥下通行的人；在“神战”之前，科尔米诺斯地区的交通要道本来就更加开放。自然而然地，那些通过桥梁的人都需要缴纳通行费，而在荒废驿堡地区进行的任何贸易活动也都需要缴纳少量税款；由于这里实际上是一个重要的交通枢纽，因此贸易活动量相当可观。帝国人们非常愿意为北境精灵生产的镜酒——也就是人们所说的冰酒——以及科尔米诺斯地区的出口商品支付高额的费用。
        
        据种种记载，几个世纪前的荒废驿堡地区相当繁荣，不仅能够自给自足，还能产生可观的盈余收入上缴给王室。有点奇怪的是，该地区并没有管辖任何土地——或许没有人愿意在帝国边境定居，但这似乎并没有削弱它的地位。
        
        从这些记录中，你所能获取的信息也就这些了。你又拿了几份记录翻阅了一下，但内容都差不多，只不过是过去几年的记录而已。

rows.original: You pick out one of the intact volumes and take a look. Several entries are written in the pale elf tongue, which is indecipherable to you, but there're a few in old Belharan — not that surprising given that the Wayfort sat on the old border with all kinds coming and going. Cultural osmosis, maybe? Whatever the case, you flip through the crumbling pages, hoping to glean anything of use... ...Which isn't much, if anything. This is a record of outrider patrols from the Wayfort, looping through the Frostwood — starting from the River Ridell, warg riders would circle out, stopping at several small temple villages before turning around at the Temple of Terrestrial Fire, then working south through the bog before following the river's northern bank upstream back to the Wayfort. The exact patrol routes would always vary in order to avoid becoming predictable, yet they nevertheless still followed the same general tack. By all accounts, the Frostwood was a peaceful place in centuries past — you flip through several entries, all easily summarized as %"nothing to report." The villagers liked the outriders and would gladly host them and their wargs when they stopped by... the land north of the River Ridell really was a lot more populated in those days, according to these logs. For Ryn's people to have been beaten back to a single city-state even so long after the Godswar itself concluded says something about the state of matters that everything was left in. By the accounts, being garrisoned at the Wayfort was considered one of the most dangerous and stressful postings that one could receive because of its location on the border with Belharan territory, and yet it was peaceful by present-day standards. The biggest problem the outriders had to deal with were imperial smugglers — mostly wyld elves because they stood out less than humans — trying to get ice wine across the river in a bid to avoid being taxed at the Wayfort. The garrison commander suspected the druids were complicit in this smuggling to feather their already gilded nests, but could never acquire any kind of concrete proof in order to challenge the powers that lay in the temples. By these accounts, life in the Marches and beyond was fairly peaceful and stable on both sides of the River Ridell. One supposes that such good fortune couldn't have lasted forever, not with such fat pickings ripe for the taking...
rows.translation: 你从中挑选出一本完好无损的书卷仔细查看。其中有几条记录是用淡色精灵语写成的，你根本看不懂；不过也有一些是用古老的贝拉兰语写的——不过这些内容你也看不懂。那个考虑到荒废驿堡位于古老的边境线上，各种人物来来去去，这就显得有些奇怪了。也许是文化之间的相互影响吧？无论如何，你翻动着那些已经破旧的页面，希望能从中找到一些有用的信息…… 然而，实际上并没有找到太多有用的东西。这是关于“远行者巡逻队”在荒废驿堡地区活动的记录：这些巡逻队会从里德尔河出发，沿着弗罗斯特伍德地区进行巡逻。他们会先绕行一周，途中会停靠在几座小型寺庙所在的村庄，然后在“大地之火神庙”处折返，接着向南穿过沼泽地，最后沿着河流的北岸向上游方向返回荒废驿堡地区。具体的巡逻路线会不断变化，以避免被预测到，但它们仍然遵循着大致相同的模式。 据各种记载，几个世纪以前，弗罗斯特伍德确实是一个宁静的地方——翻阅了几份记录，所有内容都可以简单地概括为“没有发生任何异常事件”。村民们很喜欢那些远道而来的人，每当他们造访时，村民们都会热情地招待他们以及他们的狼人伙伴。根据这些记录，在那些年代，里德尔河以北的地区确实人口更加密集。既然在神战结束后这么久，小琳的族人仍然被迫退缩到仅仅一个城邦中，这说明当时的局势已经变得非常糟糕。 据记载，因为位于与贝尔哈兰领土的边境上，被派驻在荒废驿堡被认为是最危险、压力最大的岗位之一；然而按照当今的标准来看，那里其实相当平静。外勤人员面临的最大问题，就是那些帝国走私者——其中大多是野精灵，因为他们的外貌比人类更不容易引起注意——他们试图将冰酒运过河流，以此逃避在荒废驿堡缴纳关税。驻军指挥官怀疑那些德鲁伊参与了这次走私活动，目的是让他们本已富有的地位更加稳固，但他始终无法获得任何确凿的证据来质疑那些掌握在神庙中的权力。 根据这些描述，在里德尔河两岸，边境地区以及更远的地方，生活总体上是平静而稳定的。人们或许会认为，这样的好运不可能永远持续下去，毕竟有那么多丰厚的利益在等着被攫取……

rows.original: The ale kegs remain in the back of the bar, untouched and waiting for a day that will never come. Will you put both them and Nina out of their misery and allow the two to meet, consequences be damned?
rows.translation: 那些麦芽酒桶还放在酒吧的后面，无人问津，一直在等待着一个永远不会到来的日子。你能不能帮它们和妮娜摆脱这种困境，让它们能够相见呢？哪怕会带来什么后果也罢……
rows.raw: "\n        The ale kegs remain in the back of the bar, untouched and waiting for a day that will never come. Will you put both them and Nina out of their misery and allow the two to meet, consequences be damned?"

rows.original: You know full well in your bones that this is inviting trouble, but either the need is great enough, or Nina is just that pitiful. With a wave of your hand, you motion for Nina to go do her thing. The hopeless drunk of a harpy doesn't need telling twice — flapping over smashed tables and dusty stools, she makes a beeline for the kegs, fully intent of soothing her frayed nerves by guzzling her fill. Only she never makes it. No sooner has Nina come within five feet of the ale kegs that [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |your Juice-enhanced senses blind you with the warning they scream into your mind |your gut twists and an unsettling chill worms its way into your bones ]. Wasting no time, you grab Nina by the scruff of her neck and yank her out of the way just as claws dripping glimmering star-stuff materialize from the nearest wall and swipe at her. The silly bird squawks and flaps as she pitches backwards, landing butt-first against you before the rest of her follows in a feathery flomph. No time to laugh at the absurdity of the situation, though — the shattered memories of the Wayfort's past are already upon you. Given that you were half-expecting something like this, you already have your [pc.weapon] at the ready, and rouse Nina to battle as the broken psyches close in. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 你心里十分清楚，这无异于自找麻烦；可要么需求实在迫切，要么妮娜的模样实在可怜。你挥挥手，示意她尽管去做想做的事。 这个无可救药的鹰身女妖酒鬼根本不必听第二遍——她扇着翅膀飞过碎裂的桌子和积满灰尘的凳子，直奔酒桶而去，一心想痛饮个够，安抚自己紧绷的神经。 可她根本没能走到那里。妮娜刚进入麦酒桶五英尺以内，[pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |经果汁强化的感官就在脑海中尖啸警告，强烈得令你眼前一白 |你的腹部猛然绞紧，一股令人不安的寒意钻进骨髓 ]。你毫不耽搁地揪住妮娜的后颈，把她猛拉到一旁；与此同时，沾着闪亮星质的利爪从最近的墙壁中显现，朝她挥下。那只傻鸟尖叫着扑腾翅膀向后跌去，屁股先撞上你，随后其余身体也裹着羽毛噗地落下。 不过没时间嘲笑眼前荒唐的场面——驿堡往昔的破碎记忆已经向你们袭来。你本就隐约料到会有这种事，因此早已举起[pc.weapon]；破碎的心智逐渐逼近时，你也催促妮娜投入战斗。 战斗开始！

rows.original: No, you don't need this right now. Hope may spring eternal, but the spark of life dies from Nina's good eye as you continue walking straight past the kegs. Perhaps you may have need of ale before you're out of this madhouse, but you'll come back for the kegs then and not one moment sooner.
rows.translation: 不，你现在并不需要这个。希望永远存在，但当你径直走过那些酒桶时，生命之火就从妮娜那只完好的眼睛里熄灭了。也许在离开这个疯狂的地方之前，你会需要一些麦芽酒，但那时你一定会回来取那些酒桶的，而且不会早一刻。
rows.raw: "\n            No, you don't need this right now. Hope may spring eternal, but the spark of life dies from Nina's good eye as you continue walking straight past the kegs. Perhaps you may have need of ale before you're out of this madhouse, but you'll come back for the kegs then and not one moment sooner."

rows.original: You circle around behind the bar that will eventually be Rumie's and examine what was on tap back in the day. Seeing what you're doing, Nina flaps over and starts examining every nook and cranny like a hawk, her thirst no doubt catching up with her. There's some caution to be had at the prospect of a drunk Nina in this Wayfort on the edge of madness, but on the other hand her nose for finding alcohol wherever it's hidden might be an asset here. "Man, I'm dying for a drink. Guess you are too, huh?" You have to admit this place has a knack for making people high-strung, far too much for what's actually useful for staying alive. But more importantly, if drink can survive in such a place... "The lengths we go to in order to uncover the mysteries of the universe, man. You take that side, and I'll take this one." You glance over the racks — most of the bottles and jugs are smashed and have dried out long since. Whatever calamity happened to the Wayfort in centuries past, it didn't spare the drink. There're a couple of jugs, but opening them only presents you with the sour smell of not-quite-vinegar. Given that time doesn't flow here, the drink went off before the Wayfort's past was shoved into the Ways, and that tells a whole new story. What about Nina? Has she found anything? "You gotta come over and see this, man."
rows.translation: 你绕到日后将属于露米的吧台后，查看当年供应过什么酒。妮娜看见你的举动，立刻振翅飞来，像鹰一样检查每个角落；口渴无疑已经追上了她。身处这个徘徊在疯狂边缘的驿堡，想到喝醉的妮娜自然得多加小心；但另一方面，她能从任何藏匿之处嗅出酒味的鼻子也许正是有用的资产。 “伙计，我快渴死了。你大概也一样，对吧？” 你不得不承认，这地方很会让人神经紧绷，而且早已超过求生所需的有益程度。不过更重要的是，如果酒能在这样的地方幸存…… “伙计，为揭开宇宙奥秘，我们还真是什么事都肯做。你搜那边，我搜这边。” 你扫视酒架——大多数瓶罐已经破碎，内容物也早已干涸。几个世纪前降临驿堡的灾难，无论究竟是什么，同样没有放过酒水。这里还剩几只罐子，可一打开，扑面而来的只有尚未完全变成醋的酸味。既然此处时间并不流动，这些酒必定早在驿堡的往昔被推入界间之路以前便已变质，而这一点又揭示了一个全新的故事。 妮娜那边呢？她找到什么了吗？ “伙计，你一定得过来看看这个。”

rows.original: Nina's voice sounds a little distant — she's wandered over behind a wall to where Rumie's bed will be, and instead of a cot you discover several huge kegs of brazenberry ale, each one as tall as you are and well-caulked. Looks like they were saving this for last — with all the mass and none of the fragility of the bottles outside, the kegs have survived quite admirably. "Gods, please don't let this have gone off," Nina says, her voice trembling as she clasps her hands together in mock prayer. "I don't think I could take the disappointment." A little too late for that, given that she's just found liquid disappointment. "Hey, brazenberry ale is okay, man. Don't diss it." Yeah, but Nina's special. An entire garrison with nothing but brazenberry to drown itself in is going to be down in the dumps; honestly speaking, water might be better for morale.[pc.bg soldier | You would know; you've been on more than one campaign when this exact miserable situation happened. Weak drink's worse than no drink; boiling water in one's helmet might be an exaggeration, but only barely so. ] "Yeah, okay. Whatever you say, man." Stepping up to one of the kegs, Nina shamelessly rubs herself all over the dusty wood and gives it several raps with her knuckles. Her eyebrows raise in surprise, and her smile widens. "Untouched, too. Still as full as the day she was caulked. Dear, sweet gods, how much I love you." While Nina's being all melodramatic, there is far more than enough ale in here for her to drink her fill and for you to fill several of the intact jugs with drink — a small respite from the madness of the Wayfort past. [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |As you step up, though, something in your juice-saturated sight flashes, a sudden surge of violet accompanied by an insistent buzzing in the back of your mind. You're slowly getting better at discerning what's what under the Juice's influence, but your best guess is that these kegs were quite important to someone — it makes sense, given that they were untouched all the way up until the Wayfort's demise despite it being under siege. In a place where memories and emotions are as material as flesh and blood, this is undoubtedly going to invite trouble. ] With that in mind, would you like to let Nina run free for a bit while you have some ale to go?
rows.translation: 妮娜的声音听起来有点遥远——她应该已经走到墙后面，也就是露米未来的床所在的地方。你看到的不是婴儿床，而是几桶巨大的铜莓啤酒：每一桶都有你那么高，而且密封得非常好。看来他们是打算把这些啤酒留到最后才使用的——由于这些桶体积庞大，而且并不像外面的瓶子那样容易破碎，所以它们保存得相当完好。 天啊，求你们千万别让这件事发生吧，”妮娜双手合十，假装在祈祷，声音颤抖着说道，“我想我实在无法承受这样的失望。” 不过现在说这些已经有点太晚了，因为她早已体验到了那种令人心碎的失望。 嘿，厚叶莓啤酒其实也挺不错的，别小看它。” 不过，尼娜酿造的啤酒确实与众不同。如果一个驻军基地里只有厚叶莓啤酒可供饮用，那些士兵们肯定会心情低落吧；说实话，水可能对提振士气来说反而更有效。[pc.bg soldier | 你应该很清楚；在很多次行动中，都出现过这种糟糕的情况。喝劣质酒总比不喝酒要好；虽然把沸水灌进头盔里有点夸张，但也不算完全离谱。 ] 好吧，随你便吧。”尼娜走到其中一个酒桶旁，毫不羞耻地用身体蹭着那布满灰尘的木桶，然后用指关节敲了几下。她的眉毛惊讶地挑了起来，笑容也变得更加灿烂。“居然一点都没被动过，还和刚装满酒的那一天一样。亲爱的、可爱的神明啊，我真是太爱你们了。” 而尼娜正在这里大搞戏剧性表演的时候是这里的麦酒多得足够让她喝个痛快，也足够你们把几个完好无损的罐子都装满酒——这无疑是为我们暂时逃离荒废驿堡家族过去的那些疯狂往事带来的一份慰藉。 [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |然而，当你走上前时，你的视线中突然闪过一道光芒，一阵紫色的光芒伴随着脑海中持续的嗡嗡声袭来。 在“果汁”的影响下，你逐渐能够分辨出事物的真相，但根据你的判断，这些酒桶对某个人来说应该非常重要——毕竟，在荒废驿堡被围困期间，这些酒桶竟然一直未被触动，这一点确实很合理。在一个记忆与情感如同血肉般真实存在的地方，这种行为无疑会招来麻烦。 ] 考虑到这一点，当你去喝点麦芽酒的时候，是不是可以让妮娜自由活动一会儿呢？

rows.original: You shrug and let Nina do her thing, [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |keeping a hand on your [pc.weapon] all the while. With how strong the connecting threads you saw were, it shouldn't be be long before — — And there it is. Barely has Nina unsealed the keg and tapped it that your Juice-enhanced senses blind you with the warning they scream into your mind. Nina squawks and flaps, landing backwards on her butt as several shattered specters lunge out of the walls at her, arms outstretched to defend their precious, precious drink. |keeping an eye out for danger. The old bar and mess hall may look abandoned, but you've been an adventurer enough to have honed your intuition for these kinds of situations. Which to no one's surprise, your gut feelings are proven right this time. Barely has Nina unsealed the keg and tapped it that your reflexes kick into action, grabbing Nina by the scruff of her neck and yanking her back before she can crack open the keg. The silly bird squawks and flaps indignantly as she pitches backwards, landing butt-first against you before the rest of her follows in a feathery flomph. "Dude, what was that all about? And I was so close, too!" You just point at the shattered specters lunging out of the walls, converging on where she was seconds ago. Yeah, they aren't taking well to Nina claiming their precious, precious drink for her own. ] It would be so hilarious if it weren't deathly serious — the living and the dead fighting over a measure of miserably thin piss-ale. But hey, you presumably have your reasons, don't you? It's a fight!
rows.translation: 你耸耸肩，让妮娜去做她的事，[pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |同时一只手始终按着你的[pc.weapon]。从你看到的那些连接线如此粗壮来看，用不了多久—— ——果然，就是现在。妮娜刚把酒桶开封、接上龙头，你那被果汁强化的感官就被它们在你脑中尖叫的警告刺得眼前发白。妮娜尖叫着扑腾起来，一屁股向后摔倒，因为几个破碎的幽灵从墙壁里朝她扑了出来，伸着手臂要保护它们那珍贵无比的酒。 |同时留意着危险。这家破旧的酒吧和食堂看起来或许已经废弃，但你已经当了足够久的冒险者，早就磨炼出了应对这类情况的直觉。 不出所料，这一次你的直觉又被证明是对的。妮娜刚把酒桶开封、接上龙头，你的反射神经就立刻行动起来——一把抓住妮娜的后颈，在她撬开酒桶之前把她拽了回来。这只傻鸟愤怒地尖叫扑腾，向后倒去，屁股先撞在你身上，紧接着整个身子也跟上来，发出一声羽毛般的噗通。 “老兄，那到底是怎么回事？我明明就差一点了！” 你只是指了指那些从墙壁里扑出来的破碎幽灵，它们正聚拢到她几秒前所在的位置。是啊，它们可不乐意看到妮娜把它们那珍贵无比的酒据为己有。 ] 要不是事关生死，这实在太好笑了——活人和死人居然为了一份寡淡得像尿一样的淡啤酒打起来。不过嘛，你这么做想必有你的理由，对吧？ 开打！

rows.original: Nina needs to take a load off and you need the ale.
rows.translation: 妮娜需要放松一下，而你则需要喝点麦芽酒。
rows.raw: "Nina needs to take a load off and you need the ale."

rows.original: Thinning your lips, you grab Nina by the scruff of her neck and yank her back before she can crack open the keg. The silly bird squawks and flaps indignantly as she pitches backwards, landing butt-first against you before the rest of her follows in a feathery flomph. "Dude, what was that all about? And I was so close, too!" [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |It's precisely because she's so close to drawing who knows what that you had to yank her so roughly. She's a dreamwalker, can't she see it? Even you can. Nina mumbles sourly, then squints at the keg she was about to tap, Several moments pass as she concentrates, mumbling furiously to herself, and she eventually straightens up and folds her arms. "Yeah, okay. So it's trouble, but it's nothing a good team like us can handle, man. Given the things we've beaten off so far, a couple of stray thoughts floating around aren't a match for us." You're still getting used to the extra dimension of existence that the Juice has opened up to you, but you're pretty sure what you saw was more substantial than just a couple of stray thoughts. Is she sure that this isn't her thirst speaking? Nina looks like she's about to argue further, then sighs and slumps her shoulders. "You got me, man. Being sober is pretty gods-damn awful, and I can't reach my stash from here. C'mon, man, we can just kick the stuffing out of those chumps when they show up. It'll be fine." Maybe later, if and when you actually need the ale. But if it's just to sate her thirst, you'll buy her enough drink to drown herself once you're safely out of this madhouse. "Promise?" Promise. |Look, you get that her nerves are starting to fray at the edges, but so are yours. You're all in this together, and you need Nina sober for what lies ahead. She wouldn't be happy with you if you were a blubbering mess, would she? "Yeah, but like, getting smashed just makes you black out, man. Me? Getting smashed makes me more powerful than even I can imagine." Powerful enough to force aside what's keeping you trapped here and get the both of you home? "Uh, maybe?" Safely? In one piece? "In one piece, definitely, yeah." The same shape? With all limbs attached? "No! No, I can't do it! All right, like, you've made your point, man. Damn it, I just want, like, the noise to stop." You don't hear anything, but given that you're not a dreamwalker like Nina, it doesn't come as any surprise that you're less susceptible to such attacks. Even so, you weren't lying — you need her sane and sober, and while you don't have as much control over the first the second is entirely preventable. Look, you'll buy her enough drink to drown herself once you're safely out of this madhouse. "Promise?" Promise. ] "Ugghh. All right, we'll go. But I'm holding you to your word."
rows.translation: 你抿紧嘴唇，一把抓住尼娜的后颈，在她撬开酒桶之前把她拽了回来。这傻鸟愤愤地尖叫着扑腾，向后一屁股坐倒在你身上，随后整个身子也羽毛般地噗通一声压下来。 “老兄，那到底是怎么回事啊？我明明就差那么一点了！” [pc.hasBoon JuicedUp |正是因为她就差一点就要引出不知道什么东西，你才不得不这么粗暴地把她拽回来。她是个梦行者，难道她自己看不出来吗？连你都看得出来。 尼娜酸溜溜地嘟囔着，然后眯眼盯着她刚才正要打开的那只酒桶。她专注了好一会儿，嘴里疯狂地自言自语，最后终于直起身子，抱起双臂。 “好吧，行。这确实是个麻烦，但对我们这样的好队伍来说算不了什么，老兄。想想我们至今打退过多少东西，几缕飘来飘去的杂念根本不是我们的对手。” 你还在适应果汁为你开启的那一重额外的存在维度，但你相当确定，你看到的东西绝不只是几缕杂念那么简单。她确定这不是她的酒瘾在说话吗？ “被你说中了，老兄。清醒着真是他妈的难受，而且我从这儿够不到我的私藏。来吧老兄，等那些家伙冒出来，我们把他们揍个稀巴烂就行了。不会有事的。” 也许等以后你真的需要麦酒的时候再说吧。但如果只是为了给她解渴，那等你们安全离开这个疯人院之后，你会给她买足够多的酒，让她把自己淹死在里头。 “答应我？” 答应你。 |听着，你明白她的神经已经开始绷不住了，你的也一样。你们是一条船上的人，接下来要面对的事情，你需要妮娜保持清醒。要是你哭哭啼啼地一团糟，她也不会高兴的，对吧？ “是啊，可是老兄，喝得烂醉只会让你断片而已。而我呢？喝醉之后，我会变得比我自己所能想象的还要强大。” 强大到足以强行推开困住你们的东西，把你们两个都送回家吗？ “呃，也许吧？” 安全吗？完好无损吗？ “完好无损，绝对没问题。” 形状也一样？四肢都还在吗？ “不行！不行，我做不到！好吧，你的意思我明白了，老兄。该死，我只是想让那噪音停下来。” 你什么也听不见，但既然你不像尼娜那样是梦行者，你对这类攻击没那么敏感也就不足为奇了。即便如此，你也没有说谎——你需要她神志清醒、滴酒不沾；前者你控制不了多少，但后者完全可以避免。听着，等你们安全离开这个疯人院之后，你会给她买足够多的酒，让她把自己淹死在里头。 “答应我？” 答应你。 ] “呃啊啊。好吧，我们走吧。但你得说话算话。”

rows.original: The final blow lands on the apparitions, and you feel a twinge of satisfaction as they shatter into pieces and crash down to the stone in a shower of lights that wink out after a second or two. [pc.isDK |Hope you made them remember what feeling pain was like |You'd feel sorry for them, but these aren't people any more, just fractured memories pieced together in a bid to slow you ]. "Like, we need to get going and find the way out fast," Nina says as she breathes a sigh of relief. "There's no end of disembodied memories about us, man; they're just going to keep coming so long as we're here." There's no way to permanently stop them from harassing you, is there? "Maybe. You'd need to find a way to convince the Wayfort that you're not someone who needs to be attacked, and I'm not sure how to go about that. If you see an opportunity like that, man, I guess you can give it a go. For now... you and me need to scram, like now."

rows.original: The apparitions cannot hurt you physically, but they can make you perceive and more importantly, believe in you being cut down. As you succumb to their weapons, the irony of the garrison of the Wayfort's past murdering its future [pc.mf |lord |lady ] isn't lost on you in your last coherent thoughts. It doesn't hurt, for you need a mind to perceive pain. Your body might keep going for a while longer inasmuch as that has any meaning in a place where time doesn't flow, but your sense of self shatters into dozens of fragments, blowing away into the void between the stars. Your [silly |heart may go on, but your ]adventure ends here.
rows.translation: 这些幻象并不会对你的身体造成伤害，但它们会让你感觉到自己被击中了，更重要的是，会让你相信自己确实被击中了。当你逐渐相信这些幻象所呈现的假象时，这就恰恰印证了荒废驿堡家族过去那些人是如何杀害他们自己的未来的。 [pc.mf |领主 |女士 ]在你最后的那些连贯思绪中，这一点你应该已经意识到了。 这并不会带来痛苦，因为只有拥有意识，人才能感受到疼痛。在你的身体在这样一个时间流逝不存在的地方继续运转一段时间或许还有意义，但你的自我意识却会破碎成无数碎片，然后消散在星际间的虚无之中。 你的[silly |心或许还在跳动，但你已不在了…… ]冒险就此结束。

rows.original:
The last of the apparitions shatters into innumerable fragments, three dimensions splintering into two as glimmering star-stuff falls to the ground and winks out of existence. While you catch your breath, Nina starts towards the kegs once more at a more cautious pace, glancing suspiciously at the walls. Happily, the ambush she's expecting doesn't materialize, and she embraces the nearest keg like a long-lost lover with a happy sigh.

    "Man, you have no idea how much I missed you."
    
    Look, brazenberry ale may be the nectar of the gods to her, but she has to drink just enough to keep her nerves steady and not until she's completely smashed. You reserve the right to pull her away if you think she's had — she isn't listening to you, is she?
    
    No, she isn't. Nina's already gotten the top off the keg — how did she manage that with her bare hands? — and is positively drooling over the clear, light brown liquid. For a moment, she drums her claws on the rim and looks fit to dunk her whole head in and drown in the stuff, then thinks better of it and grabs the cleanest-looking mug there's to be had. After a quick rinse, Nina's guzzling mugs of the stuff with wanton abandon, some semblance of the harpy you know returning as the alcohol takes the edge off her nerves.
    
    That can't be hygienic, but she doesn't care. Sighing, Nina slumps against the barrel and takes a brief break to let the ale settle in her, thirsty creature that she is.
    
    "Thank the gods," she groans, ale running down her cheeks. "Thank Sorra, queen of the air and all her miserable bondage rope. Man, so much of this shit around and not a drop to drink."
    
    That's one particular bit of invective that you've never heard before, but Nina's never been your average harpy. While the poor dear quenches her thirst, you crack open another of the kegs and rinse out, then fill some of the intact jugs that're lying around the bar. Save some for later, as it were...
    
    Is she done?
    
    "Just about. Man, this is weird. I keep on drinking, but while I'm already starting to get stuffed I'm not feeling more than the beginnings of a buzz. This isn't right, and it damn well isn't cool. I need to be a fair more smashed than this to put everything in perspective."
    
    Well, time doesn't flow here, so she can't get more drunk than that. Sounds reasonable to you.
    
    "Yeah, but —" she takes another swig — "it seems to be pretty damn selective on what goes and what doesn't, man. Like, how are we breathing? Or walking? Time doesn't flow in this place, right? You're not getting any hungrier or thirstier, but the blood hasn't stood still in our veins."
    
    Isn't that good news? It means that whatever's behind all this, it doesn't have as great control over this figment of the Wayfort's past than one might imagine.
    
    "It's damned irritating is what it is." Nina eyes the ale keg, then smacks the aged wood with her fist. "You bloody traitor, getting my hopes up. That's totally not cool, man. Thought we were supposed to be excellent with each other, but you stabbed me in the back."
    
    Now now, it's not the ale's fault. Though that does raise the question if the drink will hit Nina all at once when you leave this place. Well, that's getting ahead of yourself — you have to find a way out to begin with.
    
    "Let's go, man. This sucks."
rows.translation:
最后那道幻影也碎成了无数碎片，三维空间仿佛被撕裂成二维，那些闪烁着微光的星尘坠落到地面，随即消失得无影无踪。当你还在喘息时，尼娜又以更加谨慎的速度朝那些酒桶走去，不时怀疑地瞥着周围的墙壁。幸运的是，她所期待的埋伏并没有发生，于是她欣喜地抱住了最近的那个酒桶，就像拥抱了一位久别重逢的挚爱一样。

    天啊，你根本无法想象我有多想念你。”
    
    听着，对于她来说，那种野莓啤酒或许真是天赐的甘露，但她喝的量必须控制在能让自己保持清醒的范围内，绝对不能喝到烂醉如泥的程度。如果你觉得她已经喝得够多了，你完全有权利把她拉走——她根本没在听你说话，对吧？
    
    不，她并没有。妮娜已经把桶顶的盖子拧开了——她究竟是怎么用双手做到这一点的呢？——现在她正盯着那清澈、呈浅棕色的液体，口水都快流出来了。有那么一瞬间，她甚至想用爪子抓住桶边，把整个头都浸进那液体里，但最终还是理智地选择了拿起那个看起来最干净的杯子来喝。快速冲洗过后，尼娜之前那种毫无节制地大口饮酒的习惯终于有所改变——随着酒精开始缓解她紧张的情绪，那个曾经疯狂饮酒的“女妖”形象也逐渐恢复了些许常态。
    
    那肯定不卫生，但她根本不在乎。尼娜叹了口气，靠在桶上稍作休息，让这麦芽酒在她的肚子里沉淀下来——毕竟她实在太渴了。
    
    “谢天谢地，”她呻吟道，麦芽酒顺着她的脸颊流下来，“多亏了索拉，空气的女王，以及她那些该死的束缚绳索……天啊，周围到处都是这种东西，却连一滴能喝的水都没有。
    
    这种骂人的话你肯定是从没听过的，不过妮娜从来都不是那种普通的泼妇。当那个可怜的人在解渴的时候，你却打开了另一个桶，把里面的酒冲洗干净，然后把那些还完好无损的罐子装满酒。说起来，还是留一些以后用吧……
    
    她喝完了吗？
    
    “差不多吧。天啊，这太奇怪了……我一直在喝酒，可尽管已经开始感到有点醉了，却只觉得有那么一点点兴奋感而已。这肯定不对，也一点都不好玩。我得再喝得醉一点，才能把一切都看清楚才行。
    
    嗯，这里的时间并不流动，所以她不可能喝得比现在更醉了。你觉得这听起来挺合理的吧。
    
    “是啊，但是——”她又喝了一大口，“不过这个地方似乎对某些事情非常‘挑剔’，只允许某些事情发生，而拒绝其他事情。比如，我们是怎么呼吸的？又是怎么走路的？这里的时间并不流动，对吧？我们并不会感到越来越饿或者越来越渴，但我们的血液仍在血管里流动。
    
    这难道不是个好消息吗？这意味着，无论背后隐藏着什么，它对这个与韦弗特过去有关的虚构事件的控制力，并没有人们想象中那么大。
    
    “真是该死，太让人恼火了。”妮娜盯着那个麦芽酒桶，然后用拳头狠狠地敲了一下那块陈旧的木头。“你这个该死的叛徒，让我产生了希望，结果却让我大失所望。我们本来应该是关系很好的朋友啊，但你却背叛了我。
    
    好了好了，这可不是麦酒的错。不过这就引出了一个问题：当你离开这个地方后，这种酒会不会立刻对妮娜产生影响呢？嗯，现在想这些还为时过早——你首先得想办法出去才行。
    
    “我们走吧，兄弟。这种情况真是糟透了。

rows.original: Examine the bodies laid out in the recesses.
rows.translation: 检查那些摆放在角落里的尸体。
rows.raw: "Examine the bodies laid out in the recesses."

rows.original:
You keep a healthy, respectful distance from the cubbyholes and examine them at arm's length. This was once a storeroom, but it's been turned into a makeshift morgue by the Wayfort's inhabitants as losses from the Godswar mounted. The recesses clearly weren't meant for bodies, being unable to comfortably accommodate the average boreal elf's proportions, but that's all worked out since few if any of the remains are whole to begin with.

        Morbid.
        
        There's nothing useful to be had here, just old yellowed bones. With the haphazard way the corpses were treated and shoved out of sight, in addition to the stack of funerary urns up against the far wall, it's likely that this was meant as a temporary measure until the fallen could be properly cremated. Now, they still await a proper interment that will never come — while it may not have created any of the restless memories that now wander the halls of Wayfort past, one doubts that it's helped matters, either.
rows.translation:
你与那些小隔间保持着适当的距离，站在一定距离外观察它们。这里原本是一个储藏室，但随着“神战”造成的损失不断增加，荒废驿堡的居民们将其临时改成了停尸房。这些凹陷显然并不是为人类身体而设计的，因为它们根本无法舒适地容纳普通极北精灵的体型……不过，由于这些遗骸几乎都没有保持完整的形态，所以这个问题也就不存在了。

        真是令人毛骨悚然。
        
        这里没有任何有用的东西，只有那些泛黄的骨头。从这些尸体被随意处理后丢弃在隐蔽的地方，以及靠在远墙边的那些葬瓮来看，很可能这里原本只是作为临时安置场所，等阵这些遇难者会被妥善火化处理。如今，他们仍在等待一场应有的安葬仪式，然而这场仪式永远也不会到来。虽然这场仪式或许并没有引发那些如今在荒废驿堡的厅堂中萦绕不去的回忆，但人们也很难相信它对缓解现状起到了任何作用。

rows.original: Remembering Thalia's words, you stop a respectful distance from the massed, bone-filled recesses and consider your next move. While the remains are discrete from each other — as haphazardly as the corpses were treated, at least they weren't jumbled into one big bone pile — age and the cramped conditions make it virtually impossible to tell what's what. Thalia may have been a frostmander before being an Astrida, but not only did she come with a retinue from Tychris, it's also impossible to tell at a glance which remains are boreal elven, human, imperial elven, or any of the other locals who helped take up fighting arms in the last days of the Wayfort's commission. Sifting through the bones at random is not just likely to prove fruitless, but also attract the wrong kind of attention as you mess with the restless dead; the recesses are arranged in six rows and six columns, and each is further divided into upper, middle and lower sections. Unless you know exactly in which row and column, as well as what section Thalia's bones lie, trying to retrieve them is going to be a fool's errand. With this in mind, will you still persist in searching for what's left of Thalia?
rows.translation: 想起塔莉娅的话，你在距离那些布满骨头的遗迹一段适当的距离外停了下来，思考着下一步该怎么做。虽然这些遗骸彼此之间是分开的——毕竟这些尸体当初被处理的方式十分随意，至少没有被胡乱堆成一堆——但由于时间的侵蚀以及狭小的存放环境，几乎不可能分辨出哪些是人类的遗骸，哪些是其他动物的。 虽然塞莉亚在成为阿斯特里达之前可能曾是霜冻巨魔的一员，但她不仅带着来自提克里斯的随从，而且仅凭外表也根本无法分辨那些随从中哪些是北方精灵、人类、帝国精灵，又哪些是在荒废驿堡任务即将结束的那些日子里加入战斗的当地居民。 随意翻动这些骨头不仅很可能一无所获，还会因为你在摆弄这些不安宁的死者而招来不必要的注意；这些骨头的排列方式是六行六列，每一列又进一步被分为上、中、下三部分。除非你能准确知道塔莉娅的骨头位于哪一行、哪一列，以及属于哪个区域，否则试图取出它们只会是徒劳无功的。 考虑到这一点，你还会继续寻找塔莉娅的遗骸吗？

rows.original: All right, you're ready to do this. Stepping up the recesses, you make ready to rummage in search of Thalia's remains. In which row will you search?
rows.translation: 好的，你已经准备好做这件事了。登上台阶，你准备好翻找搜寻塔莉娅的遗骸。你会在哪一排搜寻呢？

rows.original: And in which column will you search?
rows.translation: 那么，你将在哪一列中进行搜索呢？
rows.raw: "\n            And in which column will you search?"

rows.original: Having narrowed down the recess, in which section does Thalia's bones lie?
rows.translation: 在确定了这个凹陷的位置之后，塔莉娅的骨头应该位于哪个区域呢？

rows.original: [var0 |You pick out the remains in question and start searching through them. It isn't long before you find confirmation that you've got the right body — a hooked, heavy claw raises suspicions, but you're only certain when you find a black scale. Faded with age and brittle, it nevertheless undeniably came from one of Nareva's famous godsworn. These have to be Thalia's remains, then. Despite the crawling sensation of the back of your neck, no shattered spirits arrive to menace you. Nevertheless, you work quickly, grabbing one of the empty urns and shoving what's left of Thalia into it. Nina works alongside you, dusting off bones, claws, teeth and scales before dumping them into the urn; thank the gods the garrison of Wayfort past kept the bodies discrete and didn't just turn this place into one huge ossuary. You try to get as little dust as possible mixed in with Thalia's remains, but it's not a pretty sight either way. At last, though, you're done. Slapping a lid onto the earthenware urn, you seal it and stow it away with your other things before dusting off your hands; Nina gives you a look, to which you can only reply with a shrug and embittered smile. Hopefully this will be enough to unanchor Thalia from the grand hall and let her come along with you; for now, you need to get going before trouble finds you. |You pick out the remains in question and start searching through them, movements growing more frantic as you realize that these can't be a frostmander's and you've gotten the wrong person. Admitting defeat, you turn your attention from the yellowed, brittle remains just as a sudden chill runs down your spine and the glow in the air dims; as you'd feared, your rummaging through the dead has attracted unwelcome attention in the form of several shattered spirits shambling your way, manifesting through the walls to grab at you. Perhaps you should double-check as to where Thalia lies before making your next attempt... It's a fight! ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你挑选出那些可疑的残骸，开始仔细检查。不久之后，你就得到了确认——你找到的确实是正确的尸体。一只钩状的、沉重的爪子引起了你的怀疑，但直到你发现了一片黑色的鳞片，你才终于确定了这一点。尽管随着时间的流逝而变得褪色且脆弱，但毫无疑问，这确实属于娜瑞瓦那些著名的神之誓约持有者之一。那么，这一定是塔莉娅的遗骸了。 尽管你的后颈会有一种刺痛的感觉，但并没有任何破碎的灵魂前来威胁你。尽管如此，你还是动作迅速地抓起一个空瓮，将塔莉娅剩下的残骸全部塞了进去。妮娜也加入了你的工作，她仔细清理那些骨头、爪子、牙齿和鳞片，然后把它们全部扔进瓮里。谢天谢地，荒废驿堡驻军的士兵们把那些尸体处理得相当隐秘，才没有把这里变成一个巨大的骨灰堂。你尽量让塔莉娅的遗骸上沾上的灰尘尽可能少，但无论如何，这一幕都显得很不美观。 终于，你完成了所有工作。你盖上陶瓮的盖子，将其密封好，然后和其他物品一起收好。在擦去手上的灰尘时，尼娜看了你一眼，你只能耸耸肩，露出一个苦涩的笑容作为回应。希望这些措施足以让塔莉娅摆脱大厅的束缚，让她能够与你一起离开；现在，你必须尽快行动，否则麻烦就会找上你。 |你挑出那些可疑的残骸开始仔细搜寻，但随着你逐渐意识到这些残骸不可能是霜冻巨人的，也就意味着你找错了目标，你的动作变得越来越慌乱。在认输之际，你正准备将注意力从那些已经泛黄、变得脆弱的残骸上移开，突然一阵寒意从脊背窜上心头，空气中的光芒也渐渐黯淡下来——正如你所担心的那样，你在这堆残骸中翻找的行为，已经吸引了某些不速之客的注意，几股破碎的灵魂正穿过墙壁朝你袭来，试图抓住你。 也许你在下一次尝试之前，应该先仔细确认一下塔莉娅到底位于哪里…… 这是一场激烈的战斗！ ]
rows.raw: " [var0 |You pick out the remains in question and start searching through them. It isn't long before you find confirmation that you've got the right body — a hooked, heavy claw raises suspicions, but you're only certain when you find a black scale. Faded with age and brittle, it nevertheless undeniably came from one of Nareva's famous godsworn. These have to be Thalia's remains, then. Despite the crawling sensation of the back of your neck, no shattered spirits arrive to menace you. Nevertheless, you work quickly, grabbing one of the empty urns and shoving what's left of Thalia into it. Nina works alongside you, dusting off bones, claws, teeth and scales before dumping them into the urn; thank the gods the garrison of Wayfort past kept the bodies discrete and didn't just turn this place into one huge ossuary. You try to get as little dust as possible mixed in with Thalia's remains, but it's not a pretty sight either way. At last, though, you're done. Slapping a lid onto the earthenware urn, you seal it and stow it away with your other things before dusting off your hands; Nina gives you a look, to which you can only reply with a shrug and embittered smile. Hopefully this will be enough to unanchor Thalia from the grand hall and let her come along with you; for now, you need to get going before trouble finds you. |You pick out the remains in question and start searching through them, movements growing more frantic as you realize that these can't be a frostmander's and you've gotten the wrong person. Admitting defeat, you turn your attention from the yellowed, brittle remains just as a sudden chill runs down your spine and the glow in the air dims; as you'd feared, your rummaging through the dead has attracted unwelcome attention in the form of several shattered spirits shambling your way, manifesting through the walls to grab at you. Perhaps you should double-check as to where Thalia lies before making your next attempt... It's a fight! ] "

rows.original: With Thalia's remains in hand, you hurry down the twisting corridors of the Wayfort past, the urn's weight making itself known every step of the way. No doubt intimidated by your sense of urgency, the shattered spirits keep a wide berth from you, and you're able to make it back to the grand hall unmolested. Thalia? It takes several moments for the Astrida's spirit to manifest, but no sooner has she seen the urn in your hands that she looks that bit more corporeal already. Her shoulders shake, and slowly she reaches out with those gnarled claws of hers, forgetting that she can't hold the urn in her state. Is... you managed it. [pc.swornGod nareva |What am I saying? Of course you managed it. I shouldn't project my own failures onto the new generation, I'm so terribly sorry. |I'd wondered... no. I should dare to hope again; forgive me for not believing in you. ] Well, you still can't be absolutely sure that you got the correct remains until she tries it and it works. If she doesn't mind? Y-yes, of course. A moment to compose myself, please. A sudden electric sensation sweeps through the air, and then the ghostly image of Thalia rises a little off the ground. The spirit's humanoid appearance dissolves upon itself, turning into a wisp of ethereal mist, then sweeps up and starts flowing into the urn in your hands. While there's a brief moment of doubt as to whether you really got the right remains or all of them, the transference of Thalia from the grand hall to the urn seems to go off without a hitch. Is everything all right in there? It's comfortable enough considering our circumstances, thank you. If you wouldn't mind, [pc.name], would you try leaving the grand hall? Any particular direction? No. Sounds easy enough. Thank the gods, the urn doesn't feel any heavier than it was before Thalia entered it; you step around the remains of the tables and make your way into the throne room, half-expecting something drastic and dramatic to happen when you cross some unseen threshold. It doesn't. You've made it all the way up to the throne when the distinct sound of joyous weeping rises from the urn. Everything's turned out all right, then? I... I've never been able to make it past any of the grand hall's exits before, Thalia says from her urn when she finally composes herself. I suppose too much of me was wrapped up in that place, trying to save the lives who were brought in while we weren't actually under attack. But now... my guess wasn't wrong. With something as important to her as her body here with you, she's finally able to leave. Tethered to this urn the same way that I was to the grand hall, but at least this can be carried around. I suppose that truly severing all attachments is something only the goddess can do for me. Yeah, just hold tight on that thought. Once you're out of here, there'll be nothing stopping you from heading straight to Tychris and Nareva's doorstep. For now, though, you need to get out of here, and having Thalia around will no doubt help with that. If she's ready? Time doesn't flow here, but it nevertheless feels like an aeon since we were all wrenched into this faux-reality. Let me assure you that I have never been more ready to depart a place.
rows.translation: 手中握着塔莉娅的遗骸，你匆匆穿过荒废驿堡城堡那些蜿蜒曲折的走廊，那个骨灰瓮的重量在每一步都让你感到明显。那些受到你急切情绪影响的幽灵们，显然被你的气势吓住了，它们都远远地避开了你，因此你得以顺利地回到大厅，没有遇到任何阻碍。 塔莉娅？ 阿斯特里达的灵魂花了好一会儿才显现出来，但当她看到你手中的骨灰瓮时，她的形体似乎立刻变得更为真实了。她的肩膀微微颤抖着，慢慢地伸出那些布满老茧的爪子，却忘记了在目前这种状态下她根本无法握住那个骨灰瓮。 你……真的做到了。 [pc.swornGod nareva |我在说什么呢？你当然做到了。我不应该把自己的失败归咎于新一代人，我真的很抱歉。 |我曾经怀疑过……不，我应该再次勇敢地抱有希望；请原谅我之前没有相信你。 ] 嗯，直到她尝试使用并且发现它确实有效之前，你仍然无法确定自己得到的确实是正确的残骸。如果她不介意的话 是的，当然可以。请给我一点时间，让我先调整一下情绪。 突然，一股电一般的感觉在空气中荡漾开来，随后塔莉娅的幽灵形象缓缓从地面升起。这个灵体的类人形态逐渐消散，化作一缕轻盈的雾气，然后缓缓流入你手中的骨灰瓮中。在这一刹那，你不禁产生了些许疑虑真的只要找到了所有正确的遗骸，将塔莉娅从大厅转移到瓮中这个过程似乎就不会出现问题。 里面一切都好吗？ 考虑到我们的实际情况，这个已经足够舒适了，谢谢。如果您不介意的话[pc.name]，你愿意试着离开这个大厅吗？ 有什么特别的建议或方向吗？ 不。 听起来挺简单的。谢天谢地，这个瓮并没有因为塔莉娅进入之后而变重；你绕过那些破碎的桌子，走进了王座厅，心里还在期待着，当自己穿过某个看不见的界限时，会发生什么惊天动地的事件。 并没有。 当瓮中传来欢快的哭泣声时，你已经登上了王位。那么，一切最终都变得好起来了，对吗？ 我……以前从来没能从大厅的任何出口逃出去过。当塔莉娅终于平静下来时，她的骨灰瓮发出了声音。我想，我在很大程度上过于执着于那个地方，一心想要拯救那些被带到那里的人们，而实际上我们当时并没有受到攻击。但现在……我的猜测并没有错。 既然她将自己如此珍视的身体交给了你，她终于可以放心离开了。 这个骨灰瓮与我与那座宏伟大厅之间的联系一样紧密，但至少这个骨灰瓮是可以随身携带的。我想，真正切断所有这些羁绊，只有女神才能为我做到。 没错，只要牢牢记住这个想法。一旦你离开了这里，就没有什么能阻止你直接前往提克里斯和娜瑞瓦的家门口。不过现在，你首先需要离开这里，而有塔莉娅在身边，无疑会帮助你实现这个目标。前提是，她已经准备好了才行。 在这里，时间仿佛并没有流逝，但自从我们都被卷入这个虚假的现实之中，感觉上仿佛已经过了漫长的岁月。我可以向您保证，我从未像现在这样迫切地想要离开某个地方。

rows.original: Either you haven't found information on where Thalia's body is in the morgue, or you need to double-check your information lest your memory be spotty. Whatever the case, you're not ready to make the attempt right now and back down. You'll be back later when you're sure of where Thalia lies...
rows.translation: 要么是你还没有找到关于塔莉娅的尸体在停尸房里的位置的任何信息，要么就是你需要重新核实一下你掌握的信息，因为你的记忆可能不太准确。无论如何，你现在都还没有准备好进行尝试，所以只好放弃了。等你确定塔莉娅的尸体在哪里之后，再回来继续行动吧……
rows.raw: "\n        Either you haven't found information on where Thalia's body is in the morgue, or you need to double-check your information lest your memory be spotty. Whatever the case, you're not ready to make the attempt right now and back down. You'll be back later when you're sure of where Thalia lies..."

rows.original: Since Nina says this place is safe, it can't hurt to try to get some shut-eye.
rows.translation: 既然妮娜说这个地方很安全，那试着睡一会儿也没什么坏处吧。
rows.raw: "Since Nina says this place is safe, it can't hurt to try to get some shut-eye."

rows.original: No sooner have you set foot in your sleeping quarters that Nina slams the creaky door shut behind you and bars it. Not that it'll keep the psychic apparitions out, but you have to admit that it gives you a little peace of mind and that's vitally important in this place. "We're safe here," she gasps. "And by safe, I mean safe safe. Or as safe as it can get in this place, man. I know what you're thinking, and yes, the door isn't going to stop them in the slightest. But this was a place of rest, of peaceful dreams, and that totally like, helps hold them at bay." Know what? That does make sense, given that you're dealing with what very well may be figments of your own nightmares, or at least your own that've been thrown into the mix. "Yeah, okay, sure. But like, more importantly, we can actually talk without worrying about being jumped." Has she figured out something she wants to tell you? A nod. "Sure, man. Like, why we're here in the first place." All right, that's worth sitting down and having a discussion, if she doesn't mind. "Yeah, okay. Just give me a moment to catch my breath, man, and we can begin."
rows.translation: 你刚踏进自己的卧室，尼娜就砰地关上了身后那扇吱嘎作响的门，还上了门闩。虽然这并不能阻止那些心灵幻影进来，但你必须承认，这确实能让你稍微安心一些——而在这个地方，这一点至关重要。 “我们在这里很安全，”她喘着气说道，“我说的安全，是指安全得不能再安全。或者说，在这个地方已经算是尽可能安全了，老兄。我知道你在想什么，没错，那扇门根本无法阻止他们分毫。但这里本来是用来休息、用来做美梦的地方，这样的环境确实有助于把他们挡在外面。” 你知道吗？考虑到你面对的很可能是你自己噩梦中的幻象，或者至少是你自己的东西被混了进来，这种说法确实有道理。 “嗯，好吧，确实如此。但更重要的是，我们其实可以交谈，而不用担心会遭到袭击。” 她是不是已经想通了什么，想要告诉你？ 她点了点头。“没错，老兄。比如，我们最初为什么会在这里。” 好吧，如果她不介意的话，这确实值得坐下来好好讨论一番。 “嗯，好的。给我一点时间喘口气，老兄，然后我们就可以开始了。”

Like, why we're here in the first place." All right, that's worth sitting down and having a discussion, if she doesn't mind. "Yeah, okay. Just give me a moment to catch my breath, man, and we can begin.""

rows.original: So... she said she's figured out why you're here in the first place. That implies that being yanked out of your journey and being trapped here is part of what's supposed to happen. Nina's guarded in her response, considering her words carefully before replying. "I think so, man." Does that mean that everything's going to turn out well, since it's part of the vision and they've never let her down? "No, man. This isn't like, part of any vision at all — I told you that when we first ended up in this place. This isn't part of any vision, and so we still can get ourselves into some really hot soup. I'm just saying that I think this is something that was supposed to happen, even if it was because my vision was subverted." All right, now she's just putting words together. Cutting to the chase — what[pc.isDK | the fuck ] could possibly be so important that it's worth all this madness? "There's no need to get so ticked off, I finally figured out what the visions were trying to have me do, why we were going around collecting all that stuff until we were so rudely interrupted and yanked into the Wayfort's past. Remember what I was saying?" Something about seeing, entering... that kind of stuff. "The brew —" she taps her head just by her eyes "— lets you see, the conjuror's concoction lets you enter, the winterstem keeps you alive. But at the end of it all, you've still got to leave, or else you'll be stuck in the dreamscape forever. That's not possible to replicate via simple alchemy, you need a jolt of power from a bona fide dreamwalker to get it going. Something about seeing that funny-mirror version of myself got my memory going, and now I've figured it all out, how to tie together all the reagents. That was the thing we're here to collect, the knowledge, and now I have it. The last piece's fallen into place." Really. So maybe the vision wasn't wrong at all, maybe you being yanked out of the ether by an unspeakable horror was all set up from the start. "Well, man, I sure as the Seven didn't see any of that in the vision. But still, you know... everything like, happens for a reason, man. Sometimes another vision will pick up where the old one left off, seamless as a latex goo. Some call it destiny, but I call it, like... um..." Nina furrows her brow and thinks really seriously, quite the achievement for her. "Look, I'm not saying anything's certain save for nine portions of brazenberry ale to four of conjuror's concoction, and one portion of winterstem. That, and to make sure that last one's properly pounded into a paste with mortar and pestle to release all the good stuff in the leaves and stem, but it's okay if you make do without." And then she mixes all that together to make this Juice thing? If it's that simple, any two-bit alchemist would've stumbled upon it long ago. Gods, even you could make it. "Well, there's just the last step, and the most important one." Nina taps her head with a clawed finger. "You've got to activate everything, make them friends so that they like, totally get along. A little mental persuasion that just putting it over a flame isn't going to do, that just makes them angry. Remembering how to do the persuading is why we need to be here to begin with; that's what I figured out after seeing that version of me and thinking on it, because it's the kind of thing that you can only learn by getting into the nitty-gritty with things." You sigh and rub your temples. All right, so this is all well and good, whatever this Juice thing is. Problem, though — you're still trapped in a horrible version of the Wayfort as it was in the past, tucked away on the edges of the Ways. Is this Juice going to help you get out of here? "Actually, that's pretty likely."
rows.translation: 所以……她说她已经弄清楚了你最初为什么会来到这里。这意味着，被强行从你的旅程中拽出来并被困在这里，其实是注定会发生的事情的一部分。 尼娜在回答时非常谨慎，她在说话之前仔细考虑了自己的言辞。我也是这么想的，伙计。” 那么，既然这是他们共同愿景的一部分，而且他们从来没有让她失望过，是不是意味着一切都会顺利呢？ “不，伙计。这件事根本不属于任何愿景的范畴——我们刚来到这个地方的时候，我就跟你说过这一点。这并不符合任何既定的规划或愿景，因此我们仍然可能会陷入一些棘手的麻烦中。我只是想说，我认为这件事本就应该发生，即便是因为我的设想被颠覆了才导致了这样的结果。 好吧，现在她只是在把一些词语组合起来而已。直接说重点吧——到底是什么？[pc.isDK | 去他的 ]没必要这么生气，我终于弄明白了那些幻象究竟想让我做什么，也明白了为什么我们要收集那些东西，直到我们被突然打断，被强行带到了荒废驿堡的过去。还记得我刚才说过什么吗？” “就是关于‘看见’、‘进入’之类的东西。” “那种药剂——”她用手指轻敲着自己的眼睛部位——“能让你看见；那个巫师调配的药剂能让你‘进入’某个境界；而冬茎草则能让你保持生命。但归根结底，你仍然必须离开，否则就会永远被困在那个梦境之中。这种效果是无法通过简单的炼金术来实现的，你需要一位真正的梦行者赋予你力量，才能让这一切发生。看到那个镜像中自己的模样，似乎触发了我的记忆，现在我终于想明白了，知道该如何把所有这些炼金材料组合起来使用了。那个这正是我们来这里所要获取的东西——那些知识，而现在我终于得到了它。最后一块拼图也终于落到了该在的位置。” 真的吗？那么也许那个预言一点都没有错，也许你被某种无法形容的恐怖力量从虚无中拽了出来，这一切其实从一开始就已经被安排好了。 “嗯，说实话，我可一点都没预见到这些那个在那个幻象之中。不过，你知道……一切事情的发生都是有原因的。有时候，另一个幻象会接上上一个幻象留下的线索，衔接得天衣无缝。有些人称之为命运，但我更愿意称之为……嗯，就这样吧。尼娜皱起了眉头，认真地思考起来——这对她来说确实是一项不小的成就。‘听着，我并不是说有什么事情是确定的，只不过是九份厚果麦芽酒、四份巫师的调配饮品，再加上一份冬茎酒而已。还有，为了确保把那些食材彻底捣成糊状，这样才能让叶子和茎中的营养成分全部释放出来；不过，如果不这样做也没关系。” 然后她把所有这些材料混合在一起，就制成了这种果汁吧？如果真的那么简单，随便哪个蹩脚的炼金术士早就发现了。天啊，连神明们恐怕也能轻易做到吧。你嗯，现在只剩下最后一步了，也是最重要的一步。”妮娜用带爪子的手指轻轻敲了敲自己的头。“你必须把所有东西都激活起来，让它们成为朋友，让它们彼此喜欢，能够很好地相处。只需要稍加劝说，让他们明白仅仅把东西放在火上烧是行不通的，那样只会让他们更加生气。之所以我们需要在这里做这些劝说工作，正是因为我们需要回忆起如何进行这样的劝说；我在看到那个版本的自己并仔细思考之后，才明白了这一点。因为这类事情，只有通过深入实际去操作，才能真正学会如何去做。你叹了口气，揉了揉太阳穴。好吧，不管这种“果汁”到底是什么，这一切听起来都还不错。但问题在于——你仍然被困在了过去那个糟糕版本的“荒废驿堡”之中，被困在那些道路的边缘地带。这个“果汁”真的能帮你离开这里吗？ “其实，很有可能吧。
rows.raw: " So... she said she's figured out why you're here in the first place. That implies that being yanked out of your journey and being trapped here is part of what's supposed to happen. Nina's guarded in her response, considering her words carefully before replying. "I think so, man." Does that mean that everything's going to turn out well, since it's part of the vision and they've never let her down? "No, man. This isn't like, part of any vision at all — I told you that when we first ended up in this place. This isn't part of any vision, and so we still can get ourselves into some really hot soup. I'm just saying that I think this is something that was supposed to happen, even if it was because my vision was subverted." All right, now she's just putting words together. Cutting to the chase — what[pc.isDK | the fuck ] could possibly be so important that it's worth all this madness? "There's no need to get so ticked off, I finally figured out what the visions were trying to have me do, why we were going around collecting all that stuff until we were so rudely interrupted and yanked into the Wayfort's past. Remember what I was saying?" Something about seeing, entering... that kind of stuff. "The brew —" she taps her head just by her eyes "— lets you see, the conjuror's concoction lets you enter, the winterstem keeps you alive. But at the end of it all, you've still got to leave, or else you'll be stuck in the dreamscape forever. That's not possible to replicate via simple alchemy, you need a jolt of power from a bona fide dreamwalker to get it going. Something about seeing that funny-mirror version of myself got my memory going, and now I've figured it all out, how to tie together all the reagents. That was the thing we're here to collect, the knowledge, and now I have it. The last piece's fallen into place." Really. So maybe the vision wasn't wrong at all, maybe you being yanked out of the ether by an unspeakable horror was all set up from the start. "Well, man, I sure as the Seven didn't see any of that in the vision. But still, you know... everything like, happens for a reason, man. Sometimes another vision will pick up where the old one left off, seamless as a latex goo. Some call it destiny, but I call it, like... um..." Nina furrows her brow and thinks really seriously, quite the achievement for her. "Look, I'm not saying anything's certain save for nine portions of brazenberry ale to four of conjuror's concoction, and one portion of winterstem. That, and to make sure that last one's properly pounded into a paste with mortar and pestle to release all the good stuff in the leaves and stem, but it's okay if you make do without." And then she mixes all that together to make this Juice thing? If it's that simple, any two-bit alchemist would've stumbled upon it long ago. Gods, even you could make it. "Well, there's just the last step, and the most important one." Nina taps her head with a clawed finger. "You've got to activate everything, make them friends so that they like, totally get along. A little mental persuasion that just putting it over a flame isn't going to do, that just makes them angry. Remembering how to do the persuading is why we need to be here to begin with; that's what I figured out after seeing that version of me and thinking on it, because it's the kind of thing that you can only learn by getting into the nitty-gritty with things." You sigh and rub your temples. All right, so this is all well and good, whatever this Juice thing is. Problem, though — you're still trapped in a horrible version of the Wayfort as it was in the past, tucked away on the edges of the Ways. Is this Juice going to help you get out of here? "Actually, that's pretty likely.""

rows.original: All right, now that's welcome news. If she's right, even if this miserable situation isn't part of any of her visions, one might charitably interpret the vision that led you here as having taken care of things. All right, how is this Juice going to help? "It'll let you see things as they might be. Could be. As they really are. All of the above, man. Doesn't sound like a lot, but I think you can agree that in a trippy place like this, clarity's coming at a premium. I think we're safe enough here for me to try making some — you did bring the ingredients I asked you to before we left, didn't you?" [var0 |Yeah, you have it all right here. "Groovy, dude. Hand over the goods, and I'll start cooking right away." |Actually... "Aww, man. Don't tell me you forgot to bring the stuff even after I reminded you before we set off." Nina sighs and shrugs. "Well, sucks. I get the feeling that old as this place is, there's still usable stuff to be salvaged here and there. Maybe if you look hard enough we'll still be able to put the pieces together. If and when we do, we can come back here where it's safe and I'll put together some Juice for you, man." ]
