rows.translation: 询问阿斯特莱娅关于她自己以及她的成长经历。在加入阿斯特里达组织之前，她过着怎样的生活？
rows.raw: "Ask Astraea about herself and her upbringing. What sort of life did she lead before she joined the Order Astrida?"

rows.original: [var0 |You already know all about the Order Astrida, having learned of them from earlier in your travels, but it’ll do you good to hear it from someone else within the Order, and Astraea seems like she’d enjoy talking about it. You ask her to tell you more about the Order, and what it means to be a 'paladin of Nareva.’ |You ask Astraea more about the Order that she mentioned that she came from. What is the Order Astrida? And she said that she was a 'paladin of Nareva’ – what does that mean? ] [atFH |Astraea sets down her flagon and drags her index finger across its rim as she recounts her time with the Order. |Astraea hums and brings her hands together, her fingers and thumbs pressing into each other as she recounts her time with the Order. ] Her body language shifts immediately – thinking about the Order has put her in a better mood. "They’re my family," she says after a moment. "Not by blood, but... in a way that binds us tighter than that. Each of us are blessed by Nareva herself – from our conception, she hand-crafts our very beings into what we are when we’re born. Each of us being bound to Nareva gives us a sort of bond and kinship that I couldn’t hope to properly express to someone outside of the Order." [pc.isDK |Ah, it’s a cult, then. ]You try and keep the topic moving by asking what the Order Astrida does – both within its own community and in the greater world. "Nareva is the goddess of magic, knowledge, and secrets. Once the Godswar had ended, the Order was created to find and protect any and all places or objects of knowledge, magic, and power – that includes anything from a place as inundated with magic as the Ways Between, to a dusty library found in some old, ruined castle or something. Knowledge is precious: knowing where and how to strike an opponent in a fight is a far greater weapon than a sword could ever hope to be." That explains why the Order would have been so interested in Matiha’s fortress, and how it started to teleport one day – magic that powerful would obviously draw some attention from a [pc.isDK |cult |group ] that focuses on magic and its study. But Astraea said that the Order is in the business of 'finding and protecting’ these objects and places. Does that mean hiding them away from the rest of the world? "If that is what Nareva, our mother, would will it," she answers. From the phrasing, that seems about as deep as you should dig into the subject. You keep the topic moving by asking what she does within the Order. She had just explained that the Order’s mission statement is to find places and things of power and then protect them, but her mission to attack Matiha and destroy her fortress was very much something different. "I’m a magehunter. The description is in the name, I should think." True enough, but... why does she hunt mages? "For the same reason a town’s guard would punish a criminal. Not every mage in this world is a good person and they don’t all use their powers for the benefit of the world or the people around them. Would you rather a person like Matiha run around without fear of retribution?" That makes sense to you. How does one join the Order? "They don’t," she answers plainly. "Nor is anyone 'invited,’ not since the end of the Godswar. Each member of the Order is hand-crafted by Nareva while they’re still in the womb." Okay... in that case, how is the mother selected? The possibility that the Order is even more 'insular’ than that, to the point that new 'recruits’ are inbred, occurs to you, but you don’t want to suggest it yourself. That’d be rude. "The mother is, invariably, the high-priestess of the goddess's church. The one closest to Nareva herself. Once a year, she engages in a tantric ritual with the finest scholars, mages, and bards, that lasts a week. And from their combined offerings, Nareva sculpts a new life, born into the Order to serve her." Astraea flexes the fingers in her glove. "That’s how I was born, and that’s why my skills with polymorphization are as adept as they are. I have the blood of the church's high priestess; the lineage of some of the most skilled and powerful magicians in Savarra; and the gift of our goddess Nareva, all within me." [pc.dcb |So, wait, back up. The high priestess of the church is commanded, by a goddess, to leave her temple; find the most accomplished [silly |nerds |scholars ] in the world; and then have a week-long orgy with them? "No," she answers. "The [silly |nerds |scholars ] are invited to the church. The high priestess does not leave." Right, your mistake. |So... you’re a bit caught up on what she said earlier. About a 'tantric ritual’ that lasts seven days. Does that mean what you think it means? "If you think it means a week-long orgy with some of the most accomplished scholars in the world, then yes," she answers. Right, as long as you’re clear. |So... back up a second. She said something about a 'tantric ritual’ that lasted seven days. You’re not so good with unique words like 'tantric;’ what does that mean? "It means the high priestess has a week-long orgy with the world’s smartest, most accomplished witches, warlocks, sorcerers and scholars," she answers simply. Oh. ... Only a week? You could go for way longer than that. ]
rows.translation: [var0 |你在旅途中早已经了解了关于阿斯特里达骑士团的一切，但再听别人讲述这些也会对你有所帮助，而阿斯特莱娅似乎很乐意谈论这个话题。你便请她再多讲一些关于这个骑士团，以及成为“娜瑞瓦的圣骑士”意味着什么。 |你向阿斯特莱娅询问了更多关于她所提到的那个组织的信息。这个名为“阿斯特里达”的组织到底是什么？她还说自己是一名“娜瑞瓦的圣骑士”——这到底意味着什么？ ] [atFH |阿斯特莱娅放下她的酒壶，用食指轻轻划过壶口，一边回忆着自己在那支组织中度过的时光。 |阿斯特莱娅轻声哼着曲子，双手交叠在一起，手指和拇指相互挤压着，同时她开始回忆自己在那个组织中度过的时光。 ]她的肢体语言立刻发生了变化——想到这个组织，她的情绪似乎变得更好了。 “他们是我的家人，”过了一会儿，她说道，“虽然不是血缘关系，但……有一种比血缘关系更紧密的纽带将我们联系在一起。我们每一个人都得到了娜瑞瓦的庇佑——从我们受孕的那一刻起，她就亲自塑造我们的本质，让我们在出生时成为现在的样子。我们每个人都与娜瑞瓦有着这样的联系，这种亲情和羁绊，对于组织之外的人来说，我恐怕永远也无法用语言准确表达出来。 [pc.isDK |啊，原来是个狂热粉丝团体啊。 ]你通过询问“阿斯特里达教团在其自身社区以及更广阔的世界中究竟做了些什么”来推动讨论的进行。 “娜雷瓦是魔法、知识与秘密的女神。在神战结束后，人们成立了这个教团，旨在寻找并保护一切与知识、魔法和力量相关的场所或物品——这些对象可能包括像‘道路之间’那样充满魔力的地方，也可能是一些位于古老废墟中的布满灰尘的图书馆之类的东西。知识才是真正的财富：在战斗中知道该在何处、如何攻击对手，这种能力远比任何一把剑都要强大。 这也解释了为什么教团会对玛蒂哈的堡垒如此感兴趣，以及为什么有一天它们突然开始使用传送魔法——如此强大的魔法，显然会引起别人的注意。 [pc.isDK |狂热追随者 |团队 ]这个组织专注于魔法及其研究。 但是阿斯特莱娅表示，这个组织的职责是“寻找并保护”这些物品和地点。那么，这是否意味着要将它们隐藏起来，不让外界知道呢？ 如果那正是我们的母亲娜瑞瓦所希望的，那么我们就应该这么做。”她的回答让人觉得，关于这个话题，似乎也就没有必要再深入探讨了。 你通过询问她在组织中担任什么职务，继续引导谈话继续进行下去。她刚刚解释过，该组织的使命是寻找那些拥有强大力量的地方和物品，并加以保护，但她攻击玛蒂哈并摧毁她的堡垒这一行动，显然与这一使命截然不同。 我是一名猎魔人。名字本身就已经说明了一切，我想应该是这样的。” 确实如此，但是…… 为什么她会追捕法师吗？ “原因和城镇卫兵惩罚罪犯是一样的。这个世界上并不是所有的法师都是好人，他们也并非都会将自己的力量用于造福世界或帮助周围的人。难道不是吗？你像玛蒂哈这样的人，能够毫无惧怕地四处行动，确实很了不起。” 你这么认为的话，那要怎么加入那个组织呢？ “他们并不会主动加入，”她简单地回答道，“自从神战结束之后，也就再也没有人被‘邀请’加入过。秩序中的每一个成员都是在还未出生时，由娜瑞瓦亲手制造的。” 好吧……那么，母亲是如何被选中的呢？你是否想过，这个秩序可能更加与世隔绝，以至于新的“成员”都是近亲繁殖的产物？但你又不愿意自己提出这个想法。那样做可太无礼了。 “母亲永远都是女神教会的高阶祭司，也是最接近娜雷瓦本人的人。每年，她都会与最优秀的学者、法师和吟游诗人一起举行为期一周的冥想仪式。通过将这些能力结合起来，娜瑞瓦塑造了一种全新的存在形式——这种存在诞生于秩序之中，旨在为她服务。“阿斯特莱娅活动着手套中的手指说道，‘我就是这样诞生的，也因此我的变形能力才会如此娴熟。我流淌着教会大祭司的血脉；继承了萨瓦拉地区一些最擅长魔法、最强大的法师的遗传基因；同时还拥有我们女神娜瑞瓦赐予我的天赋。这一切，都存在于我体内。 [pc.dcb |等等，先听我说完。这座教堂的大祭司被一位女神命令离开她的神庙，去寻找那位技艺最为精湛的人[silly |书呆子们 |学者们 ]世界上哪有这种事；然后还和他们一起疯狂地享受一周的时间？” “不，”她回答道，“没有这种事。 [silly |书呆子们 |学者们 ]被邀请来到教堂。大祭司始终没有离开。 |所以……你对她之前说的那些话还有些困惑吧？关于那个持续七天的“密宗仪式”……她的意思真的是你想象的那样吗？ “如果你认为这意味着和世界上一些最杰出的学者一起进行为期一周的狂欢活动，那么没错，”她回答道。 好吧，只要你能弄清楚这个意思就行了。 |所以……等一下。她提到了什么持续七天的“密宗仪式”？你对“密宗”这类生僻词汇不太熟悉，这到底是什么意思呢？ “简单来说，就是大祭司会与世界上最聪明、最有能力的女巫、男巫、术士以及学者们一起进行为期一周的狂欢活动。”她简单地解释道。 哦…… ……才一周而已？其实这个仪式完全可以持续更长时间才对啊。 ]
rows.raw: ' [var0 |You already know all about the Order Astrida, having learned of them from earlier in your travels, but it’ll do you good to hear it from someone else within the Order, and Astraea seems like she’d enjoy talking about it. You ask her to tell you more about the Order, and what it means to be a 'paladin of Nareva.’ |You ask Astraea more about the Order that she mentioned that she came from. What is the Order Astrida? And she said that she was a 'paladin of Nareva’ – what does that mean? ] [atFH |Astraea sets down her flagon and drags her index finger across its rim as she recounts her time with the Order. |Astraea hums and brings her hands together, her fingers and thumbs pressing into each other as she recounts her time with the Order. ] Her body language shifts immediately – thinking about the Order has put her in a better mood. "They’re my family," she says after a moment. "Not by blood, but... in a way that binds us tighter than that. Each of us are blessed by Nareva herself – from our conception, she hand-crafts our very beings into what we are when we’re born. Each of us being bound to Nareva gives us a sort of bond and kinship that I couldn’t hope to properly express to someone outside of the Order." [pc.isDK |Ah, it’s a cult, then. ]You try and keep the topic moving by asking what the Order Astrida does – both within its own community and in the greater world. "Nareva is the goddess of magic, knowledge, and secrets. Once the Godswar had ended, the Order was created to find and protect any and all places or objects of knowledge, magic, and power – that includes anything from a place as inundated with magic as the Ways Between, to a dusty library found in some old, ruined castle or something. Knowledge is precious: knowing where and how to strike an opponent in a fight is a far greater weapon than a sword could ever hope to be." That explains why the Order would have been so interested in Matiha’s fortress, and how it started to teleport one day – magic that powerful would obviously draw some attention from a [pc.isDK |cult |group ] that focuses on magic and its study. But Astraea said that the Order is in the business of 'finding and protecting’ these objects and places. Does that mean hiding them away from the rest of the world? "If that is what Nareva, our mother, would will it," she answers. From the phrasing, that seems about as deep as you should dig into the subject. You keep the topic moving by asking what she does within the Order. She had just explained that the Order’s mission statement is to find places and things of power and then protect them, but her mission to attack Matiha and destroy her fortress was very much something different. "I’m a magehunter. The description is in the name, I should think." True enough, but... why does she hunt mages? "For the same reason a town’s guard would punish a criminal. Not every mage in this world is a good person and they don’t all use their powers for the benefit of the world or the people around them. Would you rather a person like Matiha run around without fear of retribution?" That makes sense to you. How does one join the Order? "They don’t," she answers plainly. "Nor is anyone 'invited,’ not since the end of the Godswar. Each member of the Order is hand-crafted by Nareva while they’re still in the womb." Okay... in that case, how is the mother selected? The possibility that the Order is even more 'insular’ than that, to the point that new 'recruits’ are inbred, occurs to you, but you don’t want to suggest it yourself. That’d be rude. "The mother is, invariably, the high-priestess of the goddess's church. The one closest to Nareva herself. Once a year, she engages in a tantric ritual with the finest scholars, mages, and bards, that lasts a week. And from their combined offerings, Nareva sculpts a new life, born into the Order to serve her." Astraea flexes the fingers in her glove. "That’s how I was born, and that’s why my skills with polymorphization are as adept as they are. I have the blood of the church's high priestess; the lineage of some of the most skilled and powerful magicians in Savarra; and the gift of our goddess Nareva, all within me." [pc.dcb |So, wait, back up. The high priestess of the church is commanded, by a goddess, to leave her temple; find the most accomplished [silly |nerds |scholars ] in the world; and then have a week-long orgy with them? "No," she answers. "The [silly |nerds |scholars ] are invited to the church. The high priestess does not leave." Right, your mistake. |So... you’re a bit caught up on what she said earlier. About a 'tantric ritual’ that lasts seven days. Does that mean what you think it means? "If you think it means a week-long orgy with some of the most accomplished scholars in the world, then yes," she answers. Right, as long as you’re clear. |So... back up a second. She said something about a 'tantric ritual’ that lasted seven days. You’re not so good with unique words like 'tantric;’ what does that mean? "It means the high priestess has a week-long orgy with the world’s smartest, most accomplished witches, warlocks, sorcerers and scholars," she answers simply. Oh. ... Only a week? You could go for way longer than that. ]'

rows.original: Ask Astraea more about the Order Astrida. What is it, in her own words?
rows.translation: 向阿斯特莱娅进一步了解“阿斯特里达组织”吧。用她自己的话来说，这个组织到底是什么？
rows.raw: "Ask Astraea more about the Order Astrida. What is it, in her own words?"

rows.original: You broach the difficult topic of what Astraea had experienced within Matiha’s fortress in the Ways Between. The last time you and Berwyn had been inside Matiha’s tower, it was a fairly simple thing without a lot of traps or twists to it – is it the same? [atFH |Astraea’s hand remains stationary on the grip of her flagon |Astraea’s body doesn’t move at the question ]. She’s totally stationary – you aren’t even certain that she’s breathing. It takes her a moment to fully come to terms with your question[atFH |, and, before she answers, she lifts her glass to her mouth and takes another swig ]. "The Ways Between has an... effect on the architecture inside it," she explains. "There are already so few buildings in the dimension, and what few that aren’t turned to ruins are difficult to explore as it is." She turns her head towards you, her face, save for her eyes, obscured by the shroud over her head. "The fortress you and Berwyn had explored before... it has changed. Or perhaps it hasn’t, and the Ways Between alters your perception of the building once you enter it. The only thing I can definitively say is that it was anything but simple." You suppose you’ll have to see for yourself how the fortress has changed. What about Matiha, the witch herself? From what you remember, she just seemed like an ordinary witch – perhaps with some exaggerated assets, but a normal woman with magic all the same. "Hmm," Astraea hums[atFH |. She thumbs the rim of her glass as she recalls meeting her ]. "Can you describe her in more detail for me? As you remember her from your previous encounter?" That she answered your question with a question caught you a bit off-guard, but you acquiesce: you remember her being tall – or maybe her massive hat just made her look taller – with pale skin all over. She had short brown her and her outfit was awfully revealing on the thighs, and she wore high-rise stockings that certainly added to the picture. And she had... well, there’s no real way to mince it: she had massive breasts. She usually had to keep them propped up with one hand, probably to give her poor back a break. [pc.dcb |Frankly, it’s a shame she turned out to be a bitch. |It’s unfortunate that she became so... disagreeable. She was really quite beautiful, even if her assets were a little excessive. |You wipe the bottom of your mouth with the back of your hand. It’s hard to think about Matiha without getting a little randy. ] "Her skin is no longer pale," Astraea answers. "It’s more... reminiscent of my own. Or, rather, a mix of how I used to look, and what I look like now. Dark gray skin, with bluish-green-colored veins arcing all throughout her body. Her hair is longer, and it’s still brown, but the roots have been frosted, turning her hair teal-colored as it grows." She pauses[atFH |, taking another drink of her ale ]. "And her eyes... I remember her eyes being... something else. Like I was staring into something... ancient? Or maybe it was staring at me. I had a hard time believing that I was in an encounter with a human being once I got a good look at her eyes." You both pause. "And her breasts are still just as large." How about how she fought? When you and Berwyn encountered her, she had the usual witch magic – she could summon a dark clone of herself to assist her in battle, and she had some minor control over the elements, including things like conjuring fireballs for her attacks. Is there anything she can teach you about how Matiha fought? Astraea’s nostrils flare as she takes a long, drawn-out exhale. Her massive body deflates as she recalls the encounter between herself and Matiha. "The fight didn’t last long enough for me to learn much of anything," she answers somberly. "I remember the rune in her study most clearly. How the world seemed to warp around it to accommodate its existence. It was like... like it was angry, and that the very physics around it had to change and shift to placate it. Simply being near it made me weak, and in turn, it was like the rune was growing, becoming stronger and more irritated in my presence." [atFH |Astraea lifts her flagon to her mouth, moving as if she was going to finish the rest of it with one hearty swig, but she hesitates, reconsidering at the last moment – and then reconsiders again, swallowing the rest of it in just a few mouthfuls. She slams the flagon back down onto the counter, the impact reverberating through the rest of the tavern. "This damn body’s got too much tolerance in it," she curses. "Garth! I’d... like another, please." |Astraea folds her arms in front of herself, wrapping them around the underside of her chest. She stays like that for a while, her head hung low, and she doesn’t say anything for some time – eventually, she rocks back and forth slightly, her fingers readjusting their grip on her arms. Is she... hugging herself? ] "Matiha cast one spell, and that was the fight," she eventually continues. "Elexis and I weren’t prepared for fighting not only someone as strong as Matiha, but inside the Ways Between. It was like the building itself had come alive to devour us. We were separated, and all I did was run. Run as far as I could." [atFH |Garth comes by eventually, a glass filled with more amber ale in his right hand to top off Astraea’s glass. She doesn’t bring it to her mouth. |Astraea sits there, the Waystone to her back, her tail wrapped protectively around her legs and the flame on its tip dimmed to barely an ember. ] That’s probably about all you’re going to get from her.
rows.translation: 你提到了一个棘手的话题：在“道路之间”地区，阿斯特莱娅在玛蒂哈的堡垒里经历了什么。上次你和贝尔温进入玛蒂哈的塔楼时，那里的情况还相当简单，并没有太多陷阱或复杂的布局——这次还会是这样吗？ [atFH |阿斯特莱娅的手依然稳稳地握着她的酒壶。 |听到这个问题，阿斯特莱娅的身体完全没有反应，一动也没有。 ]她完全静止不动，甚至都无法确定她是否还在呼吸。她需要一些时间来完全理解你的问题。[atFH |在她回答之前，她先举起杯子喝了一口。 ]界间之路’会对其中的建筑结构产生某种影响，”她解释道，“这个维度里本来就很少有建筑物，而那些没有变成废墟的建筑，本身也很难被探索。她将头转向你，除了眼睛之外，她的整张脸都被头上的面纱遮住了。“你和贝尔温之前探索过的那座堡垒……已经变了。或者也许并没有变，只是‘幽径’在你进入那座建筑之后改变了你对它的认知罢了。我唯一可以肯定地说的是，那绝对是一件非常特别的事情。但是很简单。” 你大概得亲自来看看这座堡垒发生了哪些变化吧。那么，那个女巫玛蒂哈呢？据你回忆，她只不过是个普通的女巫罢了——或许只是有些夸大其词拥有各种能力，但终究还是个拥有魔力的普通女性。 “嗯，”阿斯特莱娅轻声说道。[atFH |她轻轻用拇指摩挲着玻璃杯的边缘，回想起与他的初次相遇。 ]你能再详细地描述描述她吗？就你之前与她相遇时所记得的那样。” 她用一个问题来回答你的问题，这让你有些措手不及，但你还是同意了：你记得她个子很高——或者也许是她那顶巨大的帽子让她的个子显得更高了。看她个子更高，全身皮肤都很白。她留着棕色的短发，她的穿着在大腿部位暴露得相当多，而她穿的那些高筒袜更是为这一形象增色不少。至于她……嗯，其实没什么好委婉的：她就是庞大的胸部。她通常得用一只手把它们托起来，大概是想让自己那可怜的背部得到一些休息吧。 [pc.dcb |说实话，她后来变成了一个泼妇，真是太可惜了。 |很遗憾，她变得如此…… 令人不悦。她确实非常漂亮，尽管她的身材有些过于火辣了。 |你用手背擦了擦嘴角。一想到玛蒂哈，就忍不住会有些冲动。 ] 她的皮肤不再苍白了，”阿斯特莱娅回答道，“现在更……有点像我自己的皮肤了。或者应该说，是她过去的外貌和现在的外貌的结合。皮肤呈深灰色，全身布满了蓝绿色的血管。她的头发变长了，颜色依然是棕色，但发根部分已经变成了冰蓝色，所以头发在生长过程中会呈现出蓝绿色的色调。”她停顿了一下。[atFH |她又喝了一口麦芽酒。 ]还有她的双眼……我记得她的双眼有着某种特别之处。就好像我在凝视着某种……古老的东西？又或许，是她在注视着我。当我仔细观察她的双眼时，我实在难以相信自己正在与一个真正的人类对视。你们俩都停下了话。“而且她的胸部依然那么丰满。” 那她战斗时的表现呢？当你和贝尔温遇到她的时候，她使用了那些常见的巫术——她能够召唤出一个自己的暗影分身来协助战斗，而且她还能对元素进行一定的控制，比如召唤火球来进行攻击。关于玛蒂哈的战斗方式，她有什么可以教你的吗？ 阿斯特莱娅长长地呼出一口气，她的鼻孔微微张开。回想起自己与玛蒂哈的那次交战，她那庞大的身躯仿佛也随之松弛了下来。那场战斗持续的时间太短了，我根本来不及了解太多事情，”她黯然地回答道，“我最清楚地记得她书房里的那个符文——当时整个世界似乎都在围绕着它运转，只是为了容纳它的存在。真是令人难以置信…………就好像那是理所当然的一样。愤怒的，而且，围绕它的整个物理规律都必须发生变化、进行调整，才能让它保持平衡。仅仅靠近它就会让我变得虚弱，而反过来，这种符文似乎也具有同样的效果。成长在我面前，它变得越来越强壮，也越来越容易发怒。 [atFH |阿斯特莱娅将酒壶举到嘴边，动作看起来像是要一饮而尽，但她在最后一刻犹豫了，又重新考虑了一下，最终还是分了几口喝完了剩下的酒。她猛地把酒壶重重放在柜台上，那撞击声在酒馆里回荡。“这该死的身体对酒的耐受力也太强了，”她咒骂道，“加斯！请再给我来一杯…… |阿斯特莱娅将双臂交叉在胸前，双手环抱住自己的身体。她就这样静静地站着，低着头，好一会儿都没有说话——最终，她开始轻轻摇晃身体，手指也重新调整了抱臂的姿势。她是在……拥抱自己吗？ ] 玛蒂哈施展了一个法术，战斗就此结束了，”她最终继续说道，“埃莱克西斯和我完全没有准备好与像玛蒂哈这样强大的对手在‘道路之间’展开战斗。那感觉就像整座建筑都活了过来，想要吞噬我们。我们被分开了，而我所能做的，就是拼命逃跑——尽可能跑得远远的。 [atFH |加斯最终走了过来，右手拿着一杯琥珀色麦芽酒，准备为阿斯特莱娅的杯子添酒。但她并没有把酒送到嘴边。 |阿斯特莱娅就坐在那里，路标石就放在她身后，她的尾巴保护性地缠绕在她的双腿上，而路标石顶端的火焰已经熄灭，只剩下微弱的余烬。 ]你大概也就只能从她那里得到这些信息了。

rows.original: Ask more about Matiha and her fortress within the Ways Between. If you and Berwyn are expected to storm the fortress, you’d like to be as informed as possible.
rows.translation: 了解更多关于玛蒂哈以及她位于“道路之间”的堡垒的信息吧。如果你和贝尔温真的要攻打那座堡垒，那么掌握尽可能多的情报当然是非常重要的。
rows.raw: "Ask more about Matiha and her fortress within the Ways Between. If you and Berwyn are expected to storm the fortress, you’d like to be as informed as possible."

rows.original: You’re ready. Astraea continues to stare at you, her eyes burning through you, trying to get you to flinch. Your resolve doesn’t crack, and, eventually, [atFH |she lifts her glass and chugs the remainder of her drink, downing it all in one breath. Once it’s gone, she slams the glass back down and wipes her mouth with the back of her arm. "Retrieve Berwyn," she instructs. "I’ll meet you at the Waystone." |she pulls herself to her feet, dusting off her pants. "Retrieve Berwyn," she instructs. "I’ll wait for you here." ] You do as she says[atFH | and you make your way upstairs while she leaves the tavern, heading towards the Waystone on the street | and make your way to the Frost Hound, leaving her by the Waystone on the street ]. Upstairs and down the hall, to the last door in the hallway. You knock twice and call out Berwyn’s name. After a moment, you hear the locks of the door slide out of place, and the door opens – and there is Berwyn, fully dressed, but with his eyebrows raised and his eyes watery and arched. His teeth bite gently into his lower lip, quivering as he nibbles into them. "I’m not ready," he admits. You promise him again that you’ll be with him for every step of the way, all the way up to Matiha. No matter what, you’re not going to let what happened to Astraea happened to him. "I know," he sighs, opening the door wider – to let you in, not to step out himself. "And I believe you when you say that. I trust you, [pc.name]." He walks back into his room – it’s cleaner than it was when Astraea first introduced herself. Before, his room was covered in papers, notes, and study and reference material; now, it’s practically spotless. He had taken to cleaning his room to try and keep his mind off encountering Matiha. "But let’s be real," he says sadly, his eyes looking up at you from underneath the wide brim of his hat. "Last time, I knew what we were up against. And now, two magehunters blessed by Nareva herself couldn’t beat Matiha. Teleporting towers; magic powerful enough to teleport a fortress into the Ways Between; and... whatever’s happened to Astraea?" You take a seat next to Berwyn. His eyes don’t follow you there; he brings both of his hands to his chin and he rests his elbows on his knees. He takes a long, deep sniffle through his nose before continuing. "This is scary," he continues. "This isn’t the same Matiha, I’ve convinced myself that it isn’t. She was always a little intense and pushy, but, like...." Berwyn doesn’t bother finishing the statement, and you don’t blame him. After all, he’s correct: you two are going up against something wholly different than when you first stormed Matiha’s tower. Berwyn was ready to stop Matiha, but now she’s someone, or something, else. "You heard what Astraea said earlier," he continues. "She can only describe the power that Matiha has as 'godlike.’ I’m not 'godlike.’ I can’t compete with something like that. And in the Ways Between, where up is down and black is white? And," he continues, turning to face you, his nostrils flaring and his brow furrowing in thought, "what am I supposed to 'convince’ Matiha of, anyway? For her to stop using her untold, godlike power? That she’s been a bad girl and it’s time to put away her toys? Do you really think a woman with that sort of power is going to listen to me?" You wrap your arm around Berwyn’s shoulders, hugging him closer to you to try and calm him down. He’s shivering underneath his robe; you get a better look at his fingers, and both of his hands are shaking from the fright. You ask Berwyn if he’d rather not do it. If he’d rather stay here, locked in his room in the Frost Hound, and wait for whatever’s happening with Matiha to blow over. You two could send Astraea on her way; she’ll get back to the Order Astrida; and they’ll send more agents into the Ways Between to deal with the issue themselves. "That’s a bullshit, leading, non-question and you know it," he spits, whacking you in the leg with his left hand. "Matiha’s only going to get stronger the longer we wait. Eventually, no magic cult in the world is going to be able to stop her – not you or me, not the Order, and maybe not Nareva herself. This isn’t a matter of what I want. We have to do it because it needs to be done." Berwyn sighs as his head falls to its left, resting on your shoulder. His mage’s hat falls off his head and onto the bed behind him. rows.translation: 你准备好了。 阿斯特莱娅依然凝视着你，她那炽热的眼神仿佛要穿透你的身体，试图让你退缩。但你的决心丝毫没有动摇，最终， [atFH |她举起杯子，一饮而尽剩余的饮料。喝完后，她猛地把杯子放下，用胳膊肘擦了擦嘴，然后命令道：“去把贝尔温带回来，我在路标处等你。 |她站起身来，拍掉裤子上的灰尘。“去把贝尔温找回来，”她命令道，“我在这里等你。 ] 照她说的做吧。[atFH | 你上楼去了，而她则离开了酒馆，朝着街上的路标走去。 | 然后前往霜冻猎犬那里，把它留在街道上的路标旁。 ]沿着走廊，一直走到尽头的那一扇门。你敲了两下门，然后呼喊着贝尔温的名字。 过了一会儿，你听到门锁被拨开的声响，门缓缓打开了——站在门口的是贝尔温，他已经穿好了衣服，不过他的眉毛紧皱着，眼睛也湿润且微微睁大着。他的牙齿轻轻咬住下唇，一边啃咬一边微微颤抖。 “我还没准备好，”他承认道。 你再次向他保证，会陪伴他走过每一阶段，直到抵达玛蒂哈。无论如何，你都不会让发生在阿斯特莱娅身上的事情也发生在他身上。 “我知道，”他叹息着，把门开得更大一些——是为了让你进来，而不是他自己要出去。“我相信你说的那些话。我信任你。 [pc.name]他走回自己的房间——这里比阿斯特莱娅第一次来的时候还要整洁。之前，他的房间里堆满了文件、笔记以及各种学习资料；而现在，房间里几乎一尘不染。他开始经常打扫房间，只是为了让自己不要总是想着玛蒂哈。 但说实话，”他悲伤地说道，帽子宽大的帽檐遮住了他的眼睛，目光从帽檐下望向你，“上次，我知道我们将会面临什么。而现在，两位受到娜瑞瓦亲自庇佑的法师猎手，竟然也无法击败玛蒂哈。传送塔；那种强大到足以将整座堡垒传送到“幽界”中的魔法；还有……阿斯特莱娅到底发生了什么？ 你坐在贝尔温旁边。他的目光并没有跟随你坐下；他双手托着下巴，将肘部放在膝盖上。他深深地吸了一口气，然后继续说道：“这太可怕了……这个玛蒂哈已经不是以前的她了，我一直在说服自己这一点。她以前确实有点强势、有点固执，但是…… 贝尔温没有继续把话说完，你也不会责怪他。毕竟他说得对：这一次，你们所要面对的，与当初冲进玛蒂哈的塔楼时完全不同。当时贝尔温已经做好了阻止玛蒂哈的准备，但如今，玛蒂哈已经变成了另一个人……或者说，是某种完全不同的存在。东西你们都听到了阿斯特莱娅之前的话，”他继续说道，“她只能将玛蒂哈所拥有的力量形容为‘神一般的’。但我并不是‘神一般的’，我根本无法与那样的力量相抗衡。而在那些‘虚无之地’里，哪里是上哪里是下，哪里是黑哪里是白呢？而且，”他转向你，鼻孔张开，眉头紧锁地思考着，“我究竟应该怎样‘说服’玛蒂哈呢？让她停止利用她那无穷的力量吗？还是因为她一直是个调皮的女孩，现在该把她那些‘玩具’收起来了？你真觉得一个拥有那种力量的女人会听我的话吗？” 你将手臂搭在贝尔温的肩上，把他拉得更靠近自己，试图让他平静下来。他裹着长袍在发抖；仔细看的话，会发现他的双手都在因为恐惧而颤抖。 你问贝林是否愿意放弃这个计划。是否愿意留在“寒霜猎犬”号上的房间里，等待玛蒂哈那边的事情平息下来。你们两个可以把阿斯特莱娅送走吧，她会回到阿斯特丽达组织，而他们会再派遣更多的特工进入那些神秘通道，亲自处理这个问题。 “这完全是一派胡言，根本不是在提问，你心里明白的，”他一边说着，一边用左手拍打你的腿。我们拖延的时间越长，玛蒂哈就会变得越强。最终，世界上没有任何魔法教派能够阻止她——无论是你、我，还是那个组织，甚至可能连娜瑞瓦本人也无能为力。这件事根本不是我该来决定的想要。我们必须这么做，因为这件事确实必须完成。” 贝尔温叹了口气，头微微偏向左侧，靠在你的肩上。他的法师帽从头上滑落，掉在了身后的床上。“我只是……”他说道，话语在口中显得有些支支吾吾，“你知道的，我也有权利感到害怕。” 你轻轻揉了揉他的肩膀。你当然明白。

rows.original:
A short walk later, and you and Berwyn at the Waystone at the center of town. Like she had promised, Astraea stands at the rock to meet you; her cloak hangs off her body and shrouds her face, but there’s no mistaking a body with that shape or size.
        
        She waits until you and Berwyn are standing squarely in front of her before she so much as acknowledges your presence. She looks [pc.heightRange 0 92 100
            |down 
            |
            |up 
        ]at you, then at Berwyn – a powerful magician in his own right, surely, but compared to an Astrida paladin? And with his stature?
        
        Her eyes have sunken into her own cheeks from her frown and although the usual fire that the salamanders are known for is still there, all of the fight’s been drained from them. [pc.isDK
            |She doesn’t think you can win and she’s not willing to admit it.
            |She doesn’t need to tell you what she’s thinking – her body says it all. Your chances aren’t great.
        ]
        
        She turns away from you and takes a deep breath through her nose as she reaches into her cloak for something. "You’ve traveled the Ways Between before, I take it," she asks, and you confirm. Her hand pulls out of her cloak, and wrapped around her fingers is the Waystone Charm she had shown you back in Berwyn’s room. "Use this one instead. It’s attuned to Matiha’s fortress; it will take you straight there and straight back once you’re done."
        
        You accept the charm, keeping the strap wrapped around your own fingers for the moment.
        
        "Um," Berwyn starts; his hands are clasped behind his back and while his eyes are lifted towards Astraea’s, he isn’t meeting her eyes. "Astraea, I have a question. About... combat. Going to combat."
        
        She stands, her own gaze down towards him – and you think she isn’t looking into his eyes, either. She patiently waits for him to ask his question.
        
        "How do you... get ready for it?" he asks.
        
        Astraea’s hands hang loose and open at her sides; her cloak swishes in the wind and ruffles her cowl, flapping over her eyes. She stands like a guardian to the Waystone, her muscles bursting with strength and her body clad in thick layers of leather armor, and yet, she’s sending in Berwyn, standing at roughly half her height and wearing little more than his usual robes. It’s a vague question, but all three of you know exactly what he means when he asks it.
        
        "I think about the victory," she answers eventually. "What it would mean to succeed."
        
        Berwyn fidgets on his feet, his head turning slightly to one side and cocking his ear for more information. "Anything else?" he asks.
        
        "No," she replies. "Don’t think about anything else. Focus on your victory and the future you want for yourself and your loved ones."
        
        He sighs through his nose and his lips curl inward. He’s clearly unsatisfied with the answer. Yet Astraea offers nothing more, and from the way she fights to keep her shoulders square, she has nothing more to offer.
        
        "The longer you wait," Astraea continues, turning her gaze to you instead, "the worse your odds become. The Ways Between is a volatile, intense place, and if I’m correct, Matiha and her rune are growing stronger with each moment that passes."
        
        She steps aside, giving you access to the Waystone. There’s nothing more to say: all that’s left is for you to step forward and press the charm against the rock, and you’ll be sent to Matiha’s fortress.
        
        You hear Berwyn take a long, deep sigh beside you – and then his fingers worm and hook between your own, interlocking yours to his. You give his hand a squeeze, letting you know that you have his back and that you’re with him every step of the way, and he squeezes back.
        
        You two take four steps forward, and, once you’re squarely in front of the Waystone, you lift the charm Astraea had given you to it. The air crackles and fizzles around you both as the Waystone reacts to your charm; then, with another step forward, the very air around you turns black.
        
        Berwyn squeezes your hand again.
rows.translation:
走了一会儿后，你和贝尔温便来到了镇中心的路标处。正如她所承诺的那样，阿斯特莱娅站在那块岩石旁等待着你们；她的斗篷披在身上，遮住了她的面容，但凭借那身形和体型，根本不可能认错她就是那个人。
        
        她一直等到你和贝尔温站在她面前，才终于注意到了你们的存在。她看着你们[pc.heightRange 0 92 100
            |下降 
            |
            |向上 
        ]首先是对你，然后是贝尔温——他本身当然也是一位强大的法师，但与阿斯特里达的圣骑士相比呢？再加上他的地位……
        
        她的眉头紧锁，双眼都深深地陷进了脸颊里。虽然她身上依然带着那些火蜥蜴特有的炽热气息，但所有的斗志都已经消散了。 [pc.isDK
            |她认为你不可能赢，而且她也不愿意承认这一点。
            |她根本不需要用言语来表达自己的想法，她的动作就已经说明了一切。你的机会其实并不大。
        ]
        
        她转过身去，通过鼻子深吸一口气，然后从斗篷里掏出什么东西。“我想你之前曾经走过这些通道吧？”她问道，你确认道确实如此。她的手从斗篷中抽出，手指上握着的就是在贝尔温的房间里给你看过的那块通道魔法石。“用这个吧。它与玛蒂哈的堡垒相连接，使用它之后，你就能直接到达那里，完成任务后再直接回来。
        
        你接受了这份魅力，暂时将那条带子缠在自己的手指上。
        
        “嗯，”贝尔温开口说道；他双手背在身后，虽然他的目光正投向阿斯特莱娅，但却没有与她对视。“阿斯特莱娅，我有个问题。关于……战斗。关于即将到来的战斗。
        
        她站立着，目光低垂地望着他——你也会以为她并没有直视他的眼睛。她耐心地等待着他提出那个问题。
        
        “你……是怎么准备迎接这一刻的？”他问道。
        
        阿斯特莱娅的双手自然地垂在身侧；她的斗篷在风中飘动，帽兜也随之翻动，遮住了她的双眼。她像一位守护者般站在路标旁，肌肉充满力量，全身披着厚厚的皮甲。然而，她却派上了贝林——一个身高只有她一半左右、身上只穿着平常长袍的人去执行任务。这个问题有点模糊，但你们三个人都清楚地知道他问这个问题的真正含义。
        
        我会思考胜利的意义，”她最终说道，“以及取得成功会带来什么。”
        
        贝林坐立不安，微微侧头，倾听着她想继续说的内容。“还有别的吗？”他问道。
        
        “没有，”她回答，“别想其他任何事情。只需专注于你的胜利，以及你为自己和所爱的人所期望的未来。
        
        他通过鼻子叹了口气，嘴唇微微撇向内侧，显然对这个答案并不满意。然而，阿斯特莱娅再也无法提供更多的信息了，从她努力保持镇定的样子来看，她也确实无能为力。
        
        “你等待的时间越长，”阿斯特莱娅继续说道，她的目光此刻转向了你，“你的机会就会变得越渺茫。界间之路是一个充满变数、危险重重的地方，如果我的判断没错的话，玛蒂哈和她的符文正在每一刻变得越来越强大。
        
        她退到一旁，为你打开了通往道路之石的道路。再没有什么需要说的了：你现在只需上前，将那枚符文石放在岩石上，就能被传送到玛蒂哈的堡垒中。
        
        你听到贝尔温在你身旁深深地叹了口气——随后他的手指轻轻缠绕在你的手指上，与你的手指紧紧相握。你紧紧握住他的手，向他表明你会支持他，会与他同行到底；他也同样紧紧回握着你的手。
        
        你们两人向前走四步，当你们正好站在路标面前时，将阿斯特莱娅给你的那件饰品举起来。路标对这件饰品产生了反应，周围的空气开始发出噼啪声和嘶嘶声；接着，再向前走一步，你们周围的空气竟然变成了黑色。
        
        贝尔温再次握住了你的手。

        You hear Berwyn take a long, deep sigh beside you – and then his fingers worm and hook between your own, interlocking yours to his. You give his hand a squeeze, letting you know that you have his back and that you’re with him every step of the way, and he squeezes back.
        
        You two take four steps forward, and, once you’re squarely in front of the Waystone, you lift the charm Astraea had given you to it. The air crackles and fizzles around you both as the Waystone reacts to your charm; then, with another step forward, the very air around you turns black.
        
        Berwyn squeezes your hand again.'

rows.original: You hear footsteps reverberating from an adjacent room, but you can’t make out where. Something very large is very close by.
rows.translation: 你听到隔壁房间里有脚步声传来，但却无法确定具体位置。有什么非常大的东西就在附近。
rows.raw: "\n You hear footsteps reverberating from an adjacent room, but you can’t make out where. Something very large is very close by."

rows.original: You approach a set of stairs [var0 |heading upward, into the spiral of the tower – and towards its peak, where Matiha probably is. That’s where she was last time. |heading down, deeper into the bowels of the fortress[flags.BERWYN_TOWER_FOUND_LAB |; last time you went down there, you had found some decent weapons, and Berwyn managed to enchant one of them with the tools available. Perhaps you’ll get lucky a second time. | – was that there before? You aren’t certain; last time you were here, you ran straight through the fort to the tower and didn’t bother to take in your surroundings. Well, whatever. ] ] Once you put one foot in front of the other, the bricks of the fortress shimmer and rattle against each other. The pulsating green veins coursing between them become more vibrant and intense – and, without warning, they break apart from each other, lifting into the air and swirling around you in a tempest of baked clay and magically-charged sand and caulk. Bricks whiz past your head and they flow like water between you and Berwyn. They rip apart the fortress, brick by brick, one at a time, causing flakes of their dust to fling from their surface and add to the cyclone swirling around you. By the time the whirling storm of brick begins to encroach on your standing position, they begin to calm, settling back down in uniform locations around the foundation of the fortress. The grating noise of brick sliding against brick echoes into a loud, unsettling cacophony; the spaces between them are filled with their caulking once more, and the spaces between that are filled with whatever grains of dust are available, until... it all stops. Berwyn is still with you; after quickly checking yourself for any injuries, you ask him if he’s alright. "Y-yeah, I think so," he says with a shaky voice, his hands running over his chest and stomach for any bruises. "They all missed, I think." You take a moment to assess what had just happened. You look around the room you’re in – and you quickly realize that you don’t recognize it. You’re in a small, mostly-featureless room with doors to your east and south (or, at least, the directions you assume to be east and south); the east door appears to lead to a staircase[var0|, just as you were heading towards]. You and Berwyn come to the same realization with a start: the fortress can change. The very layout of the building can transform on a whim. You’ll never know where you’re going; you’ll have no idea where you came from; and, you’re sure, if the fortress wanted to, it could quite literally spit you back out, into the courtyard at the entrance. You ask if this is more of Matiha’s doing. "Probably," he answers, then recants. "Maybe? I mean... she has the strength to teleport the whole damn thing into a dimension in between realities. Changing the shape of the building sounds like it’d be pretty easy in comparison." He kneels down and runs his fingers across the stone on the floor, tracing the green veins interlocking the bricks with each other. "But... it’d take a lot of concentration. That’s a lot of small moving parts, and every single one of them missed us both. It could be done, especially with the kind of power Matiha may have, but...." He turns his hand over, inspecting his fingers. They’re clean as could be. "It’d be easier if... the fortress just did that by itself." Is he suggesting that the fortress has a thought process? That it consciously did what it just did? [var1|That reminds you of the kitsune den in the Frostwood – that building sealed itself shut behind you once you entered.] "The way I see it, there are three possibilities," he continues, standing up and patting down his knees. "Either Matiha just did all of that by herself; the Ways Between did that without any input from Matiha; or some combination of the two." You ask him which of the three possibilities would be the worst for you two. "The third one," he answers immediately, his eyes locking onto yours, "because it means that Matiha is somehow communicating with the Ways Between." Perfect. One more thing to worry about. There’s a door to your east, with a spiral staircase leading upward just beyond its arches, with green veins pumping along the central pillar. To the south is a dark hallway, lit slightly by the ambient light of the glowing veins, but not well enough that you can see where it leads.
rows.translation: 你走向一段楼梯。 [var0 |不断向上攀升，穿过塔楼的螺旋通道——朝着它的顶峰前进，而玛蒂哈很可能就在那里。她上次就是在那里的。 |不断向下深入，越往要塞的内部走去[flags.BERWYN_TOWER_FOUND_LAB |上次你去那里的时候，确实找到了一些不错的武器，而贝尔温也利用手头的工具成功为其中一把武器施加了魔法效果。也许这次你也会运气好的。 | – 那东西之前就在那里吗？你也不确定吧；上次你来的时候，直接跑过了整个堡垒，径直走向了塔楼，根本没留意周围的环境。算了，不管了。 ] ] 当你迈出第一步时，堡垒的砖块开始闪烁并相互碰撞发出声响。那些在砖块之间流淌的绿色脉络变得更加鲜艳、更加剧烈——然后，毫无征兆地，这些砖块开始分离，升入空中，在你周围旋转，形成一场由烧制的黏土、充满魔力的沙子以及黏合剂构成的狂暴风暴。 砖块从你头顶飞过，它们像流水一样从你和贝尔温之间穿梭而过。一块一块地，这些砖块逐渐摧毁了那座堡垒，它们的碎片不断从表面脱落，加入到你周围旋转的尘土旋风之中。 当那些旋转着的砖块开始逼近你的站立位置时，它们会逐渐平静下来，重新均匀地分布在堡垒的基座周围。砖块相互摩擦时发出的刺耳声响成一片嘈杂而令人不安的噪音；那些缝隙中再次被填满了填缝材料，那些砖块之间的空隙也被所有能够找到的灰尘填满，直到……一切停止为止。 贝林仍然在你身边；在快速检查自己是否受伤后，你问他是否没事。“嗯……应该没事吧，”他声音颤抖着说道，同时用手抚摸着自己的胸部和腹部，检查是否有淤伤。我想，他们全都错过了。” 你花了一点时间来思考刚刚发生的事情。你环顾自己所在的房间，很快意识到你并不认识这个地方。你身处一个面积很小、几乎没有任何装饰的房间里，房间东侧和南侧各有一扇门（至少你认为是东侧和南侧）；那扇东侧的门似乎通向一段楼梯。[var0|就在你即将到达那里的时候……]你和贝尔温在开始的时候就得出了同样的结论：这座堡垒是可以被攻破的。改变。这座建筑的结构本身就可以随时发生变化。你永远无法预知自己将会走到哪里，也不会知道自己是从哪里来的；而且，可以肯定的是，如果这座堡垒愿意的话，它完全可以把你重新抛回到入口处的庭院里。 你问他，这是否更像是玛蒂哈的所作所为。他回答说：“大概吧”，但随后又改口道：“也许吧？我的意思是……她拥有将整个建筑传送到介于现实与虚幻之间的维度中的能力。相比之下，改变建筑的结构应该算是相当简单的事情吧。他跪了下来，用手指轻轻触摸地面上的石头，仔细观察那些将砖块紧密连接在一起的绿色纹理。“但是……这需要极高的专注力。其中有太多细小的活动部件了，而每一个部件都可能让我们错过关键线索。它可以这事儿本来应该很容易办到的，尤其是考虑到玛蒂哈所拥有的那种力量……但是……” 他转过手，仔细检查着自己的手指，它们干净得一尘不染。“要是那座堡垒能自己完成这件事该多好啊……” 他是在暗示那座堡垒具有思考能力吗？难道它真的有意识地做了它刚才所做的那件事？ [var1|这让你想起了冰原森林里的那只狐妖巢穴——每次你走进去，那栋建筑都会自动关闭门扉。] 在我看来，有三种可能性，”他站起身来，拍了拍膝盖继续说道，“要么是玛蒂哈独自完成了所有这些事情；要么是‘道路之间’的组织在没有任何玛蒂哈参与的情况下做了这些事；又或者这两种情况结合在了一起。” 你问他，这三种可能性中哪一种对你们两个人来说最为糟糕。 “第三种，”他立刻回答道，目光紧紧地盯着你，“因为这意味着玛蒂哈在某种程度上进行沟通还有那些隐藏在暗处的通道……” 太好了，又多了一件需要担心的事情。 你的东侧有一扇门，门拱之后有一条螺旋楼梯向上延伸，中央的柱子上布满了绿色的脉络。南侧是一条昏暗的走廊，仅有那些绿色脉络散发出的微弱光线照亮着那里，但光线实在太弱了，根本看不清走廊的尽头通向哪里。

rows.original:
You[party.hasCompanions
        |r party
    ] enters a smaller room: one with a shallower ceiling and without anything dressing the walls. It’s a plain, uninteresting, featureless place, probably explicitly meant to be a conjunction between other, more important rooms.
    
    Except... despite its utter lack of any defining features and anything interesting about it, you can still distinctly remember it. This is the room you had started in!
    
    [var0
        |Berwyn chews at his lower lip as he realizes that you’ve entered the same room for the third time. His nose scrunches and his eyes widen as his brow furrows – he’s starting to get frustrated at your lack of progress.
        
        "Alright," he grunts throatily. "Let’s try again."
        |Berwyn, for his part, seems relatively unfazed by the realization that you’ve just gone in a larger circle. His hand is at his chin, cupping it between his index finger and his thumb, and he stares at the floor as he processes what had just happened.
    
        "This may be a good thing," he says, chewing through his words as he tries to process them himself. "It means that, despite what we’re seeing and what we’ve done so far, there’s consistency to whatever’s happening in this fortress." His face stays down, but his eyes lift to yours. "Which means there’s an ending to this maze. We just need to find it."
    ]
    
    There isn’t a lot inside this room to give you any hints as to where you should go. The only really 'defining’ feature inside it are the green veins within the bricks, pumping... whatever it is they’re pumping, all in one direction: towards the spiral staircase just outside the east door.
     
    There’s a door to your east, with a spiral staircase leading upward just beyond its arches, with green veins pumping along the central pillar. To the south is a dark hallway, lit slightly by the ambient light of the glowing veins, but not well enough that you can see where it leads.
rows.translation:
你[party.hasCompanions
        |派对
    ]进入了一个较小的房间：这里的天花板较低，墙壁上也没有任何装饰。这是一个简单、毫无趣味、没有任何特色的地方，显然只是作为其他更重要房间的连接通道而存在的。
    
    然而……尽管这个房间完全没有任何明显的特征或值得注意的地方，你仍然能够清楚地记得它。因为这就是你开始这段旅程的地方啊！
    
    [var0
        |当贝尔温意识到你已经第三次进入同一个房间时，他开始咬自己的下唇。他的鼻子皱了起来，眼睛也睁得更大，眉头紧锁——对你毫无进展的表现，他开始感到恼火了。
        
        “好吧，”他低声咕哝道，“我们再试一次吧。
        |对于贝尔温来说，似乎并没有因为意识到你刚刚绕了一个更大的圈子而感到困扰。他把手放在下巴上，用食指和拇指托着下巴，低头凝视着地面，试图消化刚刚发生的事情。
    
        这也许是一件好事，”他边说边咀嚼着话语，试图自己理清这些想法。“这意味着，尽管我们目前所看到的一切以及我们所采取的行动都让人感到困惑，但这座堡垒里发生的一切其实存在着某种一致性。他的头低着，但眼睛却抬了起来，与你对视。这意味着这个迷宫终究有尽头，我们只需要找到它而已。
    ]
    
    这个房间里没有什么能给你提供关于该往哪里去的线索。里面唯一真正“具有指示性”的特征，就是那些砖块中的绿色脉络——它们正在不断地输送着某种物质，而且所有这些输送都是朝着同一个方向进行的：通往东门外的螺旋楼梯。
     
    你的东侧有一扇门，门拱之后是一条螺旋状的楼梯，楼梯向上延伸；中央的柱子上布满了绿色的脉络。南侧是一条昏暗的走廊，仅有那些绿色脉络散发出的微弱光线为走廊照亮，但光线实在太弱了，根本看不清走廊通向哪里。

rows.original:
You climb the spiral staircase, heading up to the next floor of the fortress. You hear the sound of brick shifting and moving as you climb; the room ahead is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled.
    
    The room at the top of the staircase is comparatively decently furnished: a plush rug, looking almost new, sits beneath a desk that’s little more than a stone slab sitting on top of a pile of bricks. There’s a wooden chair at the desk, facing northward – but it’s sitting on top of the table rather than next to it, making both it and the table useless. [var0
        |The chair’s been fastened tightly to the table, making it impossible to move.
        |Inquisitively, you try to move the chair, and you find it fastened to the table for good.
    ]
    
    To the north is a hole in the wall, probably meant for a door, but there’s no door to be found; the green veins within the brick curl around the frame of the opening, but they dissipate shortly after, casting the room beyond in darkness. To your east is a proper wooden door: the door and the frame it’s in look fairly well-kept and without any dust. To your south is a spiral staircase that leads down somewhere; you can’t see beyond the first bend and you have no idea what’s down there.
rows.translation:
你沿着螺旋楼梯向上攀登，前往堡垒的上一层。在攀爬的过程中，你能听到砖块被移动、重新排列的声音——当你逐渐接近前方那个房间时，那里正在被建造中；而你刚刚离开的房间，则已经被拆除了。
    
    楼梯顶层的那个房间陈设还算不错：一张看起来几乎崭新的柔软地毯铺在一张由几块砖堆起来的简易书桌下。书桌旁有一把木椅，椅子是朝北方向的——但它被放在书桌上面，而不是放在书桌旁边，因此这把椅子和书桌都派不上用场。 [var0
        |这把椅子被牢牢地固定在桌子上，根本动弹不得。
        |出于好奇，你试着移动那把椅子，却发现它已经被牢牢地固定在桌子上，无法移动了。
    ]
    
    在北侧，墙上有一个洞，原本应该是用来安装门的，但实际上那里并没有门；砖块中的绿色条纹环绕着那个洞的框架，但很快便消失了，使得洞后面的房间陷入黑暗之中。在东侧，有一扇真正的木门——这扇门及其门框看起来保养得相当好，上面没有一点灰尘。而在南侧，有一段螺旋楼梯，它向下延伸着；你无法看到第一个转角之后的情况，也不知道下面究竟有什么。

rows.original:
You traverse down the dark hallway; the light of the green veins doesn’t reach any further than the frame of the door you just entered. You hear the sound of brick shifting and scraping against each other as you go; the room ahead is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled.
     
    The dark hallway eventually opens to the open air: you’re standing on the wall of the fortress, with the spire of the tower to your east and the courtyard with the overgrown vines to your west. Whatever passes for 'wind’ billows in your elevated spot, ruffling your clothes and swishing Berwyn’s long hair behind himself.
     
    Directly ahead of you, pointed north, the wall leads back into the fortress proper via a door at the top of a much smaller tower, built primarily as a method of access rather than anything strategic. To your east is the main tower of the building, overlooking everything around it; a thick pair of stone doors sit just ajar enough to let light through, and there’s no visible locking mechanism keeping you from just opening them. To your south, a dark corridor leads you deeper into the base of the fortress.
rows.translation:
你沿着昏暗的走廊前行，那些绿色的条纹所散发出的光线，最多也只能照亮你刚刚进入的那扇门的框架而已。在前进的过程中，你能听到砖块相互移动、相互摩擦发出的声响——当你逐渐接近前方的房间时，那个房间正在被建造中；而你刚刚离开的那个房间，则已经被拆除了。
     
    暗影的走廊最终通向了户外：你站在堡垒的墙边，东边是高塔的尖顶，西边则是长满藤蔓的庭院。某种可以称之为“风”的东西在你所处的这个高处吹拂着，弄得你的衣服飘动，也使贝尔温的长发在身后飘扬起来。
     
    就在你正前方，朝北方向延伸的墙壁通过一座位于较小塔楼顶部的门，通向堡垒的主体部分。这座塔楼主要是为了提供通道而建造的，并没有什么战略意义。在你的东侧，是这座建筑的主塔，它能够俯瞰周围的一切；一对厚重的石门只是微微敞开，足以让光线透进来，而且也没有任何可见的锁具装置，因此你可以随时将它们打开。在你的南方，一条暗影的走廊将带你深入堡垒的内部。
rows.raw:
"
    You traverse down the dark hallway; the light of the green veins doesn’t reach any further than the frame of the door you just entered. You hear the sound of brick shifting and scraping against each other as you go; the room ahead is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled.
     
    The dark hallway eventually opens to the open air: you’re standing on the wall of the fortress, with the spire of the tower to your east and the courtyard with the overgrown vines to your west. Whatever passes for 'wind’ billows in your elevated spot, ruffling your clothes and swishing Berwyn’s long hair behind himself.
     
    Directly ahead of you, pointed north, the wall leads back into the fortress proper via a door at the top of a much smaller tower, built primarily as a method of access rather than anything strategic. To your east is the main tower of the building, overlooking everything around it; a thick pair of stone doors sit just ajar enough to let light through, and there’s no visible locking mechanism keeping you from just opening them. To your south, a dark corridor leads you deeper into the base of the fortress.
    "

rows.original:
With a hearty push, the stone doors leading into the base of the tallest tower swing open – and once you’re inside the room, they shut by themselves behind you. You hear the sound of brick whirling through the air and slamming into each other as they build the rooms around you and dismantle the overlook you were just on... and the spare caulking is used to seal the stone doors behind you, preventing you from heading back.
     
    You’re standing in some kind of foyer: a thick, circular mat greets your tired feet, spread underneath a number of simpler furnishings, including a bookcase in the corner, as well as a table and some chairs for a person to sit and read. And the chairs are sitting on the floor, this time. A single lit candle bearing a purple flame hangs from the center of the room, providing some unique violet lighting.
     
    To the north is an opening without a door – and across its opening is a thick stone bar, about halfway up the opening and going all the way across. If you were to go in that direction, you’d be forced to crouch underneath it. The opening leads into a dark corridor; it bends after only a few feet deep, and you can’t see where it leads.
     
    To your south is a similar opening, but long, thick vines drape over its door, preventing you from seeing what’s behind it. The vines have a number of blue-and-white flowers pulsating with green veins, just like you had seen in the courtyard. The vines don’t truly obstruct your path forward and could be brushed aside easily.
     
    To your west are the stone doors you had just entered from... but they’ve sealed themselves shut and they can’t be opened again. Green veins permeate the bricks of the room, flowing in every direction, and they head in roughly equal numbers down the north and south exits.
rows.translation:
你用力一推，通往最高塔底部的石门应声而开——一旦你走进房间，门就会自动关上。你听到砖块在空气中旋转、相互碰撞的声音，它们正在构建你周围的墙壁，同时摧毁你刚才所处的观景平台……剩下的密封材料被用来封闭你身后的石门，从而阻止你再次返回。
     
    你此刻站在一个类似门厅的地方：一块厚厚的圆形地毯铺在地面上，为你的疲惫的双脚提供了舒适的支撑。房间内摆放着一些简单的家具，角落里有一个书架，还有一张桌子和几把椅子，可以让人坐下来阅读。这一次，椅子被直接放在了地板上。房间中央挂着一支点燃的蜡烛，紫色的火焰为整个空间增添了一抹独特的氛围。
     
    北边有一个没有门的开口，而在那个开口处横着一根粗石棒，石棒大约位于开口的中部位置，并且一直延伸到另一侧。如果你想要从那个方向进入，就必须弯腰从它下面穿过。这个开口通向一条暗影的走廊；走廊在深入几英尺后就会转弯，因此你无法看到它通向哪里。
     
    在你南边，也有一个类似的入口，但是那里有长长的、茂密的藤蔓垂挂在门口，遮挡住了你视线，让你无法看到入口后面的情况。这些藤蔓上开着一朵朵蓝白相间的花朵，花朵的脉络呈现出绿色的颜色，与你之前在庭院里看到的那些藤蔓一模一样。不过，这些藤蔓其实并没有真正阻碍你前行的道路，你可以很容易地将它们拨到一边。
     
    在你的西边，有你们刚刚进入的那些石门……但它们已经自动关闭，再也无法被打开了。房间的砖块中布满了绿色的脉络，这些脉络向四面八方延伸，其中流向南北两侧出口的脉络数量大致相等。

rows.original:
The vines give way easily with the brush of your hand, showing you into a larger room than the others so far. As you step into the room, you hear the sound of bricks sliding against each other; the rooms ahead of you are being built as you approach, and the room behind you has been dismantled.
     
    The room in front of you appears to be some kind of mess room: the room that the soldiers of the fort would come to eat their food. Long wooden tables go in lines down the east and west sides of the room, extending nearly from wall to wall, and in the center is some kind of cooking area: a brick oven sits behind a semicircle stone counter, and pots, pans, and assorted plates and cutlery line the entire area. The wall behind the stove is stained black from the smoke of constant and consistent use.
     
    Behind the cooking area, to the south, are two sets of stairs, leading up to an awning that has another exit leading onward. The stairs appear to be worn smooth from thousands of heavy feet stepping up and down them. To your east is a single stone door, left slightly ajar; there’s a single, large etching along the upper half of the door, although you can’t decipher its meaning. To the west is a trapdoor built into the floor; its hatch is open, and there’s a ladder poking its top rung over the edge of the hole, inviting you downward. To the north is a dark corridor; it’s not so very long and you can see to its end, but your vision of the other side is obstructed by something.
rows.translation:
这些藤蔓在你轻轻一触之下便轻易地让开了道路，将你引入了一个比之前遇到的房间都要大的空间。当你走进这个房间时，你听到了砖块相互摩擦发出的声响——在你接近的过程中，前方的房间正在被建造中，而你身后的房间则已经被拆除了。
     
    你面前的这个房间看起来像是一间食堂：堡垒里的士兵们都会来这里吃饭。房间的东西两侧排列着长长的木制餐桌，几乎贯穿了整个房间；中间则设有烹饪区——一个砖砌的烤炉位于半圆形的石制操作台后面，锅碗瓢盆以及各式各样的盘子和餐具摆满了整个区域。由于长期不间断地使用，炉子后面的墙壁已经被烟熏得变成了黑色。
     
    在烹饪区南侧，有两组楼梯，它们通向一个遮阳篷，而那个遮阳篷还有另一条出口可以继续前行。这些楼梯显然因为成千上万的人次上下踩踏而变得十分光滑。在你的东侧，有一扇石门，门微微敞开着；门的上半部分刻有一条很大的花纹，不过你无法辨认出它的含义。在西侧，地板上有一个活板门；它的盖子是打开的，有一段梯子的最上面一节伸出了洞口边缘，仿佛在邀请你向下走去。而在北侧，有一条昏暗的走廊；这条走廊并不长，你可以看到它的尽头，但另一边的景象被什么东西挡住了，无法看清楚。

rows.original: You climb the stairs and approach the door at their top. As usual, everything seems fairly mundane and uninteresting: despite the fact that the fortress can shapeshift around you to throw off your movement, there’s only so much gray, featureless brick you can tolerate before they start to get boring. Even if they have blinking green veins pulsating across them. [var0 |Your footfalls echo through the mostly-smooth walls of the fortress, providing you with rhythmic ambience – and you realize with a bit of a start that, once again, you don’t hear anything out of the ordinary. No brick-against-brick; no whooshing noises as the fortress unmakes and remakes itself around you. You turn to Berwyn, about to ask him if he hears anything, but his eyes are narrowed and his ears are perked: he’s way ahead of you. If that’s the case, the odds are decent that you’ve found your way back to the 'midway’ point of the fortress: you’ve found Berwyn’s and Matiha’s old sleeping quarters, and they’re just beyond that door. And, just as you had guessed, the door opens to reveal Berwyn’s and Matiha’s old sleeping quarters. Berwyn’s bed and living space sit to the left of the room, completely undisturbed from the last time you were here[var1|, down to you leaving his panty drawer ajar when you raided it]. And the same goes for Matiha’s half of the room: it’s clean and well-kept, almost hauntingly so, as if she hadn’t slept it in since the day you and Berwyn first confronted her. Berwyn is notably still and contemplative once he enters the room. Like last time, he’s probably dealing with a wave of emotions – nostalgia among them. He doesn’t have much to add now that you’re here. |However, as you approach the top of the stairs, you feel Berwyn tug at your [pc.upperGarments] to stop you in your tracks. "Hold on," he whispers; his giant, furry ears poking through the brim of his hat fidget and twist on his head, trying to lock onto something in particular. "Do you hear that?" You turn your heard to one side, cocking your right ear up to the air as you listen for whatever he’s referring to. [pc.cunningRange 0 50 |But you don’t hear anything – the fortress is as quiet as the dead. "Exactly," Berwyn whispers. "It’s not moving. We must be getting close to something." To Matiha? "We’re about to find out," he grimaces, trying to maintain a steely demeanor. |You listen for anything from the errant buzz of the magic flowing through the veins in the bricks to the sound of your breathing, but nothing stands out of the ordinary. That’s when you realize it: there’s nothing out of the ordinary. In a dimension where ordinary is a verboten thing. There’s no scraping of brick on brick; there’s no howling of the wind as the stones smash through them to reassemble somewhere. The fortress has stopped. "Yeah," Berwyn agrees, his steely eyes on you. "We must be getting close to something." To Matiha? You sort of doubt it.... "So do I," he frowns, his brow furrowing. "But there’s only one way to find out." ] You put your hands on the wooden door and, gathering your courage, you give it a gentle push, ready for whatever might be on the other side of it. You keep your hand on your [pc.weapon], and Berwyn stands tensely behind you, his hands ready to cast whatever incantation he needs as soon as he needs it. But what you see on the other side of the door isn’t Matiha – it’s her old sleeping quarters. Hers and Berwyn’s. At the sight of his old bed, and his old dresser, and his old living space, Berwyn’s posture immediately deflates; his arms sink to his sides and his eyebrows rise in surprise. He steps cautiously into the room as his eyes stay glued to his old effects and belongings; everything is as exactly as you two had left it[var1|, down to you leaving his panty drawer slightly ajar when you raided it]. He steps up to the edge of his bed and he places a hand gently on its cushions, feeling it sink underneath his touch. His eyes narrow and his stare goes off somewhere else, focusing on something a million miles away; as soon as his hand touches down on the mattress of his bed, all of the memories from his time with Matiha come rushing back to him, all at once. Berwyn stays like that for a moment. He breathes gently through his nose, and, eventually, his eyelids begin to sink; he almost looks as if he might fall asleep at any moment. "Matiha’s not far from here," he says eventually, taking a deep breath as he does. "This room’s almost totally undisturbed. She wouldn’t put herself too far away from it." You ask him if he knows just how close. "I don’t know," he answers. "But... close. We just need to keep it up." His eyes go back to you, the earlier resolve and steely indignation restored to his pupils. Some of the insecurity that he had before has vanished – not all of it, but enough to straighten his spine. "Let’s get going." ] To the north is the room’s exit, leading back to the stairwell you were on when you first entered; the stairs continue upward, climbing the tower of the fortress, although there’s no guarantee that that’ll be where they continue once you leave the room. [var0 |And to the south is the trapdoor, laid flush with the floor, leading deeper into the fortress proper. Berwyn has told you before that it didn’t exist before and he has no idea where it could lead. Who really knows: down could be up in this twisted building stuck in the Ways Between. |However... to the south is a trapdoor, laid flush with the floor. You don’t remember seeing that the last time you were in this room, but maybe you just missed it. You ask Berwyn if he recognizes it; he stands on his tip-toes and leans forward to get a better look at what you’re referring to. "Nnnnnno," he answers, his mouth curling. "I’ve lived in this room for at least a year, and I’ve never seen that there before." Well. Now it’s there. Who knows where it could lead? ]
rows.translation: 你爬上楼梯，走向顶端的那扇门。和往常一样，一切看起来都极其平凡、毫无趣味：尽管这座堡垒会不断改变形态来干扰你的行动，但那些灰色的、毫无特色的砖块实在让人看腻了——即使上面还有闪烁的绿色脉络在跳动，也改变不了这种乏味的感觉。 [var0 |你的脚步声在堡垒那几乎光滑的墙壁中回荡，营造出一种有节奏的氛围——但你突然意识到，这一次，依然没有任何异常的声音。没有砖块相互碰撞的声音，也没有堡垒在周围不断变形时产生的呼啸声。你转向贝尔温，正打算问他是否听到了什么，但他的眼睛紧闭着，耳朵也竖得高高的——他显然已经先你一步发现了什么。 如果真是这样，那么你很可能会发现自己已经回到了堡垒的“中间位置”：你找到了贝尔温和玛蒂哈曾经的寝室，而那个房间就在那扇门的后面。 正如你所猜测的，门打开后，你看到了贝尔温和玛蒂哈以前的卧室。贝尔温的床铺和生活区域位于房间的左侧，自你上次来这里之后，一切都保持着原来的样子，丝毫没有改变。[var1|其实，问题就在于你偷窥他的内裤抽屉时，没有把它关好。]玛蒂哈那一半的房间也是如此：干净整洁，甚至给人一种诡异的干净感，仿佛自从你和贝尔温第一次与她对质以来，她就再没在那里睡过觉。 贝尔温一走进房间，就显得格外安静且陷入沉思。和上次一样，他此刻正在面对着一连串复杂的情绪——其中当然包括怀旧之情。现在你已经在场了，他似乎也没有什么话要补充了。 |然而，当你即将走到楼梯的顶端时，你感觉到贝尔温在拉你的衣服。 [pc.upperGarments]等等，”他轻声说道；他那巨大的、毛茸茸的耳朵从帽子边缘探出来，在他的头上不停地转动，似乎在试图捕捉某个特定的声音。“你听到吗？” 你把耳朵转向一侧，右耳贴在耳边，仔细聆听他在说些什么。 [pc.cunningRange 0 50 |但是你什么声音也听不到——这座堡垒静得如同死一般。 “正是这样，”贝尔温低声说道，“它没有任何动静。我们肯定快要接近某个东西了。” 是接近玛蒂哈吗？ “我们马上就会知道答案了，”他皱着眉头说道，努力保持着冷静的表情。 |你试图分辨出任何细微的声音——无论是魔法在砖块中流动时产生的微弱震动，还是自己呼吸的声音，但没有任何一点显得与众不同。 就在这时，你突然意识到了：其实并没有什么特别的。没什么出自普通的。在一个普通事物都被禁止存在的维度里，没有砖块相互摩擦的声音，也没有风声在石头撞击后呼啸而过。这座堡垒，已经静止了。 “是啊，”贝尔温说道，他那钢铁般的眼神紧盯着你，“我们肯定快要接近某个真相了。” 接近玛蒂哈？你对此有些怀疑…… “我也有同样的疑问，”他皱着眉头说，“但只有一个办法才能弄清楚。 ] 你将双手放在木门上，鼓起勇气，轻轻推了一下，准备迎接门另一边可能出现的任何情况。你的手依然紧握在门上[pc.weapon]贝林紧张地站在你身后，随时准备在你需要的时候施展任何必要的法术。 但是，门另一边出现的并不是玛蒂哈——而是她以前的卧室。赫尔斯和贝尔温的。 一看到他那旧床、旧梳妆台以及那熟悉的居住环境，贝尔温整个人都垮了下来；他的双臂无力地垂在身体两侧，眉毛也因惊讶而微微上扬。他小心翼翼地走进房间，目光紧紧地盯着那些熟悉的物品和财物——一切都和你们离开时一模一样。[var1|其实，关键就在于你翻他的内裤抽屉时，把它留了一点缝隙。]他走到床边，轻轻地将手放在床垫上，感受到床垫在触碰下微微凹陷。他的眼睛微微眯起，目光仿佛投向了遥远的地方，专注于某个遥不可及的事物；而就在他的手接触到床铺的那一刻，他与玛蒂哈一起度过的所有回忆，突然全都涌回了他的脑海中。 贝尔温就这样呆了一会儿。他轻轻地通过鼻子呼吸，渐渐地，他的眼皮开始下垂；看起来他随时都可能睡着。 “玛蒂哈离这里不远，”他终于开口说道，同时深吸了一口气。这个房间几乎没有任何被翻动的痕迹。她肯定不会把自己放在离它太远的地方。” 你问他是否知道这一点。如何我不知道，”他回答道，“但……差不多了。我们只需要继续坚持下去就行。”他的目光再次转向你，眼中重新恢复了先前的坚定与愤怒。他之前所感到的那些不安已经消散了一些——虽然还没有完全消失，但已经足以让他挺直腰板。“我们走吧。 ] 北边是房间的出口，出口会通向你最初进入时所在的楼梯间；那些楼梯继续向上延伸，通向堡垒的塔楼，不过一旦你离开这个房间，就无法保证楼梯会继续通向那里。 [var0 |而在南边，有一扇与地面平齐的活板门，它通向堡垒的内部深处。贝林之前已经告诉过你们，这扇门之前并不存在，他也完全不知道它通向哪里。谁又能真正知道呢？在这座位于“通道之间”的扭曲建筑里，向下走可能反而会通往上方。 |然而……在房间的南侧有一扇暗门，它的位置与地面完全齐平。 你不记得上次进入这个房间时有没有注意到它，但也许你只是没有注意到而已。你询问贝尔温是否见过它；他踮起脚尖，向前倾身仔细查看你所指的地方。“没有，”他回答道，嘴角微微上扬，“我在这个房间里住了至少一年，可从来没见过那个东西。” 好吧，现在它确实就在那里。谁知道它会通向哪里呢？ ]
rows.raw: ' You climb the stairs and approach the door at their top. As usual, everything seems fairly mundane and uninteresting: despite the fact that the fortress can shapeshift around you to throw off your movement, there’s only so much gray, featureless brick you can tolerate before they start to get boring. Even if they have blinking green veins pulsating across them. [var0 |Your footfalls echo through the mostly-smooth walls of the fortress, providing you with rhythmic ambience – and you realize with a bit of a start that, once again, you don’t hear anything out of the ordinary. No brick-against-brick; no whooshing noises as the fortress unmakes and remakes itself around you. You turn to Berwyn, about to ask him if he hears anything, but his eyes are narrowed and his ears are perked: he’s way ahead of you. If that’s the case, the odds are decent that you’ve found your way back to the 'midway’ point of the fortress: you’ve found Berwyn’s and Matiha’s old sleeping quarters, and they’re just beyond that door. And, just as you had guessed, the door opens to reveal Berwyn’s and Matiha’s old sleeping quarters. Berwyn’s bed and living space sit to the left of the room, completely undisturbed from the last time you were here[var1|, down to you leaving his panty drawer ajar when you raided it]. And the same goes for Matiha’s half of the room: it’s clean and well-kept, almost hauntingly so, as if she hadn’t slept it in since the day you and Berwyn first confronted her. Berwyn is notably still and contemplative once he enters the room. Like last time, he’s probably dealing with a wave of emotions – nostalgia among them. He doesn’t have much to add now that you’re here. |However, as you approach the top of the stairs, you feel Berwyn tug at your [pc.upperGarments] to stop you in your tracks. "Hold on," he whispers; his giant, furry ears poking through the brim of his hat fidget and twist on his head, trying to lock onto something in particular. "Do you hear that?" You turn your heard to one side, cocking your right ear up to the air as you listen for whatever he’s referring to. [pc.cunningRange 0 50 |But you don’t hear anything – the fortress is as quiet as the dead. "Exactly," Berwyn whispers. "It’s not moving. We must be getting close to something." To Matiha? "We’re about to find out," he grimaces, trying to maintain a steely demeanor. |You listen for anything from the errant buzz of the magic flowing through the veins in the bricks to the sound of your breathing, but nothing stands out of the ordinary. That’s when you realize it: there’s nothing out of the ordinary. In a dimension where ordinary is a verboten thing. There’s no scraping of brick on brick; there’s no howling of the wind as the stones smash through them to reassemble somewhere. The fortress has stopped. "Yeah," Berwyn agrees, his steely eyes on you. "We must be getting close to something." To Matiha? You sort of doubt it.... "So do I," he frowns, his brow furrowing. "But there’s only one way to find out." ] You put your hands on the wooden door and, gathering your courage, you give it a gentle push, ready for whatever might be on the other side of it. You keep your hand on your [pc.weapon], and Berwyn stands tensely behind you, his hands ready to cast whatever incantation he needs as soon as he needs it. But what you see on the other side of the door isn’t Matiha – it’s her old sleeping quarters. Hers and Berwyn’s. At the sight of his old bed, and his old dresser, and his old living space, Berwyn’s posture immediately deflates; his arms sink to his sides and his eyebrows rise in surprise. He steps cautiously into the room as his eyes stay glued to his old effects and belongings; everything is as exactly as you two had left it[var1|, down to you leaving his panty drawer slightly ajar when you raided it]. He steps up to the edge of his bed and he places a hand gently on its cushions, feeling it sink underneath his touch. His eyes narrow and his stare goes off somewhere else, focusing on something a million miles away; as soon as his hand touches down on the mattress of his bed, all of the memories from his time with Matiha come rushing back to him, all at once. Berwyn stays like that for a moment. He breathes gently through his nose, and, eventually, his eyelids begin to sink; he almost looks as if he might fall asleep at any moment. "Matiha’s not far from here," he says eventually, taking a deep breath as he does. "This room’s almost totally undisturbed. She wouldn’t put herself too far away from it." You ask him if he knows just how close. "I don’t know," he answers. "But... close. We just need to keep it up." His eyes go back to you, the earlier resolve and steely indignation restored to his pupils. Some of the insecurity that he had before has vanished – not all of it, but enough to straighten his spine. "Let’s get going." ] To the north is the room’s exit, leading back to the stairwell you were on when you first entered; the stairs continue upward, climbing the tower of the fortress, although there’s no guarantee that that’ll be where they continue once you leave the room. [var0 |And to the south is the trapdoor, laid flush with the floor, leading deeper into the fortress proper. Berwyn has told you before that it didn’t exist before and he has no idea where it could lead. Who really knows: down could be up in this twisted building stuck in the Ways Between. |However... to the south is a trapdoor, laid flush with the floor. You don’t remember seeing that the last time you were in this room, but maybe you just missed it. You ask Berwyn if he recognizes it; he stands on his tip-toes and leans forward to get a better look at what you’re referring to. "Nnnnnno," he answers, his mouth curling. "I’ve lived in this room for at least a year, and I’ve never seen that there before." Well. Now it’s there. Who knows where it could lead? ] '

rows.original:
Leaving Berwyn’s old sleeping quarters takes you back to the staircase you had been climbing: the room was a stop on the way to the summit of the stairs. Once you resume your climb, you hear the sound of bricks sliding against each other as you progress down the way; the room ahead of you is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled.
     
    Once you reach the stop of the stairs, it opens up into what appears to be some kind of soldier’s quarters. Bunk beds line the east and west walls; each of them has a chest sitting at the base of the bottom bunk, likely for storing personal effects. The beds are made, but they haven’t been disturbed in what is probably many years. The green veins permeating the stones crawl up the bedposts – and in some of the beds, they’re even coursing through the fabric of the bedding. [var0
        |You’ve been in this room before, and, from experience, you know that each of the chests are empty. You don’t bother checking them a second time.
        |You decide to check some of the chests for anything that could be of any use, but after opening the first two and finding absolutely nothing, you figure that the rest are probably empty, too.
    ]
     
    To the north of the room is a closed wooden door, obscuring your sight from whatever’s behind it. The door and the frame it’s in look fairly well-kept and dust free. The west of the room is another opening, framed by a pair of purple banners with intricate designs on them, that leads to a set of stairs heading downward; the light of the room you’re in doesn’t reach down there far enough for you to see where it leads. One of the banners has what appears to be a black handprint on it, while the other banner has more green veins coursing through it, similar to the bedsheets.
rows.translation:
离开贝林旧时的卧室后，你会重新回到之前一直在攀爬的那段楼梯：那个房间其实只是通往楼梯顶端途中的其中一个停留点。当你继续向上攀爬时，会听到砖块在相互摩擦发出的声响；当你逐渐靠近前方那个房间时，会发现那个房间正在建设中，而你之前离开的那个房间则已经被拆除了。
     
    一旦你走到楼梯的尽头，就会看到一片似乎是士兵宿舍的区域。东墙和西墙两侧排列着双层床；每张床的下层床铺旁都放着一个箱子，应该是用来存放个人物品的。这些床已经铺好了，但很可能已经很多年没有人动过它们了。那些渗透在石头中的绿色脉络蜿蜒着延伸到床柱上——在某些床上，这些脉络甚至穿透了床铺的布料。 [var0
        |你之前已经来过这个房间，根据经验，你知道这些箱子都是空的。所以你根本不会费心再去检查它们了。
        |你决定检查那些箱子，看看是否有什么有用的东西，但打开前两个箱子后什么也没找到，于是你认为剩下的箱子可能也都空着。
    ]
     
    房间的北侧有一扇紧闭的木门，挡住了你观察门后景象的视线。这扇门及其门框看起来都保养得很好，没有积满灰尘。房间的西侧还有另一个出口，那里用一对装饰着复杂图案的紫色旗帜作为门框，这条通道通向一段向下延伸的楼梯；不过你所在这个房间的光线无法照到那么低的地方，因此你无法看到楼梯通向哪里。其中一面横幅上似乎有一个黑色的手印，而另一面横幅上则布满了绿色的脉络，看起来就像床单一样。

rows.original: You traverse the dark hallway; it bends to the right shortly after you leave the room, obscuring your sight deeper into the building, but it’s also not particularly long. Shortly after you leave the room you were just in, you hear the sound of bricks slamming into each other, their clay crudely grinding against one another as they move; the room ahead of you is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled. You’re in what appears to be a headmaster’s quarters, or whatever the highest rank of whatever platoon or squadron was stationed here. That said, it’s still not a lot: there’s a standing cabinet in the corner of the room, its wood having turned green from a combination of the mold and rot over time as well as the pulsating green veins that dominate the décor of the fortress. There’s a desk with a simple wooden chair behind it, facing towards the east; atop the desk is a fresh, unlit candle with a candle holder, but... it’s upside-down, standing perfectly still on its wick. [var0 |Knowing from the last time you were here, you opt not to search the desk’s drawers – you know it’s empty. |You think to rifle through the drawers of the desk while you’re here, but you find nothing – and you somehow don’t disturb the candle. ] [var1 |There is only one way in or out of this room: an opening to the west, where the wall of the room opens into a wide corridor, but it gets narrower and brighter as it goes further down. You get the feeling that this is Matiha telling you that she’s ready to see you now. |To your east is a simple wooden door, left slightly ajar; in the dim light of the room, you can see a set of stairs trending downward, heading somewhere you can’t see. To your west, the wall of the room opens into a wide, dark corridor, but it gets narrower and brighter as it goes further down. To your south is another dark corridor, framed at its entrance on either side by a pair of purple banners with intricate designs sewn onto them. ]
rows.translation: 你穿过昏暗的走廊；刚离开房间不久，走廊就向右拐弯，使得你无法看到建筑物更远处的情况，不过这条走廊其实并不长。就在你离开刚才所在的房间后不久，你听到了砖块相互碰撞的声音——那些黏土制成的砖块在移动时发出粗糙的摩擦声。显然，你前方的房间正在建设中，而你刚刚离开的那个房间则已经被拆除了。 你现在似乎身处一位校长的办公室里，或者说，这里是驻扎在这里的某个排或中队的最高指挥官的办公场所。不过，这个办公室布置得并不复杂：房间角落里有一个立式橱柜，由于长时间受霉菌和腐朽的影响，其木材已经变成了绿色；而那些遍布在整个房间中的绿色脉络，更是成为了这个场所最具特色的装饰元素。有一张桌子，后面放着一把简单的木椅，桌子面向东方；桌子上放着一支崭新的、未点燃的蜡烛和烛台，但是……蜡烛是倒着放的，却依然稳稳地立在烛芯上。 [var0 |因为你上次来过，所以你选择不去翻找桌子的抽屉——你知道里面是空的。 |你想着趁现在把桌子的抽屉都翻一遍，但什么也没找到——而且你居然也没有碰倒那支蜡烛。 ] [var1 |这个房间只有一处进出通道：位于西侧的一处开口，通过那里，房间的墙壁会延伸成一条宽阔的走廊，而这条走廊在继续向前延伸的过程中会逐渐变窄，同时光线也会变得越发明亮。你会觉得，这就像是玛蒂哈在告诉你，她现在已经准备好见你了。 |你的东边有一扇半开的木门，在房间昏暗的光线下，你能看到一段向下延伸的楼梯，通向某个你看不见的地方。你的西边，房间的墙壁延伸成一条宽阔而黑暗的走廊，但越往深处走，走廊会变得越来越窄，光线也会逐渐变亮。你的南边也有一条黑暗的走廊，入口处两侧各挂着一面绣有复杂图案的紫色旗帜。 ]

rows.original:
You decide to head down the dark corridor; light doesn’t reach very deep into the walkway, and you’re forced to feel along the walls with your hand to keep track of where you’re going. The bulges of the veins along the fortress’s bricks press back against your fingertips. Shortly after starting down the dark corridor, you hear the sound of bricks grinding harshly against other bricks; the room ahead of you is being built as you approach, and the room you left has been dismantled.
    
    You enter what could generously be described as a terrarium: the room is dome-shaped; with four curved pillars at each of the cardinal walls, meeting in the center. There is no roof to the room, and it’s exposed to the open 'air’ of the Ways Between. A candleholder with a candle is fastened to the south pillar, and the candle appears half-used, but it’s been snuffed by the vegetation covering its wick.
    
    The floor is still hard brick, but it’s totally overrun with ivy vines twisting over each other and carpeting for floor and walls with themselves. Blue-and-white flowers, each of them large enough to wrap you up in their petals, bloom along their lengths, each of them giving off a candescent, pale-green light; when you enter the room, their bodies turn towards you simultaneously, as if you were the sun and they’re looking to you for nutrients... or, more to put it another way, their next meal.
    
    To your north is a dark corridor; whatever light is in the terrarium dies just a few feet beyond its entrance, and you can’t see beyond the first few steps. The path to the tower is stopped by a simple, raggedy wooden door that could easily be pulled open. To your south, you can see a small tower over the edge of the wall – it’s much smaller than Matiha’s tower and is likely just some form of watchtower or keep. To your west, the terrarium opens up to a wide staircase that leads downward, but the curved ceiling of the corridor prevents you from seeing where it opens up to.
rows.translation:
你决定走进那条昏暗的走廊；光线无法照亮走廊的深处，因此你不得不用手沿着墙壁摸索，才能确定前进的方向。堡垒砖块上凸起的纹理紧紧压迫着你的指尖。就在你开始沿着走廊前进不久，你听到了砖块相互摩擦发出的刺耳声响——前方那个房间正在建设中，而你刚刚离开的那个房间则已经被拆除了。
    
    你走进了一个可以被称之为“生态箱”的空间：这个房间的形状像一个圆顶，四面的墙壁上各有一根弯曲的柱子，这些柱子在房间中央交汇。这个房间没有天花板，直接暴露在“通道之间”的开阔空间中。南侧的柱子上固定着一个插着蜡烛的烛台，那支蜡烛看起来只用了一半，但它的烛芯已经被周围的植物覆盖住了，因此火焰已经熄灭了。
    
    地面依然是坚硬的砖块，但上面爬满了相互缠绕的常春藤，这些藤蔓几乎覆盖了整个地面和墙壁。沿着藤蔓生长着蓝白色的花朵，每一朵都大到足以将人完全包裹在它们的花瓣之中。这些花朵会散发出淡绿色的光芒；当你走进这个房间时，所有的花朵会同时转向你，仿佛你是太阳，而它们正在向你汲取养分……或者换句话说，它们正在等待下一顿美餐。
    
    在你的北方，有一条昏暗的走廊；饲养箱里的光线在入口几英尺外就消失了，因此你无法看清前方的道路。通往塔楼的道路被一扇简陋而破旧的木门挡住了，但这扇门应该很容易就被推开。在你的南方，你可以看到城墙边缘有一座小塔——它比玛蒂哈的塔小得多，很可能只是一座瞭望塔或防御工事。而在你的西方，那个封闭的空间通向一段宽阔的楼梯，楼梯向下延伸，但由于走廊的拱形天花板，你无法看到它最终通向哪里。
