rows.original: Sweat beads off Berwyn’s furrowed brow, his hands glowing as he concentrates his magic on the stone. "I’ve almost...!" he grunts to you, trying to speak over the general volume and chatter of the battle between you and Matiha, but whatever noise he makes is drowned in the ambience. With one last cast of his magic striking the cracked, bulbous outer layer of the rune, you feel it: a thick wave of energy emanating from the rune, washing over the room before colliding with you, Berwyn, and Matiha. It feels almost like gravity: an invisible force, not dissimilar to wind, pushing against you and forcing you away from the rune as its energy is leaked from the rock, and the closer you get to the rune, the more intense it becomes. All of the mana stored within the rune is about ready to be released into the room, but with Berwyn working his own magics on the stone, it’s imminent implosion is controlled and contained – but it’ll nonetheless be a devastating force, and you brace yourself for what’s about to happen. "No!" Matiha cries, her attention wholly turned away from you. "Berwyn, what have you done?!" He doesn’t answer: his hands continue to weave their incantations in the air towards the rune, prodding it for more of its ether. A thick beam of pale-green light bursts from one of the runes seams, flooding the room with its luster. "Berwyn, no!" Matiha shouts again[silly |. "Berwyn YES!" he shouts back. Matiha |, and she ] darts away from you – and straight for the rune rather than for Berwyn. She takes three long strides before diving headfirst onto the runestone, her arms outstretched; her body soars onto the rune on its pedestal, wrapping herself around the rock just as its light grows suddenly more intense. And just as she does, that gravity-like force is gone, covered by her body. Matiha hits the floor with the rune beneath her, and then you hear a loud, dull, muted 'thud’ as the rune detonates. All of that power is released, all at once, beneath Matiha’s body, and she uses herself to cover that immeasurable force, containing it underneath herself. The light from within the rune pierces through Matiha’s body, shining clear through her torso in many different spots, with more breaking through the skin of her body as the seconds go by. Any normal person would have perished instantly, and even then, a normal person jumping on the rune would have been like trying to put out a forest fire with a single blade of grass – but you can hear Matiha moan in pain as she huddles on top of the rune, her arms and legs pulling into the fetal position as she clutches the rune beneath herself. And suddenly... her body begins to change. Matiha takes on a massive surge of size and mass, her body shifting and transforming to accommodate that sudden massive influx of mana. Her skin turns scaly and orange, pockmarked by welts and divots, turning her formerly-perfect skin into something hardly even uniform, much less smooth. Her body shifts as it gets larger, changing from a humanoid figure with two defined arms and legs and turning into... something else without a defined shape, riddled with extra limbs and extremities, almost like antenna. You can no longer discern where her front and her back are on her torso, and yet, three sets of featherless wings sprout along the undulating, shapeless mass, writhing and flapping as she gets larger and larger. Berwyn’s hands lower from their position, his face twisted into an slack-jawed mix of shock and disgust. One of the tentacles from Matiha’s new, mutated body whips at his ankles, intent on snatching him up, and he’s too distracted to see it coming, but you’re faster: you manage to leap into him, knocking him out of the way from the whipping tentacle and keeping you both a safe distance away from Matiha’s body. She moans again, and her voice has lowered in pitch, reverberating across the room. The pale-green lights piercing through her body shift, their beams broadening and their colors turning to a darker, more vibrant green. Her body presses against the far wall of the tower’s room, and you suddenly hear the sound of brick shifting and scraping against brick as the room that formerly made up Matiha’s office is transformed into a massive, otherwise-featureless dome with no way in or out. It at least gives you more room to move.
rows.translation: 贝尔温额头上布满了汗珠，他的双手在集中魔力作用于那块石头时闪闪发光。“我差不多成功了……！”他对着你低声说道，试图盖过你们与玛蒂哈之间激烈的战斗所产生的喧嚣与嘈杂，但无论他发出多大的声音，都淹没在周围的嘈杂声中。 在他最后一次施展魔法，触碰到那枚符文裂开的外层时，你们感受到了——一股强大的能量从符文中释放出来，弥漫在整个房间里，最终冲击到了你们三人身上。这种感觉几乎就像重力一样：一种无形的力量，类似于风，不断地推挤着你们，迫使你们远离那枚符文。随着符文中的能量不断外泄，你们离它越近，这种力量就越强。 储存在那些符文中的所有魔力都即将被释放到这个房间里，但由于贝尔温正在对这块石头施展自己的魔法，它的爆发被有效地控制住了——但即便如此，这仍然会是一股毁灭性的力量，因此你得做好迎接即将发生的事情的准备。 不！”玛蒂哈惊叫道，她的注意力已经完全从你身上转移开了。“贝尔温，你究竟做了什么？！” 他没有回答：他的双手仍在空中不断挥动，对着那些符文念着咒语，试图让它们释放出更多的能量。突然，其中一道符文的缝隙中迸发出一道淡绿色的光束，那光芒照亮了整个房间。 贝尔温，不要！”玛蒂哈再次喊道。[silly |贝尔温好的！他大声回应道。 玛蒂哈 |，还有她 ]她迅速朝你的方向冲去，却直接扑向了那块符文，而不是贝尔温。她迈出三步长跑的距离，然后整个人扑向了那块立在基座上的符文，双臂伸展开来；她的身体紧紧地缠绕在符文上，就在这时，符文散发出的光芒突然变得强烈起来。而就在她这么做的时候，那种仿佛重力的力量消失了，被她的身体完全遮住了。 玛蒂哈将符文放在身下，随即传来一声沉闷而压抑的“轰隆”声——符文发生了爆炸。所有那些能量瞬间被释放出来，聚集在玛蒂哈的身体下方。她用自己的身体来抵挡这股巨大的力量，将它们全部束缚在自己体内。 符文内部散发出的光芒穿透了玛蒂哈的身体，在她的躯干上形成了许多光点；随着时间的推移，更多的光芒开始突破她的皮肤。对于任何一个普通人来说，这样的光芒瞬间就会致其死亡。即便如此，如果一个普通人试图跳到这个符文上，那无异于试图用一根草来扑灭一场森林大火——但你可以听到玛蒂哈在痛苦中呻吟着，她蜷缩在符文之上，双臂双腿呈胎儿姿势，紧紧抓住身下的符文。 突然之间……她的身体开始发生变化。 玛蒂哈的身体体积和重量急剧增加，她的身体结构也在不断变化，以适应这种突如其来的大量魔力涌入。她的皮肤变得粗糙而呈橙色，上面布满了凹痕和疤痕，原本光滑完美的肌肤如今已变得参差不齐，远不再平滑。她的身体在不断变大，形态也在发生变化——原本那个拥有清晰四肢的人形轮廓逐渐消失了，取而代之的是一个形状模糊、布满多余肢体和触手的怪物，那些触手几乎就像天线一样。此时你已经无法分辨她躯干的正面和背面在哪里了，然而，在那不断膨胀、形状诡异的躯体上，却长出了三对没有羽毛的翅膀，这些翅膀随着她身体的不断变大而扭动、拍打着。 贝尔温的手部从原来的位置松了下来，他的脸上浮现出震惊与厌恶交织的表情。玛蒂哈那具新的、发生了变异的身体中的一条触手猛地朝他的脚踝袭来，企图将他抓走，而他当时完全没注意到这一攻击——但你反应更快：你及时跳到他身边，将他从那条触手的攻击范围之外拉开，从而确保你们俩都能远离玛蒂哈的身体。 她再次发出了呻吟声，她的声音变得低沉而悠长，在房间里回荡。那些穿透她身体的淡绿色光线开始发生变化，光束变得更为宽阔，颜色也变成了更深沉、更加鲜艳的绿色。她的身体紧贴着塔室的最远墙壁，这时你突然听到砖块相互移动、摩擦的声音——原本是玛蒂哈办公室的那个空间，此刻已经变成了一个巨大的、没有任何开口的圆顶结构。这样至少能让你有更多的活动空间。
rows.raw: ' Sweat beads off Berwyn’s furrowed brow, his hands glowing as he concentrates his magic on the stone. "I’ve almost...!" he grunts to you, trying to speak over the general volume and chatter of the battle between you and Matiha, but whatever noise he makes is drowned in the ambience. With one last cast of his magic striking the cracked, bulbous outer layer of the rune, you feel it: a thick wave of energy emanating from the rune, washing over the room before colliding with you, Berwyn, and Matiha. It feels almost like gravity: an invisible force, not dissimilar to wind, pushing against you and forcing you away from the rune as its energy is leaked from the rock, and the closer you get to the rune, the more intense it becomes. All of the mana stored within the rune is about ready to be released into the room, but with Berwyn working his own magics on the stone, it’s imminent implosion is controlled and contained – but it’ll nonetheless be a devastating force, and you brace yourself for what’s about to happen. "No!" Matiha cries, her attention wholly turned away from you. "Berwyn, what have you done?!" He doesn’t answer: his hands continue to weave their incantations in the air towards the rune, prodding it for more of its ether. A thick beam of pale-green light bursts from one of the runes seams, flooding the room with its luster. "Berwyn, no!" Matiha shouts again[silly |. "Berwyn YES!" he shouts back. Matiha |, and she ] darts away from you – and straight for the rune rather than for Berwyn. She takes three long strides before diving headfirst onto the runestone, her arms outstretched; her body soars onto the rune on its pedestal, wrapping herself around the rock just as its light grows suddenly more intense. And just as she does, that gravity-like force is gone, covered by her body. Matiha hits the floor with the rune beneath her, and then you hear a loud, dull, muted 'thud’ as the rune detonates. All of that power is released, all at once, beneath Matiha’s body, and she uses herself to cover that immeasurable force, containing it underneath herself. The light from within the rune pierces through Matiha’s body, shining clear through her torso in many different spots, with more breaking through the skin of her body as the seconds go by. Any normal person would have perished instantly, and even then, a normal person jumping on the rune would have been like trying to put out a forest fire with a single blade of grass – but you can hear Matiha moan in pain as she huddles on top of the rune, her arms and legs pulling into the fetal position as she clutches the rune beneath herself. And suddenly... her body begins to change. Matiha takes on a massive surge of size and mass, her body shifting and transforming to accommodate that sudden massive influx of mana. Her skin turns scaly and orange, pockmarked by welts and divots, turning her formerly-perfect skin into something hardly even uniform, much less smooth. Her body shifts as it gets larger, changing from a humanoid figure with two defined arms and legs and turning into... something else without a defined shape, riddled with extra limbs and extremities, almost like antenna. You can no longer discern where her front and her back are on her torso, and yet, three sets of featherless wings sprout along the undulating, shapeless mass, writhing and flapping as she gets larger and larger. Berwyn’s hands lower from their position, his face twisted into an slack-jawed mix of shock and disgust. One of the tentacles from Matiha’s new, mutated body whips at his ankles, intent on snatching him up, and he’s too distracted to see it coming, but you’re faster: you manage to leap into him, knocking him out of the way from the whipping tentacle and keeping you both a safe distance away from Matiha’s body. She moans again, and her voice has lowered in pitch, reverberating across the room. The pale-green lights piercing through her body shift, their beams broadening and their colors turning to a darker, more vibrant green. Her body presses against the far wall of the tower’s room, and you suddenly hear the sound of brick shifting and scraping against brick as the room that formerly made up Matiha’s office is transformed into a massive, otherwise-featureless dome with no way in or out. It at least gives you more room to move.'

rows.original: You’ve lost track of time from watching Matiha’s body transform into something it’s not, she finally stops growing, and the writhing mass of flesh stops sprouting new limbs. The lights piercing her body dim down before disappearing entirely. You can hear Matiha groan in pained relief – the pain that she was experiencing had subsided, and now, from the lilt in her voice, it almost sounds like it was replaced with pleasure. She shifts, lifting her left arm – or, what was her left arm – out from underneath herself and planting it on the floor. It more closely resembles a fleshy hoof than a hand: it lacks digits and her wrist ends in a thick stump instead of a proper palm. Then she removes her right arm... and then her other left arm, and then her other right arm. A thick, scaly tail sprouts from where you presume her spine meets her coccyx, hitting the floor hard enough to shake the dust from the newly-formed bricks around the dome. It whips through the air with enough force to make the air sing a thick contralto tone. One additional limb lifts and wriggles above the scaly flesh, placed roughly in the center of the gross mass, and on its end is what can generously be called a human face: it has six-too-many eyes and they’re placed at asymmetrical points; its mouth is crooked, almost diagonal; and it has holes instead of a nose. But if you had to choose any part of this new creature’s body to be the head, or at least the face, it would be that. Matiha’s eight eyes focus on you and Berwyn, each of them moving individually until they roll into their final position. "Berwyn," you hear her say, although what you think is her 'mouth’ doesn’t flap in time with her words. "Berwyn... Berwyn...." Berwyn stands behind you, his staff at the ready, but his grip is loose and his knees are bent inwards. And you certainly can’t blame him. "I... feel... so... strong!" Matiha chants. Each of her many dozens of limbs and extremities flex and stretch, uncoiling to their full lengths before retracting into a more comfortable position. "This... power! It’s... mine! Mana... courses... through... me!" Some part of one of her six limbs opens up, and a ray of dark-green light shoots from it before dissipating into the air like a thick mist. The veins visible beneath her orange scales pulse with the same vibrant green light, mapping different pathways underneath her skin as the Essence flows through her. The long appendage with the face on it cranes forward. You can hear the scales on its 'neck’ click and clack against each other as it stiffly, and awkwardly, leans over the writhing mass of its body to get a closer look at you both. "Berwyn," she says again, her voice thrumming through the air. "I... forgive... you." Her eyes dart around randomly for a moment before all of them focus tightly onto you. "I... forgive... you... too." He says nothing in reply, and instead clutches his staff closer to himself. "I... want... you... to... be... a... part... of... this." Her head twists to one side, a bit too far for your liking, as a dozen of her smaller, thinner antenna slowly creep their way towards you both. "This... power. Let... me... share... it... with... you." You and Berwyn simultaneously rebuke Matiha’s advances; you by swinging your [pc.weapon] at the creeping tendrils, and Berwyn by blasting them with a spell. They flinch and pull back, but if they hurt Matiha, she doesn’t let it outwardly show. "It’s... alright," she says, noticing your [pc.isDK |apprehension |fear ]. Her massive limbs scuttle along the floor of the dome, neither approaching nor retreating, but trying to get a better angle on you both. "[silly |Be... not... afraid |I’m... still... me ]." Her head twists in the opposite direction, whipping around faster than you can blink. "I... want... to... be... with... you... Berwyn. Please...." You stand beside Berwyn, your [pc.weapon] at the ready for whatever this monstrosity that was once Matiha is going to try next. For a moment, you wonder if Berwyn is going to hesitate – less because you think he’s going to take her offer, and more because he’s afraid of hurting her. "[pc.name]," he says after a moment. From the corner of your eye, you see the tip of his staff point towards Matiha. "We’re in this together." You’re fighting Matiha!
rows.translation: 由于一直注视着玛蒂哈的身体不断发生变形，你完全忘记了时间的流逝。最终，她的身体停止了生长，那团不断蠕动、不断长出新肢体的肉块也终于不再活动了。那些刺入她身体的光芒逐渐变弱，最终彻底消失了。你可以听到玛蒂哈发出痛苦而又解脱的呻吟声——她之前所感受到的痛苦已经消失了，而从她声音中的肌肉度来看，那种痛苦似乎已经被愉悦所取代了。 她动了动身体，抬起了自己的左臂——或者说，应该是原本属于她的左臂——从身下伸出来，放在了地上。那东西看起来更像是一只肉质的蹄子，而不是手：它没有手指，手腕处也只是一块粗厚的残端，而不是正常的手掌。接着，她又把右臂也拿了出来。然后是她的另一只左臂，接着是另一只右臂。一条粗壮、布满鳞片的尾巴从她脊柱与尾骨相连的地方生长出来，它重重地砸在地板上，甚至让穹顶周围新砌的砖块上都震起了灰尘。它以足以让空气发出低沉的康塔托音调的力量，在空气中急速穿梭。 在那片鳞片覆盖的肉体上方，还有一只肢体微微动着、扭动着，大致位于那团怪异肉块的中央。它的末端，勉强可以被称为一张“人类面孔”：它有六只眼睛，而且这些眼睛的位置完全不对称；它的嘴巴歪斜着，几乎呈对角线形状；而它的鼻子部位则是一些洞洞而已。不过，如果非要在这个新生物的身体上选择一个部位来当作“头部”——或者至少是“面部”的话，那应该就是这个部位了。 玛蒂哈的八只眼睛依次注视着你和贝尔温，每一只眼睛都在独立移动，最终稳定在固定的位置上。“贝尔温，”你听到她说道，不过你注意到，她的“嘴巴”并没有随着话语的发出而动。“贝尔温……贝尔温……” 贝尔温站在你身后，手中的法杖已经准备就绪，但他的握法很松，膝盖也微微弯曲。你确实不能责怪他。 我……感觉……自己变得……如此强大！”玛蒂哈兴奋地喊道。她那数十条肢体不断地弯曲、伸展，完全伸展开来后又重新恢复到更舒适的姿势。“这种力量……属于我！魔力……正在我的体内流淌！ 她的六条肢体中的某一条突然张开，一道深绿色的光芒从其中射出，随后像浓雾一样消散在空气中。她橙色的鳞片下，那些可见的血管也闪烁着同样的鲜绿色光芒，随着精华在她的体内流动，这些血管在皮肤下形成了不同的路径。 那条长着脸的附肢向前伸展开来。你可以听到它“脖子”上的鳞片相互碰撞发出的咔嗒声，它僵硬而笨拙地将身体倾斜过来，以便更仔细地观察你们两个。 “贝尔温，”她再次说道，她的声音在空气中回荡，“我……原谅……你。”她的目光在周围随机扫视了一瞬，随后全都紧紧地聚焦在了你身上。“我……也原谅……你。 他没有回答什么，只是将手中的法杖握得更紧了。 “我……希望……你能……成为……这一切的一部分。”她的头微微偏向一侧，这个角度或许有点不太合适，因为她那十几根细长、柔软的“触角”正在缓缓地向你们俩延伸。“这种力量……让我……与你分享吧。 你和贝尔温同时斥责了玛蒂哈的举动；你则是通过挥动你的[pc.weapon]来表达反对。 面对那些蔓延而来的触须，贝琳用咒语将它们炸毁。那些生物畏缩着退了回去，但如果它们伤害到了玛蒂哈，她却丝毫没有表现出来。 “没……没事的，”她说道，注意到你[pc.isDK |担忧 |恐惧 ]的目光。她那庞大的身躯在圆顶的地板上快速移动，既不靠近也不后退，只是在试图找到一个更好的角度来观察你们两个。[silly |别……害怕…… |我……依然……还是那个我。 ]她的头朝相反的方向转动，转动的速度快得让你根本来不及眨眼。“我……想……和……你……在一起……贝尔温。求你……” 你站在贝尔温的身边，你的[pc.weapon]随时准备应对这个曾经叫玛蒂哈的怪物接下来可能会做出的任何举动。有那么一瞬间，你会怀疑贝尔温是否会犹豫——不是因为你觉得他会接受她的提议，而是因为他害怕伤害她。[pc.name]，”就这样吧，”他过了一会儿说道。你眼角的余光看到，他的法杖尖正指向玛蒂哈。 “我们同舟共济。 你正在与玛蒂哈战斗！

rows.original:
The moment you display weakness, one of Matiha’s spindly tentacles whips behind your ankles, tripping you over and landing you hard on your back. Your grip on your [pc.weapon] is knocked loose, and it flings across the room, well out of your reach.

    The tentacle wraps around your ankles several times, squeezing down on your legs; no matter how much you try and pry them apart, the tentacle’s grip on them is too strong.
    
    "[pc.name]!" Berwyn shouts, his staff pointed towards the tentacle wrapped around you, but as soon as he lets his eyes off Matiha, another one whips across the end of his staff, snapping it right in two. Berwyn’s staff is reduced to little more than a stick, and with another flick of the tentacle, that’s pulled from his hands as well, as a third one whips around his ankles just as they had to you.
    
    With a powerful yank, you’re pulled across the stony floor of the dome, towards Matiha’s main body. Your fingers claw and scratch at the floor, trying to find purchase in between the bricks, but there’s nothing for you to grip onto.
    
    "It’s... alright," you hear Matiha coo soothingly, like a mother trying to console an upset child. "It’s... alright. It’s... alright. I... will... share... my... strength... with... you. We... will... all... be... something... greater."
    
    The tentacle brings the soles of your feet to Matiha’s orange scales. There is no visible opening in her body, and for a moment, you wonder if you’re safe, and that the most she could do is just press you against her body – but, suddenly, the tough scales turn a sick, pale green, transforming into pure Essence, and you sink into her body, ankles first.
    
    You quickly lose feeling in your toes, and that’s enough for you to black out from the shock.
    
    From that point forward, you are a part of something greater.
rows.translation:
你才刚显露弱势，玛蒂哈一根细长触手便抽向脚踝后方，将你绊倒，重重摔在背上。你没能握紧[pc.weapon]，武器脱手飞过房间，落在远远够不着的地方。

    触手在脚踝上缠绕数圈，死死勒住双腿；无论你怎样尝试将它撬开，触手的力量都太过强大。
    
    “[pc.name]！”贝尔温大喊道，用法杖指向缠住你的触手；可他的视线刚从玛蒂哈身上移开，另一根触手便抽过法杖末端，将其直接折成两截。贝尔温的法杖只剩下一根短棍；触手再次甩动，把断杖也从手中夺走。与此同时，第三根触手像缠住你时一样，卷上了他的脚踝。
    
    随着触手猛然拉扯，你被拖过圆顶建筑的石质地面，滑向玛蒂哈的主体。你的手指抓挠地面，试图扣住砖石之间的缝隙，却找不到任何着力点。
    
    “没……事的，”你听见玛蒂哈温柔地低声安慰，像母亲安抚难过的孩子。“没……事的。没……事的。我……会……把……力量……分给……你。我们……都会……成为……更伟大的……存在。”
    
    触手把你的脚底带到玛蒂哈橙色鳞片前。她身上看不见任何开口；有那么一瞬，你怀疑自己是否安全，怀疑她最多只能把你压上身体——可突然间，坚硬鳞片化作病态的苍白绿色，转变成纯粹精质；你的身体从脚踝开始，沉入她的体内。
    
    你的脚趾很快失去知觉；单是这股冲击，便足以让你昏死过去。
    
    从那一刻起，你成为了某个更伟大存在的一部分。
rows.raw:
'
    The moment you display weakness, one of Matiha’s spindly tentacles whips behind your ankles, tripping you over and landing you hard on your back. Your grip on your [pc.weapon] is knocked loose, and it flings across the room, well out of your reach.

    The tentacle wraps around your ankles several times, squeezing down on your legs; no matter how much you try and pry them apart, the tentacle’s grip on them is too strong.
    
    "[pc.name]!" Berwyn shouts, his staff pointed towards the tentacle wrapped around you, but as soon as he lets his eyes off Matiha, another one whips across the end of his staff, snapping it right in two. Berwyn’s staff is reduced to little more than a stick, and with another flick of the tentacle, that’s pulled from his hands as well, as a third one whips around his ankles just as they had to you.
    
    With a powerful yank, you’re pulled across the stony floor of the dome, towards Matiha’s main body. Your fingers claw and scratch at the floor, trying to find purchase in between the bricks, but there’s nothing for you to grip onto.
    
    "It’s... alright," you hear Matiha coo soothingly, like a mother trying to console an upset child. "It’s... alright. It’s... alright. I... will... share... my... strength... with... you. We... will... all... be... something... greater."
    
    The tentacle brings the soles of your feet to Matiha’s orange scales. There is no visible opening in her body, and for a moment, you wonder if you’re safe, and that the most she could do is just press you against her body – but, suddenly, the tough scales turn a sick, pale green, transforming into pure Essence, and you sink into her body, ankles first.
    
    You quickly lose feeling in your toes, and that’s enough for you to black out from the shock.
    
    From that point forward, you are a part of something greater.'

rows.original: Matiha’s body, despite its surplus limbs and wider stance, wobbles and shifts from that final blow. Her left legs stomp onto the floor, trying to find a comfortable way to stand underneath herself, but every time they come down, they wobble underneath the weight of her own body until she’s forced down to one side. "Berwyn...," she moans. The appendage holding her 'face’ thrashes from side to side, its eyes blinding arrhythmically and wandering over the room with dilated pupils. "I... just... Please... I... can’t... I... only... wanted...." She wheezes, her lungs making a whole other sound compared to the voice you hear. Her left legs curl underneath her body while her right legs scrape along the ground, just trying to keep herself steady and upright in front of you and Berwyn. She’s just as massive and imposing, that hasn’t changed, but the fight, and her inexperience with her own body, has reduced her to a thrashing, helpless beast that’s writhing its way towards its final moments. Putting her down would be a mercy. Evidently, Berwyn agrees: he raises his staff one final time, its foci on its end beginning to glow a similar off-green light as he rests his hand behind it. His expression isn’t one of a hero about to strike down a villain: it’s of a young man about to perform a task he doesn’t know if he has the strength to perform. He closes his eyes as he mentally recites the spell necessary to put a stop to Matiha and her schemes one final time. He doesn’t apologize – his mouth is kept firmly shut. If you had to guess, if he said anything at all, his willpower might waver. Matiha grunts once more as a thick beam of dark-green light bursts from her body, dissipating into the air. With a sudden burst of strength, her body lunges forward, barreling across the floor and on a direct collision course with Berwyn. "Berwyn!" you shout, rushing toward him with your hand outstretched to try and push him out of the way. With his eyes closed, he hears it, and you, before he sees it – and when he opens them, it’s too late. He gasps and lunges backward as a blast of firey magic erupts from the tip of his staff, making a direct hit with Matiha’s main body, but it does nothing to stop the heavy mass of her form from collapsing on top of him. With a deep, resounding BOOM! Berwyn is crushed beneath the massive weight of Matiha’s scaled body. Once she lands, another dark-green light of mana erupts from Matiha’s scaled body, shining like a beacon against the far wall of the dome you’re in. Another bursts from her stock-still, perhaps-lifeless body – then another, then another, each of them bathing the dome in another stream of light. And the longer they last, the lighter in hue the colors become, going from dark to pale green, and from pale green to white. It quickly becomes too much for your eyes, and you’re forced to shield them from the light source that is Matiha’s mutated body as it detonates on top of Berwyn.
rows.translation: 尽管玛蒂哈的身体有多余的肢体和更宽的站姿，但在那最后一击之后，她还是开始摇摇晃晃、身体不稳。她的左腿重重地踩在地板上，试图找到一个稳定的站立姿势，但每次落地时，她的身躯都会因为自身的重量而摇摆不定，最终迫使她向一侧倒去。 贝尔温……”她呻吟着。那支撑着她“脸”的器官不断地左右摇晃，它的眼睛无规律地闪烁着，瞳孔放大后在房间里四处游移。“我……只是……求你……我……实在受不了了……我……只是想要而已……她喘着气，她的肺部发出的声音与她所说的话语完全不同。她的左腿蜷缩在身体下方，而右腿则在地面上拖动，只是为了让自己能在你和贝尔温面前保持稳定、直立的状态。她依然那么庞大、那么令人敬畏，这一点并没有改变，但这场战斗，以及她对自己身体的不熟悉，让她变成了一头挣扎着、无助的野兽，正在走向最后的时刻。结束她的痛苦，其实是一种仁慈。 显然，贝尔温也同意这一点：他最后一次举起了手中的法杖，法杖的顶端开始散发出类似淡绿色的光芒，而他也将手放在了法杖的后部。他的表情并不像是一位即将击败恶人的英雄，而更像是一个不确定自己是否有足够力量完成这项任务的年轻人。 他闭上眼睛，在心中默念着那个能够彻底阻止玛蒂哈及其阴谋的咒语。他没有道歉——他的嘴唇紧紧地闭着。如果让你猜的话，如果他真的说了什么，他的意志力或许就会动摇。 玛蒂哈再次发出低吼，一道浓密的深绿色光束从她体内迸发出来，随后消散在空气中。随着一股突如其来的力量，她的身体向前冲去，在地板上飞驰，直接朝贝尔温冲去。贝林！”你大喊着，冲向他，伸出手试图将他推开。他闭着眼睛，听到了你的呼唤，也看到了你；但当他睁开眼睛时，已经为时已晚。 他倒吸一口冷气，猛地向后跃去——因为他的法杖尖端迸发出炽热的火焰，这些火焰直接击中了玛蒂哈的身体，但却丝毫无法阻止她那庞大的身躯压在他身上。随着一声深沉而响亮的砰！贝尔温被玛蒂哈那覆盖着鳞片的庞大身躯压得动弹不得。 当她落地后，玛蒂哈的鳞片身上又迸发出一道深绿色的法力光芒，那光芒如同信号灯一般，在你们所处的穹顶的远墙处闪烁着。她的身体原本静止不动，仿佛已经失去了生命，但又一次，又一次，光芒从她体内迸发出来——一道又一道光芒，将整个穹顶笼罩在绚丽的光芒之中。而这些光芒持续的时间越长，它们的颜色就越变得柔和，从深绿色逐渐变为淡绿色，再从淡绿色最终变为白色。 这种光芒很快就会让你的眼睛感到难以承受，你不得不遮挡自己的眼睛，以免被玛蒂哈那具发生变异的身体在贝尔温上方爆炸时释放出的强光伤害到。

rows.original: It’s dark. Dark and cold. You can’t see where you are, if you’re anywhere at all. You try and take a deep breath, but you feel something stop you – a blockage, or an obstruction, but it feels like it’s within you rather than on top of you. You scramble to try and breathe, to break free of whatever it is that’s keeping you down, but nothing you do works: you can’t move your fingers or your toes, or your arms or your legs. You can’t even open your mouth to breathe or to speak or to shout for help. But... you don’t panic. Some part of you should have realized your predicament for what it is – a direct threat to your life – but that base, primal need to defend yourself isn’t there. You’re calmer than you had expected yourself to be. In fact, you almost feel like you’re at peace. You try and remember what had happened before. You were... in a room. A room within a giant fortress. Or... perhaps the fortress wasn’t that large, but it felt like it went forever. You had met a woman – someone you recognized. Someone you had a particular affinity for. You remember a rush of adrenaline, and fear, and a deep-seated want for things to just go the way you wanted for once. You remember a sudden shock, as if something had surprised you, followed by a voice – the voice of someone you trusted. Or... you still trust. What had happened wasn’t their fault. You remember them saying your name and running to try and catch you, to help you, but it was too late. They said the name 'Berwyn.’ That’s you. You are Berwyn. But... what are you? What is Berwyn? You try and flex your fingers in the darkness once again, but you can’t... because it feels like you don’t have fingers to begin with. It’s not that something is keeping them pressed down, but rather that you don’t have fingers to flex. Your body is amorphous, lacking clearly defined outlines, structures, and limits. You aren’t in a dark void – you simply don’t exist. Not yet, anyway. You were a magician, capable of wielding the world’s ambient magic between your fingertips to alter reality to be whatever you wanted. Remaking yourself will be the easiest task you’ve ever performed: despite your clouded, muddied memories, your wits have never felt sharper, and you’ve never felt more in-tune with the magic permeating the very space around you. It almost feels like you could do anything.
rows.translation: 天很黑。黑得伸手不见五指，也冷得刺骨。 你根本看不清自己到底在哪里，甚至不确定自己是否真的存在于这个地方。你试图深吸一口气，但却感觉有什么东西阻碍了你——像是某种堵塞物，或是某种障碍物，总之，那种感觉非常明显。在……范围内你无法动弹，甚至无法呼吸。你拼命挣扎，试图摆脱那些压在身上的东西，但无论你怎么做都无济于事：你的手指、脚趾、手臂、双腿都无法动弹，甚至连张嘴呼吸、说话或呼救都无法做到。 但是……你不要慌张。你内心深处应该已经意识到自己所处的困境究竟是什么——这是一种直接威胁到你生命的危险——然而，那种保护自己的本能却并未被激发出来。你的反应比自己预想的要冷静得多。事实上，你会有一种置身于宁静之中的感觉。 你努力回想之前发生了什么。你当时在……一个房间里。一个位于巨大堡垒内部的房间。或者……也许那个堡垒并没有那么大，但感觉到仿佛那一刻永远持续下去。你遇到了一个女人——一个你熟悉的人，一个让你特别有好感的人。你记得当时自己心中充满了肾上腺素，还有恐惧，同时也深深希望一切能按照自己的意愿发展。 你记得当时突然感到一阵震惊，仿佛有什么事情让你措手不及，紧接着你听到了一个声音——一个你信任的人的声音。或者说，你现在依然信任他们。发生的一切并不是他们的错。你记得他们叫着你的名字，跑过来试图抓住你、帮助你，但已经太晚了。 他们提到了“贝尔温”这个名字，那就是你。你是贝尔温。 但是…… 什么你是吗？贝林究竟是什么？ 你再次试图在暗影中活动手指，但却做不到……因为感觉上你根本就没有手指。并不是有什么东西把它们压住了，而是你根本就没有手指可以活动。你的身体没有明确的轮廓、结构或界限，毫无形态可言。你并不处于某个暗影的虚空中——只是根本不存在而已。 至少，现在还不存在。你曾经是一位魔法师，能够运用世间的一切魔法力量，随心所欲地改变现实，让一切变得如你所愿。重塑自我将会是你有生以来完成得最轻松的任务：尽管你的记忆已经变得模糊不清，但你的智慧却从未如此敏锐过，你也从未像现在这样，如此深刻地感受到周围空间中弥漫着的魔力。感觉几乎什么事情都能做得到。

rows.original: You focus on your own memories, putting your focus into what it was that you were and to reconstruct yourself, piece by piece, in your mind’s eye. Your fingers, your toes, your arms, your legs. You remember your mother and your father; you remember your grandfather and the appreciation you had for him and the stories that surrounded him. You remember your lineage, and with it, some of the finer details come back to you: You remember that you had long, flowing hair, full of [silly|floof|body]; you had a tail, reaching down to your ankles and no less fluffy than your hair was; your arms and legs were covered in fur from the elbows and knees downward, ending in lupine features. Your dark skin contrasted sharply with the fine, white furs of your lupine features. You had piercing blue eyes; you had triangular ears. You remember your endowments. You remember... You have a hard time remembering what it was that you had for them. You remember it being something of a conscientious topic, both in your own thoughts and with the occasional conversation with others. Try as you might, a perfect image of yourself doesn’t form in your addled mind. You remember... you think that you remember that you had...
rows.translation: 你专注于自己的记忆，把心神放在你曾经是什么之上，在自己的脑海中一点一点地把自己重新拼凑起来。你的手指、你的脚趾、你的手臂、你的腿。你记得你的母亲和父亲；你记得你的祖父，记得你对他的敬重，以及围绕着祖父的那些故事。你记得自己的血脉传承，随之，一些更细微的细节也回到了你脑中： 你记得自己有一头长长的、飘逸的头发，满是[silly|绒毛|身体]；你有一条尾巴，垂到脚踝处，蓬松程度丝毫不逊于你的头发；你的手臂和腿从肘部和膝盖往下都覆着毛皮，末端是狼族的特征。你深色的皮肤与你狼族特征上那些细白的毛皮形成了鲜明的对比。你有锐利的蓝色眼睛；你有三角形的耳朵。 你记得自己的本钱。你记得…… 你很难记起自己拥有的究竟是哪一种。你记得这件事在自己的想法里，以及偶尔与他人的交谈中，都算是个需要认真对待的话题。 无论你怎么努力，你那混乱的脑海里都拼不出一个完美的自己。你记得……你觉得你记得自己曾经有……

rows.original: [berwyn.hasVagina |You remember... that you found the feminine form very attractive. And that your own form was very feminine itself: you have slender curves that led to a pronounced lower body; you have long, flowing, gorgeous hair; and you have a flawless complexion. And, biologically, nothing is more feminine than a vagina. You prided yourself on your appearances, you distinctly remember that, so you must have had one to go with your looks. But in this world, having both masculine and feminine sexes were a matter of uncommon genetics, or a little bit of alchemy. A person could have both a vagina and a penis. Did that apply to you? Did you have a penis as well? And if so, how large was it? |You remember... people often confusing you for a woman. Not that you could blame them: you have long, flowing, beautiful hair; slender curves leading to a plush lower body; and a flawless complexion. But you weren’t a woman. In fact, you prided yourself on your masculinity, even if the subject often came up in conversation. But you distinctly remember that you did not have a vagina. But if you didn’t have a vagina, then... you most certainly had a penis. You remember having sex. A lot of it. Most of it was just with yourself, but you did it a lot. All that’s left is for you to transpose yourself into this currently-empty shell of a form you’ve created. Your mind floats in the emptiness, separate from your body; both parts of you are soaked in what feels like unlimited ether, an infinite store of magic with which you could perform any feat you can think of. With the resources available to you, placing yourself within yourself is hardly going to be a challenge. All it takes is a little bit of willpower, and Berwyn will be reborn. That’s all it takes..."

rows.original: You[party.som | and Berwyn |, [comp1.name], and Berwyn | and your companions ] search the courtyard for any sign of Matiha – and instead, you find Elexis, her body made exhausted from the events in the tower. The skin of her body is pale and the scales on her arms and legs are bleached; the flame on her tail, previously a bright and healthy blue, is now a dim and smoldering dull red, barely emitting any light. The veins crisscrossing her body are still and silent, but so is the rest of her: her breath is shallow and her body is cold, clinging to what little life is left in it. You call Berwyn’s name, and he comes running, excited at the prospect that you may have found Matiha – and when he sees Elexis’ body, he recoils in surprise, his hands coming up to his chest defensively. You tell him that she’s still breathing, but she’s not in good shape, and you don’t know how long she’s going to last without help. "Well, what do you want me to do about it?" he asks, perhaps a bit indignantly, but his eyes turn to crescents with concern. "I’m not a healer; I specialize in summoning and I wanted to learn enchantments. I don’t know the first thing about healing magic. And even if I did!" he continues, animatedly pointing his finger at you, "why should we care? She tried to kill us! And before that, she tried to kill Matiha!" [pc.isDK |True. But if you healed her, then she’d owe you. And if you find Matiha, and she’s still alive, maybe you could have her make Elexis into your bodyguard instead. Berwyn’s eyes stay narrowed on yours, but he eventually lowers his hand. "Fine, do whatever," he says, almost vindictively. |You reply that you should help Elexis anyway because it’s the right thing to do. It’s not about her getting 'what she deserves;’ it’s about treating your fellow being with respect. And besides: she only did what Matiha told her to do because she was under Matiha’s control. You can hardly fault her for that. Berwyn lets out a long, low, frustrated sigh. "Fine, whatever," he says, crossing his arms. "Let’s keep playing 'Heroes,’ then." ] [party.has cait |Naturally, the second person you turn to is Cait. Her hands are on Elexis’ body, studying the veins and putting her ear to the salamander’s chest, listening for a heartbeat. "I normally specialize in injuries, some illnesses, and mental and emotional distress," she says, sounding a little more clinical than usual, "but I know a spell that I can at least try...." She does as she says, sitting on her knees and bringing her hands together in front of herself to cast a healing spell on Elexis’ body. The spell soaks into her skin... and seemingly evaporates, leaving no evidence that Cait had done anything at all. After a moment of you all watching Elexis for any improvement on her health, Cait sighs in dejection. "Whatever Matiha’s done to her, it’s pretty advanced," she admits. "Beyond what my teachings can do." |But it still begs the question: how are you going to help her? [pc.cl whitemage |You’re a healer, sure, but Elexis has no visible injuries, and whatever affliction is causing her veins and her skin to be like that are beyond your knowledge. |There’s nobody else in your party that could help you with Elexis and her affliction – not that you’d even know where to start. She has no visible injuries, and if it’s a disease that’s making her skin and her veins look like that, you’ve never seen a disease like it. ] In fact, off the top of your head, the only sort of person that could help Elexis in her predicament right now would be Matiha. ] You inspect Elexis’ body one final time, looking her over for anything that could maybe help you with her injuries, or, at the very least, help you properly diagnose what’s even wrong with her in the first place. As your eyes map out the dark veins on her body, you catch a glimpse of a speckled light clinging off her neck; when you investigate further, you find a necklace with a blue gemstone, and on the gemstone is an insignia that... you recognize, and you know from where: it’s the same design that you say on Astraea’s armor. "That looks like..." Berwyn says, kneeling down beside you as he investigate your finding, "a Waystone charm...?" When your thumb presses down on the gemstone, your fingers begin to tingle, and a dull, off-blue light emanates from its crystal surface. The feeling arcs up through your arm, making its way across your elbow and up to your shoulder. You yank it away before it gets to your neck, but you forget to open your hands: the charm’s straps snap off Elexis’ body with the yank. Only a moment later, the blue light envelops Elexis’ body, and in the next, in a blink of white light – she disappears entirely. Vanished into the ether, the only evidence that she existed at all being the squashed vegetation leaving an indent where her body once was. Yet, her Waystone charm remains in your hand.... You glance towards Berwyn, surprised at what had just happened, and he looks just as off-guard as you. "That looked like a teleportation spell," he says after a moment. "Similar to what Matiha had used to move the tower way back when. I’d... my guess is that it just sent Elexis back to wherever the charm is designed to send her to." [pc.isDK |Well. At least she isn’t your problem anymore. |Hopefully it’s somewhere where she can get the medical attention she needs.... ]
rows.translation: 你[party.som | 还有贝尔温 |， [comp1.name]以及贝尔温 | 以及你的同伴 ]你在院子里四处寻找玛蒂哈的踪迹，却发现了埃莱克西斯——她的身体因为塔楼里发生的事情而变得虚弱不堪。她的皮肤变得苍白，手臂和腿上的鳞片也褪去了颜色；她尾巴上的火焰，原本是明亮而健康的蓝色，如今却变成了暗淡而闷热的红色，几乎不再发出任何光芒。她体内的静脉交错纵横，却一片寂静；她的整个身体也处于同样的状态：呼吸微弱，身体冰冷，仅靠着那一丝残存的生机维持着生命。 你呼唤着贝尔温的名字，他兴奋地跑了过来，因为他以为你可能找到了玛蒂哈；而当看到埃莱克西斯的身体时，他震惊得后退了一步，双手本能地护在胸前。你告诉他，她还在呼吸，但情况很糟糕，你不知道如果没有帮助，她还能撑多久。 “那么，你希望我该怎么办呢？”他问道，语气中或许带着一丝不满，但他的眼神却充满了担忧。我不是治疗专家，我专精于召唤术，而且我想学习附魔技巧。我对治疗魔法一无所知。就算我懂一些……”他激动地用手指着你继续说道，“那我们为什么要在意呢？她试图杀死我们！而在那之前，她还想杀死玛蒂哈！ [pc.isDK |没错。但如果你治好了她，那么她就会欠你一个人情。而如果你找到了玛蒂哈，而且她还活着的话，或许可以让她帮助你让埃莱克西斯你的那就派保镖去吧。” 贝尔温的目光依然紧盯着你，但最终他还是放下了手。“好吧，随你便，”他说道，语气中似乎带着一丝报复的意味。 |你回答说，无论如何都应该帮助埃莱克西斯，因为这是正确的做法。这并不是为了让她“得到应得的报应”，而是为了尊重你的同类。更何况：她之所以会那么做，只是因为受到了玛蒂哈的控制。对于这一点，你几乎无法责怪她。 贝尔温长叹一声，显得十分沮丧。“好吧，随你便，”他说着，双臂交叉在胸前，“那我们就继续玩《英雄》吧。 ] [party.has cait |你自然而然地会首先向凯特寻求帮助。她将双手放在埃莱克西斯的身上，仔细观察他的脉搏，同时将耳朵贴在蝾螈的胸腔上，试图听出它的心跳声。“我平时主要治疗外伤、某些疾病以及心理情绪问题，”她说，语气比平时更加专业，“不过我知道有一种咒语，至少可以尝试一下。她言出必行，双膝跪地，双手在身前合十，为埃莱克西斯施展治愈法术。法术渗入她的皮肤……然后似乎又消失了，没有任何迹象表明凯特真的做了什么。 在大家期待着看到埃莱克西斯的健康状况有所好转的时候，凯特却沮丧地叹了口气。“不管玛蒂哈对她做了什么，那些伤害已经非常严重了，”她承认道，“超出了我的治疗能力所能解决的范围。 |但这仍然引出了一个问题：如何你打算帮助她吗？ [pc.cl whitemage |你确实是一名治疗者，但埃莱克西斯并没有明显的伤势，而那种导致她的血管和皮肤出现这种状况的疾病，显然超出了你的认知范围。 |在你的队伍中，没有其他人能够帮助你解决埃莱克西斯和她所面临的困境——更何况你甚至不知道该从哪里开始着手。她并没有明显的伤痕，如果真的是某种疾病导致了她皮肤和静脉出现这样的变化，那么你肯定从未见过这种病症。 ]事实上，立刻就能想到，在目前这种情况下，唯一能够帮助埃莱克西斯的人就是玛蒂哈了。 ] 你再次仔细检查了埃莱克西斯的身体，试图找到任何可能有助于治疗她伤势的线索，或者至少能帮助你准确判断她到底患了什么病。当你的目光扫过她身上那些暗色的静脉时，你注意到她的脖子上有一颗闪烁着微光的小宝石；进一步仔细观察后，你发现那是一条镶嵌着蓝色宝石的项链，而那颗宝石上还刻着某种标志。你认出了它，也知道它来自哪里：这就是你在阿斯特莱娅的护甲上看到过的那种设计。 那看起来像是……”贝尔温跪在你身旁，仔细观察你的发现，说道，“一块路石护符吗？” 当你用拇指按压那颗宝石时，手指开始发麻，宝石的水晶表面散发出一种暗淡的蓝光。这种感觉顺着你的手臂向上蔓延，穿过肘部，直达肩膀。你在光线到达颈部之前迅速将宝石拿开，却忘了松开手——随着这个动作，护身符的带子从埃莱克西斯身上脱落了。 仅仅片刻之后，蓝光便笼罩了埃莱克西斯的身体，紧接着，在一道白轻型的闪现中——她彻底消失了。她仿佛融入了虚无之中，唯一能证明她曾经存在过的痕迹，只有那些被压坏的植物，它们在她的身体曾经所在的地方留下了凹痕。然而，她留下的那块“道路之石”却仍然掌握在你的手中…… 你朝贝尔温的方向瞥去，对刚刚发生的事情感到十分惊讶，而他看起来也同样措手不及。 “那看起来像是一种传送魔法，”过了一会儿，他说，“和玛蒂哈以前用来移动那座塔的那种魔法很相似。我猜……那应该就是把埃莱克西斯送回了那个魔法咒语原本打算把她送到的地方吧。 [pc.isDK |嗯，至少她不再是你需要解决的问题了。 |希望她能在某个能够得到所需医疗救助的地方…… ]
rows.raw: ' You[party.som | and Berwyn |, [comp1.name], and Berwyn | and your companions ] search the courtyard for any sign of Matiha – and instead, you find Elexis, her body made exhausted from the events in the tower. The skin of her body is pale and the scales on her arms and legs are bleached; the flame on her tail, previously a bright and healthy blue, is now a dim and smoldering dull red, barely emitting any light. The veins crisscrossing her body are still and silent, but so is the rest of her: her breath is shallow and her body is cold, clinging to what little life is left in it. You call Berwyn’s name, and he comes running, excited at the prospect that you may have found Matiha – and when he sees Elexis’ body, he recoils in surprise, his hands coming up to his chest defensively. You tell him that she’s still breathing, but she’s not in good shape, and you don’t know how long she’s going to last without help. "Well, what do you want me to do about it?" he asks, perhaps a bit indignantly, but his eyes turn to crescents with concern. "I’m not a healer; I specialize in summoning and I wanted to learn enchantments. I don’t know the first thing about healing magic. And even if I did!" he continues, animatedly pointing his finger at you, "why should we care? She tried to kill us! And before that, she tried to kill Matiha!" [pc.isDK |True. But if you healed her, then she’d owe you. And if you find Matiha, and she’s still alive, maybe you could have her make Elexis into your bodyguard instead. Berwyn’s eyes stay narrowed on yours, but he eventually lowers his hand. "Fine, do whatever," he says, almost vindictively. |You reply that you should help Elexis anyway because it’s the right thing to do. It’s not about her getting 'what she deserves;’ it’s about treating your fellow being with respect. And besides: she only did what Matiha told her to do because she was under Matiha’s control. You can hardly fault her for that. Berwyn lets out a long, low, frustrated sigh. "Fine, whatever," he says, crossing his arms. "Let’s keep playing 'Heroes,’ then." ] [party.has cait |Naturally, the second person you turn to is Cait. Her hands are on Elexis’ body, studying the veins and putting her ear to the salamander’s chest, listening for a heartbeat. "I normally specialize in injuries, some illnesses, and mental and emotional distress," she says, sounding a little more clinical than usual, "but I know a spell that I can at least try...." She does as she says, sitting on her knees and bringing her hands together in front of herself to cast a healing spell on Elexis’ body. The spell soaks into her skin... and seemingly evaporates, leaving no evidence that Cait had done anything at all. After a moment of you all watching Elexis for any improvement on her health, Cait sighs in dejection. "Whatever Matiha’s done to her, it’s pretty advanced," she admits. "Beyond what my teachings can do." |But it still begs the question: how are you going to help her? [pc.cl whitemage |You’re a healer, sure, but Elexis has no visible injuries, and whatever affliction is causing her veins and her skin to be like that are beyond your knowledge. |There’s nobody else in your party that could help you with Elexis and her affliction – not that you’d even know where to start. She has no visible injuries, and if it’s a disease that’s making her skin and her veins look like that, you’ve never seen a disease like it. ] In fact, off the top of your head, the only sort of person that could help Elexis in her predicament right now would be Matiha. ] You inspect Elexis’ body one final time, looking her over for anything that could maybe help you with her injuries, or, at the very least, help you properly diagnose what’s even wrong with her in the first place. As your eyes map out the dark veins on her body, you catch a glimpse of a speckled light clinging off her neck; when you investigate further, you find a necklace with a blue gemstone, and on the gemstone is an insignia that... you recognize, and you know from where: it’s the same design that you say on Astraea’s armor. "That looks like..." Berwyn says, kneeling down beside you as he investigate your finding, "a Waystone charm...?" When your thumb presses down on the gemstone, your fingers begin to tingle, and a dull, off-blue light emanates from its crystal surface. The feeling arcs up through your arm, making its way across your elbow and up to your shoulder. You yank it away before it gets to your neck, but you forget to open your hands: the charm’s straps snap off Elexis’ body with the yank. Only a moment later, the blue light envelops Elexis’ body, and in the next, in a blink of white light – she disappears entirely. Vanished into the ether, the only evidence that she existed at all being the squashed vegetation leaving an indent where her body once was. Yet, her Waystone charm remains in your hand.... You glance towards Berwyn, surprised at what had just happened, and he looks just as off-guard as you. "That looked like a teleportation spell," he says after a moment. "Similar to what Matiha had used to move the tower way back when. I’d... my guess is that it just sent Elexis back to wherever the charm is designed to send her to." [pc.isDK |Well. At least she isn’t your problem anymore. |Hopefully it’s somewhere where she can get the medical attention she needs.... ]'

rows.original: With Elexis and her fate resolved, you[party.som | and Berwyn |, [comp1.name], and Berwyn | and your companions ] return to your initial goal of locating Matiha – and it isn’t too long until you find her. She’s wrapped in a tangle of the ivy weeds permeating the yard, just as unconscious as Berwyn was when you found him. You do another once-over of her body for any injuries and, like Berwyn before her, she appears to be fine: her breathing and heart rate are normal and she has no obvious external injuries. What’s more, her skin had reverted to how you remember her from your first encounter with her: pale and uniform all throughout, without any of the pulsating green lights flowing throughout her veins. Whatever was in her system before seems to have been excised. And, on top of that, she’s fully dressed in the same witch’s outfit that you remember her in – and her enormous hat is easy to find among the weeds. However, she doesn’t regain consciousness nearly as quickly as Berwyn had. Once you pull her from the ivy vines and lay her on the cobblestone path of the courtyard, she remains sound asleep, totally undisturbed from all the movement. She occasionally moans and whimpers, as if she’s having a bad dream, and her eyes constantly flit and move underneath her eyelids. You ask Berwyn if he knew her to be a particularly heavy sleeper. "Yes, actually," he answers. "I’m not much of a morning person myself, but if I woke up before she did, it was a challenge and a half to get her to open her eyes, much less roll her out of bed." Now that she’s here, though, her body splayed on the ground in front of you, the obvious question hangs in the air like a mace in an alchemy shop: what now? Berwyn chews on his lips as his eyes stay on Matiha’s body, with his eyes narrowed in concentration. It’s clear from his expression that the question is hanging heavily on his mind, and that he isn’t sure what it is that he wants. You ask him what’s on his mind. "Nothing," he lies. [pc.dcb |You sigh impatiently and tell him that now, of all times, is not the time for bullshit. |You say nothing in response. He knows you know he’s lying. He’ll tell you when he’s good and ready. |"Oh, okay," you reply. Guess you were wrong. ] Berwyn takes a long, deep sigh, in through his nose and out through his mouth. "Matiha," he starts slowly, sounding out the syllables as he tries to put his thoughts to words, "is... an important person to me, [pc.name]." He pauses, carefully mapping out his next sentence in his head. "For all the bad that she’s done recently, and for all the insanity that rune had given her... she was my teacher. She encouraged me to pursue my passions. She... well, she wanted me in conjuring, and I wanted to learn enchantments, but all the same, I know what I know because of her, and I know how to progress from here." Berwyn removes his hat, putting its brim against his chest. "I wouldn’t be who I am now because of her. I wouldn’t be here because of her. And, like," he hesitates, glancing around where he is, "where I am, right here and now, this sucks, but... it was either live the life I am now, or I’d still be on my parent’s vineyard, stomping on grapes to make wine or something." After everything that’s happened – the teleporting tower, the meeting with Astraea, the journey through the transforming fortress, and the culminating battle with... whatever Matiha had transformed into – you ask him if this is the life he had wanted to live. Berwyn’s eyes stay on Matiha for a long moment as he considers the question. "In a way?" he asks, his eyes lifting from hers to yours – and a slight smile spreads across his lips. "Yeah, it is. My grandfather was a battlemage, and I’d always heard such amazing stories about the adventures that he had. I wanted to live that for myself. I wanted to have a story or two of my own to tell someone. And after all of that? Everything that we’ve been through?" He smiles wider – a genuine, enthusiastic smile that displays his teeth. "By Nareva, there isn’t a bard in the world that would believe me." The silence hangs in the air between you two for another moment as he recollects himself. "I care about Matiha, [pc.name]," he says eventually, stopping just short of admitting something stronger. "If I were... a little more selfish than I am right now, I know what I’d like to do with Matiha now that she’s not crazy and hopped-up on the unlimited power of a weird enchanted rock." His brow furrows. "Presumably." But he stops short of saying what it is his heart wants for him to do. His mouth hangs open, but the words won’t come out. Maybe what he wants is selfish. "But maybe... this isn’t the woman that I cared about before," he eventually continues, chewing through his words. "Maybe this isn’t the same Matiha." His eyes turn to yours, gently moistening along their bottoms. "Way back when, I came to you for help. Matiha... she was turning into someone I didn’t recognize. Someone I didn’t like. And you were the first person I could think of that could help me with her." He chokes through a single laugh. "And I’m very lucky that you did. I accepted this damn journey from the beginning not because I cared about Matiha sucking the magic out of Savarra or because some Astrida cultist asked me to, but because I... I wanted Matiha back. And now that she’s here..." Berwyn casts his eyes back down to Matiha’s comatose body sadly. "What if... what if she’s not back? What if she’s still crazy? What... what if... she wakes up, and she’s mad that we broke that rune, or that we had put a stop to her crazy plan to suck Savarra into the Ways Between? I mean, she wielded a lot of power, thanks to that rock, and I had lost her for a long time – what if she doesn’t forgive me?" He stops his ranting, standing over Matiha with his hat still against his chest. He takes another deep sigh, in through his nose and out through his mouth, as he wrestles with the questions he had just asked. It’s clear that he’s waiting for a second opinion. On the one hand, he could try and speak with Matiha – whether she was crazy on infinite power or not, she still had Berwyn on her mind, given how badly she wanted him to join her, even after she turned into that flesh monstrosity. On the other, maybe he could be convinced to let Matiha go. She’s a threat, after all. And you know of a fellow witch that could help in looking after her: someone with the magical chops to keep Matiha in line, for lack of a better term. [var0|There’s a third option as well: you could send Matiha to the Wayfort. You’d be in need of a witch of Matiha’s aptitude for your court, and it’s better that she stays with you than leaving her to the elements.]
rows.translation: 在解决了埃莱克西斯及其命运的问题之后，你[party.som | 还有贝尔温 |， [comp1.name]以及贝尔温 | 以及你的同伴 ]回到你最初的目标——找到玛蒂哈吧，不久之后你就能找到她。她被蔓延在院子里的常春藤缠绕着，就像你找到贝尔温时他一样处于昏迷状态。 你再次检查她的身体，看看是否有任何受伤的痕迹。和之前的贝尔温一样，她看起来也没有什么问题：她的呼吸和心率都很正常，也没有任何明显的外伤。更重要的是，她的皮肤已经恢复到了你第一次见到她时的样子：整个皮肤呈现出均匀的苍白色调，血管中也没有那种闪烁的绿色光芒了。她体内之前存在的那些东西似乎已经被彻底清除掉了。而且，她现在穿着的正是你们记忆中她所穿的那一套女巫服装——她那顶巨大的帽子在杂草丛中也很容易被找到。 然而，她恢复意识的速度却远不如贝尔温那么快。当你把她从常春藤丛中拉出来，放在庭院的鹅卵石小路上时，她依然处于沉睡状态，所有这些动作丝毫没有打扰到她。她偶尔会发出呻吟声，仿佛正在做噩梦，她的眼皮也在不停地颤动。 你问贝尔温是否知道她睡觉特别沉。他回答说：“其实知道。我自己也不是早起型的人，但如果我在她之前醒了，想要让她睁开眼睛简直就是件困难的事，更别提让她从床上爬起来了。 然而，现在她已经躺在了你面前的地上，这个显而易见的问题就像炼金术店里悬挂着的重锤一样悬在空气中：接下来该怎么办？ 贝尔温紧咬着嘴唇，目光始终盯着玛蒂哈的尸体，眉头紧锁，显得十分专注。从他的表情可以看出，这个问题在他心中占据了很重要的位置，而他自己也不清楚应该怎么做。他你问他在想什么。 “没什么，”他撒了个谎。 [pc.dcb |你不耐烦地叹了口气，告诉他：现在，绝对不是说废话的时候。 |你没有作出任何回应。他知道你明白他在撒谎。等他准备好了，他会告诉你的。 |哦，好吧，”你回答道。看来你错了。 ] 贝尔温深深地吸了一口气，从鼻子吸气，然后从嘴巴呼出。“玛蒂哈，”他缓缓开口，逐个念出每个音节，努力将自己的思绪用语言表达出来，“她对我来说……是一个非常重要的人。 [pc.name]他停顿了一下，在脑海中仔细构思着接下来要说的话。“尽管她最近做了很多坏事，也尽管那些符文让她变得如此疯狂……但她曾经是我的老师。是她鼓励我去追求自己的梦想。她……嗯，她希望我参与魔法研究，而我也想学习各种咒语。不过，正因为她，我才掌握了现在的知识，也知道接下来该怎么做。 贝林摘下帽子，将帽檐抵在胸前。如果没有她，我就不会成为现在的我。也不会来到这里。而且，”他犹豫了一下，环顾四周，“就是现在，我所处的这个位置，也是因为她。太糟糕了但是……要么就继续过我现在这样的生活，要么就会还在父母的葡萄园里，踩葡萄来酿酒之类的。” 在经历了所有这些事情之后——传送塔、与阿斯特莱娅的会面、穿过那座不断变化的堡垒，以及最终与的那场战斗…… 无论什么玛蒂哈已经发生了改变——你可以问他，这是否就是他想要过的生活。 贝尔温久久地注视着玛蒂哈，思考着这个问题。他问道：“在某种程度上吧？”他的目光从玛蒂哈身上移开，转向了你，嘴角浮现出一丝微笑。“是的，就是这样的。我的祖父是一名战斗法师，我从小就听人们谈论他太棒了那些关于他所经历的冒险的故事。我也想亲自体验那些经历，我也想拥有属于自己的故事，可以讲给别人听。而经历了这一切之后……经历了我们共同经历的一切之后，”他笑得更开了——那是一种真诚而热情的微笑，他的牙齿都露了出来，“以娜瑞瓦之名，这个世界上没有任何一位吟游诗人会相信我的故事。” 在他回过神来之后，两人之间的空气中又陷入了短暂的沉默。“我在乎玛蒂哈，”他继续说道。 [pc.name]，”如果我……比现在更自私一些，”他最终说道，却始终没有说出更直接的话。“我知道，现在玛蒂哈不再因为那块拥有神奇魔力的石头而变得疯狂、失去理智，我该怎么做。”他的眉头紧锁，“大概吧。” 但他最终还是没有说出口，心里真正想要他去做的那件事。他的嘴张开着，却始终说不出那些话。也许，他真正想要的是自私。 “但也许……这个不是那个我曾经在乎的女人，”他最终继续说道，话语中带着一丝迟疑，“也许现在的她已经不是原来的玛蒂哈了。” 他的目光转向你，眼眶里渐渐泛起湿润。“很久以前，我曾经向你寻求帮助。玛蒂哈……她正在变成一个我完全认不出来的人，一个我并不喜欢的人。而你，是第一个让我想到能帮助我应对这种情况的人。”他勉强挤出一丝笑声，“能得到你的帮助，我真的非常幸运。从一开始，我就接受了这段该死的旅程，并不是因为我在意玛蒂哈从萨瓦拉身上吸取魔法，也不是因为某个阿斯特里达教徒的要求，而是因为我……我想让玛蒂哈回到我身边。而现在，她终于回来了。贝尔温悲伤地再次低头看向玛蒂哈那处于昏迷状态的身体。“要是……要是她真的不是回去？要是她还是疯着呢？要是……她醒过来后，因为我们破坏了那个符文，或者因为我们阻止了她将萨瓦拉吸入“幽冥之路”的疯狂计划而生气怎么办？我的意思是，她可是掌握着那个力量啊很多因为那块石头，我获得了力量，但却因此与她失去了联系……如果她不肯原谅我该怎么办呢？ 他停止了 ranting，站在玛蒂哈旁边，帽子仍然紧贴着胸前。他再次深深地吸了一口气，通过鼻子吸气，然后通过嘴巴呼气，同时一直在思考自己刚才提出的那些问题。 很明显，他在等待第二种意见。 一方面，他可以试着和玛蒂哈谈谈——无论她是否因为获得了无限力量而变得疯狂，她依然非常在意贝尔温，甚至在她变成了那个肉体怪物之后，依然如此迫切地希望他能够加入自己。 另一方面，或许可以说服他放走玛蒂哈。毕竟，她确实是个威胁。而且你知道有位女巫可以帮助照看她——那位女巫拥有足够的魔法力量，能让玛蒂哈守规矩，至少可以说是这样。 [var0|还有第三种选择：你可以把玛蒂哈送到荒废驿堡去。你的宫廷需要像玛蒂哈这样有能力的女巫，让她留在你身边总比让她暴露在危险环境中要好。]
rows.raw: ' With Elexis and her fate resolved, you[party.som | and Berwyn |, [comp1.name], and Berwyn | and your companions ] return to your initial goal of locating Matiha – and it isn’t too long until you find her. She’s wrapped in a tangle of the ivy weeds permeating the yard, just as unconscious as Berwyn was when you found him. You do another once-over of her body for any injuries and, like Berwyn before her, she appears to be fine: her breathing and heart rate are normal and she has no obvious external injuries. What’s more, her skin had reverted to how you remember her from your first encounter with her: pale and uniform all throughout, without any of the pulsating green lights flowing throughout her veins. Whatever was in her system before seems to have been excised. And, on top of that, she’s fully dressed in the same witch’s outfit that you remember her in – and her enormous hat is easy to find among the weeds. However, she doesn’t regain consciousness nearly as quickly as Berwyn had. Once you pull her from the ivy vines and lay her on the cobblestone path of the courtyard, she remains sound asleep, totally undisturbed from all the movement. She occasionally moans and whimpers, as if she’s having a bad dream, and her eyes constantly flit and move underneath her eyelids. You ask Berwyn if he knew her to be a particularly heavy sleeper. "Yes, actually," he answers. "I’m not much of a morning person myself, but if I woke up before she did, it was a challenge and a half to get her to open her eyes, much less roll her out of bed." Now that she’s here, though, her body splayed on the ground in front of you, the obvious question hangs in the air like a mace in an alchemy shop: what now? Berwyn chews on his lips as his eyes stay on Matiha’s body, with his eyes narrowed in concentration. It’s clear from his expression that the question is hanging heavily on his mind, and that he isn’t sure what it is that he wants. You ask him what’s on his mind. "Nothing," he lies. [pc.dcb |You sigh impatiently and tell him that now, of all times, is not the time for bullshit. |You say nothing in response. He knows you know he’s lying. He’ll tell you when he’s good and ready. |"Oh, okay," you reply. Guess you were wrong. ] Berwyn takes a long, deep sigh, in through his nose and out through his mouth. "Matiha," he starts slowly, sounding out the syllables as he tries to put his thoughts to words, "is... an important person to me, [pc.name]." He pauses, carefully mapping out his next sentence in his head. "For all the bad that she’s done recently, and for all the insanity that rune had given her... she was my teacher. She encouraged me to pursue my passions. She... well, she wanted me in conjuring, and I wanted to learn enchantments, but all the same, I know what I know because of her, and I know how to progress from here." Berwyn removes his hat, putting its brim against his chest. "I wouldn’t be who I am now because of her. I wouldn’t be here because of her. And, like," he hesitates, glancing around where he is, "where I am, right here and now, this sucks, but... it was either live the life I am now, or I’d still be on my parent’s vineyard, stomping on grapes to make wine or something." After everything that’s happened – the teleporting tower, the meeting with Astraea, the journey through the transforming fortress, and the culminating battle with... whatever Matiha had transformed into – you ask him if this is the life he had wanted to live. Berwyn’s eyes stay on Matiha for a long moment as he considers the question. "In a way?" he asks, his eyes lifting from hers to yours – and a slight smile spreads across his lips. "Yeah, it is. My grandfather was a battlemage, and I’d always heard such amazing stories about the adventures that he had. I wanted to live that for myself. I wanted to have a story or two of my own to tell someone. And after all of that? Everything that we’ve been through?" He smiles wider – a genuine, enthusiastic smile that displays his teeth. "By Nareva, there isn’t a bard in the world that would believe me." The silence hangs in the air between you two for another moment as he recollects himself. "I care about Matiha, [pc.name]," he says eventually, stopping just short of admitting something stronger. "If I were... a little more selfish than I am right now, I know what I’d like to do with Matiha now that she’s not crazy and hopped-up on the unlimited power of a weird enchanted rock." His brow furrows. "Presumably." But he stops short of saying what it is his heart wants for him to do. His mouth hangs open, but the words won’t come out. Maybe what he wants is selfish. "But maybe... this isn’t the woman that I cared about before," he eventually continues, chewing through his words. "Maybe this isn’t the same Matiha." His eyes turn to yours, gently moistening along their bottoms. "Way back when, I came to you for help. Matiha... she was turning into someone I didn’t recognize. Someone I didn’t like. And you were the first person I could think of that could help me with her." He chokes through a single laugh. "And I’m very lucky that you did. I accepted this damn journey from the beginning not because I cared about Matiha sucking the magic out of Savarra or because some Astrida cultist asked me to, but because I... I wanted Matiha back. And now that she’s here..." Berwyn casts his eyes back down to Matiha’s comatose body sadly. "What if... what if she’s not back? What if she’s still crazy? What... what if... she wakes up, and she’s mad that we broke that rune, or that we had put a stop to her crazy plan to suck Savarra into the Ways Between? I mean, she wielded a lot of power, thanks to that rock, and I had lost her for a long time – what if she doesn’t forgive me?" He stops his ranting, standing over Matiha with his hat still against his chest. He takes another deep sigh, in through his nose and out through his mouth, as he wrestles with the questions he had just asked. It’s clear that he’s waiting for a second opinion. On the one hand, he could try and speak with Matiha – whether she was crazy on infinite power or not, she still had Berwyn on her mind, given how badly she wanted him to join her, even after she turned into that flesh monstrosity. On the other, maybe he could be convinced to let Matiha go. She’s a threat, after all. And you know of a fellow witch that could help in looking after her: someone with the magical chops to keep Matiha in line, for lack of a better term. [var0|There’s a third option as well: you could send Matiha to the Wayfort. You’d be in need of a witch of Matiha’s aptitude for your court, and it’s better that she stays with you than leaving her to the elements.]'

rows.original: Maybe he didn’t realize it in the excitement of the moments, but from the second you two had met Matiha in her office and from the first few sentences she spoke, there was one thing that was made obvious to you: it’s that she cares about Berwyn, too. She was borderline begging him to stay with her, to rejoin her and her studies, and she wanted him to be a part of her grand, master plan, as insane as it was. Even when she was a big, gross, undulating flesh-monster, all she wanted was for Berwyn to be a part of what she had. Berwyn visibly shudders at the thought of 'being a part’ of that. Yes, you admit that it’s not a pleasant thought, but he’s thinking about it on a surface level. Matiha’s one wish was to be with him. Maybe that was bullshit, and she was trying to get him to stay with her so she could suck the Essence out of him or abuse his 'potential’ or whatever – but maybe it wasn’t. Maybe she was sincere. Berwyn pauses, absorbing the words that you’re saying. The only times you ever see him this focused and determined are when he’s nose-deep in his studies. "Do you really think so?" he eventually asks, his voice rising an octave – you’ve only said a few sentences, but you’ve already given him hope, and he wants to believe in it. You reason that if Matiha were really so far gone that she wanted him back for purely selfish reasons, she probably wouldn’t have jumped on that rune when he made it fracture. He would have been the first one in the blast if she hadn’t. "I... well...," he stutters, his mouth moving but his words not coming out. "I probably would have survived that blast, but..." Berwyn’s tail swishes once behind himself. It was a slight motion, but it was enough to catch your eye. "Maybe... maybe you’re right. Maybe the Matiha I knew is still in there." There’s only one way to find out. You simply need to wait until she wakes up.
rows.translation: 也许在那些激动人心的时刻里，他并没有意识到这一点，但从你们俩在玛蒂哈的办公室见面那一刻起，从她说的第一句话开始，就有那么一点变得显而易见：她也在关心贝尔温。她几乎是在恳求他留在她身边，重新加入她的生活和学习中，她希望他能成为她那个宏伟计划的一部分，无论这个计划听起来有多疯狂。即使在她变成那个庞大、丑陋、不断变形的肉块怪物时，她所想要的也只是让贝尔温成为她生活中的一部分。 一想到要“成为其中的一部分”，贝尔温明显地感到一阵战栗。 没错，你得承认这个想法并不愉快，但他只是表面上的思考而已。玛蒂哈唯一的愿望就是能和他在一起。也许那只是谎言，她只是想让他留在自己身边，这样就能从他身上吸取精华，或者利用他的“潜力”之类的——但也许并非如此。也许她是真心的。 贝尔温停下了动作，认真地听着你所说的话。只有在他全神贯注地学习的时候，你才会看到他如此专注和坚定。“你真的这么认为吗？”他最终问道，声音提高了八度——你只说了短短几句话，但却给了他希望，而他真的很想相信这一点。 你认为，如果玛蒂哈真的已经变得如此自私，以至于仅仅出于私心才想要他回来，那么当他的符文断裂时，她应该不会立刻抓住那个符文。如果她没有那么做，他反而会第一个受到爆炸的伤害。 “我……嗯……”他结结巴巴地说，嘴巴在动，但话却说不出来。“我大概吧本应该能在那场爆炸中活下来的，但是……” 贝尔温的尾巴在身后轻轻摆动了一下。这个动作很微小，但却足以吸引人们的注意。“也许……也许你是对的。也许我曾经认识的玛蒂哈还在那里。” 只有一种方法可以弄清楚真相。你只需要等待她醒来就行了。

rows.original:
The seconds tick by without Matiha stirring too much in her sleep. Given what she had gone through and the transformation she had endured, she’s probably exhausted – who knows if she had even gotten any sleep ever since the powers of that rune stone began to seep into her?

                    Berwyn, for his part, is patient enough to not disturb her, but from the constant wagging of his tail and the occasional flick of one of his ears whenever she makes a noise, can hardly wait for her to wake up. Hopefully he has the discipline to not immediately bombard her with questions about her sanity as soon as she does.
                    
                    That gives you an idea, though: Matiha’s been through a lot with the fortress and the rune stone, but it wasn’t exactly a walk in the park for Berwyn. There have been a few questions bouncing around in your head ever since you found yourself in the fortress’s courtyard again, and now’s as good a time as any to ask them. And besides – he looks like he could use the distraction.
rows.translation:
时间一分一秒地过去，而玛蒂哈在睡梦中却丝毫没有动静。考虑到她所经历的一切以及所经历的那些变化，她恐怕已经精疲力竭了——谁知道自从那块符文石的力量开始渗入她的身体之后，她是否还有机会真正入睡过呢？

                    对于贝尔温来说，他很有耐心，不会去打扰她，但每当她发出声音时，他那不断摇动的尾巴以及偶尔抽动的耳朵，都清楚地表明他其实迫不及待地想看到她醒来。希望等她真正醒来的时候，他能有足够的自制力，不会立刻就她的状态提出一连串的问题。
                    
                    不过，这应该能让你有所了解：玛蒂哈在处理那座堡垒和那块符文石的过程中经历了许多艰难险阻，而对贝尔温来说，这件事也同样不是一件容易的事。自从你再次来到那座堡垒的庭院里，你心中肯定有一些疑问，现在正是提出这些疑问的好时机。而且，他看起来确实需要这样的分散注意力的事情来打发时间。

rows.original: During your encounter with Matiha and your exploration through the fortress, there’s one thing that’s totally, abundantly clear to you: Berwyn never left her thoughts. Maybe she was trying to goad him into staying for her own selfish reasons – but maybe she wasn’t.
rows.translation: 在与你与玛蒂哈的相遇以及你对这座堡垒的探索过程中，有那么一件事你完全清楚地意识到了：贝尔温从未离开过她的脑海。也许她只是出于自私的动机，想要刺激他留下来——但也许并非如此。
rows.raw: "During your encounter with Matiha and your exploration through the fortress, there’s one thing that’s totally, abundantly clear to you: Berwyn never left her thoughts. Maybe she was trying to goad him into staying for her own selfish reasons – but maybe she wasn’t."

rows.original: If Berwyn is so concerned about Matiha and how she’ll react towards him when she wakes up, then... in all honesty, it may be for the best for both of them if she’s sent away before she does. It’d be tough for Berwyn to go through that a second time, and his fears aren’t totally unfounded: she may try to take advantage of him a second time. Who knows how powerful she’ll be when she wakes up? "Yeah," he sighs dejectedly, his shoulders slumping. He knew that this was the advice that you could have given him, but he still hoped that it wasn’t. That said, rather than just cast her to the wastes and wash your hands of her forever, there’s an alternative: you’re the proprietor of a certain fort that was built on the road between Hawkethorne and the Winter City... "You’re suggesting we move Matiha to the Wayfort?" he asks, and you confirm. It’s a fairly tame location, at least by Matiha’s standards: there isn’t a lot that she can use there to practice her magic and become another threat, but she’ll also be close enough to home that, if he ever changes his mind and wants to visit her, she won’t be too long of a walk away. And the longer you’ve been going on your journey, the more and more populated it’s become, so it’s not like she’ll be wanting for company. "Don’t try to sugarcoat this," he snaps. "You want her displaced and thrown into an open-air prison with a bunch of other freaks and weirdos. And let’s make one thing clear," he says, pointing his finger at you accusatorily, "Matiha isn’t a freak." You ask him if he has any better ideas. He asked for your opinion, and you gave it. He stops, his fingers clenching into tight fists as he considers your words. Eventually, he lets out a frustrated, almost pained grunt, letting his hands fall to his sides again. "You do it," he says. "There’s a Waystone just outside the fortress’ walls. Use it to take her to the fort. Don’t make me do this to her." It’s the least you could do. Matiha doesn’t stir when you hoist her onto your shoulders, carrying her piggyback out of the fortress’s boundaries.
rows.translation: 如果贝尔温如此担心玛蒂哈醒来后会怎样对待他，那么……说实话，趁她还没醒就把她送走，或许对他们俩都是最好的选择。贝尔温很难再承受一次那样的事，而他的担忧也并非毫无根据：她或许会再次利用他。谁知道她醒来时会有多强大？ “是啊。”他沮丧地叹了口气，双肩垂了下来。他知道你可能会给出这个建议，却仍希望你不会这么说。 不过，你们也不必把她扔进荒野、从此撒手不管；还有另一种选择：你拥有一座坐落在鹰棘镇与冬城之间道路上的驿堡…… “你是说，把玛蒂哈送到驿堡去？”他问道，你予以确认。至少以玛蒂哈的标准来看，那里相当平静：没有多少东西能让她拿来修习魔法、再次成为威胁；同时，那里离家也足够近，倘若他日后改变心意、想去看望她，也不必走太远。而且随着你的旅程不断推进，驿堡里的人越来越多，她也不会缺少陪伴。 “别粉饰这件事，”他厉声说道，“你就是想把她赶走，扔进一个露天监狱，和一群怪胎、怪人关在一起。还有一件事得说清楚，”他伸出手指，责难地指向你，“玛蒂哈不是怪胎。” 你问他有没有更好的主意。是他征求你的意见，而你已经给出了答案。 他沉默下来，思量着你的话，双手紧紧攥成拳头。最终，他发出一声挫败而近乎痛苦的低吼，再次将手垂到身侧。“你来做，”他说，“要塞城墙外就有一座道标石。用它把她带到驿堡去。别让我亲手这样对她。” 这是你至少能为他做的事。你把玛蒂哈架到肩上，背着她走出要塞的范围时，她始终没有醒来。

"You want her displaced and thrown into an open-air prison with a bunch of other freaks and weirdos. And let’s make one thing clear," he says, pointing his finger at you accusatorily, "Matiha isn’t a freak." You ask him if he has any better ideas. He asked for your opinion, and you gave it. He stops, his fingers clenching into tight fists as he considers your words. Eventually, he lets out a frustrated, almost pained grunt, letting his hands fall to his sides again. "You do it," he says. "There’s a Waystone just outside the fortress’ walls. Use it to take her to the fort. Don’t make me do this to her." It’s the least you could do. Matiha doesn’t stir when you hoist her onto your shoulders, carrying her piggyback out of the fortress’s boundaries.'

rows.original:
The Waystone you had used to find the fortress in the Ways Between was only a dozen paces or so from the front entrance of the fortress.

                    You only need one hand to activate your Waystone charm and locate the Wayfort... but when your hand reaches into your pocket, where you normally keep your stone, your fingernails clink against two distinct charms. You realize, with a start, that you still have Elexis’ charm in your pocket.
                    
                    You pull them both out to examine them. Thankfully, they’re distinct from each other: yours is rather plain all around, while Elexis’ charm has a number of etchings and engravings across hers. Perhaps it’s some ancient script involving whatever language they speak in Tychris.
                    
                    You could go straight to Tychris from here. Or, more importantly, you could send Matiha to Tychris – Nareva had sent two of her best magehunters for her, and they had both failed. You could complete Astraea’s mission for her. And as much as Berwyn is attached to Matiha and wants the best for her, she is, all the same, a wanted criminal.
                    
                    You’d be going behind Berwyn’s back if you did this, but sending Matiha to Tychris would be justice. And you’d probably get a lot of points with the Astrida Order if you did it.
                    
                    Do you keep to the original plan and send Matiha to the Wayfort? Or do you send her to Tychris to be tried for her crimes?
rows.translation:
你之前用来在“道路之间”找到那座堡垒的引路石，其实距离堡垒的正门只有十几步的距离。

                    你只需要用一只手就能激活引路石的魔法，从而找到那座堡垒的位置……但当你的手伸进口袋——那里通常放着那块引路石时，你的指甲碰到了另外两件饰品。你顿时意识到，口袋里其实还装着埃莱克西斯的那件饰品。
                    
                    你把它们都拿出来仔细观察。幸运的是，它们是截然不同的：你的那个整体上看起来相当朴素，而埃莱克西斯的那枚上面则有许多雕刻和纹饰。或许这些纹饰代表着某种古老的文字，与他们在提克里斯使用的语言有关。
                    
                    你可以直接从这里前往提克里斯。或者，更重要的是，你可以派玛蒂哈去见提克里斯——娜瑞瓦派出了她最出色的两名法师猎手去执行这项任务，但他们都失败了。你可以替阿斯特莱娅完成她的任务。尽管贝尔温非常关心玛蒂哈，也希望她能得到最好的结果，但玛蒂哈毕竟仍是一名被通缉的罪犯。
                    
                    如果你这么做，就等于背弃了贝林的意愿，但将玛蒂哈送到提克里斯去接受审判，才是公平的做法。而且，如果你这么做了，很可能还能获得阿斯特里达组织的认可与赞赏。
                    
                    你是应该按照原计划把玛蒂哈送到荒废驿堡去，还是应该把她送到提克里斯去为她的罪行接受审判呢？

rows.original:
No, you told Berwyn that you’d do one thing in particular, and you’re going to do it. You’re no liar. And while you’ll admit that Matiha’s done some questionable things, she was also under the influence of a dangerous stone that altered her state of mind – she, herself, is a victim. She needs help, not punishment.

                        Finding the Wayfort in Savarra was a simple enough task, and[pc.isDK
                            | as soon as you did, you simply dumped Matiha there and let the Waystone do the rest of the work. In a blink and a flash of light, Matiha’s body vanishes without a trace, dumped like a sack of dirty laundry at the Wayfort. That’s one less thing to worry about, probably.
                            |, once you do, you step through it and find a spot to gently lay Matiha down in a sitting position. She’ll be confused and distraught when she wakes up – and, if you were right, she might still be violent – but, hopefully, she’d also have the sense to realize that the Wayfort is a safe place for her to be. Maybe one day she and Berwyn will be reunited.
                        ]
                        
                        That still leaves the issue of Elexis’ Waystone charm, but you think you have the answer to that. But it’ll have to wait until you get back to Hawkethorne.
                        
                        You make your way back to Berwyn. He hasn’t moved from his spot in the fort’s courtyard, and his hat remains gently placed against his chest, with his eyes downcast at where Matiha was. He’s still trying to come to terms with everything that’s happened – he could probably use a distraction.
rows.translation:
不，你告诉过贝尔温你会做某件事，而且你一定会去做。你不是一个骗子。虽然你承认玛蒂哈做过一些值得怀疑的事情，但她也是在一块会改变她心理状态的危险石头的影响下才这么做的——她本身也是受害者。她需要的是帮助，而不是惩罚。

                        在萨瓦拉找到荒废驿堡其实是一件相当简单的事情[pc.isDK
                            | 你一完成那件事，就把玛蒂哈丢在了那里，然后让路石完成了剩下的工作。转眼间，玛蒂哈的身体就消失得无影无踪了，就像一袋脏衣服被扔在了荒废驿堡那里。这样一来，至少又少了一件需要担心的事情了。
                            |一旦你完成了这些步骤，就可以走进那个地方，找一个合适的位置，让玛蒂哈坐下来。她醒来时一定会感到困惑和不安——而且，如果你判断正确的话，她可能仍然会表现出攻击性——但希望她也能意识到，荒废驿堡这个地方对她来说是安全的。也许有一天，她和贝尔温能够重逢。
                        ]
                        
                        不过，艾丽克丝的路石护符这个问题依然存在，但你觉得自己已经找到了解决办法。不过，这个答案要等到你回到鹰棘镇才能得到。
                        
                        你回到了贝尔温。他仍然站在堡垒的院子里，帽子轻轻搭在胸前，目光凝视着玛蒂哈曾经站过的地方。他仍在努力接受这一切发生的事情——他或许需要一些事情来转移一下注意力。

rows.original: Unfortunately, there’s simply no getting around the fact that Matiha’s done some awful things recently. Enough to draw the attention of one of the Seven and the cult army that she commands. Not only would sending Matiha to Tychris be justified, you also don’t want to give the Astrida a reason to dislike you as well. You gently lie Matiha on the ground – or whatever passes for it in the Ways Between – and you do as you did with Elexis: you open her hand; place Elexis’ Waystone charm in her palm; and then squeeze. As before, a blanket of blue light envelops Matiha’s body, just like it had with Elexis, and then, after another moment and with a blink, she vanishes. Gone within the ether of the Ways Between, headed towards wherever Tychris is and for whoever is waiting for her there. [pc.isDK |That’s one less thing for you to worry about. |You won’t pretend that that wasn’t difficult, but it was, overall, the right thing to do. ] You make your way back to Berwyn. He hasn’t moved from his spot in the fort’s courtyard, and his hat remains gently placed against his chest, with his eyes downcast at where Matiha was. He’s still trying to come to terms with everything that’s happened – he could probably use a distraction.
rows.translation: 不幸的是，事实就是：玛蒂哈最近确实做了一些非常糟糕的事情。这些行为足以引起“七人组”中某个人的注意，以及她所领导的那个邪教军队的注意。将玛蒂哈送到提克里斯去，不仅是合理的做法，同时你也不想给阿斯特里达任何讨厌你的理由。 你轻轻地将玛蒂哈放在地上——在那些被称为“道路之间”的地方，地面应该就是这样的吧——然后你照之前对埃莱克西斯所做的那样：打开她的手掌，将埃莱克西斯的路石护身符放在她的掌心，然后再轻轻捏紧她的手。 与之前一样，一层蓝色的光芒笼罩了玛蒂哈的身体，就如同它曾经笼罩过埃莱克西斯一样。片刻之后，随着她眨动眼睛的瞬间，她消失了——融入了那些“道路之间”的虚无之中，朝着提克里斯所在的地方，朝着那里正在等待她的人走去。 [pc.isDK |这样又少了一件烦心事。你没什么好担心的。 |你不会假装这件事并不困难，但总体来说，这确实是正确的做法。 ] 你回到了贝尔温。他依然坐在堡垒的院子里，帽子轻轻搭在胸前，目光凝视着玛蒂哈曾经站过的地方。他仍在努力接受这一切发生的事情——或许，他需要一些事情来转移自己的注意力。

rows.original: Send Matiha to Tychris, the headquarters of the Order Astrida in the Marches. She will no doubt face justice for her crimes, but so too will she never again threaten the world with her uncontrolled magic.
rows.translation: 将玛蒂哈送到位于边境地区的阿斯特里达教团总部——提克里斯吧。她无疑会为自己的罪行受到应有的惩罚，但这样一来，她的那股失控的魔力也就再也不会威胁到这个世界了。
rows.raw: "Send Matiha to Tychris, the headquarters of the Order Astrida in the Marches. She will no doubt face justice for her crimes, but so too will she never again threaten the world with her uncontrolled magic."

rows.original: If Berwyn’s really so concerned over what kind of person Matiha is when she wakes up, perhaps it’ll be best to send her somewhere she could do the least amount of damage. The Wayfort seems like a reasonable place – and she’ll have lots of company in there, too.
rows.translation: 如果贝尔温真的那么担心玛蒂哈醒来后会变成什么样的人，或许把她送到一个她不会造成太多伤害的地方会比较好。荒废驿堡似乎是个不错的选择——而且那里也会有很多人陪她。
rows.raw: "If Berwyn’s really so concerned over what kind of person Matiha is when she wakes up, perhaps it’ll be best to send her somewhere she could do the least amount of damage. The Wayfort seems like a reasonable place – and she’ll have lots of company in there, too."

rows.original: If Berwyn is so concerned about Matiha and how she’ll react towards him when she wakes up, then... in all honesty, it may be for the best for both of them if she’s sent away before she does. It’d be tough for Berwyn to go through that a second time, and his fears aren’t totally unfounded: she may try to take advantage of him a second time. Who knows how powerful she’ll be when she wakes up? "Yeah," he sighs dejectedly, his shoulders slumping. He knew that this was the advice that you could have given him, but he still hoped that it wasn’t. That said, rather than just cast her to the wastes and wash your hands of her forever, there’s an alternative that you can think of. If Berwyn isn’t comfortable with Matiha staying here in the fortress with him when she wakes up, then they could try sending her to... a friend of yours. Another witch. "You know a second witch?" he asks incredulously. "Must be a small world." Maybe, but this other witch that you know of helped you to make it that much smaller. You tell him of the tanuki witch Evergreen: she resides in the Frostwood, a few hours north from Hawkethorne. She won’t be expecting any guests, but you’re absolutely confident that she’d find it in her heart to take good care of a fellow witch, especially one of such high repute as Matiha. Berwyn watches you with some hesitancy, trying to find the lie in your words. [pc.isDK |He’s not going to find any, of course, because you’re not lying. Not directly, anyway. Every word you’ve said is the truth. |You try and maintain a neutral expression underneath his scrutiny: technically, nothing you’ve said is a lie, but there’s absolutely one or two things that you’re neglecting to mention. ] "You’re sure this Evergreen woman will take care of Matiha?" he asks again, his eyebrows arching with concern and uncertainty. That, you say again with confidence: there wouldn’t be a more capable woman in all of Savarra that could adequately look after Matiha until she’s fully recuperated. Berwyn’s eyes sadly go from yours, to Matiha’s, still comatose between you two. "Okay. I trust you," he says before turning around. "Just... don’t make me watch her leave. I need you to do it for me." It’s the least you could do. Matiha doesn’t stir when you hoist her onto your shoulders, carrying her piggyback out of the fortress’s boundaries.
rows.translation: 如果贝尔温如此担心玛蒂哈醒来后会如何对待他，那么……说实话，如果在她醒来之前就把她送走，或许对他们俩来说都是最好的结果。对贝尔温来说，再次经历这种事情肯定非常艰难，而且他的担忧也并非毫无根据：玛蒂哈很可能还会再次利用他。谁知道她醒来后会变得有多强大呢？ “是啊，”他沮丧地叹了口气，肩膀也耷拉了下来。他早就知道，这正是别人会给他的建议可以你已经给了他，但他仍然希望那并不是真的。 话虽如此，你并不一定非得把她抛弃在荒芜之地，从此不再过问她的事情。其实还有一个其他的办法可以考虑。如果贝林不愿意让玛蒂哈在醒来后继续和他一起留在这座堡垒里，那么他们可以试着把她送到别的地方去。……你的一个朋友。另一个女巫。 “你认识第二个女巫？”他难以置信地问道，“这个世界也太小了吧。” 也许吧，但你知道的那个女巫，其实让你的世界变得更小了。你告诉他关于那只名叫常青女士的狸猫女巫的事：她住在霜木林里，距离鹰棘镇以北几个小时的路程。她应该不会期待有客人来访，但你非常有信心，她一定会热心地帮助一位同为女巫的同伴，尤其是像玛蒂哈这样声望崇高的人。 贝尔温带着些许犹豫注视着你，试图找出你话中隐藏的谎言。 [pc.isDK |他当然找不到任何证据，因为你并没有说谎。至少不是直接说谎。你说的每一句话都是事实。 |在他的审视下，你努力保持着中立的表情：从技术上讲，你所说的话并没有任何谎言，但确实有一两件事你选择没有提及。 ] 你当然可以。这个永远年轻的女人真的能够照顾好玛蒂哈吗？”他再次问道，眉头因担忧和不确定而微微蹙起。而你则自信地回答道：在整个萨瓦拉地区，没有哪个女人比她更有能力，在玛蒂哈完全康复之前好好照顾她。 贝尔温的目光无奈地从你身上转向仍然昏迷不醒的玛蒂哈。“好吧，我相信你们，”他说着转身离开，“只是……请不要让我看着她离开。我真心希望你们能帮我做到这一点。” 这至少是你们能做的吧。当你把玛蒂哈抱到肩上，背着她走出堡垒的边界时，她丝毫没有动弹。
